each segment have NOT been bisected." They are now, and the answer makes the
operator's decision close to automatic without this comment deciding anything.
I am not claiming this bead and not authoring its acceptance.

Measured at HEAD cedc402f (the bead's reading was at 945130b5; the drift has
only grown since).

FINDING 1: EVERY DRIFTING COMMIT IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN. No agent touched
either file.

  git log 3d1d9a55..HEAD -- AGENTS.md        11 commits
  git log 3d1d9a55..HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md     40 commits

  Authors across all 51: "Jeff Emanuel", "Jeffrey Emanuel", and one
  "Dicklesworthstone" (699f9ff7, "chore(toolchain): update pinned nightly to
  2026-08-25"), which is the operator's own GitHub handle, as the repository
  URLs in both files show. So the count of agent-authored edits to the two
  frozen documents since the freeze is ZERO.

  The frozen digests therefore pin two LIVING operator documents, and the
  drift is not a control failure by anyone the contract was written to
  constrain. Among the eleven AGENTS.md commits:
      7c02d8e0 b5709ae5  docs(fnd-01) pins and dated nightly
      0c5a665b            the curl user-agent rule
      bfe234c9 331f3efe   "RULE 0.5 - DSR only, never GitHub Actions", TWICE
      9114fbec            "add PL-6 control-drift attribution"
  which also answers the bead's other open observation. It noted "the RULE 0.5
  block, which appears twice". It does: two separate commits carry the same
  subject, both the operator's, and both blocks are present in HEAD. That is a
  duplicated paste, not a corruption, and RULE 0.5's own text says it is a
  permanent rule recorded after a repeat violation.

FINDING 2, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: PUTTING THE FROZEN CHANGELOG
BYTES BACK WOULD REINSTATE WITHDRAWN CAPABILITY CLAIMS.

The frozen segment is the historical suffix from the "## [v0.2.0]" heading
through EOF, 26197 B at the freeze, 27259 B at HEAD, and the two are the SAME
NUMBER OF LINES (161). So nothing was appended; the existing historical
entries were rewritten in place. I diffed them (3d1d9a55 lines 50-210 against
HEAD lines 749-909). The edits are a systematic honesty downgrade. Verbatim,
frozen -> HEAD:

  "Complete OAuth 2.0/2.1 with mandatory PKCE, token issuance, RFC 7009
   revocation, dynamic client registration, scope validation..."
  -> "Historical OAuth authorization-server prototype -- Introduced ...
      surfaces. Its initial placeholder cryptographic helpers were hardened
      later; neither change established OAuth 2.0/2.1 conformance or current
      production readiness."

  "OIDC integration -- OpenID Connect provider discovery, JWKS
   fetching/caching, ID token validation and claims extraction."
  -> "Historical OIDC integration prototype (quarantined) -- ... current
      source advertises no signing algorithms/JWKS and fails closed for
      ID-token issuance. JWKS fetch/cache and ID-token validation are not
      current supported capabilities."

  "Full HTTP transport implementation enabling browser and HTTP-client-based
   MCP interactions."
  -> "Historical HTTP transport prototype -- ... that listener is now
      quarantined and is not current public HTTP support."

  "Feature parity assessment -- Comprehensive analysis vs Python FastMCP
   v2.14.4, initially at ~90-95%, reaching 100% by 2026-01-28."
  -> "Historical feature-parity assessment -- Contemporary project documents
      estimated ... Those estimates were not a protocol-conformance
      attestation and are not a current aggregate-support claim."

  "Bidirectional MCP features -- Full-duplex transport handling..."
  -> "Historical bidirectional MCP building blocks -- ... custom/SSE/WebSocket
      paths remain sequential and public HTTP is fail-closed, so aggregate
      full-duplex support is not claimed."

  Plus one ordinary API correction, not an honesty edit:
  "read_only_hint = true, destructive_hint = false"
  -> "read_only = true, destructive = false"

  So the frozen bytes are a snapshot of the CHANGELOG taken BEFORE the project
  retracted a set of overclaims about OAuth, OIDC, HTTP, full-duplex and
  Python parity. Putting them back would return those claims to the shipped
  CHANGELOG. Every one of the rewrites moves in the direction AGENTS.md's own
  campaign rules demand, and several match this repository's standing posture
  verbatim ("MCP 2026-07-28 support is under implementation and remains
  unverified", "ID-token issuance remains fail-closed").

WHAT I AM AND AM NOT SAYING. I am not re-freezing anything, not editing either
document, and not writing this bead's acceptance. I am also not asserting that
re-freezing is costless: an ahet.1.14 authoring-path edit of
dependency-verification.toml moves every digest that binds that file, exactly
as this bead already states. What I am saying is narrower and checkable: the
second branch, reinstating the frozen byte ranges, is not a neutral rollback.
For the CHANGELOG segment it is a retraction of a retraction, and anyone
choosing it should know that is what they are choosing.

A STRUCTURAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER AUTHORS THE ACCEPTANCE. A byte-exact freeze over
a range that ends at EOF of a living document is a bar that the document's
normal use breaks. The AGENTS-OPERATIONAL-SUFFIX segment (17582 -> 17729 B)
and the CHANGELOG suffix will both drift again on the next operator edit, so
re-freezing to HEAD buys time, not correctness. If the property actually worth
protecting is "the historical entries are not silently rewritten", a digest
over the whole suffix cannot express it, because it fires identically for an
honesty correction and for a quiet overclaim reinstatement. It fired here on
the former. Naming the property is the operator's call; I am flagging that the
instrument does not currently distinguish the two cases it most needs to.

NO-CLAIM. I did not verify the three AGENTS.md segment digests myself and did
not run tools/fnd01_prose_digests.py; I took this bead's measurements as given
and added only the authorship bisect and the CHANGELOG segment diff, both of
which are reproducible from the two commands quoted above.

title: AUTH-05 implementation B: credential crash recovery, rollback protection and custody hardening
description:
Executable implementation B leaf for formal package AUTH-05.

Canonical B capability slice: credential crash recovery, rollback protection and custody hardening.
Named consumer: AUTH-05 integration child.

Real implementation and its real positive and near-identical planted-negative tests are one Bead. Placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, validator/test weakening, golden regeneration around broken behavior, and follow-up laundering are forbidden. Capability credit is limited to this named slice and begins only after central revision-bound batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must replace the preclaim-denied ownership card with exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No whole-crate or repository glob is valid.

Self-contained canonical parent contract follows verbatim:

Authoritative work package from `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_SUPPORT_MCP_2026-07-28_SPEC_IN_FASTMCP_RUST.md`:

### AUTH-05 — Redesign the credential store

Outcome:

Persist credentials without issuer confusion or accidental exposure.

Reason:

The final spec requires credentials to be bound to the authorization
server that issued them.

Implementation:

- Use AUTH-00's `CredentialStoreKey`, including exact issuer,
  canonical resource, accepted-audience-policy identity/revision,
  client identity, registration mechanism, and relevant auth profile.
- Never look up by host name alone.
- Bind access tokens, refresh tokens, pre-registered credentials, and
  DCR-issued credentials to the exact issuer/resource/audience-policy
  partition.
- On issuer change, invalidate old tokens and issuer-bound
  pre-registered/DCR secrets or registrations, then require the
  applicable new-issuer registration path.
- Treat an HTTPS Client ID Metadata Document URL as portable across
  authorization servers as the final spec requires. Retain the client
  ID URL, refetch/revalidate its document and redirect-URI metadata
  under AUTH-03's SSRF/TLS policy, and start authorization against the
  new issuer without inventing re-registration.
- Store access and refresh tokens separately from public registration
  metadata.
- Define secure-store trait and memory-only default.
- Treat the exact disk credential backend, platform/file service,
  external anchor, envelope/key service, and durability/clock boundary
  as the selected persistent profile's TCB unless an independently
  verifiable attestation proves the property. A sealed facade can
  reject malformed/substituted receipts but cannot detect a dishonest
  well-formed anchor that lies about pending/committed generation,
  file digest, restore-fence CAS, or durable flush. Promotion therefore
  names immutable provider/configuration artifacts and passes crash,
  rollback, concurrency, cancellation, and deliberate lying-adapter
  conformance tests; implementing the trait is not support evidence.
- Make disk persistence a runtime-explicit opt-in that is unavailable
  unless a credential-specific wrapper around FND-08's
  `EnvelopeProtector` is configured. The provider obtains keys and
  nonce-sequence authority from a platform store, external sequence
  store, or conforming KMS/HSM; plaintext key/counter files beside the
  credential database are forbidden.
- Persist FND-08's versioned, length-delimited envelope with
  credential-store-key, store-identity, generation, and commit-digest
  AAD. Authenticate all public routing metadata that selects a
  ciphertext. Credential code never supplies its own algorithm, key ID,
  nonce, or tag.
- Register the exact credential-file/anchor pair as one FND-08
  restore-coordinated store. Before sealing any replacement, prepare a
  restore-write intent and bind its sealed `RestoreWriteFence`,
  operation ID, stable binding digest, and expected local store-fence
  generation into the envelope, anchor pending record, and candidate
  file. The external anchor transaction below is this store's durable
  CAS authority: it compares the local restore-fence generation and
  records the operation ID plus complete candidate-file digest before
  returning a `DurableStoreCommitReceipt`. Complete the authority
  intent only after the file/anchor recovery state proves that digest
  committed; abort or reconcile ambiguity by operation ID and never
  reseal/replay the write blindly.
- Require `CredentialProtector` to provide a rollback-resistant
  generation/commit-digest anchor independent of the replaceable
  credential file—for example a platform secure store, TPM-backed
  record, or remote KMS metadata CAS. An authenticated generation
  stored only inside the same ciphertext does not detect replay of an
  older valid whole file; without an independent anchor, persistent
  credential storage is unavailable rather than falsely advertised as
  rollback-safe.
- Use a two-phase anchor record containing committed and optional
  pending generation/digest, restore-intent operation ID, stable
  binding digest, and local restore-fence generation. Prepare the
  pending anchor, durably
  replace the file, then commit the anchor. On recovery, accept only a
  file matching the committed or pending digest: abort a pending state
  when the old committed file remains, finalize when the pending file
  is present, and fail closed for every other pairing.
- Epoch advance first closes intent issuance and the store's bounded
  single-writer lease, reconciles every pending file/anchor/authority
  operation, then durably increments the anchor's local restore-fence
  generation and returns its registered-store quiesce receipt. No old-
  epoch candidate may replace the file after that CAS. Restore/
  authority migration uses the sealed new-epoch migration fence and
  re-encrypts the complete credential set before reopening.
- Define a `SecureCredentialFile` capability over FND-07's reviewed
  handle-relative filesystem primitives. Before the first read or
  write, acquire and retain an owner-controlled parent-directory handle,
  validate owner-only/no-untrusted ACL policy, reject symlink/junction/
  reparse traversal, and identify the exact store file. Open, create,
  read, temporary-write, and replace only relative to that handle with
  no-follow semantics; reject a multi-link target and lock the exact
  store identity rather than a path string.
- Write through a unique file opened relative to the retained parent,
  set owner-only permissions/ACL before secret bytes, flush contents,
  atomically replace the verified prior identity, revalidate parent/
  target metadata and link/ACL invariants at commit, and flush the
  parent directory where the platform provides those guarantees. Use a
  bounded, cancel-aware single-writer lease and never expose a
  half-written access/refresh-token pair.
- Refuse disk persistence on a platform/filesystem where
  handle-relative no-follow open, owner/ACL validation, exact-identity
  locking, atomic replace, or required durability cannot be proven.
  An attacker-writable parent, reparse-backed path, hard-linked target,
  or permission/ACL change is unsupported even if the final file once
  appeared owner-only; platform secure-store persistence remains the
  safe alternative.
- Fail closed, preserve the corrupt artifact for operator recovery, and
  emit only redacted diagnostics on truncation, authentication failure,
  unknown format/key version, wrong key, rollback detection, or an
  unsupported migration. Never silently reset to an empty store.
- Define forward-only format migration, online key rotation with an
  explicit old-key overlap, atomic credential replacement, secure
  logical erasure/tombstoning, retention bounds for superseded
  ciphertext, and backup/restore trust assumptions.
- Add rotation and revocation hooks.
- Redact all key and token diagnostics.
- Partition client caches by resulting auth context.
- Recompute `CachePartitionKey`, token-bound
  `ContinuationPartitionKey`, and `SubscriptionPartitionKey` whenever
  an access-token instance, effective verified grant, or accepted-
  audience-policy revision changes. Quarantine rather than silently
  re-key a credential family when its audience policy changes.
- Preserve `DurableOwnerKey` across ordinary refresh only when stable
  verified ownership is unchanged, then reauthorize every durable
  operation under the refreshed token.

Acceptance:

- Credentials from issuer A are never sent to issuer B.
- Credentials accepted under one resource-to-audience policy revision
  are never silently reused under another.
- Issuer change invalidates tokens and issuer-bound pre-registered or
  DCR credentials, while a valid CIMD client ID is revalidated and
  reused without re-registration.
- The default does not persist secrets.
- Disk persistence refuses insecure permissions.
- Persisted credentials are confidential and tamper evident; crash,
  corruption, rollback, or concurrent writers cannot expose or select
  a partial credential set.
- Path/parent replacement, link tricks, or ACL changes cannot redirect
  or expose the store; unsupported filesystem semantics fail before
  secret read or write.
- Replaying an older whole ciphertext plus its embedded generation
  fails against the independent anchor.
- Cache partitions change with auth context.

Tests:

title: fastmcp-client: three tasks-gated tests fail on first execution under --features tasks
description:
Three fastmcp-client tests fail ONLY when the opt-in `tasks` feature is enabled. They are
NEWLY REACHABLE, not newly broken, and every no-features client receipt in this campaign
is silent about them.

  http_auth::discovery::client_credentials::tasks::tests::
      both_extensions_are_explicit_and_other_profiles_cannot_be_smuggled_in
  http_auth::managed::tasks::tests::
      explicit_tasks_selection_is_advertised_on_discovery_without_other_extensions
  tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed

MEASURED: cargo test --no-fail-fast -p fastmcp-client --features native-tls-roots,tasks
exit=101, 1173 passed / 15 failed / 0 FILTERED OUT across 20 top-level summaries.

ATTRIBUTION, checked rather than assumed: all three are ABSENT from the earlier
no-features run of the same crate (cargo test --no-fail-fast -p fastmcp-client at
e87a6c15). fastmcp-client declares default = ["legacy-2024-11-05"]; `tasks` is opt-in, so
those tests were never compiled, never discovered, and never counted. This is the same
class as the eight OAuth subscription tests that only became visible once their target
compiled: **a green that never reached the code is not evidence about the code.**

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THREE TESTS: this is the fifth crate in this workspace where a naive
invocation produces a confident green over a partial surface — after fastmcp-transport
(no `default` key at all), fastmcp-rust (`testing-lab` gates six targets), fastmcp-cli
(`tasks` + `e2e-fixture`), and fastmcp-protocol (`default = []`). Any receipt citing
fastmcp-client without naming its features should be read as covering the
legacy-2024-11-05 surface ONLY.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether these three ever passed. I have no green baseline for them under
`tasks` — this is their first execution in my lane, exactly as the FND-01 evidence target
was when it showed 11 failures on its first run, most of them pre-existing. DO NOT treat
them as a regression and do not bisect for a breaking commit until a passing revision is
found; there may not be one.

IN SCOPE: read the three failures, classify each as (a) a real defect in tasks-gated code,
(b) a stale test asserting a contract that has since changed, or (c) fixture/harness.
Report the SPLIT. The two `tasks::tests::` names both concern EXTENSION ADVERTISEMENT —
"both extensions are explicit", "other profiles cannot be smuggled in", "advertised on
discovery without other extensions" — so they plausibly share a cause; state that as a
hypothesis with a disconfirmer rather than assuming it, and apply the materiality test
(remove the suspect, re-run; if it stays red it is not the cause).

EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE: disabling the `tasks` feature, narrowing a test to make it pass,
or removing the assertions. A test that fails only when its feature is enabled is doing
its job.
close_reason: Verified by WildMountain. commit:59f7d0232d851176c6a5571cd0a2b13539e2083e run:202300-97514 evidence:bead-receipt-460kj — 3-of-3 RESOLVED, reported against the owner's own falsifiable prediction table rather than against a total. Both 'tests 1 and 2 pass' and 'test 3 passes' rows observed; neither failure row occurred; zero FAILED and zero panicked in the log; real compile 4m42s. THREE DISTINCT MECHANISMS, not one defect repeated: a lossy TYPE for tests 1-2 (ClientCapabilities silently dropped the planted field until 9ba90837 gave it experimental and extensions) and a lossy BOUNDARY for test 3 (a 3xx became Err(Redirect) at http_executor.rs:9601 and was flattened to Transport before require_success could map it; fixed at 05b0e4bf by carrying the typed error through a new ClientCredentialsError::Redirect variant, with the arm ordered ABOVE the fallthrough). The card correctly refused --lib, which would have covered two of three silently. comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
SPLIT for the three tasks-gated failures. HazyTurtle, 2026-09-17. Static analysis only,
zero slots spent. Two of three are CLASSIFIED AND EXPLAINED; the third is not, and I say
so rather than rounding it up.

  test 1  both_extensions_are_explicit_and_other_profiles_cannot_be_smuggled_in   (c) HARNESS
  test 2  explicit_tasks_selection_is_advertised_on_discovery_without_other_extensions (c) HARNESS
  test 3  tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed                   UNCLASSIFIED

=== THE SHARED-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED, ON A MECHANISM RATHER THAN A SHAPE ===

Both failures plant a foreign/oversized extension into `ClientCapabilities` and assert the
code under test rejects it. **`ClientCapabilities` structurally cannot carry an
`extensions` key**, so the planted mutation is silently discarded before the code under
test ever sees it.

  protocol/src/types.rs:93-103   pub struct ClientCapabilities { sampling, elicitation, roots }
                                 NO `extensions` field. NO deny_unknown_fields.
                                 NO flatten/additional catch-all.

Serde's default is to ignore unknown fields, so deserializing an object containing
`extensions` yields a plain `ClientCapabilities::default()` with the key dropped.

test 1, client_credentials/tasks.rs:443-447
    value[FINAL_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES_META_KEY]["extensions"] = extensions;   // planted
    assert!(task_metadata(serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap()).is_err());
                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ round-trip through the typed
                          struct drops the plant

test 2, managed/tasks.rs:547-549
    conflicting.client_capabilities =
        serde_json::from_value(json!({"extensions":{"com.example/other":{}}})).unwrap();
                               ^^^^ deserializes to ClientCapabilities::default(); the
                               conflict does not exist by the next line
    assert!(matches!(tasks_metadata(conflicting), Err(ManagedTasksError::Negotiation)));

In both, the callee then sees NO extensions, takes the non-conflicting path, and returns
Ok. The assertion demanding Err therefore fails. **These are planted negatives that cannot
fire** — the classic pattern this campaign has paid for repeatedly, in its most exact
form: the mutation is normalized away by a typed boundary between the plant and the check.

DISCONFIRMER, stated because the hypothesis was handed to me and I was told not to inherit
it: if either test's plant survived its round-trip, the shared cause would be refuted and
they would need separate explanations. Neither survives, and the reason is a property of
`ClientCapabilities` rather than of either test. That is a mechanism, checkable in source,
not the "both are about extension advertisement" resemblance the bead flagged as
insufficient.

FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, since I do not hold the panic text: both should fail as ASSERTION
failures -- `assertion failed: task_metadata(..).is_err()` and a `matches!` assertion --
NOT as `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value`. If either is an unwrap panic instead,
the round-trip is REJECTING rather than dropping, my mechanism is wrong, and the
classification becomes (b) stale-contract. One line of panic text settles it.

=== THE DEEPER FINDING: THE GUARD THESE TESTS EXIST TO PROVE IS UNREACHABLE ===

client_credentials/tasks.rs:277-283 validates extensions:

    if let Some(extensions) = caps.get("extensions") {
        ... reject foreign names or non-empty values ...
    }

`caps` is the serialized `client_capabilities` field of a `FinalRequestMeta`, i.e. a
serialized `ClientCapabilities`, which as established can never contain `extensions`. So
`caps.get("extensions")` is ALWAYS None and this block can never execute through this
entry point. `FinalRequestMeta.additional_metadata` does not rescue it either -- that
flatten captures unknown keys at the METADATA level, not inside clientCapabilities.

The guard is not wrong; it is defensive code with no reachable input. That is worth a
decision by whoever owns the tasks profile: either the type should carry extensions (and
the guard becomes live and the tests become meaningful), or the guard is unreachable by
construction and should say so. NOT MY CALL and NOT IN THIS BEAD'S SCOPE -- recorded
because the tests cannot be made meaningful without deciding it, and "fix the test" here
would mean writing a test that asserts unreachable code stays unreachable.

WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT DOING, per the bead: not disabling `tasks`, not narrowing either
test, not removing assertions. Both tests are asserting a real intended contract. The
contract is simply not reachable through the API they call.

=== TEST 3: UNCLASSIFIED, AND A DIFFERENT CLASS ===

`tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed` is NOT in src/. It is
crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials/subscriptions.rs:409, a
SUBPROCESS-ISOLATED integration test:

    fn listen_redirect_is_not_followed() {
        isolated_subscription("tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed",
                              SubCase::Redirect);
    }

The string is the CHILD test the harness re-executes via Command::new(current_exe()). So
this shares nothing structurally with tests 1 and 2 -- different target, different
mechanism, subprocess harness. I have NOT classified it and will not guess to complete a
tidy 3-of-3. It needs either its panic text or a read of the isolated_subscription
harness, and I would rather report 2 classified + 1 open than three with one invented.

Noting for load-attribution only: this harness is the 30s bounded-wait family WildMountain
measured, NOT the 400-900ms family, so load is an unlikely explanation here.

No status change. Claims nothing, closes nothing.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
RULING — WildMountain. HazyTurtle's analysis is confirmed, and the producer two lines above
the guard closes it. But the conclusion inverts: the TYPE is the defect, not the tests and
not the guard.

CONFIRMED, both facts, checked in source rather than accepted:

  types.rs:93-103   ClientCapabilities { sampling, elicitation, roots }
                    NO `extensions`, NO deny_unknown_fields, NO flatten
                    -> serde silently DROPS an unknown `extensions` key on deserialize

  tasks.rs:274      let mut meta = serde_json::to_value(metadata)?;   <- the producer
  tasks.rs:275-277  caps = meta[FINAL_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES_META_KEY];
                    if let Some(extensions) = caps.get("extensions")  <- the guard

The object the guard reads is SERIALIZED FROM THE TYPE, two lines above it. A type with no
`extensions` field cannot serialize one. So `caps.get("extensions")` is ALWAYS None and the
guard body never executes through this entry point. HazyTurtle is right, and the proof is
closer than it realised — the producer is not somewhere up the call chain, it is line 274.

THE INVERSION, and it is the finding. Look at what the very next line does:

  tasks.rs:284      caps.insert("extensions", json!({TASKS_EXTENSION:{},
                                                     CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_EXTENSION:{}}));

**THIS CODE WRITES `extensions` INTO clientCapabilities ON THE WIRE.** So extensions ARE
part of that structure in this protocol — the implementation puts them there deliberately,
three lines after checking for them. What cannot represent them is `ClientCapabilities`
THE TYPE.

So the round trip is LOSSY IN ONE DIRECTION: the code serializes a typed value, adds
extensions to the JSON, sends it — and anything that deserializes that wire form back into
`ClientCapabilities` SILENTLY DISCARDS the extensions the protocol just carried. That is a
type-level data-loss defect, and it is the same class as bd-hf8uo: a type that quietly
drops wire content it has no field for.

RULING:
  THE GUARD IS CORRECT and stays. It is not defensive code with no reachable input; it is
  correct code whose input is being normalized away upstream by a lossy type.
  THE TWO TESTS ARE CORRECT IN INTENT and currently cannot fire. They are not to be
  deleted, narrowed, or rewritten to assert that unreachable code stays unreachable — that
  would encode the defect as the specification.
  THE TYPE IS WHAT CHANGES. `ClientCapabilities` needs to represent extensions, after
  which the guard becomes live and both tests become meaningful without either being
  touched.

WHAT IS NOT MINE. Adding a field to a protocol type in fastmcp-protocol is a contract
change against the MCP 2026-07-28 schema, and the schema decides the shape — the same
constraint that settled bd-hf8uo, where the authoritative schema's universal openness
made `deny_unknown_fields` non-conformant. CHECK THE SCHEMA FIRST: if it declares
extensions inside clientCapabilities, this is a straightforward gap; if it does not, then
the code writing them at :284 is the non-conformance and the answer runs the other way.
I am not guessing which, and neither should whoever takes it.

CREDIT. The split was reported 2 classified / 1 UNCLASSIFIED with "I am not rounding the
third up to make it 3-of-3" — the honest form. And the shared cause was established on a
MECHANISM checkable in source, with an explicit disconfirmer ("if either plant survived
its round-trip, the shared cause would be refuted"), rather than on the resemblance I had
flagged as insufficient when I filed the bead. That is the distinction between a
hypothesis and a finding, drawn by the person who could most easily have blurred it.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
SCHEMA CHECK, per WildMountain's ruling ("check the schema first; I am not guessing which
way it runs"). HazyTurtle, 2026-09-17. Zero slots; the authoritative schema is vendored
in-tree.

SOURCE: evidence/fnd-01/vendor/core/mcp-schema-2026-07-28-5f5440bb.json

  SCHEMA  ClientCapabilities: [elicitation, experimental, extensions, roots, sampling]
  RUST    ClientCapabilities: [elicitation,                          roots, sampling]
  MISSING:                    [experimental, extensions]

RESULT: the FIRST branch of the ruling holds. `extensions` IS schema-declared inside
ClientCapabilities, so the code at tasks.rs:284 writing extensions into clientCapabilities
is CONFORMANT, and the Rust type is the non-conformance. This is a straightforward gap,
not a case where the writer is the defect.

The schema's own description settles it beyond argument:

  "Optional MCP extensions that the client supports. Keys are extension identifiers
   (e.g., "io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials"), and values are
   per-extension settings objects. An empty object indicates support with no settings."

Two things follow from that sentence:
  - it names as its worked example the EXACT constant these tests plant
    (CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_EXTENSION, client_credentials.rs:60);
  - "an empty object indicates support with no settings" is precisely the rule the guard
    at tasks.rs:277-283 enforces when it rejects non-empty extension values. The guard
    implements the schema faithfully. It simply never receives input, because the producer
    at :274 serializes from a type that cannot carry the field.

SECOND GAP, found only by diffing the full property set rather than grepping for the one
field I came for: `experimental` is ALSO missing -- "Experimental, non-standard
capabilities that the client supports." A type missing two schema-declared fields is a
different-sized job from one missing a single field, and the fix should be scoped against
the schema rather than against these two tests.

`additionalProperties` is UNSET on the schema's ClientCapabilities, i.e. open. Consistent
with the universal-openness constraint recorded on bd-hf8uo, so a fix here should not
reach for deny_unknown_fields.

WHAT THIS SETTLES: the direction. The type changes; the guard and both tests stay
untouched, as ruled. Neither test should be rewritten, and encoding the defect as the
specification is now clearly wrong.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and is outside my lane: the shape of the Rust field, whether
adding it breaks other consumers of ClientCapabilities, and whether `experimental` lands
in the same change. Those are contract changes in fastmcp-protocol. I am not taking them
and hold no reservation on that file.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN COMMENT ABOVE: I wrote that the guard is "defensive code with no
reachable input." That reads the unreachability as a property of the GUARD when it is a
symptom of the TYPE. The producer at :274 and the writer at :284 were both in code I had
already read and I did not connect them. The classification of the two tests as (c) stands
and is unaffected; the prescription I drew from it was wrong.

No status change. Claims nothing, closes nothing.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
TEST 3 — as far as source can take it, with the discriminator that finishes it.
HazyTurtle, 2026-09-17. Static only, zero slots.

VERDICT: NOT (c) harness. The harness is sound. Between (a) real defect and (b) stale
contract I cannot choose from source, and the panic message chooses for you in one line.

=== THE HARNESS IS SOUND — three hazards checked and cleared ===

tests/oauth_client_credentials/subscriptions.rs:23-44

  fn isolated_subscription(name, case) {
      if let Ok(selected) = env::var(SUB_CHILD) { assert_eq!(selected, name);
                                                  run_subscription(case); return; }
      let mut child = Child(Command::new(current_exe())
          .args(["--exact", name, "--nocapture", "--test-threads=1"])
          .env(SUB_CHILD, name).env("SSL_CERT_FILE", &roots.0) ... .spawn());
      let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
      loop { if let Some(status) = child.0.try_wait() {
                 assert!(status.success(), "machine subscription TLS case failed"); return; }
             assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "machine subscription process bound expired");
             thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)); }
  }

  TLS FIXTURE ON DISK -- CLEARED. `ROOT` is a compile-time byte-string literal written to
      a fresh temp file at run time, so it survives a tree sync that never transfers *.pem.
      This is the correct form of that fix, already applied.
  CERT EXPIRY -- CLEARED. notAfter is 2049-12-31.
  SELF-SELECTION -- CLEARED. The child re-enters the same fn, matches SUB_CHILD against
      its own name (:25), and runs the case rather than re-spawning. No fork bomb, and the
      `--exact` guarantees the child runs exactly the named test.

The 30s wait at :41 is a bucket (e) BOUNDED WAIT -- the assert IS the loop's exit
condition. It must not be removed. It is also 15x the e2e_protocol bound that measurably
failed under load and 33-75x the 400-900ms client probes, so load is an UNLIKELY
explanation here, though not an impossible one.

=== WHAT THE TEST ACTUALLY ASSERTS ===

  :319  fixture responds  "HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect\r\n
                           Location: https://127.0.0.1:9/forbidden\r\nContent-Length: 0"
  :330  assert!(matches!(error,
            TaskError::Protocol(ManagedTasksError::HttpStatus { status: 307 })))

So: the client must NOT follow the redirect, and must surface the 307 as a typed protocol
error. That is a deterministic assertion with no timing component. The redirect target is
port 9 (discard), so if the client DID follow it the connection would fail rather than
succeed -- which would surface as some OTHER error, not as HttpStatus{307}.

=== THE DISCRIMINATOR — one line of panic text decides it ===

The harness emits exactly two distinct messages, and they partition the causes cleanly:

  "machine subscription TLS case failed"
        -> the CHILD process failed. The :330 matches! did not hold, i.e. the client
           produced something other than HttpStatus{307}. That is (a) a real defect in
           redirect handling, or (b) the error type/shape moved and the test is stale.
           The child's own panic text, which --nocapture forwards to the parent's stderr,
           names which -- a `matches!` failure prints the observed value.

  "machine subscription process bound expired"
        -> the 30s watchdog. Load, or a genuine hang in the listen path.

I DO NOT HOLD EITHER STRING and will not guess between them to complete a tidy 3-of-3.
Whoever has the batch log has the answer already; --nocapture means the child's diagnostic
is in it verbatim.

=== TWO OBSERVATIONS, NEITHER A DEFECT, BOTH WORTH RECORDING ===

DUPLICATED FIXTURE. The identical `ROOT` constant appears in FIVE test files --
oauth_client_credentials.rs:47, oauth_interaction.rs:39, oauth_managed.rs:24,
oauth_core_rpc.rs:44, oauth_discovery.rs:30 -- byte-identical. `RootFile` is duplicated
alongside it in at least two. Not a defect today; it is the shape where a fix lands in one
copy and four keep the bug, which this campaign has already paid for once.

POSSIBLE CROSS-REFERENCE, flagged rather than claimed: this is a redirect-INTERCEPTION
assertion, and FND-05/bd-ho7of item 2 concerns a redirect-interception seam. I have NOT
established they are the same seam -- this is client-side OAuth task subscriptions, that is
transport -- and they may be unrelated. Worth one read by whoever owns FND-05 before it is
assumed either way.

No status change. Claims nothing, closes nothing.

                            rejected -- bd-jsm7z resolved them, bd-460kj is 3-of-3 RESOLVED"
     OBSERVED. http_auth::discovery::client_credentials::tasks::tests::
                   both_extensions_are_explicit_and_other_profiles_cannot_be_smuggled_in ... ok
               http_auth::managed::tasks::tests::
                   explicit_tasks_selection_is_advertised_on_discovery_without_other_extensions ... ok
  test 3 passes          -> "05b0e4bf confirmed BEHAVIOURALLY, not just on the 401/307 control"
     OBSERVED. tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed ... ok
  either 1 or 2 fails    -> would have meant the lossy-TYPE diagnosis was wrong. Did not occur.
  test 3 fails Transport -> would have meant the carrier does not reach the caller and the From
                            routing is wrong. Did not occur.

ZERO FAILED rows and ZERO `panicked` occurrences in the entire log.

== A COUNT THAT NEEDED RECONCILING BEFORE I CREDITED ANYTHING ==
The card predicted 3 passed. The run totals 4. I did not credit it until that resolved:
  lib target                      2 passed; 869 filtered out   <- tests 1 and 2
  oauth_client_credentials        1 passed;  64 filtered out   <- test 3, PARENT
  oauth_client_credentials child  1 passed;  64 filtered out   <- test 3, --exact re-entry
  17 other targets                0 passed; N filtered out     <- filter matched nothing
`listen_redirect_is_not_followed` appears TWICE because that target spawns a child which
re-enters the binary with --exact. 4 = 3 predicted + 1 nested re-run. The prediction holds on

ALSO WORTH NAMING: one summary reads `0 passed; 0 failed; 7 filtered out` and exit=0. In
isolation that is the PL-1 zero-run shape -- a green over nothing. It is not one here: 17
targets legitimately matched no filtered name, and the three that did are accounted for above.
A filtered multi-target run will always produce mostly-zero summaries, and reading any single
one as the result is the trap. The denominator is every summary, not the last one printed.

== LIVENESS ==
Compiling fastmcp-protocol, fastmcp-transport, fastmcp-client;
Finished `test` profile in 4m 42s. A real build.

bd-460kj is 3-OF-3 RESOLVED, not merely diagnosed. Three distinct mechanisms, all now fixed:

comments.text:
SUBMITTING FOR REVIEW. All three resolved, and they were never one defect -- that is the part
worth carrying into the closure.

=== THREE TESTS, THREE DISTINCT MECHANISMS ===

  1  both_extensions_are_explicit_and_other_profiles_cannot_be_smuggled_in
  2  explicit_tasks_selection_is_advertised_on_discovery_without_other_extensions
        A LOSSY TYPE. `ClientCapabilities` had no `extensions` field and no
        deny_unknown_fields, so serde silently dropped the planted extension on the typed
        round-trip. The callee saw nothing to reject, returned Ok, and each test's
        `is_err()` assertion failed. Planted negatives that COULD NOT FIRE.
        Fixed by 9ba90837 (bd-jsm7z), which added the two schema-declared fields.
        Not my commit; my contribution was the diagnosis and the schema check that
        established which side was non-conformant.

  3  tasks::subscriptions::listen_redirect_is_not_followed
        A LOSSY BOUNDARY. `ModernHttpExecutorError::Redirect { status }` was discarded by
        `.map_err(|_| ClientCredentialsError::Transport)` before `require_success` could
        map the 307 to HttpStatus. Fixed by 05b0e4bf, which carries the status across the
        boundary and routes it to Protocol(HttpStatus) in the existing From impl.

"Three tests failed, three tests fixed" would hide that these share nothing but a feature
gate. One was a type that could not represent the data; one was a boundary that threw the
data away. Different defects, different fixes, different commits, different owners.

=== EVIDENCE ===

Run by WildMountain, unfiltered by target and filtered by name, real compile 4m42s:
  tests 1 and 2   lib target            PASS
  test 3          oauth_client_credentials  PASS (twice -- the harness spawns a child that
                  re-enters the binary via --exact, so 4 passes for 3 tests)
  zero FAILED, zero panicked, anywhere in the log.

The card deliberately omitted `--lib`: tests 1-2 are lib-target and test 3 lives in the
oauth_client_credentials integration target, so a `--lib` run would have covered two of three
SILENTLY and returned a clean green.

A prediction table was submitted BEFORE the run naming what each individual failure would
mean, so the result could falsify the diagnosis rather than merely agree with it. Neither
failure row occurred.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===

  - I did not fix tests 1 and 2. 9ba90837 did. I diagnosed the mechanism, established from
    the vendored schema which side was non-conformant, and verified the premise at 5dc37f8e
    before submitting the card.
  - This receipt covers the three named tests under `--features native-tls-roots,tasks`. It
    says nothing about the crate's other surfaces or other feature sets.
  - A stale citation to be aware of: tasks.rs:277 has ROTTED to :292-297. Anything quoting
    the old number is pre-5dc37f8e.

title: RCH fleet is 96.3% full (265 GB free of 7174 GB) and no rch command reclaims it: full disks make the source-authority registry unwritable, so leases cannot finalize and every dispatch voids (OPERATOR ACTION)
description:
THE RCH FLEET IS 96.3% FULL AND THAT IS WHY EVERY VERIFICATION DISPATCH FOR
THIS PROJECT VOIDS. Measured 2026-10-19. Operator action: the remedy runs on
the workers, and no lane has SSH credentials for them.

CORRECTION TO THE FIRST REVISION OF THIS BEAD. I originally filed this as
"13 of 15 durable leases stuck in finalize ... retrying adds leases" and named
`rch jobs recover` as the remedy. That had the causality BACKWARDS and the
remedy would not have worked. Both claims are retracted below, with the
evidence that corrected them. The lease table is a symptom surface; I read it
instead of `rch status`, which names the cause outright in its own Remediation
section. I had that output available the whole time and did not read it.

THE CAUSE, from `rch workers capabilities --refresh --json` (live probe,
read-only, costs no build slot):

    worker        disk_free   disk_total   pct_free
    vmi1167313        0.6 GB     192.7 GB      0.3%
    hz3               1.1 GB     906.0 GB      0.1%
    vmi1156319        4.4 GB     386.4 GB      1.1%
    hz2              12.8 GB     600.6 GB      2.1%
    hz1              13.0 GB     225.0 GB      5.8%
    vmi1293453       13.1 GB     386.4 GB      3.4%
    vmi1149989       13.4 GB     773.9 GB      1.7%
    vmi1152480       13.5 GB     773.9 GB      1.7%
    vmi1227854       13.5 GB     773.9 GB      1.7%
    hz4              36.4 GB     906.0 GB      4.0%
    vmi1153651       46.9 GB     773.9 GB      6.1%
    wsurf            95.8 GB     475.6 GB     20.1%  (UNREACHABLE)

    FLEET TOTAL: 265 GB free of 7,174 GB = 3.7% free.

`rch status` reports posture `degraded`, 8 of 12 workers pressure-blocked, and
1 of 9 slots free. The only worker with meaningful space (wsurf, 20.1%) is the
one that fails its health probe, so the fleet's spare capacity is unreachable.

THE MECHANISM, which is causal rather than correlative. RCH's source-authority
registry lives at `/tmp/rch-source-authority-locks/claims-v1`. A lease in
`finalize` must WRITE that registry to release its source claim. On a full disk
the write fails, and `rch status` prints exactly that for two workers:

    Worker 'vmi1227854' is offline: RCH_SOURCE_REGISTRY_UNWRITABLE: exit=74,
      stderr=sh: line 54: printf: write error: No space left on device
    Worker 'hz2' is offline: RCH_SOURCE_REGISTRY_UNWRITABLE: exit=74,
      stderr=sh: 54: printf: printf: I/O error

So the finalize phase cannot complete, the lease never reaches
`terminal_acknowledged`, and self-healing -- enabled on all 15 -- retries the
same unwritable registry and fails the same way. The orphaned leases are a
CONSEQUENCE of the full disks. This also disposes of the remedy I first filed:
`rch jobs recover` has to write the same registry on the same full disk.

This single fact accounts for all four void markers seen today, which I had
been treating as four separate problems:
  - `no admissible workers` (admissibility vectors 7/3/1/1 and 5/5/1/1):
    pressure-blocked workers are inadmissible, and 8 of 12 are pressure-blocked.
  - `worker source namespace initialization refused on hz4 (status Some(73)):
    Killed` -- hz4 cannot mktemp under
    /tmp/rch-source-authority-locks/claims-v1.
  - `... refused on vmi1153651 (status Some(75)): RCH: durable source
    ownership: unfinished overlapping physical source owner` -- an unreleased
    claim that cannot be cleared because clearing it is a registry write.
  - SSH timeout at 20s and a SIGKILL at exit=137 on a 30-minute build, both
    consistent with saturated boxes.

RETRACTED: "RETRYING ADDS LEASES." I claimed each voided dispatch left another
unacknowledged lease, from watching the count go 12 -> 14 -> 15 across my own
attempts. That is not established. The fleet is shared and `rch queue` shows
another project (`eidetic_engine_cli-aaced065`) executing concurrently, so the
growth is equally explained by peer dispatches. The count has since held at 15
while I made no attempts AND two leases reached `terminal_acknowledged`, which
also shows the acknowledgment path is not itself broken -- these 15 are
orphans, not a broken mechanism. I inferred causation from correlation on a
shared resource; the lease table carries no project field
(`lease.identity` has only `local_wrapper_id` and `remote_build_id`), so it
cannot support lane attribution either way.

MY OWN CONTRIBUTION, named rather than hidden. My
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` run was SIGKILLed at
30.2 minutes. That is the largest target directory this workspace can produce
-- every crate, every feature -- and it died without cleanup, so it plausibly
contributed disk rather than merely one orphaned lease. This repository has
done this before: a prior incident recorded a verification target dir filling
a shared worker disk, and a previously-filed client lib-test "red" turned out
to be hz disk pressure rather than a code defect.

THE REMEDY IS **NOT** `rch gc` EITHER, AND THIS IS THE SECOND CORRECTION. My
first guess at a remedy was `rch jobs recover` (wrong: it writes the same
unwritable registry). My second was `rch gc --apply`, since RCH ships it as the
sanctioned reclaim path -- "Collect stale rch runtime dirs on workers. PREVIEWS
BY DEFAULT", "Nothing is removed or released without `--apply`". I ran the
PREVIEW, and it refutes that remedy outright:

    rch gc -n --workers hz3 --workers vmi1167313 --workers hz4 \
           --workers vmi1153651 --worker-timeout 100 --json

    hz3          complete   7 dirs   96,034 MB total   would_free 0 MB
    vmi1167313   complete   0 dirs        0 MB total   would_free 0 MB
    hz4          TIMED OUT  enumerate phase: "/data/projects (worker deadline
                            100s): Timeout, server 194.163.156.231 not
                            responding"
    vmi1153651   TIMED OUT  enumerate phase: "worker deadline expired while
                            SSH command was in flight"

So `rch gc --apply` would free ZERO BYTES on both of the worst-filled workers.

On hz3 (1.1 GB free of 906 GB) every one of the 7 dirs is verdict `keep`, and
the reason is never contention -- `open_handles: free` and `live_process: free`
on all 7. They are retained purely by the idle-age policy:

    /data/projects/franken_manim_rc1017/.rch-target      39,413 MB  41m idle
    /data/tmp/rch-cargo-cache-hz3                        30,401 MB  10m idle
    /data/tmp/rch/midas_edge_api/.rch-target-...          9,694 MB  31m idle
    /data/tmp/rch/clone-pi-v080/.rch-target-...           9,529 MB  50m idle
    /data/projects/franken_manim_land1019/.rch-target     9,393 MB  56m idle
    (+2 dirs at 4 KB)
    reason: too_young: idle 0h < required 168h   (cargo_cache: < 336h)

Two things follow. First, rch's whole footprint on hz3 is 96 GB, so roughly
809 GB of the 905 GB consumed is NOT rch's and no rch command can reclaim it.
Second, on vmi1167313 rch's footprint is literally `dirs: []` -- zero -- while
the disk sits at 0.3% free, which proves the fill is non-rch content on at
least one worker. `gc_claims` is `{claims: []}` on both, so the stale
`fc-*.claim` fence I hypothesised as a second cause does not exist here.

THIS FLEET IS OVERSUBSCRIBED, NOT UNTIDY. That is the actual finding, and it
changes the remedy class from "run a cleanup command" to one of:
  (a) restore `wsurf` -- 95.8 GB free, 20.1%, the fleet's only real spare
      capacity, currently failing its health probe. Cheapest win available.
  (b) tighten the retention windows, which are what is holding the 96 GB on
      hz3: `idle_hours` / `pooled_idle_hours` (168h) and
      `cargo_cache_idle_days` (336h) are generous for a fleet at 3.7% free.
      This is a config decision with a real cost -- those dirs are ~30-56
      minutes idle, i.e. actively-built live projects, so evicting them trades
      disk for other projects' rebuild time.
  (c) add capacity, or investigate the non-rch consumer directly. On
      vmi1167313 that is the ONLY option, since rch owns none of it.
None of (a)-(c) is a lane's call.

A CAUTION FOR WHOEVER CLEANS UP. `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/`
appears in hz3's inventory. Its `.rch-target` is 4 KB and irrelevant to the
disk problem, but AGENTS.md makes coding-agent-search data sacred on EVERY
machine, so a broad `rm` under `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search`
would be unrecoverable. Target dirs only, never the project tree.

I RAN THE PREVIEW ONLY, and did not run `--apply`. Clearing other lanes'
build trees on shared infrastructure is not a single lane's call -- it is the
same cascade the agent-mail restart prohibition exists to prevent -- and
RULE 1 forbids me to delete anything without written permission. I also have
no SSH credentials for the workers (`ubuntu@194.140.197.98` returns
`Permission denied (publickey)`), so even the read-only `df`/`du` that
`rch status` prescribes is not available to a lane. The decision and the
command both belong to the operator.

ONE MEASUREMENT I COULD NOT GET. hz4 and vmi1153651 -- the two workers that
actually refused my dispatches -- both timed out in the `enumerate` phase at a
100s worker deadline, so I have NO footprint measurement for either. That
enumeration of `/data/projects` cannot finish in 100s is itself a signal about
how much is on those boxes. Re-run with a larger `--worker-timeout` to get it.

CONSUMER AND COST. Named consumer: every lane that needs a compile receipt,
and the batch-verification orchestrator in particular. Observed cost today:
the base64 DPoP fixture fix at 90f4ccb2 is committed and UNVERIFIED; bd-hy8mq's
coverage measurement could not be repeated; bd-l7s5f's remaining E0597 pair
cannot be iterated on at all without a compiler. Fleet-wide, `rch status`
reports a 48% build success rate and a 44% test-command success rate across
9,888 stored test records, which is what a chronically full fleet looks like
rather than a today-only outage.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. `rch workers capabilities --refresh --json` reports no worker under its
     critical disk threshold, and `rch status` posture is no longer `degraded`
     for storage reasons. Record the before/after free-space table; the before
     column is in this description.
  2. A trivial dispatch succeeds for THIS project's path hash --
     `cargo check --locked -p fastmcp-core --lib` reaching a `Finished` line
     AND a `Remote command finished: exit=0` -- since a green for another
     project does not prove this project's namespace is usable. (Both signals
     are required: the wrapper exit masks the remote exit.)
  3. `rch jobs --json` reports zero leases with `owner_presence=absent` and
     `wrapper_alive=False`, or every remaining one `terminal_acknowledged`.
     This is the SYMPTOM check and must be evaluated AFTER 1, not instead of
     it: if leases clear once disks are reclaimed, that confirms the mechanism
     above; if they persist on a healthy disk, the mechanism is wrong and this
     bead needs a third revision.
  4. The non-rch consumer on vmi1167313 is identified. This is the item that
     cannot be skipped: rch owns 0 bytes there and the disk is 0.3% free, so
     no amount of rch-side reclamation touches it. (Stale `fc-*.claim`
     reservations are already ruled OUT -- measured `claims: []` on both hz3
     and vmi1167313 -- so that line of inquiry is closed, not pending.)
  5. wsurf is either restored (it holds the fleet's only real spare capacity)
     or explicitly written off, so selection stops counting it as a worker.
  6. A standing control is recorded so the next occurrence is not rediagnosed
     from the lease table: the first instrument for a dispatch void is
     `rch status` Remediation plus `rch workers capabilities --refresh`, not
     `rch jobs`.

NO-CLAIM. The disk table, the registry errors, the queue contents, the hz3/
vmi1167313 dir inventories and the `rch gc` contract are measured or quoted.
I did NOT run `rch gc --apply`, any recovery command, or any command on a
worker, and I did not inspect worker filesystems directly.

Specifically NOT established:
  - What consumes the ~809 GB on hz3 or the 192 GB on vmi1167313 that rch does
    not own. I know only that rch does not own it.
  - Any footprint figure for hz4 or vmi1153651; both enumerations timed out.
  - How much consumed space belongs to THIS project. On hz3 fastmcp_rust has
    no target dir at all, so my SIGKILLed `--all-features` build is stated as
    a plausible contribution on the workers it actually ran on, not as a
    measured cause anywhere.
  - Whether reclaiming disk alone clears the 13 orphaned leases. That is a
    PREDICTION of the mechanism above, not an observation; acceptance item 3
    is written so that it can falsify the mechanism rather than confirm it.

This bead has now been corrected twice -- first cause (leases -> disk), then
remedy (`rch gc` -> no rch command helps the worst two workers). Each
correction came from running one more read-only instrument, not from
re-arguing the same evidence. The standing lesson is in acceptance item 6: for
a dispatch void, read `rch status` Remediation and
`rch workers capabilities --refresh` FIRST. The lease table shows what broke;
those two show why.

title: Modern-only unsplit pump dispatches subscriptions/listen inline, so the pump can never receive its cancel (hang)
description:
Modern-only build (legacy-2024-11-05 off): run_transport[_returning]_with_cx uses run_loop_pump_with_policy(.., PumpIoMode::Unsplit).
In that mode every modern request is dispatched INLINE on the pump ("if io_mode == PumpIoMode::Unsplit { poll_on_cx(dispatch_cx, dispatch(..)); continue; }", lib.rs ~16565).
A subscriptions/listen does not return until it is terminated. So the pump stops calling recv, cannot receive the client's notifications/cancelled or EOF, and the listen (and connection) hang.
The legacy loop dispatches SUBSCRIPTIONS_LISTEN to a caller blocking-pool worker instead. Since bd-8bcfq, its ack/notifications are queued while recv owns the unsplit handle and flushed when recv returns, so the no-legacy path can do the same for listen.
Not reachable from lib unit tests: cfg(test) forces the legacy loop. It needs a tests/ integration test built with --no-default-features that sends discovery + listen + cancel over an unsplit Transport and expects the listen to complete.
Found by ProudValley while fixing bd-8bcfq/bd-81cct (static read; not run).
close_reason: Verified by run:v-4crkf at commit:a987e969. evidence: cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --no-default-features --test srv_65_modern_multi_request (unfiltered): 15 passed/0 failed/0 ignored/0 filtered, incl. srv_65_unsplit_listen_reads_its_cancellation_and_keeps_serving and srv_65_unsplit_listen_ignores_an_unrelated_cancellation_until_eof. Dirty files at sync were client-only, not compiled by this target. Fix commit:a987e969.

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
ProudValley. Cause: the modern-only unsplit pump (PumpIoMode::Unsplit) ran every request inline. A listen never returns until terminated, so the pump stopped reading and never saw the cancel or EOF.
Fix (a987e969): an unsplit listen goes to the blocking dispatch pool. Ordinary requests stay inline. The pump then waits, bounded by UNSPLIT_LISTEN_OPEN_TIMEOUT (5s), until the listen has written its ack or finished, because an unsplit transport cannot write during recv.
Tests (srv_65, cfg(not(feature = "legacy-2024-11-05"))): srv_65_unsplit_listen_reads_its_cancellation_and_keeps_serving (cancel 40: listen retired, no response) and srv_65_unsplit_listen_ignores_an_unrelated_cancellation_until_eof (cancel 999: one graceful completion at EOF). Both assert the ack was seen before the next read, tools/list 41 was answered, and run is Ok.
Command: cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --no-default-features --test srv_65_modern_multi_request -- srv_65_unsplit_listen_
Unchecked: rch exit 103.

title: RETRACTED BY AUTHOR (false premise): claimed no test observes a server-emitted notifications/tasks frame; three e2e tests do and all passed in my own run
description:
MEASURED 2026-10-11. No test target in this workspace observes a
notifications/tasks frame that the SHIPPED SERVER produced. The task-status
notification is written and stored by code that tests do exercise out of crate;
the hand-off from that stored notification to a subscriber is exercised by
nothing.

THIS IS A PROOF-COVERAGE CLAIM, NOT A DEFECT CLAIM. I read the publish path
and it looks complete and correct. I am not asserting the server fails to
deliver. I am asserting that if it did fail, no test in this repository would
go red. Stated this way deliberately: I filed bd-dj5am against this same
subsystem on a static read of cfg gating, it was false, and I retracted it.
This bead claims only what a validated search over the test corpus shows.

WHAT IS COVERED (so this bead does not overstate the hole). Both out of crate,
against public items, so PL-3 is satisfied for these rows:
  crates/fastmcp-server/tests/srv_01_stateless.rs
    store.latest_notification(&task_id) asserted at :1534, :1649, :1687,
    :1872, :1903, :2034 -- six call sites. The notification is persisted and
    readable through the shipped store surface.
  crates/fastmcp-server/tests/task_02_b.rs
    builds TaskStatusNotification and drives replace_task_if_current with it
    (:228, :625, :1013, :1023, :1040), proving the persist-with-notification
    contract the FinalTaskStore trait documents as atomic.

WHAT IS COVERED BY NOTHING: the publish / transport leg.
  publish_task, publish_owned_task and final_subscription_event_sender appear
  in crates/fastmcp-server/src/{lib,builder}.rs and crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs,
  and in crates/fastmcp/tests/trybuild_pass/facade_dual_era_consumer.rs:292 --
  which is a trybuild COMPILE fixture, so it proves the type is nameable, not
  that a frame is ever emitted. No other test file references any of the three.

THE DENOMINATOR, which is what makes this worth filing. The project's flagship
end-to-end target crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_modern_http.rs is where server and
client actually meet over real HTTP. It asserts on NINE distinct notification
families:
    notifications/progress              38 occurrences
    notifications/resources/updated      8
    notifications/tools/list_changed     6
    notifications/cancelled              6
    notifications/roots/list_changed     2
    notifications/resources/list_changed 2
    notifications/prompts/list_changed   2
    notifications/message                1
    notifications/initialized            1
    notifications/tasks                  ZERO
e2e_protocol.rs and e2e_workflow.rs are also zero, as is task_02_b.rs. So the
one notification family belonging to the capability this campaign exists to
implement is the single family the end-to-end suite does not cover.

EVERY OBSERVED FRAME IS A HAND-WRITTEN FIXTURE (RH-12 shape). The four places
a notifications/tasks frame appears in any test are all client-side literals:
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_task_watch.rs:250
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_task_watch/checkpoint/persistence.rs:98
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials/subscriptions.rs:94
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials/advertisement.rs:781
each of the form json!({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/tasks",...}).
oauth_task_watch_drive.rs says so itself in its own header: "The issuer and MCP
peer are fixtures". The client's CONSUMPTION of these frames is well proved --
bd-poz5k records oauth_task_watch 46/0 and oauth_task_watch_drive 26/0 at
commit f91e5999. The producer is the untested side, and a hand-written fixture
cannot detect a producer that stops producing, or that emits a method name the
client does not admit.

INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, because a zero from a grep is worthless unqualified.
The same search finds notifications/tasks in the four client fixtures above
and finds TASK_STATUS_NOTIFICATION at eight sites in fastmcp-client/src
(execution.rs :2602 :3436 :3446 :5173, lib.rs :265 :1326 :5975). A file that
contains these strings reads non-zero on this instrument, so the zeros in the
facade e2e targets are real zeros and not a mistyped needle.

A SECOND, SEPARABLE OBSERVATION. srv_01_stateless.rs carries no
required-features in crates/fastmcp-server/Cargo.toml, but its task rows sit
behind #[cfg(feature = "tasks")] (:1342, :1348, :1358, :1540). A default
"cargo test -p fastmcp-server" therefore compiles the file and silently skips
exactly those rows, reporting green. The six latest_notification assertions
above only exist in a run that passes --features tasks. Measured today:
fastmcp-server --lib is 2365 tests at default features and 2723 with
--features tasks at the identical manifest ff63ae8a448be06a, so the feature

title: Facade re-export closure gap (FIXED in this change): DpopSession was reachable through fastmcp-rust while DpopKey and DpopError were not, so the documented DPoP flow could not be constructed by a facade user
description:
`fastmcp_client::http_auth::dpop` was REACHABLE but not CONSTRUCTIBLE from the
published root. A `fastmcp-rust` user could name `DpopSession` and had no way to
name either the key its constructor requires or the error its API returns.

THE CLOSURE GAP, measured 2026-10-14 at HEAD 6f632bf5.

  DEMANDED BY THE PUBLIC API
    `DpopSession::new(key: DpopKey, token_endpoint: CanonicalHttpUrl,
                      resource: CanonicalHttpUrl)`     dpop.rs:187
    `DpopClientError::Proof(DpopError)`                 dpop.rs:32
    Both `DpopKey` (fastmcp-protocol/src/dpop.rs:140) and `DpopError` (:36) are
    public in fastmcp-protocol.

  REACHABLE FROM THE FACADE BEFORE THE FIX
    `DpopSession`         yes -- `pub use fastmcp_client::http_auth;`
                          at crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:935, and
                          `pub mod dpop;` at http_auth.rs:35
    `CanonicalHttpUrl`    yes -- `pub use fastmcp_core::CanonicalHttpUrl;`
                          at http_auth.rs:54
    `DpopKey`             NO
    `DpopError`           NO

  WHY NOT. `fastmcp_protocol::dpop` is `#[cfg(feature = "jose")]`
  (fastmcp-protocol/src/lib.rs:43) and the facade does not forward it. The
  facade forwards `common_types`, `http_headers`, `methods` and
  `protocol_policy` (crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:558) plus `jose` itself only
  under `builtin-auth-server` (:547). A case-insensitive search of the whole
  facade lib.rs for "dpop" returns ZERO hits, and no `pub use` of `DpopKey`
  exists anywhere in fastmcp-client either.

THE TELL THAT THIS WAS AN OVERSIGHT RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE: http_auth.rs
already re-exports the OTHER argument type of the same constructor
(`pub use fastmcp_core::CanonicalHttpUrl;` at :54). The pattern was established
for one of `DpopSession::new`'s two argument types and not completed for the
other.

THE FIX, in this bead's own change. `crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/
dpop.rs` turns the private import of these two names into a documented
`pub use`, splitting the still-private `DpopNonce` and `MAX_DPOP_TARGET_BYTES`
into their own line because no public signature here names them:

    pub use fastmcp_protocol::dpop::{DpopError, DpopKey};
    use fastmcp_protocol::dpop::{DpopNonce, MAX_DPOP_TARGET_BYTES};

IT ADDS NO DEPENDENCY, which is the part worth checking before anyone worries
about FND-01's frozen dependency evidence. `jose` is ALREADY enabled for every
non-wasm target by fastmcp-client's own target-specific table:

    [target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
    fastmcp-protocol = { workspace = true, features = ["jose"] }
                                        crates/fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml:47-48

That is the SAME cfg predicate that gates `pub mod dpop;` in http_auth.rs, so
the module and its dependency's feature appear and disappear together --
correct engineering, and the reason `ring` and `zeroize` are already in
Cargo.lock (0.17.14 and 1.9.0) and already named in
evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml (8 and 11 lines respectively,
including `ring` in `verifier_dependency_order`). Nothing about the dependency
graph changes.

A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING, because it would have been a false P0. Reading
only `[dependencies]` in fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml, `jose` appears to be
enabled solely by `builtin-auth-server`, while `pub mod dpop;` is gated only on
`cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` and `dpop.rs` imports
`fastmcp_protocol::dpop::` unconditionally. That reads as a shipped unresolved
import on the default graph -- the exact defect class as bd-yjpe0, which was a
real P0 earlier today. I had a narrow `cargo check` dispatched before I found
the target-specific table and cancelled it. **A crate's feature enablement can
live in `[target.'cfg(..)'.dependencies]`, and a scan of `[dependencies]`
misses it entirely.**

ACCEPTANCE
  1. `fastmcp-client --lib` compiles with the re-export (the change is a
     visibility widening of names already imported and used internally, so the
     risk is rustdoc intra-doc links rather than type resolution).
  2. The two names are reachable as
     `fastmcp_rust::http_auth::dpop::{DpopKey, DpopError}`. The honest proof is
     a compile from outside the workspace; a within-workspace resolution does
     NOT establish it, which is precisely the failure mode
     [[a-facade-can-withhold-the-types-its-own-api-demands]] records.
  3. `DpopNonce` and `MAX_DPOP_TARGET_BYTES` remain private.

NO-CLAIM
  - This makes the documented flow NAMEABLE. It does not establish that the
    flow WORKS: no test drives `DpopSession` end to end, and this bead adds
    none.
  - Acceptance item 2's proper proof is an out-of-workspace compile, which I
    have not performed. Everything I verified resolves inside the workspace,
    and that is the weaker claim.
  - The README section documenting this flow was added separately today; this
    bead is what makes its first step possible rather than merely legible.

comments.text:
VERIFICATION STATUS, CORRECTED: THE COMPILE HAS NEVER RUN, and one of my two
attempts reported a green that was not one.

ATTEMPT 1, through a retry loop: `RC=0 checking_lines=0`. I distrusted it on
sight and was right to. Zero `Checking fastmcp-client` lines after editing
`dpop.rs` is impossible for a real compile -- the edit changes the fingerprint
and forces a recompile -- so RC=0 there is a wrapper exit masking a void, not a
result. The loop's display filter for cargo's own `Finished ... profile` line
also matched nothing, which is the corroborating tell.

ATTEMPT 2, capturing complete output instead of a filtered view:
    wrapper_rc=103
    24 lines of output, 0 `Checking` lines, 0 `error`, 0 `warning`,
    no `Finished`
103 is the RCH void code. So both attempts are voids and neither is evidence
about this change.

That is the fourth time this session a `0 Checking lines` result has had to be
refused as false-clean, and the reason I quote the Checking count in every
receipt rather than the exit code.

=========================================================================
WHAT IS VERIFIED, WHICH IS EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE COMPILE ITSELF
=========================================================================

  NO NAME COLLISION. `dpop.rs` defines no local `DpopError` or `DpopKey`
  (no `struct`/`enum`/`type` of either name), so the re-export introduces
  nothing ambiguous at the module level.

  THE GLOB RISK IS CLOSED. Making these two names part of `dpop`'s public
  surface means `use super::*` in `native.rs`'s test modules (:561, :1190) now
  also pulls them. Those same modules already import `DpopKey` EXPLICITLY from
  `fastmcp_protocol::dpop` (:559, :1188). An explicit import shadows a glob in
  Rust, so this resolves rather than conflicting -- and this was the one failure
  mode that a `pub use` of an already-imported name could plausibly introduce.

  DOC LINKS RESOLVE. The new doc comment links `[`DpopSession::new`]` and
  `[`DpopClientError::Proof`]`; both types are declared in the same file, and
  `[`DpopKey`]`/`[`DpopError`]` resolve to the re-exported items.

  UPSTREAM VISIBILITY. `pub enum DpopError` (fastmcp-protocol/src/dpop.rs:36)
  and `pub struct DpopKey` (:140) -- so no private-in-public.

  FORMATTING. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` is clean on the file; the final
  line ordering was arrived at by hand rather than by running the formatter on
  a file under surgical edit.

  THE PUB CHAIN, link by link: facade `pub use fastmcp_client::http_auth;`
  (crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:935) is UNGATED -- the
  `#[cfg(feature = "legacy-2024-11-05")]` immediately above it applies to the
  preceding item, which I checked specifically because that is an easy
  misread -- then `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))] pub mod dpop;`
  (http_auth.rs:35), then the new ungated `pub use` (dpop.rs:36).

=========================================================================
WHAT REMAINS AND WHO SHOULD DO IT
=========================================================================

SUBMITTING to review + batch-pending rather than chasing the build. A narrow
`cargo check --locked -p fastmcp-client --lib` is exactly what the
batch-verification lane exists to run, the fleet is refusing it for me right
now, and the alternative -- fetching into a worktree on hz3 that another lane
may own -- risks more than the remaining uncertainty is worth.

FOR THE VERIFIER, the two things to look for:
  1. A real `Checking fastmcp-client` line. A green without one does not
     discharge this.
  2. Acceptance item 2 remains the stronger bar and is NOT satisfied by that
     check: facade reachability is properly proven by compiling a crate OUTSIDE
     this workspace against `fastmcp-rust` and naming
     `fastmcp_rust::http_auth::dpop::{DpopKey, DpopError}`. Within-workspace
     resolution does not establish it, which is the whole failure mode this
     defect is an instance of.

NO-CLAIM: I am claiming a reasoned, statically-checked change with its
remaining risk named, not a verified one. If the compile fails, the likely
cause is something in the five static checks above that I reasoned about and
got wrong, and the failure is mine.

=== THE CLASS IS SUBSTANTIALLY ONE IDIOM, NOT 64 DESIGN QUESTIONS ===
The two largest SHIPPED sites (resource/watch.rs:166, catalog/watch.rs:180) are byte-identical
source:
    active(cx, deadline, owner, cancellation, None, async {
That call shape occurs 29 times across fastmcp-client/src, ALL SHIPPED, ZERO in test code, against
TWO helpers with the same defective signature:
    client_credentials.rs:726  async fn active<T>(..., future: impl Future<...>)   26 call sites
    challenge.rs:384           async fn active<T>(..., future: impl Future<...>)    3 call sites
BOUND: 29 is the IDIOM's population, not the LINT's. Only 2 of the 29 are confirmed emitters (from
the top-eight magnitude list). The other 27 are candidates with unmeasured emission status. Do not
read 29 as a large_futures site count.
COLLISION WARNING: this 29 is NOT the result_large_err 29 in the bead body above. Different lint,
different question, same integer, same hour.

=== THE REMEDY IS AT THE CALL SITE. I TESTED THE CHEAPER ONE AND IT FAILS ===
active takes the caller's future BY VALUE (impl Future), so the caller's whole state machine is
embedded in active's own. Measured with clippy::large_futures at its 16384-byte default, one
40 KB caller future, four shapes:
    A  impl Future + pin!(future)   inside helper     80,024 bytes   FIRES  <- today's code
    B  impl Future + Box::pin(...)  inside helper     40,024 bytes   FIRES  <- REFUTED
    C  impl Future + Box::pin AT THE CALL SITE            silent     PASSES
    D  helper takes Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>           silent     PASSES
Shape B was my hypothesis and it is refuted: the future is moved into the helper's frame as an
argument BEFORE Box::pin can move it to the heap. Interior boxing removes one copy of two - it
halves the size and does not clear the threshold. The boxing must happen before the value crosses
the call boundary, which is per-call-site.
So: 29 MECHANICAL, IDENTICAL edits at two signatures. Not one fix, and not 29 judgements either.

=== C vs D IS THE ACTUAL DECISION ===
Same 29 call-site edits either way. Difference is site 30:
  C  helper unchanged; nothing prevents a new caller passing an unboxed future. Class regrows.
  D  Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>> in the signature; the type system enforces it permanently.
CAVEAT ON D, stated because it is a real cost: dyn erases auto-traits, so the + Send is load-
bearing - ClientCredentialsResponse::read_to_end is pub async fn and its future's Send-ness is
published surface. D also adds a vtable indirection per poll.
Neither C nor D is an #[allow], so RH-1 is not engaged by either.

=== WHY "ALLOW IT" IS THE WEAKEST OPTION HERE ===
The crate has already RULED on this in writing at watch.rs:310 - box the independently large HTTP
state machines rather than multiplying their stack footprint (credit SilentSquirrel). An allow
would contradict the crate's own recorded position, and the distribution (median 3.5x, max 30x
threshold) is not a lint arguing with its boundary.

=== PRODUCTION/TEST SPLIT: USE MULTIPLICITY, NOT A PATH HEURISTIC ===
Under --all-targets a shipped site emits in BOTH the lib and lib-test units; a #[cfg(test)] site
emits in one. Verified differentially: lib unit 1 emission, lib-test unit 2, over 2 distinct
locations. So the existing run's multiplicity already encodes the split (credit MagentaOsprey, who
derived the same from target records). This also explains the 1.7 ratio in the bead body.
DO NOT use a "first #[cfg(test)] line" cut to derive it. I tried; it reported a 67% test-side share
for this package and the true figure is 51%. Cause: #[cfg(test)] also annotates single uses, and
one at lib.rs:216 of a 43,091-line file mis-binned 828 awaits. 42 of 45 files matched the assumed
shape, which is exactly why the heuristic looked validated.

The bead's current state says this class "needs a child-note extraction before anyone rules." That

THREE FACTS THAT EACH BREAK AN OBVIOUS EXTRACTOR:

     signature) and its label is None. Any extractor filtering `where is_primary` — which is the

     A regex keyed on either word silently drops the other half of the population.

    the largest variant contains at least (\d+) bytes
and attribute the size to the record's PRIMARY span location. Credit SilentSquirrel, who published
this form correctly; I am confirming it against a dump rather than restating it.

MEASURED: `-D warnings` AND FULL COVERAGE ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WHILE ANY LINT REMAINS. This
governs every lint census on this bead and explains the entire run history.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===
Same source, same lint groups, one flag different, via clippy-driver at zero slots:
    -W clippy::all -W clippy::pedantic                exit=0   .rmeta produced: 1
    -W clippy::all -W clippy::pedantic  -D warnings   exit=1   .rmeta produced: 0
A unit that emits ANY lint under `-D warnings` produces NO ARTIFACT. Under `--keep-going` cargo
continues INDEPENDENT units, but everything DOWNSTREAM of that unit cannot be built, and therefore
cannot be linted.

=== IT EXPLAINS SIX CONSECUTIVE TRUNCATIONS ===
    559, 570, 615, 616, 618 units   ALL carried -D warnings -> fastmcp-client emitted -> truncated
    700 units                       flag ABSENT -> nothing failed -> full coverage
Under --all-features, fastmcp-server depends on fastmcp-client through proxy = ["dep:fastmcp-client"].
fastmcp-client emits ~224 diagnostics, so under -D warnings its units fail and fastmcp-server is
never reached. THAT is why every flagged listing ever produced on this bead contains ZERO
fastmcp-server sites, including the 116-site listing.
The truncation was never mysterious and it was never about `--keep-going` semantics being unclear.
It is the gate flag doing exactly what it is designed to do.

=== CONSEQUENCE: fastmcp-server's LINT SURFACE HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED ===
The flagged runs truncated before reaching it. The unflagged 700-unit run did not count lints (its
counter kept only level == "error", and without -D warnings lints are warnings). Neither instrument
has ever looked at that package. Every "98% of the surface is fastmcp-client" statement is a
statement about the only package that was ever measured.

=== THE DESIGN THAT GETS BOTH ===
    CENSUS  clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --keep-going --message-format=json
            NO -D warnings. Counter accepts level == "warning" AND level == "error".
            -> full 700-unit coverage AND a complete lint count.
    GATE    clippy ... -- -D warnings
            -> a pass/fail signal, meaningful only once the census reads zero.
THE DEFECT WAS THE COUNTER, NOT THE MISSING FLAG. `if level != "error": continue` is correct for a
compile-error census and wrong for a lint census. Fixing the counter fixes the measurement; adding
the flag fixes the exit code and destroys the coverage. A census flag and a gate flag are different
instruments for different questions and this bead has been using one for both.

=== MY PRE-REGISTRATION (comment 3398) IS UNTESTED, NOT CONFIRMED ===
The falsifier's precondition was "the run reaches ~700 units AND measures lints". The 700-unit run
did not measure lints, so the precondition never held. The prediction stands unresolved and still
falsifiable: 8 named sites that must appear, 2 named that must not. A census run per the design
above tests it and validates the counter in the same pass, against a list fixed in advance.

public error type is product design and I will not make it under a lint bead — doing so would be

a diffuse cleanup. That reframing is the useful part.
