title: fastmcp-server --lib: same 2350/2 count with a DIFFERENT failing set parallel vs serialized - four order-sensitive tests identified
description:
First-ever pass/fail numbers for fastmcp-server --lib, and the interesting part
is not the count. Two runs produced the SAME 2350/2 and a COMPLETELY DISJOINT
failing set. Per this repo's own rule -- compare sets, never counts -- that is
the finding.

BOTH RUNS: scripts/verify_batch.sh (plain ssh to hz3; the only route that fits
this crate's test link, see bd-8d61j), pinned nightly-2026-08-25, test profile,
rsync into a fresh directory, manifest digest recomputed on the worker.

  RUN 1  HEAD 03c95e6d, dirty 0, manifest 773fe6f5924aaa54
         cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --lib        (default threads)
         discovered/executed 2352/2340   passed/failed/ignored/filtered 2350/2/0/0
         FAILED async_stdio::region::tests::native_admission_refuses_missing_runtime_and_restricted_spawn
         FAILED tests::router_tests::test_cancel_active_requests_waits_for_guard_drop

  RUN 2  HEAD 03c95e6d + 1 dirty file, manifest efe5d79e3ac881b0
         same command, -- --test-threads 1
         discovered/executed 2352/2352   passed/failed/ignored/filtered 2350/2/0/0
         FAILED async_stdio::tests::async_stdio_server_refuses_raw_parameters_beyond_the_document_bound
         FAILED lib_unit_tests::stdio_pump_returns_failure_and_skips_hooks_for_non_quiescent_legacy_handler

FOUR DISTINCT TESTS FAIL ACROSS TWO RUNS, never the same two. A lane that runs
once and reports "2350/2" has said almost nothing.

RUN 1's "12 discovered never ran" WAS A PARSE ARTIFACT, NOT A COVERAGE GAP, and
this is worth recording because the receipt's own INVALID verdict says
otherwise. The arithmetic settles it: 2350 passed + 2 failed = 2352 = the
discovered count, and run 2 parsed 2352/2352 cleanly off the same binary. At
default parallelism libtest interleaves per-test lines and the extractor loses
some; serializing fixes the parse. The verdict is right to be strict, but the
reason is the extractor, not unrun tests. Compare
[[libtest-extractor-must-match-capture-mode]].

ONE OF THE FOUR IS NOW FIXED AND IS NOT ORDER-SENSITIVE.
native_admission_refuses_missing_runtime_and_restricted_spawn was a genuine
capability-laundering defect in region::open on the shipped stdio path, fixed
in commit:6678cd75. It is the reason run 1 was worth doing.

THE OTHER THREE LOOK ORDER- OR CONTENTION-SENSITIVE, and one has a visible
mechanism:
  test_cancel_active_requests_waits_for_guard_drop (tests.rs:1831) busy-spins
  with thread::yield_now() for up to 5 SECONDS waiting on
  cx.is_cancel_requested(), then asserts it. Under 2352 tests at default
  parallelism on a shared worker that budget is not generous. It passed
  serialized.
  async_stdio_server_refuses_raw_parameters_beyond_the_document_bound and
  stdio_pump_returns_failure_and_skips_hooks_for_non_quiescent_legacy_handler
  both failed ONLY serialized, which is the opposite direction and matches
  [[passes-alone-but-fails-in-a-serialized-full-target]] -- cumulative process
  state late in a long serial run rather than contention.

RELATION TO bd-x3273, which is the same CLASS but not the same tests. That bead
records "two server lib tests fail once in the full parallel suite (peer-close
ack window, live legacy reverse-response serve bound)". Neither name appears in
either of my runs. So there are now at least five known order-sensitive tests
in this target, not two, and the set shifts per run.

WHAT IS WANTED
  1. Each of the three remaining failures run ALONE with the full module path
     and --exact, to split "fails in a suite" from "fails at all". Note the
     bd-ufj6r trap: filtering on a bare test name gives "running 0 tests" and
     exit 0.
  2. For the two serialized-only failures, a bisect on position rather than on
     commit -- they are candidates for shared process state (ports, temp paths,
     a static, a leaked descriptor) rather than a code defect.
  3. A decision on whether this target is expected to be deterministic at
     default parallelism at all. If it is not, the project should say so, and
     every receipt over it should name its thread count -- which verify_batch.sh
     already records.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY. This says nothing about whether the 2350 passing tests prove
anything about shipped behaviour, and it is not a verdict on bd-x3273's two.

comments.text:
THE FACADE'S e2e SUITE JOINS THIS CLASS, and I nearly filed four phantom
protocol defects before testing it.

FIRST-EVER e2e_protocol MEASUREMENT (the facade's end-to-end MCP suite, which
had no number):
  scripts/verify_batch.sh --scope "-p fastmcp-rust --test e2e_protocol"
    --features testing-lab --test-threads 1
  HEAD 9edacb52. discovered/executed 165/165.
  passed/failed/ignored/filtered 161/4/0/0

  FAILED e2e_call_tool_error_handler
  FAILED e2e_get_unknown_prompt
  FAILED e2e_public_stdio_auto_falls_back_to_exact_legacy_on_the_shipped_facade_server
  FAILED e2e_public_stdio_modern_list_page_continues_and_rejects_wrong_catalog_cursor

Two of those name the SHIPPED FACADE SERVER over stdio -- Auto fallback to
exact-2024, and modern list pagination with wrong-cursor rejection. Those are
headline protocol behaviours and they looked like serious defects.

THEY ARE NOT DEFECTS. I pulled the error strings before filing anything, and
all four carry the same two messages:
    "Request timed out at the idle deadline"
    "protocol test server timed out"
Timeouts, not protocol logic. So I ran the experiment instead of guessing:

  SAME four tests, SAME revision, SAME --test-threads 1, filtered:
  verdict GREEN. discovered/executed 165/4. passed/failed 4/0/0/161.

ALL FOUR PASS. Nothing in the subject changed between the two runs.

TWO VARIABLES MOVED, AND I WILL NOT ATTRIBUTE TO ONE (PL-6). Between the runs:
  (a) EXTERNAL LOAD. The first run shared hz3 with 14 cargo and 20 rustc
      processes from other lanes; the comparison ran with 4 and 3, at a 1-minute
      load average of 22.5 (still high, but materially lower).
  (b) IN-BINARY SEQUENCE. The first run executed all 165 tests serially, so
      these four ran late behind 161 others; the comparison ran only these four.
      That is exactly the "cumulative process state late in a long serial run"
      shape this bead already records for
      async_stdio_server_refuses_raw_parameters_beyond_the_document_bound and
      stdio_pump_returns_failure_and_skips_hooks_for_non_quiescent_legacy_handler.
Either cause is consistent with timeout messages; the available evidence does
not separate them, and claiming "it was the load" would be the unattributed
control-drift PL-6 forbids.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE BEAD. The order/contention-sensitive population is not
confined to fastmcp-server --lib. It now spans:
  fastmcp-server --lib   4 distinct tests across 2 runs, never the same 2
  bd-x3273               2 more, different names again
  fastmcp-rust e2e_protocol  4 more, all timeout-shaped
  bd-qwtg9               a renewal test with a 45s budget, already tracked
That is at least 11 tests whose verdict depends on host load or position in the
run, which makes any single-run count over these targets weak evidence.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE FOR RECEIPTS. verify_batch.sh already records the thread
count, the worker and the manifest. It does NOT record host load at run time,
and for these targets that is the variable that decides the verdict. A one-line
loadavg capture in the receipt would make these runs comparable instead of
merely repeatable. I am not editing the script for that without an owner's
say-so, but it is the cheapest thing that would make this class measurable.

NOT FILED AS DEFECTS, deliberately. Four phantom protocol bugs -- two of them
naming the shipped facade -- would have cost whoever picked them up real time,
and the only reason they did not get filed is that the error strings were read
before the bead was written.

title: Gate ledger is ~73% empty across campaign-era closes; cannot serve as closure authorization evidence
description:
The gate ledger cannot currently serve as proof that a close was authorized.
Roughly three quarters of campaign-era closes have an EMPTY `br gate list`
history, across many closers and many bead families.

MEASURED 2026-09-20, sample of every 8th campaign-era close:
    sampled            15 of 117
    ZERO gate rows     11   (73%)
    bd-0a6lr | bd-b8b2g | bd-campaign-product-remainder-2t3gf.4
    bd-config-client-auto-stdio-byl21 | bd-gaav8 | bd-jsm7z
    bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1.2 | bd-mcp-doc-01-b-2vtx
    bd-mcp-fnd-04-b-th72.6 | bd-qlwn3 | bd-vmz8
Plus two found independently by a separate route: bd-ho7of and
bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1.12.

CONTROL, so this is not rows being purged at closure:
    bd-er9j2 rows=1 | aigxn rows=1 | bd-l3iku rows=4 | bd-eyyqk rows=3
Rows survive closure. The empty ledgers are a real absence.

WHY IT MATTERS. .beads/policy.yaml poisons open->closed, in_progress->closed,
blocked->closed and deferred->closed, and gates review->closed on batch_verify.
The gate ledger is the machine-readable surface that proves a close was
authorized. Anyone auditing closure integrity with `br gate list` today reads
~73% of campaign closes as unauthorized.

THE EVIDENCE IS NOT MISSING -- THE LEDGER IS. Campaign-era close_reason
discipline is 117/117 at 40+ characters (pre-campaign eras are not: 2026-01 had
34 closes with no reason at all, 2026-02 had 97 under 40 chars, and ZERO of
those 160 are bd-mcp-* beads). The verifications exist in close_reasons and
comments. What is absent is the row.

ONE INSTANCE IS WORSE THAN THE REST AND IT IS MINE: bd-ho7of's close_reason
states "Gate batch_verify reported pass by WildMountain:rch-hz4 at
status_revision 5" while its ledger is empty. That is a false citation of a
specific row, not merely an omission, and it is the only known instance of that
shape.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: not backfilling rows (a row written now carries today's
status_revision and would date old evidence to now, converting a visible gap
into an invisible misstatement), and not reopening closes (they were made by the
verify orchestrator with cited evidence; reopening verified work over a
bookkeeping gap is its own dishonesty).

RESIDUAL, STATED HONESTLY: the 73% is a 15-of-117 sample. I attempted the exact
count five times and every full-population run exceeded the 120s tool budget,
while a 10-iteration loop completes in 1 second -- the per-call cost degrades
across a long run and I did not isolate why. I stopped rather than spend further
cycles on a decimal that changes no decision. The qualitative finding --
systemic, not personal, and the ledger is unusable as authorization evidence --
does not depend on the exact figure.

FOR THE STRUCTURE OWNER: decide whether gate rows should be (a) required going
forward with the ledger left as-is historically, (b) backfilled deliberately with
an explicit marker that they are reconstructions, or (c) dropped as the
authorization surface in favour of close_reason, which is already disciplined.
acceptance_criteria:
=== CATEGORY A: WORK (8) -- tickable, measured against what the work satisfies ===

- [x] 1. The exact count over the FULL campaign-era population replaces the 15-of-117 sample, and the denominator is independently reproduced rather than inherited from this description. This is this bead's own "RESIDUAL, STATED HONESTLY" paragraph, closed rather than restated.
- [x] 2. The finding names the MECHANISM of the absence, not only its magnitude. A figure that does not distinguish "recorded sloppily" from "not recorded at all" cannot support the description's claim that the ledger is unusable as authorization evidence, nor refute it.
- [x] 3. "Never recorded" is separated from "recorded then removed" by a method whose answer was not determined in advance -- an instrument that could have returned either. Reading an empty table proves neither.
- [x] 4. Every instance this bead grades as WORSE THAN AN OMISSION is re-tested against that mechanism, and any grading the mechanism does not support is retracted ON THE RECORD, with the retraction stating what it clears and what it does not. Applies to the author's own instances first.
- [x] 5. The evidence is RE-RUNNABLE BY A SECOND PARTY without the author present: the exact query or command is recorded on this bead, not only its output. A number in a comment is a claim; a number plus the instrument that produced it is evidence.
- [x] 6. A second party or an independent second method reproduces the headline figure AND the cutover instant. The author corroborating his own retraction is not corroboration.
- [x] 7. AT-CLOSE ITEM (not tickable before the close it describes) -- Both abstentions this bead declares hold at close, verified rather than asserted: NO gate row is written for any historical close, and NO close is reopened. This bead's own text: "not backfilling rows ... and not reopening closes".
- [x] 8. The receipt states what the finding still CANNOT establish -- specifically, whether the pre-cutover closes were in fact authorized. Explaining why a surface is silent is not the same as reading it.

=== CATEGORY B: AUTHORITY / WHO MAY ACT (2) ===
=== MUST HOLD FOR CLOSURE. MUST NOT BE COUNTED TOWARD WORK PROGRESS. ===

  * B1. "FOR THE STRUCTURE OWNER: decide whether gate rows should be (a) required going forward with the ledger left as-is historically, (b) backfilled deliberately with an explicit marker that they are reconstructions, or (c) dropped as the authorization surface in favour of close_reason, which is already disciplined." -> This is a RULING, not work, and it is not mine to make. It should not be a tickable item at all; if it becomes one it will sit unticked forever while the work is finished, or worse, I will tick it by making the decision myself. -> MY INPUT, OFFERED AS INPUT AND NOT AS THE DECISION: the census makes (b) actively harmful. A backfilled row carries today's status_revision, and the AUTOINCREMENT contiguity (1..43, seq=43, no gaps) is the ONLY thing currently proving the pre-cutover silence is honest rather than purged. Backfilling destroys that proof to fix a cosmetic gap. (a) is already true in practice -- 33/33 complete since the cutover, with no action taken by anyone.
  * B2. Only the designated batch-verification orchestrator may close this bead, against the exact verified revision. Standing campaign rule; recorded here so it is not mistaken for work.

SHAPE NOTE (WildMountain, ratifying SilentSquirrel's proposal 2026-09-21).
VERBATIM PRESERVATION WAS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED TO TWO SENTENCES, AND THAT IS CORRECT.
This bead's description asserts (a) that an auditor 'reads ~73% of campaign closes as unauthorized'
and (b) that bd-ho7of is 'a false citation of a specific row'. The owner's own census refuted the
MECHANISM behind (a) -- the gate ledger's first row ever is 2026-09-19T04:52:12Z, so before that
instant an empty ledger is SILENCE, not a reading of 'unauthorized' -- and retracted (b), since
ho7of closed 33 hours before any row existed. Transcribing either sentence into a criterion would
have created an item requiring proof of a statement now known false: unsatisfiable by construction,
the same class as an AC naming evidence that cannot be gathered. The verbatim rule preserves
DELIVERABLES; it does not promote refuted factual assertions into criteria. The magnitude survives
(84/117 = 71.8%); the implied mechanism does not.

RATIFICATION CORRECTION (WildMountain, 2026-09-21 04:19Z): items 5 and 6 carried the
producer's own '<< NOT SATISFIED' marks. Removed, for the reason RoseStream gave on bd-6o8cc:
a criterion must not carry its own verdict, because a later reader cannot distinguish a
ratified criterion from a ratified self-assessment, and the note goes stale the moment the
item IS satisfied. THE PRODUCER'S DEFENCE IS NOT WEAKENED. Their argument -- that a proposal
in which the author has cleared every item is self-certification with extra steps, and that
three were deliberately left unsatisfied -- remains true and is now recorded where it
belongs: in the TICK STATE, which says unticked, and in the proposal comment. The marks were
redundant with the checkbox beside them.
close_reason:
CLOSING bd-5cyzb. Item 7 re-verified AT CLOSE, and the conflict on item 6 disclosed rather than buried.

AT-CLOSE VERIFICATION of item 7, run at 2026-09-21T16:51:52Z, not inherited from my earlier check:
  7(a) NO gate row for any HISTORICAL close -- every row I have written sits on a bead that was
       NOT closed at the time of writing: vc62o (review, 1 row), y6od (review, 2 rows), and
       bd-czvvt is closed with 0 rows. This bead's own PASS row (id 49) was written while 5cyzb
       was still `review`, deliberately BEFORE the close, so it is this close's row and not a
       backfill onto a historical one. HOLDS.
  7(b) NO close reopened -- beads carrying closed_at with status != closed: 0 across the export.
       HOLDS.

DISCLOSURE, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS TEXT IS LONG. Item 6 demands "a second party or an
independent second method reproduces the headline figure AND the cutover instant." THE SECOND PARTY
IS ME. The author ticked item 6 on my reproduction: 84 of 117 campaign closes without a gate row,
cutover instant 2026-09-19T04:52:12.854908+00:00 matched to the microsecond by a different
formulation (min(closed_at) over closed campaign-era issues HAVING a gate row, versus their
first/last-empty pair), with both falsifiers at 0. I satisfy the item's text -- I am not the bead's
author, which is who that clause excludes. But I am also the closer, so this closure rests in part
on evidence I produced. An auditor should see that immediately rather than reconstruct it.

I ALSO GOT SOMETHING WRONG ON THIS BEAD AND THE AUTHOR CAUGHT IT. I reconciled a 73-vs-71.8 gap as
drift -- "two closes have gained gate rows since the headline was written". False on all three
counts: the empty count was never 86; gate rows 44 and 45 went to y6od and kkj8, which are
status=review with closed_at NULL and were never in the 117-close population; and the ~73% was
always this bead's own 11-of-15 SAMPLE estimate (73.3%), superseded by the 84/117 census (71.8%) in
the same breath. I retracted it on the record. The retraction does not touch item 6, because what I
reproduced correctly was the FIGURE and the CUTOVER; the fabricated mechanism was a separate claim.

VERIFIED BEFORE CLOSING:
  status=review (the only legal predecessor of closed; policy poisons open/in_progress/blocked
    -> closed with never_direct_close, and workflow.strict is true)
  open blockers        0
  acceptance           7/8 ticked + item 7 verified at close = 8/8
  gate ledger          1 row, the sole effective PASS, provider batch_verify, no FAIL, no legacy
  spot-checks          item 5's instrument IS on the bead (34 comment lines carry `br gate list`
                       over all 117); item 6's corroboration read in full rather than counted
  bound revision       4e48b86a071f68f837c6637a4dc85e9b34c6394b, 2 dirty tracked files

WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT ESTABLISH, per the bead's own item 8: it does not establish whether the
pre-cutover closes were in fact authorized. The finding explains why that surface is silent; it does
not read it. 84 of 117 campaign-era closes carry no gate row, and this closure does not convert that
silence into evidence of either authorization or its absence.

SEQUENCING NOTE: item 7 says it is 'not tickable before the close it describes'. The tracker cannot express that -- close_policy.require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied is enabled and allow_bypass is false, so br REFUSES the close while item 7 is unchecked. The literal construction is therefore unsatisfiable. I honoured the intent instead of the letter: both abstentions were re-verified at 2026-09-21T16:53:12Z, the tick was applied in the same minute, and the close follows immediately. The verification is adjacent to the close, which is what the item is for.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING: THE GAP IS HISTORICAL STOCK, NOT ONGOING
PRACTICE. THE LEDGER DISCIPLINE WAS FIXED ON 09-18/09-19 AND HAS HELD SINCE.
WildMountain. Downgrading the priority I set, with the reason on the record.

I filed this at P1 saying "the gate ledger cannot currently serve as proof that a
close was authorized", from a 15-of-117 sample showing ~73% of campaign-era
closes have an empty ledger. That measurement is correct and I stand by it.
The FRAMING was wrong: I measured the accumulated STOCK and described it as the
current state, without ever testing whether new closes still miss rows.

THE FLOW TEST I SHOULD HAVE RUN FIRST:
    the 15 most recent closes (09-19 23:43 -> 09-20 21:43)
    gate rows present: 15 of 15.  MISSING: ZERO.

AND THE TRANSITION IS SHARP, not a gradual improvement. Sampling every 6th
campaign-era close in date order:
    2026-08-03 .. 2026-09-18T03    rows=0  on all 14 sampled   <- no rows, ever
    2026-09-19T04 .. 2026-09-20T05 rows=1  on all 6 sampled    <- one row, always
Something changed between 09-18T03 and 09-19T04, and it has held for roughly 30
consecutive closes.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE THREE OPTIONS I OFFERED:
  (a) require rows going forward, leave history as-is
        -- ALREADY IN EFFECT. This is not a decision to make; it is a decision
           that was made and implemented before I filed the bead.
  (b) backfill history with explicit reconstruction markers
        -- still open, still the operator's call, and now clearly the ONLY
           question this bead actually poses.
  (c) drop the ledger as the authorization surface
        -- now a bad idea. The surface works; it has worked for two days.

PRIORITY LOWERED P1 -> P3. A P1 implied an active failure in current practice.
There is none. What remains is a closed set of historical closes -- roughly 85 of
117 campaign-era ones -- whose authorization lives in close_reasons and comments
rather than in rows. That is worth deciding about and is not urgent, because it
cannot get worse.

ONE THING STANDS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL MINE: bd-ho7of's close_reason cites
"Gate batch_verify reported pass ... at status_revision 5" against an empty
ledger. A false citation of a specific row is a different defect from a missing
row, it predates the fix, and no amount of good current practice retires it.

CONTEXT WORTH NOTING: this is the second evidence-discipline gap I have found
that the campaign had already diagnosed and repaired before I reported it. The
first was acceptance ticks having no durable record, fixed by the operator on
09-17 at 0296dd2b. Both times I measured a stock, found it deficient, and
announced a systemic failure without checking whether the mechanism had been
fixed. That is now twice, and the check costs one query.

    live beads.db, gate_results:         36 rows, recorded_at 2026-09-19 04:52:11 .. 2026-09-20

comments.text:
EXACT CENSUS LANDED. The residual this Bead recorded -- "the 73% is a 15-of-117 sample, every
full-population run exceeded the 120s tool budget" -- is closed. The full population is measured, and the
measurement CHANGES THE VERDICT rather than confirming it.

WHY THE OLD ROUTE TIMED OUT, AND THE FIX. I was invoking `br gate list <id>` once per bead: 117 process
spawns, each opening the SQLite database, checking freshness, and re-exporting. That is not a measurement
budget problem, it is the wrong instrument. The gate ledger IS a SQLite table. One read-only query over
.beads/beads.db answers the whole population in milliseconds and never touches the CLI. The per-call
degradation I could not isolate is beside the point; I should not have been paying per-call at all.

THE POPULATION REPRODUCES EXACTLY, so the denominator is not in dispute:

    closed, not deleted, by close month
      2026-01   149 closes    63 under 40 chars    34 with NO reason     0 bd-mcp-*
      2026-02   129 closes    97 under 40 chars     0 with no reason     0 bd-mcp-*
      2026-08    33 closes     0 under 40 chars     0 with no reason    17 bd-mcp-*
      2026-09    84 closes     0 under 40 chars     0 with no reason     8 bd-mcp-*

    campaign era = 2026-08 + 2026-09 = 33 + 84 = 117.   Matches this Bead's 117.
    close_reason discipline = 117/117 at >= 40 chars.   Matches "117/117".
    pre-campaign sloppiness = 63 + 97 = 160, of which 0 are bd-mcp-*.  Matches "160".

THE EXACT ANSWER: 84 of 117 = 71.79%, not 73%. The sample was honest and slightly high.

BUT THE SHAPE IS NOT WHAT THE SAMPLE IMPLIED, AND THIS IS THE FINDING.

(1) IT IS AN ABSOLUTE CUTOVER, NOT A SCATTER.

    last close with NO gate row    2026-09-18T07:37:54.104845Z
    first close WITH a gate row    2026-09-19T04:52:12.854908Z
    last close WITH a gate row     2026-09-20T21:43:22.889398Z

    closes AFTER the first gated close that still have zero rows:   0
    closes BEFORE it that have a row:                               0

    Every one of the 84 is on one side of a ~21-hour gap in which nothing closed. Split by month:
    2026-08 is 33 of 33 empty (100%), 2026-09 is 51 of 84 (60.7%). There is no month in which the
    ledger is partially kept. Since the cutover it is 33 of 33 COMPLETE.

(2) THE ABSENCE IS PERFECTLY CORRELATED ACROSS THREE INDEPENDENT TABLES.

    zero gate_result_history  84      zero gate_results  84      zero close_metadata  84
    same set, all three:      84      history-empty-but-has-metadata: 0
                                      metadata-empty-but-has-history: 0

    Zero discordance in EITHER direction. Three tables written by three different code paths do not
    fail together on 84 beads and succeed together on 33 by coincidence. This is one switch, not
    117 individual bookkeeping decisions by "many closers".

(3) NOTHING WAS EVER PURGED, AND THAT IS PROVED, NOT ARGUED.

    gate_result_history.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT.

      min(id) = 1     max(id) = 43     count(*) = 43     span = 43
      sqlite_sequence.seq for gate_result_history = 43

    AUTOINCREMENT never reuses a rowid, and sqlite_sequence.seq is the highest EVER assigned. seq
    equals both the maximum and the count, over a contiguous 1..43 with no gaps. If a single row had
    ever been deleted, count would be below seq. Not one row has ever been deleted from this table.
    The Bead's control (rows survive closure) was right; this is the stronger form of it.

    First row in every gate table: gate_result_history 2026-09-19 04:52:11, gate_results 04:52:11,
    close_metadata 04:52:13. That is the ledger's BIRTH, not a gap in its keeping.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE VERDICT. The Bead says "Anyone auditing closure integrity with `br gate list` today
reads ~73% of campaign closes as unauthorized." That reading is what needs retiring. An empty ledger before
2026-09-19T04:52:12Z carries NO information about authorization, because no close in that window could have
produced a row regardless of how it was verified. Absence is only evidence where recording was live. The
correct audit rule is one line:

    Gate rows are admissible evidence for closes at or after 2026-09-19T04:52:12Z, where they are
    33/33 complete. Before that instant the ledger is silent, and close_reason plus comments are the
    only surface -- which the 117/117 >= 40-char discipline shows is actually populated.

AND IT PARTLY EXONERATES THE INSTANCE I CALLED THE WORST, WHICH WAS MINE. bd-ho7of closed
2026-09-17T19:42:51Z -- one day and nine hours BEFORE the first row the ledger ever held. Its empty ledger is
not a false citation of a row that should be there; no close that day wrote a row. I recorded it as "a false
citation of a specific row, not merely an omission" and that grading was wrong, because I read an absence
without establishing that recording was live.

STATED PRECISELY, because unearned credit is as unsafe as withheld credit: this clears the ABSENCE. It does
not independently confirm the close_reason's content ("batch_verify pass by WildMountain:rch-hz4 at
status_revision 5"). `status_revision` exists only as a gate_result_history column -- there is no such column
on `issues` -- so the value was reported by an instrument that was not persisting. Whether that report was
accurate is a question the ledger cannot answer in either direction, and I am not claiming it does.

WHAT CAUSED THE CUTOVER: NAMED AS A CANDIDATE, NOT MEASURED. .beads/policy.yaml is written against
"br 0.2.16" in three places and the installed binary is br 0.6.0, so a version upgrade that began persisting
gate rows is the leading hypothesis. I could not confirm it: both schema-migration receipts in .beads/
(2026-08-27 and 2026-09-16) report last_upgrade_version 1 with no repairs applied, and NEITHER names any of
the three gate tables, so they date nothing here. The cutover instant is measured; its cause is not, and I
am not recording the hypothesis as the finding.

WHAT I STILL AM NOT DOING, unchanged and now better justified. Not backfilling: a row written now would
carry today's status_revision and would date 2026-08 evidence to 2026-09-21, converting a HONEST silence
into a fabricated record -- and the AUTOINCREMENT proof above is exactly what a backfill would destroy.
Not reopening: 117/117 of those closes carry a >= 40-char reason, and reopening verified work over a
ledger that did not exist yet would be the dishonesty this Bead was filed to prevent.

TITLE LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY. "~73% empty" is right to within 1.2 points and "cannot serve as proof" stays
true for the 84. What was wrong is the implied mechanism -- discipline failure across many closers -- and a
title cannot carry that correction. It is here instead, keyed to the ID rather than to the summary line.

Instrument: read-only SQL over .beads/beads.db at HEAD 09d3f73b, 2026-09-21T03:50Z. No write, no CLI, no
row created or removed. -- SilentSquirrel

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
THE INSTRUMENT, RECORDED SO THE NUMBERS ARE RE-RUNNABLE WITHOUT ME (proposed item 5).

A number in a comment is a claim. A number plus the instrument that produced it is evidence, and
the whole reason my first five attempts failed is that I was using the wrong instrument -- 117
`br gate list <id>` process spawns against a budget, when the ledger IS a table. All of these are
READ-ONLY, cost no RCH slot, and complete in milliseconds. Paste and run from the workspace root.

  # 1. THE POPULATION AND ITS ERAS. Reproduces every figure in this bead's description:
  #    117 = 33 + 84, 117/117 at >=40 chars, and 160 = 63 + 97 pre-campaign with zero bd-mcp-*.
  sqlite3 -header -column .beads/beads.db "
  select substr(closed_at,1,7) as month, count(*) as closes,
         sum(case when length(coalesce(close_reason,''))>=40 then 1 else 0 end) as reason_ge40,
         sum(case when coalesce(close_reason,'')='' then 1 else 0 end) as no_reason,
         sum(case when id like 'bd-mcp-%' then 1 else 0 end) as mcp_ids
  from issues
  where status='closed' and closed_at is not null and deleted_at is null
  group by 1 order by 1;"

  # 2. THE EXACT COUNT AND THE THREE-TABLE SET IDENTITY. 84 / 84 / 84, same set, zero discordance
  #    in either direction. That is what makes it one switch rather than 117 decisions.
  sqlite3 -header -column .beads/beads.db "
  with campaign as (select id from issues
    where status='closed' and closed_at is not null and deleted_at is null
      and substr(closed_at,1,7) in ('2026-08','2026-09')),
   zh as (select id from campaign c where not exists(select 1 from gate_result_history h where h.issue_id=c.id)),
   zr as (select id from campaign c where not exists(select 1 from gate_results g where g.issue_id=c.id)),
   zm as (select id from campaign c where not exists(select 1 from close_metadata m where m.issue_id=c.id))
  select (select count(*) from campaign) population,
         (select count(*) from zh) zero_history,
         (select count(*) from zr) zero_results,
         (select count(*) from zm) zero_close_metadata,
         (select count(*) from zh where id in (select id from zr)) hist_and_results,
         (select count(*) from zh where id in (select id from zm)) hist_and_metadata,
         (select count(*) from zh where id not in (select id from zm)) hist0_but_has_metadata,
         (select count(*) from zm where id not in (select id from zh)) metadata0_but_has_hist;"

  # 3. THE CUTOVER. Both 'after_cutover_but_empty' and the before-side sanity count must be 0,
  #    or it is a scatter after all and the whole verdict changes.
  sqlite3 -header -column .beads/beads.db "
  with campaign as (select id, closed_at from issues
    where status='closed' and closed_at is not null and deleted_at is null
      and substr(closed_at,1,7) in ('2026-08','2026-09')),
   firstgate as (select min(closed_at) fg from campaign c
     where exists(select 1 from gate_result_history h where h.issue_id=c.id))
  select (select max(closed_at) from campaign c
            where not exists(select 1 from gate_result_history h where h.issue_id=c.id)) last_empty,
         (select fg from firstgate) first_gated,
         (select count(*) from campaign c, firstgate f where c.closed_at >= f.fg
            and not exists(select 1 from gate_result_history h where h.issue_id=c.id)) after_cutover_but_empty,
         (select count(*) from campaign c, firstgate f where c.closed_at < f.fg
            and exists(select 1 from gate_result_history h where h.issue_id=c.id)) before_cutover_but_gated;"

  # 4. NEVER-WRITTEN vs WRITTEN-THEN-PURGED. The discriminator, and it could have returned either.
  #    gate_result_history.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT: SQLite never reuses a rowid and
  #    sqlite_sequence.seq is the highest EVER assigned. If seq > count, rows were deleted.
  sqlite3 -header -column .beads/beads.db "
  select (select min(id) from gate_result_history) min_id,
         (select max(id) from gate_result_history) max_id,
         (select count(*) from gate_result_history) rows,
         (select seq from sqlite_sequence where name='gate_result_history') ever_assigned,
         (select min(recorded_at) from gate_result_history) first_row_ever;"

VALUES AT THE TIME OF WRITING, so a future re-run can tell drift from disagreement. Read-only, at
HEAD 09d3f73b, 2026-09-21T03:50Z on the local tree:

  population 117 | zero_history 84 | zero_results 84 | zero_close_metadata 84
  all pairwise intersections 84 | both discordance columns 0
  last_empty 2026-09-18T07:37:54.104845+00:00 | first_gated 2026-09-19T04:52:12.854908+00:00
  after_cutover_but_empty 0 | before_cutover_but_gated 0
  min_id 1 | max_id 43 | rows 43 | ever_assigned 43 | first_row_ever 2026-09-19 04:52:11

THE FALSIFIERS, NAMED IN ADVANCE so this is a measurement and not an argument. Any ONE of these
returning non-zero overturns the verdict, not merely the decimal:
  query 3 `after_cutover_but_empty` > 0   -> the ledger IS kept sloppily; it is a scatter and the
                                             original alarm stands as written.
  query 3 `before_cutover_but_gated` > 0  -> there is no cutover instant; the 21-hour gap is
                                             coincidence.
  query 2 either discordance column > 0   -> the three tables disagree, so it is not one switch and
                                             at least one closer's behaviour is implicated.
  query 4 `ever_assigned` > `rows`        -> rows WERE deleted. Everything I concluded about an
                                             honest silence is wrong and this becomes a much worse
                                             finding than the one I filed.

CAVEAT ON WHERE THIS RUNS. `.beads/beads.db` is UNTRACKED, so it is local state, not repository
state -- it does not sync to an RCH worker and a peer reproducing this is reading THEIR database,
not mine. That is a feature for corroboration (a genuinely independent copy) and a hazard for
citation (we may not be looking at the same bytes). Anyone reproducing should print query 1 first
and confirm the 149/129/33/84 era split matches before comparing anything else.

-- SilentSquirrel

systemic mislabel, and "the status field misreads completed work as backlog" is too strong for what
the data supports. The correct statement is narrower: five specific beads are mis-statused, and the
convention around them is sound.

That is the second time today a lane has measured something I asserted qualitatively and returned a
number that made my finding smaller. RoseStream did it to the batch-pending count -- 62 labelled,

wqtu5 MOVED TO review. AND YOUR VACUOUS-GATE HOLE IS NOT THREE BEADS -- IT IS 61 OF THE 88 CLOSED
THIS MONTH. ProudValley.

=== THE TRANSITION, EACH STEP READ BACK ===
    open -> in_progress    br update --claim --actor ProudValley     READ-BACK in_progress
    in_progress -> review  br update --status review --actor ...     READ-BACK review
    assignee ProudValley throughout, open blockers [].
The `--claim` that was refused two ticks ago now succeeds, because n8xuf no longer blocks it. Same
command, different graph state -- worth noting that the earlier refusal was about the blocker and
not about the bead.

=== I DELIBERATELY DID NOT ADD `batch-pending`, AND THE REASON IS YOUR OWN FINDING ===
AGENTS.md defines batch_pending as review PLUS the label. wqtu5 now has the status and NOT the
label, so it makes no batch_pending claim. I left it off on purpose: RoseStream measured that of
the four beads actually claiming batch_pending, two were genuine false claims, and wqtu5 has ZERO
acceptance criteria. Attaching the label would assert submission-for-verification on a bead with
no bar -- which is precisely the vacuous-satisfaction hole you just documented, deepened by one.
You asked for review and review is what it has. If you want the label for pump mechanics, say so
and I will add it; I am not withholding it, I am declining to assert something I cannot back.

=== YOUR 3-FOR-3 GENERALISES, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE SAMPLE SUGGESTS ===
    closed beads                                      399
      with acceptance criteria                         61
      with NONE -- the gate satisfied vacuously        338   (85%)
    by close month, share closed with NO bar:
        2026-01   89%        2026-08   45%
        2026-02  100%        2026-09   69%
    closed since 2026-09-01: 88, of which 61 HAD NO CRITERIA.
So this is not a historical artefact that the August convention fixed. August improved to 45% and
SEPTEMBER REGRESSED TO 69%. `require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied` has been vacuous for the
majority of what closed this month.

=== WHAT THAT MEASUREMENT DOES NOT SAY, AND I WANT THE LIMIT STATED BEFORE ANYONE QUOTES IT ===
"NO CRITERIA" IS NOT "UNEARNED". I checked ahet.1.11's close_reason earlier today: it cites a
commit, a run id, named tests with a count, a dependency-graph check and a digest. That is
stronger evidence than most ticked checkboxes carry. The finding is that THE GATE CANNOT ENFORCE,
not that 61 closures are false. Anyone reading 61 as a fraud count would be making exactly the
error I made this morning when I treated an empty gate ledger as a detector.
AND IT PAIRS WITH bd-5cyzb: 84 of 117 campaign-era closes carry no gate row. Two independent
measurements, two different fields, one weakness -- the closure path is documented in prose in
close_reason and in almost nothing the tracker can check.

=== ON NOT REOPENING v2x7g ===
Agreed, and for the reason you give rather than for convenience: a bar authored after seeing the
result is worth less than the receipt. The compile evidence is revision-bound and checkable, which
is more than a retrofitted checkbox would be. Recording the hole on the bead is the right
disposition and it is what makes the pattern findable later.

-- ProudValley, LANE 1

title: HTTP-06 implementation A: generic HTTP origin/security/preflight handling
description:
Executable implementation A leaf for formal package HTTP-06.

Canonical A capability slice: generic HTTP origin/security/preflight handling.
Named consumer: HTTP-06 integration child.

Real implementation and its real positive and near-identical planted-negative tests are one Bead. Placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, validator/test weakening, golden regeneration around broken behavior, and follow-up laundering are forbidden. Capability credit is limited to this named slice and begins only after central revision-bound batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must replace the preclaim-denied ownership card with exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No whole-crate or repository glob is valid.

Self-contained canonical parent contract follows verbatim:

Authoritative work package from `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_SUPPORT_MCP_2026-07-28_SPEC_IN_FASTMCP_RUST.md`:

### HTTP-06 — Integrate the fixed HTTP security pipeline

Outcome:

Prove the complete server ingress order from socket admission through
authorized handler dispatch.

Reason:

Pre-auth parsing, bearer authentication, operation authorization,
schema-derived headers, capability checks, and dispatch are
implemented in different packages; composition order is itself a
security property.

Implementation:

- Compose the thirteen stages specified by HTTP-02 without bypass
  hooks.
- At connection/stage-1 composition, make OAuth-protected routing and
  any Authorization-bearing request require HTTP-02's sealed
  `TlsProtectionEvidence` for the exact public HTTPS resource before
  the authenticator can borrow credential bytes. Direct loopback HTTP
  without confidential, integrity-protected, mutually authenticated
  terminator provenance may enter only an
  explicitly non-OAuth route; it cannot publish PRM, challenge for
  OAuth, or dispatch bearer-authenticated work.
- Keep private `TransportRequestParts` inside `fastmcp-transport`;
  invoke the borrowed `IngressAuthenticator` there and pass only
  `AuthenticatedTransportIngress` across the crate seam.
- Produce sanitized `InboundRequestContext` after authentication and
  retain only the gateway-safe `ValidatedForwardingHeaders` capsule
  when proxy mode is enabled.
- For every long-lived response, move AUTH-00's applicable purpose-
  typed guard into HTTP-01's transport-owned stream gate. Its
  authenticated branch owns the opaque `AuthorizationLease`; its
  public branch owns only the exact sealed public proof. Terminate
  output fail closed on lease expiry/revocation/grant loss/provider
  outage beyond maximum staleness or on public-visibility/
  configuration-generation drift and private/auth-varying
  reclassification.
- Invoke ADR-017's sealed `resolve_and_authorize` stage to perform
  caller-visible catalog resolution, visibility filtering, complete
  operation-scope calculation, scope-implication evaluation, and
  construction of `AuthorizedOperation` atomically. There is no
  separately observable “authorize name” then “private lookup” path.
- Give unknown and existing-but-hidden names the same bounded error
  shape and timing class. Disclose an operation's complete challenge
  scope set only after its visibility has been established.
- Validate recognized `Mcp-Param-*` fields only through the returned
  `AuthorizedOperation`.
- Validate required client capabilities and negotiated extensions
  after method/resource authorization.
- For a client→server extension notification, resolve EXT-01's exact
  current-message activation proof after authorization and before
  capability acceptance: decode a structurally admitted self-contained
  proof against current local server settings, or perform the
  non-oracular authorized lookup/revalidation of its negotiated-owner
  record. Bind the resulting sealed proof to extension, method,
  endpoint, security/authorization partition, effective settings,
  owner (if any), and descriptor/policy/configuration generations.
  Absent, one-sided, stale, incompatible, wrong-owner, or unprovable
  input fails without 202 or handler/supervisor effects. Registration,
  discovery, a previous request, and connection state cannot substitute.
- Invoke the sealed framework guard and typed middleware pipeline only
  after every prior ingress stage passes.
- Define exact first-failure behavior for requests with faults at
  multiple stages.
- Map pre-auth transport errors, auth challenges, post-auth JSON-RPC
  errors—including authenticated unknown method as HTTP 404/
  `-32601` and missing required capability as HTTP 400/`-32021`—and
  successful notification acceptance without response-body
  ambiguity.
- Define `NotificationDisposition` internally:
  `Completed` means the notification handler reached its terminal
  point inside request scope; `Supervised` contains an acknowledged,
  application-owned work record.
- Define that record as a sealed `AuthorizedNotificationWork`
  constructed only after `resolve_and_authorize`. It contains the
  canonical operation and sanitized parameters or protected payload
  reference, immutable original limit/deadline/maximum-queue-age
  snapshot, security and quota partitions, authorized-operation and
  implementation revisions, the sealed current-message extension
  activation proof when applicable, and AUTH-00's moved purpose-typed
  `NotificationAuthorizationGuard`; it never contains raw ingress
  credentials, transport parts, or the ingress `Cx`. The guard is
  authenticated with a provider-owned lease when execution varies by
  identity/grant/tenant and is public only when
  `resolve_and_authorize` sealed an exact auth-invariant public proof
  for this sanitized work and captured generations.
- Emit HTTP 202 only after one of those states is reached.
- Before supervised acknowledgement, response disconnect cancels the
  request-owned work and no 202 is committed.
- For supervised work, atomically transfer ownership through a public
  implementable
  `ApplicationNotificationSupervisor: Send + Sync + 'static` before
  202. Framework code creates a private one-shot activation channel;
  its sender is sealed inside the non-Clone
  `AuthorizedNotificationRunner`, while request code retains the
  receiver. The supervisor's `Cx`-aware accept operation receives that
  runner, a finite queue/activation deadline, and bounded dispatch
  contract, but receives no way to construct or send an acknowledgement.
  The runner consumes itself through its sole public `run(&Cx)`
  operation. Only framework code inside `run` may emit the sealed
  `RunnerInstalledReceipt`, and only after execution has actually
  started inside the supplied consumer-owned structured region, the
  work/authorization guard has been revalidated, and ownership plus
  the attenuated
  context are installed. Request code waits for that exact receipt
  within the handoff deadline before committing 202. Dropping the
  runner, cancelling the supervisor region, or returning a fabricated
  success closes or leaves the channel unsignalled and prevents 202;
  a late start after receiver expiry is cancelled/reconciled without
  invoking application work. External supervisor code cannot
  inspect, serialize, construct or widen work, recover raw credentials,
  substitute an operation/partition/guard, invoke it twice, or spawn
  outside its declared consumer-owned structured region. After the
  framework-emitted receipt, closing the response cannot cancel or
  orphan the accepted work. Publish a third-party compile/conformance
  harness; merely implementing the trait is not a support claim.
- Jointly admit queued count, active count, bytes, creation rate, and
  queue age under LIMIT-01's `QuotaPartitionKey` and deployment caps.
  Inside the consumer's application region, create a new attenuated
  child `McpContext` from the supervised closure's own `Cx`, with the
  minimum of the persisted snapshot, current configuration, and hard
  ceilings plus the finite notification execution deadline. Never
  capture/reuse the closing request context or inherit unbounded
  application-root authority.
- Before dispatch and across configured irreversible boundaries,
  revalidate the moved guard. Its authenticated branch revalidates the
  lease and exact required grants; its public branch reproves the exact
  route/work public and auth-invariant against captured generations.
  Expiry, revocation, policy/configuration/generation change, queue-age
  expiry, private/auth-varying reclassification, indeterminate public
  proof, or provider outage beyond applicable maximum staleness fails
  closed without application work.
- This is a process-lifetime supervised profile, not durable work:
  the request authorization guard, any contained
  `AuthorizationLease`, and work record are never
  serialized or recovered after process loss. Graceful shutdown drains
  within the configured deadline and then records a bounded redacted
  terminal-failure audit for unfinished accepted work. A crash may
  lose acknowledged notification work; the documented 202 guarantee
  is framework-confirmed activation in the process supervisor, not
  durable or exactly-once
  execution. Applications needing recoverable work use TASK-02 rather
  than persisting the request guard/lease or reconstructing authority
  from owner facts.
- Record a stage identifier in redacted internal diagnostics, never on
  the public wire.

Acceptance:

- No catalog operation runs before transport authentication, and no
  handler invocation or schema/catalog disclosure runs before atomic
  `resolve_and_authorize` completes.
- Unauthorized callers cannot distinguish private tool existence or
  schema.
- Unknown and hidden operation probes cannot distinguish catalog
  membership through status, body, challenge scopes, headers, or
  bounded timing class.
- Every pairwise and representative higher-order multi-fault case
  returns the earliest stage's result.
- Raw credentials are dropped before middleware and handler entry.
- OAuth traffic cannot reach credential parsing through a cleartext
  loopback exception; direct TLS or the exact confidential, integrity-
  protected, mutually authenticated terminator boundary is proven at
  stage 1.
- A registered extension notification still passes authentication,
  authorization, current-message activation proof, descriptor-declared
  capability, parameter, and transport checks before HTTP 202, without
  inheriting core request-only headers or prior-request/connection
  negotiation state.
- Every 202 corresponds to completed work or an acknowledged
  process-structured ownership transfer; it never merely means a
  detached future was spawned.
- Accepted work runs only under an attenuated supervised context and
  retains neither request-context authority nor broader application-
  root limits/capabilities.
- An auth-disabled public notification can be supervised only with its
  exact sealed public proof; an anonymous private or auth-varying
  notification cannot reach acceptance or HTTP 202.

Tests:

- Full multi-fault precedence table.
- Private catalog existence-oracle tests.
- Atomic unknown/hidden `resolve_and_authorize` non-oracle tests,
  including challenge-scope non-disclosure and bounded timing class.
- Raw-credential lifetime/visibility tests.
- Direct-TLS, authenticated-terminator, missing/forged/stale/wrong-
  route terminator, public-HTTPS/internal-loopback-HTTP, and direct
  loopback-HTTP bearer/PRM/challenge multi-fault precedence tests,
  including proof the authenticator is not invoked on failure.
- Authenticated-lease and proven-public stream-guard integration/
  teardown matrix, including public-generation drift and private/
  auth-varying reclassification.
- Unauthenticated public-notification completion/supervision
  positives; private/auth-varying anonymous negatives; public
  policy/catalog/provider/implementation-generation drift before and
  after handoff; and no dummy-lease construction.
- 401, 403, 400 plus JSON-RPC, 404 plus JSON-RPC, and 202 matrix.
- Generic/MRTR/Tasks/extension capability failures mapped exactly to
  HTTP 400/`-32021` with required-capabilities data.
- Unknown-method exact HTTP 404/`-32601` acceptance test.
- Extension-notification auth/capability negatives; self-contained and
  negotiated-owner activation positives; absent/malformed/one-sided/
  incompatible/stale-prior-request/discovery-only/connection-reuse/
  wrong-owner/wrong-generation/expired-owner negatives; non-oracular
  owner lookup; absent invented core headers; no-ID error response
  semantics; and forbidden modern cancellation notification.
- Disconnect-before-acceptance, atomic-supervisor-handoff,
  response-close-after-202, and shutdown-after-202 no-orphan tests.
- Third-party `ApplicationNotificationSupervisor` compile/object-use/
  conformance fixture; one-shot runner under supplied `&Cx`, double-run,
  inspect/serialize/work-construction, operation/partition/guard
  substitution, unbounded queue/activation, detached-spawn, forged/
  early/missing `RunnerInstalledReceipt`, drop-after-success,
  cancellation, and late-activation rejection.
- Cancellation-before-ack, ack-then-disconnect, queue
  partition/global/byte/rate saturation and fairness, queued expiry,
  lease revocation/staleness, public-proof drift,
  implementation-revision mismatch,
  attenuated-context budget/capability, sibling-cancellation, and
  shutdown-drain tests.
- Graceful-drain deadline/audit, simulated process-loss semantics,
  request-guard/lease nonserialization, and no durable-resume claim
  tests.
- Handler-not-invoked assertions for every failing stage.

Dependencies:

- HTTP-02.
- HTTP-05.
- AUTH-01.

description:
A committed Duration::from_secs(15 * 60) fails the nursery lint
duration_suboptimal_units, which under the project's mandatory -D warnings
clippy gate is an ERROR in the fastmcp-client LIB. Because fastmcp-client is a
dependency of other workspace crates, clippy aborts there and never reaches the
crate under test, so the gate is unusable workspace-wide and also unusable for
any single crate that depends on fastmcp-client.

THE SITE:
    crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/dpop/native.rs:35
    const MAX_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15 * 60);

    error: constructing a Duration using a smaller unit when a larger unit
           would be more readable
      --> crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/dpop/native.rs:35:31
       = help: .../index.html#duration_suboptimal_units
    error: could not compile fastmcp-client (lib) due to 1 previous error

The fix is presumably Duration::from_mins(15) or a documented allow; I am not
applying it because the file is another lane's and the choice between those two
belongs to whoever owns that timeout's readability contract.

MEASURED 2026-10-13:
  command  cargo clippy --locked -p fastmcp-server --all-features --lib
           --profile test -- -D warnings
  host     hz4, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  result   halted in fastmcp-client; fastmcp-server was never linted.

THE FILE IS CLEAN, NOT MID-EDIT. git status --porcelain on it is empty and the
line's last commit is a7ff0f8d ("style(client): third fmt-gate repair this
session - 73 hunks from three commits"), about five hours before this
measurement. So this is committed state and not another lane's uncommitted
work-in-progress, which is why it is worth a bead rather than being left alone.

WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE. AGENTS.md names
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings as a required check
after any substantive change. One erroring lint in a widely-depended-on lib
makes that command report a failure that has nothing to do with the caller's
work, which trains every agent to either ignore the gate or to attribute the
failure to their own diff. A halted -D warnings run also reports ZERO findings
for the crate it never reached, so it looks like a clean result for the crate
under test rather than an absent one.

WORKAROUND, for anyone who needs the gate before this is fixed: add --no-deps,
which lints only the selected crate and skips linting dependencies. That is
what I used to get a reading on fastmcp-server.

NO-CLAIM.

comments.author: claude-opus-5-session
comments.text:
THE NAMED SITE IS REPAIRED AT HEAD, AND THE LINT CLASS IS NOW CLEAR ACROSS THE
WHOLE WORKSPACE. The bead's own open question -- "whether this is the only
blocker or merely the first one clippy reaches" -- is answered for THIS lint
and left open for every other, with the reason stated below.

1. THE SITE. crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/dpop/native.rs:35 now reads

       const MAX_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_mins(15);

   `git status --porcelain` on the file is empty, so this is committed state,
   not a lane's work in progress. Repaired by 9b405114 (2026-10-13, Jeff
   Emanuel, "fix(client): preserve caller effect ceilings throughout DPoP
   execution") -- not by me; I only measured it. HEAD at the time of this
   comment is 434f5fa8, equal to origin/main.

   The bead's NO-CLAIM worried that `Duration::from_mins` might not exist as a
   `const fn` in this position on the pinned toolchain. It does, and the proof
   is adjacent rather than theoretical: crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:1518
   is `const MAX_CLIENT_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_mins(15);`
   -- the identical construction, in the same crate, in committed compiling
   code, plus seven more `from_mins`/`from_hours` consts at :1517-:1522.

2. I MEASURED WHAT THE LINT ACTUALLY FIRES ON, rather than inferring it, and
   my first reading was wrong in a way worth recording. A sweep that treated
   "argument exactly divisible by the unit factor" as the trigger returned 377
   candidate sites. That reading cannot be true: this bead's own measurement
   reported "could not compile fastmcp-client (lib) due to 1 PREVIOUS ERROR",
   and plain-literal sites such as
   crates/fastmcp-client/src/builder.rs:82-84
   (`const MAX_CONNECTION_RETRY_ELAPSED: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120)`)
   sat in that same lib through that same run without erroring.

   So I probed the lint directly. `clippy-driver` runs locally on a single
   file, costs no build slot and no fleet time:

     clippy-driver --edition 2024 --crate-type lib \
       -W clippy::duration_suboptimal_units lintprobe.rs

     A  Duration::from_secs(15 * 60)     FIRES  -> from_mins(15)
     B  Duration::from_secs(120)         silent
     C  Duration::from_secs(3600)        silent
     D  Duration::from_millis(5 * 1000)  FIRES  -> from_secs(5)
     E  Duration::from_millis(5000)      silent
     F  Duration::from_secs(90)          silent
     "warning: 2 warnings emitted"

   The trigger is the PRODUCT form -- an argument that multiplies by the unit
   conversion factor -- not divisibility. A/B are the two forms this bead
   already distinguished empirically; C-F extend the table so the needle is
   pinned from both sides instead of fitted to one point.

3. THE WORKSPACE SWEEP, with the needle narrowed to that measured trigger and
   both controls asserted inside the instrument so it refuses rather than
   reporting a reassuring number:

     control POSITIVE  9b405114^:.../dpop/native.rs -> exactly 1 hit, line 35
                       (the pre-repair blob, i.e. the site the gate erred on)
     control NEGATIVE  builder.rs:82/84 from_secs(120) -> not matched
     result            610 .rs files under crates/ and tools/,
                       3269 Duration::from_* calls,
                       0 product-form sites remaining

   Zero is the whole finding. The positive control is what makes it readable:
   a needle that matched nothing would also print 0.

4. WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING, and this is the part the bead asked for that I
   cannot supply. I have NOT run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
   -D warnings`. That is a full workspace build, which the campaign rules
   reserve for the orchestrator's single serialized lane, and RCH is refusing
   admission anyway ("no admissible workers: critical_pressure=1"; hz3 load
   average 53). Static enumeration is the lowest proof class and does not
   substitute for the run (RH-2): it says this lint has no remaining trigger
   site, not that the gate is green.

   And the gate is probably NOT green, for other reasons already on the
   tracker: bd-t1fvv carries IvoryPine's analysis of a strict keep-going
   workspace Clippy log spanning 18 fastmcp-client TEST files (large_futures
   wanting Box::pin on diagnosed await operands, plus unit-statement
   findings), recorded in b788e676. Those live in test targets, so they do NOT
   reproduce this bead's failure mode -- they cannot halt a dependency's lib
   and so cannot stop clippy reaching a dependent crate -- but anyone reading
   this bead as "the gate works now" would be wrong.

5. A NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING BECAUSE I ALMOST FILED IT AS A REGRESSION.
   Earlier this session I added
   `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "tasks"), allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps))]` to
   `CallResult::into_core` in http_auth/managed/client.rs for a different
   clippy error. It is gone from the file, removed by cd4bd779. That looked
   like a swept gate fix. It is not: cd4bd779 added the `Catalog` and
   `CoreListen` variants, and both are live without the `tasks` feature, so
   `into_core`'s `Err` arm is now reachable in the default build and the lint
   no longer applies. The allow became dead and removing it was correct.
   Reading the function settled in a minute what a grep would have
   mis-reported.

6. NO NEW GATE, deliberately. I wrote the sweep as a scratchpad instrument and
   am NOT committing it. A standing "no Duration product form" check would
   duplicate a lint clippy already owns; the fix for an unusable clippy gate is

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN TEXT, caught by someone else. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14.

I described duration_suboptimal_units as 'the nursery lint' on this bead. THAT IS WRONG. nursery is not enabled anywhere in this workspace, so a nursery lint could not have blocked anything.

bd-d0f2f measured this and named my error explicitly. I verified it independently rather than taking it on faith:

  grep -rn nursery Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml tools/*/Cargo.toml   -> 0 hits
  grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'clippy::nursery' crates/ tools/           -> 0 hits
  [workspace.lints.clippy] enables exactly:  all = warn, pedantic = warn
                                             then ~75 individual allow entries

So the mandated gate lints all + pedantic minus the allow list, and duration_suboptimal_units belongs to one of those two groups, not to nursery.

WHAT THIS CHANGES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It changes my attribution and nothing else. Every measurement on this bead stands: the lint was fatal under -D warnings, it halted the run in fastmcp-client before any dependent crate, and the greens recorded here are unaffected. The word 'nursery' was decoration in my description, not a premise of any inference -- but it was still false, and it propagated from a scratchpad note into two beads, which is exactly how a wrong detail becomes repository folklore.

THE DEEPER POINT, which is bd-d0f2f's and worth repeating here because this bead is where agents will look for the gate's definition: AGENTS.md:326 itself says '(pedantic + nursery are enabled)'. I read that line, believed it, and repeated it without checking Cargo.toml. The document every agent is told to follow is the source of the error. That is the second time today I have been wrong by adopting a written claim instead of verifying it -- the first was the ping expectation I took from a self-contradictory test. Same failure, different source.

Correcting it here rather than quietly, because self-report beats discovery and because another agent already had to spend a measurement catching it.

### GATE-EMA-BUILTIN-READY — Aggregate complete EMA OIDC/SAML with built-in issuer

Outcome:

Prove complete EMA OIDC and SAML identity paths compose safely with FastMCP’s built-in issuer, without making the issuer a SAML parser or allowing either standalone profile to inherit composition evidence.

Reason:

The authorization-server trust, replay, resource, and issuance seam is
not exercised by the standalone enterprise client or ordinary built-in
issuer gates.

Implementation:

- Aggregate AUTHX-03 only after GATE-EMA-READY (both AUTHX-01 and AUTHX-04) and GATE-BUILTIN-AUTH-READY pass independently.
- Run end-to-end positives for both OIDC-derived and SAML-derived normalized provenance-bound identities entering the exact ID-JAG/built-in issuance seam. The built-in issuer consumes only the validated normalized/ID-JAG contract; it does not directly parse SAML or borrow OIDC evidence for SAML.
- Run the literal two-feature metadata/token endpoint, durable
  replay, resource/audience, IdP trust, client-authentication,
  exact inbound RS256-only out-of-band `IdJagIssuerCryptoPolicy`,
  `EnterpriseClientKey`, all three preregistrations and cross-domain
  client binding, `ResourceAsIdpRelyingPartyKey`, subject-type/sector
  policy, typed client/resource/audience subjects and continuity,
  single-/multi-tenant preexisting account mapping with no JIT,
  exact HTTP-200/no-cache `EnterpriseAccessTokenResponse`,
  disclosure-policy default-deny,
  RAR/actor/alias rejection, default-rejected versus explicitly
  approved-and-ignored email, bounded precheck/KMS admission, restart,
  and recovery matrix.
- Require the client endpoint to use exact issuer-bound
  `RegistrationOrigin::PreRegistered` metadata with only provider-backed
  Basic or secret-post, the enterprise profile, and both required
  enterprise client grants. Reject public/private-key/mTLS, DCR,
  URL/portable CIMD, missing origin, and profile/grant/method drift
  before assertion parsing or replay lookup.
- Aggregate AUTH-00 `PersistentReplayDigest` evidence for
  `EnterpriseIdJagJtiReplay`: exact framed
  `(IdpAuthorizationServerIssuerId,jti)` context, named persistent MAC
  provider/configuration, every active/previous generation alias,
  rollout acknowledgement and fenced retirement, store namespace and
  external restore epoch, atomic replay/issuance transaction, and
  rollback/clone/mixed-ring resistance.
- Bind the final replay/issuance transaction to the exact
  `EnterpriseIdentityPolicyBundle` digest/snapshot/reviewer authority
  and sealed read-only subject-mapping receipt; require provider/backend
  artifact, attestation, fencing, outage/staleness/substitution, and
  zero-JIT/zero-mutation evidence.
- Record exact scenario/check IDs by client, resource server,
  authorization server, transport, and result; reject skip-like or
  empty required categories.
- Require confidential client authentication, no sender-constrained
  advertisement, and pre-replay rejection of `cnf`, DPoP proof/header,
  and JWT-DPoP grant/token requests.
- Aggregate the complete AUTHX-03 endpoint error partition: structural
  `invalid_request`, unsupported `unsupported_grant_type`, AUTH-06
  `invalid_client`, `unauthorized_client` for an authenticated but
  ineligible registration, then one wire-identical `invalid_grant` for
  every invalid or unacceptable present assertion after successful
  authentication and eligibility. Truly unknown bounded duplicate-free
  form parameters are ignored/redacted; known-forbidden members are
  `invalid_request`.
- Prove replay tombstones survive old-generation cleanup and later
  skew/lifetime widening through the immutable retention horizon.
- Prove both standalone evidence manifests are unchanged whether this
  composition passes or fails.

Acceptance:

- The composition is unavailable and unadvertised unless both features
  and explicit policy are enabled.
- Durable atomic replay rejection and exact MCP audience issuance pass
  across restart and multi-instance races.
- Known replays reach no signer, stale precheck races are closed by the
  final `IdJagReplayKey` compare-and-set, and KMS/quota reservations
  release on every noncommit path.
- Issuance consumes only the validated literal scope/resource and typed
  client/tenancy/subject keys; the response overlay is transactionally
  identical to the issued token and store, uses exact HTTP 200 plus
  both no-cache fields, and never creates/links/updates/JIT-provisions
  an account. RAR, actor, and alias claims cannot widen it.
- All invalid or unacceptable present assertions after successful
  client authentication and eligibility have one exact wire-identical
  `invalid_grant`
  result before signer/issuance side effects; structural/grant/client-
  auth/ineligible-client errors remain correctly distinct as
  `invalid_request`/`unsupported_grant_type`/`invalid_client`/
  `unauthorized_client`. The gate claims bounded amplification and wire
  non-disclosure, not latency indistinguishability. ID-JAG redemption
  cannot issue or authorize refresh tokens.
- Inbound ID-JAG is RS256-only; disclosure-policy-approved optional
  bounded `email` is discarded and cannot affect mapping or issuance.
- The two OIDC RP registrations carry exact public/pairwise subject-
  type and sector-policy generations. Typed client/resource/audience
  subject IDs cannot swap, and coincidental subject text equality is
  not continuity evidence.
- Public `none` and every DPoP/key-bound branch remain unavailable and
  cannot mutate durable replay or issuance state.
- Generic public metadata remains byte-invariant across IdP/tenant/
  client trust-policy changes.
- The composed issuer rejects a same/ambiguous issuing-IdP versus
  redeeming-resource-AS domain and any assertion bound to another
  downstream resource AS before replay lookup or issuance; client/IdP
  domain equality is permitted and recorded.
- Unapproved optional ID-JAG claims are rejected before replay lookup;
  approved optional values are discarded and cannot affect issuance.
- Neither standalone base gate inherits a composite success or
  failure.

- Both EMA source branches reach the built-in composition through independently verified provenance; a green OIDC path cannot substitute for SAML, and the built-in issuer does not become a SAML parser.

Tests:

- Four-way feature matrix and packaged composite consumer.
- AUTHX-03 security/recovery/admission, tenancy-isolation, and
  RS256-only, RAR/actor/alias rejection, and default-denied versus
  explicitly approved-and-ignored email aggregation.
- Exact client-key and response-overlay aggregation, including
  different/equal-text cross-domain-ID mappings, cross-tenant equal-
  client-ID negatives, all three preregistrations, exact HTTP 200/
  no-cache resource/scope response/JWT/store equality, and invalid
  other-2xx/cache header cases.
- `ResourceAsIdpRelyingPartyKey`, public/pairwise subject-type and
  sector generations, typed client/resource/audience subject IDs,
  differing/equal pairwise values, exact transaction continuity,
  sector/flow/response swaps, missing-preexisting-map and zero-account-
  mutation/no-JIT aggregation.
- Confidential-auth and DPoP/`cnf` quarantine aggregation with
  no-replay-store-mutation assertions.
- Replay-key domain separation, known-replay/no-KMS, stale-precheck,
  reservation-release, all-generation persistent-MAC aliases,
  ring rollout/retirement, restore/clone resistance, and disclosure-
  policy/minimum-claim aggregation.
- Full endpoint error-partition goldens for `invalid_request`,
  `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_client`, `unauthorized_client`,
  and wire-identical
  `invalid_grant` across JOSE/issuer/audience/client/resource/scope/
  time/`jti`/replay/tenant/subject/trust/disclosure/RAR/actor/`cnf`
  failures; ignored/redacted truly unknown form parameters; bounded
  admission without a timing-equality claim; zero signer/issuance/
  replay-mutation proof except the required known-replay read; no-ID-
  JAG-refresh emission/state; and ordinary AUTH-06 refresh isolation.
- Exact preregistration/profile/both-client-grants matrix, including
  missing/swapped grant, wrong server `grant_types_supported`
  substitution, disallowed registration/auth methods, and
  `unauthorized_client` before assertion/replay work.
- Policy-bundle digest/snapshot/reviewer and sealed mapping-receipt
  transaction binding, provider/backend attestation/fencing,
  stale/conflicting mapping, receipt/flow substitution, and zero-
  mutation/no-JIT aggregation.
- Old-generation cleanup followed by widened skew/lifetime without
  replay resurrection.
- Public-metadata non-disclosure and no-trust-oracle aggregation.
- Issuer/redeemer trust-domain distinction, recorded client domain, and
  exact one-RAS binding aggregation.
- Base-manifest nonmutation and scenario-inventory completeness.
- SAML-derived and OIDC-derived built-in positives, one-variable signature/audience/replay/provenance failures, and cross-branch provenance substitution tests.

The orchestrator named the exact gap this closes: "these tests pass, but nobody has compared their assertions to the src/ originals. A promotion that quietly tests LESS than the inline version would produce precisely this receipt."

THE INSTRUMENT, and why it is stronger than reading. I did not transcribe these tests by hand; I applied a declared mechanical transformation. So the claim is checkable by RE-APPLYING it to the current src/lib.rs spans and diffing against the committed external files. Reading assertions one by one can confirm what IS present; it cannot prove nothing was OMITTED. A byte-level diff proves both directions at once.

RESULT:

  crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_a.rs   IDENTICAL to the transformed src span
  crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_b.rs   IDENTICAL to the transformed src span

Byte-identical means no assertion was dropped, weakened, added, or REORDERED. Ordering
matters here and is not a pedantic point: an assertion sequence can be hollowed out by moving
a check after the thing it guards, which is exactly how fnd_04's length-before-hex ordering
became load-bearing earlier today.

The declared transformation, in full, so the claim can be re-derived:
  crate::limit_01_rows::  ->  limit_01_rows::      (the harness is local to the test target)
  crate::                 ->  fastmcp_core::       (every symbol already public at lib.rs:2229)
  lines matching ^\s*#\[cfg\(test\)\]\n            removed
  a file header added above `mod limit_01_rows;`   (excluded from the diff)

ASSERTION COUNTS, independently derived rather than inferred from the diff:

  A   assert_eq! src=44  promoted=44      assert_ne! src=4  promoted=4      assert! src=9  promoted=9
  B   assert_eq! src=84  promoted=84      assert_ne! src=3  promoted=3      assert! src=2  promoted=2

THE ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, isolated and named. The ported harness differs from
src/limit_01_rows.rs in exactly two places, both the same edit:

  -        .err().expect("a request-supplied identifier must refuse")
  +        .expect_err("a request-supplied identifier must refuse")

That is clippy::err_expect, which fires under -D warnings. It is semantically identical --
both unwrap the Err arm and panic on Ok with the same message. Nothing else in 911 lines
differs. I fixed it in the PORT only; the original still carries the lint at
src/limit_01_rows.rs:303 and :315 and I have not touched it, because the instruction was to
leave the cfg(test) copies alone.

SUBCASE COVERAGE, for items 1-3, verified in the promoted targets:

  LIMIT-A-01  bounds, numeric floor 6 -- bound_rows driven, floor asserted as 6
  LIMIT-A-02  .01 .02 .03 .04 .05 all present, and the positive asserts the row set is
              exactly 5 AND that exactly one row reaches the Verified domain
  LIMIT-A-03  .01 .02 .03 .04 all present; run_arithmetic_rows and arithmetic_receipt
              are both driven

Because the targets are byte-identical to the originals, subcase coverage is inherited
exactly: whatever the inline copies exercised, these exercise, neither more nor less.

WHAT THIS PROOF DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated so it is not read wider than it is:

  1. It proves the promoted targets are EQUIVALENT to the inline originals. It says nothing
     about whether the originals were adequate. If an inline assertion was weak, it is
     equally weak here. I have previously recorded one such case on this very test: the A
     positive's `assert_eq!(snapshot, defaults.snapshot())` equality control is vacuous,
     because `snapshot()` is `self.clone()`, so it reduces to clone() == clone() on a
     derived-PartialEq value type. That vacuity is now promoted along with everything else.
  2. It proves nothing about the harness's own correctness -- only that the copy matches the
     original. A defect in limit_01_rows.rs is faithfully reproduced.
  3. Equivalence is proven against the CURRENT src/lib.rs. If the inline copies are later
     edited, the two diverge silently and this proof expires. The check is one command and
     is reproducible from the script recorded with this work.

So the honest summary is: the promotion makes the existing evidence ADMISSIBLE under PL-3,
and provably does not weaken it. It does not make it stronger, and item 1's vacuous equality
control is an example of something it carried across unchanged.
