comments.text:
EXPLICIT (a)/(b) DETERMINATION, requested by WildMountain before any build work.

VERDICT: (b) THE FIXTURE IS WRONG. NOT the client parser. The bead's title is therefore
mis-framed -- it reads as a client defect and it is a test-fixture defect.

=== ESTABLISHED AGAINST THE WIRE CONTRACT, NOT AGAINST THE TEST ===

The client's decoder requires two things of a subscriptions listen terminal, and both
requirements are stated in the protocol crate rather than inferred from the failure:

  protocol/src/messages.rs:4260  decode_final_complete(SUBSCRIPTIONS_LISTEN, ..)?
      requires FinalMethodResult::Complete. The fixture sent resultType "empty".
  protocol/src/messages.rs:4261  subscription_id_from_result(&result)?
      requires _meta[FINAL_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_META_KEY]. The fixture sent none.
  protocol/src/messages.rs:3480  documents the field as "The REQUIRED subscription ID
      extracted from the result metadata."

So the parser is enforcing a documented contract and the fixture encodes a frame that
contract never admits. "Fixing" the parser to accept resultType "empty" with no subscription
id would make the client accept an illegal terminal permanently -- exactly the (b)-mistaken-
for-(a) outcome the instruction warns about.

CORROBORATION FROM A PASSING SIBLING, which is the strongest available evidence that the
frame shape is the variable: crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials/
subscriptions.rs:54-56 builds its terminal as
    json!({"resultType":"complete", "_meta":{(FINAL_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_META_KEY): id}})
and its equivalent tests pass against the SAME decoder. Same parser, different fixture,
opposite outcome.

=== ORDER: BOTH REQUIRED, SEQUENTIAL, DERIVED NOT MEASURED ===

:4260 runs BEFORE :4261, so resultType fails first and a fixture correcting only that would
then fail on the absent _meta. Recorded in the previous comment with both line numbers and
the derived/measured distinction stated.

=== THE SSE FALSE-GREEN CAUTION: CHECKED, AND IT DOES NOT APPLY ===

The terminal IS SSE-shaped (`data: {..}\n\n`), so the warning is apposite. It does not fire
here, and the evidence is the shape of the failure rather than an assertion:

  the false-green shape is ZERO events delivered and the test PASSING vacuously.
  what was observed is the OPPOSITE -- events delivered and the test FAILING at the third.

In the 8-passed/1-failed run the narrowing test consumed Acknowledged, then Notification,
then failed at Terminal. Two events were delivered before the failure, so the stream is not
zero-delivery. Four sibling tests consuming the same ACK/UPDATE frames passed outright.

I have separately been bitten by exactly the vacuous variant in this file -- a negative that
passed because a dropped SSE `data: ` prefix made every frame unparseable -- so the check was
run rather than waved through.

commit 6cd28e7c, TERMINAL const only, both differences in one change per the revised ruling.
Verified present at HEAD 8b3b6738.

title: SEP-2164: resources/read on a missing resource returns -32001, official suite wants -32602

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus55
comments.text:
Measured from the pinned suite @modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.10 bundle, 2026-10-03.

Check sep-2164-error-code / ResourcesNotFoundErrorCode: 'Server returns -32602 (Invalid Params) for non-existent resource (SHOULD)'. The suite's own failure message notes that -32002 was used in earlier spec versions but SEP-2164 standardizes -32602.

Ours is neither: McpErrorCode::ResourceNotFound => -32001 (crates/fastmcp-core/src/error.rs). Emitted from router.rs:6002, :6105, :8445, :8452, :8526.

Why this is NOT in the 38-failure set and was deliberately deferred: the check is SHOULD-level, so the suite records WARNING, not FAILURE. It does not move the 54/92 count.

Why it is not a one-line change: the code must stay era-scoped. Exact MCP 2024-11-05 keeps -32001, and at least four pinned tests assert McpErrorCode::ResourceNotFound directly (router.rs:19112, :23043, :23268, :24351). A global edit to the From<McpErrorCode> for i32 arm would silently change the legacy wire and break those tests. The fix is a modern-era-only mapping at the final-dispatch boundary plus a positive/negative pair proving the legacy era is unchanged (RH-5).

Acceptance:
- modern resources/read on an unknown URI answers -32602.
- exact-2024 resources/read on an unknown URI still answers -32001, proven by a test that fails if the mapping leaks across eras.
- official sep-2164-error-code reports SUCCESS rather than WARNING.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus55
comments.text:
REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT -- I FILED THIS WRONG (RealityCheck-Opus55, 2026-10-03).

I inferred this defect from source alone (McpErrorCode::ResourceNotFound => -32001 in
crates/fastmcp-core/src/error.rs) without ever observing the wire. The official suite says
otherwise.

--spec-version 2026-07-28 --suite all. Scenario server-sep-2164-resource-not-found, all three
checks SUCCESS:
  sep-2164-no-empty-contents  SUCCESS
  sep-2164-error-code         SUCCESS  details.receivedErrorCode = -32602
  sep-2164-data-uri           SUCCESS

So the modern resources/read path already answers -32602 for an unknown URI AND carries the
requested URI in error.data. The -32001 constant is simply not what that path emits; it is not

### AUTH-07 — Implement the interactive authorization flow driver

Outcome:

Turn discovery and OAuth primitives into one cancel-correct client
flow suitable for CLI, desktop, and embedded callers.

Reason:

Correct individual URLs and token requests are insufficient if the
browser handoff, loopback redirect, state lifetime, cancellation, or
token commit sequence is ambiguous.

Implementation:

- Define an `AuthorizationFlowDriver` trait with explicit UI/browser
  handoff, redirect receipt, user-decline, timeout, and cancellation
  outcomes.
- Derive LIMIT-01's `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` from the validated
  issuer/resource/client/driver/profile and reserve pending-record,
  protected-byte, listener, and deployment capacity before binding a
  listener or launching a browser. Never require or fabricate a
  post-token `QuotaPartitionKey`; release every reservation exactly
  once on the one terminal outcome.
- Provide a native loopback driver that binds a random available
  loopback port on both reviewed IPv4/IPv6 policy paths.
- Generate a one-use redirect path from its own 32-byte CSPRNG draw
  into a typed canonical Base64url path segment, independent of state
  and PKCE. Parse callbacks through the shared lower-layer
  `OAuthParameterAdmission` with AUTH-03's callback profile, compare
  the path and state in constant
  time, and close the listener/zeroize pending secrets after the first
  terminal attempt.
- Open a browser only through an injected launcher after presenting
  the exact issuer and authorization origin.
- Present all peer-controlled issuer/origin/error text through
  `UntrustedDisplayText`; browser launch receives only the separately
  validated typed URL, never display text.
- Bind state, PKCE verifier, redirect URI, issuer, resource, client
  identity, requested scopes, creation time, and expiry in one
  non-persisted pending-flow record.
- Obtain initial requested scopes from AUTH-04's exact
  challenge-first/PRM-fallback/absent-omit rule and preserve the
  authoritative challenged set through step-up.
- Enforce one-use state and authorization code handling.
- Validate RFC 9207 `iss` before rendering provider-supplied error
  text.
- Apply HTTPS requirements to metadata, authorization, token, CIMD,
  DCR, and JWKS endpoints, with the standards-permitted loopback
  redirect exception only.
- Complete token exchange and atomic credential-store commit before
  reporting success.
- Cancel listener, browser wait, discovery, and token exchange through
  the caller's `Cx`.
- Support a host-provided redirect driver for web applications without
  embedding a web framework.

Acceptance:

- A timeout, user decline, malformed redirect, duplicate redirect, or
  cancellation leaves no live listener or reusable pending state.
- The browser never opens an unvalidated issuer endpoint.
- The PKCE verifier and state never enter logs or persistent storage.
- Success is reported only after issuer/resource validation and atomic
  credential commit.
- Loopback HTTP is admitted only for the one native client redirect
  listener; it is not permission to use an insecure MCP resource,
  PRM, issuer, authorization/token endpoint, or bearer target.
- Pre-token client/source churn cannot bypass per-flow/deployment
  admission or leak a listener, pending record, or reservation.

Tests:

- Native loopback happy path on supported platforms.
- User decline, timeout, cancellation, duplicate callback, wrong path,
  state mismatch, and code replay.
- Redirect-path entropy/independence, constant-time mismatch,
  cross-flow path/state substitution, CSPRNG failure before listener/
  browser side effects, one-use cleanup, and log-redaction tests.
- Browser-launch failure.
- RFC 9207 error mix-up.
- HTTPS and loopback exception matrix.
- Atomic credential-commit fault injection.
- Initial challenge scope, PRM fallback, omitted-scope, and unrelated
  challenge/PRM set integration tests.
- No-orphan listener assertion.
- Authorization-flow key isolation, client/profile/source churn,
  per-flow/deployment saturation before browser launch, listener
  reservation, cancellation/race, and exact-once release tests.
- Malicious issuer/error ANSI/OSC/Rich/bidi/IDNA display and typed-
  URL-versus-display separation tests.

structural reason: `recursion_depth_exceeding_limit` is a
`future_incompatible` WARNING on the pinned toolchain, and a warning does not
fail `cargo test`. A green `cargo test` receipt is silent about it in exactly
the same way it is silent about every other warning.

Two different claims, and only the second is what this bead asks for:

- *"has not bitten yet"* — established by the green run, and true only while
  the workspace stays pinned to nightly-2026-08-25.
- *"cannot bite"* — requires a build that treats the warning as a failure.
  That is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, which is
  AGENTS.md's stated gate and the bead's own `INFERRED, NOT EXECUTED` item.

The pin is the only thing standing between this warning and a hard error; a
toolchain bump converts it into a build failure. So "it passed" and "it is
fixed" are separated here by a version bump nobody has scheduled.

### The fix

`crates/fastmcp-server/tests/auth_01_a.rs` now carries
`#![recursion_limit = "256"]` with a justification comment. This is the
workspace's existing idiom, not a new escape hatch — three sites already set it
for the same trait-solver reason:

```
crates/fastmcp-server/tests/srv_02_b.rs:6   256   sibling integration target
crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:67         512   nested async in serve_http_connection
crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:47         512
```

256 matches the sibling target. This raises a COMPILE-TIME trait-resolution
depth, not a runtime stack — it is not the "never raise the stack, Box::pin each
arm" case, which concerns async match arms overflowing the test thread's stack
at run time. No test behaviour changes.

### Class swept, with its limit

Across every `crates/*/tests/*.rs`: `auth_01_a.rs` uses `spawn_via_gateway` once
(now 256), `srv_02_b.rs` uses it zero times (already 256, for other nesting). No
other integration target uses the cited trigger; both `src/lib.rs` files hosting
deep async nesting already carry 512.

**Limit of that sweep, stated rather than implied:** it keys on the trigger this
bead cites. The lint fires on deep async nesting generally, so another target
could trip it by a different path. Only a compile settles that.

### Status

Committed UNVERIFIED. Per AGENTS.md the serialized RCH lane belongs to the
orchestrator, so the runner card — `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
-D warnings` — is with WildMountain rather than self-dispatched. That single run
verifies this fix AND discharges the bead's own `INFERRED, NOT EXECUTED` note.

**This bead should not close on the green server receipt.** It should close on a
gate that fails warnings.

title: AGENTS.md:326 tells every agent the mandatory clippy gate lints nursery; nursery is enabled nowhere in the workspace, and two beads already named the wrong lint group because of it
description:
AGENTS.md tells every agent that the mandatory clippy gate lints `nursery`. It
does not. `nursery` is enabled nowhere in this workspace, so a lint group the
project believes it checks has never been checked, and the belief is recorded in
the one document every agent is instructed to follow.

MEASURED 2026-10-14 at HEAD 60bb3c9b, statically and with a local probe.

THE CLAIM. AGENTS.md:326, in the "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" section whose
command the same section says must be run "after any substantive code changes":

    # Check for clippy lints (pedantic + nursery are enabled)
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

THE CONFIGURATION. `[workspace.lints.clippy]` (Cargo.toml:127) enables exactly
two groups:

    all      = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
    pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

followed by ~75 individual `= "allow"` entries. `nursery` appears at NO level:

    grep -rn nursery Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml tools/*/Cargo.toml   -> 0
    grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'clippy::nursery' crates/ tools/           -> 0

No crate re-enables it with an inner attribute either; fastmcp-client's only
crate-level attributes are `#![recursion_limit = "512"]` and
`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

So the mandated command lints `all` + `pedantic` minus the allow list, and the
parenthetical in AGENTS.md is false about half of what it names.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN SILENTLY CORRECTING. The discrepancy
has already produced a wrong inference on two beads. bd-tz38v's blocker #1 and
bd-5q6nd's description both describe `duration_suboptimal_units` as "the
nursery lint". If that were true, and nursery is off, it could not have blocked
the mandated gate -- yet it demonstrably did. I measured the group directly with
clippy-driver on a six-row file, locally, costing no build slot:

    -W clippy::all -W clippy::pedantic   -> 2 warnings, both product forms
                                            (from_secs(15 * 60), from_millis(5 * 1000))
    -W clippy::nursery                   -> nothing

So that lint is in all/pedantic on nightly-2026-08-25 and the beads named the
wrong group. Harmless there because the conclusion survived; the general case
is not harmless, because "nursery is enabled" is the premise an agent would use
to decide whether a nursery finding is in scope for the gate they are told to
run.

THE DECISION, and it is a real decision rather than a typo fix. Two defensible
dispositions:

  A. CORRECT THE DOCUMENT. Change the comment to name the groups that are
     actually enabled. Zero risk, zero new findings, and it makes the mandated
     command's coverage honest. This is the conservative choice and probably
     the right one: `nursery` is explicitly experimental upstream, its lints
     churn between releases, and this workspace already carries ~75 individual
     allows to keep `all` + `pedantic` tractable.

  B. ENABLE NURSERY. Add `nursery = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }` and
     absorb whatever it reports. Unknown cost -- I have NOT measured it and
     will not, because that is a full workspace clippy run and belongs to the
     orchestrator's serialized lane -- and it would land on a gate that only
     just reached zero after thirteen blocker sites (bd-tz38v), so it risks
     reopening the exact condition that made the gate unusable for weeks.

I recommend A, and note that A has a prerequisite I cannot satisfy: AGENTS.md
is the operator's document, and bd-3zzrz records that all three of its frozen
FND-01 byte segments plus the CHANGELOG historical suffix have already drifted
and that re-freezing versus reverting is an unmade operator decision. Editing
line 326 moves bytes inside that contract's scope. So even the one-line fix
needs the operator, which is why this is a bead and not a commit.

ACCEPTANCE, whichever branch is taken:

title: rch fleet: capability prober reports stale E205 component facts on all 4 workers
description: Observed 2026-08-23 (LavenderCoyote, FND-01 central-batch cycle): 'rch workers probe --all' reports CAPABILITY_MISSING RCH-E205 'missing rustup component(s) for nightly-2026-08-20: clippy, rustfmt' with 'Rustup components: unknown' on ALL FOUR workers (vmi1149989, vmi1152480, vmi1153651, vmi1156319), causing every 'rch exec' to exit 103 'all workers failed preflight checks'. Root cause candidates: (a) worker rchd runs as root with systemd-inherited PATH lacking /root/.cargo/bin (symlinked shims into /usr/local/bin did NOT clear E205); (b) restarting rchd on vmi1156319 did NOT clear E205; (c) probe script (rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs build_capability_probe_script) emits component facts only when its interpolated {rustup} resolves in the EXECUTING context — executing context of probes vs exec-preflight differs from manual ssh shells. Impact: entire fleet unroutable for all agents; FND-01 verification lane forced onto worker-direct SSH execution this cycle (precedent: FoggyMouse census). Also noted: vmi1149989 /tmp tmpfs 100% full (40G/40G) — left DISABLED via 'rch workers disable' (reversible with enable); assembler temp files (cc*.s) cannot be written there. Acceptance: probe --all returns 4/4 healthy without disabling anything; one zero-filter rch exec cargo check succeeds end-to-end through the normal lane.

comments.author: OxAlpha
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + FIX IMPLEMENTED (OxAlpha, omp, 2026-08-24). Claimed via br --force (decomposition-terminal edge absent here; plain atomic claim).

ROOT CAUSE: worker-side rch-wkr capability probe resolved 'rustup'/'rustc' as bare Command names through the CALLER's PATH only. Worker rchd.service runs as root under systemd whose default service PATH (/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin) has historically not carried the provisioned toolchain location; when resolution failed, probe_rustup_inventory returned silently-empty vectors, so preflight read 'components unknown' as 'clippy/rustfmt missing' and rejected ALL FOUR workers with RCH-E205 during LavenderCoyote's 2026-08-23 central-batch cycle — while ubuntu-level SSH ground truth showed both toolchains fully installed. Fleet recovered operationally once /usr/local/bin/rustup appeared on the boxes, but the silent-empty failure class remained in code.

FIX (commit 82b10330 on remote_compilation_helper main, pushed):
1. resolve_tool_binary: PATH first, then ~/.cargo/bin, ~/.local/bin, /root/.cargo/bin, /usr/local/bin — provenance tracked.
2. probe_rustup_inventory + rustc version probe use the resolver.
3. WorkerCapabilities.probe_warnings (serde default/skip-if-empty => wire-compatible with deployed 1.0.57 peers): records fallback resolutions and failed sub-probes; 'no facts' is no longer indistinguishable from 'facts show absence'.
4. rch workers probe prints non-empty warnings beside the component matrix.

LOCAL PROOF: 3 new resolver unit tests; rch-wkr 184/184; clippy clean on touched code; cargo fmt clean.

WORKER vmi1149989 DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED: binary 1.0.58 commit 82b103300e65 installed to /usr/local/bin/rch-wkr. Original-defect environment reproduction (sudo env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root): OLD behavior = 0 components silently; NEW = 102 components + explicit warnings ['rustc resolved from fallback location /root/.cargo/bin/rustc', 'rustup resolved from fallback location /root/.cargo/bin/rustup']. Normal systemd-like PATH: 102 components, zero warnings. Remaining three workers building detached (fleet load); install+verify next.

comments.author: OxAlpha
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE REFINEMENT after live reproduction (OxAlpha 2026-08-24): the 'stale component facts' are stale WORKER BINARIES, not caches. Deployed /usr/local/bin/rch-wkr on all four boxes was v1.0.57 (commit 7013f4cf, Aug 15) whose capabilities command has NO rustup inventory probing at all — its JSON omits rustup_toolchains/rustup_components entirely (captured live: 459 bytes, rustc_version present, both keys absent). Newer clients evaluate declared nightly components against those absent facts and fail closed with RCH-E205 + 'Rustup components: unknown' — exactly LavenderCoyote's storm signature. Earlier 'all healthy' readings came from an equally-old client that never evaluated components. Secondary hazard fixed in 82b10330: even current code resolved rustup/rustc as bare names through caller PATH, which silently breaks under root systemd service environments (worker rchd.service runs as root, HOME=/root, minimal PATH); resolver now falls back to ~/.cargo/bin, ~/.local/bin, /root/.cargo/bin, /usr/local/bin with provenance surfaced as WorkerCapabilities.probe_warnings.

title: RETRACTED BY AUTHOR (false premise): claimed TaskManager notifications are unwired, but the whole TaskManager subsystem is cfg(test) and documented as absent from production builds
description:
TaskManager emits task status notifications at every lifecycle transition, and in
the shipped server they are all silently discarded, because nothing outside the
crate's own cfg(test) module ever installs a notification sender.

This is an unwired-finished-code gap, not a missing implementation. Every piece
exists and is correct: the field, the setter, the three product call sites at the
right transitions, the notification params type, and passing unit tests.

MEASURED 2026-10-11 at HEAD 110578e0 (blob of tasks.rs is the subject; the
instrument was validated against two known positives first -- see below).

  crates/fastmcp-server/src/tasks.rs
    :80    pub type TaskNotificationSender = Arc<dyn Fn(JsonRpcRequest) + Send + Sync>
    :236   notification_sender: Arc<RwLock<Option<TaskNotificationSender>>>
    :258   initialised to None in TaskManager::new
    :294   pub fn set_notification_sender(&self, sender: TaskNotificationSender)

  CALL SITES of set_notification_sender, all five of them:
    :23760  :24365  :24376  :24477  :24636
  mod tests begins at :8793. Every call site is above it. There are no call
  sites in any other file: ripgrep for TaskNotificationSender across all of
  crates/ returns tasks.rs and nothing else, tests and product alike.

  PRODUCT CODE DOES CONSUME IT. Inside the spawned task future:
    :434   notify_snapshot(&notification_sender, running_snapshot)
    :452   notify_snapshot(&notification_sender, failure_snapshot)
    :505   notify_snapshot(&notification_sender, completion_snapshot)
  and the free function at :851 opens with
    let Some(sender) = sender else { return; };
  so with the slot at None every running / failure / completion notification is
  dropped with no error, no warning and no counter. PL-3 applies exactly: the
  passing unit tests at :24351 onward prove the mechanism under cfg(test) and
  cannot prove shipped behaviour, because the shipped path never installs a
  sender.

INSTRUMENT VALIDATION (the zero is a real zero, not a bad grep). The same sweep
over setter-shaped pub fns reported external_calls=1 for
fastmcp-client overlay_client_capabilities, which is the single call site added
by 7f2bc0b8, and 4 for set_client_implementation. A name with a known caller
reads non-zero on this instrument, so a zero is informative.

WIRING IS TYPE-COMPATIBLE. router.rs:81 declares
  pub type NotificationSender = Arc<dyn Fn(JsonRpcRequest) + Send + Sync>
which is structurally identical to TaskNotificationSender, and the server
already builds exactly such closures on the live outbound paths, for example
async_stdio.rs:658 and router.rs:10401. So no new plumbing type is needed.

THE HAZARD, which is why this bead does not simply say "call the setter".
The notification slot is SERVER-SCOPED, not session-scoped:
  lib.rs:13102  pub struct Server
  lib.rs:13134      task_manager: Option<SharedTaskManager>
and session.rs holds no task manager of its own. The slot holds ONE sender and
a set REPLACES the previous one, which the crate's own test
set_notification_sender_replaces_existing (:24354) pins deliberately.

Therefore installing a sender per connection on a multi-connection server is
WORSE than the current silence: the most recent connection wins the slot, and
task notifications for a task created by client A are delivered into client B's
stream. That is a cross-client leak rather than a dropped message. The
per-request senders already in the tree are also the wrong handle, because a
task future outlives the request that created it: spawn_task clones the slot
Arc into runtime.try_spawn at :413 and the notification fires whenever the task
transitions, by which time the creating request's owner may be long gone.

So the safe shapes are, in increasing order of work:
  (a) single-connection transports only, for example async_stdio, where one
      process serves one client and the slot cannot be contended. Correct today
      and testable today.
  (b) route by task ownership: record the originating session on the task and
      resolve the sender per notification rather than holding one slot.
  (c) move the slot to session scope and give TaskManager a per-session view.
(b) or (c) is required before any multi-client transport can deliver these
notifications at all. Choosing between them is a design decision about where
task-to-session ownership lives and is not the finder's to make.

SCOPE NOTE. The tasks feature is NOT in fastmcp-server's default feature set
(default = ["legacy-2024-11-05"]), so this affects consumers who enable tasks,
which is the MCP 2026-07-28 Tasks surface the campaign is implementing. It is
not a defect in a default build.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY. This bead does not claim the notification payload is wrong,
does not claim any test is wrong, and does not assert that task execution itself
is broken: tasks run, and tasks/get returns correct state. It claims exactly one
thing, that the push notification path has no installed sender in any shipped
configuration, and it is therefore unexercised outside cfg(test).

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
THE INTEGRATION GAP IS SYMMETRIC, which makes it easier to miss than a plain
missing feature. Both halves of notifications/tasks are implemented and both
halves are tested, each against a hand-written stand-in for the other, and
nothing in the suite joins them.

  SERVER EMISSION. tasks.rs calls notify_snapshot at the running, failure and
  completion transitions (:434, :452, :505). Tested at :24351 onward by
  installing a sender by hand under cfg(test). No shipped configuration
  installs one, so the product path is unexercised (the body of this bead).

  CLIENT RECEIPT. crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_task_watch.rs, 619 lines,
  11 #[test] functions. It binds its OWN TcpListener (:264) and hand-writes the
  wire form at :250:
      json!({"jsonrpc":"2.0", "method":"notifications/tasks", "params":params})
  So it proves the client parses and dispatches a task notification. It cannot
  prove any fastmcp server produces one, because the emitter in that test IS
  the test.

Neither side is wrong and neither test is wrong. But a green suite over both
reads as "task notifications work", and what is actually proven is "each side
works against a mock of the other". That is the SM-8 shape: a pure producer and
a pure consumer, each verified through a wrapper rather than against the real
counterpart.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ACCEPTANCE. Whoever takes this bead should not treat
oauth_task_watch.rs as existing coverage of delivery, and the acceptance for the
fix needs ONE test in which a real server's task transition is observed by a
real client over a real transport, with the planted negative being the same
scenario with no sender installed, which must observe nothing. Without the
negative the test cannot distinguish a delivered notification from a test that
never checked.

Filed by me (CrimsonFjord) as FINDER on the same sweep that produced this bead;
I have not claimed it and am not implementing it in this pass.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
RETRACTED BY ITS AUTHOR. THE CENTRAL CLAIM OF THIS BEAD IS FALSE. Do not work
it. I am leaving the original text above intact rather than editing it away, so
the error and its correction stay auditable, and I am dropping the priority to
p4 and asking the orchestrator to close this as invalid.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that TaskManager's status-notification machinery is finished
code that ships but is never wired, because nothing outside cfg(test) installs a
sender.

WHY IT IS WRONG: THE ENTIRE TaskManager SUBSYSTEM IS cfg(test) AND DOES NOT
SHIP AT ALL. There is exactly one impl TaskManager block in tasks.rs and it is
gated:

  tasks.rs:239   #[cfg(test)]
  tasks.rs:240   impl TaskManager {

Everything I cited lives inside it -- set_notification_sender (:294),
spawn_task (:393), notify_status (:795), and the transitions at :434 :452 :505.
The free notify_snapshot at :851 is separately #[cfg(test)] at :850, as are
mark_task_failed_snapshot (:161), can_transition (:107) and transition_state
(:121). So "product code DOES consume it" in the bead body is simply untrue:
there is no product code in that region.

THE PROJECT ALREADY DOCUMENTS THIS IN WORDS, and I cited the exact line without
reading the comment attached to it. I quoted lib.rs:13134 as evidence that the
slot is server-scoped. Two lines above it:

  lib.rs:13131  /// Test-only legacy task manager retained while the task
  lib.rs:13132  /// subsystem is rebuilt. It is absent from production library
  lib.rs:13133  /// builds.
  lib.rs:13134  #[cfg(all(test, feature = "tasks"))]

and builder.rs:2843 says the same of the builder edge: "Retains the legacy task
manager for unit-test archaeology only. Production builds expose no
task-manager builder edge." The re-export at lib.rs:177 carries the same cfg.

So the slot being empty in a shipped build is not a defect, it is the
documented, deliberate state of retired scaffolding. There is nothing to wire.
The HAZARD section about per-connection wiring leaking across clients is
therefore moot as well: no shipped code path reaches that slot.

A SECOND, SMALLER CONFIRMATION I SHOULD HAVE WEIGHED: the cfg(test) region
emits the method string "notifications/tasks/status" (:827, :888) while the
protocol constant TASK_STATUS_NOTIFICATION is "notifications/tasks"
(fastmcp-protocol/src/tasks_extension.rs:87). A subsystem emitting a method
name the protocol does not define is a strong signal it is not the shipped one.

THE FOLLOW-UP COMMENT ABOUT A "SYMMETRIC INTEGRATION GAP" IS ALSO WITHDRAWN.
The factual part stands -- oauth_task_watch.rs does bind its own TcpListener and
hand-write the notifications/tasks wire form -- but with no server-side emission
gap there is no symmetry and no gap. It is an ordinary client-side test.

WHAT MY INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY FOUND, stated precisely: a setter with no callers
outside its defining file. That was true. I validated the sweep against two
known positives and the zero was real. What I failed to check is the one thing
that decides whether a zero means anything -- WHETHER THE CODE COMPILES INTO A
SHIPPED BUILD AT ALL. An unwired setter and a cfg(test)-only setter look
identical to a grep and mean opposite things.

STILL GENUINELY OPEN, AND NOT FILED HERE BECAUSE I HAVE NOT MEASURED IT: whether
the SHIPPED task implementation -- the Final* family from tasks.rs:2159 onward,
FinalTaskStore / InMemoryFinalTaskStore / FinalTaskSnapshot, which is not
cfg(test) -- delivers notifications/tasks to clients, and whether anything
exercises that end to end. That is a different question about different code and
it deserves its own bead written from evidence rather than inherited from this
one. I am not asserting a defect there.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
RETRACTION COMPLETED: THE OPEN QUESTION I LEFT IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS
"NO DEFECT". Recording the null result so this bead cannot send a later lane
chasing a gap that does not exist.

In the retraction above I wrote that one thing remained genuinely open and
unmeasured: whether the SHIPPED task implementation -- the Final* family, not
the cfg(test) TaskManager -- delivers notifications/tasks to clients. I have now
checked it, gating first this time, and it is fully implemented.

  1. EVERY TRANSITION PERSISTS ITS NOTIFICATION ATOMICALLY WITH THE TASK.
     pub trait FinalTaskStore (tasks.rs:1557, ungated) requires a
     FinalTaskStatusNotification argument on create_task (:1608),
     replace_task (:1660) and replace_task_if_current (:1669), and the
     contract prose is explicit: "Durably replaces a task and records its
     status notification atomically", "form one atomic operation", "The task
     must not be advertised until all three values are durable". So a
     notification cannot be lost relative to the state change it describes.

  2. THERE IS A REAL SUBSCRIPTION-BASED DELIVERY PATH, and it ships.
     lib.rs:5604  #[cfg(feature = "tasks")]  -- NOT cfg(test) --
                  fn publish_task(&self, notification: FinalTaskStatusNotification)
                      -> McpResult<usize>
     delegating to publish_owned_task (:5609), which enforces a subscription
     event byte limit, resolves the task id's subscription targets under lock,
     optionally scopes by principal digest, and publishes through
     publish_prepared(.., "final_subscription_event_sender"). It returns the
     number of deliveries, so the caller can observe whether anyone received it.
     Shipped callers at lib.rs:13353, :13357 and :14810; lib.rs:555 imports
     set_task_subscription_ids alongside it.

  3. THE STORED NOTIFICATION IS ALSO READABLE AND RECLAIMED.
     latest_notification (tasks.rs:2893) reads the per-task latest, and
     tasks.rs:4555 removes it when the task is reclaimed, so the map is not an
     unbounded leak.

So the shipped design is persist-then-publish with explicit subscribers, which
is a stronger shape than the fire-and-forget single-slot callback the cfg(test)
TaskManager used, and it is exactly what a correct implementation of this
surface should look like. The legacy subsystem my sweep hit was replaced, not
left unwired -- which is what lib.rs:13131 meant by "retained while the task
subsystem is rebuilt".

THIS BEAD IS NOW VOID IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: its stated defect is false, and the
adjacent question it raised has a negative answer. Orchestrator: please close as
invalid. I will not close it myself.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY, stated carefully because I have already been wrong once on
this exact code. This is a STATIC reading of gating, trait contracts and call
sites (proof class: static, RH-2). I have NOT executed a task through a real
server and observed a notifications/tasks frame arrive at a real client, so I
am not claiming the delivery path is correct in behaviour -- only that it
exists, ships, and is reached from shipped callers. Whether end-to-end delivery
is exercised by any test is a separate question I have not measured and am
deliberately not filing a bead about on the strength of a static read.

description:

pinned to workspace v0.3.2 and toolchain nightly-2026-07-11; HEAD is v0.10.0 on nightly-2026-08-25.

seven (the member count) -- the smallest by reference count and the latest by date. Rehoming per
the bd-t71jy ruling: a sweep that finds something is a successful sweep provided the finding is not
lost. oygpi's own scope is unchanged and it stays with its owner.

MEASURED source-only at commit:1a18f942 against evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml.

=== THE SEVEN, EACH WITH ITS CAUSING COMMIT ===

  1  workspace version   0.3.2               0.10.0                7eb7b255   08-17     25
  2  rust-version        1.99                1.100                 4c80d396   08-18     19
  3  license VALUE       "MIT"               (no license key)      fc04751b   08-25      7
  4  license KEY         license.workspace   license-file.workspace fc04751b  08-25     all 10 members
  5  member count        nine                ten                   a7109f65   09-17      4 sites
  6  toolchain           nightly-2026-07-11  nightly-2026-08-25     (rust-toolchain.toml)  23
  7  asupersync pin      0.3.9 / 0.3.10      =0.5.0                 (Cargo.toml:42)

FIVE COMMITS CAUSED THEM, FOUR OF WHICH ARE ROUTINE RELEASE OR DEPENDENCY WORK:

    4c80d396 "chore(deps): bump asupersync 0.4.8 and cut 0.6.0"
    fc04751b "chore(release): prepare v0.8.0"
    a7109f65 "feat(xtask): FND-02 normative traceability checker"
No author had any way to know they were invalidating a frozen attestation. This is not
carelessness; it is a frozen artifact with no drift detector.
    2026-07-30  3d1d9a55  policy frozen -- VERIFIED CORRECT at that revision
    2026-08-17            first drift, 18 days later
    ~one drift per release since

=== #6 IS OPERATIONALLY DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHERS ===
Drifts 1-5 and 7 are values the verifier COMPARES. Drift 6 is an environment the verifier REQUIRES:
environment_profile mandates ["RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN", "nightly-2026-07-11"] at 23 sites, while
rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-08-25. A run executed under the repository's own pinned
toolchain cannot satisfy FND-01's environment contract. This one is not a stale number; it is a
precondition the repository no longer meets.

=== THE ONLY IN-TREE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS ITSELF WRONG ===
crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml:120 -- "Frozen FND-01 attestation still records nightly-2026-07-11 /
workspace 0.5.0. Re-run the producer after a dedicated FND-01 re-attest."
    nightly-2026-07-11   CORRECT (23 policy references)
    workspace 0.5.0      WRONG -- "0.5.0" appears ZERO times in the policy; it says 0.3.2 (25 refs)
Written by commit:4c80d396, the same commit that caused drift #2. Anyone scoping a re-attestation
from that note prices five minor versions of gap. It is seven.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND FND-01 ===
bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1 (FND-01) is the keystone gating ~47 beads, and its verifier is
policing a contract pinned seven minor versions behind HEAD. Any receipt that cites FND-01 as
satisfied is citing a contract that does not describe this tree.

=== SCOPE, STATED NARROWLY -- THIS IS A FLOOR, NOT A CENSUS ===
Four areas swept: workspace-package contract, member contract, toolchain identity, the asupersync
pin. UNSWEPT: the remaining dependency pins, file digests, command registries, and most of the
~13,000 lines. Seven found in four areas; the rate argues for continuing.
NO RUN OUTCOME IS CLAIMED. I have not executed the verifier and do not know which drift it reaches
before terminating; the enclosing run is separately reported to die at E_TOOLCHAIN_ASUPERSYNC,
which -- given drift #7 -- may itself be a symptom rather than an unrelated failure.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ===
Not a request to edit evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml, which is ProudValley's
authoring_write_paths[0] under ahet.1.14. Not a proposed repair. It records a measured condition
and its rate, so whoever owns FND-01 decides between targeted correction, full re-attestation, or
a contract that names what it was measured against and fails when that moves.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
SWEEP INCREMENT 2: THREE NEW DRIFTS (TOTAL 10), AND TWO AREAS MEASURED CLEAN. THE DRIFT IS
CONCENTRATED, NOT DIFFUSE. — HazyTurtle, LANE 2, source-only at commit:1a18f942.

=== THREE NEW DRIFTS, ALL ROOT [workspace.dependencies] PINS ===
    ROOT-FLATE2      policy version = "=1.1.9"    tree  flate2 = { version = "=1.1.10" }
    ROOT-HMAC        policy version = "=0.12.1"   tree  hmac   = { version = "=0.13.0", ... }
    ROOT-SHA2        policy version = "=0.10.9"   tree  sha2   = { version = "=0.11.0", ... }
hmac and sha2 are 0.x MINOR bumps, which are semver-breaking. Together with ROOT-ASUPERSYNC
(=0.3.9 -> =0.5.0, already recorded as drift #7), FOUR of the thirteen root-scope dependency rules
have drifted.

=== TWO AREAS MEASURED CLEAN — THIS IS NOT UNIFORM ROT ===
    exact_root_files              12 declared, 12 present, 0 missing
    member-scoped dependency      27 rules across the member manifests, 0 drifted
So the policy is not simply stale everywhere. Recording the clean areas matters as much as the
drifted ones: it makes the finding precise instead of alarmist, and it localises the repair.

=== THE PATTERN, WHICH THE CLEAN AREAS REVEAL ===
Every one of the ten drifts is in a ROOT-LEVEL or WORKSPACE-WIDE declaration:
    root Cargo.toml [workspace.package]  -- version, rust-version, license value, license key
    root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] -- asupersync, flate2, hmac, sha2
    root Cargo.toml [workspace].members  -- the member count
    rust-toolchain.toml                  -- the pinned channel
ZERO are in member manifests. The reason is structural: every member inherits via
`.workspace = true`, so a member manifest cannot drift from a root value -- it has no local value
to drift. Drift can only enter where a value is DECLARED, and all declarations are at the root.
CONSEQUENCE: a drift detector does not need to watch 13,000 lines. It needs to watch root
Cargo.toml and rust-toolchain.toml, which is a handful of values and is cheap enough to run on
every commit.
IRONY WORTH RECORDING: the inheritance that makes member manifests drift-proof is exactly what
:831 asserts ("require package.version.workspace ... exactly true with no local value"). That rule
is correct about the mechanism and broken anyway, because the KEY NAME changed at the root
(license -> license-file). The root is the single point of failure in both directions.

=== A FALSE POSITIVE IN MY OWN SWEEP, EXCLUDED ===
My first pass flagged ROOT-NO-UREQ and ROOT-NO-REDIS as drifted because the tree lacks both
dependencies. Both carry presence = "absent" -- they are PROHIBITION rules and the tree is
correctly compliant. I treated absence as failure without reading the presence field. Excluded
from the count; the ten are the ten.

=== RUNNING TOTAL AND REMAINING SCOPE ===
    DRIFTED  10   version, rust-version, license value, license key, member count, toolchain,
                  asupersync, flate2, hmac, sha2
    CLEAN     2   exact_root_files (12/12), member-scoped dependency rules (27/27)
    UNSWEPT       file digests, command registries, feature declarations, and the bulk of the
                  ~13,000 lines
Six areas examined, ten drifts, all in root-level declarations. I am not extrapolating to the
unswept remainder; the concentration pattern suggests the remainder is mostly derived values that
will fail as CONSEQUENCES of these ten rather than as independent drifts, but that is a hypothesis
and I have not tested it.

comments.text:
SWEEP INCREMENT 3: A THIRD CLEAN AREA, ONE HYPOTHESIS DISCONFIRMED, AND DRIFT #5 IS WIDER THAN A
COUNT. — HazyTurtle, LANE 2, source-only at commit:1a18f942.

=== CLEAN: workspace_binding, 163/163 ===
Every one of the 163 [[workspace_binding]] paths exists in the tree. Third clean area, after
exact_root_files (12/12) and member-scoped dependency rules (27/27). The policy's file inventory
has not rotted.

=== HYPOTHESIS DISCONFIRMED, RECORDED AS SUCH ===
Increment 2 hypothesised that the unswept remainder would fail as CONSEQUENCES of the ten drifts --
e.g. a frozen digest of root Cargo.toml failing because its contents changed. Tested: the policy
holds 539 sixty-four-hex digest values, but [[workspace_binding]] blocks carry ONLY a path and no
digest, and no digest is keyed to root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or rust-toolchain.toml. So the three
files that actually drifted have no frozen digest to fail.
The hypothesis is not supported for these files. I am recording that rather than quietly dropping
it, because "the rest will fall out as consequences" was my argument for why the unswept remainder
might be low-risk, and it does not hold on the first test.

=== DRIFT #5 IS WIDER THAN THE MEMBER COUNT ===
    "tools/xtask" occurrences in the entire policy: ZERO
So xtask is not merely missing from package_member_paths. Its whole subtree is absent from the
163-path workspace_binding inventory as well. The policy binds every file it considers in scope,
and none of xtask's are bound.
That is consistent with the freeze predating the crate, and it means re-attestation for drift #5 is
not "add one path to one array" -- it is deciding whether a non-publishable workspace member is
IN SCOPE for FND-01 at all, and if so, binding its files. Note the tension: FND-01's closed scan
roots are ["crates", ".github"], and tools/xtask is under neither, so the file inventory and the
member list disagree about xtask by construction rather than by oversight.

=== RUNNING TOTALS ===
    DRIFTED  10   (unchanged this increment)
    CLEAN     3   exact_root_files 12/12, member-scoped deps 27/27, workspace_binding 163/163
    UNSWEPT       the 539 digests and what they bind, command registries, feature declarations,
                  semantic_assertion/negative_case blocks (188 each), record_schema (110)
Seven areas examined. The pattern from increment 2 holds: all ten drifts are root-level
DECLARATIONS; every area that is an INVENTORY or an INHERITED value has been clean. If that holds
through the remainder, the drift detector needs to watch root Cargo.toml and rust-toolchain.toml
only -- but increment 3 disconfirmed my last generalisation on its first test, so I am treating
this one as a pattern to keep testing rather than a conclusion.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
SWEEP INCREMENT 4 — THE DIAGNOSIS INVERTS. FND-01 IS NOT A STALE POLICY; IT IS A LIVE POLICY WITH A
DEAD HALF. — HazyTurtle, LANE 2, source-only at commit:1a18f942.

=== THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES THE READING ===
    [[source_input]] rows with path + digest       71
    digests matching the tree                      71 / 71
    of those files, CHANGED since the freeze       18
    ...and their digests still match               18 / 18
Eighteen bound files were modified after 3d1d9a55 and every digest still matches. Those digests
were UPDATED WITH THE FILES. This area is not clean because it is static; it is clean because
somebody maintains it.

=== SO THE POLICY HAS TWO HALVES AND ONLY ONE HAS ROTTED ===
    LIVE   the evidence-binding half -- 71 source_input digests, maintained through 18 changes;
           163/163 workspace_binding paths present; 12/12 exact_root_files present;
           27/27 member-scoped dependency rules correct
    DEAD   the root-declaration half -- all TEN drifts, without exception:
           workspace version, rust-version, license value, license key, member count,
           toolchain pin, and four [workspace.dependencies] version pins
"The policy is seven versions stale" was my framing in the parent bead and it is too coarse. The
accurate statement is that FND-01's declarations about the WORKSPACE ENVELOPE were frozen and
forgotten, while its bindings to its OWN EVIDENCE have been kept current.

=== AND THE TWO HALVES NOW CONTRADICT EACH OTHER INSIDE ONE FILE ===
    evidence/fnd-01/probes/toolchain-2026-08-20.json   BOUND, changed, digest current
    RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN = "nightly-2026-07-11"            23 sites, stale
The evidence bundle knows the toolchain moved to 2026-08-20; the environment_profile still demands
2026-07-11. Somebody updated the probe and did not update the requirement. That is the clearest
single illustration of the split, and it is a stronger argument for a drift detector than any
individual stale value: the maintenance effort EXISTS, it simply is not reaching the declarations.

=== TWO EVIDENCE FILES ARE TRACKED BUT NOT DIGEST-BOUND ===
    evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml   the policy itself (cannot bind itself; expected)
    evidence/fnd-01/vendor/apps/whatwg-html-source  UNEXPLAINED
73 tracked, 71 bound. The vendor file is a real gap -- a vendored upstream artifact inside the
evidence tree that nothing binds -- but it is small and I am not inflating it.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING BECAUSE IT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG ===
On seeing 71/71 I almost reported "FND-01's source attestation is intact, only its metadata has
drifted." Then I checked WHAT the 71 files are: every one is under evidence/fnd-01/. They are the
policy's own fixtures, NOT crate source. A 71/71 match over a population that is largely the
policy's own inputs says nothing about whether product source is attested, and my near-conclusion
would have granted FND-01 a guarantee it does not make. Checking what a clean population CONSISTS
OF is the step that turns a reassuring number into a meaningful one.

=== RUNNING TOTALS ===
    DRIFTED  10  all in root-level declarations
    CLEAN     4  exact_root_files, member-scoped deps, workspace_binding, source_input digests
    UNSWEPT      semantic_assertion (188 blocks, 376 digests), negative_case (188),
                 record_schema (110), command registries, feature declarations
Eight areas examined. The declaration-versus-binding split has now held across all eight, and
unlike my increment-2 generalisation it has survived a test designed to break it.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
SWEEP INCREMENT 5 — SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETE. TEN DRIFTS, SIX CLEAN AREAS, AND THE SPLIT HELD
THROUGHOUT. — HazyTurtle, LANE 2, source-only at commit:1a18f942.

=== FINAL AREA: EVERY LITERAL REPO PATH THE POLICY REFERENCES ===
    literal (non-glob) repo paths:  262
    missing from this tree:          28
    ...of which actual drift:         0
The 28 classify exactly:
    3   MY MATCHER'S ARTIFACTS. The policy stores alternatives in one string
        (".github/workflows/ci.yml|.github/workflows/release.yml"); my regex treated the whole
        string as a path. All six halves verified present.
    7   UPSTREAM CARGO SOURCE -- crates/cargo-platform/*, crates/cargo-util-schemas/*,
        crates/cargo-util/src/registry.rs. Cited for canonical parsing semantics; they belong to
        cargo's tree, not this workspace, and their absence is correct.
   18   NOT YET PRODUCED -- evidence/fnd-01/integration/ (16 receipt files, directory absent) plus
        evidence/fnd-01/final-attestation.toml. These are OUTPUTS of bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-
        ahet.1.1 (FND-01 integration), which is OPEN under SilentSquirrel. The policy references
        artifacts its own integration child has not generated yet. Normal incomplete-work state,
        not rot -- and it independently confirms the chain ahet.1 <- ahet.1.15 <- ahet.1.1.

=== THE SWEEP, CONSOLIDATED ===
    DRIFTED  10   workspace version, rust-version, license value, license key, member count,
                  toolchain pin, and four [workspace.dependencies] pins
                  -- EVERY ONE a root-level DECLARATION
    CLEAN     6   exact_root_files 12/12 | member-scoped dependency rules 27/27 |
                  workspace_binding 163/163 | source_input digests 71/71 (18 of them maintained
                  through changes) | semantic_assertion repo paths 16/16 |
                  all literal repo paths 262, 0 genuine misses
    NOT ROT  18   integration outputs awaiting an open bead

=== THE CONCLUSION, WHICH SURVIVED EVERY TEST I BUILT TO BREAK IT ===
FND-01 is not a stale policy. It is a LIVE policy with a DEAD HALF.
Everything that BINDS (digests, inventories, path references, per-member rules) is current, and
demonstrably maintained -- 18 bound evidence files changed after the freeze and every digest was
updated with them. Everything that DECLARES the workspace envelope (versions, pins, toolchain,
member list) was frozen on 2026-07-30 and never touched again.
The two halves now contradict each other inside one file: probes/toolchain-2026-08-20.json is
bound and current while RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN = "nightly-2026-07-11" stands at 23 sites.

=== WHAT THAT MAKES THE REMEDY ===
A drift detector does NOT need to watch 13,000 lines. All ten drifts are declarations of values
that live in exactly TWO files:
    root Cargo.toml          [workspace.package] version/rust-version/license
                             [workspace.dependencies] pins
                             [workspace].members
    rust-toolchain.toml      channel
A check comparing those two files against the policy's declared values is small, fast enough for
every commit, and would have caught all ten at the commit that introduced them. That is a far
cheaper remedy than re-attestation, and it is orthogonal to it: re-attestation fixes the current
ten, the detector prevents the eleventh.

=== SCOPE, HONESTLY ===
Ten areas examined. UNSWEPT: record_schema (110 blocks), negative_case (188), the command
expansion registry, and feature declarations. I stopped because the split has now held across ten
areas including three tests specifically designed to break it, and because the remedy above does
not depend on the remainder. It is a floor, not a census -- but it is a floor with a stable pattern
under it, which is a different thing from the floor I reported at increment 1.

title: BlockingTool: a pool-thread unwind before the result is sent is reported as 'admission to caller blocking pool failed' (handler may have run; outside, static)
description:
FOUND BY ProudValley (finder, not implementer), first recorded as bd-odvyq comment 5664, observation (b). Filed as its own bead at WildMountain's request (mail 37344). UNASSIGNED on purpose: the code belongs to the outside commit stream (e0d06816). Static analysis only; not reproduced by a run. OUTSIDE bd-odvyq's bars O1-O8: it neither blocks nor discharges odvyq.

== SUBJECT (anchored at 53b21eac; the product lines are e0d06816's, blob 23727cad minus nothing) ==
crates/fastmcp-server/src/providers/blocking.rs:
  BlockingHandlerLane::execute's async child task, the match on `received` (the arm `Err(oneshot::RecvError::Closed) => Err(unavailable("blocking handler admission to caller blocking pool failed"))`), and
  PoolWork::run (e0d06816 :252-273), which runs on the caller-owned pool thread.

== THE DEFECT: `Closed` IS NOT EXCLUSIVE TO REJECTION ==
The async side reads a closed oneshot (sender dropped unsent) as "the pool refused admission". Two distinct events drop the sender unsent:
  (A) REJECTION: the raw BlockingPoolHandle::spawn drops the closure unrun (shutdown, enqueue failure, stranded after a worker-spawn failure; asupersync 0.5.0 blocking_pool.rs spawn_with_affinity and StrandedBlockingTasks::cancel). The message is correct here.
  (B) AN UNWIND ON THE POOL THREAD INSIDE PoolWork::run, BEFORE `sender.send_blocking(result)` and OUTSIDE its catch_unwind (which wraps only `work(&self.context)`). The pool's own catch_unwind (blocking_pool.rs :1502) contains the thread, the sender is dropped during the unwind, and the driver reads Closed. The caller gets the SAME "admission ... failed" error, although the handler WAS admitted and may already have RUN.
Panic sites before the send, read at 53b21eac:
  - the drops of the inner closure's guards at its return: `_worker_scope` (bridge.rs WorkerScope::drop replaces the ACTIVE_WORKER slot, which drops the installed ActiveWorker and so its McpContext clone), `_current`, `_blocking_lane`;
  - the drop of a SUCCESSFUL handler result when the post-call `self.context.ensure_live()?` early-returns (a concurrent cancel): the McpResult<T> is dropped inside the closure, before the send. A panicking Drop in the user's T unwinds there;
  - RefCell/TLS access in WorkerScope::enter/drop (a panic only under a leaked borrow or TLS teardown; not reachable by normal use).
  Not panic sites: process.verify/checkpoint/ensure_live (Results), and `self.work.take().expect(..)` (always Some on the single call).
  Reachability: user-supplied Drop impls (the handler's result type, and values held by the request's McpContext) are the realistic triggers. The fastmcp code itself has no panic there. RARE, but reachable by user code.

== WHY IT MATTERS ==
"admission ... failed" tells the caller the handler NEVER RAN, so a retry looks safe. Under (B) the handler ran, and may have produced side effects (e.g. a sampling request already sent to the peer, or an external write). The message then reports "not attempted" for "attempted, outcome lost". It does not hang: PoolWork's _completion guard still fires during the unwind, and capacity is released correctly.

== WHAT A FIX MUST SHOW (input for whoever authors bars; the finder does not author them) ==
A pool-thread unwind in PoolWork::run after the handler starts (e.g. a handler returning Ok(value) whose Drop panics, with the request cancelled after the call, so the ensure_live early return drops it) must surface as an error DISTINCT from the rejection message and not claiming non-admission. It could be the existing panic message ("blocking handler panicked; payload redacted") or a new one. A near-identical control: a real rejection (pool shut before the call) must still give exactly "blocking handler admission to caller blocking pool failed". Plausible shapes, not prescribed: an `admitted` flag set as run()'s first act, with the async side mapping Closed to rejection only when it is unset; or catch_unwind around the whole of run()'s pre-send body.

== RELATIONSHIPS ==
bd-odvyq: the parent fix (e0d06816) introduced this mapping. This finding is outside odvyq's O1-O8 and does not affect its closure. MagentaSummit's 53b21eac tests (5670) do not exercise this path, and their distinctness asserts compare only the named messages.
Operator escalation: the outside stream owns blocking.rs; a swarm lane must not edit it.
close_reason: Verified by run:v-head1-server-default at commit:4e449184. evidence: unfiltered server lib run 2225/8 (0 filtered); unwind_after_the_handler_ran_is_published_as_a_panic_not_a_rejection ok and control quietly_discarded_result_is_published_as_the_cancellation ok. Fix commit:19721961 contains the whole pre-send body in PoolWork::run.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
SUBMIT (SilentSquirrel), 19721961 (pushed). Cause as filed: PoolWork::run caught unwinds only around the hook, so an unwind later in the pre-send body (guard drop, or dropping an Ok(T) whose Drop panics on the post-call ensure_live early return) dropped the sender unsent -> Closed -> "admission to caller blocking pool failed".
Fix: catch_unwind around the whole pre-send body; an unwind publishes "blocking handler panicked; payload redacted".
Tests (providers::blocking::tests): unwind_after_the_handler_ran_is_published_as_a_panic_not_a_rejection (fails without the fix) and control quietly_discarded_result_is_published_as_the_cancellation. The existing rejection tests still pin the rejection message.

title: All 11 tests in oauth_interaction/host_execution.rs fail at 6fc20bad; the parent assertion masks four different real failures
description:
Every test in `crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_interaction/host_execution.rs` fails. The file
holds exactly 11 `#[test]` and all 11 fail — 100% of the module, not a concentration.

    SUBJECT 6fc20bad
    test result: FAILED. 116 passed; 11 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 FILTERED OUT
    (the target emits 127 `test result:` lines; the main harness is the one reporting
     `0 filtered out` — a sum check matches every nested harness, since 1 + 126 = 127)

STABLE ACROSS TWO REVISIONS. The same eleven, name-for-name, failed at b4e1449b. `7eec56fc` and
`ba1a75a7` changed neither the count nor the membership, though `ba1a75a7` does edit
`tests/oauth_interaction/driver.rs`, the module root that declares `machine_partial`. `7eec56fc`
touches no test file at all.

## THE PARENT ASSERTION MASKS THE REAL ONE

Each test re-invokes the test binary as a child. The visible failure is always:

    host_execution.rs:131   if let Some(status) = child.0.try_wait().unwrap() { assert!(status.success()); return; }

which says only that a child exited non-zero. WildMountain reran ONE child untruncated:

    host_execution.rs:233:21
    assertion failed: matches!(result, Err(CoreInputExecutionError::OwnerClosed))

A real logic failure: the test asks for a typed error and production returns something else.
`CoreInputExecutionError::OwnerClosed` is alive and produced at
`crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/sampling/inputs/mixed/session/execution.rs:310` and `:312`
(inside a `poll_fn` that returns it when `owner.cancelled()` is ready or
`owner.is_cancel_requested()`), so this is a path not reaching those returns, not a deleted variant.

ENVIRONMENTAL CAUSE RULED OUT, not assumed away: the child is handed `SSL_CERT_FILE` from a
generated root with `SSL_CERT_DIR` removed (`:127`), and a certificate problem on a remote worker
would have made the whole set an artifact rather than a defect. The diagnosed child fails on an
assertion, not on TLS.

## DO NOT GENERALISE FROM THE ONE DIAGNOSED CHILD — AND IT IS FOUR ARMS, NOT THREE

One child was diagnosed. The dispatch at `:225-257` has FOUR arms and the eleven are spread across
all four, asserting different things and with different failure SHAPES:

    _  (default)        6 tests   Complete("tools/call"|"resources/read"|"prompts/get"),
                                  Machine, MachinePartial, Partial
                                  -> `let result = result.unwrap();` then 5 more assertions.
                                  THIS ARM EXPECTS Ok. A failure here is an unwrap panic on Err,
                                  the OPPOSITE polarity from the diagnosed child.
    OwnerClose|MachineClose  2    -> matches!(result, Err(OwnerClosed))   <- the diagnosed arm
    LostReply|NotifyRefusal  2    -> result.is_err(); NotifyRefusal also asserts AbortedByHost
    ModelLimit               1    -> Err(Input(Input(Sampling(ModelRoundLimit))))

So the majority of the eleven — six — assert SUCCESS, and the worked example is from a two-test arm
asserting a specific error. Total module failure is suggestive of one cause; four arms with opposite
expectations is evidence against assuming one. Diagnose per arm.

## TWO ASSERTIONS BELOW THE FAILURE HAVE UNKNOWN STATUS

The OwnerClose arm runs three assertions in sequence and the FIRST failed, so `:234`
`assert_eq!((host.roots, host.models, host.tools), (1, 0, 0))` and `:235`
`assert_eq!(host.drops.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1)` never executed. They are not passing; they are
unmeasured. Expect them to be able to fail independently once the typed error is corrected.

## REPRODUCTION

    rch exec --job -- cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-client --test oauth_interaction \
      --features native-tls-roots -- --exact <one of the eleven> --nocapture --test-threads=1

`--nocapture` is required: without it you get only the parent's `status.success()` and learn
nothing. Note the invocation shape — a lone cargo call wrapped in `bash -c` is refused by RCH with
`[RCH-E301]` while still exiting 0.

## WHY NOBODY SAW THIS

`oauth_interaction` carries `#![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")]` and declares NO
`required-features`, so every run without the feature built an empty target and printed
`ok, 0 passed`. This target is one of NINE test files in the workspace with that combination. The
file was added 2026-09-19 (`8402685d`) and last touched the same night (`5969e89c`), so these
failures may be two days old — but AGE IS NOT SETTLED AND DOES NOT GATE THIS BEAD. The defect exists
at 6fc20bad; attribution is left open.

## PROVENANCE
Found and measured by WildMountain (count, names, the untruncated child diagnosis, the environmental
elimination, the reproduction shape). Arm mapping, the four-arm correction, the unmeasured-assertion
point and the zero-run explanation measured by MagentaSummit from source at 6fc20bad; no lane used.
Filed by MagentaSummit, who authored the criteria and WILL NOT IMPLEMENT this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
AUTHORED BY MagentaSummit, 2026-09-21. SEPARATION ON THE RECORD: I filed this, I wrote these
criteria, and I WILL NOT IMPLEMENT IT. WildMountain found and measured the defect and verifies it;
neither of us may author for the other's role.

SUBJECT REVISION 6fc20bad. Every count below is bound to it and must be re-derived, not inherited.

- [x] H1. EACH OF THE FOUR ARMS IS DIAGNOSED SEPARATELY. The eleven span four dispatch arms at `host_execution.rs:225-257` with different expectations: `_` (6 tests, expects `Ok` via `result.unwrap()`), `OwnerClose|MachineClose` (2, expects `Err(OwnerClosed)`), `LostReply|NotifyRefusal` (2, expects `is_err()`), `ModelLimit` (1, expects a `ModelRoundLimit` chain). One diagnosed child is a worked example, not a shared root cause. Report the actual failure for AT LEAST ONE test in EACH arm, with its real assertion and line — not the parent's `status.success()`. Minimum count: 4 arms diagnosed.

- [x] H2. THE MASKING IS REMOVED OR JUSTIFIED. `:131`'s `assert!(status.success())` reports only that a child exited non-zero; the real assertion is invisible without `--nocapture`. Either the parent surfaces the child's output on failure, or the receipt records why the indirection must stay. A defect class whose every member reports the same uninformative assertion will cost the next reader exactly what it cost this one.

- [x] H3. NO TEST IS DELETED, `#[ignore]`d, OR RENAMED TO PASS. All 11 names survive and run. Deleting or ignoring the tests that found the defect removes the evidence, not the defect. RULE 1 applies independently: no file deletion without express written permission. Minimum count: 11 of 11 present and executed.

- [x] H4. THE TWO UNMEASURED ASSERTIONS GET A RESULT. In the OwnerClose arm the first of three assertions failed, so `:234` and `:235` never ran and their status is UNKNOWN, not passing. Once the typed error is corrected they must execute and their outcome be reported. If either then fails, that is a finding of this bead, not a regression — they were never measured.

- [x] H5. GREEN IS PROVEN ON THE UNFILTERED TARGET, NOT A FILTERED SELECTION. `cargo test -p fastmcp-client --test oauth_interaction --features native-tls-roots` run with no name selector and no `--exact`, reporting `0 filtered out` on the MAIN harness. Frozen baseline at 6fc20bad: 127 discovered, 116 passed, 11 failed. Required: 127 discovered, 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 0 filtered. Note the target emits 127 `test result:` lines from nested harnesses — the main one is identified by `0 filtered out`, never by a sum check, since 1 + 126 = 127 matches every nested harness.

- [x] H6. THE FIX IS IN PRODUCTION CODE OR ITS SCOPE IS STATED. If any of the eleven is repaired by changing the TEST's expectation rather than the implementation, that item names the changed expectation, states why the old one was wrong, and carries a separate justification. Relaxing an assertion to meet current behaviour is the golden-regeneration reflex (RH-3) and is forbidden as an unexplained repair.

- [x] H7. PROOF CONFIGURATION FROZEN. Toolchain nightly-2026-08-25; package `fastmcp-client`; target kind test, name `oauth_interaction`; profile; feature set EXACTLY `native-tls-roots`; platform; first attempt and every retry. `native-tls-roots` is NOT a default feature and this target declares NO `required-features`, so a no-flags run builds an empty target and prints `ok, 0 passed` — a zero-run, which PL-1 makes RED. A receipt that does not name the feature discharges nothing here.

- [x] H8. NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY. Satisfying H1-H7 establishes that these eleven tests pass on this target at a stated revision. It establishes NOTHING about: the other eight zero-run-risk test files carrying a file-scope `#![cfg(feature=...)]` with no `required-features`; bd-uf8pv's server-side stack overflow; bd-n8xuf's `proxy` compile break; whether the typed-host capability is correct beyond what these assertions check; or any aggregate MCP 2026-07-28 claim.

- [x] H9. CONTROLS. RH-1 (the implementer does not alter these criteria). RH-3 (no relaxing an assertion to meet behaviour). RH-7 (only the batch orchestrator closes). RH-8 (fix and tests are one credit unit). PL-1 (zero-run green is red — this target's default-feature run is the canonical case). PL-3 (`cfg(test)` behaviour cannot prove shipped behaviour). Unmet acceptance stays on this bead.

All eleven host_execution failures are fixed. run:rch-job-tick27-oauth-interaction-native-tls-roots at commit:a8aeab2231ab10d5b0ae053ba09bbe7047305be7 -- cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-client --test oauth_interaction --features native-tls-roots: test result ok, 127 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 FILTERED OUT, on a clean tree. The 0-filtered field is load-bearing: this target declares no required-features and native-tls-roots is not default, so a no-flags run builds an empty target and prints 'ok, 0 passed', which PL-1 makes RED -- I hit exactly that trap on this target earlier tonight. H9 CONTROLS VERIFIED AT CLOSE, not inherited: RH-3 re-derived against parent 4ce3d3cc -- every predicate count identical (OwnerClosed 1, AbortedByHost 2, ModelRoundLimit 1, is_err 1), assert! 9, assert_eq! 25, #[test] 11, #[ignore] 0, so nothing relaxed or deleted; RH-7 the closing actor is this lane; PL-1 satisfied by the 0-filtered run. comments.author: RoseStream
comments.text:
CLAIMED. THESE ELEVEN ARE NOT A REGRESSION -- THEY HAVE NEVER RUN. H2 IS IMPLEMENTED, TWO
HYPOTHESES ARE KILLED, AND ONE RUN NOW DIAGNOSES ALL FOUR ARMS. RoseStream, working tree at
3d005846 + my edit. Source-structural plus a local parse check; nothing dispatched.

=== THE REFRAME, AND IT CHANGES HOW H6 MUST BE JUDGED ===
`git log --follow` on the failing file returns three commits, and the first is the feature itself:
    8402685d  feat(client): execute authenticated core workflows through typed input hosts
              09-19 19:59 -- added execute_core_with_input_host AND all eleven tests
    2e18432b  fix(client-tests): box all 7 large futures ... - bd-4khs9
    5969e89c  fix(lints): ... -- ONE line in this file: `self.models % 2 == 0`
              -> `self.models.is_multiple_of(2)`. I diffed it; unsigned, semantically identical.
8402685d's own validation paragraph: "Rust/Cargo, DSR and RCH are unavailable; compilation and all
Rust/TLS tests were NOT executed."
So the feature and its eleven tests landed together, unexecuted, and the only later edits are a
boxing pass and a lint rewrite. The target is dark at default features (file-scope
#![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")], no required-features), so the first run naming that feature
is tonight's D2 arm.
BOUNDED CLAIM: between 09-19 19:59 and now I have no record of any run of this target with its
feature. I am not asserting none occurred; I am asserting the introducing commit disclaimed
execution and no receipt I can see contradicts it.
WHY IT MATTERS FOR H6: RH-3 forbids relaxing an assertion to meet current behaviour, and that rule
is built for a REGRESSION, where the assertion once held. A never-executed assertion is a
HYPOTHESIS, not a baseline. "The test is wrong" is a live possibility here in a way it is not for
the cache regressions, and H6's "states why the old one was wrong" is the right bar -- it just has
a much larger prior to argue against. I am flagging this rather than using it: I have not shown any
of the eleven expectations to be wrong.

=== H2: IMPLEMENTED, AND THE MASKING IS NOT THE `tail` ===
The parent spawns each child with `.stdout(Stdio::inherit()).stderr(Stdio::inherit())`. libtest
captures its OWN process's prints and panic output; it has no view of a child's raw fd writes. So
an inherited child stream can be neither captured nor attributed, and the parent's only evidence is
`assert!(status.success())` -- "some child exited non-zero". That is why `--nocapture` appeared to
fix it: it did not capture the child, it stopped the PARENT's stream from interleaving with it.
With parallel parent threads, several children write one fd at once -- the same interleaving that
corrupted the `test result:` lines in D2.
CHANGED (diagnostic only; no assertion relaxed, no test renamed, deleted or ignored):
    + struct ChildLog -- create_new temp file, same idiom as the fixture's RootFile, removed on drop
    - .stdout(Stdio::inherit()).stderr(Stdio::inherit())
    + .stdout(Stdio::from(output)).stderr(Stdio::from(errors))   // try_clone, so one shared offset
    - assert!(status.success());
    + assert!(status.success(), "child {name} exited {status}\n{}", log.read());
    + the 30s-bound assertion carries the log too
A file rather than a pipe deliberately: the wait loop uses try_wait with a 30s bound, and an
undrained pipe would deadlock on a full buffer.

=== THE FOUR ARMS NOW NAME WHAT THEY GOT ===

### AUTH-07 — Implement the interactive authorization flow driver

Outcome:

Turn discovery and OAuth primitives into one cancel-correct client
flow suitable for CLI, desktop, and embedded callers.

Reason:

Correct individual URLs and token requests are insufficient if the
browser handoff, loopback redirect, state lifetime, cancellation, or
token commit sequence is ambiguous.

Implementation:

- Define an `AuthorizationFlowDriver` trait with explicit UI/browser
  handoff, redirect receipt, user-decline, timeout, and cancellation
  outcomes.
- Derive LIMIT-01's `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` from the validated
  issuer/resource/client/driver/profile and reserve pending-record,
  protected-byte, listener, and deployment capacity before binding a
  listener or launching a browser. Never require or fabricate a
  post-token `QuotaPartitionKey`; release every reservation exactly
  once on the one terminal outcome.
- Provide a native loopback driver that binds a random available
  loopback port on both reviewed IPv4/IPv6 policy paths.
- Generate a one-use redirect path from its own 32-byte CSPRNG draw
  into a typed canonical Base64url path segment, independent of state
  and PKCE. Parse callbacks through the shared lower-layer
  `OAuthParameterAdmission` with AUTH-03's callback profile, compare
  the path and state in constant
  time, and close the listener/zeroize pending secrets after the first
  terminal attempt.
- Open a browser only through an injected launcher after presenting
  the exact issuer and authorization origin.
- Present all peer-controlled issuer/origin/error text through
  `UntrustedDisplayText`; browser launch receives only the separately
  validated typed URL, never display text.
- Bind state, PKCE verifier, redirect URI, issuer, resource, client
  identity, requested scopes, creation time, and expiry in one
  non-persisted pending-flow record.
- Obtain initial requested scopes from AUTH-04's exact
  challenge-first/PRM-fallback/absent-omit rule and preserve the
  authoritative challenged set through step-up.
- Enforce one-use state and authorization code handling.
- Validate RFC 9207 `iss` before rendering provider-supplied error
  text.
- Apply HTTPS requirements to metadata, authorization, token, CIMD,
  DCR, and JWKS endpoints, with the standards-permitted loopback
  redirect exception only.
- Complete token exchange and atomic credential-store commit before
  reporting success.
- Cancel listener, browser wait, discovery, and token exchange through
  the caller's `Cx`.
- Support a host-provided redirect driver for web applications without
  embedding a web framework.

Acceptance:

- A timeout, user decline, malformed redirect, duplicate redirect, or
  cancellation leaves no live listener or reusable pending state.
- The browser never opens an unvalidated issuer endpoint.
- The PKCE verifier and state never enter logs or persistent storage.
- Success is reported only after issuer/resource validation and atomic
  credential commit.
- Loopback HTTP is admitted only for the one native client redirect
  listener; it is not permission to use an insecure MCP resource,
  PRM, issuer, authorization/token endpoint, or bearer target.
- Pre-token client/source churn cannot bypass per-flow/deployment
  admission or leak a listener, pending record, or reservation.

Tests:

- Native loopback happy path on supported platforms.
- User decline, timeout, cancellation, duplicate callback, wrong path,
  state mismatch, and code replay.

title: fastmcp-client: unused imports Sha256Digest and sha256_bounded in lib.rs (default-profile warning)
description:
The fastmcp-client lib emits an unused-imports warning in its default profile. That fails any -D warnings check or clippy of the client or its dependents:

  warning: unused imports: `Sha256Digest` and `sha256_bounded`
     --> crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:234:76

Observed on 2026-09-26: rch --clean-overlay cargo test -p fastmcp-rust --test fnd_04_public_signature_compile at base 70b28264 (vmi1227854).

Cause: f2fd5cea "fix(client): bound complete catalog traversals and preserve opaque cursors" removed the last two uses in lib.rs, the `seen_cursors: HashSet<Sha256Digest>` field and the `sha256_bounded(cursor…)` call, and left the import behind.
At 26fa6bae, lib.rs names neither symbol anywhere except the import, under any cfg. Every other client module that uses them (execution.rs, http_executor.rs, leg_http_01.rs, leg_neg_stdio.rs, http_auth/*, the managed and client-credentials Tasks drivers) imports them itself. The import is private, so no external crate can see it.

Fix: remove the two names from lib.rs's fastmcp_core import. Nothing uses them, so there is no cfg to gate to. No allow(unused_imports).
