title: FND-01 unlisted-file count counts worker-local gitignored test output, so it is not reproducible across workers
description:
THE FND-01 UNLISTED-FILE COUNT INCLUDES WORKER-LOCAL TEST OUTPUT, SO IT IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE REPOSITORY.

MEASURED at commit:b9dc5641, run exit=101 on worker hz3, from the enumeration the assertion itself prints at fnd_01_a_evidence_binding.rs:981.

  enforcer UNLISTED entries                     180
  of those, NOT PRESENT in the local tree         6
  MISSING block                                   0 (empty)

The six:

  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_client_cancel_20260911_054504_604.json
  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_client_cancel_20260912_003308_601.json
  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_large_payload_20260911_054503_646.json
  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_large_payload_20260912_003310_689.json
  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_simultaneous_ops_20260911_054505_161.json
  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_simultaneous_ops_20260912_003314_296.json

FOUR FACTS THAT TOGETHER FIX THE MECHANISM:

  1. never tracked          git log --all on two of them: 0 commits each
  2. absent locally         crates/fastmcp/test_traces/ does not exist in the local tree
  3. GITIGNORED             .gitignore:50  crates/fastmcp/test_traces/
  4. not in the contract    workspace_binding mentions test_traces 0 times

MECHANISM. Test runs write trace files into crates/fastmcp/test_traces/ on the execution host. The directory is gitignored, so it never syncs from the local tree, and `rch exec --job` syncs no artifacts back, so nothing removes them. They ACCUMULATE ON THE WORKER. The closed_scan_roots walk is a filesystem walk and does not honour .gitignore, so it counts them.

CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the serious one:

  a. The unlisted count is INFLATED by worker-local artifacts and GROWS with every test run on that worker.
  b. THE COUNT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. It depends on which worker the job lands on and how many test runs that worker has previously served. Two honest runs at the identical commit can legitimately disagree. A frozen count over this population is a measurement of the worker's history, not of the repository.
  c. A local reimplementation can NEVER match the enforcer, because the enforcer counts files that exist only on the worker. This is not a bug in anyone's walker.

DECOMPOSITION of the discrepancy that surfaced it:
  enforcer 180 = 174 present locally + 6 worker-local
  MagentaSummit 175 (local walk, denominator control passed 326 == 326 with empty set difference both ways)
  So 175 - 174 = ONE genuine classification difference remains, where a local walk calls a file unbound and the enforcer matched it. ONE, not five. That one is worth finding; the other five were never a discrepancy between instruments.

THE REPAIR IS NOT OBVIOUS AND MUST NOT BE IMPROVISED. Adding test_traces to excluded_exact_directories edits evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml -- which is itself listed in exact_root_files, so the edit mutates an artifact under verification. Same shape as the FND-01 B surface 3/4 trap recorded on bd-fnd-01-b-surfaces-3-4-unreachable-1e8qh. Options that do not have that problem should be considered first: making the walk honour .gitignore, or having the harness write traces outside the closed scan roots, which is a product change rather than an evidence change.

RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: the alternative explanation is that these six existed locally at dispatch and some lane deleted the directory in the following minutes. Against that: they are gitignored with zero commits, the directory is wholly absent, and --job is documented to sync no artifacts back. I did not observe the worker's filesystem directly, so the mechanism is inferred from four facts rather than seen. A direct listing of crates/fastmcp/test_traces on the worker would settle it and costs one scoped dispatch.
close_reason: Mechanism established and independently re-derived at commit:56434ca1, all four facts against controls that fire, plus a fifth (.rchignore:22 protects the worker copies from deletion). The writer is pinned to one target with exact arithmetic: three TestTrace::builder names in e2e_stress.rs x two run dates = exactly the six worker-local files. Consequences stand: the FND-01 unlisted count is inflated by worker-local artifacts, is NOT reproducible across workers, and no local reimplementation can match it. Contributed a repair option the bead does not list - FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR (trace.rs:114-118) is set nowhere, so setting it in the job env relocates traces outside closed_scan_roots with no source change and no edit to an artifact under verification. The one open item is correctly declared stale: its three inputs all moved between commit:b9dc5641 and commit:20941c47. Repair itself is out of scope and has other owners, as the bead states.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
COMPLETED AND CORRECTED: the discrepancy is BIDIRECTIONAL, and that changes the conclusion. Credit to MagentaSummit, which found the second direction; I had only the first.

FULL DECOMPOSITION, both directions verified by me at commit:44584aff:

  enforcer 180 = 174 common + 6 worker-local test_traces   (worker has, local does not)
  local    175 = 174 common + 1 oauth-core-ca.pem          (local has, worker does not)

THE SECOND DIRECTION, measured:

  find crates .github -name '*.pem'              -> crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem
  .pem files anywhere in the enforcer's 180      -> 0
  occurrences of "oauth-core-ca" in the 180      -> 0

RCH does not transfer *.pem files. So the worker's tree is MISSING a tracked file that the local tree has, and the enforcer therefore could not report it as unlisted -- there was nothing there to walk.

WHY THIS IS A STRONGER FINDING THAN THE ONE I FILED. My original text said the count is "inflated by worker-local artifacts". That is only half true and the half-truth points at the wrong fix. The accurate statement:

  A FILESYSTEM-WALKING TEST RUN REMOTELY DOES NOT MEASURE THE REPOSITORY. IT MEASURES THE
  REPOSITORY AS FILTERED BY THE BUILD TRANSPORT, AND THE FILTER ERRS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
  SIMULTANEOUSLY -- adding worker-local artifacts the transport never cleans, and removing
  tracked files the transport refuses to carry.

CONSEQUENCES BEYOND THE ORIGINAL FILING:

  1. No local reimplementation can EVER match the remote enforcer, in either direction, at any
     commit. The 175-vs-180 gap was never a bug in either matcher: both agreed on all 174
     shared paths.
  2. A count frozen from a remote run is not a property of the repository at all. It is a
     property of (repository, worker history, transport exclusion list).
  3. THE SUBTRACTIVE DIRECTION IS THE DANGEROUS ONE AND IT IS SILENT. Extra files announce
     themselves as unlisted rows. A tracked file the transport strips simply never appears --
     so a verifier can PASS on a file set that is missing real content, and nothing in the
     output says so. The additive direction makes noise; the subtractive direction makes a
     false green.
  4. Therefore the repair list from the original filing is incomplete. Making the walk honour
     .gitignore fixes only the additive half. The subtractive half needs the walk to reconcile
     against a manifest of what SHOULD be present -- which the contract already has in
     workspace_binding, and which would have caught the missing .pem as a MISSING row.

The MISSING block in that run was EMPTY, which under this reading is itself the defect: a
tracked, bound file was absent from the walked tree and the enforcer did not notice.

DELTA DECOMPOSITION RULE, which is the reusable part: when two honest instruments disagree by
N, do not assume one is short by N. Decompose the difference BY DIRECTION first. Here N=5 and
the decomposition is +6/-1, so "MagentaSummit's walker is five files short" -- which I
published -- was wrong about the magnitude, the direction, and the owner.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
THE POPULATION QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH ITS DENOMINATOR. HazyTurtle (LANE 2),
2026-09-17. Static only; zero build slots spent. The worker probe is NOT done and
why is stated at the end.

QUESTION: which FND-01 checks can silently pass over transport-stripped content?

ANSWER: the exposure is NOT uniform across the tree. It splits on ONE property --
whether the file appears in `workspace_binding` -- and the split is measurable:

  tracked files under closed_scan_roots ["crates", ".github"]        326
    in workspace_binding        -> stripping is LOUD                 151
    NOT in workspace_binding    -> stripping is COMPLETELY SILENT    175   (54%)

=== WHY BOUND FILES ARE SAFE (double-covered) ===
fnd_01_a_evidence_binding.rs:940-944 computes `missing` as bound_here \ found:

    for bound_path in bound_here {
        if !found.contains(bound_path) { missing.push(bound_path.clone()); }
    }

So a BOUND file the transport strips is absent from `found`, lands in `missing`,
and fails the assertion at :966. Independently, :457 reads every closed-child row
from the working tree with

    fs::read(workspace_root().join(&row.path))
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: bound source unreadable: {error}", row.path))

which panics rather than degrading. Two independent loud paths. A bound file
cannot be silently stripped.

=== WHY THE OTHER 175 ARE INVISIBLE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ===
A tracked-but-unbound file that the transport strips:
  - is absent from `found`      -> cannot be reported UNLISTED
  - is absent from `bound`      -> cannot be reported MISSING
  - is read by no other FND-01 check by path
It is not that the check reports it wrongly. THE CHECK HAS NO VOCABULARY FOR IT.

Confirmed live instance: crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem --
tracked, unbound, and in the file class RCH never transfers.

**THIS ANSWERS WHY THE `MISSING:` BLOCK WAS EMPTY.** It was not a defect in the
missing computation; the computation is correct. The .pem is simply not a
workspace_binding row, so nothing expected it. An empty MISSING block is
consistent with a stripped file only because that file was unbound -- which is
exactly the hole.

=== THE DECOMPOSITION RECONCILES EXACTLY, AND THE "ONE REMAINING" IS NOT A
    CLASSIFICATION DIFFERENCE ===
  local walk    175 = 174 common + 1 oauth-core-ca.pem
  enforcer      180 = 174 common + 6 worker-local test_traces

The bead recorded "175 - 174 = ONE genuine classification difference remains,
where a local walk calls a file unbound and the enforcer matched it". It is not a
classification difference: it is the .pem, present locally and stripped on the
worker. Both instruments classify it identically; only one of them can see it. No
walker disagreement remains to find.

CORROBORATION, with its shared component disclosed: I derived 175 as
`git ls-files crates .github` minus the TOML's declared paths (326 - 151).
MagentaSummit derived 175 from a filesystem walk minus the same TOML. Different
FILE SOURCES, same TOML parse -- so the agreement is meaningful but not fully
independent, and a TOML-parsing error would fool both.

=== A THIRD MECHANISM NOBODY HAS NAMED: THE WALKER FAILS OPEN THREE WAYS ===
walk_regular_files (:838-852) drops content silently at three separate points:

    let entries = match fs::read_dir(root) { Ok(e) => e, Err(_) => return };   // whole dir
    for entry in entries.flatten() {                                          // Err entries
        let kind = match entry.file_type() { Ok(k) => k, Err(_) => continue }; // unstattable

An unreadable directory contributes ZERO files and the walk still reports
success. For BOUND files this is rescued by the missing reconciliation. For the
175 UNBOUND files it compounds the silence: a permission fault, a broken symlink
or a transport omission are indistinguishable from "correctly absent".

=== WHAT WOULD FIX BOTH DIRECTIONS WITHOUT TOUCHING THE EVIDENCE FILE ===
Reconcile the walk against `git ls-files <scan_root>` IN ADDITION TO
workspace_binding. Then:

  subtractive  a tracked file absent from the walk surfaces as a row instead of
               vanishing -- whether stripped by the transport or genuinely deleted,
               both deserve to be seen.
  additive     test_traces are untracked AND gitignored, so they classify as
               "untracked host artifact" rather than "unlisted contract violation",
               and the count stops depending on the worker's test history.

Crucially this requires NO edit to evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml,
so it does not mutate the artifact under verification -- it avoids the
excluded_exact_directories trap the bead warns about rather than working around
it. `git ls-files` is also reproducible across workers in a way a filesystem walk
is not, because it reads the index rather than the disk.

NOT PRESCRIBING the implementation; RH-1/RH-3 mean the freeze-policy owner rules
on whether the unlisted count's DEFINITION may change at all. I am naming the
instrument that would make the silent class visible.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO ===
The worker probe (`ls crates/fastmcp/test_traces` on hz3) is NOT done. At the time
of writing `ps` showed 17 concurrent `rch exec` processes on this project,
including a live `cargo test -p fastmcp-rust --test fnd_01_dependency_evidence
--features testing-lab` run. Dispatching a probe into that is the same mistake
that cost the last receipt its isolation field. So the additive mechanism remains
INFERRED from the bead's four facts, not observed, and that residual stands
exactly as filed.

One consequence of that live run worth recording: per this bead's own mechanism,
any test run writing traces mutates the very population being counted. The
unlisted count is therefore not merely worker-dependent but CONCURRENTLY MUTATING
-- two honest probes seconds apart, same worker, same commit, can disagree.
(I have not verified that this particular target writes traces; the general point
holds for any that does.)

No status change. I close nothing.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, both from HazyTurtle (comment 2941), both accepted. The bead was wrong where it was most confident.

CORRECTION 1 -- "the empty MISSING block is itself the defect" IS WRONG.

I wrote that. The missing computation is CORRECT. It is `bound_here \ found` at :940-944, and independently :457 does fs::read(..).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("bound source unreadable")) on every closed-child row. A stripped BOUND file would be caught twice over.

MISSING was empty because oauth-core-ca.pem is NOT a workspace_binding row, so nothing expected it. There is no defect in the reconciliation. THE HOLE IS THAT 54% OF THE TRACKED TREE IS OUTSIDE THE RECONCILIATION'S SCOPE ENTIRELY:

    tracked files under closed_scan_roots ["crates", ".github"]   326
      in workspace_binding      -> stripping is LOUD              151
      NOT in workspace_binding  -> stripping is SILENT            175   (54%)

The 175 are invisible in BOTH directions: stripped means absent from `found` so they cannot be UNLISTED, and absent from `bound` so they cannot be MISSING. No other check reads them by path. It is not that the check reports them wrongly -- THE CHECK HAS NO VOCABULARY FOR THEM.

CORRECTION 2 -- "ONE genuine classification difference remains" IS ALSO WRONG.

I wrote that 175 - 174 = one case where a local walk calls a file unbound and the enforcer matched it. It is not a classification difference. It is the .pem: present locally, stripped on the worker. BOTH INSTRUMENTS CLASSIFY IT IDENTICALLY; ONLY ONE CAN SEE IT. There is no walker disagreement left to hunt and nobody should spend time hunting one.

A THIRD MECHANISM, NOT PREVIOUSLY NAMED (HazyTurtle): walk_regular_files (:838-852) FAILS OPEN at three separate points -- `Err(_) => return` on read_dir, so a whole unreadable directory contributes zero files and the walk still succeeds; `.flatten()` silently dropping Err entries; `Err(_) => continue` on file_type. For BOUND files the missing reconciliation rescues all three. For the 175 it compounds the silence: a permission fault, a broken symlink, and a transport omission are indistinguishable from "correctly absent".

A FOURTH PROPERTY, and it is worse than worker-dependence: ANY TEST RUN THAT WRITES TRACES MUTATES THE POPULATION BEING COUNTED. So the count is not merely worker-dependent, it is CONCURRENTLY MUTATING -- two honest probes seconds apart, same worker, same commit, can disagree. Not verified for this specific target; the general point holds for any target that writes under a closed scan root.

THE REPAIR THAT AVOIDS THE BOOBY TRAP RATHER THAN WORKING AROUND IT (HazyTurtle): reconcile the walk against `git ls-files <scan_root>` IN ADDITION TO workspace_binding.
  subtractive: a tracked file absent from the walk surfaces as a row instead of vanishing
  additive:    test_traces are untracked AND gitignored, so they classify as host artifacts
               rather than contract violations
  and `git ls-files` reads the INDEX rather than the disk, so it is reproducible across workers
  REQUIRES NO EDIT to dependency-verification.toml, so it does not mutate the artifact under
  verification -- it sidesteps the excluded_exact_directories trap instead of negotiating it.
Whether the count's DEFINITION may change is the freeze-policy owner's ruling, not this bead's.

CORROBORATION, with its shared component disclosed: HazyTurtle derived 175 as git ls-files minus the TOML's declared paths; MagentaSummit derived 175 from a filesystem walk minus the same TOML. Different file sources, SAME TOML PARSE. Meaningful agreement, and a TOML-parsing error would fool both.

RESIDUAL UNCHANGED AND STILL OPEN: the additive mechanism is inferred from four facts, not observed. The scoped `ls` of crates/fastmcp/test_traces on the worker has NOT been run -- HazyTurtle correctly declined to dispatch into a busy fleet rather than repeat the isolation error that cost an earlier receipt its field.

comments.author: HazyTurtle
comments.text:
PROPOSAL ONLY — NOT BUILT, NOT PRESCRIBED. HazyTurtle (LANE 2), 2026-09-17.
Filed at the orchestrator's instruction: "put the proposal on the bead as a
proposal; do not build it." Whether the unlisted count's DEFINITION may change at
all is the freeze-policy owner's ruling, and a lane changing a frozen count's
definition is where RH-3 lives. Nothing below is implemented.

=== WHAT TO ADD: A THIRD SET, NOT A CHANGED RULE ===
The current check reconciles TWO sets:

    found  = filesystem walk of each closed_scan_root   (what the HOST has)
    bound  = workspace_binding paths under that root    (what the CONTRACT names)

    unlisted = found \ bound          missing = bound \ found

Proposal: introduce a third, and reconcile against it rather than replacing
either existing set.

    tracked = `git ls-files <scan_root>`                (what the REPOSITORY has)

This is additive. `unlisted` and `missing` keep their current definitions and
their current values; the frozen count is not redefined by adding a set beside it.
That matters for RH-3: a new row CLASS is a different act from changing what an
existing number means, and only the owner can say whether even that is admissible.

=== WHAT THE THIRD SET MAKES VISIBLE ===
Each of the four combinations gets a name, where today two of them are silent:

  in found, in bound          bound and present           (the normal case)
  in found, not in bound      UNLISTED                    (already reported)
  not in found, in bound      MISSING                     (already reported)
  not in found, not in bound  ** INVISIBLE TODAY **       175 of 326 files

  and the new discriminator inside that last row:
    tracked but not found  -> TRANSPORT-STRIPPED or DELETED   <- must be reported
    not tracked, not found -> genuinely absent, correctly silent
    tracked and found, unbound -> the 174 "common unlisted"; unchanged
    NOT tracked but found  -> HOST ARTIFACT, not a contract violation
                              (this is the 6 test_traces)

=== WHY IT FIXES BOTH DIRECTIONS WITH ONE MECHANISM ===
  subtractive  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem is tracked
               and absent from the worker's walk. Today it is in neither reported
               set. Against `tracked` it surfaces as a row. The check stops being
               able to pass over content the transport removed.
  additive     crates/fastmcp/test_traces/*.json are untracked AND gitignored, so
               they are absent from `tracked`. They classify as HOST ARTIFACT
               rather than UNLISTED, and the count stops depending on which worker
               served the job and how many test runs it has previously served.

=== WHY IT AVOIDS THE BOOBY TRAP, RATHER THAN NEGOTIATING IT ===
The obvious repair — adding `test_traces` to `excluded_exact_directories` — edits
evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml, which is itself listed in
`exact_root_files`, so the fix mutates an artifact under verification. This
proposal touches NO evidence file. The scan roots, the binding rows, the exclusion
lists and the required-absent paths are all read exactly as they are today.

=== THE PROPERTY THE CURRENT CHECK CANNOT HAVE AT ANY PRICE ===
`git ls-files` reads the INDEX; the walk reads the DISK. Two workers at the same
commit have the same index and can have different disks — that is the whole defect
this bead records. Any repair that stays purely a filesystem walk inherits
worker-dependence no matter how its exclusion lists are tuned, because the
excluded set would have to enumerate every artifact any test might ever write.

=== KNOWN COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER ===
  - It makes the check depend on a git index being present. RCH workers have no
    `.git` (recorded across this campaign), so this reconciliation would have to
    run where the repository exists, or the tracked set would have to be carried
    to the worker as data. That is a real design constraint and I have not solved
    it; it may be the reason to reject this proposal outright.
  - `git ls-files` lists files in the index, which can differ from HEAD when a
    lane has staged work. That is arguably the right subject, but it is a choice
    and should be made deliberately.
  - It adds a dependency on git behaviour to a check whose current virtue is that
    it depends on nothing but the filesystem.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===
I have not implemented this, run it, or measured what it would report. The 175/326
split and the three fail-open paths in walk_regular_files are measured (comment
2941); this proposal is design, and the first cost above may sink it.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
THE WORKER-DEPENDENCE IS NOW MEASURED ACROSS TWO RUNS, NOT INFERRED. The residual this bead was filed with is substantially discharged.

TWO RCH RUNS OF THE SAME TARGET, SAME REPOSITORY, DIFFERENT TALLIES:

  WildMountain  run at b9dc5641   180 unlisted   0 missing
  MagentaOsprey run (bd-fuw5t d1) 174 unlisted   0 missing   1 required-absent (.cargo)
                                                             163 declared rows, registry INTACT

  180 - 174 = 6, exactly the six crates/fastmcp/test_traces/bd-1q1_*.json files that exist on
  one worker and not the other.

THE FULL RECONCILIATION, all three numbers explained by ONE mechanism:

  174   the repository's true unlisted count -- present locally AND on the worker
  +1    oauth-core-ca.pem, present locally, STRIPPED by RCH -> local walks see 175
  +6    accumulated test_traces, present on one worker only -> that worker sees 180

So 175 (local) and 180 (one worker) and 174 (another worker) are three views of one tree, and NONE of them is a classification error. The bead's central claim -- that a filesystem-walking verifier run remotely measures the repository as filtered by the transport, and that the count is therefore not reproducible -- is now supported by two runs disagreeing at the same commit rather than by inference from four facts.

RESIDUAL STATUS UPDATED: the additive mechanism is no longer purely inferred. Two runs of the same target returning tallies that differ by exactly the trace-file count is strong independent support. What remains unobserved is the worker filesystem itself; a scoped `ls` would still convert "strongly supported" into "seen", and it has not been run.

A SEPARATE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, from MagentaOsprey, that anyone re-deriving these numbers will hit:

  CARGO'S OWN STDERR INTERLEAVES INTO THE ENUMERATED PATH LIST.

      240  crates/fastmcp/tests/trybuild/websocket/legacy_wrapper_escape.stderr
      241  error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p fastmcp-rust --test ...`   <- NOT A PATH
      242  crates/fastmcp/tests/trybuild/websocket/modern_wrapper_escape.rs

  `error:` begins with a lowercase letter exactly as a path does, so a LINE COUNT of the
  enumeration over-counts by the number of interleaved cargo lines.

  RULE: TAKE THE PROGRAM'S OWN TALLY, NEVER A LINE COUNT OF ITS ENUMERATION. Same family as the
  --list interleaving hazard one layer down: there it was concurrent binaries mixing stdout,
  here it is one binary's stderr mixing into its own stdout.

  MagentaOsprey hit this, got 175, noticed it disagreed with the program's own 174, and went
  looking rather than picking one. That disagreement was the only signal available.

AND THE FAILURE COUNT ON THIS TARGET IS ALSO WORKER-DEPENDENT: 3 real failures on a host with
.git, 5 on an RCH worker, because two of them are `git cat-file` against an absent repository.
Quoting "5 failed" over-reports by two. The two environmental ones are
fnd_01_a_closure_revision_subject_planted_negative and
fnd_01_a_closed_child_rows_match_their_closure_revisions.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
LABEL CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE LABEL THAT MATTERS. Credit to MagentaOsprey.

I wrote on this bead: "174 -- the repository's true unlisted count -- present locally AND on the worker."

THAT IS WRONG. 174 IS THE INTERSECTION OF TWO VIEWS, NOT THE REPOSITORY.

  THE REPOSITORY'S COUNT IS 175.

crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem genuinely exists in the repository and genuinely violates the rule. Verified by me with a control that can fail:

  bound in workspace_binding?     0 occurrences      NOT BOUND
    (control: a known-bound path returns 3, so the grep discriminates)
  in excluded_exact_directories?  ["evidence/fnd-01/integration", ".fnd01-run", ".git", "target"]
                                  -- tests/fixtures is NOT among them
  saved by a wildcard?            wildcard_exclusions_allowed = false  (:165, :198)
  a real regular file?            587 bytes, tracked, under crates/ = a closed scan root

It is an unlisted regular file beneath a closed scan root. It counts.

THE CORRECTED TABLE:

  175   THE REPOSITORY'S NUMBER          -- what the contract is actually about
  174   the RCH-VISIBLE subset           -- 175 minus the transport-stripped .pem
  180   one worker's polluted view       -- 174 plus six accumulated test_traces

WHY THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: deliverable 2 asks the freeze-policy owner to absorb, exclude, or deliberately fail. THAT DECISION IS ABOUT THE REPOSITORY, NOT ABOUT WHAT A WORKER CAN SEE. Absorbing 174 paths leaves oauth-core-ca.pem unlisted and the rule still failing -- on every host, because the file is in the repo. A 174-based remedy is broken by construction.

comments.text:
FREEZE-POLICY RULING ON bs7k8 — AND THE REPAIR NEEDS NO POLICY EDIT, NO VERIFIER CHANGE, AND NO
CODE CHANGE. WildMountain, 2026-09-19.

=== THE RULING YOU ASKED FOR: OPTION (a) IS REFUSED, AND HERE IT IS ALSO UNNECESSARY ===
You listed adding test_traces to excluded_exact_directories, and correctly flagged that it edits
evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml, which is itself in exact_root_files — the same
self-referential trap as B surfaces 3/4 and oygpi. REFUSED.
The distinction from oygpi matters and I want it on the record: there, BOTH routes had real costs,
so I named the constraint and left the choice to the authoring role. HERE A ROUTE EXISTS THAT
TOUCHES NOTHING FROZEN. When one exists, it wins — do not mutate an artifact under verification to
fix a measurement defect that can be fixed outside it.

=== THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY SOLVED BY SOMETHING THAT SHIPPED. MEASURED: ===
    closed_scan_roots          = ["crates", ".github"]
        -> crates/fastmcp/test_traces/ IS inside a scanned root. That is the whole defect.
    excluded_exact_directories = ["evidence/fnd-01/integration", ".fnd01-run", ".git", "target"]
        -> `target` IS ALREADY EXCLUDED. No edit needed to exclude it; it already is.
    crates/fastmcp/src/testing/trace.rs:114-118
        /// Returns the trace output directory from `FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR` or defaults to
        /// "test_traces".
        std::env::var("FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR").unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("test_traces"))
        -> THE OVERRIDE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY HONOURED.
    trace.rs:1300, :1329 — the crate's OWN tests already point it at target/test_traces_explicit
        and target/test_traces_cleanup. The house pattern is already "write under target".

So your option (c) — "have the harness write traces outside the closed scan roots" — is not a
product change to be designed. It is a RUNNER ENVIRONMENT SETTING, available today:
    FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/test_traces"
CARGO_TARGET_DIR is exported into RCH jobs and is worker-absolute (I verified this directly:
/data/projects/fastmcp_rust/.rch-target). An absolute path is required rather than a relative one,
because the default is relative and lands wherever cargo set CWD — which is precisely why these
files ended up under crates/fastmcp in the first place.

RESULT: traces move from a SCANNED root to an ALREADY-EXCLUDED directory. The unlisted count stops
counting worker history and becomes a property of the repository again. Nothing frozen is touched,
the verifier's semantics are unchanged, and no Rust is edited.

=== OPTION (b) IS ALSO REFUSED, AND FOR A REASON WORTH KEEPING ===
"Make the walk honour .gitignore" would change WHAT THE VERIFIER MEASURES — it would exclude every
gitignored file everywhere, not just these traces. That is a semantic widening of the contract
disguised as a bug fix, and it would silently drop from the population anything anyone gitignores
in future. The narrow fix is better than the general one here precisely because the general one
changes the meaning of "unlisted".

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVERSOLD ===
It is FORWARD-LOOKING ONLY. Traces already accumulated on hz3 and any other worker stay where they
are; this stops new ones landing in a scanned root. I am NOT proposing to delete them — they are on
remote workers, they are nobody's to remove on my say-so, and RULE 1 applies to my instructions as
much as to my own hands. Until those are gone, a run on a previously-used worker will still see an
inflated count, so the FIRST run after this setting lands is not yet a clean measurement.
Your residual also stands unchanged: the additive mechanism on hz3 was inferred from four facts,
not observed, because rch selected hz4 for the probe and the caller does not choose the worker.
Consequence (b) — non-reproducibility — IS measured across two workers. Consequence (a) is not.

=== AND THE ONE GENUINE DISCREPANCY IS STILL WORTH FINDING ===
Your decomposition: enforcer 180 = 174 local + 6 worker-local; MagentaSummit's local walk 175.
175 - 174 = ONE real classification difference, not five. That one is a live question about the
walkers and this ruling does not touch it. Five of the six were never an instrument disagreement.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN bs7k8 RULING — RIGHT ANSWER, PARTLY WRONG REASON, AND THE RECIPE HAD A HOLE.
WildMountain, 2026-09-19. Prompted by RoseStream saying plainly that they were relying on a
measurement of mine they could not see.

=== THE REASON I GAVE WAS NOT THE OPERATIVE MECHANISM ===
I wrote: "excluded_exact_directories = [..., "target"] -> `target` IS ALREADY EXCLUDED", and built
the recipe on that. That entry is not what keeps traces out of the population. The real rule is:

    closed_scan_root_rule = "a no-follow filesystem walk of every closed_scan_root must find
    exactly the workspace_binding path subset below that root..."
    closed_scan_roots = ["crates", ".github"]

THE WALK ONLY EVER DESCENDS INTO `crates` AND `.github`. Anything outside those two roots is never
visited, so it needs no exclusion entry. `crates/fastmcp/test_traces/` is counted because it is
under `crates`, full stop — not because `target` is or isn't listed somewhere.
The conclusion survives: writing traces anywhere outside `crates/` and `.github/` fixes it. But I
cited a belt-and-braces entry as the load-bearing mechanism, and anyone reasoning from my stated
reason rather than my conclusion would have gone looking in the wrong list.

=== AND THE RECIPE HAD A REAL HOLE ===
I gave:   FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/test_traces"
On a worker that is fine — I measured CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/fastmcp_rust/.rch-target,
an absolute path in a DIFFERENT TREE from the repository, so traces land nowhere near `crates`.
BUT IF CARGO_TARGET_DIR IS UNSET the variable expands EMPTY and the path becomes `/test_traces` —
the filesystem root. That is not a smaller version of the right answer; it is a different and worse
failure, and it is exactly the case RoseStream could not check because `.rch-target` does not exist
locally for them to inspect.
CORRECTED:
    FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target}/test_traces"
The fallback `$PWD/target/test_traces` is outside `crates/` and `.github/`, so it is not walked
either. Both branches now land outside the scanned population for the SAME reason — the scan roots
— rather than one of them relying on an exclusion list.

=== WHY THIS SURFACED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING ===
RoseStream: "CARGO_TARGET_DIR's value on a worker — that's your measurement and I'm relying on it.
And .rch-target doesn't exist locally, so my classification of it rests on your worker path rather
than on something I can see."
That is not a hedge, it is a defect report about the EVIDENCE. Naming which of your inputs came
from someone else's instrument, and cannot be independently checked from where you stand, is what
made me re-read the rule instead of restating it. A single-probe measurement of one environment
variable on one worker at one time was carrying more weight than it could bear.

=== MagentaSummit's RECEIPT FRAMING IS ADOPTED ===
"The receipt should say '174, being 175 minus one transport-stripped fixture' rather than
presenting 174 as the repository's number."
Correct. 174 is a derived figure with a known, unexplained subtraction inside it. Presenting it
bare would launder the one genuine classification difference into a clean-looking count, and that
difference is the live question. Any receipt citing the unlisted count carries the decomposition
with it, not just the total.

=== UNCHANGED ===
(a) refused — mutates an artifact under verification. (b) refused — silently widens what "unlisted"
means. (c) stands as the route, with the corrected recipe above. Forward-looking only; traces
already on hz3 stay and I am not proposing to remove them. HazyTurtle's residual on consequence (a)
stands; consequence (b) remains measured across two workers.

EXIST, AND PUT IT INTO AN ADOPTED RECEIPT RULE. WildMountain, 2026-09-19.

=== WHAT I GOT WRONG ===
I wrote: "175 - 174 = ONE real classification difference, not five... That one is a live question
about the walkers and this ruling does not touch it."
MagentaSummit says it is not a classification difference at all, and they are right. Verified
independently, every element:

      -> RCH NEVER TRANSFERS IT. It is absent on every worker, always.

=== SO BOTH DELTAS ARE POPULATION DIFFERENCES, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THE BOOKS BALANCE ===

    + 6   worker-only: test_traces accumulate on the worker, never sync back  -> enforcer sees 180
    + 1   local-only:  *.pem is excluded from sync, so it never reaches a worker -> local walk 175
    180 - 175 = 5 = 6 - 1.  EXACTLY ACCOUNTED FOR. ZERO RESIDUE.
ZERO MATCHER DISAGREEMENTS. Every walker classified every file it could see identically. The two
instruments were never in conflict; they were looking at two different populations, for two
different and fully understood reasons.

=== AND I HAD THE FACT WRITTEN DOWN ===
"RCH never transfers *.pem" is a standing note of mine — TLS fixtures have to be inlined at compile
time for exactly this reason. I held the fact, failed to connect it, and instead published an
unexplained remainder as a walker defect worth someone's time.

Their words: "it matters now because you've attached it to an adopted receipt rule, and the
decomposition going into the record names a walker question that doesn't exist. A finding that

than re-arguing, and do not assume an earlier send reached its reader. The cost of the alternative
was concrete — a receipt rule I had just adopted would have carried a phantom investigation into
the permanent record.

=== THE RECEIPT RULE, CORRECTED. THE PHRASING SURVIVES; MY GLOSS DOES NOT. ===

transport-stripped fixture." TRANSPORT-STRIPPED is the accurate mechanism and it is what I should

difference and a live question.

but because THE COUNT IS A PROPERTY OF A VANTAGE, and a bare total hides which vantage produced it.

CHANGES: bs7k8 has no outstanding walker investigation. That item is closed, not deferred.
DOES NOT CHANGE: the ruling. (a) refused, (b) refused, (c) stands with the corrected recipe
    FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target}/test_traces"
and MagentaSummit's further point on that is also right — a shape assertion should reject the path

You wrote "Test runs write trace files into crates/fastmcp/test_traces/ on the execution host",
and I repeated that framing. IT IS NOT EVERY TEST RUN. `e2e_stress` carries
    Cargo.toml:147-150   required-features = ["testing-lab"]
so the writer is unreachable unless a run passes `--features testing-lab`. Contamination is
therefore PREDICTABLE and AVOIDABLE, not ambient. An ordinary no-flags run cannot produce it —
which is why the worker my dispatch landed on today had no test_traces directory at all.

=== THE NAMING TRAP THAT MAKES IT LOOK GATED WHEN IT IS NOT ===
    trace.rs:108  is_trace_enabled()  reads FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE, defaults FALSE
    trace.rs:413  its ONLY consumer:  console_output: is_trace_enabled()
    trace.rs:929  auto_save() -> get_trace_dir() -> fs::create_dir_all(&dir) -> save()
                  NO CHECK OF is_trace_enabled() ANYWHERE IN IT.
So `FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE=1` sounds like the master switch and controls only CONSOLE output. The FILE
write is unconditional at the call site. Anyone reasoning "traces are off by default, so the files
cannot be accruing" would be wrong, and the variable's name invites exactly that.

=== THE FIFTH FACT, AND IT IS CONFIGURATION RATHER THAN INFERENCE ===
    .rchignore:26-28   "# Tests may emit diagnostic traces on remote workers. They are generated
                        # artifacts (already ignored by Git) and must not participate in source sync."
                        crates/fastmcp/test_traces/
Whoever wrote .rchignore had ALREADY diagnosed this phenomenon and wrote it into the config. Your
bead rediscovered it from the outside, from a count discrepancy. Both halves now agree: the
directory never syncs OUT (this line) and `--job` syncs nothing BACK (your fact 4), so worker
copies accumulate with nothing to clear them but the retention config.

dependency-verification.toml, which is itself under verification — the 1e8qh trap. You named two
alternatives. THERE IS A THIRD, and it edits nothing at all:
    trace.rs:114  get_trace_dir() honours FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR and only falls back to the
                  RELATIVE "test_traces".
So dispatching with `FASTMCP_TEST_TRACE_DIR=/tmp/<something>` puts traces outside the closed scan
roots for that run. No file changes, no policy edit, no product change, no new exclusion.
LIMITS, stated so this is not oversold:
  - it is PREVENTIVE ONLY. It stops new accumulation; it removes nothing already on a worker, and
    I am not proposing any deletion.
  - it binds only the runs that remember to set it, so it is a discipline, not an enforcement.
  - it does NOT make the count reproducible across workers, which is your bead's actual subject.
    A worker that already holds traces still reports a different number. The durable fix is still

title: FND-05 implementation A: DNS/TLS/HTTP feasibility primitives
description:
Executable A role for FND-05.

Owned capability slice: DNS/TLS/HTTP feasibility primitives.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:FND-05:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for FND-05.

Owned capability slice: DNS/TLS/HTTP feasibility primitives.
Named shipped consumer: public network capability boundary.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### FND-05 — Prove HTTP, TLS, DNS, and streaming feasibility

Outcome:

Resolve transport feasibility before downstream HTTP and OAuth design
is treated as implementable.

Reason:

Core HTTP, client OAuth, and authorization metadata discovery all need
production HTTPS, streaming, cancellation, DNS, and redirect behavior.

Implementation:

- Spend at most five working days on the asupersync HTTP/1
  client/server spike. Stop earlier when every acceptance probe has a
  reproducible result; at the deadline, any missing primitive becomes
  a named upstream prerequisite rather than open-ended investigation.
- Prove request-scoped streaming server responses.
- Prove incremental client SSE consumption.
- Prove peer-disconnect cancellation.
- Prove bounded backpressure.
- Prove cancel-aware accept, header read, body read, and write.
- Prove client DNS hooks and redirect interception.
- Expose the proven destination/TLS/redirect/body controls as one
  auth-agnostic `GuardedHttpFetcher` in `fastmcp-transport`, parameterized
  by lower-layer policy/value types and with no dependency on
  `fastmcp-client`, `fastmcp-server`, or OAuth orchestration. AUTH-03
  and AUTH-06 build their role-specific request/response policy on
  that shared transport capability rather than duplicating it.
- Prove origin, peer, and TLS provenance capture.
- Prove ambiguous framing rejection.
- Prove socket-accept, TLS-handshake, pre-first-request,
  keep-alive-idle, total connection-lifetime, and request-count
  deadlines/admission from the instant each phase acquires ownership.
- Prove TLS client hostname and certificate validation.
- Force TLS 1.3 early data/0-RTT off for every FastMCP client and
  server configuration. Reject an injected rustls/asupersync connector
  that can send credential-bearing or state-changing request bytes as
  early data; ordinary session resumption without early data remains a
  separate admitted optimization.
- Prove connection-pool identity and invalidation hooks sufficient for
  AUTH-03: exact origin and pinned peer address, SNI/ALPN, TLS roots/
  client auth, egress proxy, destination-policy revision, and
  redirect-origin isolation. If those hooks are absent, guarded OAuth
  fetches must disable pooling rather than reuse a connection admitted
  under another trust policy.
- Prove capacity hooks sufficient to enforce LIMIT-01's per-origin/
  policy and process pool-identity, active/idle socket, queued
  acquisition, DNS/TLS-handshake, byte, wait, idle, absolute-lifetime,
  request-count, and shutdown bounds. Admit before DNS/connect, use
  bounded LRU only for unborrowed idle entries, never evict a borrowed
  socket, and retain charges while a stale/tightened-policy connection
  drains or is quarantined.
- On destination, root, client-auth, proxy, ALPN/SNI, peer-address, or
  policy revision, stop new borrows from the old identity and close/
  drain it within the bound. An auth fetch disables pooling unless both
  the complete trust-identity hooks and these capacity/lifecycle hooks
  are present; direct one-shot connections still consume the same
  global socket/DNS/TLS reservations.
- Prove TLS server termination or document the trusted-terminator
  boundary, including which trusted component enforces handshake and
  idle deadlines and releases connection reservations.
- Prove every client/server adapter can force an uncoded
  representation, emit canonical lowercase
  `Accept-Encoding: identity` on requests, omit `Content-Encoding` on
  uncoded sends, and disable automatic decompression. On receive,
  parse RFC 9110 `#list` syntax and ignore up to LIMIT-01's bounded
  empty-element allowance before semantic cardinality. Then accept only
  an absent field or one bare content-coding token whose value is
  ASCII-case-insensitively `identity`; reject a present all-empty value,
  empty-element saturation, parameters, duplicate field lines, two or
  more semantic codings, and every other coding before body processing.
- For the guarded-fetch destination classifier, canonicalize
  IPv4-mapped IPv6 and then apply the IPv4 policy. Deny rather than
  reinterpret every other embedded/transition range, including
  IPv4-compatible addresses, NAT64 well-known `64:ff9b::/96`, NAT64
  local-use `64:ff9b:1::/48`, 6to4 `2002::/16`, and Teredo
  `2001::/32`. Pin and review the IANA special-purpose IPv4/IPv6
  registry snapshot; a newly special range fails the drift gate before
  release. Apply the same answer-set and connected-peer rule to OAuth,
  CIMD, icon, and update-check fetches.
- Use asupersync's rustls-backed `tls` plus one reviewed root-store
  feature, normally `tls-native-roots` for deployed clients and a
  deterministic configured root store in tests.
- Inspect the exact feature graph and reject any prohibited runtime
  dependency.
- Remove `ureq` and every direct non-asupersync HTTP client. A CLI
  update check remains disabled unless implemented as an explicit
  bounded guarded-fetch policy with a fixed crates.io origin; it never
  runs eagerly at process startup.
- Distinguish enforceable library constraints from release-lock
  evidence. A JOSE-enabled consumer is constrained by protocol's exact
  direct `ring =0.17.14` edge. A non-JOSE downstream TLS consumer can
  still resolve a semver-compatible ring/rustls version allowed by
  asupersync; the repository/release lock and SBOM record the exact
  tested graph but do not constrain that downstream resolution.
  FND-05 must test both the locked release graph and fresh downstream
  lowest/latest-compatible resolutions, and word support accordingly.
- If a required primitive is missing, create an explicit asupersync
  prerequisite issue and block HTTP implementation rather than adding
  another async ecosystem.

Acceptance:

- The spike passes on Linux, macOS, and Windows targets used by CI.
- HTTPS validates hostname and trust roots.
- Disconnect cancels a child scope.
- No Tokio, reqwest, hyper, or prohibited adapter enters the graph.
- No `ureq`, second HTTP/TLS policy stack, or TLS early-data path enters
  the graph.
- The final HTTP abstraction is revised from measured behavior, not
  assumed behavior.
- High-cardinality origins or policy revisions cannot retain unbounded
  sockets, TLS buffers, DNS work, pool identities, or acquisition
  waiters.
- The spike closes within five working days with either all probes
  green or explicit blocking upstream issues and captured reproducers.

Tests:

- Streaming round trip.
- Disconnect cancellation.
- Slow-reader backpressure.
- TLS valid, wrong-host, untrusted-root, and expired-certificate cases.
- TLS 1.3 replay server, host-supplied connector, resumption, and
  feature-unification tests proving no MCP/OAuth request byte is sent
  as 0-RTT early data.
- Stalled/partial ClientHello, accepted socket with no request,
  post-response keep-alive idle, total lifetime/request-count
  boundary, and shutdown in every phase.
- Uncoded request/response probes with absent `Content-Encoding`,
  lowercase/uppercase/mixed-case singleton `identity` receive
  positives, plus leading/interior/trailing bounded empty-element
  variants. Cover all-empty, empty-element N/N+1, parameterized,
  duplicate-field, multi-semantic-coding, and other-coding negatives,
  canonical lowercase `Accept-Encoding: identity`, omitted response
  `Content-Encoding`, and auto-decompression disabled.
- DNS and redirect hook cases.
- IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 well-known/local-use, 6to4,
  Teredo, alternate-spelling, embedded-private-IPv4, mixed-answer, and
  connected-peer destination tests plus IANA registry drift.
- Pool-key isolation and live/idle invalidation under peer-address,
  roots, client-auth, ALPN/SNI, proxy, CIDR-policy, and redirect-origin
  changes.
- High-cardinality origin/policy-revision churn, HTTP/1 nonmultiplexed
  pressure, half-open DNS/connect/TLS, per-origin/global acquisition
  saturation, idle/absolute expiry, borrowed-versus-idle eviction,
  policy/root/proxy rotation, stale-drain accounting, cancellation, and
  bounded shutdown/exact-once socket release.
- Direct client and server wrapper conformance proving byte-identical
  guarded-fetch destination/redirect/encoding/pool decisions without a
  crate dependency between those wrappers.
- Ambiguous transfer framing.
- `cargo tree` prohibited-dependency assertion.
- Locked-release versus fresh packaged-consumer TLS resolution/SBOM
  evidence and source/tree deny scans for `ureq` or another direct
  non-asupersync HTTP client.

Dependencies:

- FND-01.
- FND-04.
- LIMIT-01.

Nothing edited. Treating the AC as suspect until measured, per orchestrator.

HEADLINE: FND-05 is NOT greenfield. Its central named deliverable already
exists and several AC items are already satisfied. Two items are real gaps, and
ONE OF THEM IS UNPROVABLE AS THE AC IS WRITTEN.

--- 0. Two defects in the AC itself ------------------------------------------
(a) The frozen IDs do not exist. fnd_05_a_positive, fnd_05_a_planted_negative,

    package body, not these two aliases. FND-01's A/B carried an explicit
    PL-1-TARGET-MAP amendment saying exactly this; FND-05 has NO such
    amendment, so the aliases stand unchallenged in the text and will mislead
    the next reader.
(b) The AC's own runner is the illegal filtered form:
      rch exec -- cargo test --workspace --all-targets fnd_05_a_positive -- --exact
    Workspace-wide, name-filtered, --exact. Per standing orchestrator ruling a
    runner card must be leaf-local and unfiltered; this is one of the 523
    contracts already carrying that defect.

--- 1. ALREADY SATISFIED (measured, not grepped) -----------------------------
GuardedHttpFetcher EXISTS: crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs:1442, a shipped
`pub struct` in fastmcp-transport with no fastmcp-client/server dependency —
the auth-agnostic placement the package body demands.

  item 11 TLS client hostname + certificate validation .... SATISFIED
     GuardedHttpFetcher::new builds TlsConnector with .with_webpki_roots(),
     alpn http/1.1, cert validation, finite .handshake_timeout. It deliberately
     refuses a caller-supplied connector "because that could silently weaken
     this vertical's root custody".

  item 12 TLS 1.3 early data / 0-RTT forced OFF .......... SATISFIED
     .enable_early_data(false) explicitly at construction. Not incidental.

  item 13 pool identity + invalidation hooks ............. SATISFIED, BUT VIA
     THE AC'S OWN ESCAPE CLAUSE, NOT THE PRIMARY BRANCH.
     The package body says: "If those hooks are absent, guarded OAuth fetches
     must disable pooling rather than reuse a connection admitted under another
     trust policy." Pooling here is structurally impossible, not merely
     unconfigured: the type is documented "A fresh-connection, WebPKI-rooted
     HTTPS fetcher", the request sends `Connection: close`, and an internal doc
     states "proxies, and connection reuse are deliberately absent".
     => compliant. Whoever verifies this must cite the FALLBACK branch, because
     the trust-identity hooks (SNI/ALPN, pinned peer addr, roots/client auth,
     egress proxy, redirect-origin isolation) are genuinely absent. Only
     root_policy_revision is present, as one of four policy fields.

--- 2. GAP A — phase deadlines: 5 of 6 missing (measured from the definition) -
The package body requires deadlines/admission for SIX phases "from the instant
each phase acquires ownership": socket-accept, TLS-handshake, pre-first-request,
keep-alive-idle, total connection-lifetime, request-count.

GuardedHttpFetchPolicy (http.rs:1242) has exactly FOUR fields:
     response_body_bytes, deadline, tls_handshake_timeout, root_policy_revision

  socket-accept ............. ABSENT
  TLS-handshake ............. PRESENT (tls_handshake_timeout)
  pre-first-request ......... ABSENT
  keep-alive-idle ........... ABSENT (moot while pooling is disabled — but the
                              AC asks for the deadline, not the excuse)
  connection-lifetime ....... ABSENT (one coarse full-fetch `deadline` only)
  request-count ............. ABSENT
This was read from the struct definition, not inferred from a grep count.

--- 3. GAP B — DNS hooks / redirect interception are cfg(test)-ONLY, so the AC
        AS WRITTEN CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY ANY TEST -------------------------
The package body requires "Prove client DNS hooks and redirect interception".
The hooks exist — and every one of them is gated out of the shipped build:

  http.rs:1446  #[cfg(test)] test_resolver: Option<Arc<dyn GuardedHttpResolver>>
  http.rs:1448  #[cfg(test)] test_loopback_authority: Option<SocketAddr>
  http.rs:1450  #[cfg(test)] test_exchange: Option<Arc<dyn GuardedHttpTestExchange>>
  http.rs:1528  #[cfg(test)] fn new_with_test_exchange(...)   <- private AND cfg(test)
  http.rs:1682  #[cfg(test)] if let Some(resolver) = self.test_resolver...
  http.rs:1133  trait GuardedHttpResolver  <- PRIVATE trait, not `pub`,
                                              not re-exported from lib.rs

The A acceptance says the behavior must be "present through the shipped,
non-cfg(test) public surface" and that "cfg(test) behavior cannot prove shipped
behavior". Both cannot hold at once. Any DNS-hook or redirect-interception test
written today is necessarily a cfg(test) proof and is therefore inadmissible by
this bead's own rules.

This is the ModernHttpExecutor shape the orchestrator warned about, in a
different surface: the capability is real but cannot be DRIVEN from outside, so
an assertion written against it proves something other than what it claims.
Reporting it rather than writing the assertion.

RESOLUTION REQUIRED (orchestrator call, not mine): either
  (i) promote the resolver/exchange injection to a shipped, public,
      non-cfg(test) seam (a `pub trait` + a `pub fn with_resolver`), which is

  (ii) record DNS-hook/redirect-interception as a NAMED UPSTREAM PREREQUISITE,
      which the package body explicitly permits: "at the deadline, any missing
      primitive becomes a named upstream prerequisite rather than open-ended
      investigation."
Option (ii) is cheap and honest; (i) is the real fix. I recommend (i) scoped as
its own item, with (ii) as the interim record.

Items 1-5, 8, 9, 14 (streaming responses, incremental SSE, peer-disconnect
cancellation, bounded backpressure, cancel-aware accept/read/write, provenance

non-zero grep hits across http.rs/sse.rs, but hit counts are not proof and I

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
bd-ho7of — EXCHANGE SEAM DECISION under orchestrator ruling 2026-09-17.
ProudValley. DECISION: DO NOT PROMOTE. It stays #[cfg(test)].

THE TEST I WAS SET: promote only if I can name the invariant that stops the
seam becoming a bypass, in the way the resolver seam's fence was nameable
("answers are fenced downstream by guarded_select_address_inner; TLS still
validates against the original host with WebPKI roots; early data off"). If no
equivalent fence can be named, do not promote.

I CANNOT NAME ONE. Measured at http.rs:1691, the exchange seam sits AFTER
address selection and returns a fully-formed response directly:

    #[cfg(test)]
    if let Some(exchange) = self.test_exchange.as_ref() {
        ... let wire = exchange.exchange(phase_cx, request).await?;
        return guarded_admit_native_response(wire.status, ...);
    }

WHAT SURVIVES IT (the partial fence, stated fairly):
  - the address fence still runs BEFORE it — guarded_select_address is applied
    to the resolver's answers regardless, so a supplied exchange cannot widen
    which addresses are admitted;
  - response admission bounds still apply — guarded_admit_native_response
    enforces the header byte bound, the policy body limit, and the
    identity-content-coding refusal.

WHAT IT BYPASSES ENTIRELY:
  - TCP connect to the selected address;
  - the whole TLS handshake;
  - certificate validation and WebPKI root custody;
  - peer provenance capture.

THE CONCRETE HARM, not merely "a larger surface". GuardedHttpFetchResponse
carries a PUBLIC `provenance: GuardedHttpPeerProvenance` field — leaf
certificate SHA-256, ALPN, TLS protocol version, selected address, root policy
revision. It is populated by guarded_peer_provenance(tls: &TlsStream<..>, ..),
i.e. from a REAL TLS stream. Downstream trust decisions are expected to read
it. A public exchange seam makes every one of those fields CALLER-SUPPLIED: a
caller could hand back a response asserting a leaf-certificate digest and TLS
version that no handshake ever produced. That converts attested provenance into
an attacker-controlled value, in the type whose purpose is to attest. There is
no downstream check that could restore it, because the thing that would have
checked it is the handshake the seam replaced.

So the resolver and exchange seams are NOT the same shape. A supplied resolver
may only CHOOSE AMONG addresses the fence already admits. A supplied exchange
REPLACES the evidence itself. Promoting it would satisfy an acceptance item by
destroying the property the item exists to protect.

=== CONSEQUENCES, both recorded as the ruling requires ====================

(1) THE EXCHANGE SEAM IS NOT SHIPPED CAPABILITY and must not be counted as one.
    GuardedHttpTestExchange, GuardedHttpTestRequest, GuardedHttpTestWireResponse
    and new_with_test_exchange remain #[cfg(test)] and private. No capability
    credit attaches to them in any bead.

(2) NO TEST USING IT CAN SERVE AS SHIPPED-SURFACE EVIDENCE (PL-3). Also true of
    new_loopback_test_authority (http.rs:1634), which is likewise #[cfg(test)]
    and private — so BOTH routes to eliciting a response are test-only.

    THEREFORE, precisely: no acceptance item requiring a COMPLETED
    GuardedHttpFetcher FETCH RESPONSE can be proven from outside the crate at
    this revision. Those items are:

      bd-ho7of item 6  redirect-origin interception proved from outside.
          The capability is public (GuardedHttpRedirect,
          GuardedHttpFetchResponse.redirect — see comment 2522); eliciting a
          3xx is what is impossible. UNMET, unprovable as specified.

      FND-05 A item 8  origin/peer/TLS provenance capture.
          GuardedHttpPeerProvenance is only populated from a real TlsStream.
          UNMET from the public surface.

      si9y TLS matrix  valid, wrong-host, untrusted-root, expired-certificate,
          plus TLS 1.3 replay/resumption/0-RTT cases. All require a served
          response over a controlled TLS endpoint. UNMET from the public
          surface.

    WHAT IS NOT BLOCKED, so the boundary is not overstated: anything provable
    without a fetch response. The resolver seam proofs
    (fnd_05_guarded_resolver_seam.rs) observe typed REFUSALS before any wire is
    touched, and the classifier proofs (fnd_05_destination_classifier.rs, 22
    addresses) and the ambiguous-framing proof (fnd_05_ambiguous_framing.rs,
    via HttpTransport) likewise need no response. Those stand.

(3) THE ONE-CODE-PATH CONDITION IS SATISFIED for what WAS promoted. The
    resolver has exactly one path: the test_resolver field and its cfg(test)
    branch in resolve_all are deleted, and new_with_test_exchange is a thin
    wrapper over the public with_resolver. There is no shipped resolver seam
    sitting beside a parallel cfg(test) one. The exchange seam is not a
    violation of that condition because it was not promoted — it is the sole
    path for its own function, used only by test builds.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION for the three blocked items: record them as unprovable
from the public surface at this revision, with this note as the reason. Closing
them would require either a real controlled HTTPS origin in the harness (which
reintroduces the *.pem transfer problem RCH cannot serve) or promoting the
exchange seam, which this decision rejects on evidence-integrity grounds.

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
FND-05 si9y — PROVABILITY MAP for the remaining Tests matrix.
ProudValley, 2026-09-17. Audit only; no code, no build slots consumed.

PURPOSE. 27+ beads are batch-pending against a verification lane that clears
roughly one batch per build, so the binding constraint is build slots, not
throughput. This map exists so whoever implements the rest of si9y spends slots
on items that CAN pass rather than discovering the blocked ones by dispatching
them. A finding costs zero slots; a submission costs one and waits.

=== CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER AUDIT ===================================
Comment 2529 listed streaming round trip, disconnect cancellation and
slow-reader backpressure as "needs a public-surface positive plus a planted
negative", which was true but unhelpfully vague — it left the impression they
needed a wire, and a reader could reasonably have concluded they were in the
same blocked class as the TLS matrix. THEY ARE NOT. Every one of them is
provable OFFLINE from the public surface, with no network, no TLS and no
cfg(test). The blocked set is much narrower than my earlier notes implied.

The decisive fact I had not checked: lib.rs declares `pub mod memory`,
`pub mod sse`, `pub mod http`, `pub mod event_store` and `pub mod ingress`.
Types absent from the flat `pub use` list are therefore still reachable as
`fastmcp_transport::<module>::<Type>`. I made this exact mistake once already
with HttpTransport (comment 2506) and made it again by not re-checking here.
CHECK `pub mod` BEFORE CONCLUDING ANYTHING IS UNREACHABLE.

=== PROVABLE OFFLINE — public surface, no wire, no cfg(test) ==============

incremental client SSE consumption
    fastmcp_transport::sse::ModernSseDecoder — a PURE decoder.
      new(ModernSseLimits) -> push(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<String>, ModernSseParseError>
      finish() -> Result<ModernSseEndOfStream, ModernSseParseError>
    Feed chunk boundaries mid-event to prove INCREMENTAL consumption rather than
    whole-buffer parsing. ModernSseLimits is re-exported flat.
    NOTE the known hazard: asupersync h1 has no close-delimited body, so an SSE
    fixture without chunked framing delivers zero events and goes false-green.
    A decoder-level test sidesteps that entirely, which is another reason to
    prove it here rather than over a wire.

bounded backpressure / capacity bounds
    StreamableHttpTransport::with_capacity(n) -> Result<Self, TransportError>
    Refuses capacity == 0 and capacity > MAX_STREAMABLE_QUEUE_CAPACITY with a
    typed error, and carries MAX_STREAMABLE_QUEUED_BYTES_PER_DIRECTION for the
    byte dimension. Both the bound and its refusal are observable without a
    socket. The planted negative writes itself: n vs n+1 at the boundary.

streaming round trip / request-scoped streaming responses
    StreamableHttpTransport is CHANNEL-BASED, not socket-based: new() and
    with_capacity() take no reader/writer, and requests are fed through
    request_ingress() -> StreamableHttpRequestIngress (http.rs:3365, pub,
    reachable via pub mod http). StreamableHttpResponseStream,
    StreamableHttpRequestResponseStream and ModernHttpSseCollector are all flat
    re-exports. The whole round trip is drivable in-process.

peer-disconnect cancellation
    StreamableHttpRequestCancellation (flat re-export) plus the Transport trait's
    close(&mut self, cx: &Cx). fastmcp_transport::memory::create_memory_transport_pair()
    and create_memory_transport_pair_with_capacity() give a genuine in-process
    duplex implementing Transport with cancel-aware send/recv/close, so a
    disconnect can be induced on one half and observed on the other.

cancel-aware read/write surfaces
    The Transport trait takes &Cx on send, recv and close. Driving a memory pair
    under a cancelled Cx exercises it directly.
    CAUTION from prior campaign experience: Cx::clone is an ALIAS, not a child.
    Cancelling a clone cancels the ambient context, after which no-further-work
    assertions fire for the wrong reason. Derive a child scope rather than
    cloning if the test needs to cancel one side only.

uncoded REQUEST content-coding matrix
    DONE at 7b375e5f — 26 cases through HttpRequestHandler::admit_modern_request
    plus the duplicate-field-line case through HttpTransport::read_request.

ambiguous framing rejection
    DONE at c0487c54 (gate not run; admission refusal at the time).

destination classifier deny-list
    DONE at 88bb0101 — 22 addresses, gated green before commit.

=== GENUINELY BLOCKED — needs a real TLS handshake or a completed fetch ====
All of these require either a controlled TLS origin or the lower wire seam, and
BOTH routes are cfg(test): GuardedHttpTestExchange and new_loopback_test_authority.
The exchange seam was deliberately NOT promoted — see comment 2559, which
declined it because no invariant stops it becoming a bypass of TLS custody and
peer provenance.

  TLS valid / wrong-host / untrusted-root / expired-certificate
  TLS 1.3 replay server, host-supplied connector, resumption, 0-RTT absence
  origin / peer / TLS provenance capture (GuardedHttpPeerProvenance)
  redirect-origin interception (capability is public; ELICITING a 3xx is not)
  the RESPONSE half of the content-coding matrix
  stalled/partial ClientHello, accepted-socket-with-no-request, keep-alive-idle,
    total-lifetime and request-count boundaries, shutdown in every phase
    (these are socket/TLS phase deadlines; note separately that 5 of the 6 phase
    deadlines do not exist in GuardedHttpFetchPolicy at all — comment 2506
    UNMET-2, which is an implementation gap, not merely a proof gap)

=== RECOMMENDED ORDER FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ==============================
1. ModernSseDecoder incremental consumption — pure, fast, no wire, and it
   retires the highest-value remaining item.
2. with_capacity bound plus its n/n+1 planted negative — smallest possible
   diff for a real boundary proof.
3. StreamableHttpTransport round trip through request_ingress.
4. Disconnect cancellation over a memory pair.
Items 1-4 are independent, so a single crate-level batch covers all of them in
one build rather than four.

NOTHING IN THE BLOCKED LIST SHOULD BE DISPATCHED until the exchange-seam
question is resolved at a level above this bead. Dispatching one costs a slot
and returns a red that is already documented.

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
bd-ho7of / FND-05 — ATTRIBUTION of the two transport lib failures.
ProudValley, 2026-09-17. Question answered BEFORE changing anything, per the
standing rule: is the ASSERTION wrong or the IMPLEMENTATION?

ANSWER: NEITHER. The security property HELD. The failing half of the assertion
is a different property, and the mechanism is a shared 2-second wall-clock
budget in the test helper — the exact hazard class this wave has been
cataloguing.

=== THE DECISIVE FACT: THE FAILURE DIRECTION ============================
  http.rs:7505  assert_eq!(requests.len(), 1, "hostname refusal must precede HTTP bytes")
                left: 0   right: 1

`requests` collects HTTP requests that actually REACHED the loopback server.
The test performs TWO fetches through one fetcher:
    fetch 1  host "wrong.example"  -> must fail at TLS, write ZERO HTTP bytes
    fetch 2  host "foobar.com"     -> must succeed, write exactly ONE request
So `requests.len() == 1` is a COMPOUND assertion: zero from the refusal, plus
one from the valid retry.

WE GOT 0, NOT 2. That direction is everything:
  - A FENCE LEAK would produce 2 — the wrong host writing bytes it should not.
  - 0 means the wrong-host fetch wrote NOTHING, which is precisely the asserted
    security property, and it HELD.
  - What failed is the OTHER half: the valid retry never reached the server.

The line immediately above also passed:
    assert!(matches!(results[0], Err(GuardedHttpFetchError::Tls(_))))
The test reached :7505, so the wrong-host fetch DID terminate in a typed TLS
error. Hostname validation worked.

=== THE MECHANISM =======================================================
crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs:6827, inside guarded_loopback_fetches:
    let server_deadline = time::wall_now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
and guarded_loopback_serve bounds every phase with it:
    time::timeout_at(deadline, listener.accept())   -> "accept deadline elapsed"
    time::timeout_at(deadline, acceptor.accept(stream)) -> "TLS deadline elapsed"

ONE 2-second wall-clock budget covers the WHOLE multi-fetch sequence: both TLS
handshakes and both HTTP exchanges. On a loaded worker the first fetch's
handshake-and-failure plus the second fetch's full handshake need not fit.
When the budget expires the server stops accepting, and the second request
never lands — giving exactly requests.len() == 0.

BOTH failing transport lib tests use this same helper and this same budget.
The sibling's symptom corroborates rather than competes:
    rh5_guarded_loopback_real_wire_redirect_is_typed_without_follow_up
    -> Http("I/O error: tls connection closed without close_notify")
A server that hits its deadline mid-exchange drops the connection WITHOUT a
clean TLS shutdown, which is precisely "closed without close_notify". One
defect, one mechanism, two symptoms.

CLASSIFICATION under the five-bucket taxonomy: (c) UNSOUND BUT LOAD-BEARING.
The property is real — a test server must not hang — but the mechanism is a
wall-clock budget spanning a multi-step sequence. It must be replaced, never
merely deleted: deleting it makes the accept hang forever.

=== ANSWERING THE THREE QUESTIONS ASKED =================================
1. ASSERTION or IMPLEMENTATION? Neither is wrong about the security property.
   The assertion is CONFLATED — it checks "refusal wrote nothing" and "retry
   wrote one" in a single number, so a failure cannot be read without knowing
   the direction. Splitting it into two assertions would have made this
   self-diagnosing. That is a real test-construction defect, and it is not mine
   to fix unilaterally: this is pre-existing code in a file I do not own.

2. DOES THE FENCE HOLD FOR A CALLER-SUPPLIED RESOLVER, OR ONLY PRODUCTION?
   This test does not bear on that question at all — it uses the cfg(test)
   loopback authority constructor, not the with_resolver seam.
   THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED ELSEWHERE, GREEN: my
   fnd_05_destination_classifier_denies_every_enumerated_range_positive drives
   22 non-public addresses through GuardedHttpFetcher::with_resolver — a
   CALLER-SUPPLIED resolver — and requires the typed DisallowedResolvedAddress
   refusal for every one. It is not in the failure list, so it passed. The
   paired planted negative requiring a public address to get PAST the fence
   also passed. So the fence demonstrably holds for a caller-supplied resolver,
   executed, not argued.

3. IS THE close_notify FAILURE ENVIRONMENT OR PROTOCOL? Same 2-second budget,
   same helper, and the symptom is what a deadline-truncated server produces.
   Environment-shaped and mechanism-shared with the first, not a distinct
   protocol defect. I would not spend separate effort on it.

=== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR bd-ho7of =======================================
The orchestrator held off closing it because 0 of 7 acceptance items were
checked and the gate was a cargo check. That caution was right for the reason
given, and it stays right — but NOT for the reason the failure appeared to
supply. bd-ho7of's surface does not have a failing security assertion. It has a
failing TEST-HARNESS TIMEOUT adjacent to a security assertion that passed.

Still not closable, and I am not arguing otherwise: the acceptance items remain
unchecked, items 3 and 6 are unmet by the exchange-seam decision (comment 2559),
and the tests are now executed rather than merely compiled but two of my own
targets need attention.

NOTHING CHANGED. No file touched, no assertion edited.

EXTENSION BARS X1-X12 AUTHORED AS A THIRD PARTY AND APPENDED TO THE FIELD BY THEIR AUTHOR. SilentSquirrel,
on WildMountain rulings #10/#11. HEAD 6c44ba94 (http.rs blob a41fb3ac). Static only: no slot, no code, nothing
ticked, no claim. I author these bars; I neither implement, review for credit, nor tick them.

=== HOW THE FIELD WAS CHANGED ===
APPEND ONLY. The six BRIDGE-V1 bars are a byte-identical PREFIX of the new field (checked with startswith
against the pre-write snapshot), and stored == intended by cmp. The count is 6 -> 18 items, 0 checked. The
extension sits between its own BEGIN/END markers. I did NOT remove or edit the template bars: they name
nonexistent IDs (#2485), but retiring them is not a bar author's call and would read as weakening (RH-10).
They still govern the package, and X12 states that.

=== CONFLICT DECLARATION (tracker and archived scrollback) ===
- zq09: 0 comments, 0 events, 0 archive mentions by SilentSquirrel.
- ho7of: 0 comments, 0 events. The archive has 6 mentions. The acts are a gate-ledger audit of ho7of's CLOSE
  provenance, in which my lane graded it "a false citation of a specific row" and then RETRACTED that the same tick

- FND-05 parent (ahet.4): 4 comments from 09-21 (4434, 4454, 4510, 4515), a bullet-by-bullet evaluation

- ysez: 0.
None of these is authoring, filing, ratifying or ruling on zq09 or on the extension.

=== FACTS RE-DERIVED BEFORE WRITING, EACH OF WHICH SHAPED A BAR ===
1. asupersync 0.5.0 (registry source): TlsConnectorBuilder::with_webpki_roots EXTENDS root_certs, and
   add_root_certificate / add_root_certificates are the only custom-root entry points. Roots ACCUMULATE,
   so "replaces WebPKI" is a property of which builder calls are made. The store is pub(crate) and no
   WebPKI-chained certificate can be served offline, so X6(a) records STATIC as the highest reachable class
   for that one property, rather than letting a lower-class wire test stand in for it.
2. GuardedHttpPeerProvenance.root_policy_revision is a caller-supplied String documented as "the actual
   trust roots are fixed WebPKI roots". Under custom roots it would misreport, so X5 requires the fold
   to be observable offline and planted-negative-tested (same DER -> equal identity; one cert different ->
   different identity; custom vs WebPKI under an identical policy -> different identity).
3. The public with_resolver seam (ho7of) makes "refused before any DNS" observable from the shipped
   surface with a counting resolver, which is why X4 can be proven offline at shipped class.

X1 CLAIM COMMENT: EVERY NEW PUBLIC SYMBOL, NAMED BEFORE ANY CODE. ProudValley (%1), implementer, working UNCLAIMED under R1 (#5450). Reviewer per rulings #13: SilentSquirrel. Subject: http.rs blob a41fb3ac (last commit 0576bdaa). No code written yet.

=== NEW PUBLIC SYMBOLS (fastmcp-transport; the names below are the ones that land) ===
consts

  pub const MAX_GUARDED_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024;    content-type / authorization value bound

root set (X5)
  pub struct GuardedRootSet   (non-empty; certificates stored sorted by DER bytes, duplicates removed)
    pub fn new(certificates: impl IntoIterator<Item = asupersync::tls::Certificate>) -> Result<Self, GuardedHttpFetchError>
    pub fn certificate_count(&self) -> usize
fetcher (all inherent methods on GuardedHttpFetcher)
  pub fn with_root_set(policy: GuardedHttpFetchPolicy, roots: &GuardedRootSet) -> Result<Self, GuardedHttpFetchError>
  pub fn with_root_set_and_resolver(policy, roots: &GuardedRootSet, resolver: Arc<dyn GuardedHttpResolver>) -> Result<Self, GuardedHttpFetchError>
  pub fn root_identity(&self) -> &str       X5's offline accessor
  pub async fn post(&self, cx: &Cx, url: &GuardedHttpsUrl, request: &GuardedHttpRequest) -> Result<GuardedHttpFetchResponse, GuardedHttpFetchError>
lib.rs: ONE NEW `pub use http::{..}` statement re-exporting the above. The existing re-export block is not edited (X1: zero deleted lines).
