FND-05 I (si9y) — FIRST AUDIT (ProudValley, 2026-09-17, HEAD 1ebf8332).
Read-only, nothing edited. Slice: "public network capability boundary."

=== STRUCTURAL POSITION ====================================================
Blocked by both producers: bd-fnd-05-implementation-a-zq09 and
bd-fnd-05-implementation-b-ysez. A is itself blocked by bd-ho7of. So the chain
is bd-ho7of -> A -> si9y, with B in parallel. si9y cannot be claimed or
submitted until A and B clear; this audit needs no claim.

Same TWO AC DEFECTS as A and B, now confirmed across all three FND-05 roles:
 - the generated IDs fnd_05_i_positive / fnd_05_i_planted_negative DO NOT EXIST
   anywhere in the workspace;
 - there is NO PL-1-TARGET-MAP amendment to retire them (FND-01's .1.1 carried
   one; FND-05 carries none on any role);
 - the AC's own runner is the illegal workspace-wide filtered form
   `cargo test --workspace --all-targets fnd_05_i_positive -- --exact`.
Writing tests named to match those aliases is RH-12. The real requirement is
the package body's Acceptance + Tests sections.

=== ALREADY DISCHARGED BY THE B AUDIT (do not re-prove) ====================
- "No Tokio, reqwest, hyper, or prohibited adapter enters the graph" — all six
  prohibited crates absent from Cargo.lock (comment 2519).
- "No ureq, second HTTP/TLS policy stack, or TLS early-data path enters the
  graph" — ureq absent; enable_early_data(false) at every connector
  construction; exactly one root-store feature, so one TLS policy stack.
- "HTTPS validates hostname and trust roots" — WebPKI roots + SNI + certificate
  validation in GuardedHttpFetcher::new, which refuses a caller-supplied
  connector.

=== THE *.pem TRAP IS ALREADY SOLVED IN-TREE — follow the precedent =========
si9y's Tests section is TLS-certificate heavy: "TLS valid, wrong-host,
untrusted-root, and expired-certificate cases" plus TLS 1.3 replay/resumption.
RCH never transfers *.pem, so a fixture-based proof would zero-run or fail on
the remote worker.

TWO WORKING PRECEDENTS ALREADY EXIST. Use them rather than inventing a third:
 1. COMPILE-TIME INLINE, crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs:6687,6698 —
    `const GUARDED_LOOPBACK_ROOT_PEM: &[u8] = br"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----..."`
    and GUARDED_LOOPBACK_CHAIN_PEM. The material is a byte-string constant, so
    it travels with the source.
 2. RUN-TIME MATERIALIZATION, crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_core_rpc.rs and
    .../oauth_core_rpc/subscriptions.rs — write the inlined material to
    `std::env::temp_dir().join("fastmcp-...pem")` at run time, with an explicit
    in-source comment naming the reason ("the remote build worker never
    receives `*.pem`").
Both halves are needed: inline at compile time AND materialize at run time.

VESTIGIAL FILE FLAGGED, NOT TOUCHED: crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/
oauth-core-ca.pem is tracked in git, but the only readers I found write their
OWN copy into temp_dir instead. It therefore looks unused. I did not delete it
(never delete a file) and it is not my lane — flagging for the fastmcp-client
owner in case it is a leftover that will mislead the next person into reading
from tests/fixtures/ and reintroducing the trap.

=== NOT YET ASSESSED — needs the central lane or the producers first ========
- Target matrix: "passes on Linux, macOS, and Windows targets used by CI".
  Producer-side audit cannot establish this; it is a central-lane result.
- "Disconnect cancels a child scope", streaming round trip, slow-reader
  backpressure: capability definitions exist and are public (FND-05 A audit,
  comment 2506 — StreamableHttpResponseStream, StreamableHttpRequestCancellation,
  with_capacity), but presence is not proof; each needs a public-surface
  positive plus a one-variable planted negative.
- "High-cardinality origins or policy revisions cannot retain unbounded
  sockets, TLS buffers, DNS work, pool identities, or acquisition waiters" —
  note pooling is structurally disabled here (Connection: close, "connection
  reuse deliberately absent"), so several sub-clauses are moot-by-design via
  the package's own fallback branch. That must be CITED as the fallback branch,
  not claimed as the primary.
- The uncoded request/response probe matrix (absent Content-Encoding,
  case-insensitive singleton identity, bounded empty-element N/N+1,
  all-empty, parameterized, duplicate-field, multi-coding negatives) is the
  largest single block of work here. The underlying enforcement exists
  (http.rs:1732 request emission, :1802-1805 receive refusal, :2196-2211
  bounded empty-element allowance) but the probe matrix itself does not.

=== THE ESCAPE CLAUSE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT MISUSED ========================
The package body permits: "The spike closes within five working days with
either all probes green OR explicit blocking upstream issues and captured
reproducers." That is the same provision used for the DNS-hook item on A
(comment 2506, prerequisite bd-ho7of). It licenses a NAMED, TRACKED, LINKED
blocking issue WITH a captured reproducer — it does not license an unmet item
being quietly reclassified. Any use of it here must carry a real reproducer.

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
bd-ho7of — EXCHANGE SEAM DECISION under orchestrator ruling 2026-09-17.
ProudValley. DECISION: DO NOT PROMOTE. It stays #[cfg(test)].

THE TEST I WAS SET: promote only if I can name the invariant that stops the
seam becoming a bypass, in the way the resolver seam's fence was nameable
("answers are fenced downstream by guarded_select_address_inner; TLS still
validates against the original host with WebPKI roots; early data off"). If no
equivalent fence can be named, do not promote.

I CANNOT NAME ONE. Measured at http.rs:1691, the exchange seam sits AFTER
address selection and returns a fully-formed response directly:

    #[cfg(test)]
    if let Some(exchange) = self.test_exchange.as_ref() {
        ... let wire = exchange.exchange(phase_cx, request).await?;
        return guarded_admit_native_response(wire.status, ...);
    }

WHAT SURVIVES IT (the partial fence, stated fairly):
  - the address fence still runs BEFORE it — guarded_select_address is applied
    to the resolver's answers regardless, so a supplied exchange cannot widen
    which addresses are admitted;
  - response admission bounds still apply — guarded_admit_native_response
    enforces the header byte bound, the policy body limit, and the
    identity-content-coding refusal.

WHAT IT BYPASSES ENTIRELY:
  - TCP connect to the selected address;
  - the whole TLS handshake;
  - certificate validation and WebPKI root custody;
  - peer provenance capture.

THE CONCRETE HARM, not merely "a larger surface". GuardedHttpFetchResponse
carries a PUBLIC `provenance: GuardedHttpPeerProvenance` field — leaf
certificate SHA-256, ALPN, TLS protocol version, selected address, root policy
revision. It is populated by guarded_peer_provenance(tls: &TlsStream<..>, ..),
i.e. from a REAL TLS stream. Downstream trust decisions are expected to read
it. A public exchange seam makes every one of those fields CALLER-SUPPLIED: a
caller could hand back a response asserting a leaf-certificate digest and TLS
version that no handshake ever produced. That converts attested provenance into
an attacker-controlled value, in the type whose purpose is to attest. There is
no downstream check that could restore it, because the thing that would have
checked it is the handshake the seam replaced.

So the resolver and exchange seams are NOT the same shape. A supplied resolver
may only CHOOSE AMONG addresses the fence already admits. A supplied exchange
REPLACES the evidence itself. Promoting it would satisfy an acceptance item by
destroying the property the item exists to protect.

=== CONSEQUENCES, both recorded as the ruling requires ====================

(1) THE EXCHANGE SEAM IS NOT SHIPPED CAPABILITY and must not be counted as one.
    GuardedHttpTestExchange, GuardedHttpTestRequest, GuardedHttpTestWireResponse
    and new_with_test_exchange remain #[cfg(test)] and private. No capability
    credit attaches to them in any bead.

(2) NO TEST USING IT CAN SERVE AS SHIPPED-SURFACE EVIDENCE (PL-3). Also true of
    new_loopback_test_authority (http.rs:1634), which is likewise #[cfg(test)]
    and private — so BOTH routes to eliciting a response are test-only.

    THEREFORE, precisely: no acceptance item requiring a COMPLETED
    GuardedHttpFetcher FETCH RESPONSE can be proven from outside the crate at
    this revision. Those items are:

      bd-ho7of item 6  redirect-origin interception proved from outside.
          The capability is public (GuardedHttpRedirect,
          GuardedHttpFetchResponse.redirect — see comment 2522); eliciting a
          3xx is what is impossible. UNMET, unprovable as specified.

      FND-05 A item 8  origin/peer/TLS provenance capture.
          GuardedHttpPeerProvenance is only populated from a real TlsStream.
          UNMET from the public surface.

      si9y TLS matrix  valid, wrong-host, untrusted-root, expired-certificate,
          plus TLS 1.3 replay/resumption/0-RTT cases. All require a served
          response over a controlled TLS endpoint. UNMET from the public
          surface.

    WHAT IS NOT BLOCKED, so the boundary is not overstated: anything provable
    without a fetch response. The resolver seam proofs
    (fnd_05_guarded_resolver_seam.rs) observe typed REFUSALS before any wire is
    touched, and the classifier proofs (fnd_05_destination_classifier.rs, 22
    addresses) and the ambiguous-framing proof (fnd_05_ambiguous_framing.rs,
    via HttpTransport) likewise need no response. Those stand.

(3) THE ONE-CODE-PATH CONDITION IS SATISFIED for what WAS promoted. The
    resolver has exactly one path: the test_resolver field and its cfg(test)
    branch in resolve_all are deleted, and new_with_test_exchange is a thin
    wrapper over the public with_resolver. There is no shipped resolver seam
    sitting beside a parallel cfg(test) one. The exchange seam is not a
    violation of that condition because it was not promoted — it is the sole
    path for its own function, used only by test builds.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION for the three blocked items: record them as unprovable
from the public surface at this revision, with this note as the reason. Closing
them would require either a real controlled HTTPS origin in the harness (which
reintroduces the *.pem transfer problem RCH cannot serve) or promoting the
exchange seam, which this decision rejects on evidence-integrity grounds.

test(fnd-05): add the uncoded request content-coding probe matrix - si9y

GATED BEFORE COMMIT: Remote command finished: exit=0 in 1612ms, with
`Checking fastmcp-transport v0.10.0` present and zero error lines.

LIVENESS CAVEAT, stated because 0.23s of cargo time is weaker evidence than a
long build. Test targets under tests/ are auto-discovered on every invocation,
so a new file is necessarily type-checked, and 0.23s is consistent with
type-checking one small file against already-built dependencies (the prior gate
on this crate was 1m55s and built everything). But unlike the earlier
fnd_05_guarded_resolver_seam gate, there is no pass/fail FLIP on this file to
point at, so this is inference from the build system's behaviour rather than
direct proof that my bytes were compiled. I did NOT plant a compile_error probe:
this is a shared crate and a probe here breaks every other lane's build.

WHAT THIS COVERS. The package body requires a request/response probe matrix over
Content-Encoding. This lands the REQUEST half, 26 cases, through the shipped
public admission entry point HttpRequestHandler::admit_modern_request.

  POSITIVES (11): absent header; canonical lowercase `identity`; uppercase;
  mixed-case; alternating-case; surrounding optional whitespace; one leading,
  one trailing, two leading and two trailing empty list elements; empty
  elements with interior whitespace; and the empty-element bound N = 16.

  NEGATIVES (14): all-empty value; all-empty with two and four elements; the
  bound N+1 = 17; parameterized `identity;q=1` with and without whitespace;
  other codings gzip, br, deflate; two semantic codings in both orders;
  duplicate semantic token; and two near-miss tokens (x-identity, identityy).

  DUPLICATE FIELD LINES (1): driven through HttpTransport::read_request
  instead, because HttpRequest::headers is a HashMap<String, String> and
  therefore CANNOT hold two Content-Encoding lines. That case is decided by the
  wire parser, so it is proved on the surface that actually decides it, paired
  with a single-field-line control so the refusal tracks duplication rather
  than the header's presence.

RH-5 DISCIPLINE. Every value-level case is built by one constructor and differs
in exactly one dimension: the Content-Encoding value. Method, path,
content-type, protocol-version mirror and body are byte-identical across the
matrix, so an outcome difference is attributable to the coding alone. The bound
contrast is asserted explicitly rather than left implicit: 16 admitted, 17
refused, two values differing by a single comma.

WHY THE NEGATIVES CARRY THE WEIGHT. The positive set would be satisfied
perfectly by a handler that admitted everything. The negatives are what
separate "admits uncoded requests" from "admits anything", which is the whole
content of the requirement.

NOT COVERED, and recorded rather than silently omitted: the RESPONSE half
(omitted response Content-Encoding, auto-decompression disabled) needs a
completed GuardedHttpFetcher fetch response, and BOTH routes to eliciting one
are #[cfg(test)] - the exchange seam and the loopback authority. See the
exchange-seam decision on bd-ho7of, comment 2559, which declined to promote the
exchange seam because no invariant stops it becoming a bypass of TLS custody
and peer provenance. si9y's response-half probes are therefore unprovable from
the public surface at this revision.

COMPILES, UNRUN. cargo check does not execute tests, so the 26 cases are built
and not demonstrated. No behavioural green claimed.

Runner card (leaf-local, unfiltered, no required-features):
  cargo test -p fastmcp-transport --test fnd_05_uncoded_probe_matrix -- --list
  cargo test -p fastmcp-transport --test fnd_05_uncoded_probe_matrix
IDs: fnd_05_uncoded_request_matrix_positives,
     fnd_05_uncoded_request_matrix_planted_negatives,
     fnd_05_uncoded_duplicate_field_line_is_refused

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
FND-05 si9y — PROVABILITY MAP for the remaining Tests matrix.
ProudValley, 2026-09-17. Audit only; no code, no build slots consumed.

PURPOSE. 27+ beads are batch-pending against a verification lane that clears
roughly one batch per build, so the binding constraint is build slots, not
throughput. This map exists so whoever implements the rest of si9y spends slots
on items that CAN pass rather than discovering the blocked ones by dispatching
them. A finding costs zero slots; a submission costs one and waits.

=== CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER AUDIT ===================================
Comment 2529 listed streaming round trip, disconnect cancellation and
slow-reader backpressure as "needs a public-surface positive plus a planted
negative", which was true but unhelpfully vague — it left the impression they
needed a wire, and a reader could reasonably have concluded they were in the
same blocked class as the TLS matrix. THEY ARE NOT. Every one of them is
provable OFFLINE from the public surface, with no network, no TLS and no
cfg(test). The blocked set is much narrower than my earlier notes implied.

The decisive fact I had not checked: lib.rs declares `pub mod memory`,
`pub mod sse`, `pub mod http`, `pub mod event_store` and `pub mod ingress`.
Types absent from the flat `pub use` list are therefore still reachable as
`fastmcp_transport::<module>::<Type>`. I made this exact mistake once already
with HttpTransport (comment 2506) and made it again by not re-checking here.
CHECK `pub mod` BEFORE CONCLUDING ANYTHING IS UNREACHABLE.

=== PROVABLE OFFLINE — public surface, no wire, no cfg(test) ==============

incremental client SSE consumption
    fastmcp_transport::sse::ModernSseDecoder — a PURE decoder.
      new(ModernSseLimits) -> push(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<String>, ModernSseParseError>
      finish() -> Result<ModernSseEndOfStream, ModernSseParseError>
    Feed chunk boundaries mid-event to prove INCREMENTAL consumption rather than
    whole-buffer parsing. ModernSseLimits is re-exported flat.
    NOTE the known hazard: asupersync h1 has no close-delimited body, so an SSE
    fixture without chunked framing delivers zero events and goes false-green.
    A decoder-level test sidesteps that entirely, which is another reason to
    prove it here rather than over a wire.

bounded backpressure / capacity bounds
    StreamableHttpTransport::with_capacity(n) -> Result<Self, TransportError>
    Refuses capacity == 0 and capacity > MAX_STREAMABLE_QUEUE_CAPACITY with a
    typed error, and carries MAX_STREAMABLE_QUEUED_BYTES_PER_DIRECTION for the
    byte dimension. Both the bound and its refusal are observable without a
    socket. The planted negative writes itself: n vs n+1 at the boundary.

streaming round trip / request-scoped streaming responses
    StreamableHttpTransport is CHANNEL-BASED, not socket-based: new() and
    with_capacity() take no reader/writer, and requests are fed through
    request_ingress() -> StreamableHttpRequestIngress (http.rs:3365, pub,
    reachable via pub mod http). StreamableHttpResponseStream,
    StreamableHttpRequestResponseStream and ModernHttpSseCollector are all flat
    re-exports. The whole round trip is drivable in-process.

peer-disconnect cancellation
    StreamableHttpRequestCancellation (flat re-export) plus the Transport trait's
    close(&mut self, cx: &Cx). fastmcp_transport::memory::create_memory_transport_pair()
    and create_memory_transport_pair_with_capacity() give a genuine in-process
    duplex implementing Transport with cancel-aware send/recv/close, so a
    disconnect can be induced on one half and observed on the other.

cancel-aware read/write surfaces
    The Transport trait takes &Cx on send, recv and close. Driving a memory pair
    under a cancelled Cx exercises it directly.
    CAUTION from prior campaign experience: Cx::clone is an ALIAS, not a child.
    Cancelling a clone cancels the ambient context, after which no-further-work
    assertions fire for the wrong reason. Derive a child scope rather than
    cloning if the test needs to cancel one side only.

uncoded REQUEST content-coding matrix
    DONE at 7b375e5f — 26 cases through HttpRequestHandler::admit_modern_request
    plus the duplicate-field-line case through HttpTransport::read_request.

ambiguous framing rejection
    DONE at c0487c54 (gate not run; admission refusal at the time).

destination classifier deny-list
    DONE at 88bb0101 — 22 addresses, gated green before commit.

=== GENUINELY BLOCKED — needs a real TLS handshake or a completed fetch ====
All of these require either a controlled TLS origin or the lower wire seam, and
BOTH routes are cfg(test): GuardedHttpTestExchange and new_loopback_test_authority.
The exchange seam was deliberately NOT promoted — see comment 2559, which
declined it because no invariant stops it becoming a bypass of TLS custody and
peer provenance.

  TLS valid / wrong-host / untrusted-root / expired-certificate
  TLS 1.3 replay server, host-supplied connector, resumption, 0-RTT absence
  origin / peer / TLS provenance capture (GuardedHttpPeerProvenance)
  redirect-origin interception (capability is public; ELICITING a 3xx is not)
  the RESPONSE half of the content-coding matrix
  stalled/partial ClientHello, accepted-socket-with-no-request, keep-alive-idle,
    total-lifetime and request-count boundaries, shutdown in every phase
    (these are socket/TLS phase deadlines; note separately that 5 of the 6 phase
    deadlines do not exist in GuardedHttpFetchPolicy at all — comment 2506
    UNMET-2, which is an implementation gap, not merely a proof gap)

=== RECOMMENDED ORDER FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ==============================
1. ModernSseDecoder incremental consumption — pure, fast, no wire, and it
   retires the highest-value remaining item.
2. with_capacity bound plus its n/n+1 planted negative — smallest possible
   diff for a real boundary proof.
3. StreamableHttpTransport round trip through request_ingress.
4. Disconnect cancellation over a memory pair.
Items 1-4 are independent, so a single crate-level batch covers all of them in
one build rather than four.

NOTHING IN THE BLOCKED LIST SHOULD BE DISPATCHED until the exchange-seam
question is resolved at a level above this bead. Dispatching one costs a slot
and returns a red that is already documented.

comments.text:
fix(fnd-05): assert WHICH guard refuses each coded request, not one error for all - si9y

MY TEST WAS WRONG; THE IMPLEMENTATION IS CORRECT. Determined by measurement
before changing either, per the standing rule.

THE FAILURE (from the transport batch, reproduced on a single target):
  1 of 14 coded or malformed request(s) were admitted.
  all-empty value: Content-Encoding: "" was ADMITTED

THAT MESSAGE WAS FALSE, AND FALSE IN THE MOST COSTLY DIRECTION: it named a
security-relevant admission that was not happening. Upgrading the diagnostic to
report the actual outcome rather than a bool showed what really occurred:

  Content-Encoding: "" -> refused-for-OTHER-reason(
      InvalidHeader("invalid value for request header content-encoding"))

The request WAS refused. An empty header value is malformed before its list
syntax is ever considered, so header-value validation catches it and it never
reaches content-coding semantics. The package body requires "reject a present
all-empty value" and the implementation does exactly that - via an earlier
guard than my test assumed.

THE DEFECT WAS MINE: `refused_for_coding` collapsed three distinct outcomes -
admitted, refused FOR THE CODING, refused for some other reason - into a bool,
so "not refused for coding" rendered as "was ADMITTED". That is the same
conflated-assertion flaw that made "hostname refusal must precede HTTP bytes"
unreadable from its left/right values alone, which I had criticised in another
file an hour before shipping it in my own.

THE FIX, which strengthens rather than relaxes:
  - admission_outcome() returns the actual result, distinguishing all three.
  - Each of the 14 cases now declares WHICH GUARD should own its refusal:
    Coding for the 13 list-syntax violations, HeaderValue for the all-empty one.
  - Two separate assertions instead of one. The security property (nothing
    coded or malformed is ADMITTED) and the attribution property (each refusal
    comes from the guard that should own it) now fail independently and say
    which one failed. A case migrating between guards is reported as "the
    boundary moved", explicitly NOT as an admission defect.

NO PRODUCTION CODE TOUCHED. is_identity_content_coding and the header
validation are unchanged; only my test file changed.

THE NEGATIVE STILL DISCRIMINATES, argued structurally rather than by planting a
mutation in a crate four other lanes build:
  - if the handler ADMITTED everything, the first assertion fails (14 admitted);
  - if it REFUSED everything, the retained 16-vs-17 contrast fails on its first
    half, which requires 16 empty elements to be ADMITTED;
  - the 16/17 pair differs by exactly one comma and demands OPPOSITE outcomes,
    so it cannot be satisfied by any handler with a constant answer.
The test therefore fails in both directions and is not vacuous.

GATE, single target, executed not compiled:
  rch exec --job -- cargo test --no-fail-fast -p fastmcp-transport \\
      --test fnd_05_uncoded_probe_matrix
  Remote command finished: exit=0 in 3283ms
  3 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered
  fnd_05_uncoded_request_matrix_positives           ok
  fnd_05_uncoded_request_matrix_planted_negatives   ok
  fnd_05_uncoded_duplicate_field_line_is_refused    ok

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PAIR: the positive beside this negative was UNPROVEN while
the negative did not fire, because a negative that cannot fire cannot
discriminate its positive. With the negative firing, the 26-case request
content-coding matrix is proved rather than merely green.

comments.text:
WITHDRAWN: my RH-12 extension to this bead. It does not hold, and this bead is not
blocked on a structure-owner ruling. — WildMountain, batch-verify orchestrator.

I published that si9y's frozen IDs are the same alias class as fnd_01_i_* and that
writing them is RH-12. RoseStream contradicted that in mail 8984. I re-derived it with
my own instruments rather than accepting the correction, because a correction is a new
claim from a new instrument. The correction survives; my claim does not.

== WHAT I MEASURED ==

1. THE _i_ SHAPE IS ORDINARY, NOT A HAZARD CLASS.
   grep -rnE '^\s*(pub )?(async )?fn [a-z0-9_]+_i_(positive|planted_negative)\b' crates tools
     38 definitions across 19 distinct families: clt_01, clt_02, leg_02, leg_03, prt_01,
     prt_02, prt_03, prt_04, srv_01, srv_02, std_01, http_01, http_02, http_03,
     auth_00, limit_01, pxy_leg_01, fnd_02, fnd_03.
   Lanes author this shape routinely. RH-12 cannot be a property of it.
   (RoseStream said "at least ten". Measured, it is 38 across 19 families.)

2. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY DECLARES fnd_05_i_* AN ALIAS.
   git grep -ln 'fnd_05_i_'  ->  .beads/issues.jsonl and one corrupt-db backup. Nothing else.
   Untracked occurrences are: 79 tracker-export copies, 5 beads_compliance_audit snapshots
   of THIS BEAD (2026-08-07), one .doctor backup of the same jsonl, one git pack object,
   and .ntm/reply-withdrawn.md -- which is my own note repeating the claim.
   ZERO source files. ZERO structure documents. ZERO specification prose.
   Every occurrence is either si9y's own acceptance text or me quoting myself.

3. THE ALIAS FRAMING ORIGINATES IN COMMENT 2529 ON THIS BEAD.
   Author ProudValley, 2026-09-17T14:29:36Z:
     "Writing tests named to match those aliases is RH-12."
   Field-scoped search: 'those aliases is RH-12' appears x1 in comments, x0 in
   description, notes, acceptance_criteria and acceptance_items. The bead's own
   authored text contains no occurrence of "nonexistent", "structure correction" or
   "2026-08-08", and its only other RH-12 mention is the campaign boilerplate line
   "RH-1 through RH-12 ... apply" carried by every bead.

== THE DISTINCTION I COLLAPSED ==

RH-12 is a rule about AUTHORSHIP: the owner of an acceptance criterion may not write the
frozen IDs that criterion names. It is not a rule about EXISTENCE.

  fnd_01_i_*  a dated structure correction declares those specific IDs to be aliases.
              That is an existence claim, and it is backed by a document.
  fnd_05_i_*  no document says anything. The IDs simply have no definitions yet.

I keyed on the symptom -- "the ID matches _i_" -- instead of the condition -- "a structure
document declares these specific IDs to be aliases." That is the same substitution of shape
for mechanism that I had spent the preceding hour diagnosing elsewhere, committed inside the
retraction of it.

== WHAT THIS BEAD ACTUALLY NEEDS ==

status=open, assignee=ProudValley, blocked by two OPEN dependencies:
  bd-fnd-05-implementation-a-zq09   FND-05 A: DNS/TLS/HTTP feasibility primitives
  bd-fnd-05-implementation-b-ysez   FND-05 B: target/feature/crypto/failure-boundary

fnd_05_i_positive and fnd_05_i_planted_negative have no definitions anywhere
(validated instrument; the same grep finds all 38 siblings).

So when A and B land, this bead needs its frozen pair WRITTEN, by any lane other than
ProudValley -- because RH-12 bars the AC's owner from authoring their own AC's IDs, which
is the one part of the original concern that was correct and which ProudValley was right
to raise. That is an ordinary assignment condition. It is not an operator ruling, and I
should not have parked it above the lanes.

== ON THE RUNNER FORM ==
Comment 2529 also calls the AC's runner "the illegal workspace-wide filtered form". I am
not ruling on that here beyond one datum: the sibling FND-02 card uses the byte-identical
shape for six IDs and documents the correct reading -- one `test result:` line per binary,
most reading `0 passed; ... 1 filtered out`, which is the correct shape for binaries that
do not hold the named test, not a zero-run. Note also that the AC's literal string is
`rch exec --`, and plain `rch exec -- cargo test` is refused with a misleading "no
admissible workers"; the working form is `rch exec --job --`. That is an operational
substitution, not an acceptance defect.

title: FND-05 verification: source/target/test receipt
description:
Executable V role for FND-05.

Owned capability slice: source/target/test receipt.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:FND-05:V:BEGIN -->
Canonical V role for FND-05.

Owned capability slice: source/target/test receipt.
Named shipped consumer: public network capability boundary.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### FND-05 — Prove HTTP, TLS, DNS, and streaming feasibility

Outcome:

Resolve transport feasibility before downstream HTTP and OAuth design
is treated as implementable.

Reason:

Core HTTP, client OAuth, and authorization metadata discovery all need
production HTTPS, streaming, cancellation, DNS, and redirect behavior.

Implementation:

- Spend at most five working days on the asupersync HTTP/1
  client/server spike. Stop earlier when every acceptance probe has a
  reproducible result; at the deadline, any missing primitive becomes
  a named upstream prerequisite rather than open-ended investigation.
- Prove request-scoped streaming server responses.
- Prove incremental client SSE consumption.
- Prove peer-disconnect cancellation.
- Prove bounded backpressure.
- Prove cancel-aware accept, header read, body read, and write.
- Prove client DNS hooks and redirect interception.
- Expose the proven destination/TLS/redirect/body controls as one
  auth-agnostic `GuardedHttpFetcher` in `fastmcp-transport`, parameterized
  by lower-layer policy/value types and with no dependency on
  `fastmcp-client`, `fastmcp-server`, or OAuth orchestration. AUTH-03
  and AUTH-06 build their role-specific request/response policy on
  that shared transport capability rather than duplicating it.
- Prove origin, peer, and TLS provenance capture.
- Prove ambiguous framing rejection.
- Prove socket-accept, TLS-handshake, pre-first-request,
  keep-alive-idle, total connection-lifetime, and request-count
  deadlines/admission from the instant each phase acquires ownership.
- Prove TLS client hostname and certificate validation.
- Force TLS 1.3 early data/0-RTT off for every FastMCP client and
  server configuration. Reject an injected rustls/asupersync connector
  that can send credential-bearing or state-changing request bytes as
  early data; ordinary session resumption without early data remains a
  separate admitted optimization.
- Prove connection-pool identity and invalidation hooks sufficient for
  AUTH-03: exact origin and pinned peer address, SNI/ALPN, TLS roots/
  client auth, egress proxy, destination-policy revision, and
  redirect-origin isolation. If those hooks are absent, guarded OAuth
  fetches must disable pooling rather than reuse a connection admitted
  under another trust policy.
- Prove capacity hooks sufficient to enforce LIMIT-01's per-origin/
  policy and process pool-identity, active/idle socket, queued
  acquisition, DNS/TLS-handshake, byte, wait, idle, absolute-lifetime,
  request-count, and shutdown bounds. Admit before DNS/connect, use
  bounded LRU only for unborrowed idle entries, never evict a borrowed
  socket, and retain charges while a stale/tightened-policy connection
  drains or is quarantined.
- On destination, root, client-auth, proxy, ALPN/SNI, peer-address, or
  policy revision, stop new borrows from the old identity and close/
  drain it within the bound. An auth fetch disables pooling unless both
  the complete trust-identity hooks and these capacity/lifecycle hooks
  are present; direct one-shot connections still consume the same
  global socket/DNS/TLS reservations.
- Prove TLS server termination or document the trusted-terminator
  boundary, including which trusted component enforces handshake and
  idle deadlines and releases connection reservations.
- Prove every client/server adapter can force an uncoded
  representation, emit canonical lowercase
  `Accept-Encoding: identity` on requests, omit `Content-Encoding` on
  uncoded sends, and disable automatic decompression. On receive,
  parse RFC 9110 `#list` syntax and ignore up to LIMIT-01's bounded
  empty-element allowance before semantic cardinality. Then accept only
  an absent field or one bare content-coding token whose value is
  ASCII-case-insensitively `identity`; reject a present all-empty value,
  empty-element saturation, parameters, duplicate field lines, two or
  more semantic codings, and every other coding before body processing.
- For the guarded-fetch destination classifier, canonicalize
  IPv4-mapped IPv6 and then apply the IPv4 policy. Deny rather than
  reinterpret every other embedded/transition range, including
  IPv4-compatible addresses, NAT64 well-known `64:ff9b::/96`, NAT64
  local-use `64:ff9b:1::/48`, 6to4 `2002::/16`, and Teredo
  `2001::/32`. Pin and review the IANA special-purpose IPv4/IPv6
  registry snapshot; a newly special range fails the drift gate before
  release. Apply the same answer-set and connected-peer rule to OAuth,
  CIMD, icon, and update-check fetches.
- Use asupersync's rustls-backed `tls` plus one reviewed root-store
  feature, normally `tls-native-roots` for deployed clients and a
  deterministic configured root store in tests.
- Inspect the exact feature graph and reject any prohibited runtime
  dependency.
- Remove `ureq` and every direct non-asupersync HTTP client. A CLI
  update check remains disabled unless implemented as an explicit
  bounded guarded-fetch policy with a fixed crates.io origin; it never
  runs eagerly at process startup.
- Distinguish enforceable library constraints from release-lock
  evidence. A JOSE-enabled consumer is constrained by protocol's exact
  direct `ring =0.17.14` edge. A non-JOSE downstream TLS consumer can
  still resolve a semver-compatible ring/rustls version allowed by
  asupersync; the repository/release lock and SBOM record the exact
  tested graph but do not constrain that downstream resolution.
  FND-05 must test both the locked release graph and fresh downstream
  lowest/latest-compatible resolutions, and word support accordingly.
- If a required primitive is missing, create an explicit asupersync
  prerequisite issue and block HTTP implementation rather than adding
  another async ecosystem.

Acceptance:

- The spike passes on Linux, macOS, and Windows targets used by CI.
- HTTPS validates hostname and trust roots.
- Disconnect cancels a child scope.
- No Tokio, reqwest, hyper, or prohibited adapter enters the graph.
- No `ureq`, second HTTP/TLS policy stack, or TLS early-data path enters
  the graph.
- The final HTTP abstraction is revised from measured behavior, not
  assumed behavior.
- High-cardinality origins or policy revisions cannot retain unbounded
  sockets, TLS buffers, DNS work, pool identities, or acquisition
  waiters.
- The spike closes within five working days with either all probes
  green or explicit blocking upstream issues and captured reproducers.

Tests:

- Streaming round trip.
- Disconnect cancellation.
- Slow-reader backpressure.
- TLS valid, wrong-host, untrusted-root, and expired-certificate cases.
- TLS 1.3 replay server, host-supplied connector, resumption, and
  feature-unification tests proving no MCP/OAuth request byte is sent
  as 0-RTT early data.
- Stalled/partial ClientHello, accepted socket with no request,
  post-response keep-alive idle, total lifetime/request-count
  boundary, and shutdown in every phase.
- Uncoded request/response probes with absent `Content-Encoding`,
  lowercase/uppercase/mixed-case singleton `identity` receive
  positives, plus leading/interior/trailing bounded empty-element
  variants. Cover all-empty, empty-element N/N+1, parameterized,
  duplicate-field, multi-semantic-coding, and other-coding negatives,
  canonical lowercase `Accept-Encoding: identity`, omitted response
  `Content-Encoding`, and auto-decompression disabled.
- DNS and redirect hook cases.
- IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 well-known/local-use, 6to4,
  Teredo, alternate-spelling, embedded-private-IPv4, mixed-answer, and
  connected-peer destination tests plus IANA registry drift.
- Pool-key isolation and live/idle invalidation under peer-address,
  roots, client-auth, ALPN/SNI, proxy, CIDR-policy, and redirect-origin
  changes.
- High-cardinality origin/policy-revision churn, HTTP/1 nonmultiplexed
  pressure, half-open DNS/connect/TLS, per-origin/global acquisition
  saturation, idle/absolute expiry, borrowed-versus-idle eviction,
  policy/root/proxy rotation, stale-drain accounting, cancellation, and
  bounded shutdown/exact-once socket release.
- Direct client and server wrapper conformance proving byte-identical
  guarded-fetch destination/redirect/encoding/pool decisions without a
  crate dependency between those wrappers.
- Ambiguous transfer framing.
- `cargo tree` prohibited-dependency assertion.
- Locked-release versus fresh packaged-consumer TLS resolution/SBOM
  evidence and source/tree deny scans for `ureq` or another direct
  non-asupersync HTTP client.

Dependencies:

- FND-01.
- FND-04.
- LIMIT-01.

title: Workspace-input anchoring check can pass while carrying a false provenance anchor
description:
Found by ProudValley on bd-refresh-direct-dependency-pins-vc62o, confirmed by the orchestrator
re-reading the function, and filed here per his decision so the finding outlives the close reason
that was corrected because of it.

ANCHOR: measured source-only at commit:f8a47e3c against
crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs.

THE FUNCTION
    fn fnd_01_check_workspace_input_anchoring(
        bindings: &[(&str, u64, &str)], provenance: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Result<(), String>
It takes TWO COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT TABLES and NEVER TOUCHES THE FILESYSTEM. It asserts set-equality
over the path columns plus a 40-character all-hex shape on each revision. It does NOT assert that
the recorded commit produced the recorded bytes, AND IT CANNOT, because it never reads them.

BEHAVIOUR AGAINST THE SCENARIO THE OWNING BEAD WAS FILED ABOUT (a dependency-pin refresh)
    regenerate Cargo.lock, touch neither table    path sets equal, hex valid   -> PASSES
    update byte_length/sha, leave the provenance  -> PASSES, and the recorded commit now
        commit unchanged                             FALSELY CLAIMS to have produced those bytes
    add or remove a path                          set equality fires           -> CAUGHT
A PIN REFRESH DOES NOT CHANGE THE PATH SET. It changes bytes. So the named-provenance error fires
only on a dropped provenance ROW, which is the narrow case the existing planted negative models.

THE FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT A NOTE
Case 2 is WORSE THAN NO DETECTION. A refresher doing the conscientious thing -- updating the digest
to match the new bytes -- produces a PASSING CHECK CARRYING A FALSE ANCHOR. The provenance table
then asserts a commit that did not produce those bytes, and asserts it with a green. No check
invites scrutiny; a green does not. The false attestation is manufactured by the very table the
detection relies on.

GENERAL FORM, worth more than this instance: A CHECK SATISFIABLE BY UPDATING ONE HALF OF A PAIR CAN
MANUFACTURE A FALSE ATTESTATION THAT LOOKS VERIFIED. The diagnostic question is "what does this
check read that it does not control?" -- if both sides of every comparison come from the same
artifact, it is a self-consistency assertion, not verification, however many clauses it has.

SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE, ALREADY IN HAND: the REL071 evaluator
(tools/xtask/src/rel_071.rs, added at commit:54a7e589) has the same shape -- it compares two
recorded columns of one fixture and never reads disk, and it does not even shape-gate its commit
fields. That instance is being repaired under bd-reconcile-071-release-9t607 and is NOT in scope
here; it is cited only as evidence that the class recurs rather than being a one-off.

THE APPROVED REMEDY SHAPE (orchestrator decision 3), applicable to both instances
  - shape-gate the identity fields inside the PURE checker, and
  - put the anchored check that READS DISK in a SEPARATE test.
Keeping them separate is what lets "no mutation path" remain a structural property of the checker
rather than reverting to a promise its author must honour.

NOT URGENT. No reachable configuration exercises this today. It is filed because the next pin
refresh is exactly the configuration that would, and because the class recurs.

DELIBERATELY UNASSIGNED, per the gizte/t71jy precedent: routing it to an absent agent is the
failure those beads recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The check can no longer pass when byte_length/sha move while the provenance commit does not.
      Demonstrated by a planted negative that performs exactly that mutation and is RED, alongside
      an accepted row in the same test that remains green -- a negative that only proves "something
      fails" does not satisfy this item.
- [x] The anchored half READS the bytes it attests to, from disk or from git, rather than comparing
      two compile-time tables. An implementation where both sides of every comparison come from the
      same artifact fails this item regardless of how many clauses it has.
- [x] The pure checker retains no filesystem, network, or mutation path, and the disk-reading check
      lives in a separate test. An implementation that achieves anchoring by making the checker
      impure fails this item.
- [x] The identity fields are shape-gated, not only compared for equality, so two equal malformed
      values cannot pass.
- [x] The receipt states what the repaired check still cannot detect. A check that reads the tree
      still cannot establish that the tree is what any external party published.
- [x] Re-measured at the then-current HEAD rather than inherited from this bead's description; if
      the function has changed, the new state is reported rather than this text assumed.

HANDED TO RoseStream PER THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ASSIGNMENT. I had claimed this at 09:25, three
minutes before the assignment; releasing rather than defending it, and the reason is the
orchestrator's own aigxn condition applied to me.

WHY INDEPENDENCE FAVOURS RoseStream HERE, NOT ME:
"Two readers sharing a starting point share its blind spot, and you would be both readers."
I FOUND this defect, I MEASURED the three anchors, and I WROTE the analysis the bead is built
from. If I also verify it, the finding and its verification come from one instrument with one
set of assumptions. RoseStream is a genuinely independent reader. That is the same author/reviewer
separation that kept me off the .1.14 implementation surface earlier today.

=== WHAT I MEASURED, HANDED OVER TO BE RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN CITED ===
Do not carry these forward as inputs. They are where to look, and each should be re-taken.

1. THE MECHANISM. fnd_01_check_workspace_input_anchoring takes TWO COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT TABLES
   and never touches the filesystem:
       bound    = bindings.map(|(path, _, _)| path).collect::<BTreeSet>()
       anchored = provenance.map(|(path, _)| path).collect::<BTreeSet>()
       if bound != anchored { Err }
       for (path, revision) in provenance { require 40 chars, all hex }
   It asserts SET-EQUALITY ON PATHS plus a hex shape. It does not assert that the recorded commit
   produced the recorded bytes, and cannot, because it never reads them.

2. THE THREE CASES.
       regenerate Cargo.lock, touch neither table   -> PASSES (path sets equal, hex valid)
       update byte_length/sha, keep the old commit  -> PASSES, and the recorded commit now
                                                       FALSELY claims to have produced the bytes
       add or remove a path                         -> CAUGHT
   Case 2 is the bead's subject and is worse than no detection: the conscientious action
   (updating the digest to match) produces a PASSING check carrying a FALSE anchor.

3. WHETHER IT IS INSTANTIATED TODAY. I read each file at its recorded provenance commit and
   compared length + sha. All three came back TRUE ANCHOR at commit:f8a47e3c
   (Cargo.toml 7224 @ a7109f65, Cargo.lock 99964 @ a7109f65, rust-toolchain.toml 239 @ 6a7e8566).
   RE-DERIVE THIS FIRST. It is the load-bearing negative and it is the one most likely to have
   moved -- and my first pass at it under-matched, reporting 1 of 3 rows, because the table uses
   numeric separators (7_224, 99_964) and my regex stopped at the underscore.

4. WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE. The detector that closes case 2 is three git reads:
   `git show <commit>:<path>` and compare length+sha. IT CANNOT RUN ON THE FLEET -- RCH workers
   have no .git. That is the same constraint that left bd-veqqv's properties 2 and 3 UNPROVEN.
   The gap is structural, not an oversight, and any proposal that requires history at test time
   hits the same wall.

=== THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS BEAD ACTUALLY NEEDS ===
How do you bind provenance to bytes when the test environment has no repository history? Every
obvious answer needs the thing the workers lack. That is a design problem, not a measurement, and
it is why this bead needs a reader rather than a run.

tms93/SilentSquirrel, ready queue at 0. The routing was right; the addressing was not.

cheap card would settle it before you build an anchored check into 44sow. You do not need the card

comments.author: RoseStream
comments.text:
RoseStream, 2026-09-19. DESIGN ANALYSIS. Source-only, nothing edited, no slot — this is the half of
44sow the verification outage does not block. Anchored at b271be0d.

=== THE OBVIOUS REPAIR SITE IS BARRED ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS ===
fnd_01_check_workspace_input_anchoring lives at fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:50539. That file is
  authoring_write_paths[1]  under authoring_owner = ahet.1.14   -> not mine to edit under 44sow
  ordered_paths[1]          under quiet_window_rule             -> any byte change RESETS the freeze
So repairing it in place hits exactly what bd-i81v0 hit: wrong owner, and a sequencing constraint
with no third slot. Establishing this BEFORE writing anything is the whole reason to check first.

=== A SECOND SITE IS FREE OF ALL THREE CONSTRAINTS AND ALREADY HAS THE CAPABILITY ===
crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_a_evidence_binding.rs appears in NONE of authoring_write_paths,
ordered_paths or exact_root_files. It already contains, at :386:
    /// Reads the bytes of `path` as of `revision`, straight from Git object storage.
    /// Fails closed. A missing `git`, a detached object store, or an unknown revision is a
    /// hard failure rather than a skip, because a check that silently examines nothing is
    /// the exact defect this capability exists to remove.
    fn blob_at_revision(revision: &str, path: &str) -> Vec<u8>
That doc comment is AC-2's requirement already built, already fail-closed, and already reasoned
about in the terms this bead cares about.

=== BUT THE CAPABILITY CANNOT RUN WHERE RECEIPTS ARE MADE ===
    .rchignore:3   .git/
RCH syncs SOURCE, not the repository. Measured split in that file: 7 #[test], and blob_at_revision
is reached from exactly TWO —
    :519  fnd_01_a_closed_child_rows_match_their_closure_revisions
    :565  fnd_01_a_closure_revision_subject_planted_negative
So 2 of 7 take the git dependency and 5 do not. Those two cannot pass in a receipt-producing run,
at any hour, on any worker. The orchestrator confirmed the structural half and correctly flagged
that he read their panic from source rather than observing it.

=== THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN ===
    TREE anchor      hash over shipped paths       computable on a worker      ENFORCEABLE
    REVISION anchor  "commit X produced these bytes"  needs .git               NOT ENFORCEABLE
AND CASE 2 IS ONLY CLOSABLE BY THE REVISION ANCHOR. Re-read the scenario this bead was filed about:
the refresher updates byte_length/sha256 to match the new bytes and leaves the provenance commit.
A tree anchor reads the file and confirms the digest matches — IT DOES, that is the whole point of
Case 2. The digest is correct; the REVISION column is false. A hash over shipped paths cannot
evaluate "commit X produced these bytes", because the shipped tree carries one revision's bytes and
no history.
SO: AC-2 as written ("from disk or from git") is SATISFIABLE by the tree half, and the bead's TITLE
("can pass while carrying a false provenance anchor") describes the half that is not. Satisfying
the AC and closing the failure mode are different acts here, and a repair could do the first while
leaving the second untouched.

=== THE THIRD FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS THE DESIGN CENTRE RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE ===
A revision anchor written with `.git/HEAD` and `unwrap_or_default()` yields "" on a worker, fails
nothing, and the receipt goes GREEN CARRYING AN EMPTY ANCHOR. That is this bead's title reproduced
BY ITS OWN REPAIR. blob_at_revision's hard panic is therefore the correct shape and must not be
softened into a skip; its doc comment already says why.

=== PROPOSED SHAPE, FOR THE OWNER'S RULING RATHER THAN MY UNILATERAL EDIT ===
Two checks with DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENT DOMAINS, labelled as such at the site:
  1. TREE ANCHOR — reads each recorded path from disk, compares byte_length and sha256 against the
     binding table. Runs everywhere including receipt-producing runs. Catches digest-vs-bytes drift.
     Does NOT catch Case 2.
  2. REVISION ANCHOR — blob_at_revision(recorded_commit, path), compares to the recorded digest.
     Catches Case 2. PANICS rather than degrades where .git is absent, so its absence is loud.
     Enforceable only where receipts are not made.
What must NOT happen is (2)'s absence reading as satisfaction. If both live in one test, a worker
run panics; if they are separate tests, a worker run silently exercises only (1) and a reader sees
green. Neither is obviously right and the choice belongs with the owner of the enforcement policy.

=== WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED ===
Whether the two git-dependent tests actually panic on a worker, or are skipped by some mechanism I
have not found — the orchestrator offered to observe it and four dispatches have since failed
environmentally. I am not building on the reading as though it were the observation.
And I have not checked whether any OTHER check in the tree already binds commit-to-bytes for the
workspace-input rows specifically; blob_at_revision's two callers are about CLOSED-CHILD rows, which
is a different table.

SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-19. I APPLIED THIS BEAD'S OWN QUESTION TO MY OWN CHECK AND IT FAILED.
Prompted by the orchestrator's framing: not "is the attestation wrong today" but "what input
makes it report PASS while being false, and does that input occur".

=== THE DEFECT I BUILT INTO THE FIX FOR THIS BEAD ===
My property-3 predicate decided "is the anchor the latest mover?" from
    git log --format=%H -- <path>
Plain `git log -- <path>` applies HISTORY SIMPLIFICATION. Across a merge it omits commits
that really did modify the file. Measured on this repository, not assumed:

    path                  default log   --full-history   hidden
    Cargo.toml                 79            103            24
    Cargo.lock                114            134            20
    rust-toolchain.toml         7              9             2
    merge commits reachable from HEAD: 79

So the discriminating input is: A MODIFYING COMMIT THAT SIMPLIFICATION OMITS. Given that, my
check reports history[0] == anchor and PASSES while a later commit has in fact moved the
path. That is precisely the shape this bead exists to close -- a check that passes while
carrying a false premise -- reproduced inside its own repair.

DOES THE INPUT OCCUR? Not as a wrong verdict today: 0df68bfe survives simplification, so both
drifting rows still reported correctly. The mechanism is present and latent, not live. I am
recording it at that strength and no higher.

=== BUT IT DID CORRUPT A NUMBER I PUBLISHED ===
My earlier comment and mail said Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock each had "1 unaccounted commit"
since their anchor. Under --full-history the anchor sits at POSITION 3, not position 1.
    CORRECTED: 3 later commits touched each path since a7109f65, not 1.
The VERDICT was right and the COUNT was wrong, understated by exactly the commits
simplification was hiding. Correcting it here rather than leaving a figure that reads precise.

=== THE REPAIR: CONTENT IS NOW THE TRIGGER, THE LOG IS ONLY ATTRIBUTION ===
    blob_at_revision(anchor, path)  vs  blob_at_revision("HEAD", path)
Byte comparison out of object storage cannot be defeated by history traversal AT ALL. The
commit list is now used only to ATTRIBUTE a drift that content has already proven, so a
traversal defect can at worst degrade the error message -- it can no longer flip the verdict.
commits_touching() additionally passes --full-history, with the measurement above recorded in
its doc comment so the flag cannot be "cleaned up" later as redundant.

TWO TRIGGERS, DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED:
    CONTENT DRIFT   bytes at HEAD differ from bytes at the anchor. The recorded digest no
                    longer describes the tree. This is what a pin refresh produces.
    LATER TOUCHER   bytes identical, but a later commit touched the path (a revert, a no-op
                    rewrite). Digest still true; only the attribution is stale.
Collapsing these to content alone would be narrowing the declared property -- ":50494 says
the anchor is the LATEST COMMIT TOUCHING that path" -- to whatever currently passes. That is
RH-1, so the weaker condition is still reported, just labelled as the weaker one.

=== VERDICTS RE-DERIVED UNDER THE REPAIRED PREDICATE ===

    Cargo.lock            CONTENT DRIFT   anchor 99,964 / HEAD 100,009      anchor at pos 3
    rust-toolchain.toml   clean           content identical, anchor at pos 0 under full history
NO NEW FALSE POSITIVE: the row that passed before still passes. --full-history lengthened
every list but did not displace rust-toolchain.toml's anchor from position 0, which was the
way this repair could have gone wrong and did not.

=== VERIFICATION AND ITS CEILING, UNCHANGED ===
rustc -Zparse-crate-root-only: exit 0, 0 bytes stderr. Logic re-validated by mirroring the
predicate against real object storage. STILL NOT TYPECHECKED -- cargo is RCH-hooked, no local

comments.text:
SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-19. THE DISCRIMINATING CASE, AND IT HAS ALREADY OCCURRED TWICE.
Answering the orchestrator's question in its own terms: what input makes the attestation
report PASS while being false, and DOES THAT INPUT OCCUR.

=== A FALSE GAP I ALMOST FILED, RETRACTED BEFORE IT TRAVELLED ===
I measured that 3 of the 12 exact_root_files carry a provenance anchor and 9 do not, including
the 913KB policy itself, and was about to report a population gap. THE SOURCE REFUTES IT. The
doc comment above the constant defines the real class:
    "A sweep of all ten bindings in this class found exactly these two stale and the other
     eight clean - rust-toolchain.toml and all seven evidence artifacts still match, because
     those are frozen artifacts nobody edits."
The class is TEN bindings: 3 toolchain/workspace inputs + 7 evidence artifacts. README.md,
LICENSE, .gitignore and the rest were never in it. "3 of 12" would have been a defect invented
by choosing the wrong population. Retracted; recording it because the next reader will compute
the same 12 and reach the same wrong conclusion.

=== THE REAL FINDING: THE CONSTANTS ROTTED A SECOND TIME, TWO DAYS AFTER A MANUAL REPAIR ===
The doc comment describes a DELIBERATE, CAREFUL re-attest - it enumerates the drift hunk by
hunk ("11 packages added, 2 removed, 87 version lines changed, ZERO hunks outside
name/version/checksum/source/dependencies"), explains why both rows had to move together, and
states plainly what it does not prove. It is the best-executed version of this repair anyone
could reasonably perform.

    db1c1766   08-30 00:43   the drift base the comment reasons from
    a7109f65   09-17 08:06   the re-attest anchors both rows here
    0df68bfe   09-19 03:25   moves BOTH files again

    path                  re-attested to    HEAD        verdict
    Cargo.toml                 7,224        7,475       ROTTED AGAIN
    Cargo.lock                99,964      100,009       ROTTED AGAIN
    rust-toolchain.toml          239          239       still holds

IT HELD FOR UNDER 48 HOURS. And the split is exactly the one the comment predicted: the two
volatile rows rotted as a GROUP, the eight it called stable stayed stable. Its own thesis -
"frozen constants measuring one artifact rot as a GROUP" - is confirmed by the very rot that
followed it.

=== SO THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION, STATED PRECISELY ===
INPUT: any commit that edits Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock without updating the constants.
WHY IT PASSES: fnd_01_check_workspace_input_anchoring compares only PATH SETS and a 40-hex
SHAPE. A pin refresh changes neither. Set equality holds, hex is valid, the check returns Ok.
WHY IT IS FALSE: the recorded digests now describe a tree that no longer exists, and the
recorded commit is no longer the one that produced the bytes on disk.
DOES IT OCCUR: YES. TWICE IN 19 DAYS - db1c1766..a7109f65, then a7109f65..0df68bfe - the
second time within two days of a deliberate manual repair by someone who understood the
mechanism and documented it thoroughly.

THAT IS THE CASE FOR THIS BEAD, and it is stronger than the original filing. The filing called
this NOT URGENT because "no reachable configuration exercises this today". The configuration is
not merely reachable; it is the steady state. Hand re-attestation is not a mechanism that
failed once - it is a mechanism that cannot hold, because it requires a human to notice
something no check reports.

=== WHAT THE REPAIR DOES ABOUT IT ===
The revision anchor added under this bead detects both rows automatically, from content rather
than from anyone noticing:
    Cargo.toml   CONTENT DRIFT since a7109f65 - anchor 7,224 bytes, HEAD 7,475; 3 later commits
    Cargo.lock   CONTENT DRIFT since a7109f65 - anchor 99,964, HEAD 100,009; 3 later commits
    rust-toolchain.toml   clean
It does not repair the rows - re-attestation stays with the mover, per :50500 - but it removes
the requirement that a human notice.

=== STATE UNCHANGED ===
Parse clean. STILL NOT TYPECHECKED, and blocked: HEAD does not compile (fastmcp-client E0615 at
admission.rs:257, RoseStream's), and crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml:94 puts fastmcp-client in

comments.text:
SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-19. "A GREEN FROM AN INSTRUMENT YOU HAVE NOT SEEN FAIL IS NOT
EVIDENCE." Applied to my own greens. It found a defect in my diagnostic and a design
justification I had not earned.

=== THE GREEN I COULD NOT JUSTIFY ===
P3 reports rust-toolchain.toml CLEAN. My planted negative plants on Cargo.toml -- the first row
with >=2 commits -- so I had NEVER seen either predicate fail ON THAT ROW. Its green was
unearned in exactly the sense named.

Four controls run against it. All four fire:
    A  stale anchor planted on THIS row        CONTENT DRIFT reported     fires
    B  fabricated 40-hex anchor, absent        git cat-file refuses -> blob_at_revision
                                               PANICS, fail-closed        fires
    C  one digest character flipped            P2 reports mismatch        fires
    D  recorded length moved by one byte       P2 reports mismatch        fires
The row's green is now evidence. Before this it was an assumption wearing a test's clothes.

=== CONTROL A EXPOSED A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN MESSAGE ===
    CONTENT DRIFT since d0517dfe - anchor 239 bytes, HEAD 239 bytes; 1 later commit(s)...
EQUAL BYTE COUNTS, AND THE CHECK STILL SAYS DRIFT. That reads as a contradiction and would
have been reported to me as "your check is broken". It is not. The bytes genuinely differ:

    d0517dfe:rust-toolchain.toml    channel = "nightly-2026-08-31"
    HEAD:rust-toolchain.toml        channel = "nightly-2026-08-25"
    239 bytes both ways.

A TOOLCHAIN CHANNEL CHANGE THAT IS BYTE-LENGTH NEUTRAL. That is precisely the drift FND-01
exists to catch, and A LENGTH-ONLY COMPARISON WOULD HAVE MISSED IT ENTIRELY.

Two things follow:
1. FIXED: the CONTENT DRIFT message now carries BOTH DIGESTS, not only lengths, so a
   same-length edit is legible instead of looking like an instrument fault. The reason is
   recorded in the doc comment at the site with this exact example, so it cannot be
   "simplified" back to lengths later.
2. EARNED: comparing full bytes rather than lengths was a choice I made without a
   justification. It now has one, from an observed case rather than from reasoning.

=== AND THE PLANTED NEGATIVES SURVIVED A REWRITE I HAD ONLY REASONED ABOUT ===
I rewrote P3 to be content-first AFTER writing its planted negative, and argued from the
message text that the negative still discriminated. Argued, not measured -- the same defect
class this bead exists to close. Measured now, by mirroring both negatives against real
object storage:
    NEGATIVE 1 digest-move      target REFUSED, witness Cargo.lock STAYED GREEN -> isolated
    NEGATIVE 2 stale-anchor     survives the rewrite: reports CONTENT DRIFT containing
                                "1 later commit(s)" and naming latest 0df68bfe -> assertion holds
    POSITIVE P2                 GREEN     POSITIVE P3     RED on Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock
My reasoning happened to be right. It was still reasoning, and one of the two rewrites this
session was not right ([[comment 6]], the log-simplification hole).

=== ONE TRAP I HIT IN MY OWN MIRROR, NOT IN THE SHIPPED CODE ===
Control C printed "recorded 239B/aa154c661832, anchor holds 239B/aa154c661832" -- a MISMATCH
rendered as two identical strings, because my mirror truncated digests to 12 characters and
the flipped character was the last one. The shipped Rust prints full digests, so the shipped
message is fine. But it is a clean demonstration that TRUNCATING A DIGEST IN A DIAGNOSTIC CAN
MAKE A MISMATCH LOOK LIKE A MATCH. Never abbreviate a digest in a refusal message.

=== STATE ===
Parse clean: rustc -Zparse-crate-root-only exit 0, 0 bytes stderr.

and crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml:94 puts it in fastmcp-rust's closure.

comments.text:
SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-19. TYPECHECKED, not merely parsed. Zero slot. This de-risks the one
outstanding dispatch rather than waiting idle for it.

=== THE METHOD ===
cargo is RCH-hooked and there is no local target dir, so the full target cannot be built here.
But rustc is NOT shimmed, and the 44sow additions reach into fastmcp_rust through exactly FOUR
helpers. Extracted all 504 lines of the additions into a standalone crate with those four
replaced by signature-identical stubs:

    rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type lib --emit=metadata standalone.rs
    exit 0, stderr 0 bytes

That is a real typecheck: types, borrows, slice patterns, let-else divergence, method
resolution, format-string arity. Everything the parse check could not see.

=== THE HARNESS IS VALIDATED, BECAUSE A GREEN FROM AN UNFALSIFIED INSTRUMENT IS NOT EVIDENCE ===
Six planted errors, all caught:
    A   format string arity, one arg dropped          exit 1  "7 positional arguments ... but"
    B1  String assigned into the usize field          exit 1  E0308 mismatched types
    B2  parameter type changed &str -> usize          exit 1  E0308 mismatched types
    B3  predicate return type Vec<String> -> Vec<usize>  exit 1  E0308 mismatched types
    C   move out of a borrowed slice pattern          exit 1  E0507 cannot move out of *path
    D   undefined identifier                          exit 1  E0425 cannot find function
Subject re-checked after each: exit 0, 0 bytes.

AND ONE CONTROL THAT PASSED, WHICH WAS MY CONTROL'S FAULT, NOT A BLIND SPOT. My first B
replaced `byte_length.replace(..)` with `byte_length.len().to_string().replace(..)` -- still
String, still .parse()s to usize, so NOTHING WAS PLANTED. exit 0 was correct. I rebuilt it as
B1/B2/B3 rather than reporting "5 of 6 fire", because "the instrument missed one" and "I handed
it a non-error" are different claims and only one of them is about the instrument.

=== THE RESULT TRANSFERS ONLY IF THE STUBS MATCH THE REAL CONTRACT, SO I CHECKED ===
    workspace_root() -> PathBuf                              MATCH
    blob_at_revision(revision: &str, path: &str) -> Vec<u8>  MATCH
    live_sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String                  MATCH
    flip_one_digest_character(digest: &str) -> String        MATCH

AND MY FIRST COMPARISON REPORTED A FALSE DIVERGENCE, caused by my own normalizer. I normalized
the stubs' unused-parameter underscores with `sed s/_revision/revision/`, which struck the
underscore INSIDE `blob_at_revision` and produced `blob_atrevision`, then diffed that against
the real name and declared a mismatch. The signatures were identical the whole time. A
normalizer that rewrites its subject before comparing can manufacture the difference it is
meant to detect -- the second time today a tool of mine has fabricated a finding.

=== WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===
ESTABLISHED: every line I added is well-typed against the real helper signatures, and the
harness that says so has been shown to fail on six distinct error classes.
NOT ESTABLISHED: the four stubbed BODIES; anything depending on fastmcp_rust's real types
(sha256_bounded, MAX_BOUND_SOURCE_BYTES, the evidence_binding imports); and above all
EXECUTION. AC-1 requires the planted negatives to be RED IN A RUN. A typecheck cannot deliver
that and a Python mirror cannot either, however faithful. The dispatch is still required:
    cargo test -p fastmcp-rust --test fnd_01_a_evidence_binding --no-run
then the run itself for AC-1.

What changed is the risk profile. The realistic failure mode for that dispatch was a type error
in 389 lines nobody had compiled; that class is now closed.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-19. THIRD FALSE-PASS INPUT, IN THE GUARD I BUILT TO CLOSE THE SECOND.
AND MY FIRST FIX FOR IT WAS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT. Caught only by running the control.

=== THE THIRD INPUT ===
Comment 7 closed "a declaration outliving its use" with
assert_workspace_input_tables_are_live(), which requires a call to the pure checker consuming
both constants. That guard is a RAW SUBSTRING SCAN, so it proves the call TEXT exists, not that
the call is live. Measured against the real source:

    every call site COMMENTED OUT          live = 2   GUARD STILL PASSES
    call sites behind an OFF #[cfg(..)]    live = 2   GUARD STILL PASSES
    call text inside a string literal      live = 2   counted as live
    CONTROL: constants rewired away        live = 0   fires correctly

So the guard I added to refuse a dead declaration could itself be satisfied by a dead call. Same
defect, one level up, for the third time in this bead. I have a standing note to myself titled
"a substring test is not a syntax test" and I wrote one anyway.

=== THE FIX I WROTE FIRST, AND WHY IT WAS WORSE ===
I added strip_rust_comments() handling both // and /* */, and argued in its doc comment that
crudeness was safe because "over-stripping can only REMOVE apparent call sites, which makes the
guard FIRE". The direction was right. THE MAGNITUDE WAS CATASTROPHIC.

    baseline real source, with that stripper:  live = 0   *** REGRESSION ***

Cause: the verifier contains `/*` INSIDE STRING LITERALS - glob patterns like "/*" and
"dist/**" - and holds 7 `/*` against only 2 `*/`. One unmatched opener consumed
2,102,460 of 4,001,124 characters (53% of the file), both call sites included.

So the guard would have read 0 live sites on perfectly good source and FAILED FOR EVERYONE,
PERMANENTLY. "Fails closed" is not automatically safe: for a guard that is supposed to always
pass, failing closed means a permanent red that blocks the very run this bead needs. A safe
error direction and a safe error MAGNITUDE are different properties, and I checked only the
first.

=== THE FIX THAT SURVIVES ITS CONTROLS ===
strip_line_comments() blanks `//` to end of line and leaves block comments alone.

                                    no-strip   line-only   verdict
    real source (must PASS)            2           2         OK
    all calls commented (must FIRE)    2           0         OK
    rewired away (must FIRE)           0           0         OK
    chars removed: 57,273 of 4,001,124 (1.4%), against 53% for the block version.

A `//` inside a string truncates that one line - bounded damage, and it can only make the guard
fire. The 2.1M-character measurement is recorded IN the function's doc comment so nobody
"completes" it later by re-adding block-comment handling.

=== RESIDUAL LIMITS, STATED ON THE GUARD ITSELF ===
A call behind an OFF #[cfg(..)], and the literal call text inside a string, both still read as
live. Neither is plausible as an accident. The guard's strength is "the call text exists outside
line comments", NOT "the call executes", and it must not be cited as the latter.

=== TALLY: THREE FALSE-PASS INPUTS, ALL MINE, ALL IN THIS BEAD'S OWN REPAIR ===
  1 (comment 6)  P3 decided staleness from a simplification-prone `git log`
  2 (comment 7)  the parse bound to a DECLARATION rather than a USE
  3 (this one)   the guard closing #2 could be satisfied by a COMMENTED-OUT call
Each was found by asking the bead's own question of my own work rather than of the subject.
Knowing the family by name has not once prevented an instance; asking the question has caught
all three.

=== STATE ===
parse: exit 0, 0 bytes.  standalone TYPECHECK with stubbed helpers: exit 0, 0 bytes.
Still unexecuted. AC-1 needs the planted negatives RED in a real run.

Surface 4 (and 44sow) need a host carrying `.git`. I looked for one rather than just naming the
requirement.

== WHAT I CHECKED ==
  LOCAL MACHINE       `.git` present, `git status` works. BUT: Darwin/arm64, no built producer in
                      target/debug/examples, and building one means `cargo`, which a PreToolUse
                      hook routes to RCH -- back to the git-less worker. The declared target for
                      this evidence is x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu regardless.
  RCH FLEET           13 workers. `.rchignore` line 3 excludes `.git/` for a stated reason:
                      "avoids remote ownership drift blocking source sync." Not an oversight.
  DSR                 RULE 0.5 names it the sanctioned build path and `dsr build` says "Build
                      artifacts locally". Whether its build hosts carry a checkout with history is
                      a question for whoever owns DSR routing; `dsr health` needs a hostname I do
                      not have, and I am not probing release infrastructure on a hunch.

== *** THE WORKAROUND SOMEBODY WILL PROPOSE, AND WHY IT IS FORBIDDEN *** ==
"Just `git init` on the worker so `git status` succeeds."

IT WOULD NOT EVEN WORK, and the reason matters more than the fact. The producer does not merely
need `git status` to exit 0. From source:

    sdk_git_oid(root, &["rev-parse", "--verify", revision], subject)
    -> requires a 40-character lowercase hex OID, validated byte by byte:
       if value.len() != 40 || !value.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&b))
           return Err(... .at("git OID"))

It resolves a NAMED REVISION to a real object. A fresh `git init` has no such object, so the
guard fires one step later with `git OID` instead of `git observation` -- a different message,
the same void.

AND MAKING IT WORK WOULD BE WORSE THAN FAILING. To satisfy it you would have to create commits on
the worker so that `rev-parse --verify <revision>` resolves. That is MANUFACTURING THE PROVENANCE
THE GATE EXISTS TO OBSERVE. FND-01's whole purpose is binding evidence to authoritative inputs;
synthesising a repository to make the binding succeed inverts it. A green obtained that way would
be the most expensive false positive in this campaign, because every downstream bead inherits it.

SO: no `git init` on a worker, no committing on a worker, no fabricated OIDs, and no "temporarily"
relaxing the `!stderr.is_empty()` guard at :47921. That guard is strict on purpose -- it fails even
a SUCCESSFUL git that writes a warning to stderr, which is the correct posture for a provenance
observation.

== WHAT A LEGITIMATE ROUTE LOOKS LIKE ==
A host that already has an authentic checkout of THIS repository at the revision under test, with
history, reached by a sanctioned path. That is a routing/infrastructure decision with an owner, and
it is the same decision 44sow has been waiting on. It is not a code change to the producer, not a
change to `.rchignore`, and not a retry.

== WHAT I AM NOT DOING ==
Not proposing that `.rchignore` ship `.git`. Its exclusion has a stated engineering reason and
changing fleet-wide sync behaviour to unblock one surface is a structure-owner call with
consequences I cannot see from here.
Not relaxing any guard. That is RH-1 in its purest form.
Not declaring surface 4 unsatisfiable. It is EVALUABLE -- just not on RCH. Unsatisfiable and
unrouted are different, and conflating them would license exactly the AC-amendment shortcut I have
refused three times tonight.

Two facts that bound the options:

    running and finding no repo -- not "command not found". Only the repository is missing.
  - .git is 539 MiB against 41 MiB of crates/. Syncing it multiplies the per-job payload by

      and reintroduces the remote-ownership-drift risk the comment was written to avoid. I would
      argue against it: it taxes every job for a handful of tests.
