title: FND-01 [1]: 397 evidence digests have committed preimages but no stated canonical encoding, so only a build can check them
description:
CORRECTION 2026-09-22, BY MagentaSummit, THE FILER AND CRITERIA AUTHOR, under WildMountain rulings #19
(RH-10 direction: TIGHTENING. It narrows what closing this bead can claim; it removes no requirement).
THE PREMISE BELOW WAS FALSE AT FILING. The observation encoding FND01OBSv1 has been DECLARED in
evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml [assertion_contract] since 3d1d9a55 (2026-07-30), seven
weeks before this bead was filed (2026-09-21). It declares the header, the toml/json/raw kind bytes,
path_encoding, selector_tuple_encoding, value_sequence, the domains and tags 0x00-0x0a, with the
selector grammar in mutation_contract. I re-verified this at 3d1d9a55 myself. I missed it by
screening for key names instead of reading the table.
Proof that the declared prose is sufficient: bd-jpmay (closed 21:12:34Z; receipt 5550) reproduced
376/376 observation digests from that prose alone, 188 baseline + 188 violating, on the first attempt.
Its readings were committed before the run, and they did not use this bead's specs.
WHAT WAS GENUINELY UNDECLARED, and is this bead's real contribution: the EFFECT of each of the nine
mutation operations. mutation_contract states their argument requirements and the FND01MUTv2
recipe-table encoding, but only one effect (insert-cr-before-lf). The 188 violating rows needed those
effects stated somewhere. bca57's C1(c) spec (comment 5441, landed at aa243b98) is the first place
they are.
Consequences, recorded here rather than left implicit: the "397 ... no stated canonical encoding"
headline, the claim that "a maintainer holding the input still cannot produce the digest without
building", and the "166 -> 563 of 934" arithmetic in WHAT THIS IS WORTH are all wrong as written. The
original text is RETAINED BELOW, unedited, so that the error stays visible. The GATE and DELETION
CONDITION sections below carry dated amendments.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (2026-09-21), RETAINED:

397 declared SHA-256 digests in the FND-01 evidence set have a COMMITTED preimage but no stated
canonical encoding, so a maintainer can only check them by running the code that produced them.

Filed by MagentaSummit on WildMountain's ratification of the FND-01 bullet [1] second-party pass
(bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1 comment 4509). Counts re-derived at filing time, not carried
from the pass.

## CONSUMER
FND-01 bullet [1], "A maintainer can reproduce every checksum", and any future maintainer
auditing the frozen inputs.

## THE DEFECT
    baseline_observation_sha256    188   evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml
    violating_observation_sha256   188   evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml
    canonical_closure_sha256        21   evidence/fnd-01/tasks-apps.toml
    TOTAL                          397
For each of these the INPUT IS IN THE REPOSITORY. Worked example,
dependency-verification.toml:9499-9509:
    source_path      = "evidence/fnd-01/probes/envelope/Cargo.toml"    <- a committed 14-line file
    selector         = "/dependencies"
    baseline_mode    = "canonical_source_value"
    observation_mode = "canonical_selected_toml"
    baseline_observation_sha256 = "13e475d8ae56261f65f8de40bb20aaa918b95653b7286a45411e9640bb27623a"
Nothing here is observed at runtime. What cannot be applied by hand is the BYTE ENCODING: the
transform lives in `observation_digest()` at crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:28471,
which parses the TOML, applies the selector, canonicalises and hashes. A maintainer holding the
input still cannot produce the digest without building and running the crate.
The `canonical_closure_sha256` rows have the same shape: tasks-apps.toml:2361-2363 places
`schema_closure = [...]` directly above the digest of it, with no encoding stated.

## THE IN-REPO PRECEDENT THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP
This evidence set ALREADY documents a canonical encoding precisely enough to implement in ten
lines of any language. evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml:172, verbatim:
    canonical_encoding = "ASCII FND01WORKv1 followed by NUL, then u32be file count, then for each
    workspace_binding in ordering: u32be path byte length, path bytes, u64be file byte length, and
    raw 32-byte SHA-256 of exact file bytes"
The work is to do the same for `canonical_selected_toml` / `canonical_source_value` observations
and for the closure digest. It is a DOCUMENTATION change, not a verification run, and it requires
no RCH slot to land.

## WHAT THIS IS WORTH
Bullet [1] currently stands at 166 of 934 digests reproducible with no build -- 22 vendor
file-content digests (WildMountain) plus 144 fixture digests (MagentaSummit), established by two
parties with zero RCH dispatches. Fixture digests are hand-reproducible because each carries its
own preimage inline: `{ literal = '...', byte_length = N, sha256 = "..." }`, verified on three
of them including a byte_length cross-check. Documenting these 397 encodings would take the
reproducible-without-a-build count from 166 to 563 of 934.

## WHO MAY NOT DO THIS WORK, AND WHY
NOT MagentaSummit. I declined to reproduce an observation digest by reimplementing the
canonicaliser, because a reimplementation that agrees with the constant is equally consistent with
"the digest is correct" and "the reimplementer repeated the original's mistake" -- especially when
the reimplementation was written by reading the original. Writing the ENCODING SPEC from that same
reading carries the identical defect one step removed: the spec would be my reading of the code,
and a third party reproducing a digest from my spec would be confirming my reading, not the
digest.
REQUIRED SEQUENCE: this bead's owner writes the encodings; a THIRD party, neither the owner nor
me, reproduces one observation digest and one closure digest BY HAND from the written spec. The
separation is what makes the reproduction mean anything.

## GATE
A third party reproduces, by hand and with no build, one `baseline_observation_sha256` and one
`canonical_closure_sha256` from the written encoding spec, and both match the declared values.
AMENDED 2026-09-22 (rulings #19), NAMING WHAT GOVERNS EACH HALF, SO NOTHING IS SUPERSEDED SILENTLY:
- The observation half stands as written: one `baseline_observation_sha256` reproduced by a third
  party from the written spec.
- The `canonical_closure_sha256` half is GOVERNED BY C11 and is NOT required of this bead. The 21
  closure rows moved to bd-8dzq6 under C11. There, RoseStream reproduced them 21/21 from the
  encoding tasks-apps.toml already declares ([apps.sdk_1_29_0.standard_reuse_closure]; 8dzq6
  #5406), and 8dzq6's A15 adds a build-time recompute.
- While 8dzq6 is not closed (it is review + batch-pending at this amendment), C11's own
  condition governs: if 8dzq6 closes without its bar met, the 21 rows are this bead's debt again.

## DELETION CONDITION
The encodings are documented in the evidence TOMLs in the style of
dependency-verification.toml:172, and the gate reproduction succeeds.
AMENDED 2026-09-22 (rulings #19): the observation encoding was already documented (see the
correction at the top). What must be documented for this condition is the mutation-effect
specification (C1(c)), landed as a comment block at aa243b98. The closure encoding is out of scope
per C11 / bd-8dzq6, as in the amended GATE.

## WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLAIM
Not that the 397 digests are wrong -- nobody has checked them, which is the point. Not that the
remaining 371 unclassified digests split the same way. Not that documenting an encoding validates
the digest it describes; it makes the digest CHECKABLE, and the checking is the gate above.
acceptance_criteria:
AUTHORED BY MagentaSummit, 2026-09-21, under WildMountain's ruling that a lane may write criteria
for a bead it will not implement. SEPARATION ON THE RECORD: I filed this bead, I wrote these
criteria, and I WILL NOT IMPLEMENT IT.

AMENDED 2026-09-22 BY MagentaSummit, THE AUTHOR, at 8b6a6f71, answering MagentaOsprey's C1
question (comment 5200) routed by WildMountain (5208/5209). MagentaOsprey was right and stopped
correctly. THREE THINGS CHANGED: the word "five", the closure rows, and a scope gap neither of us
had named. What I got wrong is recorded in the ruling comment, not hidden in this rewrite.

FROZEN POPULATION, originally re-derived at 4e48b86a, RE-MEASURED AT 8b6a6f71 and unchanged (do not
inherit these from the description; they are restated here because the criteria are measured
against them):
    baseline_observation_sha256    188      violating_observation_sha256  188
    canonical_closure_sha256        21      TOTAL                         397
I WROTE THAT THE 397 ARE COVERED BY "EXACTLY FIVE ENCODINGS". THAT IS WRONG. I counted MODE VALUES
and a family name and called the total "encodings". The structure has THREE byte encodings, and
they are discriminated by a single `kind` byte in `observation_digest`
(fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:28483-28490), keyed on `observation_mode` ALONE:
    0x01  canonical_selected_toml    181 assertions   -> 362 of the digest rows below
    0x03  raw_source_bytes             6 assertions   ->  12
    0x02  canonical_selected_json      1 assertion    ->   2   <-- THE SINGLETON, STILL NAMED
`canonical_source_value` IS NOT AN ENCODING. It is `baseline_mode`, it is invariant across all 188
rows (measured), and it NEVER ENTERS `observation_digest` -- that function does not read the field.
It selects WHICH DOCUMENT is observed: one call site (:29522) produces BOTH digests of a row, and
the pristine-vs-overlaid document is the only difference between them. The one canonical byte
stream it does appear in is FND01ASTv2 (:29650), where it is hashed as an ordinary string FIELD
alongside the others -- encoded, not an encoding.
THE 21 canonical_closure_sha256 ROWS LEAVE THIS BEAD. They are not undocumented; they are
UNPRODUCED. Disposition and the successor bead are in C11.

- [x] C1. THE THREE ENCODINGS, THE DOCUMENT RULE, AND THE MUTATION ALGEBRA ARE ALL STATED. AMENDED 2026-09-22; the original demanded "all five encodings" and was wrong twice over. ENCODING. And "five encodings" is three encodings plus a document selector. MagentaOsprey, owner.

## 2. FOUR OF THE FIVE ARE ONE FUNCTION; canonical_source_value IS NOT AN ENCODING

`observation_digest()` (:28471) produces BOTH the baseline and the violating digest. One call site
at :29522; the branch at :29525 vs :29531 selects which declared value to compare against, and the
input differs only by `assertion_document(corpus, overlay, ...)` -- pristine vs overlaid. And
`baseline_mode` is VALIDATED AT :29784 to always equal the literal "canonical_source_value".

So it is an invariant naming WHICH DOCUMENT is observed, not a byte format. Writing five encoding
specifications would emit two identical specs under different names and send a maintainer looking
for a format that does not exist.

DERIVED FROM STRUCTURE, NOT FROM OUTPUT (C6):
    ASCII "FND01OBSv1" NUL
    u8 kind: 0x01 canonical_selected_toml | 0x02 canonical_selected_json | 0x03 raw_source_bytes
    u32be len + source_path bytes
    u32be selector count; per selector u32be len + selector bytes
    per selector: the selected value, tagged
  TOML value tags (recursive, self-delimiting): 0x00 absent | 0x02 bool+u8 | 0x03 int+i64be
    | 0x04 float+f64 bits BE | 0x05 string+u64be len+UTF-8 | 0x06 array+u64be count+elements
    | 0x07 table+...
  All widths big-endian (`to_be_bytes` throughout ObservationEncoder).
  Domain rules that belong in the prose: raw_source_bytes requires EXACTLY ONE selector
  (E_OBSERVATION_DOMAIN), its selector must parse to ["bytes", "end"|<integer>], and a
  mode/document mismatch is a domain error rather than a coercion.

## 3. THE FINDING: THE 21 CLOSURE DIGESTS ARE NOT MERELY UNDOCUMENTED, THEY ARE UNCHECKED

    git grep 'schema_closure'            in the verifier -> ZERO occurrences
    git grep 'canonical_closure_sha256'  in the verifier -> ONE occurrence, :67135

    mutate -- not a producer and not a comparison.

Nothing in this repository computes a closure digest from `schema_closure`, and nothing compares
the declared value against anything. The rows are protected only as BYTES INSIDE A LARGER SUBTREE
DIGEST of the manifest, which detects that the field changed and says nothing about whether it was
ever correct.

THAT IS A STRONGER DEFECT THAN THIS BEAD STATES. The body says these digests can be checked "only
by running the code that produced them". For these 21 there is no such code. A build does not check
them either.

## 4. AND THEY MAY NOT BE REPRODUCIBLE AT ALL

Row 1 (tasks-apps.toml:2355-2364): symbol CallToolRequest, schema_closure_count = 9, a
lexicographically sorted 9-element array, canonical_closure_sha256 =
34caa08b46efc29050a1e9db35a9f580729201c77b22827c27fc73b6647816d0.

concat, NUL-joined, comma-joined, JSON compact, JSON spaced, u32be count + sized entries, u64be
count + sized entries, and three FND01-style framed variants with domain prefixes.
ZERO MATCHES. Full candidate/digest table in my session log.

That does not prove the value is wrong -- the input may include fields I did not feed it
(symbol, method, role, sdk_schema_export, the count), or a domain prefix I did not guess. It does
establish that the obvious canonical forms do not reproduce it, which is exactly the maintainer
experience bullet [1] is about.

## 5. WHAT I AM ASKING THE AUTHOR, BEFORE I WRITE C1's PROSE

C1 says "ALL FIVE ENCODINGS ARE STATED, INCLUDING THE SINGLETON". Per section 2 there are THREE
byte encodings among the 376 observation rows, plus a document selector, plus whatever the closure
rows use. Does "five" count MODES or ENCODINGS? I will not resolve that silently on someone else's
criteria. If it counts modes, the prose states three formats and explains that baseline and
violating share one over different documents -- which is more useful than five entries, two
identical.

And if section 3 holds, the closure rows may not be a documentation item at all. Documenting an
encoding nothing implements, for values nothing checks, would produce prose that cannot be wrong
because nothing can contradict it.

# C2 checker has been written at the time of freezing, and the first-attempt C2 result will be

#   encode_json_observation :28352, toml_pointer_observation :28390, json_pointer_observation :28425,
#   parse_pointer :28036, StrictJson :24001

## PRIMITIVES (all integers BIG-ENDIAN, no padding, no alignment)
    byte(b)        one raw byte
    u32(n)         4-byte big-endian unsigned
    u64(n)         8-byte big-endian unsigned
    sized_u32(s)   u32(len(s)) followed by the len(s) raw bytes of s
    sized_u64(s)   u64(len(s)) followed by the len(s) raw bytes of s
A running byte-length bound (`max_receipt_toml_bytes`) refuses over-long encodings; it changes no
accepted byte.

## FRAME — identical for all three observation modes
    ASCII "FND01OBSv1" followed by NUL            (11 bytes: 46 4E 44 30 31 4F 42 53 76 31 00)
    byte(kind)                                    0x01 canonical_selected_toml
                                                  0x02 canonical_selected_json
                                                  0x03 raw_source_bytes
    sized_u32(source_path)                        the row's `source_path`, UTF-8
    u32(selector_count)                           1, or 2 when `secondary_selector` is present
    for each selector IN ORDER: sized_u32(selector)   primary first, then secondary
    <body, per mode>
    digest = SHA-256(all of the above)
The selector list is `[selector]` or `[selector, secondary_selector]`; ORDER IS NEVER SORTED.
`raw_source_bytes` REFUSES a second selector.

## SELECTOR RESOLUTION (JSON-Pointer-like; identical rules for TOML and JSON)
Syntax: must begin with "/", must not be exactly "/", at most 512 bytes, ASCII only, no ASCII
control bytes. Split on "/" after the leading "/"; every component must be non-empty; at most 16
components. Within a component "~0" decodes to "~" and "~1" decodes to "/"; a "~" followed by
anything else is an error.
Walk left to right from the document root:
  - at a table/object: look the component up as a key. MISSING KEY -> ABSENT (not an error).
  - at an array, component parses as an unsigned integer: index it. OUT OF RANGE -> ABSENT.
    (Parsed with a plain integer parse, so a non-canonical spelling such as "007" resolves to 7.)
  - at an array, component does not parse as an integer: it MUST contain "=", read as
    `key=expected`. Select the unique element that is a table/object whose `key` is a STRING
    exactly equal to `expected`. ZERO matches -> ABSENT. TWO OR MORE -> ERROR, "ambiguous named
    array selector". A component with no "=" here is an error.
  - at any scalar (i.e. path continues past a leaf) -> ABSENT.
ABSENT is a value, encoded as the single byte 0x00. It is NOT an error and NOT an empty string.

## BODY, kind 0x01 `canonical_selected_toml`
For each selector in order, emit the encoding of the resolved TOML value:
    absent      0x00
    boolean     0x02, then one byte 0x00 (false) or 0x01 (true)
    integer     0x03, then 8 bytes: the i64 big-endian two's-complement value
    float       0x04, then 8 bytes: the IEEE-754 binary64 BIT PATTERN, big-endian
                (f64::to_bits — NOT a decimal rendering)
    string      0x05, then sized_u64(UTF-8 bytes)
    array       0x06, then u64(element count), then each element encoded by these same rules
    table       0x07, then u64(entry count), then for each entry, in ASCENDING ORDER OF THE KEY'S
                RAW UTF-8 BYTES: sized_u32(key bytes), then the value by these same rules
    datetime    0x09, then sized_u64(the datetime's canonical TOML rendering, UTF-8)
Table ordering is BY KEY BYTES, not by document order and not by any locale collation.

## BODY, kind 0x02 `canonical_selected_json`
Same shape, one added tag and one different number rule:
    absent      0x00
    null        0x01
    boolean     0x02, then one byte 0x00/0x01
    string      0x05, then sized_u64(UTF-8 bytes)
    array       0x06, then u64(element count), then each element
    object      0x07, then u64(entry count), then for each entry, ASCENDING BY KEY UTF-8 BYTES:
                sized_u32(key bytes), then the value
    number      0x0a, then sized_u64(the number's canonical textual rendering, UTF-8)
NOTE ON OBJECT ORDER: the producer iterates a BTreeMap<String, _>, so ordering is byte-wise
ascending by key. There is no explicit sort in the JSON path; the ordering comes from the
container. The OBSERVABLE RULE is identical to the TOML table rule, and an implementer should
sort explicitly rather than rely on their own language's map order.
NOTE: 0x03/0x04/0x09 (TOML integer/float/datetime) NEVER appear under kind 0x02, and 0x01 (null)
and 0x0a (number) NEVER appear under kind 0x01. The tag spaces overlap but are not interchangeable.

## BODY, kind 0x03 `raw_source_bytes`
Exactly one selector, and it must have exactly two components: "bytes" followed by either "end" or
a component that parses as an unsigned integer. The selector is VALIDATED and then DISCARDED — it
does not choose a sub-range and does not otherwise affect the bytes. The body is:
    byte(0x08)
    sized_u64(the complete file bytes)
So the digest covers the whole file, with its length, under the frame above.

## (b) THE DOCUMENT RULE — A RULE, NOT A FOURTH ENCODING
`baseline_mode = "canonical_source_value"` is NOT a byte format and there is no
"canonical_source_value encoding" to look for. It states WHICH DOCUMENT is fed to the encoding
named by `observation_mode`:
    baseline_observation_sha256  = <the row's observation_mode encoding> over the PRISTINE
                                   committed document at `source_path`
    violating_observation_sha256 = THE SAME ENCODING, THE SAME frame, the same source_path and
                                   the same selectors, over the OVERLAID document — the pristine
                                   document with the row's ONE declared mutation applied
Nothing in the frame changes between the two digests: not the kind byte, not the source_path, not
the selector list. The ONLY difference is the document the selectors resolve against. Any
maintainer who reproduces a baseline digest has, by construction, everything needed to reproduce
its violating partner except the mutation semantics, which are C1(c).

## WHAT THIS SECTION DOES NOT COVER
The mutation algebra (C1(c)) — the 9 operations and the single integrity_mode — is written
separately. Until it is, the 188 violating rows remain unreproducible, and C3 is unmet.

# bca57 C1(c): the mutation algebra, the fixture axis, and the overlaid document

Companion to `bca57_C1_spec_v1.md` (C1(a) byte encodings and C1(b) document rule, frozen at
sha256 ddb215265befd2625459f5b27572988c2fdd2ca7f1be49dc7b94c277c45296b7). Written from the
producer's STRUCTURE at `crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs` blob 0d7c5579144a
(HEAD bb3cd3a1), cited by symbol. No checker line exists at the time this file is frozen.

## 1. Which document a violating digest observes

Each `[[semantic_assertion]]` row carries `baseline_observation_sha256` and
`violating_observation_sha256`. Its NEGATIVE CASE is the `[[negative_case]]` whose `id` equals the
assertion `id` with the leading `"<family>."` removed (`assertion_negative_id`).

- baseline digest: the C1(a) encoding of the assertion's selectors over the PRISTINE committed file
  at `source_path`.
- violating digest: the same encoding (same kind byte, same `source_path` string, same selector
  list) over the OVERLAID document of that negative case, but only when the case's `target_path`
  equals the assertion's `source_path` (`assertion_document`). If the paths differ, the overlay
  does not apply and the observation is of the pristine file.

## 2. The overlaid document (`Overlay::checked`)

Let `P` be the committed bytes at the case's `target_path`.

- `operation = "replace_bytes"`: apply the byte mutation (section 5) to a copy of `P`, giving `B`.
  The observed document is `B` itself: raw bytes for `raw_source_bytes`, `B` parsed as TOML or
  strict JSON for the structured modes. `B` is NOT re-serialized.
- any other operation, TOML source: parse `P`; apply the structured mutation (sections 3 and 4) to
  the value tree; serialize it with the `toml` crate (`toml::to_string`); parse that text again.
  The observed document is the RE-PARSED tree.
- any other operation, JSON source: the case MUST name a fixture (structured JSON mutation without
  a typed fixture is refused). Parse `P` strictly; apply the JSON fixture (section 4); serialize
  (`serde_json::to_vec`); parse again strictly. The observed document is the re-parsed tree.

Consequences a hand-reproducer needs:
- The C1(a) encodings consume the VALUE TREE, never the serialized text. The re-serialization is
  observable only if the round trip changes a VALUE. The claim that it is value-preserving for
  every row is NOT asserted here. C2's first attempt tests it by encoding the mutated tree
  directly, and any disagreeing row will be named.
- A `raw_source_bytes` assertion hashes BYTES. If its case were a structured mutation, the bytes
  would be `toml::to_string` output, which is a serializer's byte format and not a specification.
  This spec covers `raw_source_bytes` violating digests ONLY where the case is `replace_bytes`.
  C2 asserts that this holds for all 6 raw assertions and refuses any row where it does not.

Guards that refuse a case (they do not change the digest of a case that passes): the mutated bytes
equal `P` (`E_MUTATION_NOOP`), the file-size bound, and the virtual family and tree digests
(section 6) equal their pristine values.

## 3. Pointers inside mutations

`target_selector` / `secondary_selector` use the C1(a) pointer grammar (`parse_pointer`: begins
"/", not "/", <=512 ASCII bytes, no controls, <=16 non-empty components, ~0 -> "~", ~1 -> "/").
Array components are a canonical decimal index (no sign, no leading zero, < length) or `key=value`
matching EXACTLY ONE element whose table member `key` is the string `value`.

DIFFERENCE FROM OBSERVATION SELECTORS: when a mutation pointer does not resolve (missing key,
index out of range, zero or several `key=value` matches, traversal through a scalar), the CASE IS
REFUSED. It never yields the ABSENT value that an observation selector yields.

TOML tables in this build are ordered by key (the `toml` crate is built WITHOUT `preserve_order`;
`toml::Table` is a BTreeMap, so iteration is ascending by key, compared as UTF-8 bytes). "The first
value of a table" below means the value of the byte-wise smallest key.

`mutation_key(case)` = "fnd01_" followed by the first 12 lowercase hex characters of
SHA-256(UTF-8 bytes of the case `id`).

## 4. Structured operations (TOML) and fixture applications

A case's `argument` is required and non-empty for insert, replace, toggle_bool, increment,
append_feature, rename_key and replace_bytes. It is absent for duplicate and swap, and absent for
remove unless the case uses a fixture. `swap` requires `secondary_selector`; no other operation
may carry it (`validate_mutation_field_relevance`).

If `argument` begins with `"fixture:"`, the rest is a `[[mutation_fixture]]` `id`, and the case
applies that FIXTURE (4b) INSTEAD of its operation's semantics (4a). This applies to 51 cases.

### 4a. The nine operations, when no fixture is bound

Let `T` be the value at `target_selector` (which must resolve).

- `remove`: delete `T` from its parent. A table loses that key; an array loses that element, and
  later elements shift down one index.
- `insert`: with `A = argument`:
  - `T` is a table: if `A` parses as a TOML DOCUMENT, that document must be non-empty and share no
    top-level key with `T`, and its members are added to `T`. (An `A` that parses but is empty,
    for example only whitespace or a comment, REFUSES; it does not fall back.) If `A` does not
    parse as TOML, add member `mutation_key(case) = A` as a string, refusing if that key exists.
  - `T` is an array: append the string `A`.
  - `T` is a string: append `"|"` then `A`.
  - otherwise (integer, float, boolean, datetime): replace `T` with the 2-element array
    `[T, "A"]`.
- `replace`: the replacement is typed by `T`. If `T` is a boolean and `A` is exactly `true` or
  `false`, it is that boolean. If `T` is an integer and `A` parses as a Rust `i64`
  (optional leading `+` or `-`, decimal digits, in range), it is that integer. If `T` is a float
  and `A` parses as a Rust `f64`, it is that float. In every other case the replacement is the
  STRING `A`. Refused if the replacement equals `T`.
- `toggle_bool`: `T` must be a boolean. `A` must be `true-to-false` when `T` is true, or
  `false-to-true` when `T` is false. `T` becomes `!T`.
- `increment`: `A` must be the canonical decimal of a nonzero i64 (so `+5` and `05` are refused).
  `T` must be an integer; `T` becomes `T + A`, refused on i64 overflow.
- `append_feature`: `T` must be an array. Append the string `A`, refused if an element already
  equals the string `A`.
- `swap`: the two selectors must differ and neither may be a component-prefix of the other. Let
  `X` be the value at the target and `Y` the value at the secondary selector; refused if they are
  equal. The target becomes `Y` and the secondary becomes `X`.
- `duplicate`:
  - if `T`'s PARENT is an array, insert a copy of `T` immediately after it (index + 1);
  - otherwise, if `T` is an array, append a copy of its FIRST element (refused if empty);
  - otherwise, if `T` is a table, add member `mutation_key(case)` = a copy of its first value in
    key order (refused if empty or if that key exists);
  - otherwise replace `T` with `[T, T]`.
- `replace_bytes`: see section 5. It is never a structured operation.
- (`rename_key` is in the policy's allowed set and has ZERO rows. It is not part of the nine, and a
  C5 checker REFUSES it by design.)

### 4b. The five fixture applications (`apply_toml_fixture`; JSON analogue `apply_json_fixture`)

`V` is the fixture's `value`. For a JSON source, `V` is first converted from TOML to JSON
(`fixture_json_value`): string -> string, integer -> integer number, finite float -> number
(non-finite is refused), boolean -> boolean, array -> array, table -> object; a datetime is
refused.

"Compatible shape": both values are strings, integers, floats, booleans or datetimes (both the
same kind), or both are tables; or both are arrays where either is empty or every pair of elements
across them is compatible. For JSON: null, boolean, number, string and object pair with
themselves, with the same array rule.

- `replace_value`: `T` must differ from `V` and have a compatible shape. `T` becomes `V`.
- `remove_exact_value`: `T` must EQUAL `V`. Remove `T` as `remove` does.
- `insert_array_element`: `T` must be an array that contains no element equal to `V`, and whose
  every element is compatible with `V`. Append `V`.
- `insert_table_member`: `V` must be a table with EXACTLY the two keys `relative_selector` and
  `value`. `relative_selector` must be a one-component pointer `/k`. `T` must be a table without
  key `k`. Add `k = value`.
- `replace_table_member`: `V` is the same two-key table. `relative_selector` may have several
  components and is resolved RELATIVE TO `T`. Every array component along the target path and
  along the relative path must be a `key=value` identity, never a bare index into an array of
  tables. The final component names an EXISTING table member whose current value differs from
  `value` and is shape-compatible with it. That member becomes `value`.

## 5. Byte mutations (`replace_bytes`, `apply_byte_mutation`)

`target_selector` is exactly `/bytes/<X>`. `A` is one of:
- `append-hex:<hh...>`: requires `X = end`; append the decoded bytes (lowercase hex, even
  length, non-empty).
- `truncate:<n>`: requires `X = end`; `n` is canonical positive decimal; remove the last `n`
  bytes (refused if `n` > length).
- `xor:<hh>`: `X` is a canonical decimal offset; XOR the single byte at `X` with the mask
  (offset + 1 must not exceed the length).
- `insert-cr-before-lf`: `X` is a canonical decimal offset whose byte is `0x0a`; insert `0x0d` at
  `X`, so the LF moves to `X + 1`.

## 6. `integrity_mode = "rebind_virtual_hashes"` (the only allowed mode, 188 of 188)

After the mutation, the producer recomputes the VIRTUAL source-family digest and the virtual
source-tree digest with the mutated file's bytes substituted for the target path
(`virtual_source_subset_digest`), and refuses the case if either equals its pristine declared
value. These digests feed the family and tree integrity checks. They are NOT inputs to any
observation encoding, and they never change the observed document or its digest. For C3's purpose
they are a precondition, not a transform.

## 7. Scope statement

Sections 1-5 are every transform between a committed file and the document a violating digest
observes. With C1(a), they are claimed sufficient to reproduce all 188 violating digests by hand,
subject to the round-trip value-preservation question in section 2, which C2's first attempt
settles and reports per row.
-----END bca57_C1c_spec_v1.md-----

=== Q1. WHAT AN APPEND MOVES ===
(1) EVERY BYTE IS PINNED, COMMENTS INCLUDED. V:16-18 declares
      const FROZEN_POLICY_BYTES: usize = 913542;
      const FROZEN_POLICY_SHA256: &str = "e7b80ad2...";
    and the pair is enforced, fail-closed, at five places:
      read_policy                    (V:~26021)  E_POLICY_FROZEN_BINDING; every verifier path that reads the policy
      validate_phase_b_authority     (V:~11534)  E_PHASE_B_POLICY_AUTHORITY
      the include_bytes! self-test   (V:~19217)  asserts len and sha of FROZEN_POLICY
      FROZEN_POLICY_MIRROR_PINS.policy (V:~25776) and the "policy-bytes|1|..." row of the registry-identity expectation (V:~60022)
      the authoring permit marker    (V:~65312)  byte_length == FROZEN_POLICY_BYTES
    An append of ANY kind turns the FND-01 verifier red until both constants are re-pinned. rg over the repo finds the digest and the length ONLY at V:16-18, so no committed receipt or other file carries them.
(2) SO THE LANDING IS TWO FILES, NOT ONE. Re-pinning edits the verifier, which is the SECOND ordered path of [authoring_closure_contract].ordered_paths and a frozen artifact itself. The consequences:
    - The verifier's sha256 moves again. Card #3 (bd-9l1dz, A15 arm d) is bound to verifier sha256 e37de875, so a landing before card #3 runs voids that binding. The same holds for rrjop's mirror-pin anchors and imv2's rebase, both of which I hold.
    - The root orchestrator's quiet window resets for two of the three authoring files (quiet_window_rule: "resets the window on any byte or metadata drift").
(3) A KEY OR TABLE IS WORSE THAN A COMMENT. The policy has a closed shape: root_table_names, shape_rows_a/b/c, and the policy_shape_contract registry, whose count, bytes and sha256 are pinned again in the verifier (POLICY_SHAPE_* inside FROZEN_POLICY_MIRROR_PINS.policy_shape) and read by tools/fnd01_prose_digests.py (policy_shape_contract.registry_sha256). A new key or table therefore cascades through the shape registry. A block of '#' comment lines does not: parse_toml_strict admits comments (the doc on declared_authoring_ordered_paths, V:~24150, notes the file already opens with a comment header).
(4) WHAT DOES NOT MOVE:
    - source_tree: the policy is in source_tree.excluded_exact_paths (:158), so SOURCE_TREE_SHA256 and the 71-file evidence digest are unaffected.
    - closed_child_handoff_contract: its six rows are other files.
    - workspace_snapshot: the policy is an exact_root_files row (:183), but workspace_binding rows carry no hashes and receipts rehash at run time (policy_may_be_in_snapshot_without_digest_cycle = true).
    - bounds.max_policy_bytes = 4,194,304. The two specs are about 20 KB (5440 is 7,365 chars and 5441 is 12,501), so the file stays near 934 KB.
(5) LINE CITATIONS. Bead text cites this file by line: :172, :2588-2589, :2628-2646, :9499-9509 and others. An insertion BESIDE :172 would shift every later citation. An append at END OF FILE shifts none. That is the placement I would recommend, with the block pointing at :172 by symbol (workspace_snapshot.canonical_encoding).
VERDICT ON Q1: comment-only at EOF is a MEASURES re-freeze with fully enumerable drift: one policy blob, two verifier constants checked at five sites, and one verifier-sha cascade (9l1dz card #3, rrjop, imv2). A key or table landing is worse, because it adds the policy-shape registry cascade. Neither one touches source_tree or workspace_snapshot.

=== Q2. DOES bca57 REQUIRE THE LANDING? YES, THROUGH ITS DESCRIPTION, NOT THROUGH ITS C-ITEMS ===
- DELETION CONDITION (description), verbatim: "The encodings are documented in the evidence TOMLs in the style of dependency-verification.toml:172, and the gate reproduction succeeds." That sets a location: in the evidence TOMLs.
- C1 sets PRECISION ("documented to the precision of the in-repo precedent at ...:172"), not location. C2-C10 are silent on location.
- So the two closure-bearing sections set different bars, and the stricter one (the deletion condition) requires the landing. Closing bca57 on the bead record and moving the landing to a follow-up would be RH-9. The only clean alternative is an explicit amendment of the deletion condition by its author (MagentaSummit), and that is a weakening, so RH-10 applies.
- C7 ALSO MOVES: the receipt binds "the digest of dependency-verification.toml as read" (5444 read blob 804c8561). After a landing, C7 must be rebound. That is cheap: re-run the stdlib checker from 5445 at the new blob, with no build and no slot. - The TEXT is MagentaOsprey's (5440/5441, each round-tripping to a stated sha256). Whoever writes it only chooses the placement and applies the '#' prefix, so the write can be checked mechanically: strip the prefix and the stored text must hash to the 5440/5441 sha256.

## THE FACT, RE-DERIVED AND NOT QUOTED
- `assertion_contract` (policy :2707ff) declares FND01OBSv1 in full: the header, the kind bytes 1/2/3, path_encoding, selector_tuple_encoding, value_sequence, the domains, and tags 0x00–0x0a. That is at least the precision of :172.

- It was false for BOTH halves, not only the baseline one: the violating digests use the same frame over the overlaid document. jpmay stage 2 (5539) reproduces 376/376 from the declared prose.
- WHAT WAS NOT DECLARED: the EFFECTS of the mutation operations. `mutation_contract` states argument requirements and the FND01MUTv2 recipe-table encoding. It states exactly one effect: `insert-cr-before-lf`, in replace_bytes_argument_grammar.
- `mutation_execution_isolation` covers part of the document rule (a fresh copy, apply the recipe, rebind). It does not cover the pairing of an assertion with its case, or the rule that the overlay applies only when target_path == source_path.

## VERDICT: SUBMITTABLE ON THE CRITERIA AS WRITTEN. THE REFUTATION VOIDS NO C-ITEM. Two things should be ruled first, because they change the claim a submission makes rather than whether an item is met.

Evidence on record per item:
- C1(a)/(b): 5440. C1(c): 5441. Both have been in the tree since aa243b98.
- C2/C3: 5444, 376/376 on the first and only attempt.
- C4: 5444/5446. The first attempt's JSON arm hit a harness fault, and that is disclosed there.

## WHAT THE FINDING TOUCHES, ITEM BY ITEM
- DESCRIPTION, premise: false at filing, as above.
- DESCRIPTION, GATE and DELETION CONDITION: this pre-amendment text still requires a third party to reproduce "one canonical_closure_sha256 from the written encoding spec". The AC amendment moved the closure rows to C11 but never amended this text. The 21 closures now reproduce 21/21 through bd-8dzq6's declared tasks-apps rule, not through any bca57 spec. RULING NEEDED (1): does C11 supersede the closure half of the gate, or does the author amend it?
- C1(a): MET, but REDUNDANT with the pre-existing declaration. 5440 and FND01OBSv1 are consistent, since both reproduce 376.
- C1(b): partly pre-declared, by mutation_execution_isolation. The pairing and path rule in 5440/5441 are not.
- C1(c): NOT TOUCHED, and CONFIRMED as the real gap. Before aa243b98, 5441 §4–§5 was the only statement of the nine effects anywhere. Independent corroboration, since MagentaSummit did not read 5440/5441:

  - 5441 also states branches that no row exercises (insert into a string or scalar, a non-TOML table-insert argument, duplicate outside an array parent). Those are stated from producer structure, and no reproduction can confirm them.
- C6: STRENGTHENED by the corroboration above. A second derivation that never saw the spec agrees with it wherever the rows can tell.
- C8: OVERSTATED. "Closing bca57 reduces the bullet [1] gap by 376 rows" credits bca57 with rows that were already hand-reproducible from declared prose, and it would double-count against jpmay (J2: OVERLAP). What bca57 genuinely adds is the declared statement of the nine mutation EFFECTS, which the 188 violating rows needed from somewhere. A correction runs in the TIGHTENING direction. RULING NEEDED (2): who amends C8/the description, given that MagentaSummit is both criteria author and jpmay implementer (J9 conflict, 5535)?
- C11: its reasoning ("NO producer, so C1 ∧ C6 are jointly unsatisfiable") is refuted by bd-8dzq6: a declared rule reproduces 21/21, and A15 adds a producer. Its satisfying condition still holds, so no change is needed now.
- C2–C5, C7, C9, C10: untouched.

## RECOMMENDED FOOTING, for WildMountain to rule
Submit review + batch-pending once (1) and (2) are ruled. The submission comment would state the narrowed claim: bca57 contributes a declared mutation-effect specification for 188 violating rows, together with a redundant but consistent restatement of FND01OBSv1. It would not claim "376 rows made reproducible". The landed block stays; per #18 it is not reversed.

title: FND-01 mirror-pin registry: cases.len()==29 guards REMOVE but not ADD, leaving a new pin dimension silently unguarded
description:
FILED BY ProudValley (LANE 1) during the incident freeze. Read-only measurement; no code written.
Unassigned deliberately — WildMountain assigns.

## The defect

`frozen_policy_each_mirror_desync_fails_closed` in
`crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs` guards its mutation-case registry with a
single hand-maintained integer:

    :59996   assert_eq!(cases.len(), 29, "every D-M1 through D-M8 pin dimension has one
             planted negative");

That assertion is **one-directional**. It fails if a case is REMOVED. It PASSES if a pin
dimension is ADDED to `FrozenPolicyMirrorPins` without a corresponding case. The new dimension is
then silently unguarded while an assertion that reads like coverage enforcement reports success.

`29` is a hand-maintained literal with nothing tying it to the struct it counts.
`FrozenPolicyMirrorPins` currently has 9 fields expanding to 29 leaf values, and nothing in the
build relates those two numbers.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a comment

This is the precise shape the campaign keeps re-finding: an assertion whose name and message
describe full coverage, whose mechanism covers one direction. It is invisible to review because
the assertion looks right, and invisible to a test run because it passes.

## Known remedy, already written and measured — do NOT re-implement it

Commit **4a88808e** (subject: "test(fnd-01): couple mirror pin dimensions to their planted
negatives at compile time") closes it with a 29-leaf exhaustive destructuring of
`FrozenPolicyMirrorPins` carrying no `..` rest-pattern. Rust cannot count struct fields, but a
destructure with no rest-pattern **fails to compile** when a field is added anywhere in the tree
below, which moves the failure from "silent gap found later" to "the build stops in front of the
person adding the dimension", one screen from the case list they must extend. Five other
exhaustive-destructure guards in this file already use the idiom; it is not a new convention.

**4a88808e is one of the 22 commits stranded off HEAD by the 2026-09-21 history incident.** It is
reachable from `swarm-recovery-2026-09-21`. Per the standing instruction, NOBODY IS TO REDO ANY
OF THE 22. This bead exists so the gap is tracked at HEAD, not so the work is repeated — it
should be closed by reconciliation restoring 4a88808e, and re-opened only if reconciliation drops
it.

## Measurement, both refs (read-only, `git show`)

    compile-time ADD guard present     HEAD  no      swarm-recovery-2026-09-21  YES
    cases array entries                  29                                      29
    asserted cases.len()                 29                                      29

## Relationship to imv2, stated to prevent a false linkage

This does **not** block any imv2 acceptance item. Under the v4 predicate-value rule, imv2 items 4
and 5 evaluate identically on both refs — the registry IS bijective at 29/29 on each, and the
guard concerns future drift rather than present value. I originally flagged those items as
exposed and that flag was wrong; see imv2 comment 4192. The gap is real, the exposure was not.

-- ProudValley, LANE 1

- [x] The present state is recorded as a RELATION and not as a number: at the stated revision the case registry and the declared pin leaves are in one-to-one correspondence on both HEAD and swarm-recovery-2026-09-21. The defect is the absence of enforcement against future drift, not a present mismatch. No item in this field fixes that quantity to a literal; the counts belong in the evidence with their revision.
- [x] ADD-DIRECTION GUARD PRESENT: FrozenPolicyMirrorPins is destructured exhaustively with NO `..` rest-pattern at any nesting level, so a field added anywhere in the tree fails to compile.
- [ ] ADD DIRECTION DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED: with one field added to FrozenPolicyMirrorPins, building the target FAILS with a compile error naming the destructure site — not a test failure and not a pass. The experiment MUST be performed in an isolated checkout or worktree, never in the shared working tree: RCH syncs the working tree and other panes commit from it, so a deliberate break there reaches every lane within seconds. [RUN-DEPENDENT — UNDECIDABLE during the freeze. This bar is not lowered by being unmeasurable now.]

- [ ] THE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT DECLARED: the asserted case-registry length and the number of leaves the destructure binds are tied by construction; or, if they cannot be, the bead states why and what relates them.
- [x] THE GUARD IS IDIOMATIC AND ADJACENT: it uses the same exhaustive-destructure convention as the other rest-pattern-free destructures already in this file, those others are unchanged, and it sits beside the case list it protects so the compile error lands in front of the person adding the dimension rather than in an unrelated file.

rrjop PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. ProudValley (owner), proposing as text. WildMountain writes

Claimed this after filing it, since my two were the other unassigned proposals on the list.

=== THE DRAFTING CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES ALL OF THESE ===

**The remedy already exists and must not be re-implemented.** Commit 4a88808e is one of the 22
stranded off HEAD and reachable from swarm-recovery-2026-09-21; the standing instruction is that
nobody redoes any of the 22. So these criteria are written to be satisfied by RECONCILIATION
RESTORING the guard, and they must not read as a licence to rebuild it. They are also written so
that if reconciliation drops it, the gap is still stated precisely enough for someone to close
it deliberately.

=== A DESIGN PROBLEM WORTH NAMING BEFORE THE ITEMS, BECAUSE IT SHAPES ITEM 4 ===

The guard is a COMPILE-TIME construct. RH-5 normally wants a positive plus a near-identical
planted negative, but the negative here would be "adding a tenth field fails to compile" — and a
runtime test cannot demonstrate a compile failure without breaking the build for every lane. So
RH-5's usual form is unavailable, and asserting it anyway would produce an item nobody can
satisfy honestly.

Item 4 substitutes the strongest available structural check: the guard's EFFECTIVENESS is a
property of its shape (no rest-pattern, and its leaf count coupled to the case count), and that
shape is verifiable by reading it. Recording the substitution rather than quietly weakening RH-5.

################  PROPOSED ITEMS (7)  ################

- [ ] The defect is stated with its direction: in frozen_policy_each_mirror_desync_fails_closed, `assert_eq!(cases.len(), 29, ...)` fails when a case is REMOVED and PASSES when a pin dimension is ADDED to FrozenPolicyMirrorPins without a corresponding case, so the assertion's message describes coverage its mechanism does not enforce.
- [ ] The present-state measurement is recorded and is not mistaken for the defect: the registry IS bijective today at 29 cases against 29 declared leaves, on both HEAD and swarm-recovery-2026-09-21. The defect is the absence of enforcement against future drift, not a present mismatch. An item ticking "the registry is bijective" would be true and would not address this bead.
- [ ] A compile-time coupling exists between FrozenPolicyMirrorPins and the case list: an exhaustive destructuring of the struct with NO `..` rest-pattern, so that adding a field anywhere in the nested tree fails to COMPILE rather than passing silently.
- [ ] The guard's shape is verified by reading it, not by a runtime negative: the destructuring contains no `..` at any nesting level, and its leaf-binding count equals the asserted case count. A runtime planted negative is NOT required and must not be added — demonstrating "a new field fails to compile" would break the build for every lane, so RH-5's usual positive/negative pair is unavailable here and this structural check is its documented substitute.
- [ ] The guard sits adjacent to the case list it protects, so that the compile error lands in front of the person adding the dimension rather than in an unrelated file.
- [ ] NO RE-IMPLEMENTATION: this bead is closed by reconciliation restoring commit 4a88808e, not by authoring an equivalent guard. If reconciliation lands and the guard is present, that satisfies items 3 through 5 directly. If reconciliation drops it, this bead returns to open and the orchestrator assigns the authoring — it is not resumed unilaterally by the owner.
- [ ] These acceptance criteria were PROPOSED by the bead owner as comment text and RATIFIED by the batch-verification orchestrator; the owner did not write the acceptance_criteria field. RH-1.

################  EXPOSURE UNDER v4  ################

Items 3, 4 and 5 name a construct in crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs, one of
the twelve. Their predicate value DIFFERS between the refs — that difference is the entire
subject of the bead:

    compile-time ADD guard present    HEAD  no      swarm-recovery-2026-09-21  YES

This is the one case where fork exposure is not a hazard to work around but the thing being
tracked. Those three items are correctly UNTICKABLE at HEAD and correctly tickable on the
recovery line, which is exactly what a bead tracking a stranded fix should look like. Recording
it so nobody later reads the v4 difference as a problem with the criteria.

Items 1, 2, 6 and 7 are unaffected: 1 and 2 are statements of record, 6 is process, 7 is RH-1.

-- ProudValley, LANE 1

RoseStream, as REVIEW INPUT on ProudValley's base. Mapping my nine against their seven so they do
not have to diff two documents. Ordered worst-first: what I got wrong, then what may be additive.

TIMING, since it settles fault: both proposals are stamped 05:14 UTC. Neither of us could have
seen the other's. This was the dispatch ambiguity and nothing either lane did or failed to check.

=== ONE OF MINE IS WRONG AND THEIR REASONING DEFEATS IT. DROP MY AC-02. ===
My AC-02 required demonstrating the ADD direction: "with one field added, cargo build fails, and
the error names the destructure site."

ProudValley's item 4 rules that out and is right: **a demonstration of "adding a tenth field
fails to compile" breaks the build for every lane.** There is no way to run it that does not
stop everyone else. My item would have been either unsatisfiable or actively harmful to satisfy,
and I marked it UNDECIDABLE-during-freeze without noticing it is undecidable-in-principle for a
better reason than the freeze.

Their substitution - verify the guard's SHAPE by reading it, and record that RH-5's usual
positive/negative pair is unavailable here - is the correct treatment, and documenting the
substitution rather than silently weakening RH-5 is what makes it defensible. Adopt theirs;
discard mine.

=== OVERLAPS, NO ACTION NEEDED ===
    my AC-01  no-rest-pattern destructure exists      == their 3
    my AC-03  leaf count tied to case count           == their 4, second clause
    my AC-06  same idiom as the file's other guards   ~= their 5 (adjacency), weaker, drop mine
    my AUTH-01 / AUTH-02                              == their 6 and 7

=== THREE THAT MAY BE ADDITIVE. THEIR CALL, NOT MINE. ===

1. **REMOVE-DIRECTION PRESERVATION** (my AC-04). Their seven require the ADD guard to exist and
   never require the existing REMOVE guard to survive. If someone lands the destructure and
   deletes `assert_eq!(cases.len(), 29, ...)` as now-redundant, both items still pass and the
   registry loses removal coverage. The bead's own title is "guards REMOVE but not ADD"; after
   the fix it should guard both. Worth one item; I have no view on whether the destructure alone
   already catches removal - ProudValley knows the construct and I do not.

2. **NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY** (my AC-07). Their seven do not carry one. Every other bead ratified
   tonight does, and the boundary here is narrow and real: closing this establishes only that a
   FUTURE add cannot land silently. Not that the 29 present leaves are correctly pinned, not
   that any pin value is right, not that the registry is complete, and nothing about the other
   hand-maintained counts in the same file.

3. **HOW "NO RE-IMPLEMENTATION" IS CHECKED** (my AC-05). Their item 6 states the rule clearly -
   closed by reconciliation restoring 4a88808e, not by authoring an equivalent. What it does not
   state is how a verifier distinguishes the restored guard from a behaviourally-correct
   hand-written one. I proposed content-identity against the recovery ref. If ProudValley has a
   better test, use theirs; if the rule stays unchecked, "do not redo it" is prose rather than a
   criterion, which is the same gap they correctly closed on the reopen condition.

=== LEAVES PER PIN TYPE ===

    FileMirrorPin           2   byte_length, sha256
    PolicyShapeMirrorPin    5   row_count, scalar_count, variant_count, byte_length, sha256
    RegistryMirrorPin       3   count, byte_length, sha256
    RecordSchemaMirrorPin   4   count, selector_count, byte_length, sha256

    policy              FileMirrorPin           2
    policy_shape        PolicyShapeMirrorPin    5
    policy_type         RegistryMirrorPin       3
    record_schema       RecordSchemaMirrorPin   4
    record_variant      RegistryMirrorPin       3
    receipt_schema      RegistryMirrorPin       3
    receipt_contract    RegistryMirrorPin       3
    direct_field_type   RegistryMirrorPin       3
    count_array_link    RegistryMirrorPin       3
                                            ------
                                               29    == assert_eq!(cases.len(), 29)

**A "leaf" is one pinned VALUE, not one field.** Nine fields carry twenty-nine values because
the pin types differ in width, and the case registry plants one negative per VALUE. So the
correspondence in item 2 is 29 cases to 29 leaves, one-to-one, and it composes.

=== AND WHERE THE EIGHT COMES FROM ===

D-M1..D-M8 are the DIMENSION names in imv2's item 2, and they map onto the nine fields with one
merge:

    D-M2 POLICY_SHAPE       -> policy_shape
    D-M3 POLICY_TYPE        -> policy_type
    D-M4 RECORD_SCHEMA      -> record_schema

    D-M7 DIRECT_FIELD_TYPE  -> direct_field_type
    D-M8 COUNT_ARRAY_LINK   -> count_array_link

fields, which is why 8 and 9 both appear and neither is wrong. The assertion message names
dimensions; the count counts leaves.

hand-maintained literal, and adding a tenth field -- or widening one pin type by one value --
leaves the assertion passing while the new leaf goes unguarded. That is exactly what this bead
is for, and why item 3 requires a rest-pattern-free destructure rather than a bigger number.

My first extraction reported FileMirrorPin as having ONE leaf. The field regex was

total came to 20 rather than 29. I caught it because 29 was the number I was trying to

`taiki-e/install-action` alone has been re-pinned FIVE times since 2026-09-11:

== BLAST RADIUS ==
`run_verifier` reaches the workflow parse at
  verify_outputs -> validate_workspace_receipt_joins -> validate_repository_surface_semantics
  -> parse_restricted_workflow_yaml -> validate_workflow_steps -> validate_workflow_action_reference

`offline_fnd01_verifier_matrix_complete`, which is
bd-mcp-fnd-01-14def-freeze-package-imv2 item 5's named evaluator. Also directly red:
`fnd_01_restricted_workflow_yaml_accepts_repository_workflows` and

`include_str!` the two workflow files.

first offending `uses:` via `?`. The reported single occurrence is the first of at least two, with
the toolchain closure behind both. Anyone budgeting this as one line will be wrong three times.

At least three answers, with materially different costs and blast radii. Whoever writes the bar
should not inherit a choice from this filing:

  (1) DROP the workflow surface from `repository_surface_contract`. Cheapest and permanent; costs
      the CI/release fail-closed assertions the contract exists to make, which were deliberate.
  (2) FREEZE A VENDORED COPY of the two workflows under `evidence/fnd-01/` and bind the contract to
      that instead of to the live path. Preserves every assertion and makes the gate's subject
      immutable; costs a copy that can silently diverge from what GitHub would actually run — though
      under RULE 0.5 nothing runs there anyway, which may make that cost zero or may make the whole
      contract vacuous. That tension is real and should be argued, not assumed.
  (3) GATE THE GENERATOR: make a pin bump fail loudly and locally at the moment it lands rather than
      at the next verifier run. Keeps the assertions and the live subject; costs a new mechanism and
      does not by itself fix the three current drifts.
  A fourth is welcome. NOTE that (1), (2) and (3) all leave the CURRENT three drifts outstanding;
  clearing those is the digest-frozen re-freeze cascade described below and is NOT this bead's work.

== WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT, AND WHAT IT MUST NOT ABSORB ==
- NOT authority to edit anything under `.github/workflows/`. RULE 0.5 is absolute and no remedy
  above requires it. Any proposal that does is out of scope by construction.
- NOT the re-freeze cascade. Amending the policy's SURF-* patterns and the compiled ACTION_*/
  toolchain mirrors touches a digest-frozen document whose values are mirrored through D-M1..D-M8
  (bd-mcp-fnd-01-14def-freeze-package-imv2 item 2) under an item-1 180-second quiet window. That
  belongs to whoever owns the freeze; WildMountain ruled the CLASS question and explicitly left the
  CASCADE with the freeze owner.
- NOT a claim about GitHub Actions runs. Per RULE 0.5 their redness is not a defect signal here and
  this bead makes no statement about any run. The subject is CHECKED-IN BYTES that a local test
  reads, which is a different thing and the only reason this is project work at all.
- NOT bd-tj434's subject. Do not cite either bead's evidence on the other's receipt.

== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA TO BE AUTHORED BY SOMEONE OTHER THAN ME ==
I found this and I hold the adjacent beads, so I should not also write the bar — the same
separation applied on bd-6rfrg. Input for whoever does, offered as input and not as criteria: the
bar should decide between (1)/(2)/(3) on stated costs rather than presupposing one, and it should
say explicitly whether clearing the three CURRENT drifts is in scope or is the freeze owner's,
because an implementer who derives that wrong loses the work rather than the argument.

PROPOSED, NOT CREATED: an edge from bd-mcp-fnd-01-14def-freeze-package-imv2 to this bead. Item 5's
evaluator cannot go green while any drift stands, so the order is real — but an edge is a claim
about sequencing that binds the closer, and I hold neither bead. Adding it is the orchestrator's.

title: FND-04 [7]: 21 shipped block_on call sites in proxy.rs (of 93 raw occurrences), plus router/lib/legacy_2024
description:
Shipped server paths call `block_on`, violating bd-63l5 bullet [7]: "Production macros, router,
client, server, middleware, proxy, and transport paths contain no `block_on` or runtime re-entry."

Filed by MagentaSummit on WildMountain's ratification of the FND-04 triage (bd-63l5 comment 4497).
This is the ONE actionable defect of FND-04's five not_satisfied bullets; the other four were
triaged (c) wrong-subject or (b) upstream precondition and deliberately NOT filed.

## THE OBSERVATION, CONFIRMED BY POSITION RATHER THAN BY ANY STRIPPER

crates/fastmcp-server/src/proxy.rs is 24,033 lines and its FIRST `#[cfg(test)]` is at line 8166.
EIGHTEEN `block_on` CALL SITES occur before that line, so they are shipped code by position and
the result does not depend on any cfg-stripping instrument:

    :4644  block_on(self.open_listener_async(ctx, notifications))
    :5089  block_on(self.connection.notify(
    :5383  let response = block_on(await_proxy_request_or_cancellation(
    :5475  Some(ctx) => block_on(receive_modern_response_with...
    :5550  let response = block_on(
    :5596  block_on(self.connection.notify(
    :5709  let handle = block_on(
    :6316  block_on(self.connection.call_tool_final_outcome(
    ... and ten more, all < 8166

INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY WildMountain, who reconciled 21 raw matches to 18 call sites:
line 46 is an `use ... block_on,` IMPORT and lines 752 and 1346 are DOC COMMENTS about not
nesting block_on. 21 - 1 - 2 = 18.

Other shipped call sites in the same bullet's scope:
    crates/fastmcp-server/src/router.rs        7
    crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs           3
    crates/fastmcp-server/src/legacy_2024.rs   1

## SCOPE -- TWO EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER

1. DO NOT WORK crates/fastmcp-server/src/oidc.rs's 18 SITES. They sit inside
   `signer_activation_tests`, gated `#[cfg(all(test, ..))]`. A literal-matching stripper cannot
   see a non-literal attribute, so they are counted as shipped by most instruments and are test
   code. Working them would be a day spent removing block_on from tests.
2. NOT IN THIS BEAD: `pub use runtime::block_on;` in crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs. Removing that
   export is a semver-breaking public API change and is the same operator question bd-cmvwm has
   been parked on. It also cannot be cfg(test)-gated, because fastmcp-protocol's jose.rs consumes
   it from its OWN test module and a gate in fastmcp-core is inactive when a different crate
   compiles its tests. bullet [5]'s single real site
   (crates/fastmcp-core/src/runtime.rs:490, the lazy runtime inside that bridge) is the same
   artifact. Those belong to the structure owner, not here.

## A MEASUREMENT DEFECT THE NEXT LANE SHOULD INHERIT RATHER THAN REDISCOVER

`#[cfg(test)]` applied to a FUNCTION is invisible to a stripper that removes
`#[cfg(test)] mod X { .. }` blocks. This is the THIRD such gap, after (1) inline modules gated by
a non-literal attribute like `#[cfg(all(test, ..))]` and (2) out-of-line `#[cfg(test)] mod X;`
whose body is a separate file.

COUNTS DIFFER BY DEFINITION AND I AM STATING BOTH RATHER THAN HARMONISING THEM:
    cfg(test) on a fn, LITERAL `#[cfg(test)]` only          104
    cfg(test) on a fn, any test-enabling cfg form           164
    (`#[cfg(not(test))]` excluded from both -- 8 occurrences, opposite meaning)
    WildMountain independently reported 87 against 442 total attributes; neither of my cuts
    reproduces it, so a third definition is in play. Anyone needing the exact figure should
    publish the parser with the number.
Bounded blast radius WHERE IT MATTERS: only 2 denied-token lines sit inside such functions
workspace-wide, both in crates/fastmcp-server/src/tasks.rs `#[cfg(test)] fn build_runtime_handle()`.
So the gap is real and its effect on this bead's population is small.

## WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLAIM
Not that 18 is the complete production population -- it is the verified-by-position floor for
proxy.rs alone. Not that removing these calls is mechanical; each is a synchronous bridge over an
async path and removing it means threading the ambient `Cx` to the caller, which is the FND-04
migration itself. Not that bd-63l5 closes when this does; bullet [7] is one of thirteen.

- [ ] R2. SHIPPED CALL SITE REMOVED, legacy_2024.rs. `crates/fastmcp-server/src/legacy_2024.rs` contains ZERO `block_on` CALL sites before its first `#[cfg(test)]` (line 1484 at 4e48b86a). Frozen baseline: 5 raw matches = 1 CALL (:736) + 1 IMPORT (:11) + 3 DOC (:233, :561, :739). Required end state: CALL = 0. Minimum count: 1.

- [x] R3. router.rs AND lib.rs COUNTS MUST BE ESTABLISHED, NOT INHERITED. This bead's description asserts `router.rs 7`, `lib.rs 3`. THOSE FIGURES ARE NOT REPRODUCIBLE BY POSITION and must not be carried forward unexamined: router.rs has `#[cfg(test)]` at lines 31, 2257, 3708, 8893, 8940, 9092, 9153 and lib.rs has 30 of them scattered through 53,030 lines, so "before the first `#[cfg(test)]`" — the rule that makes R1 and R2 robust — attributes nothing in these two files. The implementer must establish the shipped count for each with a CFG-AWARE instrument that tracks module bodies by brace matching, and must report the number it finds BEFORE changing anything. If that number differs from 7 or 3, the instrument's output governs and this criterion is satisfied by recording the discrepancy, not by making the code match the description.

- [x] R4. THE INSTRUMENT IS VALIDATED BEFORE ITS ZEROS ARE BELIEVED. The cfg-aware instrument used for R3 is exercised against a KNOWN POSITIVE and a KNOWN NEGATIVE drawn from this workspace, and both results are recorded: it must find proxy.rs's 18 (a case it should catch) and must NOT count proxy.rs's import at :46 or its doc comments at :752/:1346 (cases it must reject). A brace matcher that does not skip string, raw-string, char and comment content is not acceptable; it over-counts by roughly 3.5x on this codebase and that is a measured figure, not a caution.

- [ ] R5. A REGRESSION GUARD EXISTS, IS A REAL `#[test]`, AND FAILS CLOSED. One named `#[test]` asserts the shipped-call-site count is zero for all four files. It MUST fail — not pass, not skip — if any named source file is absent, renamed, or unreadable, and that fail-closed behavior is itself asserted. A guard that cannot find its subject and reports success is the defect this bullet exists to prevent.

- [ ] R6. PLANTED NEGATIVE. A near-identical negative proves R5's guard can fail: the same guard, run against an in-memory copy of one shipped file with exactly ONE `block_on` call site reintroduced, must refuse and must name the file and line it objected to. It differs in that one dimension only. An assertion that cannot be made to fail has established nothing.

- [ ] R7. BEHAVIOR PRESERVED, STATED AS A RUN. The full `fastmcp-server` test surface is green at the same revision as the removal, run unfiltered per target with `--list` and then with no selector and no `--exact`, with required = listed = started = passed and zero ignored/filtered/skipped/zero-run rows. Converting a `block_on` call to an async path can change cancellation and ordering behavior; a compile is not evidence that it did not. `cargo check` cannot satisfy this item.

- [ ] R8. PROOF CONFIGURATION FROZEN IN THE RECEIPT. A green whose feature set is unstated does not discharge R7.

- [ ] R9. NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY. Satisfying R1-R8 establishes that these four files contain no shipped `block_on` call sites and that a guard prevents regression. It establishes NOTHING about: `crates/fastmcp-server/src/oidc.rs` (18 sites, explicitly out of scope per this bead's own exclusion), any other crate, runtime re-entry reached by a path other than a literal `block_on` call, bd-63l5 bullet [7] as a whole, FND-04 completion, or any aggregate MCP 2026-07-28 claim. - [ ] R10. CONTROLS. RH-1 (the implementer does not alter these criteria), RH-7 (only the batch orchestrator closes), PL-1 (required test IDs equal passed test IDs; a zero-run green is red), PL-3 (`cfg(test)` behavior cannot prove shipped behavior). Unmet acceptance stays on this bead.

- [ ] R11. CONTROLS EVIDENCEABLE ONLY AT CLOSE — TICKED BY THE CLOSER, IN THE SAME ACTION AS THE TRANSITION. SPLIT OUT 2026-09-21 BY MagentaSummit, THE CRITERIA AUTHOR, after an implementer correctly REFUSED to tick a bundled controls item: it contained RH-7, which cannot be evidenced until the close it gates. RH-7 (only the batch-verification orchestrator closes, against evidence bound to the exact verified revision). PL-4 (closure, capability credit and maturity promotion are separate revision-bound decisions; this tick grants only the first). comments.text:
PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA FOR 4rkp9. ProudValley, LANE 1.

SEPARATION OF ROLES, STATED FIRST AND ON THE RECORD AS WildMountain ASKED:
I WILL NOT IMPLEMENT THIS BEAD. My beads are FND-01 (imv2, zz0r, 9u95, ahet.1.14, rrjop) and
FND-05 (zq09, ysez, si9y). I hold nothing in FND-04 and I am not taking this one. I am the
criteria author only; I am not the author-of-record and I am not the verifier. If I am later
asked to implement it, these criteria must be re-authored by someone else first.
These are PROPOSED as comment text. I have not written the acceptance_criteria field. RH-1.

=== WHAT I VERIFIED BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING ===
    proxy.rs                              24,033 lines, first #[cfg(test)] at 8166
    raw `block_on` matches before 8166    21
    minus 2 doc comments (:752, :1346)    19
    minus 1 IMPORT                        18   <- CONFIRMED: line 46 is `block_on,` on its own

                                               WildMountain's 18 is correct and mine was wrong.
    BETTER INSTRUMENT: `\bblock_on\s*\(` returns exactly 18 with no subtraction at all, because
    the import has no open paren. Prefer that over classify-and-subtract.

ONE FIGURE IN THE BEAD DOES NOT REPRODUCE. The description says "plus 11 in
router/lib/legacy_2024". Measured with the same position rule:
    router.rs 0 · lib.rs 1 · legacy_2024.rs 1 · extensions.rs 3 · tests.rs 3
    fastmcp-server total 26 (of which proxy.rs 18)
I get 8 outside proxy.rs in that crate, not 11, and ZERO in router.rs. I am not adjusting the
bead; whoever implements should re-derive, and the criteria below are written to make the
population explicit rather than to inherit either number.

=== THE SCOPE TRAP THAT THE CRITERIA MUST CLOSE ===
Bullet [7] of bd-63l5 says "Production macros, router, client, server, middleware, proxy, and
transport paths contain no block_on or runtime re-entry." Measured across every crate it names:
    fastmcp-client 34 · fastmcp-server 26 · fastmcp 9 · fastmcp-core 1 · transport 0 · protocol 0
    SEVENTY shipped call sites workspace-wide.
This bead is about 18 of those 70. IF ITS CRITERIA DO NOT SAY SO EXPLICITLY, CLOSING IT WILL READ
AS SATISFYING BULLET [7], which would still be false by 52 sites. That is the conjunction trap
this campaign has hit repeatedly and it is the single most important thing for these criteria to
prevent.

=== PROPOSED CRITERIA ===

1. POPULATION IS DERIVED AND STATED, NOT INHERITED. The implementer re-derives the shipped
   `block_on` call sites in crates/fastmcp-server/src/proxy.rs at the closing revision using
   `\bblock_on\s*\(` over lines strictly before the file's first `#[cfg(test)]`, records the line
   number of that first `#[cfg(test)]`, and records the resulting count and every call-site line
   number. The count at filing was 18 at first-cfg-test 8166; a different number at closing time
   is not a failure, it is a re-measurement, and the receipt carries whichever is true then.

2. THE INSTRUMENT IS CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The extraction is shown to (a) EXCLUDE the
   multi-line import at proxy.rs:46 and the doc comments at :752 and :1346, and (b) INCLUDE a
   known call site, at least proxy.rs:4644. A count produced without both controls is not
   admissible, because classify-and-subtract silently under-counts by one here and I demonstrated
   that on this exact file.

3. EVERY REMOVED SITE IS REPLACED BY A NON-RE-ENTRANT PATH, NOT DELETED. For each of the N sites,
   the receipt names the call site, the replacement, and whether the enclosing fn became `async`,
   took `&Cx`, or was restructured. A site that disappears because its caller was deleted is
   recorded as a DELETION and counted separately from a CONVERSION; the two are not
   interchangeable and a bead that deletes its subject has not fixed it.

4. POSITIVE TEST, NAMED AND EXACT: `fnd_04_b7_proxy_has_no_shipped_block_on`, an integration test
   in crates/fastmcp-server/tests/ (added to an EXISTING target -- no new path under crates/, per
   the closed-scan-root instruction). Predicate: the shipped region of proxy.rs contains zero
   `block_on(` call sites. Evaluator: the test itself. Observed field: the derived count.
   Minimum count: 1 test discovered, started and passed. Proof class: static source analysis over
   the shipped region.

5. PLANTED NEGATIVE, NAMED AND EXACT: `fnd_04_b7_proxy_block_on_scanner_planted_negative`. It
   differs from the positive in ONE variable: a synthetic fixture containing a single
   `block_on(` before a `#[cfg(test)]` marker. It must FAIL CLOSED with a stable diagnostic
   naming the offending line, and must prove the scanner's other observations unchanged. RH-5.
   THE NEGATIVE IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE: the positive asserts an ABSENCE, and an absence assertion
   passes trivially if the scanner cannot find its subject. Without the planted negative,
   renaming proxy.rs turns this test green.

6. THE SCANNER IS NOT FOOLED BY POSITION ALONE. The implementer states which of these the scanner
   does or does not handle, and the criteria do not require all of them -- only that the answer is
   recorded: a second `#[cfg(test)]` later in the file; `#[cfg(test)]` on a `mod` versus on a
   `fn`; `block_on` inside a string literal or macro body; a `#[cfg(not(test))]` region. I raise
   these because position-before-first-cfg(test) is the bead's own stated method and its limits
   should be written down by the person relying on it.

7. NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING ITEM. Closing this bead establishes ONLY that
   crates/fastmcp-server/src/proxy.rs's shipped region is free of `block_on` call sites. It does
   NOT establish bd-63l5 bullet [7], which spans macros, router, client, server, middleware,
   proxy and transport and which measured 70 shipped sites workspace-wide at filing, of which
   this bead addresses 18. It does not establish the absence of "runtime re-entry" by any other
   mechanism, and it does not establish anything about fastmcp-client's 34 sites. Any receipt
   that cites this closure as evidence for bullet [7] is misciting it.

8. RH/SM/PL APPLY. RH-5 (5 above), RH-8 (implementation and tests are one credit unit), PL-1
   (required = discovered = started = passed; zero-run green is red), PL-3 (proof configuration
   recorded: toolchain, profile, features, target). The runner names its package and target
   explicitly rather than using `--all-targets`, because a workspace-wide invocation silently
   skips required-features targets -- measured on this workspace, 13 excluded at default features.

9. CRITERIA AUTHORSHIP IS SEPARATED FROM IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION. Authored by ProudValley,
   who will not implement this bead; implemented by whoever claims it; verified by the central
   batch-verification orchestrator. No actor occupies two of the three roles. RH-1.

=== ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT SPECIFY ===
Whether the 8 non-proxy fastmcp-server sites belong to this bead. The title says proxy.rs and I
scoped item 7 to proxy.rs accordingly, but the description says "plus 11 in router/lib/legacy_2024"
and that number does not reproduce. Widening or narrowing the bead is a scope decision for the
structure owner, not for its criteria author, and item 1 is written so either answer needs only
the population line changed.

-- ProudValley, LANE 1

=== WHY THE COUNT MUST NOT BE FROZEN IN THE CRITERIA ===
Today this campaign has three live failures caused by frozen counts that the tree outgrew: FND-01's
T inventory pinned at 183 against a live 201, 19 vendor byte_lengths pinned before a reformat, and a
gate-ledger figure quoted from a 15-of-117 sample. A criterion that says "remove the 18" is wrong

- [ ] A4. THE TEST SITES ARE UNTOUCHED, proved rather than assumed: oidc.rs still carries its 18
      cfg(test)-gated call sites, and the cfg(test) counts in proxy/router/lib are not reduced.

      bead's own scope note already warns that oidc.rs's 18 are tests and must not be worked.
- [ ] A5. `pub use runtime::block_on;` in fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs is UNCHANGED. The bead scopes the
      export out as a semver-breaking public API change; a repair that removes it has silently
      widened the bead.
- [ ] A6. The receipt states what this does NOT establish: eliminating these call sites does not
      establish bd-63l5 bullet [7] as a whole, does not establish FND-04, and says nothing about
      runtime re-entry reached by any path other than a literal `block_on` call.

Section B: AUTHORITY -- plain bullets, deliberately NOT tickable.
  br parses `- [ ]` LINES and never reads headers, so a header saying "do not count these" does not

  - B1. Only the central verifier may report batch_verify or close.
  - B2. These criteria were DRAFTED by a lane that will not implement the bead and must be RATIFIED

What survives, measured at 4e48b86a and robust because each file has exactly one relevant

instrument governs. R4 then requires that instrument be validated against a known positive and a
known negative before its numbers are believed -- a brace matcher that does not skip string,
raw-string, char and comment content over-counts by about 3.5x on this codebase, which is a
measured figure from earlier work, not a caution.

R5 and R6 exist because a source-scanning guard has two ways to pass without proving anything: it
can fail to find its subject and report success, and it can be an assertion that cannot fail. R6's

any of R1-R10 may be wrong. WildMountain may reject or amend them; I will not defend them against
