comment 5312 was too narrow. MagentaSummit.

THE PREDICTION, registered publicly in 5312 before the test: 'reproducibility tracks whether a
contract declares an EXPLICIT FIELD ORDER list ... Contracts to watch on that basis:
fixture_contract declares no field-order list at all.'

IT DOES NOT DECLARE A LIST, AND IT REPRODUCES ANYWAY. It declares the field order as an inline
GRAMMAR STRING instead:
    canonical_record = 'id || NUL || application || NUL || value_kind || NUL ||
                        lowercase value_digest_sha256 || LF, sorted by raw UTF-8 id bytes'
So the real property is 'the contract states its field order SOMEHOW' -- as a list OR as prose. My
version privileged the FORM the first four examples happened to use. That is the same error class
as matching a key by a guessed name: I generalised from the shape of my sample rather than from
what the shape was doing.

THE RESULT:
    fixture_contract.canonical_sha256   declared 6552 B / 3abebcd4…
                                        computed 6552 B / 3abebcd4…    MATCH, first attempt
AND IT IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE RESULT SO FAR, because it is not one encoding but two composed:
  (a) FND01FIXv1 per-value digests -- sha256 over ASCII FND01FIXv1 + NUL + one recursively encoded
      fixture value using the assertion_contract TOML value tags (0x02 bool, 0x03 i64be, 0x04 f64
      bits, 0x05 u64be-length string, 0x06 u64be-count array, 0x07 u64be-count map with members
      sorted by raw UTF-8 key and u32be key lengths). I had to implement that recursive encoder
      from the declared tag table to get anywhere.
  (b) the canonical_record concatenation above, over all 51 rows.
The 51 PER-VALUE DIGESTS ARE TRANSITIVELY CONFIRMED by the registry match: the registry hashes each
value digest, so a wrong one could not have produced the declared registry digest. I am recording
that as transitive rather than direct, because I did not compare 51 declared per-value digests
one-by-one -- the rows do not carry them; only the registry does.

RUNNING TOTAL: 54 digests reproduced directly (5 Class-A registries + fixture_contract + 48
Class-B vectors), plus 51 transitively confirmed. Still ZERO MISMATCHES.

WHAT THE FALSIFICATION CHANGES FOR WHOEVER CONTINUES: do not screen the remaining contracts by

The fixture registry is the deepest of the twelve: it composes TWO encodings, because each row
carries a value digest that must itself be built by FND01FIXv1 (ASCII prefix + NUL + one recursively
encoded TOML value using the assertion_contract tag table — 0x02 bool, 0x03 i64be, 0x04 f64 bits,
0x05 u64be-length string, 0x06 u64be-count array, 0x07 u64be-count map with members sorted by raw
UTF-8 key). Its match TRANSITIVELY CONFIRMS all 51 per-value digests: the registry hashes them, so a
wrong one could not produce the declared registry digest. Recorded as transitive because the rows
do not carry those digests individually — only the registry does.

=== 2. THE THIRTEENTH, AND IT IS A CLEAN FINDING ===
    bootstrap_manifest_contract.canonical_document_sha256   7329 B  ba29adcd…   UNDERDETERMINED
That table declares THREE digests. Two of them — direct_dependency_registry and
union_only_registry — carry a full `*_encoding` key and both reproduce above. The third carries
only `canonical_document_bytes` and `canonical_document_sha256`. There is NO
`canonical_document_encoding`, and no other key in the table describes how the document is built.
I searched the table for any prose mentioning "document" and found none.
So this is not prose that is too vague. It is prose that IS ABSENT, for a digest sitting between
two siblings that have it. The gap is ONE MISSING KEY, and the fix is to declare
`canonical_document_encoding` the way its two neighbours already do.
I am NOT attempting to guess it. Searching candidate constructions until one matches is the
transcription failure mode this exercise exists to avoid, and a guessed encoding that happened to
match would be indistinguishable from a documented one while being worth nothing.

=== 3. TOTALS ===
    Class-A canonical registries reproduced       12
    Class-A underdetermined                        1   (named above)
    Class-B content-encoded vectors reproduced    48   (37 utf-8, 3 hex, 4+4 content-addressed)
    -------------------------------------------------
    DIRECT                                        60
    TRANSITIVELY CONFIRMED                        51   (the FND01FIXv1 per-value digests)
    MISMATCHES                                     0
Against the 1 digest this bead was filed with. Still zero mismatches, which I record as a fact
about this evidence set and not as a reason to relax: a mismatch is the outcome the bead was filed
to hunt, and finding none over 60 is itself evidence the declared encodings are accurate.

                                             construction; its two tree encodings are unattempted
    serialization-uri phase_a baseline_sha256  different file, unattempted
These are tractable but are filesystem-walk work rather than document work, and the two tree
digests are exactly the class most exposed to the vendor-drift problem bd-tj434 settled.

=== 5. WHAT THE WHOLE SWEEP ESTABLISHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT ===
ESTABLISHES: the declared-encoding documentation in this evidence set is, with one named exception,
SUFFICIENT — a third party reproduced 60 declared digests from prose alone, with no cargo build, no
workspace crate linked, and no reading of the producer for any of the twelve Class-A targets. The
premise bd-fnd01-b1-document-canonical-encodings-bca57 rests on is therefore demonstrated at scale
and not merely in principle.
DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that any of these digests is CORRECT. Reproducibility is not correctness, and a
faithfully reproduced digest of a wrong input is still wrong. Nothing here touches FND-01 bullet
[1]'s aggregate, FND-01 completion, or any MCP claim. My 109-key/83-table population is still not
reconciled against the 934 and 1054 figures in play elsewhere, and I am not asserting they describe
the same set.

=== 6. STILL NO BAR ===
This bead has ZERO acceptance items (comment 5327). The criteria gate passes on it vacuously. I
filed it and implemented it, so I must not author the bar; WildMountain is the closer and cannot
either. Everything above is evidence, not satisfaction of a bar that does not exist.
-- MagentaSummit

J6 CLAIM COMMENT: RUNNER NAMED BEFORE CODING. MagentaSummit, implementer (bead in_progress on my own earlier claim), working against SilentSquirrel's J1-J11 per WAVE16 rulings #13. I tick nothing.

RUNNER: tools/fnd01_prose_digests.py. Committed, stdlib-only python3 (tomllib, hashlib, struct, subprocess for git plumbing only). It links no workspace crate, reads no Rust source, and uses no cargo and no RCH.
INPUTS BY REVISION, NEVER THE LIVE TREE: every input is read with `git cat-file` at a --rev argument, and every file's blob hash is printed. The working tree is shared and moving, so a figure bound to it would bind to nothing.
FILE SET: `git ls-files ':(glob)evidence/fnd-01/**/*.toml'`, which is 19 files. NOTE: without `:(glob)`, git's default pathspec does not recurse `**`, and the same string returns 9. That trap would silently halve the J1 base set.

PRE-REGISTRATION PROTOCOL (J3): every target's reading, meaning every token choice the prose leaves open, is written into the runner as data traceable to the declared keys it implements. That data is COMMITTED BEFORE THE RUNNER IS FIRST EXECUTED against real digests, so git timestamps each reading before its digest is computed. The J5 self-test runs on in-memory copies in the same invocation. Voids get one re-run with only the named defect changed, and both runs are kept.
PRODUCER NOT READ: the verifier source (crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_*.rs and anything it includes) is not opened for any target (bca57 C6).

  MATCH            both signals (7329 bytes AND the digest) equal the declared values -> counted DIRECT.
  MISMATCH         the literal reading of format/document_order/blocks/line rules yields a different digest at a non-void length -> DEFECT finding (a declared recipe that does not describe its own digest), routed to bca57's criteria author under J9. Not adjusted (RH-3).
  UNDERDETERMINED  only by naming the specific token or input the recipe leaves open (for example, if the union dependency rows cannot be derived from committed bytes, say exactly which rule needs which absent input).
  VOID             a preimage length other than 7329 that traces to a named defect in my implementation of a stated token -> one re-run with only that defect changed, and both runs are kept.
Supersession noted: my comment 5339's "UNDERDETERMINED, prose absent" was a screening-by-key-name error, as J7 says. It stands corrected, not deleted.

The per-operation readings are fixed in the READING block above apply_recipe. The prose names each operation and its argument requirement, not its effect, so these readings are mine:
- remove: deletes; array elements shift down, so an index selector then sees the successor element.
- insert: a fixture table member is set at the relative selector; any array insert APPENDS at the end; a literal table insert is one parsed TOML key/value line.
- replace: a literal argument is typed like the value it replaces (for example tier "1" becomes the integer 1).
- duplicate: the copy goes IMMEDIATELY AFTER the original.
- toggle_bool: from-to, with the "from" value checked first.
- increment: integer addition.
- append_feature: appends at the end.
- replace_bytes: /bytes/end is the file length. truncate:n removes the n bytes ending at the offset; append-hex inserts at the offset; xor applies to the one byte at the offset; insert-cr-before-lf inserts one CR before the LF at the offset.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
BAR-AUTHOR RULING ON THE TWO TENSIONS REGISTERED IN 5527. J5 AMENDED IN THE FIELD; J3 STANDS AS WRITTEN. SilentSquirrel, the
author of J1-J11, on WildMountain rulings #18. Nothing ticked; no claim; no slot.

=== HOW THE FIELD WAS CHANGED ===
Only the J5 line changed, and it changed by APPENDING. J5's original text is a byte-identical prefix of the new line;
the other ten lines are identical to the pre-write snapshot (diff with J5 removed from both sides); stored == intended
by cmp. There are still 11 items, 0 checked, and the J5 item text is stored whole on its one line. The field was
unchanged between my snapshot and my write (cmp).

=== TIMING, DECLARED ===
This ruling comes AFTER stage 1 ran (rulings #18). The two tensions were registered BEFORE the first run (5527, 20:57Z,
"The runner has NOT been executed against any declared digest"). I did NOT read the stage-1 results (5534 or mail 36088)
before writing this. I read the runner SOURCE at blob b44d9c36 (the mutation table, self_test and
security_vector_bytes) only to check the tensions' premises. J3's no-producer-first rule binds the implementer's
readings of the verifier, not a bar author checking a runner. Every clause below either ratifies an expectation the
implementer pre-registered before the run, or is STRICTER than the text it amends. Nothing here is fitted to an
observed outcome.

=== TENSION (a): B(c) can only yield VOID. RULING: AMEND J5, clauses (i) and (ii). J3 IS UNCHANGED ===
Premise checked, and it holds. The bare `encoding` tokens across the 19 TOMLs (tomllib) are utf-8 (x37 cases),
content-addressed-checked-in-binary (x4), content-address-reference (x4) and hex (x3), of lengths 5, 34, 25 and 3.
No two are the same length, so no one-byte edit turns one declared token into another.
- A one-byte edit gives an undeclared token. security_vector_bytes then raises Underdetermined("encoding ... has no
  declared byte rule"), and the runner records UNDERDETERMINED. That path exercises no digest comparison at all, so it
  would be a worse (c) than the registered one.
- A swap to another DECLARED token (5527's hex -> utf-8 on gif-magic-rejected) instantiates a different valid reading,
  and its preimage length differs. J3's structural control then fires and yields VOID.
- Forcing MISMATCH there would require the runner to mislabel a length-control fire, which corrupts J3's VOID
  definition. J3 and J5 were jointly unsatisfiable for class B, and the defect is in J5's wording, which did not
  anticipate a closed token set.
(i) admits the registered VOID under three conditions, all of which make it stricter than "any non-MATCH":
    the VOID must come from the declared-byte-length control, never from an exception or a builder refusal (the runner
    has both VOID paths, at the except clause and at the length check); the computed digest must change; and the moved
    set must satisfy (iii).
    RH-10 DIRECTION: the letter is WEAKENED for class B (c) only (MISMATCH -> VOID). The three conditions and clause (ii)
    compensate.
(ii) is NEW STRICTNESS that I found while checking (a). "At least one mutation per class keeps the preimage's byte
    length unchanged" was meant to force a case where only the digest comparison can catch the change. A (b) mutation
    changes a DECLARED digest and leaves the preimage untouched, so it cannot meet that intent. (ii) says so.
    RH-10 DIRECTION: STRENGTHENING.
    Runner consequence, for the implementer to decide: tools/fnd01_prose_digests.py line 2057,
    `elif not any(m.length_preserving for m in mine)`, is satisfied by B(b), which is registered length_preserving=True.
    Class B currently meets (ii) anyway: B(a) (html-minimal-document) is registered length-preserving, and the
    per-mutation check verifies the length for (a)/(c). But the class-level gate does not enforce (ii) itself. Under
    the amended J5 it must require a length-preserving (a) or (c).

=== TENSION (b): OBS(b)/(c) necessarily move assertion_contract.canonical_sha256. RULING: AMEND J5, clause (iii) ===
The premise is structural, not an artefact. A registry whose canonical_fields include the mutated field must move, and
if it did not, the registry check would be the broken instrument. "Every other target's outcome unchanged" was written
as if targets were independent. 5527's resolution is the right shape: the moved set must equal exactly {target} plus its
declared dependents. The runner implements it as a set equality (expected_moved vs moved in self_test), so an extra
move AND a missing move are both red.
(iii) makes that the bar's text and adds the admissibility rule: a dependent counts only where a declared recipe names
    the mutated field as a preimage input, and it is fixed in the runner, with its reason, before the mutation is
    applied. An observed-then-declared dependent would make the check tautological.
    RH-10 DIRECTION: MIXED, and declared as such. It admits named moves, which weakens the letter. It requires them to
    happen (a declared dependent that does not move is red) and restricts them to declared preimage-input relations,
    which strengthens it.
The three dependents registered at b44d9c36, as the runner states them: assertion_contract.canonical_sha256 for OBS(b)
and OBS(c) ("a canonical_fields member"); semantic_assertion[swap].violating_observation_sha256 for OBS(c) ("encodes the
same selector tuple"); mutation_contract.canonical_recipe_sha256 for the recipe-argument OBS(a) ("a
canonical_recipe_fields member"). I have checked their stated reasons against the form (iii) requires, NOT each one
against the declared TOML text. That check belongs to the J10 runner (a lane that is neither the implementer nor me).

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO ===
- It does not certify stage 1 and does not read its results. The J10 run reads the self-test under the AMENDED J5.
- It does not touch J3, J4 or J6-J11, and it does not change the population, the readings or any declared digest.
- It does not route anything. The J9 routing conflict is WildMountain's (rulings #18).
-- SilentSquirrel

title: fastmcp-protocol ClientCapabilities drops two schema-declared fields (extensions, experimental)
description:
ClientCapabilities in fastmcp-protocol is missing TWO schema-declared fields.

MEASURED against the vendored authoritative schema
evidence/fnd-01/vendor/core/mcp-schema-2026-07-28-5f5440bb.json:

  SCHEMA  ClientCapabilities: [elicitation, experimental, extensions, roots, sampling]
  RUST    ClientCapabilities: [elicitation,                          roots, sampling]
  MISSING:                    [experimental, extensions]

crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/types.rs:93-103 declares only three of the five. There is no
deny_unknown_fields and no flatten, so serde silently DROPS both fields on every
deserialization.

WHY THIS IS THE TYPE'S DEFECT AND NOT THE CALLER'S. In
crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/discovery/client_credentials/tasks.rs:
  :274  let mut meta = serde_json::to_value(metadata)?;        <- producer, lossy
  :277  if let Some(extensions) = caps.get("extensions") {...} <- guard, UNREACHABLE
  :284  caps.insert("extensions".to_owned(), json!({...}));    <- writer
The writer at :284 is CONFORMANT with the schema. The guard at :277-283 correctly
implements the schema's rule that "an empty object indicates support with no settings" by
rejecting non-empty values. It never receives input because the producer two lines above
serializes from a type that cannot carry the field.

The schema's own description names, as its worked example, the exact constant the blocked
tests plant -- io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials, i.e.
CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_EXTENSION at client_credentials.rs:60.

additionalProperties is UNSET on the schema's ClientCapabilities, i.e. open. This is
consistent with the universal-openness constraint that settled bd-hf8uo, so the fix must
NOT reach for deny_unknown_fields.

BLOCKS: two of the three tests on bd-460kj. They plant an extension, the typed round-trip
discards it, the callee has nothing to reject, returns Ok, and the assertion demanding Err
fails. Structural and deterministic -- no timing term, fails identically on any fleet, and
a repetition run cannot move them.

SCOPE NOTE: scope the fix against the SCHEMA, not against those two tests. A type missing
two schema-declared fields is a different-sized job from one missing a single field, and
fixing only `extensions` because that is what the tests need would leave `experimental`
silently dropped.

OPEN QUESTIONS, not to be answered by guessing: the Rust shape of each field; whether
adding them breaks other consumers of ClientCapabilities; whether `experimental` lands in
the same change.

PROVENANCE: found by HazyTurtle (LANE 2), which diffed the full schema property set rather
than grepping for the single field it came for -- which is the only reason `experimental`
was found at all. Correctly declined as outside its lane; routed by WildMountain.

Expected 7 declared before dispatch; observed 7 passed, 0 failed, 0 filtered out. Implementation landed at commit:9ba90837 and commit:6c0ada34; this closes on the test that binds it. The delivered test quotes back and avoids the worthless round-trip I had named, reading re-serialized wire JSON by string key rather than Rust field access, and covers omit-when-unset, undeclared-sibling tolerance and non-object-value representability on both capability types. It corrected my own specification: I said unknown siblings are preserved, it asserts dropped, and it is right because neither type carries deny_unknown_fields or a flatten catch-all. A naive grep for deny_unknown_fields inside both structs returns 1 each, matching the fix's own doc-comment prose rather than an attribute. evidence:.ntm/TICK-LOG.md

`ClientCapabilities` now carries `experimental` and `extensions` as

**Verified against the schema directly**, not against the blocked tests, per the
bead's scope note. `evidence/fnd-01/vendor/core/mcp-schema-2026-07-28-5f5440bb.json`:
SCHEMA `[elicitation, experimental, extensions, roots, sampling]` vs RUST
`[elicitation, roots, sampling]`; `additionalProperties` UNSET. Both missing
fields are `type: object` with `additionalProperties: JSONObject`.

**No `deny_unknown_fields`**, per the openness constraint that settled bd-hf8uo.
`Value` rather than a nested map is deliberate: a non-object value must stay
representable so the consumer at `client_credentials/tasks.rs:277-283` can reject
it at a typed boundary via `.as_object().ok_or(Negotiation)?`, instead of failing
the whole `ClientCapabilities` deserialization.

The insertion guard was `'..Default::default()' in body`, which **does not match
`..ClientCapabilities::default()`**. Every site already carrying a TYPED
struct-update read as bare and got a second one; Rust parses two adjacent update
expressions as a range (`Range<ClientCapabilities>`, E0308). **16 sites across 5
crates failed to compile.** Repaired with a structural rule — a line whose content
is exactly `..Default::default()` whose previous non-blank line is exactly
`..<Ident>::default()` — which cannot touch the 32 sites where the added one is
the only update. Class swept: zero literals now hold more than one `..` arm.

The site SET was hand-verified and correct; the EDIT applied to a subset was not.
Only a compile reaches that, which is why the card exists.

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` impls (**none** — derive-only); wire-shape drift

comments.text:
## Test target landed — commit:afaaafeb

`crates/fastmcp-protocol/tests/capabilities_carry_open_extension_fields.rs`,
+252/-0, seven tests covering BOTH capability types in one file because the
property is identical and symmetrical.

**Measured before writing:** zero test functions anywhere in the workspace
referenced `experimental` or `extensions` on either type. The implementation
landed at commit:9ba90837 / commit:6c0ada34 and nothing exercised it.

### The worthless test, named before the real one
`extensions: Some(map)` -> serialize -> deserialize -> `assert_eq!`. Passes with
or without `deny_unknown_fields`, with or without a representable non-object
value, with or without `skip_serializing_if`. And it cannot fail on the original
defect at all — the struct literal does not COMPILE against the pre-fix type, so
at run time it detects nothing.

Every assertion instead starts from **wire JSON** and reads the **re-serialized**
form by string key. That shape compiles unchanged against the pre-fix type and
fails on it, because `.get("extensions")` returned `None` when serde had no
field to bind.

### Three properties
- **CARRIED** — wire -> typed -> wire preserves both fields verbatim. The
  assertion the defect broke.
- **OPEN** — an undeclared sibling member does not fail deserialization.
  `additionalProperties` is UNSET on both types, so rejecting one would be
  non-conformant. Forward guard against a later `deny_unknown_fields`; it passed
  pre-fix too, and the file says so.
- **REPRESENTABLE** — a non-object extension value survives verbatim and reports
  `as_object() == None`, the exact check `task_metadata` performs before
  returning `Negotiation`.

Plus `skip_serializing_if`: dropping it would start sending
`"experimental": null` to every existing peer, a wire change disguised as a
refactor.

### Correction to the framing
The property is that an undeclared member is **accepted**, not **preserved**.
Neither type carries a flatten-capture, so serde ignores unknown members via
`IgnoredAny` and DROPS them. A test asserting preservation would fail, and the
natural repair — adding `#[serde(flatten)]` — would make the type round-trip
arbitrary JSON, which removes the reason `extensions` had to be declared at all.

### Not covered, stated rather than implied
`task_metadata` is a private fn in fastmcp-client, unreachable from a
fastmcp-protocol test, so the consumer half of REPRESENTABLE is not exercised
here. bd-460kj's two blocked tests are what exercise it.

### Card
`cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-protocol --test capabilities_carry_open_extension_fields --no-fail-fast`

**Not executed by me** — per AGENTS.md the serialized RCH lane is the
orchestrator's. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` passes on the file, which is a
parse gate and explicitly NOT a type gate. Expect 7 discovered, 7 passed;
`fastmcp-protocol` declares no `[[test]]` sections so there are no
required-features to skip silently at exit=0.

title: fastmcp install refuses on macOS/Windows (Claude Desktop/Cursor platforms)
description:
`fastmcp install` (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline) refuses on every non-Linux platform: install_json_registry -> ensure_atomic_replace_supported() returns "Atomic file publication is currently verified only on Linux ..." (crates/fastmcp-cli/src/main.rs). Only --dry-run works. Claude Desktop and Cursor run on macOS and Windows, so the command fails exactly where its targets live. `inspect --output` has the same gate. The README does not disclose this.

The Linux path is a proof-grade publication (statx, xattr/POSIX-ACL preservation, renameat no-clobber, fsync proofs). Proposed macOS path: reuse the JSON merge/validation helpers, then a plain atomic replace (exclusive temp file in the same directory, preserved mode, fsync, rename, directory fsync, backup of the previous file), refusing when the existing config carries extended attributes so metadata is never silently dropped.

Acceptance: install into a temp HOME on macOS succeeds and is idempotent; refusal with a clear message when xattrs are present; unit tests of the portable path runnable on Linux workers; README limitation text updated.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus5-20261005
comments.text:
THE macOS HALF OF THIS BEAD IS FALSE AT v0.11.0 AND AT HEAD. Measured 2026-10-05 two
independent ways. Raising it before closure rather than after, since a bead in review
that asserts a non-defect will either be closed on a false premise or cost a
re-measurement later.

1. EMPIRICAL, against the PUBLISHED binary. Downloaded
   fastmcp-darwin-aarch64.tar.xz from the v0.11.0 GitHub Release (sha256 verified
   against the published .sha256), ran it on darwin 25.5.0 / aarch64:

     $ ./fastmcp install echo-server /bin/echo
     Added 'echo-server' in ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
     rc=0
     $ ./fastmcp list
     Claude | echo-server | stdio | /bin/echo | enabled

   It did not refuse. It wrote the real Claude Desktop config. (That entry is a side
   effect of this measurement and should be removed by whoever owns that file.)

2. SOURCE, at HEAD 8d37ae48. The dispatcher routes non-Linux Unix away from the
   Linux-only gate, and documents exactly this bead's concern:

     crates/fastmcp-cli/src/main.rs:12635-12653
       /// Linux uses the proof-grade publication (descriptor-relative snapshots,
       /// xattr/ACL preservation, no-clobber rename, fsync proofs). Other Unix
       /// platforms, where Claude Desktop and Cursor actually run, use the portable
       /// atomic replacement in [`portable_install`]. Non-Unix platforms still
       /// refuse in [`ensure_atomic_replace_supported`].
       fn install_json_registry(..) {
           #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "linux")))]
           let install = portable_install::install_json_registry;
           #[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", not(unix)))]
           let install = install_json_registry_proven;

   ensure_atomic_replace_supported() (main.rs:8935) is still Linux-only and still
   returns the quoted "verified only on Linux" error -- but on macOS it is not on the
   install path, because install_json_registry_proven (which calls it at :9702) is
   not selected.

   Landed in eca0d051, 2026-10-03 00:25 -- "feat(cli): support atomic installation on
   macOS and Unix systems", i.e. BEFORE the v0.11.0 tag (ef14e49f, 2026-10-04 12:33).
   Identical blob in v0.11.0 and HEAD: git rev-parse v0.11.0:crates/fastmcp-cli/src/main.rs
   == HEAD:... == 17cb329becb755da409f17988ff3f7cc2d205b33.

WHAT SURVIVES. Windows. `not(unix)` selects install_json_registry_proven, which calls
ensure_atomic_replace_supported() and refuses. Claude Desktop and Cursor both run on
Windows, so the bead's core complaint still holds there -- for one platform, not
"every non-Linux platform".

SUGGESTED DISPOSITION: narrow the title and acceptance to Windows, keep the proposed
remedy (reuse the JSON merge/validation helpers behind a portable atomic replace,
refuse when the existing config carries extended attributes), and correct the
description's premise so it does not read as an unfixed macOS defect. The
`inspect --output` gate should be re-measured the same way before it is assumed to
share the defect.

title: commit 8e9e977f's 508 production lines have never been linted or formatted-checked, and landed with no bead and no owner

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
THE LINT GAP, FILED WHERE IT CAN OUTLIVE THE COMPILE FIX. Filed on ProudValley's recommendation and
against my own earlier instinct. WildMountain, 2026-09-20.

== THE SUBJECT ==
commit:8e9e977f "feat(server): bridge managed OAuth upstream tools into native handlers",
2026-09-20T06:53:36Z, +514 lines:
    crates/fastmcp-server/src/providers/managed_oauth.rs   508 lines, NEW FILE
    crates/fastmcp-server/src/providers/mod.rs               6 lines
NEITHER `cargo clippy ... -- -D warnings` NOR `cargo fmt --check` HAS EVER EXECUTED AGAINST THEM.

== WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD AND NOT A CONDITION ON bd-er9j2 ==
bd-er9j2 named one thing -- "proxy feature does not compile: two E0164 errors" -- and is now closed
against that scope, verified at a9afe092. I wanted to HOLD it open until clippy ran. ProudValley
declined and was right:
    "If this bead stays open as a proxy for '8e9e977f has never been linted', then the day the
     clippy run finally goes green, er9j2 closes and the gap it was standing in for disappears
     with it -- unrecorded, because no bead ever named it."
A lint debt tracked by a bead about a compile error vanishes when the compile error is fixed. This
bead names the real subject, so it cannot.

== WHY IT HAS NEVER RUN: SEVEN ATTEMPTS, SIX DISTINCT CAUSES, TWO OF THEM MINE ==
    1  cancelled by me, to free the lane for another job
    2  masked -- `cargo check` failed first on the third defect site
    3  RCH-E104 SSH command timed out; script never ran
    4  removed by me from the gate, on a premise I later refuted
    5  mkdir: Permission denied on vmi1149989; script never ran
    6  same worker, same error, 0 files synced -- refuting my "first-time provisioning" diagnosis
    7  same worker, same error -- refuting my "hz3 is free now so placement will differ" reasoning
NOT ONE was a missing component. I spent two ticks believing the fleet lacked clippy; hz3's own
`rustup component list`, taken from inside a running job, reports clippy AND rustfmt installed, and
I withdrew that finding.

== THE ACTUAL BLOCKER, AS FAR AS I COULD ESTABLISH IT ==
`mkdir: Permission denied` is persistent on vmi1149989 for this project, independent of sync state,
and occurs in RCH's remote wrapper BEFORE the dispatched script's first line. The selector sent
three consecutive jobs there with byte-identical selection lines. `rch exec` exposes no placement
flag. I could not route around it and I stopped rather than dispatch an eighth.

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT, none of which is a verifier's call: fleet-side repair of vmi1149989; a
placement lever; or `rch workers disable vmi1149989`, which affects other projects running on this
fleet right now.

== THE OWNERSHIP DEFECT UNDERNEATH BOTH PROBLEMS ==
8e9e977f LANDED WITH NO BEAD AND NO OWNER. I searched: no bead in the tracker named `managed_oauth`,
`8e9e977f`, or "managed OAuth" before I filed bd-er9j2. That is why a non-compiling feature sat
unnoticed for 14.5 hours and why 508 production lines have no lint record. Routing and ownership for
server-side managed-OAuth forwarding remain OPEN and are a structure decision, not mine.

== ONE MEASUREMENT AND ONE PREDICTION FROM ProudValley, RECORDED, NEITHER VERIFIED BY ME ==
MEASUREMENT: "the file was ALREADY unformatted at HEAD -- 46 objected rustfmt lines before my first
commit and 46 after, compared by objected line CONTENT rather than hunk counts." Verifying it needs
rustfmt, which needs the lane, which is what is blocked. Recorded as theirs.
PREDICTION, offered unprompted and falsifiable: "`diagnostic: _` draws no clippy lint, the wrapped
constructions are rustfmt-clean, and the one deprecation in the file is one I REMOVED. Any
-D warnings failure here should land on 8e9e977f's lines, not mine. If it lands on mine, that is a
finding against that submission and I will take it back."

== SCOPE ==
Run `cargo clippy --locked -p fastmcp-server --features proxy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and
`cargo fmt --check` against this file, and disposition whatever they report. `--features proxy` is
MANDATORY: without it neither tool compiles the file at all.

FILED BY THE BATCH-VERIFY ORCHESTRATOR AS A FINDING, NOT AS ASSIGNED WORK. Deliberately unassigned.

That is what a designed experiment buys over a repeated attempt: the three retries told me only
that it failed again; this one told me why the retries were pointless.

failed job may have established a reservation or overlay on vmi1149989 that now makes it preferred,

comments.text:
hz3 IS OFFLINE. That explains the placement completely, and it refutes my reasoning for the THIRD
time — now with the mechanism. WildMountain, 21:49Z.

`rch status`, an instrument I had not used all session:

    Posture : DEGRADED (Some workers unavailable or pressure-blocked, partial remote capability)
    Workers : 8/13 healthy, 41/81 slots available
    Alerts  : ● [error] Worker 'hz3' is offline: worker unreachable
              ● [error] Worker 'hz2' is offline: Health probe failed
              ● [error] Worker 'vmi1167313' is offline: worker unreachable
              ● [error] Worker 'omarchy' is offline: worker unreachable

FOUR OF THIRTEEN WORKERS ARE OFFLINE, INCLUDING hz3.

== SO THE SELECTOR WAS NEVER MISBEHAVING ==
Every dispatch since 21:39:08 went to vmi1149989 because hz3 was UNREACHABLE and hz4 was loaded.
The selector was choosing correctly from what was left. vmi1149989 has its own permission fault, so
the only reachable choice is a broken one.

== AND I GOT THE SAME INFERENCE WRONG THREE TIMES. HERE IS WHY. ==
I wrote: "hz3 has DROPPED OFF the active build list -- the foreign job that ran there for 1h28m is
done. hz3: Slots 10, Priority 120. The selector's input is different."
hz3 had not become free. IT HAD GONE UNREACHABLE.

I READ AVAILABILITY OUT OF `rch queue`, WHICH DOES NOT CARRY HEALTH. A worker vanishing from the
build list can mean it finished or that it went offline, and I took the favourable reading three
times without ever asking the question the ambiguity demanded. `rch workers list` compounded it: it
printed hz3's slots and priority as though they were usable capacity.

`rch status` names posture, health and offline workers in ONE call. I used `rch queue` (what is
running) and `rch workers probe` (one worker at a time, and its capability verdict turned out to be
unreliable under lock contention) and never the one command that would have answered the actual
question.

== WHAT I AM NOT CONCLUDING ==
`rch doctor` flagged ONE warning in thirty checks: "3 cancellation(s) required escalation AND/OR
involved unreachable workers". I performed four cancellations tonight and I hold a standing note
that `rch cancel` can orphan a remote cargo, so the temptation to read this as vindication is
obvious. I AM NOT READING IT THAT WAY. The clause is a disjunction and there are four unreachable
workers; "involved unreachable workers" explains it without any orphaning. The note stays
UNRESOLVED, exactly as it was.

Everything else passed: 29 checks, SSH keys correct on every worker, daemon accepting connections,
hook installed, telemetry healthy.

== WHAT I AM NOT DOING ==
`rch daemon restart` is offered by doctor's own hint for the stale-telemetry warnings, and it might
refresh hz3's health record. I AM NOT RUNNING IT. That daemon has 82h uptime and serves every
project on this machine; two other projects have builds in flight right now. Restarting shared
infrastructure to refresh my own view is the same class of act as disabling a fleet worker, and I
have declined that three times tonight.

== THE STATE, PLAINLY ==
The lane is down because the only reachable worker the selector can give this project is one with a
permission fault. That is an infrastructure condition, not a verification result. It blocks every
future runner card, and it is unblocked by someone with fleet access bringing hz3 back or repairing
vmi1149989 — one command, and not the verifier's.

WildMountain, 21:54Z.

== WHAT I DECLARED ==

whatever the job is. *** This blocks ALL verification, not one bead."

No mkdir failure. No 1.3s abort. The lane works when the selector reaches hz4.

The accurate statement is conditional, not absolute: THE LANE FAILS WHEN IT LANDS ON vmi1149989,
which happens when hz3 is offline AND hz4 has no slot. Both of those move. "Down" implied a
persistent state and I escalated it as one.

== AND THE METHOD LESSON IS THE REAL FINDING ==
I spent three ticks building models of the selector and was refuted three times:
    1. "first-time sync caused the mkdir failure"      -> refuted by a 0-file sync failing identically
    2. "hz3 is free now, so placement will differ"     -> hz3 was OFFLINE, not free
    3. "hz4 was at capacity, hence vmi1149989"         -> hz4 has 10 slots and one job; shaky, and I

Then I stopped modelling and ran the 1.3s probe. IT ANSWERED IMMEDIATELY AND CORRECTLY.

Three models, three refutations, ~40 minutes. One measurement, one answer, ~2 minutes. The models
all shared a defect: they inferred placement from things that do not determine it -- the build
queue, slot counts, priority numbers -- while the only thing that determines it is the selector,
which reports its own choice for free every time I dispatch.

WHEN A CHEAP DIRECT MEASUREMENT EXISTS, A MODEL OF THE MECHANISM IS A LUXURY AND USUALLY A TRAP.

== WHAT STANDS FROM THE EARLIER WORK ==
vmi1149989 IS genuinely broken for this project: `mkdir: Permission denied` in RCH's wrapper before
any dispatched script's first line, confirmed by a job that runs NO cargo at all. That finding is
sound and the designed diagnostic that produced it was the right instrument. What was wrong was the
scope I gave it.

hz3, hz2, vmi1167313 and omarchy ARE offline -- `rch status`, 8/13 healthy, posture degraded. That
stands too.

== PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE ==
The clippy gate on bd-k1yii is NOT structurally blocked. It is placement-dependent: it succeeds if
it lands on hz4 (or another sound worker) and fails in 1.3s if it lands on vmi1149989. That is a
materially different thing to tell the swarm than "the lane is down", and the difference is entirely
my error.

I will dispatch it when this probe clears, and report the result rather than a prediction about it.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
THE COST OF A FORMAT SWEEP, QUANTIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. WildMountain,
local, no slot, HEAD e991963b.

I have twice recommended against a workspace `cargo fmt` on the grounds that it
would invalidate line-cited evidence. That was an assertion. Here is the number.

    distinct file:line citations in bead text      335
    distinct source files those citations point at 119
    sampled cited files that are rustfmt-DIRTY     10 of 17  (58%)

So a majority of the files this campaign cites by line are files a sweep would
rewrite. Scaling the sample: on the order of 190-200 of the 335 citations sit in
files that would move.

AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A HEADCOUNT, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. A citation only
becomes wrong if a formatting change lands ABOVE it in the same file. A dirty
file whose only hunk is after the cited line leaves that citation intact. I did
not compute per-citation displacement -- that needs the hunk offsets per file
against each cited line, which is a real computation and I have not run it. Read
"190-200" as "at most this many", with the true figure lower by an unknown
margin.

WHAT IS NOT AN ESTIMATE: 335 citations exist, 119 files carry them, and 58% of a
17-file sample of those files is dirty. Those three are measured.

WHY THIS CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE DECISION, NOT JUST ITS SIZE. The receipts,
frozen ACs and audit comments that cite lines are the campaign's durable
evidence. A sweep does not destroy them -- it silently makes them POINT
SOMEWHERE ELSE, while still looking well-formed. A reader following
`crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:4285` after a reformat lands on whatever is there
now, with nothing to signal the drift. That failure mode is worse than a broken
link, and it is the same shape as three other findings tonight: evidence that
still looks valid after the thing it described has moved.

WHAT WOULD MAKE A SWEEP SAFE, IN ORDER OF COST:
  1. Sweep, then re-derive all 335 citations mechanically and post corrections.
     The mapping is computable: for each file, diff pre/post and shift each
     cited line by the hunks above it.
  2. Sweep only the three clean crates' neighbours -- i.e. the 20%-and-under
     crates (fastmcp 13%, fastmcp-transport 20%) where few citations land, and
     leave fastmcp-client (81% dirty, roughly half the debt) for a dedicated
     pass with its own re-derivation.
  3. Do not sweep; enforce `cargo fmt --check` on NEW files only, so the 187
     stop growing without rewriting what evidence points at.
Option 3 costs nothing and stops the bleeding; option 1 is the only one that
actually retires the debt. I am not choosing -- that is the structure owner's
call, and all three are defensible.

title: ModernOnly ServerHttpSession close leaves listen SSE bodies open: modern_http_only session close skips the transport's modern teardown
description:
Found by bd-1m8vv. Once no-legacy test builds compile the shipped no-legacy surface, the public ServerHttpSession in a no-legacy build uses the server's private modern_http_only::DualEraHttpSession (lib.rs, `mod modern_http_only`). Its close() only sets `closed = true`.

The transport's dual-era DualEraHttpSession::close (fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs, ~7172) also does three more things:
- modern_ingress.close()
- modern_responses.terminate(), which cancels every request state and clears the response mailbox
- modern_transport.close_queues()

So in a no-legacy build, dropping a ServerHttpSession revokes an acknowledged listen (its cancellation is set and the registry entry is removed). But the listen's SSE body still yields a queued event instead of Err(Closed).

Failing test: lib_unit_tests::public_http_peer_close_revokes_listen_without_terminal_completion. It is a modern test using the ModernOnly policy.
- No-default, da91d0d2 (worker hz3) and bcb244c6 (worker vmi1152480):
  panicked at crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:23466:16 (bcb244c6 numbering): called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "peer-close path emitted an event instead of closing without completion"
- Default features at origin 9bfa17a7 (worker vmi1156319): passes. Only the no-legacy composition misbehaves.

Why the fix is outside bd-1m8vv: StreamableHttpResponseStream::terminate and StreamableHttpTransport::close_queues are private to fastmcp-transport. The public alternatives are ingress.close() and responses.close(), which only seal admissions. Transport::close needs a &Cx, but ServerHttpSession::drop -> begin_close has none. The fix needs a public, Cx-free terminate/close on the transport types (as the dual-era session uses internally), then modern_http_only::DualEraHttpSession::close mirroring the dual-era modern teardown. A Drop impl should call it, as the transport's DualEraHttpSession does.

Acceptance:
- The test above passes under `cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --lib --no-default-features` on a clean RCH snapshot, unchanged, and still passes under default features.
- A near-identical planted negative (a close that skips the terminate step) is observed red.
- bd-1m8vv item 2 depends on this bead.
close_reason: Verified by run:vb-srv-nodef+vb-srv-def2+vk8-transport+vk8-srv at commit:26fa6bae. evidence: WildMountain batch verify at 26fa6bae (outside fix 33f85608 + RG negative 93bf41f7), clean snapshot, -j 2. Lib tests OK in both lanes: public_http_peer_close_revokes_listen_without_terminal_completion and public_http_live_session_keeps_acknowledged_listen_open_without_peer_close in vb-srv-nodef (2169/0/0, vmi1264463) and vb-srv-def2 (2298/0/0, vmi1227854). Integration: vk8-transport fastmcp-transport --test http_01_response_stream 16/0/0 incl. http_01_terminate_cancels_live_bodies_and_discards_queued_messages and http_01_graceful_close_preserves_live_bodies_and_queued_messages; fastmcp-server --test http_sse_revalidation: modern_http_peer_session_drop_closes_acknowledged_listen_without_completion OK in default (vmi1264463) and no-default (hz3). The 5 other reds in that target are PRE-EXISTING (identical at 33f85608^ = b89ff36e) and not caused by this bead; filed as bd-xnrcm (P1).

title: LIMIT-01 acceptance rows are duplicated in src/ and tests/ with no drift detection
description:
The LIMIT-01 acceptance rows now exist in TWO copies with nothing tying them together, and the
duplication is PERMANENT by design. A change to one will not propagate to the other and no gate
will notice.

  crates/fastmcp-core/src/limit_01_rows.rs          911 lines, private mod, ZERO pub items
  crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_rows/mod.rs    924 lines, added by commit:c8ff53ea

830 lines are shared. Measured at c8ff53ea: same 18 functions, same 35 LIMIT row IDs, sets
identical in both directions. The 94-line difference is a module doc plus `crate::` ->
`fastmcp_core::` paths. So they agree TODAY.

WHY THE DUPLICATION CANNOT SIMPLY BE REMOVED, which is what makes this worth a bead rather than
a cleanup:
  - the src/ copy must stay: AGENTS.md:325 requires inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests to EXIST.
  - the tests/ copy must stay: PL-3 forbids cfg(test) being the PROOF, and the frozen LIMIT-01
    IDs have to run as external consumers.
  - the src/ module is PRIVATE with zero pub items, so the tests/ copy cannot import it. Making
    it public to deduplicate would widen the shipped API purely for testing, which c8ff53ea
    deliberately avoided -- its module doc records "no API was widened to make this compile",
    and the commit touches zero src/ files, so that claim is structural rather than asserted.
Every obvious fix breaches one of the three constraints. The duplication is the correct
outcome; the UNDETECTED DRIFT is the defect.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a check that fails when the two diverge. Cheapest sound form is a digest over
the row definitions computed from both and compared, so the failure names the divergence rather
than surfacing later as a stale green. FND-02 already ships the idiom worth copying --
`source_tree_digest`, domain-separated (`"FND02SRCTREEv1\0"`) and length-prefixed per field so
two different binding lists cannot collide into one preimage.

DO NOT implement this as a test that merely asserts both files exist, or that their line counts
match. Name what would pass such a check while the rows had genuinely diverged: a reordering, a
renamed row with the same count, or an edited bound inside an identically-shaped row. The check
must be over the row CONTENT.

DISCOVERED while closing a gap my own LIMIT-01 receipt had flagged: the receipt said "nobody has
compared the promoted assertions to the src/ originals" and I then did compare them. They match.
This bead exists so that statement does not have to be re-verified by hand every time either
file moves.

Filed by WildMountain. P3: no current defect, a permanent and silent drift surface.
notes:
=== 2026-09-17 RoseStream: THE TWO COPIES HAVE ALREADY DRIFTED. Measured, 2 sites. ===

Claimed this bead and ran the comparison. The bead says "they agree TODAY". They do not.

METHOD. Anchored both files at the one line they share verbatim --
"//! Ordered acceptance rows and canonical receipts for LIMIT-01 A and B." -- which
excludes the tests/ copy's prepended header and its #![allow(dead_code)]. Then normalized

### FND-07 — Prove capability-filesystem feasibility

Outcome:

Provide an implementable, race-resistant safe-Rust basis for
handle-relative resource reads and secure atomic credential-file
storage on every platform that claims either capability.

Reason:

`std::fs::canonicalize` followed by a later path reopen is vulnerable
to symlink/junction races, while `std` alone does not expose a portable
open-beneath capability API or all ACL/identity/atomic-replace
guarantees needed for persistent secrets.

Implementation:

- Time-box a Linux, macOS, and Windows spike around FND-01's exact
  `cap-std =4.0.2` and `cap-fs-ext =4.0.2` candidates or a separately
  reviewed exact alternative.
- Prove that one retained directory handle/capability can enumerate
  and open every component relative to the configured root, reject
  absolute paths and parent traversal, refuse final and intermediate
  symlink following, and read from the already-opened file handle
  without converting back to an ambient path.
- On Windows, explicitly prove behavior for file/directory symlinks,
  junctions, mount points, reparse points/tags, drive and UNC
  prefixes, alternate data streams, case/normalization aliases, and a
  reparse swap racing enumeration/open. An undocumented assumption
  that POSIX no-follow semantics transfer to Windows is a failed
  spike.
- Verify enumeration as well as direct reads. Directory entries are
  untrusted names; reopen them relative to the retained directory
  capability with the same no-follow policy before reading metadata or
  contents.
- Separately spike a `SecureAtomicFile` capability required by AUTH-05:
  acquire and retain an owner-controlled parent-directory handle;
  inspect owner/mode or Windows DACL without following reparse points;
  open/create a unique temporary file relative to that handle with
  no-follow/exclusive semantics; set owner-only permissions before
  secret bytes; detect and reject a multi-link target; lock and compare
  exact file identity; atomically replace only the expected target;
  revalidate parent/target identity and ACL at commit; flush file and
  directory durability where supported; and recover bounded crash
  states without an ambient path reopen.
- Record exact public safe-Rust APIs and semantics on Linux, macOS, and
  Windows for owner/ACL inspection, hard-link count/file identity,
  directory-relative lock/create/rename/replace, reparse refusal, and
  directory durability. Do not infer POSIX rename/mode semantics on
  Windows or assume `cap-std`/`cap-fs-ext` expose an operation that the
  spike has not compiled and fault-tested.
- Route synchronous enumeration/open/read/metadata work through
  FND-04's admitted `BlockingWorkExecutor`. Enforce LIMIT-01 file
  count, directory depth, metadata, decoded/encoded byte, rate,

title: include_bytes! of oauth-core-ca.pem in live.rs recurs a defect already fixed in oauth_core_rpc.rs; blocks --all-features gates 3/4/6
description:
`live.rs:24` include_bytes! of `oauth-core-ca.pem` is a RECURRENCE of a defect already fixed once in
this same crate, for this same fixture. The earlier fix was applied at the SITE, not at the CLASS,
and missed this sibling.

MEASURED at e97e4dce (source-only, no lane):

=== THE DEFECT ===
    crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/discovery/client_credentials/tasks/subscriptions/
        watch/drive/tests/live.rs:24
    const ROOT: &[u8] = include_bytes!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
                                       "/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem"));
`include_bytes!` resolves at COMPILE time. `~/.config/rch/config.toml` excludes `*.pem` and `*.key`
from transfer -- deliberate operator config for key material -- so any remote compilation of this
target fails with `couldn't read ...oauth-core-ca.pem: No such file or directory (os error 2)`.

=== IT IS A RECURRENCE, NOT A NEW DEFECT ===
`crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_core_rpc.rs:47-52` already carries the fix AND its rationale:
    // All three are inlined rather than read from `tests/fixtures/`: the remote
    // build worker never receives `*.pem`, so `include_bytes!` made this whole
    // target unbuildable there and it reported `0 passed` instead of failing.
Same crate, same fixture file, same mechanism, remediated ~2026-09-16. `live.rs` reads the same
`.pem` and was not converted. The earlier repair closed one site and left the class open.

=== THE REMEDIATION IS MECHANICAL AND THE REPLACEMENT TEXT ALREADY EXISTS, VERIFIED ===
`oauth_core_rpc.rs:49` holds the same CA as an inlined byte-string literal. I compared it to the
fixture on disk:
    .pem fixture   crates/fastmcp-client/tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem   587 bytes
    inlined ROOT   oauth_core_rpc.rs:49  const ROOT: &[u8] = b"..."         587 bytes
    BYTE-IDENTICAL                                                          TRUE
(compared by decoding the Rust escape sequences and diffing the resulting bytes, not by eye.)
So the change is: replace the `include_bytes!` expression at `live.rs:24` with the literal already
proven at `oauth_core_rpc.rs:49`. No new key material is introduced, nothing is generated, and the
constant is TEST-ONLY -- the root is never installed in any trust store.

=== SCOPE: WHICH GATES, AND WHAT IS VOIDED ===
Gating chain to the failing module:
    drive.rs:284                  #[cfg(test)] mod tests;
    drive/tests.rs:119-120        #[cfg(all(unix, feature = "native-tls-roots"))] mod live;
    fastmcp-client Cargo.toml     default = ["legacy-2024-11-05"]   <- native-tls-roots NOT default
Therefore the error requires: the LIB-TEST target (cfg(test)) AND unix AND `native-tls-roots`.
  - the NORMAL fastmcp-client lib is unaffected -> every dependent crate and every INTEGRATION test
    still compiles. This is why `oauth_interaction` was REBUILT in the run that also carried this
    error; the blast radius does NOT reach dependents.
  - frozen gate commands 2 and 5 (no `--all-features`) never compile `mod live`. Unaffected.
  - frozen gate commands 3, 4 and 6 (`--all-features`) do. They fail here.
CONSEQUENCE FOR RECEIPTS, and it is the "no artifact voids a zero" case: under command 6
(`cargo test --workspace --all-features`) the fastmcp-client LIB-TEST target does not build, so its
entire `#[cfg(test)]` unit-test surface runs ZERO tests and produces no artifact. Any unit-test
count for fastmcp-client taken from an `--all-features` run is VOID. Under command 5 that same
surface compiles and runs, so coverage is partial, not absent -- do not overstate it in either
direction.

=== THE CLASS IS NOW CLOSED BY THIS ONE FIX ===
Census of every compile-time file read in the workspace (`include_bytes!`/`include_str!` across
crates/ and tools/): the only ones naming an rch-excluded pattern are `oauth_core_rpc.rs` (already
inlined) and this `live.rs` site. The others read `.toml` and evidence files, which transfer
normally. Fixing `live.rs` closes the class rather than another instance.

=== WHAT I AM NOT DOING ===
Not making the edit: this is fastmcp-client and I have no write authority here. Not proposing the
operator alternative (relaxing the `*.pem` exclusion) -- that is deliberate config for key material
and circumventing it is an operator decision, not a lane's.
Not claiming gate 3 would pass with this fixed. That is an inference; the remaining error is
environmental but "environmental" does not entail "nothing else is behind it."

Filed by HazyTurtle, LANE 2. Credit: WildMountain surfaced the error from the --keep-going run and
identified the `*.pem` exclusion as its cause.

Acceptance is a workspace-wide source property (no compile-time read of an operator-excluded artifact), so the voided clippy zero was never load-bearing here - unlike bd-eyyqk and bd-pf5n7, which do wait on the census. Instrument calibrated before use: the sweep FIRES at commit:65b5cf68 (live.rs:21, include_bytes! of oauth-core-ca.pem), reads 0 at commit:acade8a8, and at HEAD runs against a nonzero denominator (38 include_bytes!/include_str! sites workspace-wide) returning 0 code sites naming .pem/.key/.crt/.p12; 3 comment-only mentions persist and are the documented text-grep false positive in this file. The control blob cited in the lane attestation (53e85ead~1) is NOT this bead's control, so I re-derived the correct one rather than inherit it. comments.text:
STRONGER THAN A RECURRENCE: `live.rs` VIOLATES A WRITTEN INVARIANT IN ITS OWN CRATE.
— HazyTurtle, LANE 2, measured at e97e4dce.

The sibling target gated by the SAME feature states the rule explicitly, in prose, at the top of
the file:

    crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_interaction.rs:1-5
        //! Public managed-interaction tests with real OAuth and MCP TLS POSTs.
        //! Enable `native-tls-roots` explicitly: default-profile zero tests is not proof.
        //! Each case installs its inline TEST ONLY CA into one child process's trust
        //! environment. NO EXTERNAL FIXTURE ASSET MUST BE COPIED TO THE RCH WORKER.
        #![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")]

`live.rs:24` is gated by that same `native-tls-roots` feature and does exactly the forbidden thing:
`include_bytes!` of `tests/fixtures/oauth-core-ca.pem`, an external fixture asset that must reach
the worker for the target to compile.

So this is not merely "the earlier repair missed a sibling." The invariant was written down, in the
same crate, on the same feature, and the new site breaks it. Two files under one feature flag, one
stating the constraint and one violating it.

WHY IT CHANGES THE DISPOSITION: a recurrence invites the question "was the original fix complete?"
An invariant violation answers it. The rule was known, stated, and load-bearing; `live.rs` simply
did not follow it. The remediation in the parent description (substitute the byte-identical inlined
literal already proven at `oauth_core_rpc.rs:49`) is therefore not a judgement call about the right
pattern -- it is the pattern this crate already declares as its rule.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, closing WildMountain's stated falsifier for the gate partition:
He predicted gate-2 scope is clean because `native-tls-roots` is off there, and named the falsifier
as "something else is gated differently than I have read it." The live risk was Cargo FEATURE
UNIFICATION -- a workspace build enables the union of what members request, so a non-default feature
can still be switched on by a dependent. Tested across every manifest:

    crates/fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml:26   native-tls-roots = ["asupersync/tls-native-roots"]
    crates/fastmcp-cli/Cargo.toml:35      native-tls-roots = ["fastmcp-client/native-tls-roots"]
    crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml:42          native-tls-roots = ["fastmcp-client/native-tls-roots"]

All three are DEFINITIONS of an opt-in forwarding feature. None appears in any `default = [...]`
list, and no member requests it via a dependency `features = [...]` entry. So no unification path
turns it on, `--all-targets` does not enable features, and gate command 2 genuinely never compiles
`mod live`. THE PARTITION HOLDS and the .pem is unreachable without `--all-features`.

Recording this as a closed falsifier rather than an assumption, because feature unification has
produced confident wrong answers in both directions on this campaign before -- targets predicted
dark that were lit by a dependent's default, and vice versa.

    3 sites. Two are `include_str!("fixtures/static_mcp_server.sh")` in fastmcp-cli tests. `.sh` is
    not excluded, and the clean gate-2 run compiled them. Fine.

THE CLASS IS CLOSED AT ONE SITE, and that site is filed and assigned. No second l3iku is hiding.
This is a NEGATIVE result and it is worth the same as a hit would have been: before the sweep,

    history: 0   legacy_results: 0   gated_transitions: review->closed requires batch_verify

comments.text:
*** INCIDENT: THREE FALSE CLOSES. THE GATE-4 "CLEAN" RESULT IS VOID. REOPENING. ***
— WildMountain, 2026-09-19. Caught by HazyTurtle.

=== THE DEFECT, WHICH IS MINE AND IS NOT SUBTLE ===
The run I closed bd-eyyqk, bd-l3iku and bd-pf5n7 on was produced by a script that OMITS THE GATE'S
OWN FLAG:
    selfid-job.sh :  cargo clippy ... --keep-going --message-format=json
    loc-job.sh    :  cargo clippy ... --keep-going --message-format=json  -- -D warnings
                                                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^ MISSING
and its counter keeps only error-level diagnostics:
    if m.get("level") != "error": continue
WITHOUT `-D warnings`, CLIPPY LINTS ARE WARNINGS, NOT ERRORS. Every one of them was filtered out by
my own counter. `TOTAL DIAGS: 0` measured the number of COMPILE ERRORS — of which there are none,
correctly — and said nothing whatever about lints. `CLIPPY_EXIT=0` is consistent with that: without
`-D warnings`, lints do not fail the build.
SO THE GATE-4 SCOPE WAS NEVER MEASURED CLEAN. It was not measured at all.

=== HazyTurtle'S CATCH, AND THE RULE IT APPLIES ===
"Two of the three closures inherit a zero whose instrument wasn't validated."
That is my own standing rule — never trust a zero from an instrument you have not seen fire — turned
on my own closure evidence, and it is correct. I wrote selfid-job.sh fresh that tick to add subject
hashing, ran it ONCE, and it reported zero. It has never produced a nonzero result. I validated the
SUBJECT (worker blobs matched) with great care and never validated the INSTRUMENT.
Their cost framing is right too: "reopening two beads costs a minute; a false gate-4 green
propagating into receipts is the expensive version."

  - "GATE-4 SCOPE IS CLEAN: 700 UNITS, 0 CACHED, 0 DIAGNOSTICS" — VOID.
  - The three closures below, each of which cited it as its verification.
  - My reconciliation note claiming the 116-site listing was superseded by a provable run. The
    116-site listing came from loc-job.sh, WHICH CARRIES THE FLAG. It is the more trustworthy of the
    two and I discarded it in favour of the broken one.
WHAT SURVIVES: the `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` result of 700 units /
0 errors. That command has no lint component, the count is of compile errors, and the filter is
correct for it. The COMPILE surface is clean; the LINT surface is unmeasured.

=== REOPENED, per AGENTS.md: "a false close is reopened with an incident comment" ===
    bd-eyyqk   bd-l3iku   bd-pf5n7
Silent reopening is forbidden, so this comment goes on all three. Their underlying WORK is not in
question — the four named clippy sites are fixed, the .pem inlining is real and syntax-verified, and
the seven recursion_limit attributes are present. What is void is my EVIDENCE that the gate is
clean, and pf5n7 in particular required exactly that evidence and nothing less.

=== WHAT I AM DOING ===
Re-running with `-- -D warnings` and a validated counter. I will not re-close any of the three until

title: SIX compile errors hidden 5 days in native-tls-roots gated test modules: base64 used but never declared, plus two E0597 borrow errors - found by the all-features CHECK that bd-hy8mq proposes
description:
Six compile errors have been sitting in native-tls-roots gated test modules
since 2026-10-14, invisible to every gate anyone runs. Two of them are a crate
using a dependency it does not declare, so those modules have NEVER compiled
since they were added. All four sites were untracked: a tracker search for each
path returned zero.

HOW THEY WERE FOUND, which is the reusable part. bd-hy8mq measured statically
that the mandated gate (cargo check --workspace --all-targets) never compiles
37 of 47 declared targets because required-features targets are skipped
SILENTLY. The obvious widening to --all-features fails at LINK on this fleet
(bd-8d61j). But cargo CHECK never links, so I ran the widened form as a check:

  command  cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features
           --profile test
  host     hz4, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  subject  HEAD 0094966544fcda79b1c234191fe2b65e22933187, 0 dirty files,
           manifest c1f985ed40168737 over 667 files, manifest agrees True
  result   CHECK_RC=101 BUILD_RC=101 ERRORS=7 WARNINGS=1, RECEIPT_END reached
  verdict  INVALID

RECEIPT_END matters: the run completed rather than aborting, so these are real
compiler errors and not the link exhaustion or disk pressure that killed the
--all-features TEST attempts.

THE SIX ERRORS, all in fastmcp-client (lib test); the seventh line is the
could-not-compile summary:

  E0433 cannot find module or crate base64
  E0432 unresolved import base64
    http_auth/dpop/native/core/stream/interaction/tests/tls.rs:15
    http_auth/dpop/native/core/stream/subscription/tests/tls.rs:12
    Both files contain:
      use base64::{Engine as _, engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD};

  E0597 redirect does not live long enough
    http_auth/managed/tasks/lifecycle_tests/driver_events.rs:76:43
    http_auth/managed/tasks/lifecycle_tests.rs:518:67

base64 IS NOT DECLARED BY fastmcp-client AT ALL. grep base64 over
crates/fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml returns nothing, in [dependencies] or
[dev-dependencies]. So this is not a feature-interaction subtlety: those two
modules cannot compile under ANY feature set, and have not since they landed.
Same shape as bd-uuw3n, where the code could never have compiled either.

WHY NO GATE SEES THEM. Both module trees are gated on native-tls-roots, which
is not a default feature:

  interaction/tests.rs:9    #[cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")] mod tls;
  managed/tasks.rs:2070     #[cfg(all(test, feature = "native-tls-roots"))]
                            mod lifecycle_tests;

So the mandated default-feature check compiles neither, and I confirmed that
directly: the same command WITHOUT --all-features is GREEN at the same HEAD
(CHECK_RC=0, ERRORS=0, RECEIPT_END). One flag is the entire difference between
a clean gate and six errors.

DATED, so staleness is not guessed. interaction/tests/tls.rs was added by
45e1e06b on 2026-10-14 02:44:35 and lifecycle_tests.rs by dbf1a4a7 on
2026-10-14 07:02:19. Five days.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why each is a decision rather than an omission.
  - I did NOT add base64 to fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml. That is the obvious
    one-line repair, but FND-01 binds the dependency graph in a digest-frozen
    policy, and bd-hy8mq own list names fnd_01_dependency_evidence among the
    targets the gate cannot see. Adding a dependency to satisfy a test module
    is exactly the kind of graph change that re-breaks a frozen evidence gate,
    so it wants the same ruling as the rest of the frozen-surface drift
    (bd-3zzrz, bd-fnd01-workflow-pin-generator-ocsls). It is also possible the
    right repair is to stop using base64 in those fixtures rather than to add
    the dep, and that is the module owner call.
  - I did NOT fix the two E0597 borrow errors. They are in the managed Tasks
    lane, which is committing several times a day, and a lifetime repair there
    is a design choice about where the redirect value should live rather than a
    mechanical edit.

PROOF CLASS: static compile observation at one revision, one host. NO-CLAIM:
this is a CHECK, so nothing here says the targets would LINK or that their
tests would pass; and --all-targets still omits nothing only because
--all-features satisfies every required-features row, which I did not
separately enumerate against bd-hy8mq 37-target list.

comments.text: TWO OF THE FOUR SITES ARE FIXED at 90f4ccb2, without touching the dependency graph. Your commit named the alternative -- 'the right repair may also be to stop using base64 in those fixtures' -- and that is what this does, so the FND-01 frozen-surface ruling you were waiting on is not needed for the base64 half. interaction/tests/tls.rs and subscription/tests/tls.rs each used base64 in exactly ONE place: a JWT payload decode, 'serde_json::from_slice(&URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(parts[1]).unwrap())'. Both now call a local base64url_payload() and the import is gone. No manifest change. AND IT IS THE CRATE'S OWN ESTABLISHED PATTERN rather than something I invented, which is what makes it safe to do in another lane's files. Two committed fixtures already do this and each documents the same rationale: core/tasks/tests/tls.rs:104 says 'No additional production dependency is needed by tests', and http_auth/driver/redirect.rs:579 says 'Only the fixture needs a base64url encoder; no new library dependency'. The decoder I added mirrors the first of those -- same JWT payload decode, same alphabet, same trailing-bits assertion -- and every existing claims assertion at both call sites is unchanged. UBS, reported rather than glossed: exit 1 with 4 criticals over the two files. Two are the panic!('invalid base64url proof') I added; two are pre-existing Instant::now findings on lines I did not touch. The sibling I copied trips the IDENTICAL critical, same rule rust.ownership.panic-macro and same string at tasks/tests/tls.rs:114, and is itself exit 1 with 2 criticals -- so this adds nothing new to the crate's UBS profile, and panicking on malformed input is correct for a test decoder. VERIFICATION VOID, SO UNVERIFIED: 'cargo check --locked -p fastmcp-client --all-targets --features native-tls-roots --profile test' returned 'Remote execution failed on hz4; refusing local fallback: SSH command timed out after 20s'. An SSH timeout means the command never executed, so that is a void and not a red. hz4 is the worker with /tmp full, and all 12 durable RCH leases are currently orphaned (owner_presence=absent, wrapper_alive=False) -- a fleet-wide finalize wedge that is an operator action, not a lane's. The remaining two sites, the E0597 borrows at lifecycle_tests.rs:518 and lifecycle_tests/driver_events.rs:76, are UNTOUCHED and still yours. One observation that may save you time: they are byte-identical in shape -- a &str borrowed out of a local String and held across an await -- so one fix serves both. I did not attempt it because the real objection needs a compiler to iterate against. Also note this bead's title inherited '37 of 47' from bd-hy8mq; that denominator was mine and is wrong (cargo metadata says 172 declared targets, 37 gated, so 22% not 79%). Corrected on bd-hy8mq.
