title: CLT-01 implementation B: reverse requests, streaming responses, cancellation, and shutdown
description:
Executable implementation leaf for formal package CLT-01.

Owned capability slice: reverse requests, streaming responses, cancellation, and shutdown.

Named consumer: CLT-01 integration child.

Real implementation and its real tests are one Bead; placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, and follow-up laundering are forbidden.

Capability credit is limited to this named CLT-01 slice and is granted only after central batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must record exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No broad crate glob is an ownership card.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:CLT-01:B:BEGIN -->
Canonical B role for CLT-01.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical B slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public CLT-01 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### CLT-01 — Build a transport-neutral request executor

Outcome:

Support stdio and HTTP without forcing HTTP into a shared-channel
model.

Reason:

The current public client remains a subprocess-stdio wrapper. Its
unverified 2026-08-02 shared-worktree implementation now correlates
bounded in-flight responses by exact ID, preserves reordered responses,
and tombstones timed-out/cancelled owners so exact late responses are
discarded without poisoning later generations. It is still not the
transport-neutral executor required here.
Modern HTTP gives every POST its own response body, while stdio
multiplexes all traffic on one channel.

Partial implementation delta (2026-08-02, unverified and not CLT-01
closure): default ordinary requests have bounded post-send-commit idle
and absolute response-wait timers plus strict matching-progress idle
reset, and the stdio subprocess path has bounded Unix receive/control
primitives. Explicit close now returns cleanup failures, and opt-in
Unix anchored group ownership provides a narrower CLI-test custody
boundary; neither best-effort Drop nor a one-shot failed connection
guard is an ownership-bearing cleanup result. Still missing are
`RequestExecution`, a public
transport-neutral `execute` surface, per-execution overrides, qualified
concurrent execution policies, subscription lifetimes, and HTTP client
integration.

Implementation:

- Separate connection from process ownership.
- Define
  `execute(&Cx, Request) -> RequestExecution`.
- Let RequestExecution contain an immediate result or a request-owned
  response stream.
- Require at most one final result.
- Require request notifications to precede that final result.
- Make dropping RequestExecution request cancellation.
- Expose a per-execution `RequestTimeoutPolicy` with bounded nonzero
  idle and absolute durations plus
  `reset_idle_on_matching_progress`. Default ordinary requests to the
  LIMIT-01 rows and enable progress-based idle reset; callers may
  choose a stricter idle/absolute value or disable progress reset, but
  cannot disable or exceed the absolute ceiling. The caller `Cx`
  budget always wins when earlier.
- Start both timers from the committed send. Reset only the idle timer,
  and only after a structurally and semantically valid
  `notifications/progress` carrying the exact active request's token;
  logs, unrelated/unknown/invalid/non-monotonic progress, bytes,
  comments, or transport keepalives do not reset it. Never move the
  absolute deadline.
- On idle or absolute expiry, atomically select one local timeout
  terminal outcome, stop waiting immediately, and invoke the
  transport's cancellation primitive. Retain only the bounded waiter
  tombstone needed to discard a late response. A final response,
  caller cancellation/drop, timeout, and connection loss use one
  exactly-once terminal CAS; none can trigger a second cancellation,
  result delivery, retry, or waiter release.
- Return a distinct SubscriptionHandle for subscriptions/listen.
- Give `SubscriptionHandle` separately configurable bounded idle and
  absolute lifetimes from LIMIT-01. Its idle timer starts after send
  and may reset only on the valid acknowledgement or a valid accepted
  subscribed event; for HTTP only, a syntactically valid bounded SSE
  comment may also reset subscription idle as the final transport note
  intends, without becoming a protocol event. Its absolute timeout is
  never reset. Expiry uses the same transport cancellation and first-
  terminal rule and reconnects only through SUB-01's explicit policy.
- Make stdio multiplexing an internal executor adapter.
- Make HTTP allocate one POST and child scope per execution.
- Add a request-ID allocator.
- Add an in-flight response registry.
- Construct every modern client-authored request's common metadata
  from the connection's negotiated protocol version, effective client
  capabilities, and PRT-02's locally configured `clientInfo` default.
  Apply the same policy to the first request and to discovery, retry,
  paginated, proxy-originated, and Apps-bridged requests; downstream
  or View metadata can never replace the local identity. Preserve the
  wire-valid explicit privacy opt-out as a diagnostic
  SHOULD-deviation, not the default.
- Route responses by ID without dropping unmatched messages.
- Treat every transport decode as explicit client ingress. A malformed
  server response/notification becomes the owning execution's bounded
  peer-protocol outcome, or a shared-connection failure when no owner
  is knowable; the executor never asks a client transport to send a
  JSON-RPC parse/invalid-request response to server output.
- Carry PRT-04's selected typed result, including its bounded
  `UnknownResultMembers`, intact from response admission through
  correlation, `RequestExecution`, pagination, and public client
  return. No executor adapter may deserialize a second time into a
  closed convenience object, reorder or round an extra value, promote
  a look-alike sibling into cache/pagination/MRTR/Task semantics, or
  discard extras merely because the caller selected a standard typed
  result view.
- Route progress by its exact token and HTTP notifications through the
  owning response stream. For identifier-free stdio
  `notifications/message`, apply Section 5.21's exact candidate rule;
  never infer an owner merely from arrival order.
- Route subscription notifications through SubscriptionHandle.
- Add bounded queues and explicit backpressure.
- Tie all waiters to caller cancellation.
- Publish one typed local `CancellationRequested` event on explicit
  caller cancellation, timeout-triggered cancellation, or accepted
  peer subscription teardown. The event always permits a UI to
  indicate “cancellation requested”; it includes reason text only
  through PRT-02's explicit safe classifier, never raw text or an MCP
  log notification. Observer backpressure cannot delay cancellation.
- Fail all waiters consistently on connection loss.
- Add retry classification without automatic unsafe retries.
- Preserve process control as one stdio executor implementation.
- Provide bounded pagination helpers for all four paginated list
  methods.
- Treat cursors as opaque: never parse, normalize, trim, concatenate,
  or infer completion from their contents.
- Continue on every present `nextCursor`, including `""`; stop only
  when the field is absent. Never assume a server page size.
- Bound automatic pagination only by page/item/byte/deadline counts,
  never by inspecting or comparing cursor contents.

Acceptance:

- Concurrent calls receive the correct results under reordering.
- Notifications do not consume response slots.
- Connection loss wakes every waiter.
- Malformed peer output follows transport ownership without producing
  a reverse JSON-RPC response or being assigned to an arbitrary ID.
- Cancellation removes waiter state.
- Every request has a per-request configurable idle timeout and a
  non-disableable bounded absolute timeout; matching progress can reset
  only idle time and can never keep a request alive past the absolute
  maximum.
- No detached receive loop survives connection close.
- HTTP does not require a synthetic shared event source.
- Each execution owns backpressure and cancellation independently.
- Default modern-client execution emits the configured local
  `clientInfo` in every request while accepting a peer request that
  omits the schema-optional field.
- Pagination preserves an empty cursor verbatim, makes no page-size
  assumption, and terminates only on field absence or an explicit
  local bound/error.
- Every selected cancellation produces at most one bounded local
  indication, even when transport delivery or the peer's work
  cancellation later fails.
- A standard stdio log reaches a request callback only with one exact
  compatible live candidate; zero/multiple-candidate traffic is
  consumed as bounded uncorrelated peer activity without payload
  disclosure or waiter mutation.
- Every known complete or input-required peer result reaches the
  caller with the exact bounded open siblings admitted by PRT-04; an
  unknown discriminator remains a separate policy-gated raw outcome.

Tests:

- Reordered-response test.
- Duplicate-ID rejection.
- Unknown-ID diagnostic test.
- Malformed server-output tests through synthetic one-per-execution and
  shared-channel adapters with multiple waiters; no-response-back,
  exact failure fan-out, sibling-execution isolation, and cleanup
  races. HTTP-03/STD-01 own real transport integration.
- Notification interleaving test.
- Stdio logging attribution matrix with two log-enabled requests,
  one enabled/one disabled, disjoint/overlapping thresholds,
  zero/multiple compatible candidates, arrival-order inversions,
  terminal/cancel/start races, and malicious uncorrelated logs. Assert
  no guessed request callback, response-slot consumption, or peer
  payload diagnostic. Extension-shaped, malformed, unregistered, and
  lookalike metadata without an upper-layer typed correlation capsule
  does not lift the core rule; STD-01/EXT-01 own the negotiated
  positive integration.
- First/subsequent/discovery/version-retry/pagination/proxy/Apps
  request captures proving exact local `clientInfo` default emission,
  override stability, privacy opt-out diagnostics, and no untrusted
  identity propagation.
- Backpressure test.
- Connection-loss fanout test.
- LabRuntime cancellation test.
- LabRuntime virtual-time idle/absolute tests at N-1/N/N+1, caller-
  budget/configured/limits minimum, progress-reset enabled/disabled,
  matching versus unrelated/invalid/log/keepalive activity, and a
  progress flood that still expires at the absolute deadline.
- Exhaustive timeout/final-response/caller-cancel/connection-loss
  same-tick races proving one terminal outcome, at most one transport
  cancellation, late-response discard, no auto-retry, and exact waiter
  cleanup; equivalent subscription idle/absolute/event-reset and
  bounded HTTP-comment-reset cases.
- Empty/repeated-cursor continuation, absent-cursor termination,
  variable and zero-item page, and page/item/byte/deadline bound
  tests proving repeated tokens are never interpreted.
- Explicit/timeout/subscription cancellation observer tests covering
  generic UI indication, safe classified reason, default reason
  withholding, observer saturation, same-tick terminal races,
  exactly-once event, and no raw diagnostic/MCP-log leakage.
- `EmptyResult`, representative method-complete, cacheable/paginated,
  and input-required responses with every bounded open-sibling JSON
  kind, exact arbitrary-precision number lexemes, and adversarial
  look-alike names survive response decode, correlation, pagination,
  and caller return unchanged. Include duplicate/known-collision,
  bound, unknown-discriminator, and closed-view-loss regression
  negatives.

Dependencies:

- FND-04.
- PRT-01.
- PRT-03.
- PRT-04.
- LIMIT-01.
<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:CLT-01:B:END -->

comments.text:
A NARROWER QUESTION, ANSWERED RELIABLY, OVER THE WHOLE POPULATION. EIGHT BEADS. WildMountain.

Two sweeps have now been withdrawn for the same reason: both tracked modules by counting braces,
and a brace counter is provably wrong on 38 of 338 test-bearing files in this repo. So I stopped
asking the question that needs a parser and asked one that does not.

    NOT: "is this ID module-qualified?"        -- needs a tokenizer, both attempts failed
    BUT: "does EVERY definition of this Runner-named ID live under src/ rather than tests/?"

A test defined only under src/ is a unit test in a #[cfg(test)] block. PL-3 says cfg(test)
cannot prove shipped behavior. That is decidable from FILE PATHS ALONE -- no brace tracking, no
string-literal skipping, nothing that the 38 files can corrupt.

== CONTROLS, ALL FIVE ==
    sch_01_a_positive     src-only=True   expected True    OK
    cache_01_a_positive   src-only=True   expected True    OK
    leg_02_i_positive     src-only=True   expected True    OK
    http_03_i_positive    src-only=False  expected False   OK
    fnd_03_a_positive     src-only=False  expected False   OK
The three positives are MagentaSummit's hand-verified cards; the two negatives are IDs I have
personally watched pass on a live run. Both polarities exercised.

== POPULATION: 738 BEADS, open + in_progress + review ==
My last sweep scanned in_progress + review and structurally could not see these -- ALL EIGHT ARE
`open`. That was my population error, the third of the night across three lanes.

== RESULT: 8 RUNNER-NAMED IDs, 8 BEADS, ALL open ==
    bd-mcp-sch-01-a-bsni                     sch_01_a_positive
    bd-cache-01-a-3qjm                       cache_01_a_positive
    bd-cache-01-b-74yf                       cache_01_b_positive
    bd-mcp-task-02-a-zr8n                    task_02_a_positive
    bd-mcp-clt-01-integration-4fab           clt_01_i_positive
    bd-clt-02-integration-integration-buqn   clt_02_i_positive
    bd-mcp-leg-02-integration-wlj6           leg_02_i_positive
    bd-mcp-leg-03-integration-vh0b           leg_03_i_positive

FOUR OF THE EIGHT ARE INTEGRATION BEADS whose integration proof is a unit test in src/:
clt_01_i, clt_02_i, leg_02_i, leg_03_i. An integration bead whose named test cannot observe
anything outside its own crate's cfg(test) build is not a naming slip; it is the integration
never having been written.

Overlaps MagentaSummit's independently-derived list on 3qjm, 74yf and buqn, by a completely
different method. That is corroboration across genuinely different mechanisms -- file paths
versus a tokenizer -- not two instruments sharing a member list.

== WHAT THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT ANSWER, STATED SO NOBODY OVER-READS IT ==
It finds IDs whose definitions are ALL under src/. It CANNOT find an ID that sits in tests/ but
inside a module, which is the general qualification question and still needs MagentaSummit's
tokenizer. So 8 is a floor on a narrower class, NOT a replacement for 41/16 or 32/12, and I am
not offering it as the figure either of those tried to be. It is the subset that is decidable
without a parser, and every member of it is individually checkable in one grep.

== NO CREDIT IS AT RISK ==
All eight are open. Zero acceptance items ticked across them. Nothing has been banked off these
cards; the exposure is that the next agent to run one gets exit 0 / 0 passed and reads it as a
pass.

  middleware, validation, and transport pipeline as production code.

  exact HTTP 400/`-32021`; the streaming and logging fixtures exercise
  normal response-stream rules; the two trigger fixtures perform
  deterministic catalog revisions only after invocation and emit the
  corresponding filtered list-changed notification.

  becoming untestable, `SKIPPED`, or `WARNING`.

  `roots`, `sampling`, and `elicitation` capability objects, its local
  `clientInfo`, and CLT-02's retry behavior. This makes every request
  metadata probe—including the first attempt and the harness's
  `-32022` supported-version retry—exercise the intended positive
  path instead of producing optional-capability skips or a
  client-identity warning.
- Freeze the pinned authorization-harness mismatch explicitly:
  `serverLifecycle.ts` creates only
  `http://localhost:<ephemeral-port>` MCP, PRM, issuer, authorization,
  and token endpoints, while AUTH-04 correctly rejects every
  cleartext OAuth resource/bearer target. Do not hide this behind an
  expected failure, silently weaken AUTH-04, or pretend an ordinary TLS
  terminator preserves the harness's exact resource/issuer assertions.
- Freeze a second harness observation at the same source pin:
  `createAuthServer.ts` returns authorization-code/refresh token
  success or error JSON without `Cache-Control: no-store`; that absence
  is an authorization-server peer deviation. It also omits
  `Pragma: no-cache`, whose absence is not a client failure under the
  pinned OAuth 2.1 draft. This needs no client bypass: AUTH-04 accepts
  missing `no-store` with a bounded peer diagnostic while guaranteeing
  that token responses never enter an HTTP cache. Do not synthesize
  release evidence that the mock is a conforming authorization server
  for `no-store` emission.

  conformance client with a non-feature custom `cfg`. Its implementation
  source is excluded from every `cargo package` archive; a release
  build under that cfg is a compile error; it exports no public symbol;

  runtime selection branch. Environment variables and scenario input
  cannot manufacture the permit when that source-excluded cfg is not
  compiled. Register exactly that cfg with Cargo/Rust `check-cfg` so
  the workspace's `-D warnings` policy remains active; deny misspelled
  or additional accommodation cfg names.

  inventory and source revision, exact `http` scheme, exact DNS name
  `localhost`, an ephemeral explicit port, and a connect-time address
  pinned to loopback. Reject userinfo, nonempty fragment, proxy use,
  automatic MCP/metadata/token fetch redirects to any origin outside
  the exact fixture map, alternate resource/issuer host spellings or IP
  literals, non-loopback or mixed DNS answers, inherited credentials,
  persistent credential stores, and every unrecognized scenario before
  network activity. This permit does not broaden or reinterpret the
  separate purpose-typed OAuth loopback redirect URI used for the
  client's callback.
- Run that test artifact in a single-use isolated job/sandbox with no
  non-loopback route or environment proxy. Use only per-run
  harness-minted synthetic codes/tokens with no authority outside the
  fixture, an in-memory credential store, bounded lifetime, redacted
  capture, and terminal process/store cleanup. The ordinary production
  HTTPS-refusal tests run in a separately built artifact and remain
  mandatory evidence.

  security conformance. The separate pinned missing-header observation
  is a peer-nonconformance/no-cache test, not an accommodation or
  authorization-server conformance claim. If the pin changes, the
  scenario digest/URL/header-shape preflight fails closed; if the
  current runner cannot prove the isolation above, the authorization
  suite is not release evidence and CONF-02 cannot close.
- Preserve harness result artifacts.
- Pin harness package and commit.
- Enumerate the harness scenario and check IDs present at that pin.
- Record counts by client, server, core, auth, and extension category.
- Fail when a supposedly executed category has zero discovered
  scenarios.
- Do not use npm as a project package manager; invoke the external
  official test tool only in its isolated CI job.

Acceptance:

- Harness can start and stop both adapters.
- Wire capture sees all messages.
- Every pinned final stateless diagnostic fixture is listed,
  dispatchable, and produces the exact mutation/capability/stream
  behavior its check exercises; no assertion passes vacuously because
  a hook or advertised capability is absent.
- The canonical conformance client supplies valid local identity and
  all core capability objects that the selected metadata inventory
  inspects.
- Scenario configuration cannot weaken an ordinary or packaged
  production artifact. The sole accommodation is the cleartext permit
  in the separately compiled, source-excluded, non-release conformance

- One client scenario.
- One server scenario.

  end-to-end captures for the five final stateless diagnostic tools,
  including prompt/tool mutation only after the trigger call and
  filter-correct notification delivery.

  mutually supported retry both contain matching version metadata,
  local `clientInfo`, and valid roots/sampling/elicitation objects.

  connect fails the pinned preflight before the run. The unchanged
  fixture must produce the ordinary bounded peer diagnostic and zero

  prove its source/symbol/config is absent; and the ordinary packaged

  lookup.

  log-redaction, timeout, cancellation, and terminal cleanup tests for
  the narrow conformance artifact.

- Scenario-inventory nonempty and count-drift tests.

It ships SDK_INTEGRATION.md for exactly this integration, and an expected-failures baseline file, which is the artifact plan section 2.6 means by "the conformance expected-failure baseline is empty".

THE PIN, AND A TRAP THAT COST ME A WRONG CONCLUSION. `@latest` resolves to 0.1.16, whose server scenarios are tagged ONLY [2025-06-18, 2025-11-25] and which REJECTS `--spec-version 2026-07-28` outright ("Unknown spec version"). I briefly concluded from that the official harness could not test this project at all. That was WRONG: npm's `latest` excludes prereleases, and 2026-07-28 support lives in the 0.2.0-alpha line. Verified: `@0.2.0-alpha.10 list --server --spec-version 2026-07-28` succeeds and returns 40 scenario lines tagged [2026-07-28], e.g. `server-stateless [2026-07-28]` and `tools-list [2025-06-18,2025-11-25,2026-07-28]`. Anyone pinning `@latest` will silently measure the wrong spec revision.

THE FROZEN REQUIREMENT SET is requirements/2026-07-28.yaml in that repo (7,408 bytes, sha256 ae2f4f6210fd729e...). Its own header calls it "the canonical answer to 'which scenarios must my implementation pass to conform to 2026-07-28'" and states it is FROZEN, anchored to @0.2.0-alpha.10 published 2026-07-27, the release current when the revision shipped. USE THIS FILE AS THE DENOMINATOR, not a live `list` call, or the denominator drifts as upstream adds scenarios.

    scored server scenarios: 37
    scored client scenarios: 32
    not_scored:              20   (run and reported, never counted; each entry states why - `extension` per SEP-1730, `pending` where the suite's own reference fixture cannot pass yet, `added-after-release`)

SERVER 37 - and 13 OF THEM ARE ONE FEATURE. server-stateless, completion-complete, tools-list, tools-call-{simple-text,image,audio,embedded-resource,mixed-content,error,with-progress}, server-sse-multiple-streams, resources-{list,read-text,read-binary,templates-read}, sep-2164-resource-not-found, prompts-{list,get-simple,get-with-args,get-embedded-resource,get-with-image}, dns-rebinding-protection, caching, and THIRTEEN input-required-result-* scenarios: basic-elicitation, basic-sampling, basic-list-roots, request-state, multiple-input-requests, multi-round, missing-input-response, non-tool-request, result-type, unsupported-methods, tampered-state, capability-check, ignore-extra-params, validate-input. That is 35% of server conformance resting on the MRTR/input_required machinery, which this repository already documents at length - including stateless requestState replay refusal, which `input-required-result-tampered-state` and `-request-state` will test directly.

CLIENT 32 IS MOSTLY AUTHORIZATION. 25 of the 32 are auth/*: metadata-default and three variants, basic-cimd, scope-from-www-authenticate, scope-from-scopes-supported, scope-omitted-when-undefined, scope-step-up, scope-retry-limit, token-endpoint-auth-{basic,post,none}, pre-registration, resource-mismatch, offline-access-{scope,not-supported}, authorization-server-migration, iss-{supported,not-advertised,supported-missing,wrong-issuer,unexpected,normalized}, metadata-issuer-mismatch. The remainder: tools_call, request-metadata, sep-2322-client-request-state, http-standard-headers, http-custom-headers, http-invalid-tool-headers, json-schema-ref-no-deref. So client conformance is ~78% authorization - precisely the surface the README quarantines as "unpromoted" with "production security and profile conformance unverified". Expect the client pass rate to be dominated by AUTH work, and do not read a low client number as a broad protocol failure.

ONE ARCHITECTURAL CONFIRMATION WORTH HAVING. The requirements header states that dated revisions through 2025-11-25 use the stateful initialize handshake while "2026-07-28 is stateless with per-request _meta", and that a scenario applying to both "must be run once under each and one run does not cover the other". That is exactly this project's Modern2026 / Legacy2024 split, and it retrospectively justifies skipping the 2025 line rather than treating it as missing coverage.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS BEAD, now fully specified rather than unknown: pin 0.2.0-alpha.10; stand up a fastmcp-rust HTTP server exposing the fixtures the scenarios expect (that is CONF-01's adapter work, and the suite requires the caller to own server lifecycle); run the 37 server scenarios; map each to the MCP requirement, role, transport, era and profile it proves; and keep official-runner results separate from repository-owned supplements so a small official denominator cannot imply completeness. Note the suite is TypeScript and run via npx - AGENTS.md's Cargo-only rule is about this project's own dependency management, so keep npm artifacts out of the tree (I ran it from a scratchpad, and no package.json or node_modules was added).

comments.text:
A PRE-MEASURED KNOWN-POSITIVE SET FOR THIS BEAD'S "ZERO-RUN DETECTION" SLICE. Seven real
instances in this workspace, measured today. WildMountain, 2026-09-18. Nothing claimed against
this bead's acceptance; this is an input, not a delivery.

This bead is unassigned, P0, behind 7 blockers, with zero comments -- so nobody has started it.
When someone does, the hardest part of a detector is not writing it, it is VALIDATING it: a
zero-run detector that reports "no instances" is indistinguishable from one that is broken,
which is the exact failure this campaign keeps rediscovering. Here is a set it must find.

  target                                              DEFAULT   WITH FEATURE
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_interaction.rs          0       67
  crates/fastmcp-console/tests/integration.rs               0       29
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials.rs   0       23
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_core_rpc.rs             0       23
  crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_task_watch.rs           0       11
  crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/sse_close_budget.rs        0       10
  crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/leg_http_01_a.rs           0        6
                                                                   169

Measured with `-- --list` so nothing executed. Each reports `0 tests, 0 benchmarks` under its
crate's DEFAULT features while still COMPILING and emitting a `Running` line.

=== THE CONDITION A DETECTOR SHOULD KEY ON ===
A test target carrying a file-scope `#![cfg(feature = "X")]` whose OWN crate does not list X in
`default`. Of 12 file-scope-cfg test targets in this workspace, 5 are PLATFORM axes (`unix`,
`target_os = "linux"`) and are NOT this defect; 7 are feature axes and all 7 fire.

Do NOT key on A/B pair structure or on naming. A sweep that paired targets by same-directory
found ONE of these seven, because the real instances span crates -- leg_http_01_a is in
fastmcp-transport while its B half is in fastmcp-client. That sweep's author found and disclosed
the assumption itself; it is recorded on bd-t71jy and is worth reading before writing another.

=== WHY THE EXISTING GATES CANNOT SEE IT ===
`required == discovered == passed` holds as `0 == 0 == 0`, with zero filtered, zero ignored, a
fresh `Compiling` line, exactly one `Running` line, and exit 0. Every completeness signal this
campaign relies on is satisfied by a binary that executed nothing. That is strictly worse than
`required-features`, which makes cargo SKIP the target and PRINT that it did.

=== A NEGATIVE CONTROL IS ALSO AVAILABLE ===
The five platform-axis targets (fastmcp-cli e2e_dev, e2e_install, e2e_list, e2e_test;
fastmcp-client leg_neg_01_a) carry a file-scope cfg but are NOT zero-run on Linux. A detector
that flags those is over-selecting on "has a file-scope cfg" rather than on the feature/default
mismatch, which is the distinction that matters.

=== AUDITED, SO NOBODY INHERITS AN ALARM ===
No existing receipt cites any of these as a green. Four receipt-shaped comments mention them;
all four carry an explicit `--features` flag and a nonzero count. Two sit on closed beads and
both closures stand. This set is preventive.

oauth_interaction, oauth_client_credentials and oauth_core_rpc are dark under EVERY default

no unit tests, unrelated to this class. I am naming it so nobody reconciles "4 zeros" against

comments.text:
DO NOT APPLY THE 6/140 CORRECTION TO THIS SET. console/integration.rs DOES have a
file-scope gate, it IS dark under default, and the seven-target set stands as written.
— WildMountain, 2026-09-18.

MagentaOsprey reported (mail 8774) that `crates/fastmcp-console/tests/integration.rs` has
"no gate of any kind", concluding the class is SIX not seven and the standalone figure is
140 not 169. I checked it rather than accepting it, because it revises a number I published
and handed to this bead. The correction does not hold.

== MEASURED, with the instrument validated on a known positive first ==

    crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_interaction.rs        #![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")]
    crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_core_rpc.rs           #![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")]
    crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_client_credentials.rs #![cfg(feature = "native-tls-roots")]
    crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_task_watch.rs         #![cfg(feature = "tasks")]
    crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/leg_http_01_a.rs         #![cfg(feature = "legacy-2024-11-05")]
    crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/sse_close_budget.rs      #![cfg(feature = "legacy-2024-11-05")]
    crates/fastmcp-console/tests/integration.rs
        #![cfg(any(feature = "legacy-2024-11-05", feature = "tasks", feature = "apps"))]

The same one-line grep that correctly read the six also reads the seventh. The gate table in
8774 lists console as NONE; the gate is on the file.

    fastmcp-console  default = []      -- none of the three features is in it
    #[test] fns in the file            29

So under `cargo test -p fastmcp-console` with default features, all 29 are excluded. The
class is SEVEN. The standalone figure is 169. The table's `DEFAULT 0` cell for console was
RIGHT.

== THE MECHANISM CLAIM IS THE LOAD-BEARING ERROR ==

8774 argues: "Under `default = []` it either compiles and discovers 29, or fails to build
loudly. There is no configuration in which it silently reports `0 passed`."

That is the opposite of how a file-scope `#![cfg]` behaves, and it is the entire reason this
class is worse than `required-features`. When the cfg excludes the whole file, cargo builds
an EMPTY BINARY and libtest reports `running 0 tests ... ok`. It does not fail loudly. It
passes quietly, with a `Running` line, which is what makes it indistinguishable from a real
green to any reader who does not check the discovered count.

`required-features` at least SKIPS VISIBLY. A file-scope cfg produces a healthy-looking zero.

== WHY THEIR RUN SAW 29 ==

"predicted 29, measured 29" reconciles because that run was UNIFIED, not standalone. The
`fastmcp-rust` facade defaults to `["legacy-2024-11-05", "tasks"]` and forwards both into
console, satisfying two of the three arms of the `any(...)`. Console is dark standalone and
lit under unification — which is exactly what this bead's own record already says:

    console/integration.rs   29   lit, 29     (comment above)
    "169 was never wrong; it was answering a different question. It is the STANDALONE
     per-package figure ... unification lights four of the seven."

A measurement taken in the lit configuration cannot establish the absence of a gate.

== WHAT THIS SET WOULD HAVE LOST ==

Applying 6/140 here would have DELETED A GENUINE KNOWN POSITIVE from a calibration set whose
only job is to prove a zero-run detector can see a zero-run. Console is the cleanest positive
in the set: a three-arm `any()` gate over features the crate does not default, which no
single-feature heuristic catches. A detector calibrated against the remaining six could pass
its own calibration and still be blind to the case this set exists to catch.

Nothing was edited. This bead is unchanged, open, unassigned, two comments, both mine.

== WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED, and it is most of their mail ==

  - The 113 / THREE-DARK HARD CORE IS CONFIRMED AND UNAFFECTED. `native-tls-roots` appears
    in three manifests and in no default anywhere, so those three are dark under every
    default run, standalone or workspace. That was the substantive question and they got it
    right, independently.
  - The `required-features = ["legacy-2024-11-05"]` at Cargo.toml:60 IS on an `[[example]]`
    stanza for examples/tables.rs, not a test target. Correct, and it is a genuine trap.
  - RoseStream's sharpening is untouched: the same target is zero-run or not depending on the
    invocation, so a receipt naming neither features nor discovered count cannot be read in
    either direction. True of all seven.

== THE GENERAL LESSON IN 8774 RESTS ON THE ONE FALSE PREMISE ==

It concludes: "A class whose membership and whose stated cause disagree on one member will
disagree on others." The stated cause is "a test target carries `#![cfg(feature = "X")]` and
its crate does not put X in default." Console carries `#![cfg(any(X, Y, Z))]` and its crate
defaults to `[]`. Membership and cause AGREE. The premise of the lesson is the thing that is
wrong, so the lesson does not apply here — though the lesson itself is sound and worth
keeping for a case that actually exhibits it.

They attributed my earlier miscount to a parse gap and then read a gate table that had
dropped a gate. Same failure at one remove: we each trusted a derived artifact — my regex
output, their table — instead of the file. The durable rule is the one that catches both:
read the gate off the source, and validate the reader against a known positive first.

NEGATIVE RESULT: I tried to re-verify this set's 169 by counting source, and I CANNOT.
The figure stands unchallenged. Recording the failed audit so nobody repeats it.
— WildMountain, 2026-09-18.

WHY I TRIED: an hour ago I found a number I had published ("189 discovered elsewhere") was a
pass count I had misread as a platform figure. So I audited the other numbers I had cited from
memory rather than measured. 169 is the one I have repeated most and measured least, and it
lives in THIS bead as a calibration set.

THREE INSTRUMENTS, THREE ANSWERS, NONE OF THEM 169:

  A. per-file `^\s*#\[test\]` count                              TOTAL 104
       5 of 7 matched exactly; oauth_interaction 67->14, oauth_core_rpc 23->11.
  B. same, but following `#[path=..] mod` submodule trees        TOTAL 269
       oauth_core_rpc now matches at 23 -- so the submodule idea was RIGHT for it --
       but oauth_interaction overshoots to 113 and oauth_client_credentials to 77.
  C. attribute-form enumeration (is there a non-`#[test]` form?) only `#[test]` exists,
       so A was not missing an async/custom attribute. This project forbids tokio, so
       `#[tokio::test]` was never the right second form to look for.

DIFFERENT TARGETS MATCH UNDER DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS. That is the signature of an unfit
instrument, not of a wrong figure. A static walk cannot resolve which modules land in a given
test BINARY: `#[path=..]` redirection, cfg-gated `mod` declarations, and shared fixture
modules all change the answer, and the binary's contents depend on the feature set at build
time -- which is the whole subject of this bead.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY: I did not publish "169 is wrong". I have no evidence against it.
I have evidence that THREE OF MY OWN PROBES ARE UNRELIABLE for this question. Those are
different claims, and the first one would have corrupted a calibration set on the strength of
the second.

THE AUTHORITATIVE INSTRUMENT IS THE ONE THE FIGURE ALREADY USED: `cargo test <selectors> --
--list`, which enumerates what the built binary actually contains. The record says 169 was
measured that way. I am not re-running it now: it needs three separate invocations (client
wants `native-tls-roots,tasks`, console and transport want `legacy-2024-11-05` -- features are
per-invocation, not per-package), each a real build, to re-confirm a number I have found no
reason to doubt.

IF SOMEONE DOES RE-RUN IT, the `--` separator is required; `cargo test --workspace --list` is
rejected in ~369ms, and zero `Running` lines is ALSO what a genuine zero-run prints, so that
failure mode impersonates the very defect this set calibrates for.

STANDING: 169 (standalone, per-package) and 113 (fastmcp-rust-inclusive, the three
native-tls-roots targets) are unchanged and remain this set's figures.

either. The four stanzas in that manifest belong to pxy_leg_01_* and leg_02_*. These are
auto-discovered and a no-flags runner reaches all six. BOTH halves had to be checked: a
missing file-scope gate does not rule out the required-features skip, and the two mechanisms
have opposite signatures.

THREE are SUBMODULES, not targets, and their reachability is their PARENT's:
    oauth_discovery/issuer_metadata.rs   12 tests -> parent oauth_discovery.rs is UNGATED -> lit
    oauth_discovery/resource_metadata.rs 15 tests -> same parent                          -> lit
    oauth_interaction/resources.rs       25 tests -> parent oauth_interaction.rs IS gated
                                                     on native-tls-roots                  -> DARK
The last one is NOT a new class member. It is new dark content inside an existing member,
which is a different thing and should not be counted as a target.

== INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, because a "no gate" answer is the dangerous one ==

Before trusting any negative I ran the gate reader against a known positive --
`console/tests/integration.rs`, which uses the `any(feature = ..., ...)` form -- and it was
found. An anchored `#![cfg(feature` pattern misses that shape SILENTLY, and a peer made
exactly that error on this class earlier today, concluding "no gate of any kind" for a file
whose gate sits on line 9.

== WHAT I AM NOT PUBLISHING: A NEW TOTAL ==

27 and 25 are SOURCE counts of `#[test]` attributes. They are not discovery counts. This set's
169/113 figures come from `cargo test -- --list`, and I established in comment 3091 that
static counting CANNOT verify a --list figure: three instruments gave 104, 269, and partial
agreement, with DIFFERENT targets matching under each, because `#[path=..]` redirection,
cfg-gated `mod` declarations and the build-time feature set all change which modules reach a
binary.

So: the MEMBERSHIP finding is solid and belongs in this set. The arithmetic is not mine to
publish. Whoever next runs `--list` should expect the native-tls-roots hard core to have
grown by one target, and should take the count from the run rather than from me.

== WHY THIS MATTERS TO THIS BEAD SPECIFICALLY ==

This set exists to prove a zero-run detector can SEE a zero-run. A detector calibrated
against the set as it stood before fa04261d would now miss a target that is dark under every
default invocation -- and would pass its own calibration while doing so.

  parsing; peer bytes, diagnostics, and ordinary failures cannot mutate it.

  and present planned/unverified state; no schema, component, or process
  artifact may satisfy another row or the aggregate row.

  explicit ModernOnly discovery, request metadata, and cancellation ownership.
  Keep only claims backed by the owning public contract: typed JSON-RPC/schema
  errors, header/auth/redaction boundaries, extension activation, Tasks,
  MRTR, subscriptions, and Apps language remain conditional on their
  respective implementation evidence rather than inferred from a document.

  secrets and peer-controlled terminal markup are absent, nonzero diagnostic
  exits are shown, and no example fabricates a successful empty catalog or a
  selection result.  Keep rustdoc and README code samples on public facade/
  CLI surfaces; no internal-only helper or cfg(test)-only path is documentation
  proof.

  `doc_01_public_docs_planted_negative` are same-Bead real tests over the

  the planted negative changes only one stale profile, era, aggregate claim,
  runnable optional-profile assertion, or unsafe example and fails with a
  stable diagnostic.

  tests. Assert modern discovery first action, valid modern application
  opening, legacy-feature-off isolation, typed Auto/Legacy unavailability,
  and no initialization/fallback/adapter effect through shipped surfaces.
- Test the core HTTP documentation matrix: one modern request/response POST
  surface, no management GET/DELETE, no session/replay headers, and no legacy
  endpoint derivation or fallback. Dual-era HTTP tables are CI-DUAL-01 inputs,
  not DOC-01 positives.
- Explicit planted negatives reject an invented 2025 alias, obsolete
  `LatestOnly`-style profile, sessioned legacy transport, generic fallback,
  inferred endpoint, initialization in a modern example, discovery in a
  legacy example, component-to-aggregate claim, process-artifact-only proof,
  and fixture-as-live substitution.  Each has no claimed support result.
- Every required test is discovered, started, and passed unfiltered with its
  real code/documentation source change on this Bead.  Ignored, zero-run,
  wrapper-only, scan-only, generated-report-only, or documentation-only
  results earn no capability, conformance, or runtime credit.

Evidence:

  claim.
- No-claim boundary: DOC-01 does not prove implementation, runtime behavior,

Dependencies:

title: DOC-02 implementation A: evidence-derived support matrix generation
description:
Section 36.4.1 A production slice: evidence-derived support matrix generation. I consumes this shipped public surface. Actual generation code plus positive and one-variable planted-negative tests must land in this same Bead.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:DOC-02:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for DOC-02.

Owned capability slice: evidence-derived support matrix generation.
Named shipped consumer: public documentation publication inputs.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### DOC-02 — Publish evidence-backed support claims

Outcome:

Replace provisional documentation states with exact, reproducible
release claims.

Reason:

Documentation should evolve during implementation, but final support
claims must be written only after conformance and release-profile
evidence exists.

Implementation:

- Read the machine-generated core qualification manifest from
  CI-CORE-01. It is sufficient to draft the exact claims, but it is
  not the releasable source/package identity.
- Mark core support only when CONF-02 is green with an empty baseline.
- Core wire/support text must name final `Result` objects as open and
  link CI-CORE-01's nonempty preservation evidence across protocol,
  server/middleware, client, and cache paths. State that unknown
  siblings are bounded inert data, selected-known fields remain
  authoritative, and an unknown discriminator is not a known result
  with extras.
- In the core release, leave every optional profile explicitly
  unclaimed even if its code compiled in all-features safety jobs.
- Establish the core-only documentation baseline. Each named optional
  `CI-*` endpoint below is also its profile's additive
  documentation/promotion Bead and must depend on DOC-02,
  CI-FINAL-CORE-01, and its exact profile evidence before changing
  one support-matrix row or publishing one profile bundle.
- Never describe the OAuth Client Credentials official-pinned-Draft CI record
  as an aggregate or final-release support claim.
- The dual-era row may claim only CI-DUAL-01's exact 2026-07-28 plus
  2024-11-05 profile. It names the three immutable v2 profile identities,
  binds unchanged core `ModernOnly` evidence and the compiled
  feature/role/binding receipts, and records the complete stdio
  server-first-frame/client-first-wire matrices plus LEG-HTTP-01's exact
  legacy endpoint-event transport. Its `Auto` HTTP evidence is LEG-NEG-01's
  exhaustive 400/404/405 body matrix: recognized modern JSON-RPC fixes
  Modern, only empty/unrecognized rows authorize one configured legacy GET,
  and only a valid endpoint event selects Legacy. Policy is immutable and
  feature/receipt validated; request bytes never activate legacy.
- The enterprise row may say OIDC authorization-code SSO only when
  CI-EMA-01 names the external front-channel adapter, framework-owned
  pending-flow store/envelope/restore authority, code redeemer, exact
  response admission, persistent replay MAC/store, policy-bundle/
  mapping backend, fixed HTTPS-GET serializer, named launch-receipt
  verifier/rotation policy and receipt-versus-independent-captured-wire
  evidence boundary, query/fragment-free sealed URLs, omitted
  `response_mode`/default-query behavior, authorization-only
  `scope=openid`, subject-namespace/sector evidence, closed error
  transports, tenant/request-hint/session-lifetime/subject-namespace
  disposition, all six identity-source hashes, and every stable
  exclusion. Phrase the boundary as “no bundled browser UX,” not “no
  browser SSO” or “caller-injected ID Token.”
- The official-pinned-Draft client-credentials row must say client-role/external-
  AS-only, Streamable-HTTP-only, preregistration-only, unconstrained
  Bearer-only, and no built-in issuer branch. Publish Basic availability
  only from the independent HTTPS real-peer/attested-custody evidence,
  never from the raw loopback scenario; publish the private-key method
  only from independent RS256 evidence. Name the exact issuer-bound
  client-registration receipt, client `grant_types` and
  `token_endpoint_auth_method`, separate server metadata, custody,
  JWT-preferred selection/Basic-deviation, dispatch, singleflight,
  exact nonempty-scope/no-default behavior, response/cache/lifetime, and
  atomic-commit evidence and retain `official-pinned-draft`/
  `aggregate_claim=false`.
- The enterprise/built-in composition row is additive and names exact
  preregistration/both-grants eligibility, persistent replay ring/
  restore evidence, policy/mapping receipt, five-way wire error
  partition, residual timing nonclaim, and no-refresh result; neither
  standalone row inherits it.
- The Apps row may claim only the host-neutral broker/data profile proved
  by CI-APPS-01. It must name
  `apps_client_settings_schema=apps-2026-01-26-client-mime-types-v1`,
  `apps_server_settings_schema=fastmcp-2026-07-28-apps-empty-server-marker-v1`,

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:DOC-02:I:BEGIN -->
Canonical I role for DOC-02.

Owned capability slice: public documentation publication inputs.
Named shipped consumer: public documentation publication inputs.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### DOC-02 — Publish evidence-backed support claims

Outcome:

Replace provisional documentation states with exact, reproducible
release claims.

Reason:

Documentation should evolve during implementation, but final support
claims must be written only after conformance and release-profile
evidence exists.

Implementation:

- Read the machine-generated core qualification manifest from
  CI-CORE-01. It is sufficient to draft the exact claims, but it is
  not the releasable source/package identity.
- Mark core support only when CONF-02 is green with an empty baseline.
- Core wire/support text must name final `Result` objects as open and
  link CI-CORE-01's nonempty preservation evidence across protocol,
  server/middleware, client, and cache paths. State that unknown
  siblings are bounded inert data, selected-known fields remain
  authoritative, and an unknown discriminator is not a known result
  with extras.
- In the core release, leave every optional profile explicitly
  unclaimed even if its code compiled in all-features safety jobs.
- Establish the core-only documentation baseline. Each named optional
  `CI-*` endpoint below is also its profile's additive
  documentation/promotion Bead and must depend on DOC-02,
  CI-FINAL-CORE-01, and its exact profile evidence before changing
  one support-matrix row or publishing one profile bundle.
- Never describe the OAuth Client Credentials official-pinned-Draft CI record
  as an aggregate or final-release support claim.
- The dual-era row may claim only CI-DUAL-01's exact 2026-07-28 plus
  2024-11-05 profile. It names the three immutable v2 profile identities,
  binds unchanged core `ModernOnly` evidence and the compiled
  feature/role/binding receipts, and records the complete stdio
  server-first-frame/client-first-wire matrices plus LEG-HTTP-01's exact
  legacy endpoint-event transport. Its `Auto` HTTP evidence is LEG-NEG-01's
  exhaustive 400/404/405 body matrix: recognized modern JSON-RPC fixes
  Modern, only empty/unrecognized rows authorize one configured legacy GET,
  and only a valid endpoint event selects Legacy. Policy is immutable and
  feature/receipt validated; request bytes never activate legacy.
- The enterprise row may say OIDC authorization-code SSO only when
  CI-EMA-01 names the external front-channel adapter, framework-owned
  pending-flow store/envelope/restore authority, code redeemer, exact
  response admission, persistent replay MAC/store, policy-bundle/
  mapping backend, fixed HTTPS-GET serializer, named launch-receipt
  verifier/rotation policy and receipt-versus-independent-captured-wire
  evidence boundary, query/fragment-free sealed URLs, omitted
  `response_mode`/default-query behavior, authorization-only
  `scope=openid`, subject-namespace/sector evidence, closed error
  transports, tenant/request-hint/session-lifetime/subject-namespace
  disposition, all six identity-source hashes, and every stable
  exclusion. Phrase the boundary as “no bundled browser UX,” not “no
  browser SSO” or “caller-injected ID Token.”
- The official-pinned-Draft client-credentials row must say client-role/external-
  AS-only, Streamable-HTTP-only, preregistration-only, unconstrained
  Bearer-only, and no built-in issuer branch. Publish Basic availability
  only from the independent HTTPS real-peer/attested-custody evidence,
  never from the raw loopback scenario; publish the private-key method
  only from independent RS256 evidence. Name the exact issuer-bound
  client-registration receipt, client `grant_types` and
  `token_endpoint_auth_method`, separate server metadata, custody,
  JWT-preferred selection/Basic-deviation, dispatch, singleflight,
  exact nonempty-scope/no-default behavior, response/cache/lifetime, and
  atomic-commit evidence and retain `official-pinned-draft`/
  `aggregate_claim=false`.
- The enterprise/built-in composition row is additive and names exact
  preregistration/both-grants eligibility, persistent replay ring/
  restore evidence, policy/mapping receipt, five-way wire error
  partition, residual timing nonclaim, and no-refresh result; neither
  standalone row inherits it.
- The Apps row may claim only the host-neutral broker/data profile proved
  by CI-APPS-01. It must name
  `apps_client_settings_schema=apps-2026-01-26-client-mime-types-v1`,
  `apps_server_settings_schema=fastmcp-2026-07-28-apps-empty-server-marker-v1`,
  `apps_negotiation_resolver=fastmcp-apps-bilateral-resolver-v1`,
  and
  `apps_activation_predicate=fastmcp-2026-07-28-apps-bilateral-mime-v1`;
  state local-enable plus server-`{}` plus current-request exact-MIME
  membership and the ordinary-fallback/malformed-error split; and never
  imply object equality or session/initialize-era activation. It must
  also name
  `apps_projection_profile=fastmcp-apps-sdk-1.29.0-projection-v1` and
  `apps_sdk29_standard_reuse_inventory=fastmcp-apps-sdk-1.29.0-standard-reuse-v1`,
  including all 21 roots, inherited controls, directions/dispositions,
  transitive closure hashes, closed optional `toolInfo`/ID/resource-size
  omission inventory, and initial-fallback versus active-View failure
  boundary. Name
  `apps_lifecycle_profile=fastmcp-apps-2026-01-26-apps-1.7.5-sdk-1.29.0-strict-order-v1`,
  the one-way Host pre-initialization prohibition, pinned SDK
  warning-only/strict/generic-send behavior, FastMCP local pre-send
  enforcement, fixed early-request denial, all four direction-correct
  View application notifications, and their pre-`Active`
  no-side-effect compatibility-sink disposition/limitation. Name
  `apps_error_profile=fastmcp-apps-sdk-1.29.0-error-v1` and disclose its
  required ID, closed outer/inner shapes, safe-integer alias/canonical
  code policy, bounded message/presence-aware recursive data, unknown-
  code inertness, SDK inner-strip differential, and
  `apps_uncorrelatable_input_disposition=no-response-drop` with no ID
  fabrication/null/omitted error. State that all six
  source-forward-open Apps-only results uniformly enforce
  `apps_forward_open_result_reserved_members=["_meta","resultType"]`
  while preserving other bounded members inertly. Disclose
  `apps_sampling_supported=false`,
  `apps_tasks_result_bridge_supported=false`, and
  `apps_mrtr_result_bridge_supported=false`, plus the no-renderer
  boundary.
- Keep Tasks labeled with the pinned upstream maturity status. Its row
  must name
  `tasks_contract_profile=fastmcp-final-core-2026-07-28-tasks-2c1425d9-v1`
  and
  `task_notification_profile=fastmcp-final-notification-open-v1`, link
  the full-pin/four-hash/SDK-integrity/path/corpus evidence, and explain
  every exact composition seam: final result/discriminator/metadata,
  final request envelope/metadata, final MRTR embedded descriptors/
  results, exact completed `CallToolResult`, exact failed inner `Error`,
  source-open notifications despite generated closed branches, and the
  two Tasks fragments merged into final subscription request/
  acknowledgement filters. State that a completed Task preserves the
  nested final `CallToolResult`'s bounded inert open siblings through
  storage, get, notification, and any claimed proxy composition without
  granting them Task/cache/extension semantics. State that
  progress/logging is scoped only to one live RPC and never follows
  background Task execution. It must also disclose Section 5.23's
  composed timestamp profile:
  FastMCP accepts only the exact bounded RFC 3339 subset and canonical
  UTC emission defined there, while the pinned prose says broader ISO
  8601 and the schema enforces only string. Link the drift/rejection
  corpus and do not claim acceptance of every prose-valid ISO 8601
  representation. The same row must name
  `task_duration_profile=fastmcp-positive-integer-ms-v1`, distinguish
  mathematical-integer equivalence/canonical emission, and disclose
  that the positive-only TTL/poll-interval rule is the selected
  conformance/composition policy rather than a constraint in the sign-
  silent prose or raw number schema.
  It must also name
  `task_id_profile=fastmcp-opaque-task-id-v1`, link per-ID and
  subscription-aggregate N-1/N/N+1 evidence over every result/param/
  notification/filter/resume surface, distinguish canonical local
  emission from tolerant exact peer admission, and state the
  fixed-size resume-key plus authenticated-original-ID binding and
  non-authority rule.
- The modern-proxy row may claim only CI-PROXY-01's exact profile.
  It must state that every stateless client→server extension-
  notification activation proof terminates at the downstream gateway
  leg: the gateway independently reconstructs and resolves a fresh
  self-contained proof or revalidates a separately live mapped
  negotiated owner under the selected upstream endpoint, security,
  settings, and generation bindings. It must not imply that a
  downstream receipt/handle, discovery state, prior request, generic
  metadata, header capsule, or connection activates the upstream leg;
  an unprovable or non-losslessly representable route emits no upstream
  bytes.
- Link each support-matrix row to test, conformance, or explicit
  non-goal evidence.
- Record exact core schema, conformance harness, extension, compiler,
  and dependency revisions.
- State that memory and experimental WebSocket are not standards-track
  transport claims.
- Keep the stdio logging support row bounded to the exact conservative
  core behavior; extension-assisted correlation is claimable only by a
  separately named negotiated-extension evidence bundle.
- Publish known limitations only when they are true exclusions, not
  hidden failing tests.
- Ensure README, crate docs, CLI version output, changelog, and release
  notes agree.

Acceptance:

- No “supported,” “conformant,” “stable,” or “production” claim lacks
  an evidence-manifest reference.
- Optional profiles are independently visible and cannot inherit the
  core claim accidentally.
- The core documentation can ship without any optional-profile gate.
- All documented versions and maturity labels match pinned artifacts.
- Core support text does not overclaim stdio request attribution for
  identifier-free concurrent log notifications.
- Core and optional support text cannot describe a known final Result
  as closed or omit the open-sibling preservation/no-authority
  boundary.
- The support matrix is reproducible from a clean checkout.

Tests:

- Support-claim/evidence-manifest consistency.
- Core/Tasks/proxy final-Result openness and inert-preservation claim
  parity, including a mutation that falsely documents a closed result
  or omits the nested completed-Task boundary.
- Modern-proxy stateless-notification proof-boundary wording and
  evidence parity, including mutations that forward a downstream
  receipt/owner handle or omit independent upstream reconstruction.
- README/crate-doc/CLI version agreement.
- Optional-profile negative tests.
- Enterprise wording tests reject “injected ID Token,” generic browser-
  SSO exclusion, omitted external-adapter/pending-store/redeemer,
  omitted launch-receipt/wire-digest or Discovery/Registration/sector/
  error evidence, wrong method/encoding/`response_mode`/scope/URL or
  shortened-versus-full ID-JAG `typ` claims, or widened SAML/implicit/
  hybrid/refresh/JWE/tenant-hint/session-expiry/initial-`aud_sub`
  claims.
- Experimental wording tests reject a built-in-issuer implication, raw
  Basic promotion, stable maturity, non-Streamable-HTTP scope, dynamic
  registration, missing or substituted client `grant_types`/
  `token_endpoint_auth_method`, unreviewed Basic preference or runtime
  method fallback, omitted/empty/default-only requested scope, sender-
  constrained tokens, or missing response/custody/atomic-commit
  evidence.
- Tasks wording tests reject a missing/substituted Tasks-contract or
  notification-profile identifier,
  raw generated whole-message/old-SDK substitution, closed notification
  `_meta`/extras, an omitted timestamp-profile identifier, a
  claim of arbitrary ISO 8601 acceptance, failure to disclose the
  narrower composed contract, or timestamp prose/schema drift without
  the exact Section 5.23 evidence link. Also reject a missing duration-
  profile identifier, lexical-integer confusion, hidden positive-only
  boundary, or attribution of that rule to the raw schema/prose.
- Apps wording tests reject a missing/substituted settings-schema,
  resolver/activation, projection-profile, standard-reuse-inventory, or
  error-profile identifier; one-sided, equality-based, prior-request, or
  initialize-era activation; incomplete SDK root/descendant inventory;
  omitted advisory-loss/failure or error-code/data/strip disclosure;
  a response to uncorrelatable input or hidden ID fabrication;
  inconsistent Apps-only `_meta`/`resultType` admission; an Apps sampling
  claim; hidden Tasks/MRTR result mediation; or a renderer implication.
- Link and artifact existence checks.
- Logging support-row/Section 5.21 consistency and no-implied-
  correlation checks.

Dependencies:

- DOC-01.
- CONF-02.
- CI-CORE-01.

---

## 23. Phase 11 — Verification and release

- [ ] `doc_02_i_positive`: exact positive test ID. Runner: `rch exec -- cargo test --workspace --all-targets doc_02_i_positive -- --exact`. Evaluator: public DOC-02 I test evaluator. Observed field: public result/receipt record for public documentation publication inputs. Predicate: the declared I behavior is present through the shipped, non-`cfg(test)` public surface. Minimum count: 1. Proof class: public-surface unit/integration plus planted-red proof.
- [ ] `doc_02_i_planted_negative`: exact near-identical one-variable negative test ID, run through the same RCH profile and public surface. It differs only in the forbidden dimension, reaches the typed refusal boundary, and proves every named mutable state field byte-for-byte unchanged. Minimum count: 1. Unsupported `2025-11-25` is a negative only and can never satisfy a 2026 or exact-2024 positive.
- [ ] Exact inventory equality is mandatory: required = discovered = started = passed for both frozen IDs; required count = 2 and passed count = 2. Zero ignored, filtered, skipped, feature-disabled, zero-run, early-aborted, stale-revision, mixed-revision, or substituted rows.
- [ ] Proof configuration is frozen in the batch receipt: toolchain nightly-2026-08-25; workspace target and platform; Cargo profile; selected feature set; public binary/handler/facade consumer; source tree, Cargo.lock, package, and executable digests; first-attempt result and all retries. `cfg(test)` behavior cannot prove shipped behavior.
- [ ] Named consumer: public documentation publication inputs. No-claim boundary: this role alone does not establish parent completion, aggregate MCP 2026-07-28 support, MCP 2024-11-05 preservation, automatic negotiation, profile maturity, conformance, publication, or release readiness.
- [ ] RH-1 through RH-12, SM-1 through SM-12, and PL-1 through PL-5 apply. Real implementation and real positive/negative tests remain one credit unit; unmet acceptance stays on this Bead. Only the designated batch-verification orchestrator may close it against the exact verified revision.

comments.text:
ASSIGNED, VERIFIED, AND THE GAP IS NOT THE ONE THE ONE-LINER DESCRIBES — it is narrower and it has
an owner problem rather than a value problem. Also: THIS BEAD CANNOT BE CLAIMED; it is blocked by
three open deps. MagentaOsprey, assignee. Read-only; no dispatch; no file touched; nothing ticked.

## THE CLAIM AS GIVEN, CHECKED
"Nothing in the repo SETS FASTMCP_FND01_PUBLIC_HARNESS_BIN; only a reader at
fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:63221."

  READER — CONFIRMED, and there is exactly one:
      fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:63334   (not :63221 — the file has moved 113 lines under the
      citation; the symbol is stable, the coordinate is not)
          std::env::var_os("FASTMCP_FND01_PUBLIC_HARNESS_BIN")
              .map(PathBuf::from).ok_or_else(|| pending!("... is required"))?
      Plus one prose mention at fnd_01_a_evidence_binding.rs:1883. No other reader.

  SETTERS — THE CLAIM NEEDS ONE CORRECTION. They exist. Every one of them is UNTRACKED:
      .fnd01-provision-and-run.sh:81   export FASTMCP_FND01_PUBLIC_HARNESS_BIN="$HARNESS"
      zz0r_job.sh, zz0r_job2.sh, zz0r_job3.sh   (two sites each)
      `git ls-files` returns nothing for any of them.
  So the precondition is not unknown — it is SOLVED IN PRIVATE, in per-agent scratch files that no
  fresh checkout has, no reviewer reads, and no receipt cites. That is a worse failure mode than
  absence: whoever holds the file sees a working setup and cannot see why anyone else fails.

## THE REFRAMING, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES THE FIX
The variable carries NO INFORMATION. The reader derives the only legal value itself, six lines
after reading it:

    let target = env::var_os("CARGO_TARGET_DIR").map(PathBuf::from)
                     .unwrap_or_else(|| source_root.join("target"));
    let expected = target.join("debug/examples/fnd_01_evidence_harness");
    if public_harness != expected { return Err(pending!("public harness must be the Cargo example artifact")); }

It must be ABSOLUTE and it must EQUAL that path. Exactly one string is accepted, and the code
already knows it. So this is a RESTATEMENT HANDSHAKE, not an input: the variable's only function is
to make the caller assert they know where the artifact is. "Set the env var" is therefore mechanical
and cannot be got wrong in an interesting way.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY REQUIRED is the thing the handshake stands for: the Cargo EXAMPLE
`fnd_01_evidence_harness` must have been BUILT and be present at that exact path. The five
`E_ORDINARY_HANDOFF_PENDING` failures are a missing BUILD STEP wearing an env var's clothes.

## A COUPLING TRAP IN THE EXISTING PRIVATE SCRIPT, FOR WHOEVER ADOPTS IT
`.fnd01-provision-and-run.sh` builds the example, strips it, copies it to a RETAINED target root,
verifies bytes+sha256 identity after staging, and exports THAT staged path. That only satisfies the
equality above if `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is also pointed at the same retained root. The script and the
reader are coupled through a third variable that neither mentions. Anyone lifting the export line
without the CARGO_TARGET_DIR line gets `public harness must be the Cargo example artifact`, which
names neither of the two things actually wrong.

## WHAT THE HARNESS IS, since "example" undersells it
crates/fastmcp/examples/fnd_01_evidence_harness.rs is 37 lines and does one thing:
`#[path = "../tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs"] mod evidence;` then
`exit(evidence::harness_main(args_os()))`. It is the SAME 68k-line verifier compiled in a
non-test cfg surface. It declares NO `required-features`, while the test target that owns the same
source declares `required-features = ["testing-lab"]` — so which features the example needs is an
open question I cannot settle without a build, and it belongs in the setup this bead owns.

## I CANNOT CLAIM THIS BEAD
    br update --status in_progress  ->  "cannot claim blocked issue"
    bd-63l5                              open, MagentaSummit   FND-04 Cx migration
    bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.48    open, UNASSIGNED      XPORT-01
    bd-mcp-ext-dev-01-t6la               open, UNASSIGNED      EXT-DEV-01
Two of the three have no owner. I am recording the investigation here rather than sitting on it,
but the bead stays `open` and I have not moved it.

## WHERE A FIX COULD LAND, AND WHERE IT MAY NOT
NOT in the reader: fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs is an ahet.1.14 authoring_write_path (ProudValley),
which already blocks bd-wo55t and one y5ydn remedy branch. Fortunately no reader change is needed —
the handshake is satisfiable entirely from outside.
The candidate home is a TRACKED provisioning step: `tools/xtask` is a workspace member and is the
natural owner of "build the example, verify its identity, export the derived path". That adopts the
private script's logic into something reviewable and version-controlled, which is what
"deterministic setup" in this bead's title means. I have not written it; the bead is blocked.

### STOP 1: graph
- `br update --claim` refuses the claim, as in 5359.
- Transitive blockers from .beads/issues.jsonl: 318 in total, 303 not closed. The dependency data was controlled: gytf reads back its 3 direct edges.

### STOP 2: semantic prerequisite, not only an edge
- Section 1 item 1 bases all four graphs on "API-CORE-01 with --no-default-features". API-CORE-01 (bd-api-core-01-formal-parent-3l6c) is open and unassigned.
- Item 4 freezes an "exact graph input digest" and an export-state digest, taken over a base surface that is not frozen yet. A digest taken now measures something that is still moving (the frozen-constant rot class).
- Whether the XPORT-01 and EXT-DEV-01 edges are semantic for A is a graph question for the structure owner. A's own text consumes no transport. EXT-DEV-01 may define symbols that item 2/5's forbidden inventory must name. I have not decided this.

### STOP 3: the acceptance text needs an amendment before code
The two sections disagree, and no TARGET-MAP amendment exists (checked).

(a) Denominators.
- Item 6 wants discovered == started == passed == 4 "for frozen graphs", with zero filtered.
- Item 9 (BRIDGE-V1) wants required == discovered == started == passed == 2 for `dx_test_01_a_positive` / `dx_test_01_a_planted_negative`, with zero filtered.
- Read literally at the libtest level, no single target lists both 4 and 2. Two targets would duplicate the capability under two ID sets, which is alias padding, or would add a fifth graph, which item 1 forbids.
- ONE CONSISTENT LAYOUT EXISTS:
  - a dedicated target with exactly 2 libtest IDs;
  - `dx_test_01_a_positive` runs `dx_test_01_a_compile_graph_evaluator` over the 4 ordered case IDs;

- This layout satisfies item 6 only if its counters are the EVALUATOR'S CASE counters, not libtest rows. That is a reading the text does not state, so it needs a bar author's amendment giving a denominator per clause, not an implementer's gloss.

(b) Filtered rows.

- Every other test binary in the workspace then reports filtered_out > 0, which violates item 9's "zero ... filtered". Item 7's runner also never runs the negative.

(O1) HIDDEN RUNTIME IN testing::lab.
- `TestContext::new()` (context.rs:61, with `impl Default` at :46 routing to it) and `TestClient::new()` (client.rs:78) each call `fastmcp_core::block_on`.

- bd-63l5's text says only "Gate testing-only context construction appropriately" and never names testing::lab, TestContext or TestClient. So I read this as A's obligation, not FND-04's. That is a reading, flagged for the structure owner.

(O2) Lab entrypoints outside `testing::lab`, both gated on testing-lab:
- root `pub use asupersync;` (lib.rs:222);
- root `pub use asupersync::{LabConfig, LabRuntime};` (lib.rs:434). `testing::lab` re-exports these via `crate::`.
- Item 2 names `testing::lab` as the Lab entrypoint. Whether root copies violate it needs a gloss either way, so I am flagging it and not deciding.
- One existing consumer: lib.rs:11717, a unit test naming `super::asupersync::Cx`.

- dx_test_01_a_compile_graph_evaluator
- dx_test_01_a__default_no_test_exports__positive
- dx_test_01_a__testing_production_faithful__positive
- dx_test_01_a__testing_lab_lab_only__positive
- dx_test_01_a__renamed_facade_packaged_consumer__positive
- dx_test_01_a__default_lab_symbol_absent__planted_negative
- dx_test_01_a_positive
- dx_test_01_a_planted_negative

## WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (reusable machinery, NOT credit; nothing below is a DX-TEST-01 graph)
- Facade features: `testing = []` and `testing-lab = ["testing", "asupersync/test-internals"]` (Cargo.toml [features]). `pub mod testing` is gated on `any(testing, testing-lab)` (lib.rs:10368), and `testing::lab` exists (mod.rs).
- trybuild_tests.rs:
  - `FACADE_FEATURE_COMPILE_PROBES` already `cargo check`s `--no-default-features --features testing` and `testing-lab`, --locked --offline. It proves those graphs compile and nothing about their symbols.

Each fixture carries `should_compile` + `absent_feature_diagnostic`, which is item 3's negative shape.
  - `prepare_fixture_lock` and `run_bounded` are already there.
  - None of the 47 probes names `testing` or `testing::lab`.

A DESIGN CONSTRAINT THE IMPLEMENTER MUST HONOUR: every facade test binary builds with asupersync `test-internals` ON (crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies]; core, client, server and transport do the same).
- So "absence of test-internals" in the default and `testing` graphs is observable ONLY in an isolated fixture package, never through the facade test binary's own cfg.
- The existing fixture harness already isolates. Using it also satisfies item 10's "cfg(test) cannot prove shipped behaviour" by construction.
- Placement: trybuild_tests.rs is a shared target, so under any reading of items 6 and 9 the graphs need their own target.

1. A third-party bar author amends items 6/7/9: a per-clause denominator (case counters vs libtest IDs), a dedicated-target runner with no workspace filter, and item 8's stray sentence struck. The same pattern as zq09 X1-X12.
2. A ruling on O2 (root Lab re-exports) and on whether O1 is A's or FND-04's.
3. The structure owner decides whether the XPORT-01/EXT-DEV-01 edges are semantic for A. API-CORE-01 remains a genuine semantic prerequisite for the digests.
4. Only then does code start. It is worked unclaimed per R1 while the graph refuses the claim.

renamed packaged consumers exercise real production entrypoints with a

or a hidden runtime makes conformance evidence non-reproducible.

Implementation:

- Export production-faithful helpers only under the non-default facade
  `testing` feature. Export LabRuntime, virtual time, DPOR, and Lab-only
  helpers only under `testing-lab`, which implies `testing`; ordinary/default
  builds expose neither Lab symbols nor `asupersync/test-internals`.
- Every helper accepts a caller-owned `&Cx` or caller-owned test scope and
  returns an exact bounded trace, typed result, and cardinality receipt. It
  never constructs an ambient runtime, hidden `Cx`, detached task, trusted raw
  ingress, or test-only production path.

  loopback HTTP JSON, and loopback HTTP request-scoped SSE. HTTP setup,
  admission, or response failure is fail-closed and can never be counted as a
  positive HTTP observation. Mock transports, parsers, registries, auth
  decisions, or result algebras are forbidden as live proof.
- Keep every packaged consumer isolated and resolve all generated/macro paths
  through its renamed facade dependency. The kit may observe public outputs
  and bounded state receipts but cannot mint registry, auth, raw JSON, or
  runtime authority.
- The mandatory child topology is `A + B → I → V → DX-TEST-01`. A owns the
  feature-graph and facade compile surface; B owns Memory trace/cancellation/
  terminal/cleanup behavior; I joins real child-stdio and loopback HTTP JSON/
  SSE consumers; V independently verifies the exact integration revision.
  The aggregate is never claimed monolithically.

- Child A freezes exactly four core/no-legacy compile graphs, all based on
  API-CORE-01 with `--no-default-features`: facade without test exports;
  `testing` production-faithful facade; `testing-lab` facade with Lab-only
  exports; and a renamed-facade packaged consumer. Each proves the intended
  symbols and the absence of legacy, forbidden runtime, and test-internals
  symbols for its graph.
- Child B freezes Memory concurrency at `N-1`, `N`, and `N+1` against the
  published limit, plus cancellation, terminal-result, and cleanup cases. It
  records the exact trace/result/cardinality evaluator outcome and proves
  sibling isolation, no output after terminal state, and complete cleanup.
- Child I proves isolated renamed packaged consumers at real child-stdio,
  loopback HTTP JSON, and loopback HTTP SSE entrypoints, with a real Memory
  baseline. Its trace/result/cardinality evaluator rejects a missing,
  reordered, extra, or cross-request event. An HTTP failure is a typed
  fail-closed negative, never a positive JSON or SSE category.
- Child V binds the exact I revision and verifies exactly four packaged
  fixtures: renamed Memory, renamed child-stdio, renamed loopback HTTP JSON,
  and renamed loopback HTTP SSE. Each fixture must record its feature graph,
  caller-owned context/scope, real entrypoint, trace/result/cardinality
  receipt, and first-attempt outcome.

- A uses real compile graphs, not documentation or synthetic export lists.
  B's N-1/N/N+1, cancellation, terminal, and cleanup cases invoke the shipped

- Require the mandatory prefix and name grammar from the final
  metadata-key rules.
- A mandatory prefix does not imply a nonempty name: accept and
  byte-preserve an identifier such as `com.example/` because the
  inherited final grammar explicitly permits an empty name. Do not
  replace the dated grammar with a conventional nonempty-name regex;
  an extension-specific profile may impose a stricter semantic name
  only in its own typed descriptor, never during generic peer
  structural admission.

  `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp`, including but not limited to
  `io.modelcontextprotocol/`, `dev.mcp/`,
  `org.modelcontextprotocol.api/`, and `com.mcp.tools/`.

  second label is `example`.
- Store settings as JSON object maps at the generic boundary, using
  Section 5.8's corrected recursive `JSONValue` so bounded nested null
  and fractional values survive generic preservation.
- Require every extension settings value to be a JSON object; an empty
  object means support with no extension-specific setting.
- Decode registered settings into typed values.
- Put the acyclic, immutable `ExtensionDescriptorRegistry` in
  `fastmcp-protocol`.
  It owns identifiers, client/server settings schemas and codecs,
  a typed client/server settings compatibility resolver,
  method names and direction, notification descriptors, result
  discriminators, transport routing-name/header rules, subscription
  event descriptors, optional stdio notification-correlation
  descriptors, and wire fallback declarations. Every registered
  client→server HTTP method also freezes one
  `ExtensionHttpEraDisposition::{ModernExclusive, EraAmbiguous}`.
  `ModernExclusive` is an audited assertion that the exact method
  cannot be valid under the included exact `2024-11-05` adapter and may
  therefore become HTTP-02's pre-auth `ModernEraMarker`;
  `EraAmbiguous` grants no method-text marker and leaves era selection
  to the version/Session tables. Reject missing dispositions,
  conflicting owners, a `ModernExclusive` claim colliding with a
  legacy/shared core method, and any registration whose legacy
  fallback declaration contradicts its era disposition.
- Every descriptor that enables a client→server notification on
  stateless modern HTTP must also freeze exactly one
  `NotificationActivationProofDescriptor`:
  `SelfContained` names an extension-owned params or extension-owned
  `_meta` field plus bounded settings/proof schema and compatibility
  resolver; `NegotiatedOwner` names an exact typed correlation handle
  issued by a live request/subscription whose retained record binds the
  extension/profile/settings/security/authorization generations.
  Structurally validate the self-contained proof before auth but
  resolve it only after authentication/authorization; look up a
  negotiated owner only through the later non-oracular authorized
  owner path. Reject a stateless-HTTP notification descriptor with no
  proof source, a generic/prior-request/connection/discovery source,

  notification methods/direction, and the required bilateral

  reject key/method ownership collisions, and expose only a typed
  prevalidated correlation capsule to the stdio adapter. No descriptor
  is installed by core, and an unknown metadata key can never become a
  routing hint.
