comments.text:
FND-04 B (a)/(b) TRIAGE OF THE 6 RED ROWS - OrangePike, 2026-09-17. Nothing implemented, nothing closed, no box checked.

BASIS: last verified run at 77164b50 (RubyOriole, hz3): required = discovered = 17, zero ignored/filtered, 11 passed / 6 failed. The binding unmet acceptance items are 1 (all 15 subcases passed and unfiltered) and 8 (required=discovered=started=passed=2 for both frozen IDs). Both reduce to the same 6 red rows; there is no separate reachable AC work behind them.

(a) REACHABLE AT asupersync 0.5.0 - 2 rows, NEITHER startable by me unilaterally.

B-03 transport-close-budget. Reachable and mechanical. Surveyed: 67 close impls (Transport 27 / RecvHalf 23 / SendHalf 17; 29 production, 38 test) plus 3 inherent wrappers (server/lib.rs:21342/21376/21424); ~20 production call sites, every one already holding or storing a Cx. Exactly one dyn Transport exists workspace-wide (fastmcp/src/lib.rs:13351, a type-check-only line), so `fn close(&mut self, cx: &Cx)` stays object-safe; an async close would not be and would break every Drop. The single Drop -> Transport::close chain (DualEraHttpSession, transport/http.rs:6254 -> :6233 -> :6240) dissolves: StreamableHttpTransport::close is exactly { self.close_queues(); Ok(()) } and that type's own Drop already calls close_queues().
BLOCKED BY: (i) the standing orchestrator ruling that B-03 remains a recorded finding and is not to be done now; (ii) it is one atomic change - the trait and all 67 impls move together or nothing compiles - spanning fastmcp-transport, fastmcp-server and fastmcp-client plus four test files in CoralMaple's and TealSalmon's crates, far beyond my lease. It cannot be split across panes.
CAVEAT, restated so a future green is not misread: adding &Cx lets close OBSERVE a budget at a checkpoint (the http_checkpoint pattern, http.rs:4319). It does not make a wedged flush() interruptible - stdio.rs:1548, sse.rs:784 and stdio.rs:926 stay unbounded. B-03 and B-10 are the same defect family, and fixing B-03 does not fix B-10.

B-07 production-deny-inventory. 267 denied sites: 155 out-of-band-cx, 94 production-block-on, 12 private-runtime, 3 public-runtime-bridge-export, 2 private-thread, 1 test-internals. collect_deny_inventory scans every shipped source file outside the single application boundary (crates/fastmcp-cli/src/), so the remediation IS the FND-04 migration itself - lifecycle entry points made async and &Cx-first across transport/server/client/core/protocol - not a local fix.
BLOCKED BY: the orchestrator ruling "measured, not fixed"; and workspace-wide cross-crate scope.
ONE SUB-ITEM THAT LOOKS TRIVIAL AND IS NOT: the `pub mod runtime;` + `pub use runtime::block_on;` export (core lib.rs:52, :2238) now has no production consumer, but it cannot simply be cfg(test)-gated, because fastmcp-protocol's jose.rs consumes it from its OWN test module, and a cfg(test) gate in one crate does not apply when a different crate compiles its tests.

(b) GENUINELY UNREACHABLE AT 0.5.0 - 4 rows, each with its specific upstream reason.

B-12 candidate-drift. Prerequisite cancel-aware-cross-platform-process-stdio unsatisfied, and there is no newer candidate to drift to: 0.5.0 IS the latest, verified against the LIVE crates.io sparse index rather than the local cache (which was four days stale) - published tail 0.4.9, 0.4.10, 0.4.11, 0.5.0, not yanked. The upstream development tree is also 0.5.0 (HEAD b48d0dc2b) and contains no own-process stdio work, so no unpublished fix is in flight. The other two prerequisites (ambient-child-region-owner, detectable-non-inline-blocking-facility) ARE satisfied at 0.5.0.

B-13 cross-platform-stdio. Two blockers of very different size; conflating them is the mistake to avoid.
  UNIX - one missing accessor. Source (runtime/reactor/source.rs:75, AsRawFd + Send + Sync), Interest (reactor/interest.rs:43) and IoDriverHandle::register (runtime/io_driver.rs:557) are all public and implementable for fd 0/1. The chain breaks at exactly one link: Cx exposes only timer_driver() (cx/cx.rs:1951) and has no public io_driver(); ReactorRegistration::arm is pub(crate) (net/udp.rs:1732).
  WINDOWS - structural, not visibility. Source on Windows is AsRawSocket + Send + Sync (source.rs:193); Windows stdin/stdout are console/pipe HANDLEs and cannot implement Source at all, so exposing an accessor would not help. asupersync 0.5.0 also has NO async stdio on Windows even for spawned children - process.rs:3209/3247/3357/3457 each return ErrorKind::Unsupported.
  TRAP 1: the Unix accessor already exists as Cx::io_driver_handle() (cx.rs:1125) but carries #[cfg_attr(feature = "test-internals", visibility::make(pub))] - public only under the feature this AC names as forbidden (fnd_04_runtime_conformance.rs:630-632; FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME_FEATURE :92). Because crates/fastmcp dev-deps unify asupersync/test-internals into every target under crates/fastmcp/tests/, an adapter prototyped there would compile and pass and could never ship: PL-3 dressed as a green row. Anyone reporting B-13 newly passing must be asked which feature set produced it.
  TRAP 2: B-13's P3 receipt does not test for driver access at all - it looks textually for `pub fn stdin(` in src/cx/cx.rs, or `pub fn stdin(`/`pub fn stdout(` in src/io/mod.rs (fnd_04_runtime_conformance.rs:636-639). Neither string exists in 0.5.0. So promoting io_driver_handle to pub would close the real capability gap and LEAVE P3 RED. The upstream ask must deliberately choose which of the two it is for.

B-10 hung-endpoint-and-recovery. Upstream, and for a reason DISTINCT from the stdio gap - a fourth upstream limitation, not part of B-12/B-13. Cx::spawn_blocking (cx/cx.rs:4661) routes through spawn_cancellation_dominant (:4449) with SpawnCompletionPolicy::CancellationDominant (:4470), whose documented contract is that it "discards a value produced after cancellation" (:4446-4448). That governs WHICH VALUE a cancelled join reports, not WHEN the join resolves. An admitted, non-cooperative blocking job therefore runs to completion; the join resolves only when the worker finishes, and then reports Cancelled. The run measured exactly that: hung_result = Err(Cancelled) at caller_release_ms = 10001 against a 2000ms bound, worker_occupied_at_caller_release = true, pool_recovered_after_release = true. asupersync 0.5.0 exposes no abandon-on-cancel path for an already-admitted blocking job.
NO FASTMCP CODE IS IN THIS PATH: the subcase calls Cx::spawn_blocking and TaskHandle::join directly, so no in-tree change can move the row. It could be made green by racing the join against a timeout, which would measure my own timeout instead of the runtime's cancellation delivery - the exact weakening that is forbidden, so I have not done it.

fnd_04_b_positive. Aggregates its constituents and cannot pass while any is red. Not independently fixable.

NET: 0 of the 6 red rows are both reachable AND unblocked for me right now. I wrote no code and committed nothing on this bead, because (a) contains no work I can start without cross-pane leases the orchestrator has to schedule.

DECISION NEEDED (one): take B-03 now with expanded leases across fastmcp-transport/src/{lib,stdio,sse,websocket,http,memory}.rs, fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs, fastmcp-client/src/{lib,execution}.rs and the four named test files, with CoralMaple and TealSalmon standing off those paths - or leave it deferred. It is one atomic change and cannot be partially landed.

comments.author: OrangePike
comments.text:
FND-04-B-10: THE UPSTREAM MECHANISM, RECORDED STANDALONE SO IT IS FINDABLE.
OrangePike, 2026-09-17. (Also stated inside the (a)/(b) triage, comment 2400; repeated here on its own because a reader arriving at B-10 should not have to find it inside a six-row triage.)

WHAT B-10 MEASURES. subcase_10_hung_endpoint_and_recovery (fnd_04_runtime_conformance.rs:1672) opens a child region, submits a non-cooperative blocking job via Cx::spawn_blocking, cancels the region, then awaits hung.join(region.cx()). It requires the caller to be released in under 2000ms (:1740) even though the occupied worker cannot be preempted.

WHAT WAS MEASURED at 77164b50: hung_result = Err(Cancelled), caller_release_ms = 10001, caller_released_within_bound = false, worker_occupied_at_caller_release = true, pool_recovered_after_release = true. The 10001ms is the hung closure's own 10-second self-deadline (:1697) elapsing - i.e. the join waited for the closure, then reported cancellation.

THE MECHANISM, read from the pinned archive rather than inferred:
  Cx::spawn_blocking            asupersync-0.5.0/src/cx/cx.rs:4661
  -> spawn_cancellation_dominant                          :4449
  -> SpawnCompletionPolicy::CancellationDominant          :4470
  Its doc comment at :4446-4448 states it is the "internal own-region variant for wrappers whose documented contract DISCARDS A VALUE PRODUCED AFTER CANCELLATION (for example, Self::spawn_blocking)".

THE POINT: CancellationDominant governs WHICH VALUE a cancelled join reports, NOT WHEN the join resolves. An already-admitted, non-cooperative blocking job runs to completion; the join future resolves only when the pool worker finishes, and the policy then discards the produced value and reports Cancelled. Cancellation dominated the value; it never touched the timing. asupersync 0.5.0 exposes no abandon-on-cancel path for a blocking job that a worker has already claimed.

DO NOT MISREAD "cancellation-dominant" AS A TIMING PROMISE. That is the trap this row exists to expose, and the name invites exactly the wrong reading.

WHY THIS IS A FOURTH UPSTREAM GAP, NOT PART OF B-12/B-13. B-12 and B-13 are the cancel-aware own-process stdio gap. This is the blocking-pool join gap. They are independent: shipping own-process async stdio would not change B-10, and an abandon-on-cancel join would not change B-13. Anyone drafting a single upstream ask for "FND-04" must carry both, and they are different asks.

WHY NO IN-TREE CHANGE CAN MOVE THIS ROW. There is no fastmcp code anywhere in the measured path. The subcase calls Cx::spawn_blocking and TaskHandle::join directly, both asupersync APIs. Nothing in this workspace sits between the cancellation and the caller's release.

THE TEMPTING WRONG FIX, NAMED SO IT IS NOT RE-PROPOSED. The row can be made green by racing the join against time::timeout_at or selecting on the cancellation. Do not. The subcase exists to measure whether cancelling a region releases a caller awaiting a blocking join; a timeout wrapper would measure the timeout, not the runtime's cancellation delivery, and the row would report green while the capability remained absent. Adjudicated by the orchestrator, 2026-09-17: refusing that substitution was the correct call.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ROW: an upstream abandon-on-cancel path for an already-admitted blocking job - i.e. a join that resolves Cancelled when the region cancels, leaving the worker to finish and be reclaimed independently. The existing observations already prove the reclaim half works: pool_recovered_after_release = true.

THE ONE STRUCTURAL RESTRUCTURE, re-verified at debf9d81:
  impl Drop for DualEraHttpSession      transport/http.rs:6254 calls self.close()

THE SUBSTANTIVE DECISION, AND A FINDING THAT OUTLIVES IT. sse.rs already guarded
ten I/O sites with `cx.is_cancel_requested()`, and its module doc advertises that
as the module's pattern. THAT GUARD CANNOT SEE AN EXPIRED DEADLINE - it reads the
explicit cancellation flag and nothing else, so a caller who has run out of time
but was never cancelled passes straight through into blocking I/O.

sse_checkpoint mirrors stdio_checkpoint and http_checkpoint: it observes deadline
exhaustion, cancellation, and poll/cost quota exhaustion, and reports Timeout
distinctly from Cancelled. The orchestrator specified the checkpoint pattern and
it is the stronger instrument; I used it rather than the module's local idiom.

CONSEQUENCE, recorded rather than silently fixed: sse.rs is now MIXED - one
checkpoint site and ten older is_cancel_requested sites. Those ten are send and
receive paths; each needs its own behavioural proof, and converting them under
cover of this change would be precisely the batching this increment was scoped to
avoid. FINDING FOR SEPARATE WORK: ten cancellation guards in sse.rs are blind to
an expired deadline. The same question should be asked of every module that uses
is_cancel_requested as its guard.

comments.text:
TEMPLATE: HOW TO MAKE A close() CONSUME THE CALLER'S BUDGET, AND HOW TO PROVE IT.
OrangePike, 2026-09-17, derived from the three landed conversions (53584e04,
5557718f/f9d5f7e4, cf8126cb, 47882c23). Written so the next agent does not
rediscover the shape.

=============================================================================
STEP 0 - THE SCOPING GATE. MOST CLOSES MUST NOT BE CONVERTED.
=============================================================================

Do NOT apply this template to all 56 remaining `_cx` closes. Measured breakdown:

    50   INERT - close a channel, set a flag, drop a registry. NO blocking I/O.
     4   test doubles in test files.
     2   production blocking closes - the entire real remaining surface:
            transport/src/sse.rs:1780    SseClientTransport::close
                                         flush, legacy-2024-11-05 ONLY
            transport/src/stdio.rs:1563  AsyncStdioTransport::close
                                         flush_unchecked, default reach

CONVERTING AN INERT CLOSE IS A DEFECT, not a no-op. A close that performs no
blocking I/O has no budget to spend, so a checkpoint buys nothing and costs
something real: it makes cleanup paths that legitimately run AFTER cancellation
begin to fail. The `_cx` on those fifty is CORRECT AND FINAL.

THE GATE: convert a close only if its body performs blocking I/O - flush,
flush_unchecked, write_all, a socket shutdown, a protocol close frame. If the
body only flips a flag or drops a channel, leave `_cx` alone.

=============================================================================
STEP 1 - THE SOURCE CHANGE
=============================================================================

Use the module's checkpoint helper, which maps an exhausted budget to a typed
refusal. The canonical form is http_checkpoint (transport/src/http.rs:4319);
stdio_checkpoint (stdio.rs:76) and sse_checkpoint (sse.rs) are identical twins:

    cx.checkpoint().map_err(|error| {
        use asupersync::{CancelKind, error::ErrorKind};
        match cx.cancel_reason().map(|reason| reason.kind) {
            Some(CancelKind::Deadline | CancelKind::Timeout) => TransportError::Timeout,
            Some(_) => TransportError::Cancelled,
            None => match error.kind() {
                ErrorKind::DeadlineExceeded | ErrorKind::CancelTimeout => TransportError::Timeout,
                ErrorKind::Cancelled
                | ErrorKind::PollQuotaExhausted
                | ErrorKind::CostQuotaExhausted => TransportError::Cancelled,
                _ => TransportError::Cancelled,
            },
        }
    })

DO NOT use `cx.is_cancel_requested()`. It reads the explicit cancellation bit
ONLY, so a caller whose DEADLINE expired passes straight through into the
blocking I/O. sse.rs still has ten sites carrying that weaker guard; they are a
separate finding, not a model to copy.

PLACEMENT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN - two rules, both load-bearing:

  (a) AFTER the already-closed / terminal early return.
      An already-closed close performs no I/O, so it has no budget to spend, and
      it must not begin failing merely because the request that once owned the
      transport was cancelled. Cleanup legitimately runs after cancellation.

  (b) BEFORE the write-side commit - before any `self.closed = true`,
      `mark_closed()`, or `writer.take()`.
      A refusal must leave the object UNTOUCHED and retryable. This is not a new
      invention: close_and_reap_child (stdio.rs:730-747) already documents
      exactly this contract in prose.

Rename the parameter `_cx` -> `cx` in the same edit; the debt metric
(`grep -c '_cx: &Cx'`) must move by exactly one per conversion.

=============================================================================
STEP 2 - THE FIVE-CASE PROOF, AND WHAT EACH CASE RULES OUT
=============================================================================

External-consumer target under the crate's tests/ directory. Construct through
the public constructor, call the public method, assert only public observables.

  1. LIVE CONTROL         <close>_under_a_live_context_commits_and_flushes
     Rules out: an unconditional failure masquerading as budget awareness.
     Without it, a refusal proves nothing - the close might refuse always.

  2. CANCELLATION REFUSAL <close>_under_a_cancelled_context_refuses_before_the_flush
     Rules out: no budget observation at all. Differs from case 1 in EXACTLY ONE
     BIT, which is what makes it a controlled experiment.

  3. EXPIRY AS TIMEOUT    <close>_under_an_expired_deadline_refuses_as_timeout
     Rules out: a guard that only reads the cancellation flag. No cancellation
     bit is set here; only the deadline has passed. This case is the one that
     fails if someone "simplifies" the checkpoint to is_cancel_requested, and it
     proves Timeout is reported distinctly from Cancelled.

  4. REFUSAL IS RETRYABLE <close>_refusal_leaves_the_<thing>_closable
     Rules out: a budget-aware close that WEDGES the object on every cancelled
     caller - which would be worse than the unbudgeted close it replaced. After
     a refusal, a fresh budget must still close, and must perform the one flush
     the refusal skipped.

  5. IDEMPOTENT UNDER CANCELLATION
     <close>_stays_idempotent_under_a_cancelled_context
     Rules out: terminal close starting to fail for callers whose original
     request was cancelled. Proves rule (a) of the placement above.

THE LOAD-BEARING OBSERVABLE IS THE FLUSH COUNT, NOT THE RETURNED ERROR. A
recording writer that counts flushes separates "refused BEFORE doing blocking
I/O" from "did the I/O and reported an error afterwards". The returned error
alone cannot distinguish those, and only the first is the capability.

Fixtures:
    fn cancelled_context() -> Cx {
        let cx = Cx::for_testing();
        cx.set_cancel_requested(true);
        cx
    }
    fn expired_context() -> Cx {
        Cx::for_testing_with_budget(
            asupersync::Budget::new().with_deadline(asupersync::Time::ZERO))
    }

Worked reference: crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/stdio_close_budget.rs (two
closes x five cases) and tests/sse_close_budget.rs.

=============================================================================
STEP 3 - CHECKS BEFORE COMMITTING. Each of these caught a real defect.
=============================================================================

  FEATURE GATING. If the type under test is behind a cfg feature, so is its
  `Cx` import - and a helper you add UNGATED will fail to resolve and break the
  LIB for every downstream crate. Read the lines ABOVE an import, not just the
  import. Gate a new helper to match its only caller. Gate the test file with an
  inner `#![cfg(feature = "...")]` as leg_http_01_a.rs does, NOT a [[test]]
  required-features entry, which makes the target invisible to a no-flags runner.
  State in the module doc that a default-feature run reports zero tests there -
  that is absence of the capability, not evidence about it.

  BLAST RADIUS. Existing tests may close under a cancelled context and expect
  Ok. Scan for cancelled/expired context bindings and closes WITHIN THE SAME
  function body, brace- or indent-matched. VERIFY THE INSTRUMENT: print the
  count of overlapping function ranges; if it is not zero the scan is garbage. A
  line-window heuristic crossed test boundaries three separate times here and
  once reported 42 false hits where the true answer was zero.

  NAME COLLISIONS IN THE SWEEP. `send_closes` (a counter field) matches a
  `send_close` pattern; a probe double inside a cfg(test) module looks like
  production. Both inflated my candidate list before correction.

=============================================================================
STANDING BOUNDARY
=============================================================================

    3 of 77 closes consume a caller budget, each proving both spend limbs, all
    blocking-I/O, all through public observables at bound revisions:
        StdioTransport::close  - default reach
        StdioSendHalf::close   - default reach
        SseWriter::close       - legacy-feature only
    56 remain `_cx`, of which 50 are INERT and correctly final, 4 are test
    doubles, and 2 are genuine candidates.
    Shutdown is still NOT cancellable: the checkpoint refuses BEFORE blocking and
    cannot preempt a flush already in progress. That is B-10, and B-10 is
    upstream.

comments.text:
OWNER DECISION, NOT STALLED WORK: AsyncStdioTransport::close needs a test seam.
OrangePike, 2026-09-17. Filed for the orchestrator to carry alongside bd-ak9t6
(caller admission) and the leg_http_01_b limit conflict.

THE ITEM. transport/src/stdio.rs:1563, AsyncStdioTransport::close, is the last
production close that performs blocking I/O and does not consume the caller's
budget. It is the ONLY remaining item of its kind: 0 convertible, 9 correctly
final, 45 test doubles (comment 2450).

WHY IT IS NOT CONVERSION WORK. Every other conversion was: add a checkpoint, add
a five-case external proof, done by a pane inside its own lease. This one cannot
be, and the reason is structural rather than difficult:

  * `writer: AsyncStdout` is a CONCRETE field. No recording writer can be
    injected, so the flush-count observable - the load-bearing one, the only
    thing that separates "refused BEFORE blocking I/O" from "did the I/O and
    reported an error afterwards" - does not exist for this type.
  * It exposes no `is_closed()`, so the terminal-state observable is absent too.
  * `new()` takes no arguments and binds the PROCESS's real stdin/stdout.
    `AsyncStdout::flush_unchecked` acquires a process-wide STDOUT_LOCK
    (async_io.rs:273). A live-control row would flush the test harness's own
    stdout and serialize against every other test in the binary.
  * It has never been exercised by an external test; the single internal test
    that constructs it covers read failures, not close.

Consequence: only 2 of the 5 template cases are expressible, and only from inside
the crate - which cannot prove shipped behaviour (PL-3). Converting it anyway
would move the `_cx` metric from 55 to 54 while producing NO external evidence.
That is signature plumbing wearing a capability's clothes, and the boundary on
this bead exists to deny exactly that. NOT DONE, deliberately.

WHAT THE DECISION IS. Whether to add a test seam to a production type - an
injectable writer on AsyncStdioTransport, or an equivalent constructor - purely
so its close can be proven. That trades a widened production API for provable
cancellation behaviour on the process stdio path. It is a public-surface change
on a shipped type and belongs to an owner, not to a pane converting closes.

Three outcomes are all defensible and none is mine to pick:
  (a) add the seam, then convert and prove it in the five-case shape;
  (b) decline the seam and record AsyncStdioTransport::close as permanently
      unprovable, leaving `_cx` correct-by-documentation rather than by proof;
  (c) decide the process stdio path does not need budget-aware close at all,
      because the caller that owns the process is the CLI boundary.

THE FRAMING THAT MATTERS: this is FND-04 work correctly STOPPING at a boundary
only an owner can move, not FND-04 work stalling. The close-budget surface is
otherwise complete. Nothing is blocked on a pane.

comments.text:
TEMPLATE v2: MAKING AN OPERATION CONSUME THE CALLER'S BUDGET, AND PROVING IT.
OrangePike, 2026-09-17. SUPERSEDES comment 2441. The change in v2 is section 3 -
a per-case validity gate, after %24 showed the shape can manufacture false
assertions when applied without it.

=============================================================================
0. THE SCOPING GATE - MOST OPERATIONS MUST NOT BE CONVERTED
=============================================================================
Convert only if the body performs BLOCKING I/O - flush, write_all, a socket
shutdown, a protocol close frame. If it closes a channel, sets a flag, or clears
a buffer, leave `_cx` alone: a checkpoint buys nothing there and costs something
real, because it makes cleanup paths that legitimately run AFTER cancellation
begin to fail. Nine production closes in this workspace are correctly final for
exactly this reason.

Check the SUBJECT is production, not a test double. Three signals must agree:
file location, enclosing-impl indentation, and `#[cfg(test)]` on BOTH the impl
line and the type definition. A gated item at column 0 defeats an indentation
test - four websocket closes nearly entered a conversion list that way.

=============================================================================
1. THE SOURCE CHANGE
=============================================================================
Canonical helper, http_checkpoint at transport/src/http.rs:4319; stdio_checkpoint
(stdio.rs:76) and sse_checkpoint (sse.rs) are identical twins:

    cx.checkpoint().map_err(|error| {
        use asupersync::{CancelKind, error::ErrorKind};
        match cx.cancel_reason().map(|reason| reason.kind) {
            Some(CancelKind::Deadline | CancelKind::Timeout) => TransportError::Timeout,
            Some(_) => TransportError::Cancelled,
            None => match error.kind() {
                ErrorKind::DeadlineExceeded | ErrorKind::CancelTimeout => TransportError::Timeout,
                ErrorKind::Cancelled
                | ErrorKind::PollQuotaExhausted
                | ErrorKind::CostQuotaExhausted => TransportError::Cancelled,
                _ => TransportError::Cancelled,
            },
        }
    })

DO NOT use `cx.is_cancel_requested()`. It reads the explicit cancellation bit
only, so a caller whose DEADLINE expired walks straight into the blocking I/O.

PLACEMENT, two rules, both load-bearing:
  (a) AFTER the terminal / already-done early return. That path performs no I/O,
      has no budget to spend, and must not start failing because the request that
      once owned the object was cancelled.
  (b) BEFORE the write-side commit - before any `closed = true`, `mark_closed()`,
      or `writer.take()`. A refusal must leave the object UNTOUCHED and retryable.

Rename `_cx` -> `cx` in the same edit. The debt metric
(`grep -c '_cx: &Cx'`) must move by exactly one per conversion.

=============================================================================
2. THE FIVE CASES, AND WHAT EACH RULES OUT
=============================================================================
External-consumer target under tests/. Public constructor, public method, public
observables only.

  1. LIVE CONTROL - commits and performs the I/O exactly once.
     Rules out: an unconditional failure masquerading as budget awareness.
  2. CANCELLATION REFUSAL - differs from case 1 in EXACTLY ONE BIT.
     Rules out: no budget observation at all.
  3. EXPIRY AS TIMEOUT - deadline passed, cancellation bit never set.
     Rules out: a guard that reads only the cancellation flag. Fails if someone
     "simplifies" the checkpoint to is_cancel_requested.
  4. REFUSAL IS RETRYABLE - after a refusal, a fresh budget still succeeds and
     performs the one operation the refusal skipped.
     Rules out: a budget-aware path that WEDGES the object on every cancelled
     caller - worse than the unbudgeted version it replaced.
  5. IDEMPOTENT UNDER CANCELLATION - a second call on a terminal object stays Ok
     and performs no second operation.
     Rules out: terminal cleanup starting to fail for cancelled callers.

THE LOAD-BEARING OBSERVABLE IS THE OPERATION COUNT, NOT THE RETURNED ERROR. A
recording sink that counts flushes/writes separates "refused BEFORE doing the
I/O" from "did the I/O and reported an error afterwards". The returned error
alone cannot distinguish those, and only the first is the capability.

    fn cancelled_context() -> Cx {
        let cx = Cx::for_testing(); cx.set_cancel_requested(true); cx
    }
    fn expired_context() -> Cx {
        Cx::for_testing_with_budget(
            asupersync::Budget::new().with_deadline(asupersync::Time::ZERO))
    }

Worked references: tests/stdio_close_budget.rs (two subjects x five cases) and
tests/sse_close_budget.rs.

=============================================================================
3. *** THE VALIDITY GATE - NEW IN v2, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION ***
=============================================================================
EVERY CASE MUST BE CHECKED AS TRUE OF THE SUBJECT BEFORE IT IS ASSERTED. The five
cases are not a checklist to satisfy; they are claims, and a claim that is false
of the subject is a manufactured assertion no matter how green it runs.

  CASE 5 REQUIRES IDEMPOTENCY BY CONTRACT. It is valid for `close`, whose
  contract is terminal-and-idempotent. It is NOT valid for an operation that is
  not idempotent. %24 correctly DECLINED case 5 for HTTP-03.15/.16 because
  `request_json` is not idempotent, and asserting it would have CONTRADICTED
  .16's no-retry claim. Two green rows asserting opposite contracts is worse than
  one missing row.

  CASE 4 REQUIRES RETRY TO BE PERMITTED. Where a refusal is defined as terminal,
  "still usable after refusal" is false by design. Assert the terminal behaviour
  instead, and say so.

  CASE 3 REQUIRES THE GUARD TO DISTINGUISH LIMBS. Only meaningful where the
  checkpoint maps deadline and cancellation to different errors. Against a guard
  that cannot tell them apart, the row is vacuous - and that vacuity is itself
  the finding worth reporting.

  CASE 1 REQUIRES THE COMMIT PATH TO BE OBSERVABLE WITHOUT SIDE EFFECTS ON THE
  HARNESS. AsyncStdioTransport::close fails this: its live-control row would
  flush the test process's own stdout under a process-wide lock. When the control
  is not expressible, the set is not expressible, and the honest answer is to
  record the subject as unprovable rather than ship two of five and imply five.

WHEN A CASE IS INVALID, DROP IT AND SAY WHY IN THE TEST MODULE. A four-case proof
with a written reason is stronger evidence than a five-case proof containing one
false claim. Do not reshape the subject to fit the template.

=============================================================================
4. CHECKS BEFORE COMMITTING - each caught a real defect here
=============================================================================
  FEATURE GATING. If the subject is behind a cfg feature, so is its `Cx` import.
  A helper added UNGATED breaks the LIB for every downstream crate. Read the
  lines ABOVE an import, not just the import. Gate the test file with an inner
  `#![cfg(feature = ...)]` as leg_http_01_a.rs does, NOT a [[test]]
  required-features entry, which makes the target invisible to a no-flags runner.
  Say in the module doc that a default run reports zero tests there - that is
  absence of the capability, not evidence about it.

  BLAST RADIUS. Existing tests may perform the operation under a cancelled
  context and expect Ok. Scan for tainted contexts and calls WITHIN THE SAME
  function body, brace- or indent-matched, and PRINT THE OVERLAPPING-RANGE COUNT:
  if it is not zero the scan is garbage. A line-window heuristic crossed test
  boundaries three times here and once reported 42 false hits against a true
  answer of zero.

  CLASSIFICATION IS PROVISIONAL UNTIL THE BODIES ARE READ. On this bead an I/O
  regex missed `close_with_frame`; brace-matched cfg(test) ranges broke on a
  52,962-line file; indentation ignored attribute gating. Three counts, three
  wrong, each caught only by reading the code.

You wrote: "narrowing a deny population is a validator relaxation on AGENTS.md's

    fnd_04_runtime_conformance.rs:309
      let is_module = source[probe..].starts_with("mod ")

A `mod X;` DECLARATION satisfies that probe identically to a `mod X { .. }`
definition. So matching_brace_end starts from a SEMICOLON and matches the next
balanced brace group -- a real shipped item -- and everything from the attribute
through it is deleted from the scanned text. Confirmed. And fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs
carries #[cfg(test)] at line 54 of 3211, so a forward swallow from there is
exactly the shape that produces your 2,149-line figure.

TWO DEFECTS IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS IN ONE INSTRUMENT. 234 of 278 denied sites
are test code (false positives, true production population 44), AND 2,173 lines
are invisible to denial at all (false negatives). An instrument that only
over-reports gets caught the first time someone reads the list. An instrument
that over-reports AND under-reports looks plausible from either end, because each
error class supplies cover for the other.

owns the runtime bridge B-07 exists to police. The blind spot is centred on the
subject.

title: FND-04: remove hidden-runtime HTTP client constructors
description: Remove every public fastmcp-client and fastmcp-rust HTTP connection constructor that enters fastmcp_core::block_on or obtains Cx::current internally. Retain the existing async caller-owned-Cx path as the sole public HTTP connection surface. Production implementation and public compile evidence stay on this issue; this issue earns no aggregate FND-04 or MCP capability credit.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance:
- Public fastmcp_client ClientBuilder HTTP connection surfaces require an explicit &Cx and contain no fastmcp_core::block_on/Cx::current bridge.

Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### FND-04 — Complete runtime-managed `Cx` migration

Outcome:

Remove production dependence on asupersync `test-internals`.

Reason:

Modern HTTP streams, subscriptions, MRTR, and Tasks all require real
structured cancellation.

Implementation:

- Execute existing Beads issue `bd-63l5`.
- Make library lifecycle entry points async and `&Cx`-first:
  server serve/accept, client connect and request execution, router
  dispatch, middleware, handlers, transport close/flush, and proxy
  forwarding all execute under the caller's capability context.
- Permit only application-owned binary boundaries, including the
  FastMCP CLI, to construct and drive one explicit top-level runtime.
  Do not expose a library convenience that creates or re-enters a
  runtime.
- Make macro expansions return or await handler futures directly;
  they must never wrap async handlers in nested `block_on`.
- Make production `block_on`, out-of-band `Cx` creation, reentrant
  runtime entry, and the current global private runtime
  non-exported and test-only or remove their production reachability
  without deleting files.
- First prove a public asupersync API that derives an owned child
  region from ambient `&Cx`, with independent cancellation plus
  close/drain/quiescence semantics.
- Treat pinned `Cx::scope()` and `Cx::scope_with_budget()` as
  same-region APIs, not child-region ownership.
- If the public primitive is absent—as it is in audited workspace
  baseline `0.3.9` and current registry candidate `0.3.10`—open and
  resolve a concrete upstream prerequisite and keep FND-04, HTTP-01,
  and all dependent work blocked. Do not emulate it with
  `ServerRequestRegion`, an unregistered root task, or a private
  runtime.
- Resolve the eventual runtime to an exact `=version` or immutable Git
  revision, update FND-01's checksum/feature evidence, and reject a
  floating Cargo range before relying on any new primitive.
- After that prerequisite is pinned, derive every request child
  region from the ambient `Cx`.
- Pass `&Cx` into transport shutdown and flush paths.
- Obtain task contexts inside supervised spawned closures.
- Gate testing-only context construction appropriately.
- Remove `test-internals` from the production dependency feature set.
- Prove that independent requests do not share cancellation state.
- Inventory every production `std::sync::{Mutex, RwLock, Condvar,
  mpsc}`, blocking filesystem call, synchronous Redis operation,
  private thread, and other blocking call site.
- Permit a standard-library lock only for a proven non-async,
  bounded critical section that cannot span an await; document every
  exception in a machine-checked allowlist.
- Use asupersync cancel-aware locks, channels, and structured scopes
  for async paths, and prove no lock guard crosses an await.
- Route an unavoidable blocking filesystem, crypto, or synchronous
  Redis operation through one bounded, consumer-owned, `Cx`-aware
  blocking facility with admission control.
- Admit only a blocking job class whose underlying OS/library
  operation has a proven finite connect/acquire/read/write/compute
  bound below its remaining budget and a documented late-completion
  reconciliation path. A worker occupied by an indefinitely hung
  synchronous call is an unsupported configuration, not acceptable
  merely because concurrency is bounded.
- Require that capability to report absence of a real blocking pool;
  do not accept the asupersync zero-blocking-thread inline fallback.
  Current candidate `0.3.10` still executes `Cx::spawn_blocking`
  inline when its pool handle is absent. If the runtime cannot provide
  a detectable non-inline facility, resolve it as a second explicit
  upstream prerequisite rather than spawning a private executor.
- Prove a public, cancel-aware asupersync path for this process's own
  stdin/stdout and spawned-child stdin/stdout that works without
  `test-internals`, a private I/O-driver handle, a per-stream thread,
  or a blocking Windows pipe fallback. At audited asupersync `0.3.9`
  and candidate `0.3.10`, only spawned-child adapters are publicly
  exposed for this need and relevant Windows pipe paths can block;
  treat the missing cross-platform own-process/child capability as a
  third explicit upstream prerequisite.
- Correct the root `Cargo.toml` comment that currently presents
  `scope_with_budget` as a child-region solution.
- Reconcile an operation that finishes after caller cancellation:
  discard pure reads, and for mutations verify or compensate the
  durable outcome before reporting the four-valued result.
- Add one core `ProcessGenerationGuard` installed before any runtime,
  process-local key, nonce/cursor/MRTR store, quota registry, or
  supervisor becomes usable. Every process-local protector, handle
  store, limiter, and supervisor operation verifies the creator process
  identity/generation and fails closed after Unix `fork()` or any
  detectable process-generation change. A child must `exec` or build a
  wholly new FastMCP instance; it cannot redraw a key while retaining
  inherited ciphertext, continuations, counters, work, or quota state.
  Raw fork-without-exec after initialization is unsupported.
- State the non-detectable boundary explicitly: process-memory
  checkpoint/restore, CRIU, VM snapshot, or container clone can
  duplicate a PID, key, nonce sequence, and one-use state. No
  process-local profile claims safety under such cloning. A deployment
  permitting live-memory snapshots must disable ephemeral protected/
  continuation state or use a conforming persistent provider with an
  external rollback-and-clone-resistant epoch before support is
  enabled.

Acceptance:

- Production code calls no testing-only `Cx` constructor.
- Cancelling one request does not cancel a sibling request.
- Server shutdown cancels all owned request regions.
- Transport close participates in the caller's budget.
- No feature constructs a private runtime.
- Public library lifecycle signatures cannot hide a runtime or
  synchronous block.
- Production macros, router, client, server, middleware, proxy, and
  transport paths contain no `block_on` or runtime re-entry.
- No blocking lock guard survives an await and no unbounded blocking
  work occupies an executor worker.
- Every permitted standard lock or blocking call has a reviewed,
  bounded allowlist entry.
- Cancellation races with stateful blocking work produce a verified
  or compensated outcome, never an ambiguous success.
- The pinned runtime provides a tested ambient child-region owner and

  filesystem/platform termination-guarantee rejection, and bounded
  shutdown/worker-recovery tests.

  the three prerequisite observations above; a later version can

  probes on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including a proof that Windows
  pipe polling never blocks an executor worker.

  parent/child sequence/replay/quota/supervisor use, fork+exec, PID/
  generation simulation, and fail-closed inherited-state tests.

  external-epoch positive scenario evidence; never pretend a PID check

  Current candidate `0.3.10` still executes `Cx::spawn_blocking`
  inline when its pool handle is absent. If the runtime cannot provide
  a detectable non-inline facility, resolve it as a second explicit
  upstream prerequisite rather than spawning a private executor.
- Prove a public, cancel-aware asupersync path for this process's own
  stdin/stdout and spawned-child stdin/stdout that works without
  `test-internals`, a private I/O-driver handle, a per-stream thread,
  or a blocking Windows pipe fallback. At audited asupersync `0.3.9`
  and candidate `0.3.10`, only spawned-child adapters are publicly
  exposed for this need and relevant Windows pipe paths can block;
  treat the missing cross-platform own-process/child capability as a
  third explicit upstream prerequisite.
- Correct the root `Cargo.toml` comment that currently presents
  `scope_with_budget` as a child-region solution.
- Reconcile an operation that finishes after caller cancellation:
  discard pure reads, and for mutations verify or compensate the
  durable outcome before reporting the four-valued result.
- Add one core `ProcessGenerationGuard` installed before any runtime,
  process-local key, nonce/cursor/MRTR store, quota registry, or
  supervisor becomes usable. Every process-local protector, handle
  store, limiter, and supervisor operation verifies the creator process
  identity/generation and fails closed after Unix `fork()` or any
  detectable process-generation change. A child must `exec` or build a
  wholly new FastMCP instance; it cannot redraw a key while retaining
  inherited ciphertext, continuations, counters, work, or quota state.
  Raw fork-without-exec after initialization is unsupported.
- State the non-detectable boundary explicitly: process-memory
  checkpoint/restore, CRIU, VM snapshot, or container clone can
  duplicate a PID, key, nonce sequence, and one-use state. No
  process-local profile claims safety under such cloning. A deployment
  permitting live-memory snapshots must disable ephemeral protected/
  continuation state or use a conforming persistent provider with an
  external rollback-and-clone-resistant epoch before support is
  enabled.

Acceptance:

- Production code calls no testing-only `Cx` constructor.
- Cancelling one request does not cancel a sibling request.
- Server shutdown cancels all owned request regions.
- Transport close participates in the caller's budget.
- No feature constructs a private runtime.
- Public library lifecycle signatures cannot hide a runtime or
  synchronous block.
- Production macros, router, client, server, middleware, proxy, and
  transport paths contain no `block_on` or runtime re-entry.
- No blocking lock guard survives an await and no unbounded blocking
  work occupies an executor worker.
- Every permitted standard lock or blocking call has a reviewed,
  bounded allowlist entry.
- Cancellation races with stateful blocking work produce a verified
  or compensated outcome, never an ambiguous success.
- The pinned runtime provides a tested ambient child-region owner and
  a detectable, admitted non-inline blocking capability plus
  cancel-aware cross-platform process stdio before this package can
  close.
- Those primitives are available from an exactly pinned registry
  release (or separately published reviewed fork) consumable by
  `cargo package`; a Git/workspace patch proves only the interim spike.
- A post-initialization fork cannot use inherited runtime, crypto,
  continuation, quota, or supervisor state; snapshot-capable
  deployments cannot claim process-local replay/nonce safety.

Tests:

- LabRuntime sibling-cancellation test.
- Shutdown tree test.
- Transport-close budget test.
- Task-supervisor ownership test.
- Dependency-feature assertion.
- Exact runtime-pin and lockfile-regeneration drift assertions.
- Public-signature compile tests.
- Macro/router/client reentrant-runtime negative tests.
- Static production deny inventory for `block_on`, out-of-band `Cx`
  construction, private runtimes/threads, guards-across-await, and
  unallowlisted blocking primitives.
- LabRuntime lock cancellation, fairness, starvation, and shutdown
  tests.
- Bounded blocking-facility admission, cancellation-before-start,
  cancellation-after-mutation, reconciliation, and saturation tests.
- Hung endpoint/half-open socket, slow reply, pool exhaustion,
  filesystem/platform termination-guarantee rejection, and bounded
  shutdown/worker-recovery tests.
- Compile/runtime probes proving `Cx::scope()` is not mistaken for a
  child region and that a zero-thread blocking configuration is
  rejected before serving.
- Candidate-drift probes pinned to the recorded `0.3.10` archive prove
  the three prerequisite observations above; a later version can
  change the result only through a new checksum-qualified API/runtime/
  packaging audit, never version-number inference.
- Own-process and child-process stdin/stdout cancellation/backpressure
  probes on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including a proof that Windows
  pipe polling never blocks an executor worker.
- Fork before/after encryption and continuation minting, concurrent
  parent/child sequence/replay/quota/supervisor use, fork+exec, PID/
  generation simulation, and fail-closed inherited-state tests.
- Live-memory/CRIU/VM/container snapshot-clone configuration denial and
  external-epoch positive scenario evidence; never pretend a PID check
  detects a same-PID memory clone.

Tracker mapping:

- FND-04 is the plan identity for existing Beads issue `bd-63l5`.
- Update and reuse that issue; do not create a second FND-04 issue.

Dependencies:

- FND-02.

comments.text:
## PRODUCER CONSTRAINTS READ OUT OF MY OWN AC AND SENT TO THE PRODUCERS — before the manifest exists

MagentaSummit. Not claiming, not starting, not pre-writing. WildMountain asked me
to flag early if the upstream work would change my verification criteria; this is
the reverse direction and the more urgent one — **my criteria constrain what the
producers must record, and after `fnd-04-integration-manifest-v1` exists those
constraints are expensive.**

Sent to MagentaOsprey (`ymje`) and RoseStream (`jmi7`), cc WildMountain/OrangePike.

### THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS ITEM 4, NOT ITEM 1

Item 1 names three targets. **Item 4 is what makes them load-bearing:** the
one-variable negative *"changes only the recorded WINDOWS target receipt digest."*

If the manifest carries a single linux row there is no Windows digest, the negative
has nothing to mutate, `FND-04-V-04 three-target-receipt-matrix` (item 2) is
unsatisfiable, and **this bead is structurally dead** — discoverable only when
someone sits down to write the test.

### AND THE FLEET CANNOT EXECUTE THREE TARGETS

Every RCH run reported tonight is `linux-x86_64`; WildMountain's platform detector
discriminates 197 vs 188 and observed 197. So darwin/windows *execution* is not
available to any producer.

### THE TRAP, NAMED BEFORE ANYONE WALKS INTO IT

**Synthesising three rows from one measurement makes my own planted negative
vacuous.** A Windows digest copied from linux, or a placeholder, means item 4
mutates a value that was never a Windows measurement — the negative passes while
proving nothing. **An unsatisfiable acceptance item can be escalated; a vacuous one
cannot be detected.** I would rather have the first.

### FND-01 HAS THE PATTERN THAT WORKS

It never claims cross-platform execution. It binds targets by **declaration plus CI
matrix rows** — `dependency-verification.toml:832` (rust-toolchain raw bytes),
`:852` `production_graph_targets`, `:1610`/`:1719` a five-row release matrix where
each row carries a distinct runner identity AND a distinct artifact path. **Rows of
that shape are genuinely different objects**, so a one-variable negative can
distinguish them without anyone claiming the evaluator ran on Windows.

### THREE SMALLER FIELDS FROM ITEM 1, EASY TO MISS

    profile           must be recorded as `core-candidate`   -- compared, not inferred
    product features  must EXCLUDE asupersync/test-internals -- an enabled flag fails my predicate
    consumer          must be `bd-63l5`                      -- a wrong value fails a field
                                                                nobody would think to check

### STATUS UNCHANGED

`open`, blocked on `ymje`, not claimed. Item 12 bars V from mutating anything and
item 11 reserves closure to the batch-verification orchestrator; reading my own
acceptance items and telling the producers what they imply is neither. If any
constraint above conflicts with what integration actually needs, that is a
bead-text question for WildMountain, and it is far cheaper now than after the
manifest is frozen.
