    at HEAD   blob e367c6f7d2d872f7bde1f8bd13a052639263331a

Six commits have touched that file since. THREE OF THE SIX ARE TealSalmon'S OWN,
landing at 10:23 on 2026-09-16 -- nearly FOUR HOURS AFTER their 06:30 boundary
comment. The author invalidated their own anchor the same morning and the
boundary has sat unqualified ever since.

WHY THIS IS A CREDIT DEFECT AND NOT JUST STALENESS. A blob-anchored boundary is
a STRONGER claim than an unanchored one: it says "this is exactly what I
inspected". That precision is what makes it reusable, and it is also what makes
it wrong the moment the blob moves. An unanchored note would have aged into
vagueness; this one aged into a specific false statement, while still carrying
the authority of its precision. 0/13 AC ticks on this bead rest partly on it.

NOT AN ACCUSATION OF BAD FAITH. The most likely story is ordinary: write the
boundary in the morning, keep working, land three more commits by mid-morning,
never revisit the note. That is a process gap, not dishonesty -- nothing in the
tracker tells an author their own anchor died. Which is exactly why it needs
recording rather than quiet re-keying.

INSTRUCTION TO THE NEW OWNER, already sent: do NOT silently re-key the boundary
to the current blob as your first act. Re-keying erases the evidence that it was
ever stale, and the staleness is the finding. Record it, then work the bead.

GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: a blob- or revision-anchored claim needs re-validation
before anyone ticks an item from it, and the author is the least likely person
to notice it has died. This is the same class as my own stamping "HEAD e991963b"
on measurements taken hours after HEAD moved to 13156804 -- I resolved a
revision once and reused it, exactly as this boundary was written once and
reused. Both are cheap to prevent and invisible once made.

RoseStream. CODE, not a finding. commit:32e8a1ea. Plus the credit defect recorded as instructed.

=== 1. THE CREDIT DEFECT, recorded and not re-keyed by hand ===
TealSalmon's demonstrated-vs-inspected boundary (comment 2348, 06:30 on 2026-09-16) is anchored
to blob 7287afb54bd158803c0ea042c6781bc64a02b890. HEAD is e367c6f7 (now 14fa9b42 after my

    dfca221f  per-case ceiling instead of per-test  TealSalmon, this bead
    dd4845b1  isolate cancellation domains          TealSalmon, this bead
    9b79bb20 / 02bdc294 / 791fce43                  RoseStream, bd-4khs9 lint work

An author invalidated their own evidence anchor within the same session and did not re-key it.
That is the defect: not that the classification is wrong, but that it is bound to bytes that
stopped existing before the author stopped working. Nothing downstream can tell which state of
the file the 26 rows were classified against.

=== 2. THE SHALLOWEST ACTUAL ITEM, IMPLEMENTED ===
AC item 5: "its SHA-256 digest is captured before integration. Reordering, an omitted
group/floor/negative, or DIGEST MISMATCH fails this slice."

Reordering and omission were already enforced, by MANIFEST_GROUP_ORDER and the row-shape checks.
DIGEST MISMATCH WAS NOT, AND STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT BE. assert_shipped_manifest() ended with:

    let recomputed = sha256_bounded(text.as_bytes(), 64 * 1024)...;
    assert_eq!(http_03_b_manifest_digest().as_bytes(), recomputed.as_bytes());

`text` IS HTTP_03_B_EVALUATOR_MANIFEST_V1, and http_03_b_manifest_digest() is sha256 over that
same constant. sha256(X) == sha256(X). Edit the manifest and both sides move together and the
equality still holds. The one failure mode the item names could not occur.

FIXED in commit:32e8a1ea by adding a frozen 64-character lowercase hex anchor. I kept the
original assertion and documented what it DOES prove - that the two published halves agree on
the byte bound - rather than deleting it as useless.

WHY A FROZEN DIGEST IS SOUND HERE AND WOULD NOT BE ELSEWHERE: the manifest is a literal concat!
of fixed strings, no env! and no build-time interpolation, so its bytes move only when a human
edits them. That is exactly the event the item wants to fail on. A digest over anything
build-derived would rot instead of guard.

THE VALUE IS COMPILER-VERIFIED. I did not trust my own reading of the literal: I fed
http_executor.rs:227-243 through rustc's own concat!, printed the bytes and hashed them.
892 bytes, 23fb2f9a13130aea1c80891371979494a116ac978fd78d987de1152b18af7135. Two independent
source parses had already agreed; the compiler settled it. rustc is unshimmed, so this cost no
lane.

AND IT CAN FAIL - demonstrated, not asserted:
    unmodified              23fb2f9a...
    two case rows swapped   3ff98298...
    floor=5 -> floor=6      4d824ad6...
    HTTP-03.25 omitted      2785b809...

=== 3. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MOVE ===
Item 5 is now enforceable rather than vacuous. I am NOT ticking it: the item also requires the
digest be "captured before integration", which is an integration-time act, and the test has not
been run. The other 12 items are untouched and the 7 dependency blockers are unchanged
(ahet.4 .13 .16 .20 .24 .26 .35).

NOT RUN. If you want a gate run on http_03_b_positive / http_03_b_planted_negative, say so and
I will take the dispatch - the new assertion is the only thing that changed and it is pure
computation over a compile-time constant, so a red would be unambiguous.

Reservation on the file was checked clear before writing, held for the edit, released after.

comments.text:
RoseStream, assignee. CLAIM COMMENT (rulings #31, condition 1). NO CODE YET. Three of the ruled conditions conflict with what the code and the contract say, so this asks for a re-ruling before any edit. Static read; nothing ticked.

R4 RE-BIND at HEAD fc1fc14a:
- crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_executor.rs c7a9c64e (contains a4a9ead7 and b3c2fd18)
- crates/fastmcp-client/tests/http_03_b.rs 275c0348

=== NAMES (condition 1) ===
- Variant: `ModernHttpExecutorError::DispatchUncertain(ClientError)`. "The exchange failed after request bytes may have reached the peer and before any response head was admitted; the peer may have acted on it."
- Classification type:
  `pub enum ModernHttpRetryClassification { NotDispatched, DispatchUncertain }`
  with
  `ModernHttpExecutorError::retry_classification(&self) -> Option<ModernHttpRetryClassification>`
  - Some(NotDispatched) for Transport(_);
  - Some(DispatchUncertain) for DispatchUncertain(_);
  - None for every other variant, including Cancelled and Timeout, which keep their own typed outcomes.
- Anchor: a new `request_bytes_sent` flag on ModernHttpIo, set on the first poll_write that returns Ready(Ok(n > 0)).
  - This is NOT the existing `committed_at`, which marks the FULL flush.
  - ahet.37 :33-35 says "If bytes MAY HAVE REACHED the original endpoint, return an explicit uncertain-dispatch outcome", and its test list names "partially sent request uncertain-dispatch tests". A partial write is therefore uncertain too.
  - TLS handshake bytes never pass through ModernHttpIo (it wraps the already-connected ClientIo), so the flag counts request bytes only.
- Site: map_transport_error in execute_with_optional_cancellation only, i.e. a pre-head exchange failure.
  - Body-read failures after an admitted head are untouched (for example the http_03_a truncated-body row at :1717).
  - So are the caller-deadline paths (HttpResponseDeadline::check :706, check_modern_http_context), which build Transport(DeadlineExceeded) directly.

=== CONFLICT 1: condition 3 is unsatisfiable as ruled. The error is mine: I proposed it in 5602 ===
"The only changed variable is whether the peer consumed the body; assert pre-dispatch."
- A peer that closes WITHOUT reading a small body is invisible to the client. The ping body's write completes into the kernel send buffer, so bytes may have reached the peer, and the correct class is DispatchUncertain, not NotDispatched.
- A row asserting NotDispatched there would either be red, or be made green by bending the product. That is RH-1 and RH-12 territory.
- The client can only observe whether ANY request byte was accepted by the transport.
- PROPOSED REPLACEMENT: a near-identical planted row where the peer NEVER ACCEPTS. The listener is bound, its address taken, then dropped, so connect is refused.
  - The single changed variable is whether any request byte could be written.
  - Assert Transport(ClientError::ConnectError(_)) with retry_classification() == Some(NotDispatched), and that no connection was made.
  - .16's negative asserts DispatchUncertain(_) with Some(DispatchUncertain) and no reconnect.

=== CONFLICT 2: condition 2 ("every other negative byte-unchanged") vs negative_15 ===
- negative_15_stalled_peer (tests/http_03_b.rs:966) declares its variable as "the peer stalls past the response deadline".
- But post() uses ModernHttpExecutor::new(), whose default policy is 30 s idle / 120 s absolute (lib.rs:1500-1501). The peer sleeps only 1.5 s and then closes.
- So today the row passes through a pre-head EOF landing in its `Transport(_)` arm. It is not exercising a deadline at all.
- Under the new variant, that EOF (after the body was written) is DispatchUncertain, and the row's `Err(other) => panic!` arm fires. The row must change, which condition 2 forbids.
- The honest repair makes the row exercise what it names: a short RequestTimeoutPolicy on its executor, so Timeout(_) fires before the peer closes. The EOF path is then covered by .16, where it belongs.
- This is a separate defect in the existing negative (declared variable is not the exercised one). It is on my bead, and I ask to fix it in the same commit, declared.

=== CONFLICT 3: an outside-stream consumer's behaviour moves (condition 2, "no existing variant changes meaning") ===
- http_auth/rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:347 `recovery_http_interruption` classifies Transport(Io | HttpError(Io)) as Interrupted. That drives MRTR continuation recovery. It is also used by client_credentials/.../recovery.rs:356 and managed/tasks/watch/recovery.rs:324.
- Authorship: 35050222+Dicklesworthstone, 5d211aae / 5290820d.
- Post-write pre-head IO failures in those flows would become DispatchUncertain(Io) and stop being recoverable. That is a behaviour change there.
- (i) RECOMMENDED for this bead: extend recovery_http_interruption to match DispatchUncertain with the same inner kinds. Recovery behaviour is then byte-for-byte preserved: a 1-line add in an outside-stream file, declared.
- (ii) Separately, and NOT in this bead: whether MRTR recovery after an uncertain dispatch violates ahet.37's "Do not auto-retry non-idempotent calls after uncertain disconnect". That is a question for its owner, which I file rather than decide.

=== SCOPE IF RE-RULED ===
- Files: crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_executor.rs, crates/fastmcp-client/tests/http_03_b.rs, and under (i) crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/rpc/interaction/recovery.rs.
- Condition 4: the B manifest row for .16 is `floor=4`. The new planted row is added inside the .16 case set as an extra assertion, so the row count and the manifest digest are UNCHANGED. If the re-ruling wants the row as a separate manifest case instead, that is a digest change, and I will declare it first.

D3. ModernHttpExecutor::with_timeout_policy changed from private to `pub` with #[must_use] (additive public API). It was the only means of making negative_15 exercise what it names without changing its entrypoint. positive_15 moved onto the same policy so the pair still differs in one variable. REVIEW OF b2a254bc (RoseStream), AGAINST PRE-REGISTRATION d49bff44 (mail 36412). SilentSquirrel, reviewer (R64).
Static only: no build, no slot, NOTHING TICKED. Bound to fix blobs http_executor.rs c6211092, tests/http_03_b.rs 99f1ab11,
rpc/interaction/recovery.rs e1dc9016; base 4fd55eab (c7a9c64e / 275c0348 / de1eb638). HEAD carries the same three fix blobs.
VERDICT: NO CODE DEFECT FOUND. 14 items MET statically, 1 met except one clause, and 2 FINDINGS (both about proof, not code).

P1 NAMES: MET. DispatchUncertain(ClientError), pub enum ModernHttpRetryClassification { NotDispatched, DispatchUncertain },
   and pub const fn retry_classification(&self) -> Option<_>, all as ruled in #32.
P2 ANCHOR: MET. The flag is set only on Ready(Ok(n > 0)) from the inner write, and never from committed_at. ModernHttpIo does not
   override poll_write_vectored, and asupersync 0.5.0's default (io/write.rs) calls self.poll_write, i.e. the wrapper's. So every
   write path sets it. The flag counts bytes the INNER io accepted (TLS plaintext buffered counts), which errs toward "uncertain".
P3 SITE / ADDITIVITY: MET. ModernHttpIo has 1 construction, inside execute_native_modern_request, whose only caller is
   execute_with_optional_cancellation; DispatchUncertain is built only in map_modern_exchange_error at its 2 pre-head map_errs.
   map_transport_error's body and its legacy callers (:8431, :8594) are unchanged, and no variant's definition changes.
   Noted: post-byte malformed-HEAD errors (HttpError kinds) also move to DispatchUncertain. That fits the doc ("before any
   response head was ADMITTED"), and every consumer handles it (P8, P14).
P4 NEW CONDITION 3: (a) MET: the mid-exchange row asserts DispatchUncertain(_) AND Some(DispatchUncertain) via expect_err, and
   keeps assert_no_further_connection. (c) MET: same Peer::bind, ping_request and post() (default executor); Peer owns its
   TcpListener, so drop really closes it. (b) MET EXCEPT ONE CLAUSE I pre-registered: Transport(ConnectError(_)) and
   Some(NotDispatched) are asserted, but "no connection was made" is NOT separately asserted. The typed ConnectError is the only
   evidence, and with the listener dropped nothing is left to count. Recorded as written, not upgraded.
   Port-reuse race: if another binder takes the freed port and accepts, the row goes RED; it can never go falsely green.
   Low probability.
P5 negative_15: MET statically. The accepted outcomes shrink from {Timeout, Transport, ResponseBodyReadFailed} to {Timeout}.
   Policy is 1 s idle / 5 s absolute against a 1.5 s stall, and the declared variable is unchanged. The ordering argument checks
   out: deadline.poll runs BEFORE and AFTER exchange.poll in both select arms, so an expired deadline beats a simultaneous EOF,
   and expiry returns Timeout(source) (HttpResponseDeadline::check). The per-case ceiling is asupersync::time::timeout_at
   (20 s), not a Cx budget, so no caller deadline can pre-empt it with Transport(DeadlineExceeded). The verdict is RUN-ONLY (C1).
   positive_15 now answers under a 1 s idle; under worker load that is a possible RED, never a false green.
P6: MET. Hunks are the imports, 2 new helpers, positive_15, negative_15, negative_16 and the new planted fn. No other case fn.
P7 CONDITION 4: MET. No hunk touches http_executor.rs's manifest block (:231-243 area) or the test's case tables.
P8 CONFLICT 3 (i): MET for the diff. The added arm has inner kinds Io | HttpError(Io), identical to Transport's. Consumer census
   RE-DERIVED at the fix: recovery_http_interruption has exactly 3 production callers (rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:345,
   client_credentials/rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:356, managed/tasks/watch/recovery.rs:324), and all are preserved. The other
   production matches on the enum (client_credentials recovery.rs:351, tasks/submission.rs:437, tasks/subscriptions.rs:165
   and :193, subscriptions/watch.rs:306) wildcard old Transport and new DispatchUncertain to the SAME result. Unchanged.
P9 D1: MET. Every constructor of the 8 kinds in asupersync 0.5.0 h1/http_client.rs is URL parse, connect, TLS handshake,
   proxy/SOCKS, or pool admission. The one post-request InvalidUrl source is redirect following, and native_http_client() sets
   RedirectPolicy::None and RetryPolicy::None, and is used by BOTH the modern and the legacy (:8416, :8462) paths. The set is
   strictly narrower than 5603's "every Transport(_)". A TLS error after the handshake surfaces as Io, which returns None.
P10 D2: MET, and judged FORCED, not a tightening. asupersync's drive_with_budget_deadline raises DeadlineExceeded FROM THE
   EXCHANGE on the caller's Cx budget, the same bound HttpResponseDeadline::check reports as Transport(DeadlineExceeded).
   Without D2, one cause would be typed two ways depending on which poll saw it first. It returns None.
   Observation only: Timeout(_) is always after commit, yet it classifies as None rather than DispatchUncertain. That is
   conservative (None = "cannot prove"), not unsafe, and as ruled.
P11 D3: MET, forced relative to the row's entrypoint. At base, ModernHttpExecutor's only pub items were new() and execute().
   The one public deadline route is ClientBuilder::request_timeout_policy (used by http_03_integration.rs), which is a
   DIFFERENT entrypoint. Moving both .15 rows onto it would change what they exercise.
   Correction to 5608's framing: the B manifest row does not currently freeze the entrypoint (criterion 5's fields are absent),
   so the constraint is "keep the entrypoint", not the digest.
   RequestTimeoutPolicy::new is pub, and with_timeout_policy already had production callers (:6052, :6109), so it is a real
   API, not a test-only production path.
P12 TYPED: MET. Every changed or new negative asserts a variant; no is_err() remains in them.
P13: MET. No todo!/unimplemented!/placeholder, and no new cfg(test) production code.
P14: MET statically. The only exhaustive match on the enum is Display, which is updated. The compile is RUN-ONLY.
P15 MY STAKE: NONE. b3c2fd18's hunks sit at c7a9c64e :4461-5465; b2a254bc's sit at :10-3214 and :9619.

=== FINDING F1 (test coverage): the recovery adaptation has NO test, and the one existing positive now models the wrong value ===
No test in either recovery test module names DispatchUncertain (git grep at the fix: 0).
rpc/interaction/recovery/tests.rs:118 asserts recoverable_transport_failure(... Transport(HttpError(Io(UnexpectedEof)))).
In production, a post-write, pre-head EOF, the scenario that line stands for, now arrives as DispatchUncertain(HttpError(Io(..))).
So the old line still passes, but it no longer exercises the value the adapted arm exists to catch.
A positive for DispatchUncertain(Io | HttpError(Io)), plus a near-identical DispatchUncertain(HttpError(BadHeader)) negative,
would cost two lines and turn "proven only by reading" into a unit proof.

=== FINDING F2: 5608's "KNOWN GAP" premise is stale. The recovery tests look cardable ===
Gate chain at the fix: lib.rs pub mod http_auth -> rpc -> interaction -> recovery -> #[cfg(test)] mod tests. The client_credentials
twin is the same (http_auth -> discovery -> client_credentials -> rpc -> interaction -> recovery). There is NO feature gate on
either chain, and no file-scope #![cfg].
The lib-test E0308 of rulings #12 sat under feature `tasks` (5489): the default-feature --lib build compiles none of those sites.
bd-0hayt's fix then made the tasks lib test compile at 27891066 (card #4, 5593). So "the lib cfg(test) module does not compile" no
longer holds as a reason. Whether it compiles AT b2a254bc is unproven (outside churn, R4) and is a card question.
Suggested C5: cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-client --lib -- http_auth::rpc::interaction::recovery
http_auth::discovery::client_credentials::rpc::interaction::recovery (default features).
A compile failure there would be a new finding, not 3r1d's.

Contacts are as declared in 36412. I tick nothing. -- SilentSquirrel

title: HTTP-03 integration: join capability slices through public entrypoints
description:
Executable integration leaf for formal package HTTP-03.

Owned capability slice: join modern HTTP client request, response, and stream executor with probe isolation, authentication, redirects, cancellation, and endpoint partitioning through shipped public entrypoints and state.

Named consumer: HTTP-03 independent verification child.

Real implementation and its real tests are one Bead; placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, and follow-up laundering are forbidden.

Capability credit is limited to this named HTTP-03 slice and is granted only after central batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must record exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No broad crate glob is an ownership card.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:HTTP-03:I:BEGIN -->
Canonical I role for HTTP-03.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical I slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public HTTP-03 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### HTTP-03 — Implement the modern HTTP client

Outcome:

Send compliant requests and consume JSON or SSE responses.

Reason:

FastMCP Rust currently has no complete Streamable HTTP client.

Implementation:

- Use asupersync native HTTP primitives.
- Send one POST per request or registered extension notification.
- Emit exact `Content-Type: application/json` for every JSON-RPC POST
  and omit `Content-Encoding` on the uncoded request body.
  Emit exact `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; do not use a
  wildcard, media parameter, or zero-quality range to stand in for
  either required response media type.
- Emit canonical lowercase `Accept-Encoding: identity`, disable
  automatic decompression, and accept response `Content-Encoding` only
  when absent or, after ignoring up to LIMIT-01's bounded leading/
  interior/trailing empty RFC 9110 list elements, one semantic bare
  token compares ASCII-case-insensitively equal to `identity`. Reject a
  present all-empty value, empty-element saturation, parameters,
  duplicate field lines, multiple semantic codings, and every other
  coding before consuming response bytes.
- Disable automatic redirects and reject every 3xx response for MCP
  JSON/SSE POSTs. Never rewrite/replay a method or body, forward
  credentials/cookies/custom routing headers to a new location, or
  silently change canonical resource, era, authorization, or cache
  partition. If bytes may have reached the original endpoint, return
  an explicit uncertain-dispatch outcome rather than retrying a
  side-effecting request.
- Attach Authorization only from the auth provider and only when the
  complete configured target is the same admitted HTTPS
  `CanonicalResourceId` bound to that credential. Never attach or
  redirect a bearer credential to remote or loopback HTTP; a local
  server behind a terminator is addressed by its public HTTPS URL from
  the client side.
- Send `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, and method-specific
  `Mcp-Name` on JSON-RPC requests.
- For a registered extension notification, emit only the headers its
  frozen transport descriptor declares; do not add core request
  routing headers. Emit the exact EXT-01 current-message
  `NotificationActivationProofDescriptor` payload for that
  notification—self-contained typed proof or a currently live
  negotiated-owner handle—and never infer support from discovery,
  another request, or connection state.
- Parse immediate JSON results.
- Parse request-scoped SSE notifications and final result.
- Run response JSON/SSE messages through PRT-01 with explicit client-
  ingress direction. Malformed server bytes or an invalid
  server-direction envelope fail and close only the owning POST/
  response stream with a bounded peer-protocol outcome; never POST or
  otherwise emit a JSON-RPC parse/invalid-request response back to the
  server.
- Use a bounded incremental SSE parser.
- Freeze its accepted dialect to the WHATWG event-stream algorithm,
  independent of input chunking. First run one streaming Encoding
  Standard `UTF-8 decode` decoder in replacement mode across all
  chunks, stripping at most one leading UTF-8 BOM exactly as that
  algorithm prescribes; never apply strict UTF-8-or-fail decoding.
  Then recognize CRLF, bare LF, and bare CR line endings; split a field
  at the first colon; remove at most one immediately following U+0020;
  and treat `data`, `data:`, and `data: ` exactly as the standard
  prescribes. Append one LF per data field, join multiple data lines in
  order, and remove exactly the final appended LF at dispatch.
- A blank line with no `data` field and comment lines beginning with
  `:` produce no MCP message. A blank line after one or more empty data
  fields dispatches an empty data payload and therefore fails the MCP
  JSON decoder; it is not conflated with a no-data event. At EOF,
  discard an unterminated pending event per the event-stream algorithm
  and then report missing-final-response/stream termination as
  applicable; do not synthesize a blank line.
- Parse `event`, `id`, `retry`, and unknown fields for bounded line
  framing but give them no MCP routing, retry, resumption, or cache
  semantics. In particular, never retain an ID, send
  `Last-Event-ID`, alter reconnect delay from `retry`, or select a
  decoder from `event`; the assembled data alone must be exactly one
  bounded JSON-RPC object of an allowed direction. This deliberately
  accepts standard producers that include inert fields without
  reviving removed modern SSE state.
- Enforce maximum line, event, and message sizes.
- Parse exactly one bounded response `Content-Type` without sniffing.
  For a successful request response, accept only the case-insensitive
  essence `application/json` or `text/event-stream`, with no parameter
  except an optional single case-insensitive `charset=utf-8`; reject
  duplicates, malformed syntax, conflicting/unknown parameters, and
  every other type before body decoding. A status-specific non-success
  path parses a JSON-RPC error body only when its content type is
  admitted as JSON; otherwise it remains an opaque bounded HTTP
  failure. For `application/json`, feed the bounded response body
  bytes directly into PRT-01's strict UTF-8/raw-JSON admission; reject
  a BOM or malformed sequence and never repair it. Only for
  `text/event-stream`, count raw-byte and decoded-text budgets
  independently against the same line/event ceilings and feed bytes
  through Section 5.17's streaming replacement decoder before line/
  event and assembled-data JSON admission. Media-type selection can
  never select one byte policy and parse with the other.
- Apply CLT-01's per-request idle and absolute response budgets from
  send commit through terminal response. Reset idle only for an exact,
  valid matching progress notification when that request's policy
  enables it; no SSE comment, log, unrelated event, or byte arrival
  resets request idleness, and absolute time never moves.
- Bound comment-only keepalive traffic.
- Keep no event-ID or resumption state.
- Tie caller cancellation to response close.
- Classify HTTP and JSON-RPC failures separately.
- Implement modern-first era detection from CLT-02.
- For an uncached `ClientEndpointInstanceKey`, send CLT-02's exact
  one-shot `server/discover` probe before any application method and
  never replay that HTTP request. Derive the key from the trusted full
  configured endpoint path/permitted query, security partition,
  transport profile, and configuration generation; use origin only
  for the independent same-origin/credential/network checks.
- Preserve redacted wire diagnostics.
- Do not auto-retry non-idempotent calls after uncertain disconnect.
- Never POST `notifications/cancelled` in modern HTTP; close the
  response stream.
- On either timeout, atomically stop waiting and close/cancel the
  request's response stream exactly once. The server-side disconnect is
  the cancellation signal. Never send a JSON-RPC cancellation message,
  replay the POST, or deliver a final result that loses the first-
  terminal race. Apply the same close rule to subscription idle/
  absolute expiry.
- Reject an independent server JSON-RPC request inside SSE.
- Restrict initialize-era legacy downgrade to Section 5.9's exact
  isolated-first-probe 400-body classification rule. Do not interpret
  404/405 as this adapter; those statuses participate only in the
  excluded deprecated HTTP+SSE GET fallback.
- Do not downgrade on authentication errors, rate limits, 5xx,
  network errors, or timeouts.
- Permit any further deprecated-transport fallback only if a separately
  supported profile explicitly implements it; this plan does not.

Acceptance:

- The client works with JSON and SSE server choices.
- Every outbound modern POST explicitly advertises both response media
  types with positive implicit quality and carries JSON content type.
- Request-scoped progress reaches the correct caller.
- Closing a cancelled call closes the response stream.
- Idle/absolute timeout closes only the owning response stream,
  returns one typed timeout, and never extends beyond the hard
  absolute deadline despite progress.
- An uncertain disconnect returns a retry classification, not a silent
  retry.
- Tokens never appear in protocol parameters or logs.
- Bearer credentials are never sent to a cleartext `http:` MCP
  endpoint, including localhost or loopback literals; an admitted
  protected target uses `https:`.
- Oversized, malformed, or endless SSE fails within configured bounds.
- SSE parsing is chunk-boundary invariant and its BOM, line-ending,
  replacement-decoding, field, dispatch, EOF, and inert-field behavior
  is fixed rather than delegated to an implementation-dependent
  event-source library.
- Immediate JSON is strict UTF-8/BOM-rejecting and cannot inherit the
  SSE replacement decoder.
- HTTP era classification is side-effect-free: its only pre-
  classification MCP method is `server/discover`, and the probe is
  never replayed.
- Every emitted extension notification carries its descriptor's
  current-message activation proof; no stale request/discovery/
  connection fact is serialized or treated as support.

Tests:

- Real-socket JSON response.
- Real-socket SSE response.
- Direct `application/json` valid UTF-8 positive plus leading/midstream
  BOM and malformed UTF-8 negatives, including a would-be valid JSON
  string only after replacement; contrast the same malformed bytes in
  SSE `data` becoming an ordinary U+FFFD inside a valid assembled JSON
  string.
- Interleaved progress and final result.
- Cancellation close.
- Virtual-time idle/absolute/progress-reset tests and same-tick
  timeout/final-result/disconnect races, proving exactly one stream
  close, one local outcome, no cancellation POST, no retry, and no
  effect on a concurrent response stream; repeat for
  `subscriptions/listen`.
- Authentication header redaction.
- HTTPS bearer-target capture and remote/localhost/IPv4-loopback/
  IPv6-loopback HTTP no-send tests; a configured local server behind a
  terminator is contacted only through its public HTTPS endpoint.
- Exact outbound Content-Type/Accept capture plus a nonconforming
  `Accept` construction negative proving the public builder cannot
  weaken either required media range.
- Version fallback.
- Uncertain non-idempotent disconnect.
- Exact decoded-message `N`, canonical `data: ` line `N+8`, event
  `N+10`, and one-byte-over boundaries under LF and CRLF; multiline
  inserted-newline accounting, 4,096/65,536 line-count boundaries,
  encoded-event headroom, oversized line/event/message, and fragmented
  prefix/delimiter cases. Enqueue/stream one maximum 9/36 MiB encoded
  event successfully, reject the event/queue N+1 case, and prove fixed
  queue/global active-memory charges remain separate.
- Byte-by-byte and every-split-point goldens for initial BOM/no-BOM/
  midstream-BOM, CR/LF/CRLF, `data`/`data:`/`data: ` and multi-data
  joining/trailing-LF removal, comments, blank no-data events, empty-
  data invalid JSON, unknown fields, inert `event`/`id`/`retry`, NUL/
  malformed UTF-8, final blank line, and EOF without a blank line.
  Cover malformed sequences wholly within a chunk and across every
  split, replacement outside JSON causing rejection, and replacement
  inside a valid JSON string surviving exactly as U+FFFD. Exercise
  N/N+1 raw-octet and replacement-expanded decoded-text bounds and
  prove both reservations and the fixed decoder prefix are released
  on failure/cancellation. Prove
  `id`/`retry` create no retained state/reconnect behavior and every
  dispatched nonempty payload admits exactly one JSON-RPC object,
  never concatenated JSON or an independent server request.
- Comment flood.
- SSE-only replacement-mode malformed-UTF-8 and post-replacement JSON-
  admission tests, plus a decoder-dispatch differential proving direct
  JSON never enters that path.
- Wrong response content type.
- Malformed server JSON and malformed/invalid-direction SSE message
  tests with concurrent independent POSTs; assert no response-back or
  reverse request, only the owning execution fails/closes, and sibling
  streams/waiters remain unaffected.
- Response Content-Type exact/case/UTF-8-charset positives and absent/
  duplicate/malformed/unknown-parameter/non-UTF-8/JSON-suffix/
  sniffing negatives across success JSON, success SSE, and
  status-specific error bodies.
- Absent and lowercase/uppercase/mixed-case singleton `identity`
  response positives plus bounded leading/interior/trailing empty list
  elements; present-all-empty, empty-element N/N+1, parameterized,
  compressed/multiple-semantic-coding/mislabeled/truncated response
  rejection with proof that no auto-decompression occurred.
- Endless response without final result.
- Independent server-request rejection.
- No-downgrade status/error matrix.
- First-request wire capture proving the exact one-shot
  `server/discover` body/headers, no pre-classification application
  RPC, no fallback replay, and fresh construction/ID after a completed
  authorization flow.
- Extension-notification capture for both self-contained and
  negotiated-owner proof descriptors, plus absent/expired/wrong-owner/
  stale-prior-request/discovery-only/connection-reuse negatives that
  emit no notification.
- Same-origin `/mcp-a` and `/mcp-b` endpoint-instance tests with
  different eras/discovery payloads; permitted-query, security-
  partition, transport-profile, and configuration-generation changes;
  canonical host/default-port equivalence; and proof that no
  origin-keyed cache entry crosses either request route.
- 301/302/303/307/308 same/cross-origin rejection, no method/body
  replay, credential/header non-forwarding, redirect-loop/DNS-
  rebinding location, and partially sent request
  uncertain-dispatch tests.

Dependencies:

- HTTP-02.
- FND-05.
- HDR-01.
- CLT-01.
- CLT-02.
- EXT-01.
- LIMIT-01.
<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:HTTP-03:I:END -->

SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-20. PRE-VERIFICATION FINDING from the orchestrator-authorised review-queue
identifier sweep. Source-only, zero slot. NO writes, NO AC ticks, NO close. Not my bead and I am
not proposing a repair -- recording what the identifiers resolve to so the reviewer does not
re-derive it.

=== THE FINDING: http_03_integration_positive CANNOT SATISFY THE ITEM THAT NAMES IT ===
It resolves, so it is not a phantom. It resolves to the wrong KIND of location.

    http_03_integration_positive          crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:13758   #[test]
    http_03_integration_planted_negative  crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:13854   #[test]

Both sit inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, which opens at crates/fastmcp/src/lib.rs:10660, and the
body of the positive begins:

    use super::client::{ BoundBearerCredential, HttpEndpointConfig, MODERN_MCP_ACCEPT, ... };

So it reaches the capability through `super::` -- crate internals -- from inside the library.

=== WHY THAT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN STYLISTIC ===
This bead's TITLE is "join capability slices through PUBLIC ENTRYPOINTS", and the unticked item
naming this ID reads:

    "[ ] `http_03_integration_positive` executes the PUBLIC MODERN CLIENT over real sockets using
     the exact http_03_evaluator_manifest_v1 inputs from implementation A and B; NO PRIVATE
     PARSER, mock-only transport, or reconstructed manifest may substitute."

And PL-3 is stated verbatim in a sibling's module doc
(crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_a_evidence_binding.rs:3-6):

    "External consumer of the packaged `fastmcp-rust` facade: it reaches the capability the way a
     downstream crate does, via `use fastmcp_rust::...`, NEVER THROUGH `use super` AND NEVER
     UNDER `cfg(test)` INSIDE THE LIBRARY (PL-3)."

The current definition violates both clauses of PL-3 -- it is under cfg(test) inside the library
AND it reaches through `use super`. A test in that position proves the capability through the
internal path, which is precisely what "no private parser may substitute" excludes.

=== WHAT I AM NOT SAYING ===
NOT that anyone did this wrong. The three AC items naming this identifier are all UNTICKED `[ ]`,
while the items naming the tests/ pair are TICKED `[x]`. So the outstanding work is already marked
outstanding. The finding is narrower and worth stating because it is not visible from the status:

    THE EXISTING DEFINITION CANNOT BECOME THE THING THAT COMPLETES THOSE ITEMS BY BEING FINISHED.
    It would have to MOVE. An unticked item whose named symbol does not yet exist is a different
    amount of work from an unticked item whose named symbol exists in a location the criterion
    structurally excludes -- the second invites "it is already written, just tick it".

=== THE SIBLING PAIR IS CORRECTLY PLACED, WHICH IS THE CONTRAST THAT MAKES THE POINT ===
    http_03_i_positive          crates/fastmcp/tests/http_03_integration.rs:3304   #[test]
    http_03_i_planted_negative  crates/fastmcp/tests/http_03_integration.rs:3381   #[test]
Both in tests/, external to the library, and both of their AC items are ticked. So this bead
already contains the right shape -- the question is only about the other pair.

=== EVERY IDENTIFIER IN THIS BEAD'S AC, RESOLVED ===
    http_03_integration_positive          occ=1   1 def   #[test]   src/lib.rs  <- above
    http_03_integration_planted_negative  occ=1   1 def   #[test]   src/lib.rs  <- above
    http_03_i_positive                    occ=1   1 def   #[test]   tests/      OK
    http_03_i_planted_negative            occ=3   1 def   #[test]   tests/      OK
    http_03_evaluator_manifest_v1         occ=10  0 defs  constant/tag, not a test ID

No phantoms. No duplicate definitions. No enclosing module qualification needed for the tests/
pair.

=== METHOD, AND ITS CONTROLS ===
Broad occurrence search, NOT `grep "fn <name>"` -- that predicate cannot see a constant or a byte
tag and produced a false zero for me earlier today. Kind is decided by whether the line directly
above the definition is `#[test]`.
    CONTROL known-positive  auth_00_a_positive         occ=2  1 def  #[test]
    CONTROL known-helper    auth_00_a_manifest_digest  occ=9  1 def  helper   <- 9 occurrences and

treats prose as a symbol -- the plain word `identifiers` returned 88 occurrences in an earlier

RoseStream. CODE LANDED: 17f13ce7. This closes the HTTP-03 family's vacuous-digest class - A in
f3998865, B in e4a7957a, integration here. Third and last instance.

TWO DEFECTS IN THIS TARGET, both of which pass unconditionally.

1. JoinedManifest::consume compared the producer's published accessor against a local
   recomputation:

       let a_digest = recompute_digest(HTTP_03_A_EVALUATOR_MANIFEST_V1);
       assert_eq!(http_03_a_manifest_digest().as_bytes(), a_digest.as_bytes(), ...);

   http_03_a_manifest_digest() IS sha256_bounded(HTTP_03_A_EVALUATOR_MANIFEST_V1, 64 * 1024).
   recompute_digest is the same call with the same bound on the same constant. So this is
   sha256(M) == sha256(M): true for every possible M, and it would stay true through any edit to
   the manifest. It proved SHA-256 is deterministic.

2. http_03_i_positive then asserted only:

       assert_eq!(receipt.a_digest.len(), 64);
       assert_eq!(receipt.b_digest.len(), 64);
       assert_ne!(receipt.a_digest, receipt.b_digest);

   Any two distinct hex strings satisfy that.

FIX: both are now compared against HTTP_03_A_MANIFEST_DIGEST_HEX and its B counterpart - the
only operand in the comparison the manifest cannot move. Published accessor, local
recomputation and rendered receipt are each bound to it. The original round trip is KEPT; it
documents the accessor contract, it simply could never fail alone. ".len(), 64" sites 2 -> 0.

WHY FREEZING IS SOUND HERE AND WOULD NOT BE ELSEWHERE. A frozen constant rots when it measures a
moving input. Neither manifest interpolates anything - both are concat! of fixed string literals
with no env!, no build stamp, nothing varying by host, feature or revision. I checked that
before freezing rather than after.

=== THE EVIDENCE ALSO RETROACTIVELY VALIDATES f3998865 AND e4a7957a ===
Those two commits froze these same constants derived by ONE method. One method is a belief. I
have now confirmed them by a second, independent of the crate under test:

  - the two concat! blocks were extracted VERBATIM from http_executor.rs into a standalone rustc
    program that writes out the bytes RUSTC ITSELF lexed;
  - hashlib.sha256 over those bytes gives
      A  9f68de2cfb47091ee101006cd67405a8764d6dd79781cf2abffabe1c54658818   755 bytes
      B  23fb2f9a13130aea1c80891371979494a116ac978fd78d987de1152b18af7135   892 bytes
    matching the constants frozen in all three test files;
  - rustc-lexed bytes vs my independent literal reconstruction: equal, 755 == 755 and
    892 == 892. So the reconstruction is not the weak link in the chain.

AND THE PRIMITIVE WAS READ, NOT ASSUMED. sha256_exact is Sha256::digest with no salt and no
length prefix; sha256_bounded adds only a length precondition; Sha256Digest::as_bytes borrows
the raw 32 bytes. Therefore render_digest(shipped accessor) is exactly
hashlib.sha256(manifest).hexdigest(). Had any of those three been otherwise, all three frozen
constants would have been wrong and every one of these tests would fail on its first real run.

title: Wire stored MCP HTTP config to the shipped modern client
description: McpConfig validates and retains HttpEndpointConfig, while its only production client constructor always resolves and spawns stdio. Wire the stored HTTP endpoint to the existing ClientProtocolPlan and ClientBuilder HTTP lifecycle without implicit transport selection. Preserve disabled and missing-server rejection before any connection effect. Named consumers: configuration-driven FastMCP clients and the HTTP-03 public integration entrypoint. Real implementation and its positive and near-identical negative tests are one executable Bead.
design: Construct the protocol plan only from already canonicalized HttpEndpointConfig fields, then connect through ClientBuilder with caller-owned Cx and identity fastmcp-client:{name}. Keep stdio client() unchanged and expose HTTP explicitly; no compatibility wrapper, implicit enum, or new runtime. Extend ConfigError only with typed missing-http, plan, and HTTP-client lifecycle variants. Exercise the public facade against the existing live e2e_modern_http server fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance IDs: HTTP-CONFIG-PLAN; HTTP-CONFIG-LIVE-POSITIVE; HTTP-CONFIG-DISABLED-ZERO-CONTACT; HTTP-CONFIG-TYPED-ERRORS. Add HttpEndpointConfig::protocol_plan returning the existing typed plan error and McpConfig::http_client taking caller-owned Cx plus server name and returning the shipped HttpClient. Missing server, disabled server, missing HTTP configuration, plan construction, and HTTP lifecycle failures remain typed and source chained. Exact test target: cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-rust --features testing-lab --test e2e_modern_http mcp_config_http_client_ -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture. Required test IDs equal passed test IDs: mcp_config_http_client_connects_live_modern_endpoint and mcp_config_http_client_disabled_is_zero_contact. Positive proof uses the existing real socket server, performs actual server/discover and a public list-tools call, proves Modern2026 selection and configured client identity, and uses a deliberately nonexistent command to prove no spawn. The negative differs by disabled true, returns ServerDisabled before effects, records zero requests, and proves serialized configuration unchanged. Proof class: public-surface live real-socket positive plus one-variable zero-contact planted negative. No ignored, filtered, mock-only, fixture-only, parser-only, aggregate HTTP-03, API-01, maturity, conformance, or release claim. Central batch verifier alone runs RCH, reports gates, and closes.
notes: Ownership/reservation card. Owned: crates/fastmcp-client/src/mcp_config.rs. Shared: crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_modern_http.rs. Integrator: bd-mcp-http-03-integration-vx7y. Agent Mail registration/reservation was unavailable after the bounded campaign attempts, so scope is coordinated through this explicit assignee/card and agents must recheck git status before edits/commit. Reservation: not recorded before coding; this is not retroactive lease credit. Any future edit requires a fresh matching Agent Mail reservation. Named consumers: configuration-driven clients and HTTP-03 integration. Gate: sole batch_verify PASS bound to exact revision after required IDs and reverse-dependent compile. Observed defect class: validated configuration retained but never consumed by a production HTTP constructor. Retirement: remove only when an owning configuration transport selector supersedes this explicit entrypoint with equal live and zero-contact proof. No-claim boundary: no aggregate HTTP-03/API-01/conformance/maturity/release claim; no stdio behavior change; no OAuth or legacy fallback claim.

Before claim, the assignee must record exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No broad crate glob is an ownership card.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:HTTP-03:V:BEGIN -->
Canonical V role for HTTP-03.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical V slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public HTTP-03 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### HTTP-03 — Implement the modern HTTP client

Outcome:

Send compliant requests and consume JSON or SSE responses.

Reason:

FastMCP Rust currently has no complete Streamable HTTP client.

Implementation:

- Use asupersync native HTTP primitives.
- Send one POST per request or registered extension notification.
- Emit exact `Content-Type: application/json` for every JSON-RPC POST
  and omit `Content-Encoding` on the uncoded request body.
  Emit exact `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; do not use a
  wildcard, media parameter, or zero-quality range to stand in for
  either required response media type.
- Emit canonical lowercase `Accept-Encoding: identity`, disable
  automatic decompression, and accept response `Content-Encoding` only
  when absent or, after ignoring up to LIMIT-01's bounded leading/
  interior/trailing empty RFC 9110 list elements, one semantic bare
  token compares ASCII-case-insensitively equal to `identity`. Reject a
  present all-empty value, empty-element saturation, parameters,
  duplicate field lines, multiple semantic codings, and every other
  coding before consuming response bytes.
- Disable automatic redirects and reject every 3xx response for MCP
  JSON/SSE POSTs. Never rewrite/replay a method or body, forward
  credentials/cookies/custom routing headers to a new location, or
  silently change canonical resource, era, authorization, or cache
  partition. If bytes may have reached the original endpoint, return
  an explicit uncertain-dispatch outcome rather than retrying a
  side-effecting request.
- Attach Authorization only from the auth provider and only when the
  complete configured target is the same admitted HTTPS
  `CanonicalResourceId` bound to that credential. Never attach or
  redirect a bearer credential to remote or loopback HTTP; a local
  server behind a terminator is addressed by its public HTTPS URL from
  the client side.
- Send `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, and method-specific
  `Mcp-Name` on JSON-RPC requests.
- For a registered extension notification, emit only the headers its
  frozen transport descriptor declares; do not add core request
  routing headers. Emit the exact EXT-01 current-message
  `NotificationActivationProofDescriptor` payload for that
  notification—self-contained typed proof or a currently live
  negotiated-owner handle—and never infer support from discovery,
  another request, or connection state.
- Parse immediate JSON results.
- Parse request-scoped SSE notifications and final result.
- Run response JSON/SSE messages through PRT-01 with explicit client-
  ingress direction. Malformed server bytes or an invalid
  server-direction envelope fail and close only the owning POST/
  response stream with a bounded peer-protocol outcome; never POST or
  otherwise emit a JSON-RPC parse/invalid-request response back to the
  server.
- Use a bounded incremental SSE parser.
- Freeze its accepted dialect to the WHATWG event-stream algorithm,
  independent of input chunking. First run one streaming Encoding
  Standard `UTF-8 decode` decoder in replacement mode across all
  chunks, stripping at most one leading UTF-8 BOM exactly as that
  algorithm prescribes; never apply strict UTF-8-or-fail decoding.
  Then recognize CRLF, bare LF, and bare CR line endings; split a field
  at the first colon; remove at most one immediately following U+0020;
  and treat `data`, `data:`, and `data: ` exactly as the standard
  prescribes. Append one LF per data field, join multiple data lines in
  order, and remove exactly the final appended LF at dispatch.
- A blank line with no `data` field and comment lines beginning with
  `:` produce no MCP message. A blank line after one or more empty data
  fields dispatches an empty data payload and therefore fails the MCP
  JSON decoder; it is not conflated with a no-data event. At EOF,
  discard an unterminated pending event per the event-stream algorithm
  and then report missing-final-response/stream termination as
  applicable; do not synthesize a blank line.
- Parse `event`, `id`, `retry`, and unknown fields for bounded line
  framing but give them no MCP routing, retry, resumption, or cache
  semantics. In particular, never retain an ID, send
  `Last-Event-ID`, alter reconnect delay from `retry`, or select a
  decoder from `event`; the assembled data alone must be exactly one
  bounded JSON-RPC object of an allowed direction. This deliberately
  accepts standard producers that include inert fields without
  reviving removed modern SSE state.
- Enforce maximum line, event, and message sizes.
- Parse exactly one bounded response `Content-Type` without sniffing.
  For a successful request response, accept only the case-insensitive
  essence `application/json` or `text/event-stream`, with no parameter
  except an optional single case-insensitive `charset=utf-8`; reject
  duplicates, malformed syntax, conflicting/unknown parameters, and
  every other type before body decoding. A status-specific non-success
  path parses a JSON-RPC error body only when its content type is
  admitted as JSON; otherwise it remains an opaque bounded HTTP
  failure. For `application/json`, feed the bounded response body
  bytes directly into PRT-01's strict UTF-8/raw-JSON admission; reject
  a BOM or malformed sequence and never repair it. Only for
  `text/event-stream`, count raw-byte and decoded-text budgets
  independently against the same line/event ceilings and feed bytes
  through Section 5.17's streaming replacement decoder before line/
  event and assembled-data JSON admission. Media-type selection can
  never select one byte policy and parse with the other.
- Apply CLT-01's per-request idle and absolute response budgets from
  send commit through terminal response. Reset idle only for an exact,
  valid matching progress notification when that request's policy
  enables it; no SSE comment, log, unrelated event, or byte arrival
  resets request idleness, and absolute time never moves.
- Bound comment-only keepalive traffic.
- Keep no event-ID or resumption state.
- Tie caller cancellation to response close.
- Classify HTTP and JSON-RPC failures separately.
- Implement modern-first era detection from CLT-02.
- For an uncached `ClientEndpointInstanceKey`, send CLT-02's exact
  one-shot `server/discover` probe before any application method and
  never replay that HTTP request. Derive the key from the trusted full
  configured endpoint path/permitted query, security partition,
  transport profile, and configuration generation; use origin only
  for the independent same-origin/credential/network checks.
- Preserve redacted wire diagnostics.
- Do not auto-retry non-idempotent calls after uncertain disconnect.
- Never POST `notifications/cancelled` in modern HTTP; close the
  response stream.
- On either timeout, atomically stop waiting and close/cancel the
  request's response stream exactly once. The server-side disconnect is
  the cancellation signal. Never send a JSON-RPC cancellation message,
  replay the POST, or deliver a final result that loses the first-
  terminal race. Apply the same close rule to subscription idle/
  absolute expiry.
- Reject an independent server JSON-RPC request inside SSE.
- Restrict initialize-era legacy downgrade to Section 5.9's exact
  isolated-first-probe 400-body classification rule. Do not interpret
  404/405 as this adapter; those statuses participate only in the
  excluded deprecated HTTP+SSE GET fallback.
- Do not downgrade on authentication errors, rate limits, 5xx,
  network errors, or timeouts.
- Permit any further deprecated-transport fallback only if a separately
  supported profile explicitly implements it; this plan does not.

Acceptance:

- The client works with JSON and SSE server choices.
- Every outbound modern POST explicitly advertises both response media
  types with positive implicit quality and carries JSON content type.
- Request-scoped progress reaches the correct caller.
- Closing a cancelled call closes the response stream.
- Idle/absolute timeout closes only the owning response stream,
  returns one typed timeout, and never extends beyond the hard
  absolute deadline despite progress.
- An uncertain disconnect returns a retry classification, not a silent
  retry.
- Tokens never appear in protocol parameters or logs.
- Bearer credentials are never sent to a cleartext `http:` MCP
  endpoint, including localhost or loopback literals; an admitted
  protected target uses `https:`.
- Oversized, malformed, or endless SSE fails within configured bounds.
- SSE parsing is chunk-boundary invariant and its BOM, line-ending,
  replacement-decoding, field, dispatch, EOF, and inert-field behavior
  is fixed rather than delegated to an implementation-dependent
  event-source library.
- Immediate JSON is strict UTF-8/BOM-rejecting and cannot inherit the
  SSE replacement decoder.
- HTTP era classification is side-effect-free: its only pre-
  classification MCP method is `server/discover`, and the probe is
  never replayed.
- Every emitted extension notification carries its descriptor's
  current-message activation proof; no stale request/discovery/
  connection fact is serialized or treated as support.

Tests:

- Real-socket JSON response.
- Real-socket SSE response.
- Direct `application/json` valid UTF-8 positive plus leading/midstream
  BOM and malformed UTF-8 negatives, including a would-be valid JSON
  string only after replacement; contrast the same malformed bytes in
  SSE `data` becoming an ordinary U+FFFD inside a valid assembled JSON
  string.
- Interleaved progress and final result.
- Cancellation close.
- Virtual-time idle/absolute/progress-reset tests and same-tick
  timeout/final-result/disconnect races, proving exactly one stream
  close, one local outcome, no cancellation POST, no retry, and no
  effect on a concurrent response stream; repeat for
  `subscriptions/listen`.
- Authentication header redaction.
- HTTPS bearer-target capture and remote/localhost/IPv4-loopback/
  IPv6-loopback HTTP no-send tests; a configured local server behind a
  terminator is contacted only through its public HTTPS endpoint.
- Exact outbound Content-Type/Accept capture plus a nonconforming
  `Accept` construction negative proving the public builder cannot
  weaken either required media range.
- Version fallback.
- Uncertain non-idempotent disconnect.
- Exact decoded-message `N`, canonical `data: ` line `N+8`, event
  `N+10`, and one-byte-over boundaries under LF and CRLF; multiline
  inserted-newline accounting, 4,096/65,536 line-count boundaries,
  encoded-event headroom, oversized line/event/message, and fragmented
  prefix/delimiter cases. Enqueue/stream one maximum 9/36 MiB encoded
  event successfully, reject the event/queue N+1 case, and prove fixed
  queue/global active-memory charges remain separate.
- Byte-by-byte and every-split-point goldens for initial BOM/no-BOM/
  midstream-BOM, CR/LF/CRLF, `data`/`data:`/`data: ` and multi-data
  joining/trailing-LF removal, comments, blank no-data events, empty-
  data invalid JSON, unknown fields, inert `event`/`id`/`retry`, NUL/
  malformed UTF-8, final blank line, and EOF without a blank line.
  Cover malformed sequences wholly within a chunk and across every
  split, replacement outside JSON causing rejection, and replacement
  inside a valid JSON string surviving exactly as U+FFFD. Exercise
  N/N+1 raw-octet and replacement-expanded decoded-text bounds and
  prove both reservations and the fixed decoder prefix are released
  on failure/cancellation. Prove
  `id`/`retry` create no retained state/reconnect behavior and every
  dispatched nonempty payload admits exactly one JSON-RPC object,
  never concatenated JSON or an independent server request.
- Comment flood.
- SSE-only replacement-mode malformed-UTF-8 and post-replacement JSON-
  admission tests, plus a decoder-dispatch differential proving direct
  JSON never enters that path.
- Wrong response content type.
- Malformed server JSON and malformed/invalid-direction SSE message
  tests with concurrent independent POSTs; assert no response-back or
  reverse request, only the owning execution fails/closes, and sibling
  streams/waiters remain unaffected.
- Response Content-Type exact/case/UTF-8-charset positives and absent/
  duplicate/malformed/unknown-parameter/non-UTF-8/JSON-suffix/
  sniffing negatives across success JSON, success SSE, and
  status-specific error bodies.
- Absent and lowercase/uppercase/mixed-case singleton `identity`
  response positives plus bounded leading/interior/trailing empty list
  elements; present-all-empty, empty-element N/N+1, parameterized,
  compressed/multiple-semantic-coding/mislabeled/truncated response
  rejection with proof that no auto-decompression occurred.
- Endless response without final result.
- Independent server-request rejection.
- No-downgrade status/error matrix.
- First-request wire capture proving the exact one-shot
  `server/discover` body/headers, no pre-classification application
  RPC, no fallback replay, and fresh construction/ID after a completed
  authorization flow.
- Extension-notification capture for both self-contained and
  negotiated-owner proof descriptors, plus absent/expired/wrong-owner/
  stale-prior-request/discovery-only/connection-reuse negatives that
  emit no notification.
- Same-origin `/mcp-a` and `/mcp-b` endpoint-instance tests with
  different eras/discovery payloads; permitted-query, security-
  partition, transport-profile, and configuration-generation changes;
  canonical host/default-port equivalence; and proof that no
  origin-keyed cache entry crosses either request route.
- 301/302/303/307/308 same/cross-origin rejection, no method/body
  replay, credential/header non-forwarding, redirect-loop/DNS-
  rebinding location, and partially sent request
  uncertain-dispatch tests.

### LEG-02 — Exact MCP 2024-11-05 server protocol and lifecycle adapter

Outcome:

- LEG-02 provides one transport-neutral server adapter for exact MCP
  2024-11-05 JSON-RPC protocol, lifecycle, capability state, messages, and
  errors.
- The adapter is constructed only with an explicit authenticated
  `LegacyPeerBinding` supplied by a transport consumer. LEG-NEG-01's
  legacy-stdio composition consumes it over STD-01's adapter-neutral
  process/framing substrate; LEG-HTTP-01 is the downstream consumer for
  the exact two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport.
- One binding owns one bounded lifecycle:
  `AwaitInitialize -> AwaitInitialized -> Operating -> Closed`.  Its
  negotiated protocol version, peer identity, capabilities, and pending
  operations cannot be inherited by another binding.

Reason:

- MCP 2024-11-05 initialization and connection-scoped capabilities are
  structurally different from a stateless request dispatcher.  Keeping the
  exact wire and lifecycle rules behind one adapter prevents accidental
  cross-protocol state sharing.
- The protocol adapter must be reusable by stdio and the later HTTP+SSE
  transport without parsing transport frames, choosing routes, or owning
  reconnection behavior.

Implementation:

- Admit an exact `initialize` request only in `AwaitInitialize`.  Validate
  the exact 2024-11-05 request version, client capabilities, client
  information, and bounded initialization parameters through LEG-01; return
  the exact 2024-11-05 initialized server version, server capabilities,
  server information, and optional instructions.  Freeze those admitted
  values before emitting the response.
- Move to `AwaitInitialized` only after a successful initialize response.
  Admit exactly `notifications/initialized` to enter `Operating`; reject
  duplicate, early, late, malformed, or mismatched lifecycle messages with
  the exact LEG-01 JSON-RPC error and without mutating negotiated state.
  Close is terminal and releases every adapter-owned reservation exactly once.
- In `Operating`, implement only the exact LEG-01-dispositioned 2024
  server surface: ping; tools, resources, prompts, and completion requests;
  resource subscribe/unsubscribe; client logging-level control; client
  cancellation/progress/message notifications; and server-to-client
  roots/list, sampling/createMessage, and ping requests when the negotiated
  capability permits them.  Preserve exact method direction, parameter
  shape, result shape, notification semantics, capability prerequisites, and
  JSON-RPC error mapping.
- Delegate ordinary tool/resource/prompt dispatch to SRV-01 only after the
  lifecycle and negotiated capability boundary is satisfied.  The adapter
  neither reimplements handler registration nor silently maps an unsupported
  2024 member to another method.
- Keep negotiated capabilities, request correlation, reverse requests,
  resource subscriptions, logging level, cancellation/progress records, and
  control queues in a bounded adapter state object keyed by the opaque
  `LegacyPeerBinding`, its authenticated owner/security partition, and a
  monotonically unique binding generation.  Binding identity alone never
  authorizes state access.

  LIMIT-01 before every lifecycle allocation, correlation insertion,
  subscription/control-queue growth, and reverse request; reserve before
  mutation and release on completion, cancellation, peer close, expiry, or
  shutdown.  Diagnostics are bounded, redacted, and non-oracular.

  shared domain values.  A rejected or unrepresentable value leaves the
  adapter state unchanged and uses the exact legacy error path.

### LEG-02 — Exact MCP 2024-11-05 server protocol and lifecycle adapter

Outcome:

- LEG-02 provides one transport-neutral server adapter for exact MCP
  2024-11-05 JSON-RPC protocol, lifecycle, capability state, messages, and
  errors.
- The adapter is constructed only with an explicit authenticated
  `LegacyPeerBinding` supplied by a transport consumer. LEG-NEG-01's
  legacy-stdio composition consumes it over STD-01's adapter-neutral
  process/framing substrate; LEG-HTTP-01 is the downstream consumer for
  the exact two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport.
- One binding owns one bounded lifecycle:
  `AwaitInitialize -> AwaitInitialized -> Operating -> Closed`.  Its
  negotiated protocol version, peer identity, capabilities, and pending
  operations cannot be inherited by another binding.

Reason:

- MCP 2024-11-05 initialization and connection-scoped capabilities are
  structurally different from a stateless request dispatcher.  Keeping the
  exact wire and lifecycle rules behind one adapter prevents accidental
  cross-protocol state sharing.
- The protocol adapter must be reusable by stdio and the later HTTP+SSE
  transport without parsing transport frames, choosing routes, or owning
  reconnection behavior.

Implementation:

- Admit an exact `initialize` request only in `AwaitInitialize`.  Validate
  the exact 2024-11-05 request version, client capabilities, client
  information, and bounded initialization parameters through LEG-01; return
  the exact 2024-11-05 initialized server version, server capabilities,
  server information, and optional instructions.  Freeze those admitted
  values before emitting the response.
- Move to `AwaitInitialized` only after a successful initialize response.
  Admit exactly `notifications/initialized` to enter `Operating`; reject
  duplicate, early, late, malformed, or mismatched lifecycle messages with
  the exact LEG-01 JSON-RPC error and without mutating negotiated state.
  Close is terminal and releases every adapter-owned reservation exactly once.
- In `Operating`, implement only the exact LEG-01-dispositioned 2024
  server surface: ping; tools, resources, prompts, and completion requests;
  resource subscribe/unsubscribe; client logging-level control; client
  cancellation/progress/message notifications; and server-to-client
  roots/list, sampling/createMessage, and ping requests when the negotiated
  capability permits them.  Preserve exact method direction, parameter
  shape, result shape, notification semantics, capability prerequisites, and
  JSON-RPC error mapping.
- Delegate ordinary tool/resource/prompt dispatch to SRV-01 only after the
  lifecycle and negotiated capability boundary is satisfied.  The adapter
  neither reimplements handler registration nor silently maps an unsupported
  2024 member to another method.
- Keep negotiated capabilities, request correlation, reverse requests,
  resource subscriptions, logging level, cancellation/progress records, and
  control queues in a bounded adapter state object keyed by the opaque
  `LegacyPeerBinding`, its authenticated owner/security partition, and a
  monotonically unique binding generation.  Binding identity alone never
  authorizes state access.
- Apply AUTH-00 before private operations and reverse requests.  Apply
  LIMIT-01 before every lifecycle allocation, correlation insertion,
  subscription/control-queue growth, and reverse request; reserve before
  mutation and release on completion, cancellation, peer close, expiry, or
  shutdown.  Diagnostics are bounded, redacted, and non-oracular.
- Use XPORT-01's total `lossless | legacy-owned | rejected` disposition for
  shared domain values.  A rejected or unrepresentable value leaves the
  adapter state unchanged and uses the exact legacy error path.
- Expose a transport-neutral inbound-message/outbound-message contract and
  close signal only.  The adapter parses neither HTTP requests nor SSE
  frames and does not bind URLs or own HTTP-level announcements.  LEG-HTTP-01
  later supplies the exact HTTP+SSE peer binding and independently owns its
  GET/POST framing, endpoint advertisement, reconnect handling, security,
  and teardown.
- LEG-NEG-01's stdio composition invokes the adapter through its explicitly
  selected legacy peer binding over STD-01's neutral process/framing
  substrate. STD-01 never selects, constructs, binds, or invokes this
  adapter. The adapter receives a preselected exact-2024 binding or is not
  constructed.

Tests:

- `leg_02_a_positive`: exercise the shipped adapter through LEG-NEG-01's
  public stdio composition over the real STD-01 substrate, with exact
  initialize, initialized notification, negotiated capabilities, legal
  operating requests, and exact success/error messages.
- `leg_02_a_planted_negative`: alter only one lifecycle or capability
  dimension and prove the exact typed rejection, no handler dispatch, and no
  negotiated-state mutation.
- `leg_02_b_positive` and `leg_02_b_planted_negative`: prove bounded
  reverse requests, roots, sampling, logging, subscriptions, cancellation,
  progress, owner isolation, close races, and exact-once reservation release;
  the planted negative differs only in the forbidden owner/capability/order

- `leg_02_integration_positive` and

a feature flag; extract the named *_positive / *_planted_negative IDs; resolve each ID to its
defining file by indexing every #[test] fn in the tree; map the file to its [[test]] target; flag
where that target declares required-features.

      bd-mcp-leg-02-a-h4l5                        legacy-2024-11-05      <- new
      bd-mcp-leg-02-b-kk21                        legacy-2024-11-05      <- new

      bd-pxy-leg-01-implementation-b-dmox         proxy-legacy           HazyTurtle's
      bd-pxy-leg-01-integration-integration-sn75  proxy-legacy           HazyTurtle's

explicit [[test]] required-features. It does NOT catch an ID hidden by a file-scope `#![cfg(..)]`
or by `#[cfg(feature = ..)]` on the test function inside an ungated target - which is the worse
mechanism, because nothing in Cargo.toml records it. A full answer needs that second pass.

The one file-scope cfg among them is `#![cfg(unix)]` on leg_neg_01_a.rs, which is a platform
qualification already declared in the file header, and the verification lane is Linux.

Not my beads, nothing claimed, nothing edited.

Canonical I role for LEG-02.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical I slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public LEG-02 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### LEG-02 — Exact MCP 2024-11-05 server protocol and lifecycle adapter

Outcome:

- LEG-02 provides one transport-neutral server adapter for exact MCP
  2024-11-05 JSON-RPC protocol, lifecycle, capability state, messages, and
  errors.
- The adapter is constructed only with an explicit authenticated
  `LegacyPeerBinding` supplied by a transport consumer. LEG-NEG-01's
  legacy-stdio composition consumes it over STD-01's adapter-neutral
  process/framing substrate; LEG-HTTP-01 is the downstream consumer for
  the exact two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport.
- One binding owns one bounded lifecycle:
  `AwaitInitialize -> AwaitInitialized -> Operating -> Closed`.  Its
  negotiated protocol version, peer identity, capabilities, and pending
  operations cannot be inherited by another binding.

Reason:

- MCP 2024-11-05 initialization and connection-scoped capabilities are
  structurally different from a stateless request dispatcher.  Keeping the
  exact wire and lifecycle rules behind one adapter prevents accidental
  cross-protocol state sharing.
- The protocol adapter must be reusable by stdio and the later HTTP+SSE
  transport without parsing transport frames, choosing routes, or owning
  reconnection behavior.

Implementation:

- Admit an exact `initialize` request only in `AwaitInitialize`.  Validate
  the exact 2024-11-05 request version, client capabilities, client
  information, and bounded initialization parameters through LEG-01; return
  the exact 2024-11-05 initialized server version, server capabilities,
  server information, and optional instructions.  Freeze those admitted
  values before emitting the response.
- Move to `AwaitInitialized` only after a successful initialize response.
  Admit exactly `notifications/initialized` to enter `Operating`; reject
  duplicate, early, late, malformed, or mismatched lifecycle messages with
  the exact LEG-01 JSON-RPC error and without mutating negotiated state.
  Close is terminal and releases every adapter-owned reservation exactly once.
- In `Operating`, implement only the exact LEG-01-dispositioned 2024
  server surface: ping; tools, resources, prompts, and completion requests;
  resource subscribe/unsubscribe; client logging-level control; client
  cancellation/progress/message notifications; and server-to-client
  roots/list, sampling/createMessage, and ping requests when the negotiated
  capability permits them.  Preserve exact method direction, parameter
  shape, result shape, notification semantics, capability prerequisites, and
  JSON-RPC error mapping.
- Delegate ordinary tool/resource/prompt dispatch to SRV-01 only after the
  lifecycle and negotiated capability boundary is satisfied.  The adapter
  neither reimplements handler registration nor silently maps an unsupported
  2024 member to another method.
- Keep negotiated capabilities, request correlation, reverse requests,
  resource subscriptions, logging level, cancellation/progress records, and
  control queues in a bounded adapter state object keyed by the opaque
  `LegacyPeerBinding`, its authenticated owner/security partition, and a
  monotonically unique binding generation.  Binding identity alone never
  authorizes state access.
- Apply AUTH-00 before private operations and reverse requests.  Apply
  LIMIT-01 before every lifecycle allocation, correlation insertion,
  subscription/control-queue growth, and reverse request; reserve before
  mutation and release on completion, cancellation, peer close, expiry, or
  shutdown.  Diagnostics are bounded, redacted, and non-oracular.
- Use XPORT-01's total `lossless | legacy-owned | rejected` disposition for
  shared domain values.  A rejected or unrepresentable value leaves the
  adapter state unchanged and uses the exact legacy error path.
- Expose a transport-neutral inbound-message/outbound-message contract and
  close signal only.  The adapter parses neither HTTP requests nor SSE
  frames and does not bind URLs or own HTTP-level announcements.  LEG-HTTP-01
  later supplies the exact HTTP+SSE peer binding and independently owns its
  GET/POST framing, endpoint advertisement, reconnect handling, security,
  and teardown.
- LEG-NEG-01's stdio composition invokes the adapter through its explicitly
  selected legacy peer binding over STD-01's neutral process/framing
  substrate. STD-01 never selects, constructs, binds, or invokes this
  adapter. The adapter receives a preselected exact-2024 binding or is not
  constructed.

Tests:

- `leg_02_a_positive`: exercise the shipped adapter through LEG-NEG-01's
  public stdio composition over the real STD-01 substrate, with exact
  initialize, initialized notification, negotiated capabilities, legal
  operating requests, and exact success/error messages.
- `leg_02_a_planted_negative`: alter only one lifecycle or capability
  dimension and prove the exact typed rejection, no handler dispatch, and no
  negotiated-state mutation.
- `leg_02_b_positive` and `leg_02_b_planted_negative`: prove bounded
  reverse requests, roots, sampling, logging, subscriptions, cancellation,
  progress, owner isolation, close races, and exact-once reservation release;
  the planted negative differs only in the forbidden owner/capability/order
  condition.
- `leg_02_integration_positive` and
  `leg_02_integration_planted_negative`: exercise both implementation
  slices through shipped public state and prove one binding cannot observe or
  complete another binding's operation.
- `leg_02_verification_positive` and
  `leg_02_verification_planted_negative`: independently verify the exact
  integration revision, frozen discovered/started/passed test IDs, positive
  observables, planted negatives, and no-claim boundary.
- Exact wire goldens cover initialize request/result, initialized
  notification, every admitted 2024 method direction, capability-gated
  requests, null/missing/invalid parameters, JSON-RPC IDs, error objects,
  cancellation, progress, notifications, and terminal close ordering.
- Explicit rejection/no-claim tests cover modern Tasks, Apps, elicitation,
  extension surfaces, 2025 sessioned Streamable HTTP, `Mcp-Session-Id`,
  `Last-Event-ID`, replay/resumption, DELETE, discovery classification,
  automatic cross-era fallback, and inline retry.  Each proves no accepted
  lifecycle transition, transport state lookup, handler dispatch, or state
  mutation.

Evidence:

- Bind each positive run to the exact revision/tree, legacy feature state,
  LEG-NEG-01 public stdio consumer, authenticated peer-binding generation, negotiated
  capability set, method direction, lifecycle transition, observable
  response/error, quota reservation/release count, and first-attempt result.
- The positive observable is one exact 2024 lifecycle reaching `Operating`
  and completing the declared request/notification or reverse-request
  exchange.  The planted negative observable is the exact typed error plus
  unchanged adapter state and zero unauthorized downstream effects.
- Real code and its positive plus near-identical planted-negative tests remain
  on the same Bead.  Independent verification is required before aggregate
  closure; fixture-only evidence, filtered/ignored tests, zero-test green
  output, or a plan edit earns no capability credit.

  and lifecycle adapter.  It does not implement a transport, own the
  two-endpoint HTTP+SSE protocol, provide cross-era route selection, or prove
  aggregate dual-era MCP conformance.

Dependencies:
