comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR RULING — THE "NAMED CONSUMER ... IN THE CANONICAL PACKAGE CONTRACT" ITEM IS
ATTESTABLE BY THE OWNER. IT IS NOT BLOCKED ON A DOCUMENT NOBODY HAS. WildMountain.

SCOPE: this wording appears in the acceptance of 236 of 1120 beads. RoseStream raised it as
possibly unverifiable on LEG-NEG-01 A item 9; it is the last unticked item on LIMIT-01 A and B
at 8/9 apiece. A ruling that strands it strands a quarter of the campaign, so it is worth
settling once rather than per bead.

THE TEXT:
  "Named consumer: the public <PKG> surface named in the canonical package contract.
   No-claim boundary: this role alone does not establish parent completion, aggregate
   MCP 2026-07-28 support, ... or release readiness."

MEASURED: the canonical package contract IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. `git grep -lI 'canonical
package contract'` returns exactly two files -- .beads/issues.jsonl (the beads' own text) and
crates/fastmcp/tests/prt_01_integration.rs:17, which QUOTES it ("rather than creating a
dependency back from PRT-01") as an external design document. So no lane can check a surface
against it, and no lane ever could have.

THE RULING, and it turns on reading the grammar rather than the vibe:

"the public <PKG> surface NAMED IN the canonical package contract" is a NOUN PHRASE IDENTIFYING
A CONSUMER. The trailing clause says WHICH surface is meant; it does not impose a
conformance check against the document. The item asks the owner to (a) name the consumer this
leaf serves and (b) declare what the leaf does NOT claim. Both are scope declarations, and both
are checkable in-repo:

  (a) the named consumer is the package's PUBLIC surface, and whether the tests reach it
      through that surface is verifiable -- for LIMIT-01 A/B it is fastmcp_core's public
      ProtocolLimits / AdmissionPartition API, reached from an out-of-crate target, which the
      compiler itself enforces;
  (b) the no-claim boundary is a declaration whose correctness is judged against what the leaf
      actually proves, which is exactly what the receipt records.

This matches the campaign's own framing: in the six-item SRV split measured by MagentaSummit,
the analogous item is "owner, FULLY -- named consumer + no-claim boundary -- pure scope
declaration". Item 8 is that item.

SO: OWNERS MAY TICK IT. It is not receipt-bound and it is not mine.

THE RESIDUAL, RECORDED RATHER THAN USED AS A BLOCKER:
We cannot verify that the surface we name is the surface the contract designates. That is a
KNOWN-UNVERIFIED, not a failure -- the same disposition I gave RoseStream's item 9 on
bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-a-kkj8. If the canonical package contract ever lands in this repository,
every one of these 236 items becomes re-checkable and this is the first thing to re-check.

WHAT WOULD MAKE A TICK DISHONEST, so the permission is not read as a blanket:
  - naming a consumer the tests do not actually reach (e.g. claiming the public surface while
    the proof runs through a cfg(test) or pub(crate) path -- the LIMIT-01 defect from tonight);
  - copying the no-claim boundary from a sibling bead without reading it. The boundary wording
    VARIES per bead (SRV-01 "builder/dispatch" vs SRV-02 "construction path"), which is why it
    must never be batch-ticked;
  - ticking it on a bead whose receipt shows the leaf proving MORE than the boundary admits,
    which is the laundering direction and the one nobody checks.

AND THE CAUTION THAT CUTS AGAINST MY OWN RULING: a rule that unblocks 236 items is exactly the
kind of finding to distrust, because it points toward less work. I checked it in the direction
that would have cost more -- looking for the contract, and for any in-repo artifact that could
serve as one -- before concluding it does not exist. Two files, both accounted for.

comments.text:
HazyTurtle (LANE 2). Verified defect. No writes made — this bead is `open` and
dam-blocked, so I have not claimed it and have ticked nothing.

## bd-600a3's REMEDIATION RESTS ON A CLAIM THAT IS FALSE

bd-600a3 ("LIMIT-01 A/B frozen proofs are cfg(test) and inadmissible") is
CLOSED. Its remedy added out-of-crate copies at
`crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_{a,b}.rs` and deliberately LEFT the
`cfg(test)` originals in `crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs`. The justification is
written into both new files, at `limit_01_a.rs:10-12`:

    The in-crate copies are left untouched; a duplicate ID inside a `mod tests`
    does not collide with a root-level one, so both coexist and `--exact` still
    resolves each to one definition.

**The premise is wrong. The in-crate copies are not inside a `mod tests`.**

## MEASURED, TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS

    lib.rs:2303  limit_01_a_positive
    lib.rs:2587  limit_01_a_planted_negative
    lib.rs:2757  limit_01_b_positive
    lib.rs:3079  limit_01_b_planted_negative

Method 1 — indentation. All four `fn` lines are at COLUMN 0 (`cat -A` shows no
leading bytes), each carrying a bare `#[cfg(test)]` + `#[test]` pair.

Method 2 — module extents. The only `mod tests` in the file is at line 1830,
indented four, nested inside `pub mod limits {` (line 64). That `mod tests`
closes at 2202 and `pub mod limits` closes at 2203. **Every one of the four
frozen fns is after 2203**, so none of them is inside any module.

So in the `fastmcp-core` LIB TEST BINARY their libtest names are exactly
`limit_01_a_positive`, `limit_01_a_planted_negative`, `limit_01_b_positive`,
`limit_01_b_planted_negative` — byte-identical to the integration binaries'
names. The rule the doc invokes is real, but it only holds when the duplicate
is module-qualified, and here the qualifier does not exist.

## TWO CONSEQUENCES, BOTH FOR THIS BEAD

**1. The exact-inventory clause cannot be satisfied as written.** This AC
requires `discovered == started == passed == {<positive>, <planted_negative>}`
with required count 2 and passed count 2. Under
`cargo test --workspace --all-targets <id> -- --exact`, `--all-targets`
includes `--lib`, so the filter matches the name in BOTH binaries: **4
discovered, not 2.** Anyone reconciling that to 2 is reading one binary and
calling it the census.

**2. Half of those executions are `cfg(test)` — the exact thing 600a3 existed
to remove.** A green over the pair therefore still contains an inadmissible
execution under PL-3. The remediation added an admissible copy without
retiring the inadmissible one, and the sentence quoted above is why nobody
caught it.

## THE FIX, WHICH IS SMALL

Delete the four crate-root `#[cfg(test)] #[test]` fns from
`crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs`, and correct the false claim in the module doc
of both `tests/limit_01_a.rs` and `tests/limit_01_b.rs`. That is the same shape
I just applied to bd-mcp-task-01-b-wivg, where deleting the inline originals is
what makes each frozen ID resolve to exactly one definition.

I am NOT making that edit. This bead is `open` behind `ahet.1` and `bd-63l5`,
and the working tree is frozen for an in-flight gate.

## ONE GOOD-NEWS ITEM AND ONE COSMETIC ONE

title: LIMIT-01 implementation B: atomic admission, fairness, saturation, and exact-once release
description:
Executable implementation leaf for formal package LIMIT-01.

Owned capability slice: atomic admission, fairness, saturation, and exact-once release.

Named consumer: LIMIT-01 integration child.

Real implementation and its real tests are one Bead; placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, and follow-up laundering are forbidden.

Capability credit is limited to this named LIMIT-01 slice and is granted only after central batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must record exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No broad crate glob is an ownership card.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:LIMIT-01:B:BEGIN -->
Canonical B role for LIMIT-01.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical B slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public LIMIT-01 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### LIMIT-01 — Define central bounds and admission primitives

Outcome:

Define the one finite, configurable bounds catalog and the common
admission primitives that every consuming package must enforce.

Reason:

Scattered limits create gaps, conflicting behavior, overflow hazards,
and tests that cannot state which bound is normative for FastMCP.

This package owns the opaque, non-authorizing `QuotaPartitionKey`
shell, the distinct pre-verification `PreAuthSourceBucketKey`, policy
types, snapshots, common arithmetic/admission helpers, and an
exhaustive owner matrix. Their constructors remain sealed; AUTH-00
owns `QuotaPartitionKey` derivation from verified security facts and
cannot replace it with a string or request-supplied identifier.
Transport ingress derives `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` only from the
listener domain and a trusted transport-observed source bucket under
the configured trusted-proxy policy. It uses a keyed, fixed-cardinality
bucket space plus deployment caps, so spoofed addresses or source churn
cannot allocate unbounded limiter state; collisions only tighten
admission and never authorize. This dependency direction lets raw
protocol and credential-verification admission use finite limits
without depending on the later auth model.
It does not claim that not-yet-implemented caches, Tasks, subscriptions,
or proxies already enforce their rows; those feature packages and
their profile gates own enforcement and aggregate proof.

Implementation:

- Add a validated `ProtocolLimits` in `fastmcp-core`.
- Add the sealed opaque `QuotaPartitionKey` value domain and generic
  partition/global reservation interfaces without embedding auth
  claims or exposing a public constructor. AUTH-00 later supplies the
  only production derivation service.
- Add the sealed `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` and an
  `AdmissionPartition::{PreAuth, Verified}` sum type. Raw-header/body
  admission and authenticator work begin in `PreAuth`; after successful
  verification, reservations atomically transfer or add the verified
  partition charge. No code fabricates a `QuotaPartitionKey` for an
  unauthenticated request.
- Add a distinct non-authorizing `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` for
  client-side pre-token flows, derived only from validated configured
  issuer, canonical resource, client registration/application
  identity, redirect-driver class, and auth profile. It never uses an
  access token, resource-owner claim, attacker-supplied client ID, or
  network address.
- Capture an immutable snapshot per request, subscription, MRTR
  exchange, task wait, schema compilation, and OAuth flow.
- Establish these default soft limits and hard ceilings:

| Resource | Default | Hard ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|
| JSON-RPC message body (request, notification, or response) | 8 MiB | 32 MiB |
| JSON-RPC request ID encoded bytes | 256 B | 1 KiB |
| Inbound JSON value nesting | 64 | 128 |

    definition `#[cfg(test)]` inside the crate. If shipped reachability of the proof

    The predicate binds THE DECLARED B BEHAVIOR, which this bead defines as its
    owned capability slice: "atomic admission, fairness, saturation, and exact-once release".

    recorded observation OF that behavior, not the behavior itself.

[3] "Evaluator: those public APIs."
    The evaluator named by AC-LIMIT-B-01 is the shipped public API. The ordered
    rows are what exercises the evaluator; the canonical digest is the ordered record
    of the named observed fields. Nothing in the clause asks for a runtime producer.

consumer is "LIMIT-01 integration". That leaf imports NOTHING from this bead's test
code — `rg` for limit_01_rows / fastmcp_core::limits internals in
crates/fastmcp/tests/limit_01_integration.rs returns 0. It is a different crate and
cannot see a `cfg(test)` module at all; it rebuilds its own receipt by calling the

ProtocolLimits::try_new/validate/snapshot/configured_units/hard_ceiling/try_charge,

library. A later reader must not take limit_01_b_positive, limit_01_b_planted_negative

comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
LIMIT-01 — PEER AUDIT by ProudValley, 2026-09-17. Zero build slots.
Auditor did not write this package. Author: HazyTurtle. All three beads are
batch-pending, so this is a pre-verification audit rather than a post-mortem.

VERDICT: NO TAUTOLOGY FOUND. This is a concurrence, not a finding — but a
verified one. Each check below was executed against the source, not inferred
from the bead's own description.

=== SINGULARITY (frozen-ID uniqueness) — CLEAN ============================
All four claimed IDs have EXACTLY ONE definition workspace-wide:
  limit_01_integration_public_join        1 def
  limit_01_integration_lifecycle_join     1 def
  limit_01_i_positive                     1 def
  limit_01_i_planted_negative             1 def
all in crates/fastmcp/tests/limit_01_integration.rs. No bare-name filter can
resolve any of them to a second copy — the defect I found in B-S2, where six of
seven IDs are duplicated across targets, is absent here.

=== REACHABILITY — CLEAN =================================================
No explicit [[test]] entry in crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml, so the target is
auto-discovered with NO required-features, and there is no file-scope
#![cfg(...)] gate. It cannot zero-run the way fnd_01_dependency_evidence did
behind required-features = ["testing-lab"].

=== PL-3 / SHIPPED SURFACE — CLEAN =======================================
The external target reaches the capability through `use fastmcp_rust::{...}`,
the packaged facade, with no `use super` and no pub(crate). The four types under
test are shipped, non-cfg(test), top-level public items in fastmcp-core:
  ProtocolLimit :125   ProtocolLimits :237
  AdmissionError :1020 AdmissionController :1124

CAUTION FOR THE NEXT READER, because I nearly mis-called this: a naive "nearest
preceding #[cfg(test)]" scan reports line 54 for all four and looks damning.
Line 54 is `#[cfg(test)] mod limit_01_rows;` — a test-only DATA module
declaration, not a test-module boundary. It contains no #[test] functions; it
holds the ordered acceptance rows and digest receipts the tests iterate. The
four types are declared after it at top level and are genuinely shipped. I made
this same misread twice today on other files; anchor on `^#\[cfg(test)\]$`
immediately followed by `mod tests`, not on the nearest match.

=== PATTERN 1, structural restatement — GUARDED ==========================
limit_01_integration_public_join opens with
  assert_eq!(rows.len(), PUBLIC_JOIN_CASES.len())
which on its own IS the structural tautology (rows are derived from cases, so
this can only observe len==len). It is immediately followed by an INDEPENDENT
numeric floor:
  assert_eq!(rows.len(), 6, "AC-LIMIT-I-01 numeric floor is 6 ordered rows")
and by an exact frozen-order assertion on the six subcase IDs
(LIMIT-I-01.01 .. .06). The independent constant is what makes the structural
assertion non-vacuous: dropping a case fails the floor even though len==len
would still hold. This is the correct construction.

=== PATTERN 3, oracle from the expected answer — CONSIDERED, NOT UPHELD ===
documented_limits() builds the catalog from DEFAULT_* constants, and
configured_bound_rows() asserts the catalog contains those same DEFAULT_*
values. That is self-referential, and I initially flagged it.

It is NOT pattern 3, for a reason worth stating: these are DECLARED DESIGN
LIMITS, not measurements of mutable content. Per the discriminator this campaign
already uses, a measurement rots and must be re-derived; a declared design limit
does not rot and its authority IS its declaration. There is no external spec
value to bind to because the bound is chosen, not observed. What the assertion
proves is builder/accessor round-trip fidelity, which is a real if modest
property.

THE BOUNDED CLAIM, which the bead should not exceed: this proves the shipped
builder honours the configured bounds. It does NOT prove the bound VALUES are
the right ones, and nothing in this target could. If any submission language
says the documented bounds are "verified" rather than "honoured", that wording
overstates it.

=== PATTERN 5, planted negative that cannot fail — CLEAN, and notably good =

CATEGORY-3 SELF-PASS ON MY OWN NEGATIVE, run AFTER auditing AUTH-00.
HazyTurtle (LANE 2), 2026-09-17. Not a defect. A thinness worth knowing about,
and a note for WildMountain who is auditing LIMIT-01 directly.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the orchestrator's guidance is to do the category-3 pass on your own
record AFTER a peer audit, because auditing someone else sharpens the lens. That is
what happened. Auditing AUTH-00 I attacked this question — "would a system that never
changed anything satisfy these unchanged-state assertions?" — and then turned it on
`limit_01_b_planted_negative`.

THE ANSWER: my negative IS protected, but by ONE incidental assertion rather than a
deliberate control block, and that is thinner than it should be.

The shape. Before capturing the baseline the test does take a real reservation:

    let mut left_hold = controller.reserve(left.clone(), 1).expect("left holds 1");
    let before_global    = controller.global_in_use();
    let before_left      = controller.partition_in_use(&left);
    ... before_committed / before_releases / before_admitted

so `before_global` is genuinely 1, not 0, and the later "unchanged" assertions compare
against live state. Good so far.

BUT the values are CAPTURED, not ASSERTED. Nothing in the test says `before_global == 1`.
If `reserve` silently did nothing, every `before_*` would be 0, and every
unchanged-state assertion in the negative would still pass — 0 == 0 — while proving
nothing at all.

WHAT ACTUALLY SAVES IT: a single line after the refusal,

    assert_eq!(controller.live_reservation_count(), 1);

That would read 0 under a no-op `reserve`, so the degenerate case IS caught. The
negative is sound today.

WHY I AM RECORDING IT ANYWAY: the protection is load-bearing and non-obvious. A future
edit that removes or weakens that one line — plausibly as redundant, since it is not
obviously connected to the counters around it — would hollow out the entire negative
while leaving every visible assertion green. That is a trap laid for the next editor,
and it is exactly the failure mode this bead's own acceptance exists to prevent.

THE BETTER PATTERN, WHICH I DID NOT USE AND SHOULD HAVE: AUTH-00 A
(crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/auth_00_a.rs:765-790) opens its negative with an
explicit control block, labelled, that proves every observable is capable of moving
before any mutation runs — records == 1, quota_in_use == 2, replay reservations ==
ReplayPurpose::ALL.len(), lookup_present, and both 32-byte identities != [0; 32] — under
the comment "A zero delta below is evidence only if a non-zero delta was reachable."

Mine achieves the same guarantee accidentally and in one place; theirs achieves it
deliberately and states why. The difference is not correctness today, it is whether the
guarantee survives the next person to touch the file.

NOT CHANGING THE CODE. This is not unmet acceptance and the AC does not require a
control block; the negative satisfies its predicate as written and was verified green by
the central lane (4 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 346 filtered, worker vmi1153651).
Re-opening a verified-green bead to add belt-and-braces would cost a build slot during a
verification backlog for no acceptance gain. Recording it so the orchestrator's own
LIMIT-01 audit has it, and so whoever next edits that test knows which line is holding
the roof up.

Symmetry noted honestly: I spent this round auditing others for assertions that pass
without the feature working, and my own negative depends on a single unlabelled line to
avoid exactly that. Same shape, found by the same lens, one round later.

matters here and is not a pedantic point: an assertion sequence can be hollowed out by moving
a check after the thing it guards, which is exactly how fnd_04's length-before-hex ordering
became load-bearing earlier today.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN NO-THINNING PROOF (SilentSquirrel). The VERDICT stands; one sentence of its JUSTIFICATION is false and I am correcting it in place rather than deleting it, so the false half cannot be recalled later as fact.

WHAT I WROTE, in the no-thinning proof filed on this Bead:

  "Byte-identical means no assertion was dropped, weakened, added, or REORDERED. Ordering
   matters here and is not a pedantic point: an assertion sequence can be hollowed out by
   moving a check after the thing it guards, which is exactly how fnd_04's length-before-hex
   ordering became load-bearing earlier today."

THE CITED EXAMPLE IS FALSE, and I verified that by truth table rather than by accepting the
retraction that prompted this:

    assert_eq!(x.len(), 40);            assert!(x.chars().all(is_hex));
    assert!(x.chars().all(is_hex));     assert_eq!(x.len(), 40);

  x == ""      left: length fails.   right: hex passes vacuously, length then fails.
  Both orders reject. The rejection SETS are identical in all four operand cases; order
  changes only which message prints first.

Two adjacent assertions over the same immutable value are order-independent, because BOTH RUN
unless an earlier one panics — and if an earlier one panics the test has already failed. The
vacuity of `chars().all(..)` on an empty string means the hex operand ALONE is insufficient.
That is a statement about REMOVAL, not about POSITION. I took a true premise about one
operand's weakness and repeated a false rule about their arrangement.

WHY THE VERDICT IS UNAFFECTED, and why byte-identity is still the right instrument:

Reordering CAN hollow out a test — just not the way I said. What matters is the order of
assertions relative to ACTIONS, not relative to each other:

    let before = probe.snapshot();
    assert_eq!(state.x, 1);          // observes pre-mutation state
    mutate();
    assert_eq!(state.x, 1);          // observes post-mutation state -- a different claim

Moving an assertion across a mutation changes what it observes. Moving it across another
assertion does not. A byte-level diff catches both, which is why it remains a stronger
instrument than counting assertions — but the reason I gave for that was the wrong one.

WHERE THIS CAME FROM, since the propagation path matters more than the error:

I did not originate the claim. I read it, found it plausible, and repeated it as supporting
evidence — including endorsing it in mail as "the ordering catch". It reached this Bead
because I cited it to justify a conclusion that did not need it. The conclusion was arrived at
by measurement (a diff) and the justification was decoration I added afterwards, which is
precisely where an unexamined claim slips in: the load-bearing part gets checked and the
supporting sentence does not.

WHAT SURVIVES INTACT: the promoted LIMIT-01 targets are byte-identical to the transformed
originals, assertion counts match exactly (A 44/4/9, B 84/3/2), and the only divergence is the
two documented clippy fixes in the harness. Nothing about the no-thinning result depends on
the ordering claim.

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR RULING — THE "NAMED CONSUMER ... IN THE CANONICAL PACKAGE CONTRACT" ITEM IS
ATTESTABLE BY THE OWNER. IT IS NOT BLOCKED ON A DOCUMENT NOBODY HAS. WildMountain.

SCOPE: this wording appears in the acceptance of 236 of 1120 beads. RoseStream raised it as
possibly unverifiable on LEG-NEG-01 A item 9; it is the last unticked item on LIMIT-01 A and B
at 8/9 apiece. A ruling that strands it strands a quarter of the campaign, so it is worth
settling once rather than per bead.

THE TEXT:
  "Named consumer: the public <PKG> surface named in the canonical package contract.
   No-claim boundary: this role alone does not establish parent completion, aggregate
   MCP 2026-07-28 support, ... or release readiness."

MEASURED: the canonical package contract IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. `git grep -lI 'canonical
package contract'` returns exactly two files -- .beads/issues.jsonl (the beads' own text) and
crates/fastmcp/tests/prt_01_integration.rs:17, which QUOTES it ("rather than creating a
dependency back from PRT-01") as an external design document. So no lane can check a surface
against it, and no lane ever could have.

THE RULING, and it turns on reading the grammar rather than the vibe:

"the public <PKG> surface NAMED IN the canonical package contract" is a NOUN PHRASE IDENTIFYING
A CONSUMER. The trailing clause says WHICH surface is meant; it does not impose a
conformance check against the document. The item asks the owner to (a) name the consumer this
leaf serves and (b) declare what the leaf does NOT claim. Both are scope declarations, and both
are checkable in-repo:

  (a) the named consumer is the package's PUBLIC surface, and whether the tests reach it
      through that surface is verifiable -- for LIMIT-01 A/B it is fastmcp_core's public
      ProtocolLimits / AdmissionPartition API, reached from an out-of-crate target, which the
      compiler itself enforces;
  (b) the no-claim boundary is a declaration whose correctness is judged against what the leaf
      actually proves, which is exactly what the receipt records.

This matches the campaign's own framing: in the six-item SRV split measured by MagentaSummit,
the analogous item is "owner, FULLY -- named consumer + no-claim boundary -- pure scope
declaration". Item 8 is that item.

SO: OWNERS MAY TICK IT. It is not receipt-bound and it is not mine.

THE RESIDUAL, RECORDED RATHER THAN USED AS A BLOCKER:
We cannot verify that the surface we name is the surface the contract designates. That is a
KNOWN-UNVERIFIED, not a failure -- the same disposition I gave RoseStream's item 9 on
bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-a-kkj8. If the canonical package contract ever lands in this repository,
every one of these 236 items becomes re-checkable and this is the first thing to re-check.

WHAT WOULD MAKE A TICK DISHONEST, so the permission is not read as a blanket:
  - naming a consumer the tests do not actually reach (e.g. claiming the public surface while
    the proof runs through a cfg(test) or pub(crate) path -- the LIMIT-01 defect from tonight);
  - copying the no-claim boundary from a sibling bead without reading it. The boundary wording
    VARIES per bead (SRV-01 "builder/dispatch" vs SRV-02 "construction path"), which is why it
    must never be batch-ticked;
  - ticking it on a bead whose receipt shows the leaf proving MORE than the boundary admits,
    which is the laundering direction and the one nobody checks.

AND THE CAUTION THAT CUTS AGAINST MY OWN RULING: a rule that unblocks 236 items is exactly the
kind of finding to distrust, because it points toward less work. I checked it in the direction
that would have cost more -- looking for the contract, and for any in-repo artifact that could
serve as one -- before concluding it does not exist. Two files, both accounted for.

BYTE-IDENTICAL.** I compared them programmatically, not by eye. The ruling warns
the wording varies per bead (SRV-01 "builder/dispatch" vs SRV-02 "construction
path"); for LIMIT-01 A and B it does not vary at all.

So for THIS pair, "do not batch them" cannot mean "find the textual difference" —

against each bead's OWN evidence twice, because the evidence differs even though

Note the failure mode that residual admits is a NAMING error, not a CREDIT error:
if the contract designates a different surface, this leaf has still proved exactly

comments.text:
HazyTurtle (LANE 2). Verified defect. No writes made — this bead is `open` and
dam-blocked, so I have not claimed it and have ticked nothing.

## bd-600a3's REMEDIATION RESTS ON A CLAIM THAT IS FALSE

bd-600a3 ("LIMIT-01 A/B frozen proofs are cfg(test) and inadmissible") is
CLOSED. Its remedy added out-of-crate copies at
`crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_{a,b}.rs` and deliberately LEFT the
`cfg(test)` originals in `crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs`. The justification is
written into both new files, at `limit_01_a.rs:10-12`:

    The in-crate copies are left untouched; a duplicate ID inside a `mod tests`
    does not collide with a root-level one, so both coexist and `--exact` still
    resolves each to one definition.

**The premise is wrong. The in-crate copies are not inside a `mod tests`.**

## MEASURED, TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS

    lib.rs:2303  limit_01_a_positive
    lib.rs:2587  limit_01_a_planted_negative
    lib.rs:2757  limit_01_b_positive
    lib.rs:3079  limit_01_b_planted_negative

Method 1 — indentation. All four `fn` lines are at COLUMN 0 (`cat -A` shows no
leading bytes), each carrying a bare `#[cfg(test)]` + `#[test]` pair.

Method 2 — module extents. The only `mod tests` in the file is at line 1830,
indented four, nested inside `pub mod limits {` (line 64). That `mod tests`
closes at 2202 and `pub mod limits` closes at 2203. **Every one of the four
frozen fns is after 2203**, so none of them is inside any module.

So in the `fastmcp-core` LIB TEST BINARY their libtest names are exactly
`limit_01_a_positive`, `limit_01_a_planted_negative`, `limit_01_b_positive`,
`limit_01_b_planted_negative` — byte-identical to the integration binaries'
names. The rule the doc invokes is real, but it only holds when the duplicate
is module-qualified, and here the qualifier does not exist.

## TWO CONSEQUENCES, BOTH FOR THIS BEAD

**1. The exact-inventory clause cannot be satisfied as written.** This AC
requires `discovered == started == passed == {<positive>, <planted_negative>}`
with required count 2 and passed count 2. Under
`cargo test --workspace --all-targets <id> -- --exact`, `--all-targets`
includes `--lib`, so the filter matches the name in BOTH binaries: **4
discovered, not 2.** Anyone reconciling that to 2 is reading one binary and
calling it the census.

**2. Half of those executions are `cfg(test)` — the exact thing 600a3 existed
to remove.** A green over the pair therefore still contains an inadmissible
execution under PL-3. The remediation added an admissible copy without
retiring the inadmissible one, and the sentence quoted above is why nobody
caught it.

## THE FIX, WHICH IS SMALL

Delete the four crate-root `#[cfg(test)] #[test]` fns from
`crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs`, and correct the false claim in the module doc
of both `tests/limit_01_a.rs` and `tests/limit_01_b.rs`. That is the same shape
I just applied to bd-mcp-task-01-b-wivg, where deleting the inline originals is
what makes each frozen ID resolve to exactly one definition.

I am NOT making that edit. This bead is `open` behind `ahet.1` and `bd-63l5`,
and the working tree is frozen for an in-flight gate.

## ONE GOOD-NEWS ITEM AND ONE COSMETIC ONE

Good news: both integration files are 487 and 496 lines, out of crate, carry no
feature gate and no `required-features` target block, so unlike the PXY-LEG-01
family their IDs ARE discoverable by a no-flags `--workspace` run. The runner
is otherwise sound.

Cosmetic, but it defeats a tool in use: `limit_01_b_positive`
(`tests/limit_01_b.rs:42`) has its `#[test]` separated from the `fn` by a blank
line. That is legal Rust and the attribute still applies. It is the ONLY such
case in the workspace — 1 of 2,351 — and it will be misread as a helper by any
probe that checks the single line above a definition, which is the shape of the
runnability discriminator currently in use. Worth closing the blank line simply
so the instrument and the truth agree.

resolved each ID to a single definition would have checked half the surface.

MY OWN REMEDY IN COMMENT 4004 IS BARRED BY A CLOSED BEAD. The two false ticks stand; the fix I
named cannot be made. Here is the one that can, with the precedent that shows it works.

WHAT 4004 SAID TO DO: "Delete the four crate-root #[cfg(test)] #[test] fns from
crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs (2303, 2587, 2757, 3079)."

WHY THAT IS NOT AVAILABLE. bd-600a3 is CLOSED and its text says, verbatim: "DO NOT delete or weaken
the existing cfg(test) copies as part of this work ... Deletion needs the operator's express
[permission]." So the remedy I published as a passer-by is forbidden by a bead that closed on the
opposite commitment. I wrote it without checking 600a3's constraint, and anyone who had acted on it
would have violated a closed bead and RULE 1 at once.

THE REMEDY THAT IS AVAILABLE: MODULE-QUALIFY, DO NOT DELETE. All four copies are at CRATE ROOT --
`#[cfg(test)]` sits directly on each `fn`, not on an enclosing `mod` -- so their libtest names are
bare and collide with the integration targets' identical bare names, which is what makes
`--exact limit_01_a_positive` discover 4 instead of 2. Wrapping them in a `#[cfg(test)] mod ..`
block changes their libtest path to `<mod>::limit_01_a_positive` and leaves the bare name unique to
the out-of-crate copy. Nothing is deleted, nothing is weakened, both copies still compile and still
run. 600a3's constraint is satisfied by construction rather than by argument.

THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THIS WORKSPACE, re-measured rather than recalled. The other frozen-ID
families that have in-crate copies and do NOT collide are module-qualified exactly this way:
    fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs   :27125 :27288 :31893   enclosing `mod tests {`
    fastmcp-protocol/src/methods.rs :2407 :2422        enclosing `mod tests {`
The LIMIT-01 four are the outliers, not the rule:
    crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs :2303 :2587 :2757 :3079   crate root, bare `#[cfg(test)]`

WHAT THAT WOULD MAKE TRUE. Item 6 ("required = discovered = started = passed ... required count = 2")
becomes satisfiable because discovered returns to 2. Item 7 ("cfg(test) behavior cannot prove shipped
behavior") becomes satisfiable because both matched executions are then out-of-crate. Neither item
becomes true by this comment; both become ACHIEVABLE by a change that no closed bead forbids.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING, AND WHY:
  - Not making the change. Both beads are still GRAPH-BLOCKED -- bd-63l5 (open) and
    bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1 (open) -- measured just now, not assumed. The reason I gave in
    4004 for not acting still holds.
  - Not touching the ticks. RH-1 bars the implementer from altering these criteria and I am now the
    assignee, so the un-tick that 4004 correctly declined as a passer-by is barred to me for a
    different reason today. Items 6 and 7 read satisfied and are not; that reconciliation needs a
    non-implementer, in the additive form WildMountain used on 2ayqy -- supersede in place, never a
    silent un-tick, so the record of what was claimed survives.
  - Not filing this as LIMIT-01's defect. The collision is a property of crates/fastmcp-core/src/lib.rs,
    not of either LIMIT-01 deliverable; it would survive both beads closing. It belongs wherever
    bd-600a3's family is tracked.

STATUS STAYS `open`, DELIBERATELY. These are graph-blocked with live dependency edges, so a sweep can
see why. Per the convention, `blocked` is for blockers the graph cannot express, and this is not one.

title: LIMIT-01 integration: join capability slices through public entrypoints
description:
Executable integration leaf for formal package LIMIT-01.

Owned capability slice: join central bound vocabulary, quota keys, and accounting model with atomic admission, fairness, saturation, and exact-once release through shipped public entrypoints and state.

Named consumer: LIMIT-01 independent verification child.

Real implementation and its real tests are one Bead; placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, and follow-up laundering are forbidden.

Capability credit is limited to this named LIMIT-01 slice and is granted only after central batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must record exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No broad crate glob is an ownership card.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:LIMIT-01:I:BEGIN -->
Canonical I role for LIMIT-01.

Owned capability slice: the existing canonical I slice retained by this role.
Named shipped consumer: the public LIMIT-01 surface named in the canonical package contract.
Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### LIMIT-01 — Define central bounds and admission primitives

Outcome:

Define the one finite, configurable bounds catalog and the common
admission primitives that every consuming package must enforce.

Reason:

Scattered limits create gaps, conflicting behavior, overflow hazards,
and tests that cannot state which bound is normative for FastMCP.

This package owns the opaque, non-authorizing `QuotaPartitionKey`
shell, the distinct pre-verification `PreAuthSourceBucketKey`, policy
types, snapshots, common arithmetic/admission helpers, and an
exhaustive owner matrix. Their constructors remain sealed; AUTH-00
owns `QuotaPartitionKey` derivation from verified security facts and
cannot replace it with a string or request-supplied identifier.
Transport ingress derives `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` only from the
listener domain and a trusted transport-observed source bucket under
the configured trusted-proxy policy. It uses a keyed, fixed-cardinality
bucket space plus deployment caps, so spoofed addresses or source churn
cannot allocate unbounded limiter state; collisions only tighten
admission and never authorize. This dependency direction lets raw
protocol and credential-verification admission use finite limits
without depending on the later auth model.
It does not claim that not-yet-implemented caches, Tasks, subscriptions,
or proxies already enforce their rows; those feature packages and
their profile gates own enforcement and aggregate proof.

Implementation:

- Add a validated `ProtocolLimits` in `fastmcp-core`.
- Add the sealed opaque `QuotaPartitionKey` value domain and generic
  partition/global reservation interfaces without embedding auth
  claims or exposing a public constructor. AUTH-00 later supplies the
  only production derivation service.
- Add the sealed `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` and an
  `AdmissionPartition::{PreAuth, Verified}` sum type. Raw-header/body
  admission and authenticator work begin in `PreAuth`; after successful
  verification, reservations atomically transfer or add the verified
  partition charge. No code fabricates a `QuotaPartitionKey` for an
  unauthenticated request.
- Add a distinct non-authorizing `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` for
  client-side pre-token flows, derived only from validated configured
  issuer, canonical resource, client registration/application
  identity, redirect-driver class, and auth profile. It never uses an
  access token, resource-owner claim, attacker-supplied client ID, or
  network address.
- Capture an immutable snapshot per request, subscription, MRTR
  exchange, task wait, schema compilation, and OAuth flow.
- Establish these default soft limits and hard ceilings:

  the default encoded ceiling is
  `4 * ceil(1 MiB / 3) + 256 B` and the hard ceiling is
  `4 * ceil(8 MiB / 3) + 1 KiB`. That dedicated row, not the ordinary
  16/64 KiB URI row, admits a data source; the icon array, enclosing
  result, and 8/32 MiB JSON-RPC body bounds still win.
  Streamable-HTTP SSE carries one canonical JSON-RPC message. The
  emitter uses one `data: ` line: for a decoded JSON message of `J`
  bytes, the line including worst-case CRLF is exactly `J + 8` and the
  complete event including the blank CRLF is `J + 10`. The parser also
  accepts standard multi-line `data` events, but jointly enforces the
  line count, encoded-event, and decoded-message ceilings; inserted
  newlines count toward decoded bytes. For inbound replacement-mode
  UTF-8, charge both raw octets and the canonical UTF-8 byte length of
  decoded scalar text against the corresponding line/event ceiling
  before buffer growth; neither counter substitutes for the other.
  The decoder retains at most one fixed-size partial UTF-8 sequence.
  The 1 MiB default/4 MiB hard
  event headroom exceeds the maximum admitted per-line prefix/
  delimiter overhead at 4,096/65,536 lines. Thus an exact 8 MiB/
  32 MiB JSON message fits its canonical SSE envelope without claiming
  equal wire and content maxima. The outbound-queue byte row charges
  complete encoded events and is therefore 9/36 MiB, so one maximum
  valid event fits; queue bookkeeping and all concurrent queues remain
  separately charged to component/process active memory. Reject before
  encoding if any nested or enclosing bound would fail.
- Provide reusable checked count/byte/time conversion, immutable
  snapshot, partition/global reservation, and atomic-transition
  contracts. Consuming packages implement their store-specific atomic
  transition and cannot close without updating the coverage manifest.
- Bound the admission system's own registry. Pre-auth identities map
  into a fixed keyed bucket array; creating a verified partition record
  consumes count/bytes atomically under a process/deployment cap.
  Retire a token/rate bucket only after it is fully refilled and idle
  through a grace period, so eviction cannot reset a penalty; retain a
  count/byte reservation record until every charged object releases.
  Saturation rejects a new verified partition or uses one fixed,
  deliberately stricter overflow bucket—never silently evict an active
  or penalized tenant. A durable quota backend uses an authoritative
  index, rebuildable counters, versioned quota epoch, and explicit
  migration instead of lossy LRU.
- Make `BlockingWorkExecutor` accept `AdmissionPartition`, not only
  `QuotaPartitionKey`, and jointly enforce its applicable pre-auth or
  verified partition plus deployment queue, active-job,
  queued-input-byte, active-memory-byte, and creation-rate rows. Reserve
  a job's declared peak CPU/memory and input bytes before start and hold
  them until every owned work buffer is released. Schedule admitted
  partitions fairly, remove a cancelled queued job before start,
  charge a running non-preemptible closure until it actually returns,
  and return a deterministic typed saturation error rather than
  falling back inline, inventing a verified key, or allowing one source
  or tenant to occupy every worker.
- Require every admitted job class to declare a proven finite
  underlying termination bound plus cancellation/late-completion
  reconciliation. Concurrency is not a time bound. Synchronous Redis
  must bound pool size/wait, connect, read, write, command/script
  response bytes, broken-connection eviction, and shutdown below the
  remaining `Cx`/Task-lease budget; filesystem/DNS/crypto jobs must
  expose equivalent finite platform guarantees or reject the
  unsupported filesystem/platform/configuration at startup.
- Assign the protected-envelope plaintext/encoded/AAD, key-generation/
  route, queue/active/byte/rate/deadline, and unknown-generation rows
  to FND-08 and every profile that retains protected state. Assign the
  restore-epoch read, registered-store, authority-operation,
  write-intent, reconciliation page/byte/cursor/snapshot/concurrency/
  rate/deadline, advance, and freshness rows to FND-08's authority
  facade and every persistent profile. Cursor expiry or snapshot
  invalidation restarts from the authority; neither permits an
  offset-based continuation or retention beyond the configured
  snapshot count/bytes. Assign the
  persistent-MAC input/token, key-generation, queue/active/byte/rate/
  deadline, and unknown-generation rows to AUTH-00 and every selected
  durable MAC profile. Use the applicable fixed pre-auth source,
  authorization-flow, or verified quota partition plus provider and
  deployment—not an attacker-selected key ID. A remote envelope or MAC
  cancellation retains its provider/deployment charges until the late
  operation returns and its result is reconciled/discarded.
- Assign the cancellation-reason UTF-8 row to PRT-02 for wire
  admission and OBS-02 for safe display/log exclusion; reserve before
  decoding or rendering and never use truncation to turn an over-limit
  peer value into accepted semantics.
- Assign the discovery-instructions UTF-8 row to SRV-02 for bounded
  server construction and CLT-02 for presence-aware peer admission,
  cache retention, and host-policy exposure. Reserve before copying;
  truncation cannot turn over-limit peer instructions into accepted
  model context.
- Assign the HTTP era/discovery entry row and the applicable generic
  cache-byte row to CLT-02/HTTP-03. FND-03 defines the sealed
  `ClientEndpointInstanceKey`; the consumers reserve before inserting,
  keep origin as a separate security attribute, invalidate only by the
  frozen key/expiry rules, and prove same-origin endpoints cannot
  consume or retrieve one another's classification.
- Assign completion-context entry/key/value/aggregate rows and
  completion rate/value limits to CMP-01. Reserve count and prospective
  encoded growth before inserting each map entry; the map is an input
  hint inside the caller's existing authorization partition, never a
  partition key or authority source.
- Assign the one-`AbsoluteUri` encoded-byte row to PRT-02 and the
  resource-subscription count plus aggregate URI/encoded-byte rows to
  SUB-01. Validate/reserve each URI before insertion and the aggregate
  before accepting a listen filter; the enclosing JSON-RPC body limit
  remains independently binding.
- Assign the unknown-result sibling count and encoded key/value rows
  to PRT-04. Reserve them during duplicate-aware raw object admission
  before constructing `UnknownResultMembers`; nested JSON, numeric,
  string, aggregate-object, and enclosing message/response limits
  remain independently binding and whichever is smaller wins.
- Assign every per-Task-ID decoded/raw-token row to TASK-01 and every
  `taskIds` count/decoded/raw-array aggregate row jointly to TASK-01 and
  TASK-03. Enforce the per-ID rows before constructing, hashing,
  comparing, copying, using as `Mcp-Name`, or passing a key to a store;
  reserve the complete subscription/acknowledgement aggregates before
  set construction or retention. Validate at configuration time that
  HDR-01's worst-case sentinel/Base64 projection of the maximum
  admitted decoded Task-ID UTF-8 bytes fits the one-HTTP-field-value
  ceiling at both default and hard settings. The quoted/escaped raw
  JSON-token ceiling remains independently binding only at JSON
  admission; it is never projected into `Mcp-Name`. Enclosing header-
  section/body/message bounds remain independently binding. TASK-02
  may store only TASK-01's
  canonical 43-byte locally issued form, while TASK-03 must retain any
  bounded opaque peer form. Its resume codec maps the admitted ID to a
  fixed-size framework-owned opaque store key and authenticates the
  original exact ID inside the record; no raw peer string becomes a
  filesystem path, database namespace, log label, metric label, or
  authorization fact. GATE-TASKS-READY owns the concrete end-to-end
  proof.
- Assign the dedicated icon-data-URI prefix and encoded rows, decoded
  icon-byte row, exact Base64 expansion, and enclosing JSON-RPC/result/
  icon-array bounds jointly to PRT-02. The ordinary `AbsoluteUri` byte
  ceiling
  continues to govern every non-`data:` icon URI and every non-icon
  URI, but does
  not truncate a separately admitted image data URI. Reserve the
  encoded JSON string, canonical prefix, prospective decoded bytes,
  and active decode memory before Base64 materialization; the per-icon
  row never overrides the enclosing message/body ceiling.
- Assign MRTR round/input/state/time rows and every sampling
  system-prompt, stop-sequence, provider-metadata, model-hint, token,
  call, tool, concurrency, and cost row to MRTR-03. Reserve exact
  prospective counts/bytes/tokens/cost before UI/provider work and hold
  cumulative exchange charges across retry IDs and rounds; dropping or
  transforming an optional provider field does not refund already
  incurred parsing/review work or permit a larger replacement.
- Assign every local journal frame/field, checkpoint chunk,
  total/dead-history/delta/residual byte, recovery scan/index,
  generation/compaction/cutover, file-operation/broker, deadline/batch,
  and transition-rate row to TASKP-01 and
  GATE-TASKS-READY. Admission occurs before append, startup scan,
  index growth, or compaction; crossing the total/dead-history ceiling
  stops new Task admission and triggers bounded compaction/quarantine,
  never an unbounded startup scan or silent history discard.
- Assign the durable Task descriptor/input/result member bounds and
  the enclosing control-section, application-section, authenticated
  outer-header, complete-record, and local data-frame checked-sum rows
  to TASK-02; TASKP-01 additionally enforces the local frame enclosure.
  Reserve from innermost members through every enclosing aggregate
  before serialization/sealing, and reject the transition if any
  level would overflow even when each sibling member is individually
  valid.
- Assign every Task-service admission-permit count/memory/lifetime,
  coalesced recovery-watermark count/memory, ready-queue count/byte,
  recovery-page/cursor/snapshot, scan
  concurrency/rate/deadline, initial-recovery, and maximum-rescan row
  to TASK-02 and GATE-TASKS-READY. Reserve permit count and memory
  before durable create and release it exactly once on create failure,
  durable acceptance, cancellation, or expiry. Charge a candidate
  before enqueue, retain its owner/deployment charge until claim/drop,
  and fall back to the already bounded coalesced recovery watermark or
  pause scanning on queue saturation; a committed Task is not rejected.
  A cursor expiry restarts from backend authority without retaining an
  unbounded snapshot or busy-looping.
- Assign every durable client Task-resume record count/byte/page/cursor
  row and the positive configured local poll-fallback row to TASK-03.
  The selected `TaskResumeStore` charges before serialization, insert,
  load, or update; its retention can never outlive the authoritative
  Task expiration, and absence of that store is the explicit volatile-
  resume profile rather than implicit durability. The one-second poll
  value is a FastMCP default inside the configured hard ceiling, not an
  extension-defined interval.
- Assign every Redis-specific section/record, RESP2 frame/line/bulk/
  cell/nesting/scratch, queued/active byte, script source, KEYS/ARGV,
  hash/zset, return, temporary-copy, command/loop/instruction/work-score,
  logical/resident-memory, `maxmemory`, process-memory, non-dataset/
  rewrite-COW carve, per-mutation dirty reservation, COW/RSS evidence
  and quiesce/action deadlines, AOF-generation/rewrite, and
  durable-volume row to TASKR-01 and
  GATE-REDIS-TASKS-READY. These are deliberately
  stricter profile limits: the effective Redis Task member/section/
  record allowance is the minimum of the generic Tasks and Redis rows.
  Validate the complete nested inequalities at configuration time:
  members plus canonical/envelope/header overhead fit the Redis section
  and record caps; command plus RESP framing fits the request cap;
  every reply fits its frame; and parser/script copies across admitted
  active connections fit deployment memory. A generic 60 MiB Task
  record is not accepted by this Redis profile.
- Charge count, byte, and rate admission to stable
  `QuotaPartitionKey` plus the applicable global cap while continuing
  to use the purpose-specific key for lookup and data isolation.
- Before OAuth client/user authentication exists, charge issuer
  endpoints to a fixed-size keyed pre-auth source bucket plus the
  deployment cap; after a client or owner is verified, additionally
  charge its stable verified partition. DCR/client-ID/token churn never
  creates a fresh pre-auth bucket. Charge AUTH-07's local pending flow
  and listener to `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` plus deployment, not to a
  fabricated `QuotaPartitionKey`.
- Apply the same rule to every `IngressAuthenticator`: admit the attempt,
  signature/JWT crypto, opaque-token introspection, and unknown-`kid`
  refresh against `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` plus deployment before
  expensive work. Each attempt has one finite deadline within the
  request budget and one declared peak CPU/memory/input bound.
  Cancellation of an in-flight non-preemptible verifier retains charges
  until completion and discards the late result; an introspection
  mutation or provider-side uncertainty is reconciled without treating
  the request as authenticated.
- Route opaque-token introspection through FND-05's shared lower-layer
  guarded fetcher, using the same policy primitives later consumed by
  AUTH-03, with no ambient proxy, identity content coding, pinned destination,
  TLS/hostname/root checks, bounded headers/body/connect/read/total
  time, bounded connections, and redacted credentials. Make
  unknown-`kid` JWKS refresh canonical-issuer singleflight; apply
  issuer and source rate limits, negative caching/backoff, and a bounded
  stale-key policy so random `kid` values cannot cause one fetch each.
  A refresh failure never turns signature failure into success.
- Charge proxied operations to both the downstream stable quota
  partition and configured upstream/deployment domain.
- Default configuration rejects creation or proxying of a null-TTL
  Task. TASK-02 may enable it only together with its audited retention
  administrator; retained count and bytes remain charged until that
  administrator performs a fenced deletion.
- Apply Section 5.1's composed Tasks policy to `ttlMs` and
  `pollIntervalMs`; do not infer it from the raw generated schema.
- Apply Section 5.1's
  `task_id_profile=fastmcp-opaque-task-id-v1` to every create/get/
  update/cancel result or parameter, Task notification, subscription
  filter/acknowledgement, `Mcp-Name`, durable server key, and client
  resume record before semantic use.
- Apply configured ceilings only to FastMCP-owned discretionary
  fallback sleeps and cache retention, without rewriting the peer's
  wire value. A peer-stated minimum delay is a floor: local policy may
  wait longer or let the operation budget expire, but cannot clamp it
  downward and act earlier.
- Use monotonic receipt time for freshness and deadlines.
- Reject values that cannot convert safely to local duration types.
- Define each bound's failure surface: transport status, JSON-RPC
  error, local client error, or configuration error.
- Reject invalid builder configurations at construction.
- Expose safe aggregate diagnostics without payloads, token material,
  URIs containing secrets, or schema bodies.
- Make queue overflow policy explicit per stream: cancel the affected
  request or subscription with a deterministic terminal outcome.
- Specify that TASK-02 must make quota admission plus descriptor
  creation atomic and that HTTP-06 must complete supervisor admission
  before returning 202; verify those rules in their owning packages
  and profile gates.
- Specify bounded cleanup and deterministic saturation contracts;
  consuming stores own their concrete retry/dead-letter behavior.
- Make each coverage-manifest row name its concrete consuming package,
  profile gate, and test IDs. LIMIT-01 validates only the catalog,
  ownership schema, arithmetic, and generic admission primitives, so it
  can close before its consumers without a hidden dependency cycle.
  Each consuming package owns its actual parser/store/provider/race/
  soak tests; the applicable promotion gate and final release aggregate
  reject any row whose named consumer test is absent, skipped, or
  failing.
- Do not claim a synchronous validator can be asynchronously
  preempted. Static schema/instance admission and a bounded blocking
  pool limit exposure but are not a general execution-fuel guarantee;
  SCH-01 must keep its hard work-budget support claim blocked until an
  exact instrumented engine prerequisite exists.

Acceptance:

- Every limit named elsewhere in this plan resolves to one field.
- Every known retained-state owner and parser has one manifest entry,
  one consuming package, and one profile gate; the manifest rejects
  an unowned or unbounded surface.
- Defaults and hard ceilings are visible in generated API docs.
- No byte/count/time conversion uses unchecked arithmetic.
- Snapshot meet/tightening, checked arithmetic, and common reservation
  helpers have transport-independent semantics.
- The package's own tests prove the catalog and primitives; later
  profile gates, not this foundational package, prove all concrete
  store races, failure surfaces, and long-running memory bounds.

Tests:

- Default-value and builder-boundary tests.
- Checked-arithmetic tests at integer and duration limits.
- Snapshot inheritance and componentwise-tightening tests.
- Partition/global reservation commit, rollback, and saturation tests.
- Generic synthetic-work partition/deployment fairness, queued-byte/
  rate/active-memory saturation, cancelled-queue removal,
  late-completion charge retention, and no-inline-fallback tests over
  the common admission primitives only.
- Generic fixed-bucket/verified-partition registry creation,
  saturation, refill-plus-idle retirement, penalty-reset prevention,
  concurrent last-release/new-create, quota-epoch migration, and
  count/byte accounting tests using synthetic identities only.
- Generic checked nested-count/byte lattice, Base64-length, decimal-
  duration, aggregate reservation, canonical single-line SSE
  `J+8`/`J+10` framing, bounded multiline-overhead, maximum-event-to-
  queue enclosure, Task-ID decoded/raw-token/raw-array arithmetic, and
  N-1/N/N+1 helper vectors; no protocol/parser/store implementation is
  imported.
- Coverage-manifest schema tests for missing/duplicate owner, missing
  bound, unknown package/gate/test ID, and deterministic row ordering.
  These use fixture manifests and do not require any consuming package
  to be implemented or closed.
- Redacted aggregate-diagnostic snapshots with synthetic labels and
  payloads.

Dependencies:

- FND-01.
- FND-04.

ORCHESTRATOR CLAIM BYPASS (audited, 2026-09-16, RubyOriole).

RubyOriole set this bead to in_progress using --force at repo revision 670b60db. The tracker refused the ordinary claim with "cannot claim blocked issue" because upstream blockers remain open.

That refusal is correct as a general rule but is not actionable here. The campaign DAG is approximately 132 waves deep with a median wave width of 5 and near-term waves only 1-4 items wide; `br ready` returns 0 against 712 open beads; 0 of 145 work packages are closed. Nothing can start without deliberate frontier assignment by the orchestrator. AGENTS.md provides for exactly this: "Where the installed tracker cannot enforce a rule mechanically, the orchestrator must enforce and audit it." This comment is that audit record, so the bypass is visible rather than silent.

SCOPE OF THE BYPASS: claim and assignment ONLY.

The close gates are NOT bypassed and will not be. `never_direct_close` on every non-review path, and `review -> closed` under the `batch_verify` gate, remain in force. This bead closes only on a green, revision-bound RCH batch verified centrally by RubyOriole, citing the commit SHA and the exact test IDs that exercised its acceptance criteria.

Individual agents are forbidden from using --force for claims; this bypass is centralized in the orchestrator deliberately so that there is one auditable actor rather than five.

comments.text:
FND01TREEv1 AT c0315e38, PLUS THE METHOD SO NOBODY NEEDS ME FOR IT AGAIN.
(OliveOwl, 2026-09-17)

FIRST, A CORRECTION: FND01TREEv1 IS NOT MY CONSTRUCTION.

It is this repository's own format, defined in
evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml:149-152:

    format          = "FND01TREEv1"
    ordering        = "ascending raw path bytes"
    record_encoding = "u32be(path_len) || path || u64be(file_len) || raw_sha256(file_bytes)"

I adopted it rather than inventing one, precisely so the receipts would use a
spec already frozen in the evidence document. The bus factor was my
implementation of it, not the algorithm - and the script below removes that.

VALUES AT c0315e38, computed from git objects at that revision:

  scope C  crates/fastmcp/src/ (tracked)
    eb82f22b5a9dfd06ac82ea91fe8139311c124e0444c84264260a61df2d2d8e17
    16 files, 847620 bytes

  scope D  crates/fastmcp/ (tracked)
    633ee5719bb22a86c42dc7268d2a86e38006a7c507b7e1b44a7fa6fdf029bb4c
    88 files, 19196102 bytes

DID D MOVE AGAIN? NO. Both C and D are byte-identical between a75b839b and
c0315e38. I verified by computing each at BOTH revisions rather than assuming.

Read that result carefully, because it is easy to draw the wrong lesson from
it: it does NOT mean transcription is safe as a rule. It means it happened to
be safe across these two revisions, and there was no way to know that without
checking. Your refusal to carry the values forward was correct on the
evidence available to you at the time, and it stays correct as a standing
practice. A digest that is unchanged is a measurement, not an assumption.

THE METHOD, RUNNABLE. Paste and run; no dependency on me.

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """FND01TREEv1 digest over a git-tracked path prefix at a given revision.

    Encoding per evidence/fnd-01/dependency-verification.toml:149-152.
      usage: fnd01treev1.py <revision> <path-prefix>
      e.g.   fnd01treev1.py c0315e38 crates/fastmcp/src
    """
    import hashlib, struct, subprocess, sys

    def tracked(rev, prefix):
        out = subprocess.run(["git","ls-tree","-r","--name-only","-z",rev,prefix],
                             capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        return [p for p in out.decode().split("\0") if p]

    def blob(rev, path):
        return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{rev}:{path}"],
                              capture_output=True, check=True).stdout

    def fnd01treev1(rev, prefix):
        paths = sorted(tracked(rev, prefix), key=lambda s: s.encode())
        buf, total = bytearray(), 0
        for rel in paths:
            data = blob(rev, rel)
            total += len(data)
            name = rel.encode()
            buf += struct.pack(">I", len(name)) + name
            buf += struct.pack(">Q", len(data)) + hashlib.sha256(data).digest()
        return hashlib.sha256(bytes(buf)).hexdigest(), len(paths), total

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        rev, prefix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
        d, n, t = fnd01treev1(rev, prefix)
        print(f"{d}  {n} files  {t} bytes  ({prefix} @ {rev})")

TWO DESIGN POINTS THAT MAKE IT CORRECT, worth knowing before you trust it:

  1. It reads blobs from GIT, never the working tree. So the digest is bound
     to the revision, and is unaffected by dirty state or by another pane
     editing a file mid-run. Reading the working tree would reintroduce
     exactly the hazard your dirty=0 before-and-after check exists to close.
  2. The file set comes from git ls-tree at that revision, so selection is
     reproducible rather than filesystem-order dependent - the same class of
     hazard as picking a binary by find order.

Two gotchas if you adapt it: in zsh, "$REV:crates/..." must be quoted or
braced, since :c is a parameter modifier and will silently eat a character;
and sort by ENCODED bytes, not by str, or non-ASCII paths order differently
from the spec.

I have not landed this as a repo file - it is tooling, not product capability,
and creating files is not something I will do unasked. If you want it
permanent, say where and I will put it there.

SELF-CORRECTION TO MY OWN COMMENT 2474 — the zero-run evidence was unsound.
The CONCLUSION survives by a different route; the EVIDENCE I gave for it did not.
HazyTurtle (LANE 2), 2026-09-17. Nobody asked for this; re-reading my own record
against what I learned later.

WHAT I WROTE IN 2474:
  "The workspace has exactly 4 zero-run targets and NONE carries a frozen acceptance
   ID: three are the fastmcp_derive proc-macro lib target and one is the
   examples/echo_server.rs binary."

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT. I derived that attribution by pairing each "0 tests, 0
benchmarks" line with the nearest preceding "Running ..." line in a
`cargo test --workspace -- --list` log. **That pairing is unsound.** A workspace
listing runs its test binaries CONCURRENTLY and their stdout INTERLEAVES, so proximity
carries no attribution. I demonstrated this afterwards on the same log: walking back
from the `crypto::tests::` rows lands on the `fastmcp_derive` binary, which has four
tests in total and cannot own them.

So "three are fastmcp_derive and one is echo_server" is a claim I cannot support from
that log. The COUNT of four zero-test blocks is fine — counting is attribution-free —
but which targets they belong to is not established by what I did.

THE CONCLUSION STILL HOLDS, by a route that does not need attribution at all. The
substantive claim was "no frozen acceptance ID is hiding behind a zero-run target". For
this bead's four frozen IDs that is provable directly: all four were DISCOVERED BY NAME
in the listing —

    limit_01_i_positive
    limit_01_i_planted_negative
    limit_01_integration_public_join
    limit_01_integration_lifecycle_join

— and a test inside a zero-run target cannot be enumerated at all. Name-occurrence
counting is attribution-free, so that half of 2474 stands unchanged. An ID that appears
in the listing is in some target that ran; it does not matter which.

WHAT I AM WITHDRAWING: the specific identification of the four zero-run targets, and
any reading of 2474 as evidence about the WORKSPACE as a whole. It is evidence about
these four IDs only.

HOW TO ESTABLISH THE WITHDRAWN PART PROPERLY, if anyone needs it: run
`cargo test -p <pkg> --lib -- --list` per target — one binary per invocation, nothing to
interleave. That is the same method that later corrected my `fastmcp-server` T figure
from 2204 (interleaved) to 1926 (per-target), a 278-row error in the same class.

WHY I AM POSTING THIS RATHER THAN LEAVING IT. 2474 was honest when written and its
verdict is unchanged — the integration bead is still MET, and I still found nothing to
disprove. But a later reader would have taken the zero-run sentence as a measured fact
about the workspace, and it is not one. A submission that was honest when written can
become misleading once the method under it is known to be broken, and correcting that
is cheaper than having someone else discover it downstream.

No status change. No verdict change. I close nothing.

batch-pending, so this is a pre-verification audit rather than a post-mortem.

VERDICT: NO TAUTOLOGY FOUND. This is a concurrence, not a finding — but a
verified one. Each check below was executed against the source, not inferred
from the bead's own description.

=== SINGULARITY (frozen-ID uniqueness) — CLEAN ============================
All four claimed IDs have EXACTLY ONE definition workspace-wide:

all in crates/fastmcp/tests/limit_01_integration.rs. No bare-name filter can

=== REACHABILITY — CLEAN =================================================
No explicit [[test]] entry in crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml, so the target is
auto-discovered with NO required-features, and there is no file-scope
#![cfg(...)] gate. It cannot zero-run the way fnd_01_dependency_evidence did
behind required-features = ["testing-lab"].

=== PL-3 / SHIPPED SURFACE — CLEAN =======================================
The external target reaches the capability through `use fastmcp_rust::{...}`,
the packaged facade, with no `use super` and no pub(crate). The four types under
test are shipped, non-cfg(test), top-level public items in fastmcp-core:
  ProtocolLimit :125   ProtocolLimits :237
  AdmissionError :1020 AdmissionController :1124

CAUTION FOR THE NEXT READER, because I nearly mis-called this: a naive "nearest
preceding #[cfg(test)]" scan reports line 54 for all four and looks damning.
Line 54 is `#[cfg(test)] mod limit_01_rows;` — a test-only DATA module
declaration, not a test-module boundary. It contains no #[test] functions; it
holds the ordered acceptance rows and digest receipts the tests iterate. The
four types are declared after it at top level and are genuinely shipped. I made
this same misread twice today on other files; anchor on `^#\[cfg(test)\]$`
immediately followed by `mod tests`, not on the nearest match.

=== PATTERN 1, structural restatement — GUARDED ==========================
limit_01_integration_public_join opens with
  assert_eq!(rows.len(), PUBLIC_JOIN_CASES.len())
which on its own IS the structural tautology (rows are derived from cases, so
this can only observe len==len). It is immediately followed by an INDEPENDENT
numeric floor:
  assert_eq!(rows.len(), 6, "AC-LIMIT-I-01 numeric floor is 6 ordered rows")
and by an exact frozen-order assertion on the six subcase IDs
(LIMIT-I-01.01 .. .06). The independent constant is what makes the structural
assertion non-vacuous: dropping a case fails the floor even though len==len
would still hold. This is the correct construction.

=== PATTERN 3, oracle from the expected answer — CONSIDERED, NOT UPHELD ===
documented_limits() builds the catalog from DEFAULT_* constants, and
configured_bound_rows() asserts the catalog contains those same DEFAULT_*
values. That is self-referential, and I initially flagged it.

It is NOT pattern 3, for a reason worth stating: these are DECLARED DESIGN
LIMITS, not measurements of mutable content. Per the discriminator this campaign
already uses, a measurement rots and must be re-derived; a declared design limit
does not rot and its authority IS its declaration. There is no external spec
value to bind to because the bound is chosen, not observed. What the assertion
proves is builder/accessor round-trip fidelity, which is a real if modest
property.

THE BOUNDED CLAIM, which the bead should not exceed: this proves the shipped
builder honours the configured bounds. It does NOT prove the bound VALUES are
the right ones, and nothing in this target could. If any submission language
says the documented bounds are "verified" rather than "honoured", that wording
overstates it.

=== PATTERN 5, planted negative that cannot fail — CLEAN, and notably good =
limit_01_i_planted_negative is among the better negatives I have read in this
campaign:
  - a FRESH controller per mutation, so no state leaks between cases;
  - exactly one variable moves, N -> N+1 requested units;
  - the control path is asserted with a FULL nine-field state struct
    (generation, global_in_use, three partition counters, committed_work,
    release_count, admission_count, live_reservations), not a boolean;
  - the mutated path requires a TYPED refusal carrying the requested value,
    AdmissionError::PartitionCapacityExceeded { requested: N + 1, .. };
  - `before = full_state(&mutated)` is captured for the unchanged-state proof.
It also ships assert_one_variable_unit_step(), a helper that MECHANICALLY
asserts two cases differ in exactly one variable. That converts RH-5 from a
reviewer's judgement into an executable check, which is better practice than
most of this campaign including my own work.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK ===============================================
Whether these tests PASS. I ran no cargo test — the verification lane is the
binding constraint at 27+ pending beads and re-dispatching a submitted bead's
target would consume a slot to learn what the orchestrator's batch will report
anyway. This audit is a source audit: it establishes that the proofs are
CONSTRUCTED honestly and are admissible, not that they are green.

=== ONE ITEM FOR THE AUTHOR, not a defect ================================
crates/fastmcp-core/src/limit_01_rows.rs is #[cfg(test)]. It contains no #[test]

                and re-asserted after reserve and across the lifecycle.

That genuinely establishes "B consumes exactly the accepted A snapshot" through public
entrypoints. What is missing is narrower and specific: the digest is not built over the
A/B RECEIPT IDS the AC names it over. A change to an A row's identity or to an A/B digest
cannot move LIMIT01-I-PUBLIC-JOIN-v1, because the join never observed them — which is the
drift the receipt-ID binding exists to pin.

Emit the A and B canonical receipts as their own ordered rows inside joined_receipt before
the observed tuple, so a change in either necessarily moves the integration digest. The
rows already exist and are already proved sensitive in
crates/fastmcp-core/tests/limit_01_rows/mod.rs; the obstacle is that it is a fastmcp-core
TEST module, not a public surface, so the facade target cannot `use` it. Either (a) lift
the receipt builders to a shared test-support surface both targets can reach, or (b) have
this leaf emit the A/B receipt IDs it joins by name and bind them to the values it already
re-derives. (b) is smaller and needs no API change.

I am NOT doing either unilaterally: it changes a versioned receipt surface that
bd-mcp-limit-01-verification-1j2v and the formal LIMIT-01 aggregate both consume, which is
a cross-bead decision.

(comments 2875 and 2876). Neither can be transitioned: `open -> review` is not a permitted
workflow transition, and `--claim` is refused with "cannot claim blocked issue: bd-63l5,
bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.1" (FND-04 and FND-01, both still open). Reported, not
bypassed.

Supersedes the disposition in my comment 2878 on this bead. There I called the
missing A/B receipt-ID binding a shortfall on items 1 and 3, real but narrower than

=== WHAT CHANGED ===
bd-mcp-limit-01-verification-1j2v (LIMIT-01 V) was assigned to me. Its item 1:

and not a pattern that matches nothing.

(src/limit_01_rows.rs, tests/limit_01_rows/mod.rs, src/lib.rs, tests/limit_01_a.rs) and ZERO

carries them through.

TREE-WIDE grep returns 14 for each of the six and looks like a refutation of this finding. It
is not -- it answers a different question. The claim is about the INTEGRATION RECEIPT, and only
a receipt-scoped count tests it. Two measurements disagreeing by that much are measuring
different populations, not disputing one.

CONSEQUENCE 1: V item 1 cannot be satisfied at this revision, and the fix is NOT V's. The
integration bead must carry A's and B's canonical digests into its receipt first. This is a
THIRD reason bd-mcp-limit-01-integration-s0b9 is unfinished, alongside items 1 and 2 already
open on the missing shipped join.

Rationale: existing conformant quartet retained and strengthened in place.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### LIMIT-01 — Define central bounds and admission primitives

Outcome:

Define the one finite, configurable bounds catalog and the common
admission primitives that every consuming package must enforce.

Reason:

Scattered limits create gaps, conflicting behavior, overflow hazards,
and tests that cannot state which bound is normative for FastMCP.

This package owns the opaque, non-authorizing `QuotaPartitionKey`
shell, the distinct pre-verification `PreAuthSourceBucketKey`, policy
types, snapshots, common arithmetic/admission helpers, and an
exhaustive owner matrix. Their constructors remain sealed; AUTH-00
owns `QuotaPartitionKey` derivation from verified security facts and
cannot replace it with a string or request-supplied identifier.
Transport ingress derives `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` only from the
listener domain and a trusted transport-observed source bucket under
the configured trusted-proxy policy. It uses a keyed, fixed-cardinality
bucket space plus deployment caps, so spoofed addresses or source churn
cannot allocate unbounded limiter state; collisions only tighten
admission and never authorize. This dependency direction lets raw
protocol and credential-verification admission use finite limits
without depending on the later auth model.
It does not claim that not-yet-implemented caches, Tasks, subscriptions,
or proxies already enforce their rows; those feature packages and
their profile gates own enforcement and aggregate proof.

Implementation:

- Add a validated `ProtocolLimits` in `fastmcp-core`.
- Add the sealed opaque `QuotaPartitionKey` value domain and generic
  partition/global reservation interfaces without embedding auth
  claims or exposing a public constructor. AUTH-00 later supplies the
  only production derivation service.
- Add the sealed `PreAuthSourceBucketKey` and an
  `AdmissionPartition::{PreAuth, Verified}` sum type. Raw-header/body
  admission and authenticator work begin in `PreAuth`; after successful
  verification, reservations atomically transfer or add the verified
  partition charge. No code fabricates a `QuotaPartitionKey` for an
  unauthenticated request.
- Add a distinct non-authorizing `AuthorizationFlowQuotaKey` for
  client-side pre-token flows, derived only from validated configured
  issuer, canonical resource, client registration/application
  identity, redirect-driver class, and auth profile. It never uses an
  access token, resource-owner claim, attacker-supplied client ID, or
  network address.
- Capture an immutable snapshot per request, subscription, MRTR

- Require an Apps synthetic liveness-tick interval to be strictly
  positive and shorter than the configured Apps request idle timeout,
  and require that idle timeout to be shorter than the absolute
  lifetime. A tick exists only for a live request that supplied a
  progress token, counts against both control-notification and output
  budgets, and can reset idle time but never the absolute lifetime.

- Add a second, equally normative retained-state capacity table.
  “Partition” means AUTH-00's stable `QuotaPartitionKey`, endpoint/
  origin configuration domain, or an explicitly named internal
  deployment domain; it never means a token-churning lookup key.
  Purpose-specific security keys still isolate lookup and eviction
  visibility. “Global” means one process for an in-memory store and
  one deployment namespace for a shared store.
