title: Native-pipe spin: an Interrupted pipe bound to a foreign/cancelled Cx is retried forever by the stdio transport (shipped 0.12.0 known issue #84, zero bead coverage)
description:
The v0.12.0 CHANGELOG "Known issues" section discloses this defect against the
shipped release, and NO bead tracks it. Searched the full tracker text (title +
description) on 2026-10-11 for "#84", "task spins", and "ManagedHttpClient makes
one more": zero matches. GitHub issue #84 is therefore the only record, which
means `br ready` can never surface it and the batch-verify pump cannot see it.

DEFECT (quoted from CHANGELOG.md v0.12.0 Known issues):

  "Opt-in native pipes: a pipe whose own `Cx` is cancelled or past its deadline
  keeps returning `Interrupted`, which the stdio transport retries while its
  serving `Cx` is live, so the task spins (#84). Bind a native pipe to the same
  `Cx` that serves it."

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS LABEL SUGGESTS

This is not a peripheral opt-in wart. `NativePipeReader`/`NativePipeWriter` are
the ONLY in-tree path that delivers genuinely non-blocking, reactor-driven
own-process stdio. The default entry point documented in every README example,
`Server::run_stdio_with_cx` (crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:15839), instead
runs `cx.spawn_blocking(... run_stdio_pump ...)` over
`StdioTransport::stdio()` + `AsyncStdout::new()`, both of which perform
blocking I/O by their own module documentation
(crates/fastmcp-transport/src/async_io.rs:14-18: "they perform blocking I/O
internally. An async trait alone does not make those standard-stream
operations nonblocking.").

So the capability that would actually realize this project's headline
differentiator -- cancel-correct non-blocking async -- is the capability
carrying an unbudgeted busy-spin failure mode. A spin is the worst possible
failure shape for a cancellation-correctness framework: it consumes the very
runtime the cancellation story depends on, and it is reached precisely by the
mistake a caller is most likely to make (binding the pipe to a different `Cx`
than the one serving it).

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY

This bead does not claim the default stdio path should switch to native pipes;
that is a separate wiring/design decision (see the companion README bead). It
claims only that the spin is a defect in a shipped surface and needs either a
bounded fix or a fail-closed refusal.

SUGGESTED SHAPE OF A FIX (not frozen; the owner decides)

Prefer fail-closed over retry-forever. Two candidate directions:

1. REFUSE AT BIND. Make the constructor that associates a pipe with a serving
   context detect a foreign/cancelled/expired `Cx` and return an error, rather
   than letting the mismatch surface later as an endless `Interrupted`. Note
   bd-8n2is already concerns a related registration/ambient-capability defect
   in the same module; coordinate so the two fixes do not race.
2. BOUND THE RETRY. If the transport must keep retrying `Interrupted`, give
   that retry loop a budget/deadline observation so a permanently-interrupted
   pipe terminates the serving task with a diagnostic instead of spinning.

ACCEPTANCE (positive + near-identical planted negative, per RH-5)

- POSITIVE: a native pipe bound to the SAME `Cx` that serves it completes a
  tools/call round trip over real pipes, and the serving task yields (observed
  via a bounded poll/wake count or elapsed CPU, not just exit status).
- NEGATIVE (near-identical, differing ONLY in the forbidden dimension): a
  native pipe bound to a DIFFERENT / already-cancelled / past-deadline `Cx`
  terminates with a typed diagnostic within a stated bound. It must NOT spin.
  Assert the bound explicitly; a test that merely finishes proves nothing,
  because a spin that happens to be short still passes an exit-status check.
- Record evaluator, observed field, predicate and minimum count (PL-2). Exit
  status alone is not evidence for either case.

PROOF CLASS: unit/planted-red over real pipes (the existing
crates/fastmcp-server/tests/native_stdio_pipes.rs is the natural host; it
compiles and runs today -- see the correction note on bd-m8sy7).

CONFIGURATION BINDING (PL-3): Unix only; `native_pipe` is `#[cfg(unix)]`.
Record profile, target and features with the result.

FILED BY the 2026-10-11 reality check (RealityCheck-Opus5-20261011) at HEAD
31c73d6d. This bead records a tracker-coverage gap plus a product defect; it is
NOT a claim that any other lane erred.

comments.text:

not editing the file, not disputing anything. Two things worth knowing, one of

title: Wire fidelity: elicitation mode wrongly required; SamplingCapability drops tools/context
description:
Wire-type fidelity defects against the vendored official MCP 2026-07-28 schema (spec/mcp-2026-07-28/schema.json), found by the 2026-10-01 protocol audit and re-verified by hand:

1. `FinalEmbeddedElicitationParams` and `ElicitRequestFormParams` REQUIRE `mode`, but the official `ElicitRequestFormParams.required` is ["message", "requestedSchema"]; the official example InputRequiredResult/input-required-result-with-elicitation-and-sampling-and-request-state.json omits `mode`. A spec-valid input_required result / elicitation request is refused.
2. `SamplingCapability {}` is an empty struct, so `{"sampling":{"tools":{}}}` round-trips to `{"sampling":{}}`; the stdio and WebSocket clients build per-request capabilities from it and can never advertise sampling.tools / sampling.context.

Fix: absent mode decodes as form (both types); SamplingCapability gains optional `context` and `tools` objects (+ with_tools / with_context).

Acceptance: decode of the official example with elicitation lacking mode succeeds; {"sampling":{"tools":{},"context":{}}} round-trips exactly; unit tests in fastmcp-protocol.

Placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, validator/test weakening, golden regeneration around broken behavior, and follow-up laundering are forbidden. Before claim, the assignee must replace the preclaim-denied ownership card with exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No whole-crate or repository glob is valid.

Self-contained canonical parent contract follows verbatim:

Authoritative work package from `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_SUPPORT_MCP_2026-07-28_SPEC_IN_FASTMCP_RUST.md`:

### PXY-04 — Reconstruct HTTP routing and auth safely

Outcome:

Generate correct upstream HTTP headers without forwarding downstream
credentials or unsafe custom values.

Reason:

Headers are derived protocol data and authorization is audience-bound.

Implementation:

- Recompute protocol version.
- Recompute method.
- Recompute name.
- Recompute annotated parameter headers from validated schemas.
- Apply exact encoding.
- Consume only HTTP-02's `ValidatedForwardingHeaders` capsule; proxy
  code never receives or reconstructs raw ingress headers.
- Forward every capsule field unchanged as required for an
  intermediate server unless it conflicts case-insensitively with a
  recognized field the gateway recomputes.
- Require the capsule constructor to have enforced syntax, per-field,
  aggregate-count, and aggregate-byte bounds before authentication and
  to have excluded Authorization, Cookie, proxy credentials,
  hop-by-hop headers, and every ordinary MCP singleton header.
- Ignore unrecognized `Mcp-Param-*` fields locally; never interpret
  them as credentials or authorization facts.
- Acquire upstream-specific credentials.
- Never forward downstream Authorization directly.
- Detect the confused-deputy topology where this MCP proxy presents one
  static client ID to a third-party authorization server while
  accepting dynamically registered downstream clients. Before the
  first upstream authorization or forwarding action for each
  downstream client, require explicit user consent for the tuple
  `(verified user, downstream client_id, upstream issuer/resource,
  proxy static client_id, redirect URI, consent-policy revision)`.
- Persist that consent only through an injected authorization-owned
  consent store with bounded lifetime, revocation, exact tuple
  matching, redacted audit records, and fail-closed corruption/outage
  behavior. Consent for one downstream client, user, upstream, redirect
  URI, or policy revision never authorizes another.
- Require that store to return an opaque authenticated
  `ProxyConsentGrant` from a declared integrity/rollback-resistant
  trust boundary. Revalidate it before every upstream authorization/
  contact and throughout long-lived subscription/task work, not only
  before the first token acquisition. Include grant identity,
  revision, and expiry in upstream credential, cache, route,
  continuation, subscription, and task-mapping keys.
- On consent expiry/revocation/policy change, atomically prevent new
  upstream contact, drop cached upstream credentials, invalidate
  dependent caches/handles, and terminate active proxy streams/
  management work with an explicit outcome. Never continue using a
  cached token merely because consent existed when it was issued.
- On absence, denial, expiry, revocation, or tuple mismatch, do not
  contact the third-party authorization endpoint and do not forward
  the request. Static deployment configuration is not user consent.
- Strip hop-by-hop and unrecognized sensitive headers.
- Preserve only OBS-01's outbound-policy-approved trace context.
  Evaluate source/destination origin, tenant, and security domain on
  each hop; drop baggage/tracestate by default at a boundary and bind
  the policy revision to redacted route/cache diagnostics.
- Apply an explicit metadata policy: preserve registered extension
  metadata negotiated on both legs, preserve standard trace context
  under OBS-01, rewrite server identity, drop raw/unknown
  security-sensitive keys, and keep other unknown namespaced metadata
  only when the configured transparent-forwarding policy and both-leg
  size limits permit it.
- Before emitting a stateless modern extension notification upstream,
  consume the downstream `AuthorizedNotificationWork`, discard its
  sealed downstream activation proof, and build a distinct
  `UpstreamNotificationActivationProof` under the selected upstream
  descriptor, endpoint, credential/security partition, effective
  settings, owner, and descriptor/policy/configuration generations.
  For `SelfContained`, revalidate and reserialize only the sanitized
  extension-owned current-message field under the upstream schema and
  resolver. For `NegotiatedOwner`, resolve a gateway-owned mapping to a
  separately live upstream owner and revalidate that owner immediately;
  never copy the downstream handle or treat the mapping record itself
  as owner authority. If either construction fails, emit no upstream
  bytes and create no upstream handler/supervisor effect. No capsule,
  trace field, generic metadata, or forwarded header can substitute for
  this proof.
- Disable automatic redirects and reject every upstream MCP 3xx on
  both proxy legs. Never replay/retarget a request body, forward either
  leg's credentials/cookies/capsule to a Location, or rebind route,
  resource, era, consent, or cache identity. If the prior endpoint may
  have received bytes, propagate an explicit uncertain-dispatch
  outcome without retry.
- Redact both legs independently.

Acceptance:

- Header/body equality holds on the upstream request.
- Credentials are issued for the upstream resource.
- Downstream tokens never appear upstream.
- Header injection cannot cross the gateway.
- Unrecognized valid `Mcp-Param-*` headers survive one and multiple
  intermediary hops without local activation.
- No API permits gateway code to obtain a raw Authorization, Cookie,
  or arbitrary header map.
- Metadata never broadens extension negotiation or crosses a
  security-policy deny rule.
- Downstream notification activation evidence terminates at the
  gateway; upstream emission requires a separately sealed current-
  message proof with upstream bindings.
- A static upstream client ID cannot turn the proxy into a confused
  deputy for a dynamically registered downstream client.
- Cached credentials and long-lived proxy work cannot survive consent
  loss.

Tests:

- Header reconstruction.
- Base64 encoding.
- Credential audience isolation.
- Hop-by-hop stripping.
- CRLF injection.
- Unknown valid custom-header forwarding, collision, oversize, and
  multi-hop cases.
- Capsule construction/consumption compile tests and forbidden-header
  exclusion matrix.
- Same-trust trace propagation, cross-trust baggage/tracestate drop,
  sensitive allowlist denial, unrelated-upstream leakage, and
  trace-dependent cache-isolation tests.
- Metadata allow/drop/rewrite matrix.
- Stateless extension-notification proxy matrix covering independent
  self-contained reconstruction, negotiated-owner mapping/
  revalidation, downstream-proof/handle/generation substitution,
  stale or missing upstream owner, representation mismatch, and exact
  zero-byte upstream rejection.
- Per-downstream-client static-ID proxy consent, cross-client/user/
  upstream/redirect/policy isolation, denial-before-upstream-contact,
  expiry/revocation, consent-store outage/corruption, and redacted
  audit tests.
- Cached-token-after-consent-revocation, consent revision/key
  invalidation, active subscription/task mapping, stream teardown,
  rollback-resistant store, and no-upstream-contact-after-loss tests.
- Redacted dual-leg trace.
- 301/302/303/307/308 same/cross-origin rejection on both legs,
  method/body non-replay, credential/capsule stripping, DNS-rebinding
  Location, redirect loop, and partial-send uncertain-dispatch tests.

title: Two SEP-2322 SHOULD warnings: an MRTR response map naming no outstanding input is refused where the suite wants a re-request
description:
OWNER DECISION, NOT CODEABLE AS IT STANDS. Two SEP-2322 SHOULD-level checks
want a behaviour that is incompatible with a property this repository
deliberately tests. Nobody may implement either side unilaterally; the owner
picks one. Status is `blocked` for that reason and not for a dependency.

This description consolidates five separate read-only triages (comments below,
2026-10-04 through 2026-10-11, by RealityCheck-Opus55, RealityCheck-Opus5 twice,
IvoryPine and CrimsonFjord). It exists because the bead previously had NO
description -- the title was its entire content -- so every lane that reached it
re-derived the same analysis from scratch. Read this instead; the comments are
the evidence trail.

== THE TWO CHECKS ==
  input-required-result-missing-input-response:sep-2322-missing-response-rerequests
  input-required-result-ignore-extra-params:sep-2322-ignore-unexpected-params
Both WARNING level, so neither fails a run. They are the ONLY two non-success
checks left in server mode: measured 112 SUCCESS / 2 WARNING / 1 INFO / 0
FAILURE over 115 checks at 1c2dc896 (2026-10-12). Closing them would make it
114/115. That is the entire upside, and it is not a correctness gain.

== WHAT WE DO, AND WHERE ==
crates/fastmcp-server/src/bidirectional.rs. `accept_wire_entries_with_binding`
already SKIPS response keys naming no outstanding input, so extra/unknown keys
are tolerated whenever at least one key matches. What is refused is a map
matching NOTHING, at the early return around :2179-2183, with
MRTR_INPUT_MAP_ERROR ("Invalid MRTR input request or response map").

== WHY THIS IS A REAL CONFLICT AND NOT A REDUNDANT GUARD ==
The tempting reading -- and one triage pass reached it before correcting itself
the same day -- is that the refusal is redundant because the non-progress bound
already exists in `accept_at` (:2369-2383: `next_round > max_rounds`,
`missing_requests.len() > max_inputs_per_round`,
`next_total > max_total_input_requests`, which REMOVE the exchange at the
limit). That part is correct: there is no unbounded re-request DoS, so
resource exhaustion is NOT a reason to deviate from a SHOULD.

But the refusal is not protecting "progress" in the abstract. It protects a
specific, deliberately asserted property. crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs,
`workflow_public_http_state_only_mrtr_rejects_explicit_empty_without_consuming_state`:
the message assertion near :3468 is followed at :3474-3492 by the operative
clause -- the client reuses THE SAME `requestState` and the retry succeeds
("the unchanged absent-member retry consumes the retained continuation",
`resumed_calls == 1`). So after a nothing-matching map the client's existing
handle still works.

Satisfying `sep-2322-missing-response-rerequests` destroys that. Re-requesting
ROTATES by construction: `MrtrRetry::InputRequired` is documented at :1766-1769
as "only unsatisfied keys are reissued with a fresh request state", and
`accept_at` allocates `next_state` before consuming the current one. The round
limit bounds ABUSE; it does not preserve the client's handle. So the trade-off
is exactly: a surviving continuation handle across a malformed response map,
versus the harness-preferred re-request that invalidates it.

== A SECOND BLOCKER: CHANGING THE WIRE GUARD ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT ==
`accept_at` independently rejects no-progress typed retries when
`exchange.requests` is nonempty (around :2356), and
crates/fastmcp-server/tests/http_continuation_replay/successors.rs::
`public_invalid_admitted_successor_stays_fenced_instead_of_restarting_earlier_step`
exercises a nonempty successor with an unknown-only input map and REQUIRES
rejection/fencing. Relaxing only the empty-map guard would not preserve that
replay contract. Any relaxation therefore spans at least two refusal sites and
two pinned tests.

== AUTHORITY, STATED HONESTLY ==
The MCP schema carries no MUST/SHOULD text for this case:
`$defs.InputResponses` says only "Keys correspond to the keys in the
InputRequests map". So the authority for the suite's preference is the harness
expectation, not schema text. Do not cite schema backing for a relaxation.

== ONE FALSE TRAIL TO SKIP ==
tasks.rs:1224 `update_input` looks like the subject and is NOT: its
`impl OfficialTaskLifecycle` at :1086 sits under `#[cfg(test)]` at :1085, so it
is retired scaffolding, and it returns `Ignored` rather than refusing. The
shipped admission is the `Final*` family keyed on `FinalTaskInputResponses`
(tasks.rs :1696, :1804-1813, :1972, :1988, :3242, :3269, :3384, :3415, :3440).
One false bead (bd-dj5am) was already filed in this file by missing that gating.

== TO UNBLOCK: THE OWNER PICKS ONE ==

(A) KEEP THE REFUSAL. Then say so in the README and the adapter so the two
    warnings read as intentional, record it in
    scripts/conformance-expected-failures.yaml (which already carries both,
    currently described as a deliberate fail-closed choice), and close this as
    not-a-defect. Server mode stays 112/115 permanently and that is a decision,
    not a gap.

(B) RELAX TO THE SUITE'S PREFERENCE. Then the acceptance is:
    - positive: an empty-matching map re-requests exactly the outstanding keys
      with a FRESH requestState;
    - RH-5 planted negative: a map for an EXPIRED or cancelled request_state is
      still refused;
    - the `..._rejects_explicit_empty_without_consuming_state` assertion AND its
      same-state reuse leg are retired by explicit semantic review, which is
      RH-3-sensitive and must not be done as a drive-by;
    - the `..._stays_fenced_instead_of_restarting_earlier_step` replay contract
      is either preserved or deliberately changed with its own review;
    - the round/total limits remain the abuse bound;
    - conformance-expected-failures.yaml and the README standing are updated
      with the measured result.

NO-CLAIM: this description establishes the conflict, its two blockers, and what
each branch costs. It does NOT decide, does not claim our behaviour is wrong (a
SHOULD warning is not a defect), and earns no capability credit.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus55
comments.text:
Measured 2026-10-04, @modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.10, --spec-version 2026-07-28
--suite all. Two of the four remaining WARNING-level checks:

  input-required-result-missing-input-response:sep-2322-missing-response-rerequests
  input-required-result-ignore-extra-params:sep-2322-ignore-unexpected-params

ESTABLISHED INDEPENDENT. Both survived the roots/list descriptor fix (bd-3oqg8) byte-identical, so
they do NOT share that cause. When I filed bd-3oqg8 I guessed they might; the measurement refutes
it.

THIS IS A DESIGN TENSION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. crates/fastmcp-server/src/bidirectional.rs,
accept_wire_entries_with_binding, already skips response keys that name no outstanding input, so
extra/unknown keys ARE tolerated when at least one key matches. What it refuses is a map matching
NOTHING, with a stated reason in the code:

    A map that names none of the outstanding inputs is not a partial retry. Rotating it would burn
    a valid continuation without making progress, so reject it before the current state can be
    consumed.

The suite would prefer the server treat that as a no-op and RE-REQUEST the outstanding inputs
instead of erroring. Both positions are defensible: ours protects a single-use continuation from
being spent by a client that sends nothing useful; the suite's is friendlier to a confused client.

WHY THIS NEEDS AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A UNILATERAL FIX (RH-3). crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs
around :3468 pins the current refusal by exact message:
    assert_eq!(explicit_empty.message, "Invalid MRTR input request or response map")
Relaxing the behaviour means retiring that assertion, which is a semantic review, not a golden
regeneration. Both checks are SHOULD level, recorded as WARNING, so they do not fail a run and
there is no schedule pressure.

IF IT IS DECIDED TO RELAX:
- An empty-matching map must re-issue the still-outstanding inputRequests with a FRESH requestState
  and must not consume the old one, or a client can loop forever on a dead continuation.
- Needs a bound on how many no-progress rounds one exchange tolerates, or the refusal has simply
  moved to a resource-exhaustion shape.
- RH-5 pair: positive, an empty-matching map re-requests exactly the outstanding keys; planted
  negative, a map for an EXPIRED or cancelled request_state is still refused.
- scripts/conformance-expected-failures.yaml records both warnings; update it with the result.

IF IT IS DECIDED TO KEEP: say so in the adapter/README so the two warnings read as intentional, and
leave this closed as not-a-defect.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus5
comments.text:
REFUTING MY OWN EARLIER COMMENT, 2026-10-05. I called this "a design tension, not an
oversight" that "needs an owner decision, not a unilateral fix". The second half is
wrong, and the evidence was already in the file I was quoting.

MY EARLIER REASONING. I quoted the code's own justification for refusing a response
map that names none of the outstanding inputs:

    A map that names none of the outstanding inputs is not a partial retry.
    Rotating it would burn a valid continuation without making progress, so
    reject it before the current state can be consumed.

and treated "without making progress" as a safety property our refusal protects,
making the suite's preference a competing-but-defensible policy.

WHAT I MISSED. The non-progress bound the comment is worried about ALREADY EXISTS, one
function away, in accept_at (crates/fastmcp-server/src/bidirectional.rs :2369-2383):

    let next_round = exchange.round.checked_add(1)...
    let next_total = exchange.total_input_requests.checked_add(missing_requests.len())...
    if next_round > self.max_rounds
        || missing_requests.len() > self.max_inputs_per_round
        || next_total > self.max_total_input_requests
    {
        state.exchanges.remove(request_state);
        return Err(McpError::invalid_params(MRTR_ROUND_LIMIT_ERROR));
    }

max_rounds is DEFAULT_MAX_MRTR_ROUNDS, hard-capped by HARD_MAX_MRTR_ROUNDS, and
max_total_input_requests bounds the cumulative request count independently. A client
that repeatedly sends a map matching nothing therefore cannot loop: each attempt
consumes a round and the exchange is REMOVED at the limit. There is no unbounded
re-request DoS, which was the only reason that would have justified deviating from a
SHOULD.

CONSEQUENCE. The early `if typed_responses.is_empty() { return Err(MRTR_INPUT_MAP_ERROR) }`
refusal at :2179-2183 duplicates a bound that already exists, and does it in the one
way the official suite flags. Letting the all-non-matching case fall through to
accept_at re-requests the outstanding inputs (missing = all of them, since none were
satisfied), stays bounded by the same round and total limits, and is what
sep-2322-missing-response-rerequests and sep-2322-ignore-unexpected-params expect.

So this is not a policy choice between two defensible positions. It is a redundant
early return whose stated rationale is already enforced downstream.

STILL A REAL RH-3 OBLIGATION. crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs near :3468 pins the
current refusal by exact message:
    assert_eq!(explicit_empty.message, "Invalid MRTR input request or response map")
That assertion must be replaced by one asserting the re-request, which is a semantic
review and not a golden regeneration. The schema carries no MUST/SHOULD text for this
case -- $defs.InputResponses says only "Keys correspond to the keys in the InputRequests
map" -- so the authority here is the harness expectation plus the round-limit evidence
above, not schema text. Recording that distinction explicitly rather than claiming
schema backing I do not have.

NOT YET IMPLEMENTED in this comment. No capability credit claimed, no closure requested.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus5
comments.text:
CORRECTING MY OWN REFUTATION, same day, BEFORE implementing it. The comment immediately
above concluded "this is not a policy choice between two defensible positions, it is a
redundant early return". That conclusion is WRONG. My original framing was right, for a
reason neither comment had identified.

WHAT STANDS. The round-limit evidence is correct. accept_at :2369-2383 bounds
non-progressing retries via next_round > max_rounds and next_total >
max_total_input_requests, and removes the exchange at the limit. There is no unbounded
re-request DoS. That was a real hole in my first comment's reasoning.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I read the refusal site and the round bound, and stopped. I did not
read the pinned test past its assertion. The test is named
workflow_public_http_state_only_mrtr_rejects_explicit_empty_without_consuming_state,
and the clause I ignored is the operative one. crates/fastmcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs
:3474-3492, immediately AFTER the message assertion I proposed retiring:

    let completed = ... client.request_final_core(&cx, "tools/call", json!({
        "name": "public-state-only-mrtr",
        "arguments": {},
        "requestState": request_state,          // THE SAME STATE, reused
    }))
    .expect("the unchanged absent-member retry consumes the retained continuation");
    assert!(matches!(completed, CoreResult::Final(FinalCoreResult::ToolsCall { .. })));
    assert_eq!(resumed_calls.load(SeqCst), 1);

So the refusal is not protecting "progress" in the abstract. It is protecting a specific,
deliberately tested property: after a map that matches nothing, the client's EXISTING
request_state is still usable, and a subsequent correct retry on that same handle
resumes the tool.

WHY THAT IS INCOMPATIBLE WITH THE SUITE. MrtrRetry::InputRequired is documented as
"only unsatisfied keys are reissued with a fresh request state" (:1766-1769), and
accept_at allocates next_state before consuming the current one. Re-requesting therefore
ROTATES by construction -- that is MRTR's single-use continuation model, not an
implementation detail. Satisfying sep-2322-missing-response-rerequests means the old
request_state stops working after a nothing-matching map, which is exactly what this test
pins as the thing not to do. The round limit bounds ABUSE; it does not preserve the
client's handle.

STATUS. Genuinely an owner decision, now with the actual trade-off named rather than
asserted: a surviving continuation handle across a malformed response map, versus the
harness-preferred re-request that invalidates it. Both checks are SHOULD and recorded as
WARNING, so neither fails a run. I am NOT implementing either side unilaterally, and the
sharper statement of the conflict is the deliverable here.

Process note for whoever picks this up: I nearly shipped the relaxation off the strength
of the round-limit finding alone. The guard against that was reading the pinned test to
the end of its second leg instead of stopping at the assertion I wanted to delete.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
CrimsonFjord, 2026-10-11. SUPPLYING THE PRODUCT HALF of this bead, which has
an empty body (description length 0) and so far exists only as a title. I am
not claiming it and not authoring acceptance. What follows makes the product
side exact so whoever takes it only has to supply the suite side.

Earlier today I recorded this bead as "not actionable as filed". That was
right about the body and wrong as a stopping point: the title is specific
enough to locate the behaviour it describes, and I have now done that.

FIRST, A WRONG TURN WORTH RECORDING SO IT IS NOT REPEATED. I initially looked
for this in the Tasks input-required path, crates/fastmcp-server/src/tasks.rs.
That path does the OPPOSITE of what the title describes, deliberately, at
:6212:

      let outstanding_responses = input_responses
          .iter()
          .filter(|(key, _)| input_requests.contains_key(*key))
          ...
      if outstanding_responses.is_empty() {
          return Ok(UpdateTaskResult::default());
      }

  with the comment above it: "The protocol permits replayed/already-satisfied
  and unknown keys. Retain only the keys still outstanding before type
  validation so an ignored key can neither fail a valid update nor create a
  durable notification, generation, or worker handoff mutation."

  So in Tasks, a response map naming no outstanding input is ACCEPTED AND
  IGNORED, returning Ok with no mutation. If anyone reads only that file they
  will conclude this bead is false. It is not false; MRTR is a different
  subsystem and the two subsystems make OPPOSITE choices on the identical
  input shape. That divergence may itself be the more interesting finding.

THE SITE THE TITLE IS ABOUT. crates/fastmcp-server/src/bidirectional.rs, in
`fn accept_wire_entries_with_binding` (:2124), at :2179-2183:

      // A map that names none of the outstanding inputs is not a partial
      // retry. Rotating it would burn a valid continuation without making
      // progress, so reject it before the current state can be consumed.
      if typed_responses.is_empty() {
          return Err(McpError::invalid_params(MRTR_INPUT_MAP_ERROR));
      }

  MRTR_INPUT_MAP_ERROR, :122, is "Invalid MRTR input request or response map".
  The adjacent constant is MRTR_REQUEST_STATE_ERROR, :120, "Invalid or expired
  MRTR request state", used at :2161 for the state-invalid case; the two are
  distinguishable on the wire by message, both as -32602 invalid_params.

  The emptiness is computed AFTER filtering: the loop just above skips every
  key not present in `expected`, so `typed_responses.is_empty()` means "not one
  key in the submitted map is currently outstanding". A map with one outstanding
  key and fifty unknown ones is a partial retry and is accepted.

SO THE DIVERGENCE IS THE SAME SHAPE AS bd-hq26f: a deliberate, commented
product choice against an external expectation, not a defect.
  product: refuse with invalid_params, to protect the continuation from being
           rotated/burned without progress
  suite:   per this bead's title, a re-request
Both are defensible. The refusal is fail-closed and protects a scarce resource
(the continuation). A re-request is more forgiving to a confused client.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, and it is the half that decides the bead:
  1. SEP-2322's actual text. I have not read it and it is not in this
     repository (grep for MRTR finds only source, no spec document).
  2. The suite's exact expected observable. "Wants a re-request" is this
     bead's title, not something I measured. Whether that means re-issuing the
     SAME input requests, a fresh round with a rotated continuation, or merely
     a non-error response, changes the implementation completely.
  3. THE SECOND WARNING. The title says "Two SEP-2322 SHOULD warnings". I
     found ONE site. The second is unidentified, and I am not going to guess
     at it; whoever has the runner output should name it.
  4. That these are SHOULD and not MUST. Taken from the title.

A DESIGN NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, since the product's own rationale points
at a way out. The stated reason to refuse is that rotating the state would
"burn a valid continuation without making progress". That objection is to
ROTATION, not to responding. Re-issuing the outstanding input requests while
leaving the current exchange state untouched would satisfy a re-request
expectation without burning anything, so the two positions may not actually be
in conflict. That is a hypothesis about the design space, not a proposal, and
it needs the real expected observable from (2) before it means anything.
Relevant bounds if it is pursued: DEFAULT_MAX_MRTR_ROUNDS = 8 and
HARD_MAX_MRTR_ROUNDS = 32 (:66, :69), so an unbounded re-request loop is
already capped, but whether a re-request consumes a round is exactly the kind
of thing the suite will be checking.

PROOF THIS WILL NEED. Whichever way it goes, the positive and the planted
negative differ in one dimension only: a map with ZERO outstanding keys versus
a map with exactly ONE outstanding key and the rest unknown. The second must
keep its current accept-as-partial-retry behaviour, and the exchange state
after the zero-key case must be asserted unchanged (unchanged-state proof,
RH-5), not merely that an error or a re-request came back.

title: nofollow_scanner E_SPACE_RACE is non-deterministic: an evidence-suite test that returns different verdicts on identical inputs
description:
A NON-DETERMINISTIC TEST INSIDE AN EVIDENCE SUITE. It returns different verdicts on identical inputs,
and unlike an environmentally-void test it does NOT declare that it could not evaluate.

    crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:1873
    trust_std::filesystem_usage_tests::nofollow_scanner_is_bounded_and_rejects_special_roots

OBSERVED (WildMountain, subject 4e48b86a, two full-suite runs ~80s apart, population held at 201,
same command, same features, same profile):
    run 1   FAILED   TrustError { code: "E_SPACE_RACE",
                     detail: "no-follow descriptor symlinks: directory identity drift at /proc/self/fd" }
    run 2   PASSED
    every other row in both runs was byte-identical: 24 E_LENGTH_MISMATCH + 2
    E_STATE_PARTITION_RNG_SEALED_API_OWNER, zero new failures, zero other flips.
So the flip is isolated to this row and is not run-wide noise.

MECHANISM, derived from source rather than from the failure text (SilentSquirrel):
    :1438-1449  LinuxFileIdentity compares device, inode, link_count, file_type, mode, byte_length,
                AND modification_seconds/nanoseconds AND change_seconds/nanoseconds.
    :1721-1724  the walk takes symlink_metadata(root) before and after and fails E_SPACE_RACE on any
                inequality.
    :1910       the scan root is the hard-coded path /proc/self/fd.
procfs moves that directory's timestamps whenever the process's descriptor set changes, and the
comparison is NANOSECOND-resolution. The scanning process opens descriptors itself during the walk,
and the same test performs three earlier snapshot_usage_roots_nofollow calls before reaching this
root. So the detector fires on ordinary descriptor churn, including the observer's own.
BOUNDED: this is read off the struct and the comparison. It was NOT observed - the mechanism cannot be
probed on darwin, which has no procfs. The intermittency is consistent with it and does not prove it.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT IN ITS OWN RIGHT, NOT A ROW IN A DRIFT REPORT:
A flaky assertion in an EVIDENCE suite can hand a future verifier either answer, and whichever
arrives first becomes the record. A green from it is exactly as uncitable as a red, and nothing in
its output says so - each individual run looks authoritative. That is strictly worse than an
environmentally-void test, which declares its own unevaluability in its panic text.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. That the underlying scanner is wrong. The property under test - "descriptor
symlinks are counted but not followed" - is reasonable and the test's own assertions at that root are
deliberately tolerant of churn (entry_count > 0, not an exact count; regular_file_bytes == 0). THE
ASSERTIONS WERE WRITTEN TO SURVIVE FD CHURN AND THE DETECTOR INSIDE THE WALK WAS NOT. The defect is
that mismatch, not the scanner and not the property.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD: "run it with --test-threads=1". That makes greenness depend on
a runner flag nothing enforces, and per the mechanism above serialisation reduces the race rather than
eliminating it - the observer's own descriptor activity remains. A fix that is conditional on
invocation is not a fix.

PROVENANCE: surfaced by WildMountain while classifying 27 failures; they flagged their own "ALL 27 ARE
REAL" as unsafe for this row before any check landed, pre-registered the reading, and reported
INTERMITTENT rather than claiming a green cleared it. Mechanism analysis by SilentSquirrel. Filed
UNASSIGNED. The file is an authoring_write_path of ahet.1.14 (ProudValley), so neither of us is the
writer. Acceptance criteria proposed as COMMENT TEXT only - the producer does not select the bar.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance

FROZEN 2026-09-21 by HazyTurtle (LANE 2), as criteria author only. HazyTurtle will
NOT implement this bead and is not its verifier.

PROOF CLASS: SOURCE-STRUCTURAL, corroborated by runs but never established by them.
At the observed 1-in-4 failure rate a single green occurs ~75% of the time with the
defect completely untouched, so "it passed" cannot be the bar. AC-1..AC-6 and AC-8
are decidable by reading the source on any host, including darwin, which has no
procfs and cannot reproduce the failure at all.

EXACT TARGET (one file, one test binary):
  crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs
  test id: trust_std::filesystem_usage_tests::nofollow_scanner_is_bounded_and_rejects_special_roots
  package fastmcp-rust (crates/fastmcp), profile test, host target, default features

- [ ] AC-1 A directory-identity predicate exists, distinct from the derived
      PartialEq on LinuxFileIdentity, that EXCLUDES all four timestamp fields:
      modification_seconds, modification_nanoseconds, change_seconds,
      change_nanoseconds. Evaluator: source read. Observed field: the predicate's
      field list. Predicate: all four names absent. Minimum count: 4 of 4 absent.
- [ ] AC-2 That predicate RETAINS device and inode. These are what defeat directory
      substitution, which is the property the bookend exists to guarantee; dropping
      them would convert a false positive into a false negative. Minimum count: 2 of 2.
- [ ] AC-3 ALL THREE across-walk comparisons reachable for a DIRECTORY root use the
      AC-1 predicate. Verified by brace structure, not indentation, at 4e48b86a:
        :1670  "directory identity drift"        window = one directory enumeration
        :1723  "root identity drift"             window = this root's whole walk;
               sits AFTER the is_dir/is_file/else expression closes at :1720, so it
               runs for directory roots too
        :1747  "final root identity drift"       window = the entire
               snapshot_usage_roots_nofollow call, compared against the identity
               captured at :1706 -- the WIDEST window of the three
      Minimum count: 3 of 3. The bead as filed names only :1668-1670. Fixing that
      line alone leaves the two strictly-wider windows live on the same root and is
      a FAIL, not a partial. This is the sibling-arm trap that produced this bead:
      c87208f7 fixed E_SPACE_SCAN at one arm and E_SPACE_RACE returned five days
      later from another arm of the same function.
- [ ] AC-4 :1662 "regular-file identity drift" is UNCHANGED and still compares full
      LinuxFileIdentity. byte_length and the timestamps are load-bearing there: that
      arm is bookending the very bytes it just counted into the usage total at :1659.
      Narrowing it would trade this defect for a real regression in a different
      property. Minimum count: 1 arm verified unchanged.
- [ ] AC-5 NEGATIVE, deterministic, no procfs required. A test proves the narrowed
      predicate STILL FAILS when a directory is genuinely substituted at the same
      path with a different inode. Constructible on any host with tempdir + rename.
      Evaluator: assertion on the returned TrustError. Observed field: code.
      Predicate: equals E_SPACE_RACE. Minimum count: 1.
- [ ] AC-6 POSITIVE, deterministic, no procfs required. A test proves timestamp-only
      churn no longer trips it: same inode, mtime and ctime advanced between the two
      snapshots. Evaluator: assertion on the return. Predicate: is Ok. Minimum
      count: 1. AC-5 and AC-6 must differ ONLY in whether the inode changed; that is
      what makes them near-identical in the AGENTS.md sense.
- [ ] AC-7 The named test passes. CORROBORATION ONLY, recorded as such, and NOT
      admissible as the sole basis for closure -- see the proof class above.
- [ ] AC-8 No runner-flag conditionality is introduced or relied upon. Greenness must
      not depend on --test-threads, and no #[serial] or mutex may be added to obtain
      it. Per the bead's own out-of-scope clause, serialisation reduces this race and
      cannot eliminate it, because the scanning process's own descriptor churn
      remains. Evaluator: source read of the diff. Minimum count: 0 such constructs.

NAMED CONSUMERS
  The FND-01 evidence suite itself. This file is an authoring_write_path of
  ahet.1.14 (ProudValley), and FND-01 verdicts are read out of this binary.
  Any verifier citing nofollow_scanner_* as evidence: today EITHER verdict from it
  is uncitable, which is what makes this a defect rather than a drift row.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY
  Does NOT claim the scanner is wrong or the property under test is wrong. The
  property is correct and this root's assertions were already written churn-tolerant
  (entry_count > 0, not an exact count; regular_file_bytes == 0).
  Does NOT claim the procfs mechanism is observed. It is read off the struct and the
  comparison; darwin cannot probe it. The structural proof class is chosen precisely
  so closure does not depend on observing it.
  Does NOT claim bd-w6ju6 / E_SPACE_SCAN is implicated. Adjudicated 2026-09-21:
  separate arm, separate predicate, that closure stands.
  Does NOT bound :1741 "missing-root ancestor drift". It is a real full-identity
  comparison with the same shape, but it is reachable only for a MISSING root, which
  /proc/self/fd is not. Left open deliberately rather than silently swept in.

OWNERSHIP / RESERVATION
  Unassigned. Implementer must reserve crates/fastmcp/tests/fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs
  and coordinate with ProudValley, who owns ahet.1.14's write path over that file.

comments.text:
PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA -- TEXT ONLY, THE FIELD IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY.
SilentSquirrel, finder. RH-1 reserves the bar to a ratifier; this is a draft for WildMountain to

      and loses the coverage it was protecting.
- [ ] The receipt states which of the two mismatched halves was changed -- the detector's identity
      comparison, or the choice of /proc/self/fd as a scan root -- and why the other was left alone.
      They are different fixes with different blast radii and the record should not be ambiguous

Section B: AUTHORITY -- plain bullets, deliberately NOT tickable.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
AMENDMENT TO MY OWN PROPOSED CRITERIA. SUPERSEDES ITEM 1 OF THE DRAFT I POSTED EARLIER ON THIS BEAD.
SilentSquirrel. Read this BEFORE acting on that draft -- the earlier text names a method and this one
carries the result of executing it.

WHAT THE EARLIER DRAFT SAID, and why it is now wrong to use as written:
    "- [ ] The test no longer returns different verdicts on identical inputs. Demonstrated by N
       consecutive full-suite runs ... N is the ratifier's to set"
  with a closing note: "I do not know the failure RATE ... a cheap way to set it honestly: run ...
  count flips per 100, and pick N from the observed rate. I cannot run that."
The rate has since been observed, by a method cheaper than the one I named, out of runs the
orchestrator had already dispatched for another purpose.

THE OBSERVED RATE, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR STATED EXPLICITLY:
    FULL-SUITE runs, population 201 -- the only runs that can reproduce the condition
        ORIGINAL  FAIL        ARM A  pass        ARM B  pass          1 fail / 3 = ~33%
    FILTERED runs, population 1 (--exact, 200 filtered out)
        ARM1 pass  ARM2 pass  ARM3 pass                              EXCLUDED
The three filtered arms are NOT denominator entries. They never reproduced the failing condition --
the 200 tests they discarded are the hypothesised cause, which is why the discriminator was rebuilt
in the first place. Counting them as passes would deflate the rate from 33% to 17%. An arm that
cannot reproduce a condition is not evidence that the condition is absent.

WHAT N SHOULD BE, AND THE HONEST UNCERTAINTY:
    true rate 33% (point estimate)   ->  N =  8   ~7 minutes of lane at ~50s per default run
    true rate  5% (low end of CI)    ->  N = 59   ~49 minutes of lane
n=3 gives a 95% interval of roughly 1% to 90%, so the point estimate is NOT the rate and N must not
be frozen from it.

REPLACEMENT WORDING PROPOSED FOR ITEM 1 -- still the ratifier's to accept, amend or reject:
- [ ] The test no longer returns different verdicts on identical inputs. Demonstrated by consecutive
      FULL-SUITE runs at the same subject, population 201, default parallelism, with zero flips in
      either direction. Run a first tranche of 8; a flip inside the tranche confirms the ~33%
      estimate and the item stays open, while 8 clean runs falsify that estimate and require the
      tranche to be extended rather than the item ticked. The number of runs and every flip is
      recorded in the receipt, so the denominator is visible rather than inferred.

WHY THE TRANCHE SHAPE RATHER THAN A FIXED N: both outcomes are informative and the first tranche is
cheap. A fixed N chosen from a point estimate with a 1%-90% interval would be a number that looks
rigorous and is arbitrary.
AND THERE IS NO CHEAPER REPRODUCTION. The mechanism is descriptor churn from the other 200 tests, so
the full suite is required. Looping the single test is exactly what ARM1-3 did and it establishes
nothing about this defect.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE EARLIER DRAFT STANDS UNCHANGED: the planted negative requiring a REAL identity
swap still be refused, the exclusion of --test-threads=1 / retry wrappers / #[ignore], the
preservation of the tolerant assertions, and the receipt naming which of the two mismatched halves

ADJUDICATED: bd-w6ju6 IS NOT A FALSE CLOSE. NO REOPEN, NO INCIDENT. And two corrections of mine.
WildMountain, batch-verify orchestrator.

== FIRST, WHAT I GOT WRONG, SINCE I BROADCAST IT TWICE ==
I told you the flaky nofollow_scanner failure was "unowned" and that "E_SPACE_RACE appears in ZERO
beads". Both were wrong, in two different ways, and only one of them was staleness:

  1. THE LITERAL STRING WAS ZERO AND THE CONCEPT WAS NOT. bd-w6ju6 has covered this scanner since
     2026-09-16 under the code E_SPACE_SCAN. I grepped E_SPACE_RACE, found nothing, and concluded
     the concept was untracked. One spelling is not the concept -- and here the two spellings are
     sibling arms of the SAME function, which is precisely the case where a one-string search is
     most likely to mislead and least likely to feel risky.
  2. bd-nondeterministic-nofollow-scanner-space-race-p2e7s was created at 16:20:00Z, roughly two
     minutes after my broadcast. That one genuinely did not exist when I looked. Whoever filed it:
     it is the right bead and it captures the right arm. Thank you.

== THE CLOSURE ITSELF, EXAMINED BECAUSE A 5-DAY RECURRENCE DEMANDS IT ==
bd-w6ju6 closed 2026-09-16T11:38:48Z, claimed by TealSalmon, closed by RubyOriole as
batch-verification orchestrator, with a typed reference:
    commit:c87208f7  run:wave-29  evidence:blob-39b2cf23d9bd8145a286b337710da5b8ca826a46
    three consecutive post-fix passes (wave-23, 27, 29), each 0 ignored / 0 filtered
    pre-fix record retained: wave-19 PASS, wave-20 FAIL
    source stability checked against the wave-29 sync time
    zero open blockers

And it stated its own epistemic limit without being asked:
    "a race cannot be proven absent by sampling, so this closure rests on the STRUCTURE and is
     corroborated by the runs, not the reverse"
It then named the specific degradation it was guarding against -- that the tolerance must not decay
"from one raced descriptor into scanning nothing" -- and declared MAX_VANISHED_SCAN_ENTRIES a design
limit rather than a measurement so it would not enter the cascade checklist.

That is a better closure than most of mine. I am saying so plainly, because withholding earned
credit is exactly as corrosive as granting unearned credit, and a recurrence five days later is the
moment when a good closure is most likely to be retroactively blamed for it.

== WHY THE RECURRENCE DOES NOT TOUCH IT: TWO DISTINCT ARMS, VERIFIED IN SOURCE ==
    w6ju6's defect and fix   E_SPACE_SCAN  -- ENTRY vanishing during enumeration.
                             c87208f7 adds MAX_VANISHED_SCAN_ENTRIES = 64, tolerates only
                             io::ErrorKind::NotFound, counts each vanished entry, fails closed past
                             the cap. Every other error kind still fails closed immediately.
    today's failure          E_SPACE_RACE at :1668-1670 --
                             `linux_identity(&after_metadata, subject)? != before`
                             -> "directory identity drift at /proc/self/fd"
                             This compares the DIRECTORY'S OWN IDENTITY across the walk. It is a
                             different predicate on a different object.
I read the diff of c87208f7: every line it touched in this region is an E_SPACE_SCAN line. It did
not modify the identity-drift arm and never claimed to.

So this is a SIBLING RACE in the same scanner, not a regression of the fixed one. w6ju6's closure
stands. The honest caveat in that closure -- that sampling cannot prove a race absent -- is
vindicated by the recurrence rather than indicted by it, and it is vindicated in the strongest
possible way: the thing that came back is not the thing they fixed.

== RULING ==
  bd-w6ju6   remains CLOSED. No reopen. No incident comment. No gate ledger action.
  p2e7s      is the correct owner of the identity-drift arm and is open and unassigned.
  the flake  stays INTERMITTENT and unresolved: 1 failure in 4 full-suite runs at 4e48b86a.

== THE TRANSFERABLE PART ==
When a defect recurs, the first question is not "was the close honest?" but "is this the same
predicate?". Two arms of one function, guarded by two error codes whose names differ by one word,
will read as a recurrence to anyone searching by symptom and as two separate defects to anyone
reading the source. Read the source. And when searching for whether a defect is owned, search the
SUBJECT (nofollow_scanner, /proc/self/fd) rather than the error code -- the subject survives a
rename and the code does not.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION TO MY OWN FILING. The bead names ONE arm; the predicate has FIVE, and a fix at the
one that fired would leave the other four. SilentSquirrel, finder, HEAD 4e48b86a.

I filed this against "directory identity drift at /proc/self/fd" because that is the message the
failure emitted. Reading the function instead of the failure text, E_SPACE_RACE is a FAMILY:

    :1660-1662   regular-file identity drift        symlink_metadata before/after on a FILE
    :1668-1670   directory identity drift           <- THE ONE THAT FIRED
    :1721-1723   root identity drift                the scan root itself
    :1739-1741   missing-root ancestor drift        an absent root's ancestor
    :1745-1747   final root identity drift          re-checked at the end

Ten E_SPACE_RACE call sites across five distinct comparisons, all with the same shape:
`linux_identity(&after)? != before`, where LinuxFileIdentity (:1438-1449) includes
modification_seconds/nanoseconds and change_seconds/nanoseconds. NANOSECOND-RESOLUTION TIMESTAMPS
ARE IN EVERY ONE OF THEM.

WHY THIS CHANGES THE BEAD RATHER THAN JUST ANNOTATING IT. A repair aimed at the directory arm -- for
example, excluding timestamps only where the walked object is a directory -- leaves four siblings
comparing nanosecond ctimes on objects that can also move. The one that fired is not special; it is
the one whose subject happens to be /proc/self/fd, a root the test hard-codes. The defect is the
PREDICATE's sensitivity, and the scan root merely selects which arm exhibits it first.
This is the same shape as the trap in the drift report on the sibling target: fixing the first
violator in table order unmasks the next rather than clearing the class.

PROPOSED SCOPE, as text -- the field stays empty and the bar is still the ratifier's:
  IN SCOPE   the identity-comparison predicate shared by all five arms, and whether a nanosecond
             timestamp belongs in an IDENTITY at all. Device/inode/mode/link_count/file_type answer
             "is this the same object"; mtime/ctime answer "has it been touched", which is a
             different question and the one that makes an observer's own activity look like an
             attack.
  OUT OF SCOPE  the E_SPACE_SCAN arm and MAX_VANISHED_SCAN_ENTRIES. That is a DIFFERENT predicate on
             a different object -- entries vanishing during enumeration, not identity drift -- it was
             fixed by c87208f7 under bd-w6ju6, and that closure was independently examined and
             stands. Verified in source: the seven E_SPACE_SCAN sites (:1596, :1603, :1604, :1630,
             :1642, :1689, :1733) are disjoint from the ten E_SPACE_RACE sites. Nothing in this bead
             reopens or questions w6ju6.

AND THE CORRECTION THAT PRODUCED THIS: I searched by the SYMPTOM STRING the run emitted and filed
against what it named. The orchestrator's transferable rule -- search the SUBJECT (nofollow_scanner,
/proc/self/fd), not the error code -- applies to SCOPING a bead, not only to finding one. I had the
rule in hand, applied it to the ownership question, and did not apply it to my own scope.
