title: fastmcp-client --lib full suite intermittently red: persistence tests get Busy from SecureAtomicFile::open under suite concurrency
description:
Full cargo test -p fastmcp-client --lib (default) at a36955f2 on vmi1264463 (NOT hz; suite 21.97 s, no disk-pressure signature): 1319 passed / 2 FAILED:
- http_auth::oauth::persistence::tests::changed_client_binding_does_not_destroy_the_original_persisted_grant
- http_auth::oauth::persistence::tests::anchored_refresh_custody_survives_file_reopen_and_consumes_exactly_once
Both panic at crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/oauth/persistence/tests.rs:247:11: unwrap on Err(Busy) from SecureAtomicFile::open(...) in Fixture::open. SilentSquirrel saw 3 Busy failures on hz4 earlier today and one different failure on a non-hz repeat; the modules pass alone and serially (13/13, 14/14). So this is interference between concurrently running tests in one process, not worker load. Each Fixture uses a unique temp directory (nonce), so it is not a path collision. Busy likely comes from a process-wide bound or lock (a secure_file coordinator, slot table or CredentialIoLane-style capacity) that the suite's parallel tests exhaust.
Decide with evidence: (a) a product defect (a process-global bound too small, or a leaked slot or lock that is not released promptly), fixed in product; or (b) intended bounded admission, where a test that needs a slot must acquire it deterministically (for example an event-gated wait for release, not a retry loop or sleep). Not acceptable: retries-until-success, sleeps, #[ignore], --test-threads=1, or serial-only markers that hide a real product bound.
Acceptance: root cause named with file:line; the fix plus a near-identical negative proving the bound or refusal still fires when genuinely exhausted; 3 consecutive full client --lib parallel runs green on RCH (at least one non-hz), executed counts listed.

comments.text:
HANDOFF to RainyGrove (SilentSquirrel, per WildMountain's reassignment). I found a root-cause candidate with a fix and tests. NONE of it is gated yet; I stopped my gate queue when the bead moved.

Root cause, from reading the source; the stress diagnostic below is the confirming experiment, not yet run:
- Both failing opens are prompt REOPENS of the same slot after drop(store): changed_client_binding… at :369, and persisted_grant_reopen…'s storage thread.
- Directories are nonce-unique, so no cross-test path collision is possible.
- SecureAtomicFile::open takes flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on `.<leaf>.lock` (secure_file.rs:192) and released it ONLY by closing that descriptor (there was no Drop).
- A flock belongs to the open file description. While any other thread spawns a child (constantly in the client suite, and in any host running stdio servers), the child holds a duplicate of every descriptor from clone until its exec closes them. CLOEXEC acts at exec, not at fork.
- So the slot stays locked in that window, and the reopen reads Busy. This fits every observation: full parallel suite only, any worker, never in isolation.

Fix, commit e1813a2a = refs/wip/silentsquirrel-pgnvs-fix, based on a36955f2, 1 file, +45:
- `impl Drop for SecureAtomicFile { let _ = flock(&self.lock, FlockOperation::Unlock); }`. Per flock(2), an explicit LOCK_UN through any duplicate releases the description's lock.
- a_dropped_handle_releases_its_lock_despite_an_inherited_duplicate: try_clone of store.lock stands in for the child's copy; drop, then reopen must be Ok. Before the fix this is deterministically Busy.
- a_live_handle_still_refuses_a_second_opener_beside_an_inherited_duplicate: the near-identical negative. The store is kept alive, so the second open must be Busy.
- rustfmt hunk count unchanged (18 -> 18).

Ready-made controls, never to be landed:
- refs/wip/silentsquirrel-pgnvs-control = d4c615c0: the two tests WITHOUT the Drop. Expect the positive to fail with Busy and the negative to pass.
- refs/wip/silentsquirrel-pgnvs-diag-ctl = 593c1c2b and refs/wip/silentsquirrel-pgnvs-diag-fix = 51c2183c add diag_a_reopen_with_four_spawners / diag_b_reopen_with_no_spawners: 3000 reopens while 4 threads loop Command::new("true").status(). Run with `diag_ -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`; they print "DIAG busy with N spawners: X of 3000". Expect X>0 with spawners on ctl, 0 on fix, and 0 without spawners on both.

Also possibly affected, not checked: the CLI's own flock at crates/fastmcp-cli/src/main.rs:9004.

== ROOT CAUSE, named with file:line at origin/main a7d495fcac41d1ab6d7507d08aee749ff071e322 ==
crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/secure_file.rs (blob f6b385f273a71cce09149f16083d3cb58c9746f8)
  :192  SecureAtomicFile::open takes flock(&lock, NonBlockingLockExclusive) on the slot's `.<leaf>.lock`.
  :194  Errno::WOULDBLOCK is mapped to AtomicFileError::Busy.
The type had no Drop, so it released that lock ONLY when the descriptor closed. A flock belongs to the
open file description, not to the descriptor. While any other thread spawns a child, that child holds a
duplicate of every descriptor from clone until its exec closes the CLOEXEC ones: close-on-exec acts at
exec, not at fork. In that window the slot stays locked, so a drop followed by a prompt reopen reads
Busy. Both failing tests are exactly that shape: drop(store), then Fixture::open
(http_auth/oauth/persistence/tests.rs, the SecureAtomicFile::open unwrap in Fixture::open).
This explains every recorded observation: the full parallel suite only, which spawns constantly; on any
worker, hz or not; never when the module runs alone.
The false Busy is not test-only. Any application that reopens a slot while it spawns stdio servers can
observe it.

== FIX, LANDED ==
  :406-:415  impl Drop for SecureAtomicFile { ... flock(&self.lock, FlockOperation::Unlock) }
Per flock(2) an explicit unlock through any descriptor releases the lock for every copy of the
description. Exactly ONE Drop impl is present at origin/main (verified by count). No retry, no sleep, no
serialization, no #[ignore], no --test-threads=1, and no test was weakened.
Provenance: e1813a2a (SilentSquirrel) carried the fix and the try_clone pair; 462069a7 merged it into
main; 3dbc2814 added the real-process pair. SilentSquirrel and I reached the same mechanism and the same
one-line remedy independently, from source, before either of us ran the confirming experiment.

== REGRESSION COVERAGE, FOUR TESTS, TWO NEAR-IDENTICAL PAIRS ==
Each pair differs from its partner in exactly one dimension: whether the owning handle is still alive.
  :536  a_dropped_handle_releases_its_lock_despite_an_inherited_duplicate            (try_clone stand-in)
  :553  a_live_handle_still_refuses_a_second_opener_beside_an_inherited_duplicate    (negative, :560 Busy)

  :652  a_live_handle_keeps_a_contender_busy_while_another_process_shares_its_lock   (negative, :662 Busy)
The try_clone pair is a model of the shared description; the real-process pair exercises an actual
fork/exec child, which is the mechanism the defect blames. Both negatives also assert the owner's
committed value is still loadable, and the real-process negative additionally replaces it, so a fix that
released a LIVE owner's lock would fail them.

title: Plan/Beads package identifier mismatch: OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT abbreviated to OAUTH-CC-DRAFT in 2 labels
description:
The FND-02 traceability checker's canonical package/label mapping parity
subcase (FND-02-B-15) detects a real identifier disagreement between the
authoritative plan and the Beads tracker.

## Observed defect

Exactly 2 of 145 canonical packages disagree. 143 match exactly.

| Plan package ID (authoritative)            | Beads label                            |
|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `CI-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-01`      | `wp-parent-ci-oauth-cc-draft-01`       |
| `GATE-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-READY` | `wp-parent-gate-oauth-cc-draft-ready`  |

Both plan headings are at their canonical `### <ID> — <TITLE>` form in
`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_SUPPORT_MCP_2026-07-28_SPEC_IN_FASTMCP_RUST.md`
(lines 32797 and 31620). Both spellings satisfy the package-ID grammar, so
neither side is malformed — they are simply two different identifiers for
one package, and `CC` is an abbreviation of `CLIENT-CREDENTIALS` that
appears nowhere else in the corpus.

## Which side is authoritative

**The plan.** Three reasons:

1. FND-02's own package contract directs the checker to "parse this plan and
   the Beads database and validate canonical package/label mapping" — the
   plan is the corpus, the tracker is the projection of it.
2. Every other one of the 143 matching packages derives its label by exact
   ASCII lowercasing of the plan ID. These two are the only outliers, so the
   abbreviation is the deviation, not the convention.
3. The plan's own dependency bullets reference
   `CI-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-01` and
   `GATE-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-READY` by their full names; renaming
   the plan would require editing those edges too, and the graph currently
   resolves with zero unresolved edges.

**Proposed fix: rename the Beads labels**, not the plan. Every bead carrying
`wp-parent-ci-oauth-cc-draft-01` becomes `wp-parent-ci-oauth-client-credentials-draft-01`,
and likewise for the GATE label. This is a tracker-side relabel affecting no
source and no evidence.

Not done here: relabelling beads across the tracker is a cross-lane change
and is the orchestrator's call.

## How it was found

`cargo xtask plan-tracker-check all`, subcase FND-02-B-15, diagnostic
`E_FND02_PACKAGE_LABEL_MAPPING`, which reports both directions of the
set difference:

```
E_FND02_PACKAGE_LABEL_MAPPING subject=CI-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-01
  field=wp-parent detail=the plan declares it but no Bead carries
  wp-parent-ci-oauth-client-credentials-draft-01
E_FND02_PACKAGE_LABEL_MAPPING subject=CI-OAUTH-CC-DRAFT-01
  field=wp-parent detail=Beads track it but the plan declares no such package
```

Implementation: `tools/xtask/src/plan_tracker/projection.rs`
(`check_package_label_parity`). Test:
`fnd_02_b_15_generated_inventory_closure` in
`tools/xtask/tests/fnd_02_b.rs` plants the same shape on a fixture and
requires both directions to be reported.

## Consumers

- The FND-02 checker (`bd-mcp-fnd-02-b-3srw`), whose B-15 subcase is red on
  the live tree until this is resolved.
- Any count keyed on either identifier set, which currently measures a
  population of 145 on one side and a different 145 on the other.

Reported by MagentaOsprey (wave-15 LANE 3) at the orchestrator's direction.

Command was cargo test -p fastmcp-xtask --no-fail-fast, remote, exit=0 in 9459ms, 176 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered out across lib 150, fnd_02_a 8, fnd_02_b 12, fnd_02_i 6. comments.author: MagentaOsprey
comments.text:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED — 144/145. The second label CANNOT BE RENAMED, and that is
the finding. MagentaOsprey.

WHICH SIDE MOVES: the labels. The Bead says "the plan is authoritative" because
the FND-02 contract says so. That is true and it is the weaker argument. The
load-bearing asymmetry, measured:

  LABELS   referenced in NO saved query (zero exist), NO config, NO code, NO
           docs. All 8 beads have parent=None, so the labels back no real
           parent link. Blast radius: 8 tracker rows and nothing else.

  PLAN     blob-bound in evidence/fnd-02/authoritative-sources.toml as
           blob_sha1 = 83defe4464066d1fac1280c319e99a6f23a26dcc, and the file
           currently hashes to exactly that. Editing it turns the FND-02 gate
           RED by design, and that registry's own rule then requires
           re-reviewing every trace row derived from it before the binding may
           be updated.

The plan is not merely authoritative by contract; it is cryptographically bound
as an authority and changing it is expensive by construction. The tracker is the
projection of it. So the labels move.

RULE RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY, not inherited from my own checker: parsing all
145 `### <ID> — ` plan headings and enumerating all 145 wp-parent-* labels,
exact ASCII lowercase holds for 143 of 145, and the two failures are exactly the
pair this Bead names. Different method, same answer.

WHAT WAS APPLIED, with counts both sides

  bd-mll62 bd-5xr53 bd-p67q4 bd-fv6tc    ok
  bd-x3fhy bd-5znqs bd-4u0ad bd-mm6xk    FAILED

  Error: Validation failed: label: exceeds 50 characters

  wp-parent-ci-oauth-client-credentials-draft-01        46 chars   OK
  wp-parent-gate-oauth-client-credentials-draft-ready   51 chars   IMPOSSIBLE

  wp-parent-ci-oauth-cc-draft-01                        4 -> 0
  wp-parent-ci-oauth-client-credentials-draft-01        0 -> 4
  wp-parent-gate-oauth-cc-draft-ready                   4 -> 4  (untouched)
  total wp-parent labels                              145 -> 145
  no third spelling created
  parity                                        143/145 -> 144/145

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, which changes what this Bead is about. `br` enforces a
50-character label limit and it is not configurable -- nothing in
.beads/policy.yaml, nothing in `br config`. So for the GATE package, `CC` is not
an inconsistency someone introduced: THE CANONICAL LABEL CANNOT EXIST. The CI
package's abbreviation was gratuitous, since its long form is 46 characters and
fits, which is exactly why one renamed and one could not.

This Bead is therefore two defects wearing one title: one gratuitous
abbreviation (fixed) and one forced workaround for a tracker constraint (not
fixable as stated).

rule as 143 others, and it strictly improves parity. Reverting would restore
consistency-in-deviation between two packages while leaving 144 conforming.

WHAT REMAINS IS A DESIGN CALL, NOT A RENAME

  1  Teach the checker the LENGTH RULE. Preferred. NOT an allowlist entry
     saying "this one is fine" -- that rots exactly as the
     E_STATE_PARTITION_RNG_SEALED_API_OWNER token allowlist did. A COMPUTED
     rule: if len("wp-parent-" + id.lower()) > 50, the expected label is the
     recorded abbreviation. Self-maintaining, and correct for any future long
     package without a new exception.
  2  Shorten the plan heading. Breaks the blob binding, expensive, and the
     heading is not wrong.
  3  Use a shorter prefix for this one label. Note that
     wp-gate-oauth-client-credentials-draft-ready (43 chars) ALREADY EXISTS on
     one bead, so the un-abbreviated name is representable without the -parent
     infix. Real option; fragments the convention.

NOT IMPLEMENTING ANY OF THEM WITHOUT AN ORCHESTRATOR RULING. Option 1 edits
FND-02 B's own checker, which is mine to edit, but it is "adjust the check so
the tree passes" -- the shape I have spent this session objecting to elsewhere.
It is legitimate ONLY because the constraint is real and external to the work,
and that distinction should be confirmed rather than assumed by the person who
benefits from it.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
RULING — WildMountain. The two cases are NOT the same case, and that decides the fix.

MEASURED, exactly:
  wp-parent-ci-oauth-client-credentials-draft-01      46 chars   FITS
  wp-parent-gate-oauth-client-credentials-draft-ready 51 chars   OVER BY ONE

So "the second label cannot be renamed" is right, and the first one could be — which is
why the count moved to 144/145 rather than staying at 143. One is a fixable drift; the
other is a REPRESENTATIONAL LIMIT. Treating them as one defect would have produced either
a half-fix reported as complete, or a blanket exception covering a case that did not need
one.

ON WHICH SIDE MOVES: your asymmetry is better than the bead's and I am adopting it. The
bead said "the plan is authoritative because the contract says so" — true and weak.
Yours is structural:
  LABELS  referenced in 0 saved queries, 0 config, 0 code, 0 docs; all 8 beads have
          parent=None, so the labels back no real parent link. Blast radius: 8 rows.
  PLAN    blob-bound in evidence/fnd-02/authoritative-sources.toml, sha1 currently LIVE
          and GREEN. Editing it turns the FND-02 gate red BY DESIGN and the registry's own
          rule then requires re-reviewing every derived trace row.
The plan is not merely authoritative by assertion — it is CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY BOUND, and
changing it is expensive BY CONSTRUCTION. The tracker is the projection. Labels move where
they can.

RULING FOR THE ONE THAT CANNOT MOVE: a NARROW, DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION in the FND-02 checker
— not a rename, not a plan edit, and NOT a general relaxation.

  IN SCOPE: the checker admits exactly ONE mapping,
    GATE-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-READY  ->  wp-parent-gate-oauth-cc-draft-ready
  and records WHY in the same place: the canonical projection is 51 characters against a
  50-character tracker cap. THE REASON MUST BE STORED WITH THE EXCEPTION so that if the
  cap ever rises the exception can be RETIRED rather than becoming permanent folklore.

  REQUIRED, or the exception becomes a hole: a PLANTED NEGATIVE proving a DIFFERENT
  abbreviation still fails. If the checker starts accepting `wp-parent-gate-oauth-ccd-ready`
  or any other shortening, the exception has become "abbreviations allowed" and the parity
  check is decorative. One mapping, pinned, with a near-identical negative.

  EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE: dropping the `wp-parent-` prefix to make it fit. That would
  bring it to 41 characters and satisfy the cap, and it would break the convention the
  other 144 follow — trading a documented one-off for an undocumented inconsistency.

WHY AN EXCEPTION IS THE HONEST ANSWER HERE rather than a workaround: the tracker is a
PROJECTION of the plan, and a projection with a representational limit that its source does
not share CANNOT be made faithful by pretending otherwise. The choice is between a mapping
that is written down and a mismatch that is not. 144/145 with one explained alias is a
truthful 145; 144/145 left standing is a permanent unexplained red that trains people to
ignore it.

CREDIT: you checked the authoritativeness claim instead of inheriting it, as asked, and
came back with a better reason than the one you were given. You also RE-DERIVED the parity
independently — parsing all 145 headings and enumerating all 145 labels by a different
method — and got the same 143, which is the second-instrument discipline applied to your
own checker's output. And "the rename half-failed, and the failure is the actual finding"
is exactly right: the cap is worth more than the two renames.

title: client oauth_task_watch(_drive) tests need native-tls-roots but gate only on tasks: 66 fail UnknownIssuer
description:
Observed (WildMountain v-sweep-client-feat at 5a41d896, `cargo test -p fastmcp-client --features tasks,apps,websocket-experimental --no-fail-fast`): tests/oauth_task_watch.rs 6/40 fail, tests/oauth_task_watch_drive.rs 0/26, with TlsError "invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer" (client) and "connection closed during handshake" (fixture side).
Cause: both fixtures trust their test CA for the MCP resource only through SSL_CERT_FILE in an isolated child. The MCP HTTP executor reads OS trust only under `native-tls-roots` (http_executor.rs: with_native_roots vs with_webpki_roots). with_extra_root_certificate is documented and scoped to the token endpoint, and it is pre-admitted via RootCertStore::add, so nothing is silently dropped. The sibling fixtures using the same mechanism (oauth_interaction, oauth_challenge, oauth_tool_catalog, oauth_core_rpc, oauth_client_credentials) all gate on native-tls-roots; these two gate on `tasks` only.
Fix: gate both on all(tasks, native-tls-roots). Harness bug, not product.
close_reason: Verified by run:v-b8-client-tls at commit:f91e5999. evidence: cargo test -p fastmcp-client --features tasks,apps,native-tls-roots,builtin-auth-server: tests/oauth_task_watch 46/0 and tests/oauth_task_watch_drive 26/0 (previously 6/40 and 0/26 under UnknownIssuer). Fix commits:c48c2e97 (native-tls-roots gating), cdc76410 (dark-target compile fixes). Only dirty file was server proxy.rs, not compiled by these targets.

- Connect list changes to subscriptions and cache invalidation.
- Remove modern per-session prompt disablement.

  prompt-message attachment site for every locally produced

  dynamically after prompt registration or MRTR continuation.

- Allow MRTR input requests.
- Apply capability checks.
- Produce request-associated progress and logging through the exact
  transport policy; identifier-free stdio logs remain subject to
  Section 5.21 rather than being guessed onto a prompt request.
- Bound generated message count and total content size.

- Missing required arguments fail before handler invocation.
- Unknown prompts and every invalid argument shape use `-32602`;
  internal failures use `-32603`, and neither path invokes or exposes a
  partial handler result.
- Final content variants round-trip.
- MRTR retries retain semantic parameters.
- Result size limits are enforced.

- Argument validation.

  malformed/non-object/null arguments, non-string value, duplicate/
  unknown name policy, and internal failure; assert `-32602` versus
  `-32603`, zero handler calls for admission failures, no tool-style
  result, and bounded/redacted messages.

- Dynamic prompt `ResourceLink`/`EmbeddedResource` policy tests,

  custom scheme, and stale/wrong-use admission token.
- MRTR prompt get.
- Capability negative tests.
- Size-limit tests.

Dependencies:

- MRTR-01.
- HTTP-04.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### PRT-03 — Implement final capabilities, versions, and errors

Outcome:

Make per-request version and capability validation exact.

Reason:

Version negotiation moved from initialization to every request.

Implementation:

- Implement final ClientCapabilities.
- Implement final ServerCapabilities.
- Add the namespaced extensions maps.
- Preserve documented experimental/open capability fields where the
  final schema permits them.
- Model the explicitly open top level of both capability objects with
  a bounded, presence-aware ordered unknown-member set (or an
  equivalent lossless raw field set) for every key other than the
  exact known fields. Preserve each admitted key and any bounded JSON
  value—including null, boolean, exact number, string, array, or
  object—during peer/proxy round trip. A key that exactly collides with
  a known capability must validate as that known field and can never
  fall back to the unknown set; a case variant or look-alike remains
  unknown. Unknown top-level members are inert regardless of name,
  truthiness, or nonemptiness: they cannot satisfy a core or
  registered-extension capability, required-capability path, routing,
  authorization, cache partition, or feature grant. Safe local
  constructors expose custom top-level emission only through an
  explicit bounded custom-capability registration; standard
  extensions continue to use `extensions`.
- Preserve the same bounded ordered inert extras on the generated
  schema's open structural child objects: client `roots`, `sampling`,
  and `elicitation`, plus server `prompts`, `resources`, and `tools`.
  An exact known-child collision must validate its declared
  object/boolean shape and cannot fall back to an extra; every other
  child key may retain any bounded JSON value. Parent presence still
  grants only its baseline capability, while unknown children never
  grant sampling context/tools, elicitation form/URL,
  prompts/tools-list change, or resources list-change/subscription.
  For elicitation specifically, literal `{}` alone retains the dated
  form shorthand; a nonempty object containing only unknown children
  violates the peer's MUST to declare at least one known mode and is
  rejected, while inert extras alongside `form` and/or `url` are
  preserved.
- Decode every open capability `JSONObject` through Section 5.8's
  corrected recursive `JSONValue`, preserving bounded nested null and
  fractional values rather than inheriting the raw generated
  definition's integer-only narrowing. Generic preservation never
  activates an extension or grants a capability.
- Model capability presence and sub-capability presence exactly.
  `roots: {}` is roots support; `sampling: {}` does not imply
  `sampling.tools` or `sampling.context`. Elicitation follows the
  dated backward-compatible shorthand exactly: absent `elicitation`
  grants neither mode; present `{}` grants form mode; present
  `{form:{}}` grants form; present `{url:{}}` grants URL; and both
  members grant both. Safe local constructors canonically emit the
  explicit `form` member rather than the shorthand, but peer-empty is
  valid and semantically equivalent to form—not a diagnostic or
  grant-none state. Unknown members never grant a mode, and the
  unknown-only invalid case follows the preceding rule.
- Treat `false` child notification flags as not enabled, without
  rewriting their wire presence during a lossless peer round trip.
  Required-capability checks operate on semantic presence/true state,
  never on a nonempty unknown object or an extension key that merely
  resembles a core capability.
- Add required-capability path evaluation.
- Implement the exact `HeaderMismatchError` code. It has no
  mismatch-specific required data shape: preserve an admitted peer's
  bounded generic optional `Error.data`, but canonical local HTTP
  mismatch emission does not fabricate or require `data`.
- Implement MissingRequiredClientCapability error and data.
- Serialize its `data.requiredCapabilities` as the exact
  `ClientCapabilities` object the server requires; retain flattened
  capability paths only for internal diagnostics.
- Implement UnsupportedProtocolVersion error and data.
- Reserve the final MCP error range.
- Preserve decoding of grandfathered error codes from `-32019`
  through `-32000`, inclusive, without
  assigning them cross-implementation meaning.
- Do not allocate new FastMCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32019, -32000]`.
- Do not allocate undefined MCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Do not emit retired `-32002` or `-32042` in modern mode.
- Put new application-defined error codes outside JSON-RPC's reserved
  inclusive interval `[-32768, -32000]`.
- Classify known codes only after exact integer parsing and checked
  range conversion. Preserve an unknown arbitrary-precision integer
  code as an unknown peer/application error rather than overflowing,
  rounding, or remapping it.
- Stop emitting retired modern resource errors.
- Add HTTP status mapping separately from JSON-RPC code mapping.
- Map `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` exactly to HTTP 400 plus
  JSON-RPC `-32021`.
- Define one canonical peer-facing internal-failure constructor with a
  fixed code/message and no arbitrary source/panic text. Accept only
  bounded typed public error data explicitly owned by another package;
  incident IDs, backtraces, Rust type names, panic payloads, and error
  chains remain local and cannot be flattened into `Error.data`.
- Provide version-aware parsing for the legacy adapter.

Acceptance:

- Unsupported versions list exact supported versions.
- Missing-capability errors contain the exact required-capabilities
  object and diagnostics identify its leaf paths.
- Roots, sampling context/tool use, elicitation form/URL, logging,
  completions, catalog, list-change, resource-subscription, and
  extension predicates agree with the exact parent/child capability
  shape.
- No application-defined code uses the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Unknown tool, prompt, resource, and invalid cursor map to the final
  Invalid Params behavior.
- Legacy clients may still recognize their historic missing-resource
  code inside the legacy decoder.
- A handler/middleware/extension panic or opaque internal error can map
  only to the canonical sanitized peer shape, never its payload.

Tests:

- Error-code allocation table test.
- Fractional/non-integral error-code rejection plus exact known,
  unknown, exponent-form integer, and beyond-`i64` code tests.
- Retired-code emission denylist.
- Exact error-data golden tests.
- Header-mismatch canonical absent-data golden plus bounded generic
  optional-data peer round trip; no local path requires invented
  mismatch data.
- Capability-path positive and negative tests.
- Capability presence matrix: absent/present-empty roots and sampling;
  sampling context/tools independently; elicitation form-only,
  URL-only, both, absent-grant-none, peer-empty-grants-form, canonical
  local explicit-form emission, unknown extras alongside a known mode,
  and unknown-only rejection; server child absent/false/true; and
  look-alike experimental/extension keys that grant nothing.
- Open structural-child goldens for roots/sampling/elicitation and
  prompts/resources/tools: every JSON-kind extra, ordered
  preservation, bounds, known-name collision, parent-baseline
  semantics, and no child-feature activation.
- Nested capability extension/experimental object/array/null/
  fractional-value corrected-oracle goldens, raw-artifact expected
  mismatch, bounds, and no-activation-from-preservation tests.
- Client/server unknown-top-level capability goldens for null,
  boolean, exact integer/fractional number, string, array, and object;
  ordered round trip, empty/look-alike/case-variant keys, exact-known
  collision, duplicate-member admission rejection, per-value and
  aggregate bounds, explicit custom registration, and proof that no
  unknown value activates negotiation, required-capability
  satisfaction, routing, authorization, caching, or a feature.
- Version fallback tests.
- HTTP status plus JSON-RPC body tests.
- Exact HTTP 400/`-32021` goldens for generic capability-gated,
  MRTR, Tasks, and registered-extension requests.
- Canonical internal-error goldens plus payload/backtrace/type-name/
  incident-ID/error-chain substitution negatives and exact absence of
  those values from JSON-RPC, HTTP, and SSE bytes.

Dependencies:

- FND-03.
- PRT-01.
- PRT-02.

comments.text:
PATTERN 4 FINDING (systematic sweep, MagentaOsprey) — two constants hold one wire value, and no test would fail if they diverged.

Pattern 4: no control that would fail if the mechanism were absent.
Found by the wave-15 positive sweep; cross-cutting between PRT-03 and
FND-03, so it is filed on both. Reviewer only; I have edited nothing.

THE TWO DECLARATIONS, neither defined in terms of the other:

  crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/protocol_version.rs:13
    pub const FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2026-07-28";
  crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/protocol_policy.rs:17
    pub const MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2026-07-28";

Each is independently pinned to the literal, which is good practice and is
why I nearly dismissed this:
  FINAL  pinned at prt_03_contract.rs:76, prt_03_integration.rs:46,
         fastmcp-protocol/src/lib.rs:269
  MODERN pinned at fnd_03_a.rs:47, fnd_03_i.rs:112

WHY THE PINS DO NOT CLOSE IT. Each pin compares its own constant to the
literal it was written beside. Nothing anywhere compares the two constants
to EACH OTHER -- I grepped every line mentioning both names across crates/
and tools/ and every hit is a usage (FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION_META_KEY paired
with MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION as a value), never an equality assertion.

THE FAILURE PATH IS CONCRETE, not hypothetical. On the next revision bump,
an agent updates FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION and the three pins that name it, and
does not know MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION exists. MODERN's own pins still assert
the OLD literal, so they pass. The tree is now green with two different
values for one wire field, and:

  crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:2382 writes MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION into
    the FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION_META_KEY meta field
  the PRT-03 admission path validates against FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION

so the server would advertise one revision and admit another. That is a
wire-visible defect reachable by an ordinary, careful edit, and no test in
the wave-15 set fails on it.

WHY THIS IS PATTERN 4 RATHER THAN A STYLE COMPLAINT. The suite has five
assertions about these constants and not one of them can fail if the
mechanism -- a single source of truth for the revision -- is absent. Remove
the shared identity entirely and every existing assertion still passes.
That is the definition the orchestrator gave: no control that would fail if
the mechanism were absent.

CHEAPEST FIX, one line, no behaviour change:

    pub const MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = crate::protocol_version::FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION;

That makes divergence unrepresentable rather than merely untested, which is
better than adding a cross-check assertion. If the two are deliberately
independent -- one naming the narrow modern surface's revision and the other
the policy surface's, with a future where they legitimately differ -- then
the right artifact is an explicit assertion that they are equal TODAY, plus
a comment saying under what circumstance they may diverge. Either is fine;
silence is not.

I did not apply either. protocol_policy.rs is LANE 4/5 territory and
protocol_version.rs is not mine; this is a reviewer note.

CONTEXT ON WHAT I ALMOST REPORTED INSTEAD. I first flagged the PRT-03
round-trips (assert_eq!(admission.protocol_version().as_str(),
FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION) at prt_03_contract.rs:72/89 and
prt_03_integration.rs:63) as pattern 3, an oracle taken from the code under
test. Re-derived before reporting and WITHDREW it: prt_03_contract.rs:76
pins the constant to the literal in the same test body, so the round-trip
proves plumbing over a pinned value and is sound. RoseStream did that
correctly. The residual gap is only the missing cross-check above.

Sweep denominator for this pass: 467 assert_eq! statements across 31
wave-15 positive bodies, 11 flagged as computed-on-both-sides and read by
hand.

comments.text:
SELF-FINDING AND REPAIR — my own source comment cited a proof that was not where it said
Worker: RoseStream. Found by doing the category-3 record pass AFTER a peer audit rather than before, per the
orchestrator's instruction. Recording it because the finding is mine and the mechanism that found it is
reusable.

WHAT WAS WRONG

crates/fastmcp-protocol/tests/prt_03_contract.rs, the doc comment on `method_requires_name`, said:

    "both facts are proved independently by `prt_03_a_positive`, which admits `tools/list` with no name mirror
     at all and admits `tools/call` only with one."

Only the first half was true. `prt_03_a_positive` admitted `tools/list` with no name mirror (the `nameless`
case), but it NEVER exercised `tools/call` without a name. "Admits `tools/call` only with one" is an
existential claim — it requires showing the absent-name case is REFUSED — and that observation lived in
`prt_03_b_positive`'s precedence ladder (rung 11, `MissingNameHeader`, reached with `tools/call` mirrored on
both sides), not in `prt_03_a_positive` at all.

WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A MISCITATION

`method_requires_name` hard-codes production behaviour:

    "tools/call" => true,
    "tools/list" => false,
    other => panic!(...)

That is a frozen constant about the shipped surface, and the ONLY thing that makes it legitimate rather than an
assumption is that both facts are proved nearby. A hard-coded constant whose justification cites the wrong test
is unfounded in the way that actually bites: a reader checking it looks in the named place, does not find the
proof, and cannot distinguish an unproven constant from a correctly-proven but misfiled one. The oracle is used
by the B swap-proof to decide which rules apply, so an unfounded entry there would propagate into every
precedence conclusion.

THE REPAIR — supply the evidence, do not soften the claim

I closed the gap rather than weakening the comment to match it. `prt_03_a_positive` now carries the complement
directly, from the same `admissible()` baseline:

    assert_eq!(
        mismatch_reason(FinalHttpRequestMetadata { header_name: None, body_name: None, ..admissible() }),
        HeaderMismatchReason::MissingNameHeader,
        "a method that requires Mcp-Name must refuse the absent mirror that tools/list accepts"
    );

That makes the attribution true and is a real strengthening independently of the comment: the conditionality of
the name stage is now a DISTINCTION — the same absent mirror admitted for one method and refused for another —
rather than a single observation. Before this, "the name stage is conditional" could have been satisfied by a
surface that never required a name at all.

The corrected doc comment records what was wrong and why, rather than quietly reading as though it was always
right.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, SINCE THE METHOD IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART

I had already done a category-3 record pass earlier and found nothing here. I found this only after auditing
FND-05, where the finding was a SOURCE comment whose premise had become false — and where I argued a stale
source comment is worse than a stale bead comment because it carries no ordering information. Turning that same
question on my own files produced this within minutes.

The orchestrator's instruction to run the category-3 pass AFTER the peer audit rather than before is correct,
and this is a worked instance: the peer audit installs a specific question, and the question is what finds your
own instance. My earlier pass had no such question and found nothing.

This is the fourth defect of my own I have found this wave (arithmetic assertion, oracle written from the
answer, a planted negative refusing for an unnamed reason, and now a miscited proof). The first three were
surfaced by execution or by the verification lane. This one was surfaced by reading, which is cheaper, and the
difference was having just audited the same shape in someone else's work.

title: PRT-03 implementation B: request admission precedence and typed errors
description:
Executable B role for PRT-03.

Owned capability slice: request admission precedence and typed errors.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:PRT-03:B:BEGIN -->
Canonical B role for PRT-03.

Owned capability slice: request admission precedence and typed errors.
Named shipped consumer: public modern protocol ingress.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### PRT-03 — Implement final capabilities, versions, and errors

Outcome:

Make per-request version and capability validation exact.

Reason:

Version negotiation moved from initialization to every request.

Implementation:

- Implement final ClientCapabilities.
- Implement final ServerCapabilities.
- Add the namespaced extensions maps.
- Preserve documented experimental/open capability fields where the
  final schema permits them.
- Model the explicitly open top level of both capability objects with
  a bounded, presence-aware ordered unknown-member set (or an
  equivalent lossless raw field set) for every key other than the
  exact known fields. Preserve each admitted key and any bounded JSON
  value—including null, boolean, exact number, string, array, or
  object—during peer/proxy round trip. A key that exactly collides with
  a known capability must validate as that known field and can never
  fall back to the unknown set; a case variant or look-alike remains
  unknown. Unknown top-level members are inert regardless of name,
  truthiness, or nonemptiness: they cannot satisfy a core or
  registered-extension capability, required-capability path, routing,
  authorization, cache partition, or feature grant. Safe local
  constructors expose custom top-level emission only through an
  explicit bounded custom-capability registration; standard
  extensions continue to use `extensions`.
- Preserve the same bounded ordered inert extras on the generated
  schema's open structural child objects: client `roots`, `sampling`,
  and `elicitation`, plus server `prompts`, `resources`, and `tools`.
  An exact known-child collision must validate its declared
  object/boolean shape and cannot fall back to an extra; every other
  child key may retain any bounded JSON value. Parent presence still
  grants only its baseline capability, while unknown children never
  grant sampling context/tools, elicitation form/URL,
  prompts/tools-list change, or resources list-change/subscription.
  For elicitation specifically, literal `{}` alone retains the dated
  form shorthand; a nonempty object containing only unknown children
  violates the peer's MUST to declare at least one known mode and is
  rejected, while inert extras alongside `form` and/or `url` are
  preserved.
- Decode every open capability `JSONObject` through Section 5.8's
  corrected recursive `JSONValue`, preserving bounded nested null and
  fractional values rather than inheriting the raw generated
  definition's integer-only narrowing. Generic preservation never
  activates an extension or grants a capability.
- Model capability presence and sub-capability presence exactly.
  `roots: {}` is roots support; `sampling: {}` does not imply
  `sampling.tools` or `sampling.context`. Elicitation follows the
  dated backward-compatible shorthand exactly: absent `elicitation`
  grants neither mode; present `{}` grants form mode; present
  `{form:{}}` grants form; present `{url:{}}` grants URL; and both
  members grant both. Safe local constructors canonically emit the
  explicit `form` member rather than the shorthand, but peer-empty is
  valid and semantically equivalent to form—not a diagnostic or
  grant-none state. Unknown members never grant a mode, and the
  unknown-only invalid case follows the preceding rule.
- Treat `false` child notification flags as not enabled, without
  rewriting their wire presence during a lossless peer round trip.
  Required-capability checks operate on semantic presence/true state,
  never on a nonempty unknown object or an extension key that merely
  resembles a core capability.
- Add required-capability path evaluation.
- Implement the exact `HeaderMismatchError` code. It has no
  mismatch-specific required data shape: preserve an admitted peer's
  bounded generic optional `Error.data`, but canonical local HTTP
  mismatch emission does not fabricate or require `data`.
- Implement MissingRequiredClientCapability error and data.
- Serialize its `data.requiredCapabilities` as the exact
  `ClientCapabilities` object the server requires; retain flattened
  capability paths only for internal diagnostics.
- Implement UnsupportedProtocolVersion error and data.
- Reserve the final MCP error range.
- Preserve decoding of grandfathered error codes from `-32019`
  through `-32000`, inclusive, without
  assigning them cross-implementation meaning.
- Do not allocate new FastMCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32019, -32000]`.
- Do not allocate undefined MCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Do not emit retired `-32002` or `-32042` in modern mode.
- Put new application-defined error codes outside JSON-RPC's reserved
  inclusive interval `[-32768, -32000]`.
- Classify known codes only after exact integer parsing and checked
  range conversion. Preserve an unknown arbitrary-precision integer
  code as an unknown peer/application error rather than overflowing,
  rounding, or remapping it.
- Stop emitting retired modern resource errors.
- Add HTTP status mapping separately from JSON-RPC code mapping.
- Map `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` exactly to HTTP 400 plus
  JSON-RPC `-32021`.
- Define one canonical peer-facing internal-failure constructor with a
  fixed code/message and no arbitrary source/panic text. Accept only
  bounded typed public error data explicitly owned by another package;
  incident IDs, backtraces, Rust type names, panic payloads, and error
  chains remain local and cannot be flattened into `Error.data`.
- Provide version-aware parsing for the legacy adapter.

Acceptance:

- Unsupported versions list exact supported versions.
- Missing-capability errors contain the exact required-capabilities
  object and diagnostics identify its leaf paths.
- Roots, sampling context/tool use, elicitation form/URL, logging,
  completions, catalog, list-change, resource-subscription, and
  extension predicates agree with the exact parent/child capability
  shape.
- No application-defined code uses the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Unknown tool, prompt, resource, and invalid cursor map to the final
  Invalid Params behavior.
- Legacy clients may still recognize their historic missing-resource
  code inside the legacy decoder.
- A handler/middleware/extension panic or opaque internal error can map
  only to the canonical sanitized peer shape, never its payload.

Tests:

- Error-code allocation table test.
- Fractional/non-integral error-code rejection plus exact known,
  unknown, exponent-form integer, and beyond-`i64` code tests.
- Retired-code emission denylist.
- Exact error-data golden tests.
- Header-mismatch canonical absent-data golden plus bounded generic
  optional-data peer round trip; no local path requires invented
  mismatch data.
- Capability-path positive and negative tests.
- Capability presence matrix: absent/present-empty roots and sampling;
  sampling context/tools independently; elicitation form-only,
  URL-only, both, absent-grant-none, peer-empty-grants-form, canonical
  local explicit-form emission, unknown extras alongside a known mode,
  and unknown-only rejection; server child absent/false/true; and
  look-alike experimental/extension keys that grant nothing.
- Open structural-child goldens for roots/sampling/elicitation and
  prompts/resources/tools: every JSON-kind extra, ordered
  preservation, bounds, known-name collision, parent-baseline
  semantics, and no child-feature activation.
- Nested capability extension/experimental object/array/null/
  fractional-value corrected-oracle goldens, raw-artifact expected
  mismatch, bounds, and no-activation-from-preservation tests.
- Client/server unknown-top-level capability goldens for null,
  boolean, exact integer/fractional number, string, array, and object;
  ordered round trip, empty/look-alike/case-variant keys, exact-known
  collision, duplicate-member admission rejection, per-value and
  aggregate bounds, explicit custom registration, and proof that no
  unknown value activates negotiation, required-capability
  satisfaction, routing, authorization, caching, or a feature.
- Version fallback tests.
- HTTP status plus JSON-RPC body tests.
- Exact HTTP 400/`-32021` goldens for generic capability-gated,
  MRTR, Tasks, and registered-extension requests.
- Canonical internal-error goldens plus payload/backtrace/type-name/
  incident-ID/error-chain substitution negatives and exact absence of
  those values from JSON-RPC, HTTP, and SSE bytes.

Dependencies:

- FND-03.
- PRT-01.
- PRT-02.

comments.text:
SUBMISSION — bd-prt-03-implementation-b-gid1 (PRT-03 implementation B: request admission precedence and typed errors)
Worker: RoseStream (WAVE-15 LANE 5). Not closed by me.

REVISION: 425581ff  (shared with bd-prt-03-implementation-a-l1qd)
FILES: crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/protocol_version.rs   (production: +FinalAdmissionRule,
         +FINAL_ADMISSION_PRECEDENCE, +RequestAdmissionError::rule())
       crates/fastmcp-protocol/tests/prt_03_contract.rs  (B pair rewritten)

FROZEN TEST IDS: prt_03_b_positive, prt_03_b_planted_negative
Target: integration test `prt_03_contract`, package fastmcp-protocol. NO required-features, NO file-scope cfg.
SINGULARITY: the src/protocol_version.rs copies were renamed to prt_03_b_unit_*; `rg -c "fn prt_03_b_positive\b"`
=> exactly 1. Same for the negative.

THE PRODUCTION GAP — an invariant that was real but unnamed:
  The order in which admission evaluates its sixteen rules is wire-visible contract. A peer violating several at
  once must get the same refusal from every conforming implementation, or it cannot diagnose itself: told
  EmptyHeader when it ALSO mismatched its method mirror, it fixes the header, resends, and is refused again for a
  reason it was never told about.
  That order existed only as the statement order of `?` operators inside admit_final_request and
  admit_final_http_request. Unnamed, unpinned, silently reorderable by any refactor that moved a line, and
  therefore something nobody could be shown to have broken.
  SHIPPED: FINAL_ADMISSION_PRECEDENCE (16 entries, three stages) and RequestAdmissionError::rule(), which joins a
  refusal back to the declared rule. Purely additive; no existing signature moved.

MAKING THE RULES CONTEND (the orchestrator's explicit requirement):
  A precedence test passes trivially when only one rule ever matches. prt_03_b_positive walks the declared order
  repairing exactly ONE rule per rung, using the minimum value that satisfies that rule and nothing more — an
  empty string where emptiness is next, a real-but-unsupported version where support is next, a mirrored-but-wrong
  value where the mirror is next. At every rung the request still violates EVERY later rule, so each assertion is
  a contest between the declared winner and all its successors. Repairing the last rule must admit; if it did not,
  some rung above was being satisfied by an unrelated repair rather than by precedence.
  The repair table is keyed on the RULE, never on its ordinal, so renumbering the published precedence cannot
  silently re-point a repair at the wrong rule.

THE SWAP-PROOF — reordering must change the answer:
  For each of the 15 adjacent pairs, prt_03_b_planted_negative takes a request violating both, asks what the
  shipped order predicts, then asks what the SAME order with those two entries EXCHANGED predicts, and requires
  the prediction to CHANGE. It then requires the implementation to follow the shipped answer and NOT the swapped
  one. If reordering the rules does not change the answer, the rung is not testing precedence — and that is
  asserted rather than assumed.
  14 of 15 pairs get the full swap-proof. Exactly one is structurally gated rather than ordered: the admitter
  cannot judge a name mirror until the method mirror has agreed on a method. That gating is asserted explicitly
  (successor inapplicable now; applicable the instant the gate is repaired) and `gated_pairs == 1` is pinned, so a
  change that quietly makes more pairs non-contending FAILS instead of passing with less coverage.

A DEFECT I FOUND IN MY OWN ORACLE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WOULD HAVE PASSED:
  The independent oracle deciding which rules apply deliberately does not call the admitter — a precedence test
  whose notion of "violated" comes from the thing under test can only confirm itself.
  My first draft wrote that oracle FROM THE EXPECTED OUTCOME: it required HeaderBodyVersionMismatch to have both
  values non-empty, and UnsupportedProtocolVersion to have an agreeing mirror. Neither is a shipped condition —
  the shipped checks are bare `header != body` and `header != FINAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION`. Those preconditions are
  CONSEQUENCES of the ordering, not part of the rules.
  With that oracle, pairs (3,4) and (4,5) evaluated as non-contending, the swap changed nothing, and the
  precedence became untestable by construction — while every assertion still passed. Each rule now models only
  its own condition. This is the RH-1 failure mode arriving through an oracle rather than through an assertion.

TYPED ERRORS: MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError carries the exact ClientCapabilities object
(`{"requiredCapabilities":{"roots":{"listChanged":true}}}`), not flattened leaf paths; 400 / -32021. The three
final ingress codes are asserted distinct (-32020 / -32021 / -32022) so a peer can tell a header problem from a
version problem from a capability problem.

PLANTED NEGATIVE also covers: stage contention (a request breaking BOTH the version mirror and the name mirror is
refused by the version stage, and repairing only the version mirror then surfaces the name failure — proving it was
present all along and suppressed by precedence rather than absent); and a typed-error data-shape refusal
(a non-object required-capabilities value is refused as NotAnObject rather than coerced).
NAMED MUTABLE STATE unchanged byte-for-byte: the published precedence slice and the re-admitted protocol version.

GATE: as recorded on bd-prt-03-implementation-a-l1qd — Checking fastmcp-protocol, Finished in 31.08s, exit=0,
zero ^error after ANSI stripping. 11 dispatches; the first 10 were RCH worker faults, not code.

UNMET ON THIS BEAD (stated, not spun out — RH-9):
  - Runner/inventory/receipt require the orchestrator's lane. COMPILE-VERIFIED, NOT EXECUTED.
  - The package body's error-code allocation work (reserved MCP range, grandfathered -32019..-32000 decode
    preservation, the retired-code denylist, fractional/beyond-i64 code rejection, the canonical sanitized
    internal-failure constructor) is NOT implemented and is NOT in this slice's file surface. Recorded as
    unmet package-level work rather than absorbed here to make this bead look complete.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this role alone does not establish PRT-03 parent completion or any aggregate claim.

title: PRT-03 verification: version/error receipt
description:
Executable V role for PRT-03.

Owned capability slice: version/error receipt.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:PRT-03:V:BEGIN -->
Canonical V role for PRT-03.

Owned capability slice: version/error receipt.
Named shipped consumer: public modern protocol ingress.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### PRT-03 — Implement final capabilities, versions, and errors

Outcome:

Make per-request version and capability validation exact.

Reason:

Version negotiation moved from initialization to every request.

Implementation:

- Implement final ClientCapabilities.
- Implement final ServerCapabilities.
- Add the namespaced extensions maps.
- Preserve documented experimental/open capability fields where the
  final schema permits them.
- Model the explicitly open top level of both capability objects with
  a bounded, presence-aware ordered unknown-member set (or an
  equivalent lossless raw field set) for every key other than the
  exact known fields. Preserve each admitted key and any bounded JSON
  value—including null, boolean, exact number, string, array, or
  object—during peer/proxy round trip. A key that exactly collides with
  a known capability must validate as that known field and can never
  fall back to the unknown set; a case variant or look-alike remains
  unknown. Unknown top-level members are inert regardless of name,
  truthiness, or nonemptiness: they cannot satisfy a core or
  registered-extension capability, required-capability path, routing,
  authorization, cache partition, or feature grant. Safe local
  constructors expose custom top-level emission only through an
  explicit bounded custom-capability registration; standard
  extensions continue to use `extensions`.
- Preserve the same bounded ordered inert extras on the generated
  schema's open structural child objects: client `roots`, `sampling`,
  and `elicitation`, plus server `prompts`, `resources`, and `tools`.
  An exact known-child collision must validate its declared
  object/boolean shape and cannot fall back to an extra; every other
  child key may retain any bounded JSON value. Parent presence still
  grants only its baseline capability, while unknown children never
  grant sampling context/tools, elicitation form/URL,
  prompts/tools-list change, or resources list-change/subscription.
  For elicitation specifically, literal `{}` alone retains the dated
  form shorthand; a nonempty object containing only unknown children
  violates the peer's MUST to declare at least one known mode and is
  rejected, while inert extras alongside `form` and/or `url` are
  preserved.
- Decode every open capability `JSONObject` through Section 5.8's
  corrected recursive `JSONValue`, preserving bounded nested null and
  fractional values rather than inheriting the raw generated
  definition's integer-only narrowing. Generic preservation never
  activates an extension or grants a capability.
- Model capability presence and sub-capability presence exactly.
  `roots: {}` is roots support; `sampling: {}` does not imply
  `sampling.tools` or `sampling.context`. Elicitation follows the
  dated backward-compatible shorthand exactly: absent `elicitation`
  grants neither mode; present `{}` grants form mode; present
  `{form:{}}` grants form; present `{url:{}}` grants URL; and both
  members grant both. Safe local constructors canonically emit the
  explicit `form` member rather than the shorthand, but peer-empty is
  valid and semantically equivalent to form—not a diagnostic or
  grant-none state. Unknown members never grant a mode, and the
  unknown-only invalid case follows the preceding rule.
- Treat `false` child notification flags as not enabled, without
  rewriting their wire presence during a lossless peer round trip.
  Required-capability checks operate on semantic presence/true state,
  never on a nonempty unknown object or an extension key that merely
  resembles a core capability.
- Add required-capability path evaluation.
- Implement the exact `HeaderMismatchError` code. It has no
  mismatch-specific required data shape: preserve an admitted peer's
  bounded generic optional `Error.data`, but canonical local HTTP
  mismatch emission does not fabricate or require `data`.
- Implement MissingRequiredClientCapability error and data.
- Serialize its `data.requiredCapabilities` as the exact
  `ClientCapabilities` object the server requires; retain flattened
  capability paths only for internal diagnostics.
- Implement UnsupportedProtocolVersion error and data.
- Reserve the final MCP error range.
- Preserve decoding of grandfathered error codes from `-32019`
  through `-32000`, inclusive, without
  assigning them cross-implementation meaning.
- Do not allocate new FastMCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32019, -32000]`.
- Do not allocate undefined MCP errors in the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Do not emit retired `-32002` or `-32042` in modern mode.
- Put new application-defined error codes outside JSON-RPC's reserved
  inclusive interval `[-32768, -32000]`.
- Classify known codes only after exact integer parsing and checked
  range conversion. Preserve an unknown arbitrary-precision integer
  code as an unknown peer/application error rather than overflowing,
  rounding, or remapping it.
- Stop emitting retired modern resource errors.
- Add HTTP status mapping separately from JSON-RPC code mapping.
- Map `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` exactly to HTTP 400 plus
  JSON-RPC `-32021`.
- Define one canonical peer-facing internal-failure constructor with a
  fixed code/message and no arbitrary source/panic text. Accept only
  bounded typed public error data explicitly owned by another package;
  incident IDs, backtraces, Rust type names, panic payloads, and error
  chains remain local and cannot be flattened into `Error.data`.
- Provide version-aware parsing for the legacy adapter.

Acceptance:

- Unsupported versions list exact supported versions.
- Missing-capability errors contain the exact required-capabilities
  object and diagnostics identify its leaf paths.
- Roots, sampling context/tool use, elicitation form/URL, logging,
  completions, catalog, list-change, resource-subscription, and
  extension predicates agree with the exact parent/child capability
  shape.
- No application-defined code uses the inclusive interval
  `[-32099, -32020]`.
- Unknown tool, prompt, resource, and invalid cursor map to the final
  Invalid Params behavior.
- Legacy clients may still recognize their historic missing-resource
  code inside the legacy decoder.
- A handler/middleware/extension panic or opaque internal error can map
  only to the canonical sanitized peer shape, never its payload.

Tests:

- Error-code allocation table test.
- Fractional/non-integral error-code rejection plus exact known,
  unknown, exponent-form integer, and beyond-`i64` code tests.
- Retired-code emission denylist.
- Exact error-data golden tests.
- Header-mismatch canonical absent-data golden plus bounded generic
  optional-data peer round trip; no local path requires invented
  mismatch data.
- Capability-path positive and negative tests.
- Capability presence matrix: absent/present-empty roots and sampling;
  sampling context/tools independently; elicitation form-only,
  URL-only, both, absent-grant-none, peer-empty-grants-form, canonical
  local explicit-form emission, unknown extras alongside a known mode,
  and unknown-only rejection; server child absent/false/true; and
  look-alike experimental/extension keys that grant nothing.
- Open structural-child goldens for roots/sampling/elicitation and
  prompts/resources/tools: every JSON-kind extra, ordered
  preservation, bounds, known-name collision, parent-baseline
  semantics, and no child-feature activation.
- Nested capability extension/experimental object/array/null/
  fractional-value corrected-oracle goldens, raw-artifact expected
  mismatch, bounds, and no-activation-from-preservation tests.
- Client/server unknown-top-level capability goldens for null,
  boolean, exact integer/fractional number, string, array, and object;
  ordered round trip, empty/look-alike/case-variant keys, exact-known
  collision, duplicate-member admission rejection, per-value and
  aggregate bounds, explicit custom registration, and proof that no
  unknown value activates negotiation, required-capability
  satisfaction, routing, authorization, caching, or a feature.
- Version fallback tests.
- HTTP status plus JSON-RPC body tests.
- Exact HTTP 400/`-32021` goldens for generic capability-gated,
  MRTR, Tasks, and registered-extension requests.
- Canonical internal-error goldens plus payload/backtrace/type-name/
  incident-ID/error-chain substitution negatives and exact absence of
  those values from JSON-RPC, HTTP, and SSE bytes.

Dependencies:

- FND-03.
- PRT-01.
- PRT-02.

title: Client progress re-emits progressToken with a canonicalised exponent (4.2e1 -> 4.2e+1): 590dbc97's own exact-spelling test fails on main
description:
The client lib test execution::tests::executor_progress_preserves_exact_values_and_orders_mathematically, added by outside commit 590dbc97 (committed unrun), FAILS on main:

    panicked at crates/fastmcp-client/src/execution.rs:4331:17
    assertion `left == right` failed  left: "4.2e+1"  right: "4.2e1"

Observed by WildMountain run v27b (clean RCH snapshot 5297585a = 9582bb5d + 71e952e3's change; -p fastmcp-client --lib --all-features-free default, filter execution::; 581 passed, 1 failed).

What is wrong: the progress frame sends "progressToken":4.2e1. The re-emitted notification's progressToken is "4.2e+1". progress and total keep their exact lexemes (they are rebuilt at execution.rs ~3444-3455 from as_str()), but the token is rebuilt at ~3457 via ProgressMarker::Number(marker).to_number(). JsonInteger::to_number returns its retained Number unchanged, so the JsonInteger already holds "4.2e+1": the exponent spelling is canonicalised earlier, when the token is decoded into ProgressMarker (the comment at ~3436 notes serde_json::to_value normalises exponent spellings). 590dbc97's contract says it retains original number spellings, so the product breaks its own contract; the test is right.

Acceptance:
- [x] The progressToken keeps its exact wire lexeme through admission and re-emission (fix at the decode that canonicalises, not by relaxing the test).
- [x] The existing test passes unchanged, plus a near-identical negative showing a different token spelling is not treated as the same owner only when the canonical identities differ (590dbc97's canonical-identity ownership must keep working).
- [x] Clean-snapshot RCH: cargo test -p fastmcp-client --lib -- execution:: green.
close_reason: Verified by run:v31a+v31b at commit:4f5705b7. evidence: Fix 4f5705b7 (ProudValley): ProgressMarker gets a hand-written Deserialize that reads the raw-value token as JsonInteger does, so the exact exponent spelling survives; ownership still keys by canonical RequestId identity. Item 1: the failing test's expectation was untouched, and execution::tests::executor_progress_preserves_exact_values_and_orders_mathematically now passes. Item 2: executor_progress_token_owns_by_canonical_identity_not_spelling ok (4.3e1 names 43 and never reaches the stream; 420e-1 names 42 and is owned); executor_progress_tokens_reject_active_numeric_aliases_and_allow_terminal_reuse ok. Item 3: v31a cargo test --locked -j 4 -p fastmcp-client --lib -- execution:: at clean snapshot 4f5705b7 (vmi1152480): 46 passed 0 failed. Also v31b cargo test -p fastmcp-protocol --lib UNFILTERED at 4f5705b7: 663/0/0, incl. messages::tests::progress_marker_keeps_an_integral_exponent_spelling_and_rejects_a_fractional_one. description:
Executable A role for PXY-01.

Owned capability slice: upstream discovery, Tool admission, union catalog, trusted route identity, and typed EXT-DEV descriptor routing.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:PXY-01:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for PXY-01.

Owned capability slice: upstream discovery, Tool admission, union catalog, trusted route identity, and typed EXT-DEV descriptor routing.
Named shipped consumer: public gateway downstream/upstream path.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### PXY-01 — Negotiate both proxy legs independently

Outcome:

Make the gateway an honest MCP endpoint on both sides.

Reason:

Client-facing and upstream servers may support different versions and
extensions.

Implementation:

- Run discovery/version policy on each upstream.
- Build a union catalog of independently routable upstream behavior.
- Admit each upstream `tools/list` page through TOOL-01/SCH-01 before
  it can enter the union catalog. A page with one unadmitted Tool
  fails that upstream page atomically; the gateway neither filters it,
  commits a partial route/cursor/cache, nor forwards malformed schema
  metadata to a modern downstream leg. Other independently healthy
  upstream catalogs remain isolated, but no error path silently
  presents the failed upstream as a shorter successful catalog.
- Attach an internal `UpstreamInstanceId` routing set plus a separate
  security-origin set to each advertised tool, resource, prompt,
  completion source, and extension-backed item. An origin is an
  authorization/credential attribute, never a unique route identity.
- Reject duplicate downstream tool names, prompt names, concrete
  resource URIs, resource-template identities, or completion
  identities by default.
- Permit a collision only when configuration assigns validated,
  stable upstream aliases/namespaces or explicitly groups
  byte-equivalent descriptors under one deterministic route set.
- Construct one frozen opaque `UpstreamInstanceId` from trusted local
  configuration: deployment/config generation, a stable unique
  config-entry identity, transport kind, and that transport's complete
  endpoint identity. For HTTP, include the validated canonical
  absolute endpoint URI through its full path and any explicitly
  permitted query, with scheme, canonical host, and effective port;
  the origin alone is insufficient because one origin can host
  multiple MCP endpoints. For stdio, include the stable config-entry
  identity and a bounded digest of the configured executable identity,
  argv, working-directory policy, and nonsecret environment profile;
  two intentionally duplicated commands remain distinct by config
  entry. A custom transport must provide an equally explicit,
  configuration-bound endpoint identity or is ineligible for union
  routing. Never derive an
  alias, namespace, route key, instance ID, or collision winner from the
  self-reported `serverInfo.name` (or any other `serverInfo` field);
  self-reported identity remains display/log/debug-only.
- Treat same-name descriptors with different schemas, annotations,
  auth requirements, or behavior metadata as ambiguous even if one
  upstream currently has higher health.
- Do not invent an automatic name/URI rewrite.
  A configured alias becomes the actual advertised downstream
  identity, must satisfy the applicable MCP grammar, and maps back
  losslessly to the upstream identity.
- Expose only each item's behavior that the gateway can fulfill end to
  end against at least one eligible upstream.
- Compute core capability and extension intersections only after an
  operation selects one upstream or an intentional fan-out set.
- Treat every stateless modern client→server extension-notification
  activation proof as leg-local. Consume and terminate the sealed
  downstream proof at the gateway; never forward its receipt, owner
  handle, endpoint/security/settings bindings, or generation claims as
  upstream evidence. For each selected route, require the independently
  frozen upstream descriptor and effective settings, then either
  reconstruct and resolve a fresh `SelfContained` proof from the
  sanitized current upstream message or map to and revalidate a
  separately live upstream `NegotiatedOwner`. Reject the route before
  upstream emission when the proof cannot be represented losslessly or
  independently established. A downstream proof, registration,
  discovery record, prior request, or gateway connection never
  activates the upstream leg.
- Route an EXT-DEV-01 out-of-tree descriptor only through its public
  typed codecs, activation contract, authorization requirements, result
  discriminator, and subscription descriptors. The proxy must not
  downcast to private built-in types or expose an unchecked JSON
  passthrough merely because both legs register the same identifier.
- Apply registered fallback rules per route, not globally.
- Select a route by stable configured priority after capability,
  authorization, extension, and health eligibility filtering.
- Permit fan-out only for an explicitly configured operation whose
  merge semantics, error policy, ordering, and idempotency are
  declared; never fan out a side-effecting tool merely because names
  collide.
- Track upstream era per `UpstreamInstanceId` and connection, never per
  origin alone.
- On the core proxy path, reject a legacy-classified upstream with an
  actionable profile-disabled error; PXY-LEG-01 adds mixed-era
  translation.
- Keep downstream request context separate from upstream client
  context.
- Freeze endpoint role at each proxy codec boundary: malformed
  downstream client request bytes follow the server-ingress error rule,
  while malformed upstream server output fails that upstream
  execution/connection with no JSON-RPC response sent upstream. Never
  copy an omitted-ID error disposition or raw-decode failure across
  legs.
- On both the downstream server and upstream client legs, reject a top-level
  JSON-RPC batch array, including array-of-one-valid-request and mixed-array
  forms, through PRT-01 raw admission before catalog routing, dispatch,
  correlation, authorization, cache, task/session/subscription, proxy
  forwarding, response, or leg state effects. The downstream leg uses only
  its server-ingress disposition; the upstream leg fails only its owning
  execution/connection and emits no response upstream.
- Never copy self-reported identity into auth context.
- Emit gateway server identity in downstream results.
- Expose upstream identity only as diagnostic metadata.
- Handle partial upstream availability deterministically.
- Freeze upstream alias, priority, and grouping configuration into the
  catalog revision and proxy fingerprint.
- Contribute bounded route availability, upstream-dependency health,
  saturation, rejection-class, retry, and failover observations to
  OPS-01 without using endpoint URLs, self-reported names, extension
  identifiers, principals, or handles as metric labels.

Acceptance:

- Gateway discovery never advertises an unusable capability.
- A downstream stateless-notification proof never crosses the proxy
  boundary as upstream authority; each advertised notification route
  can independently reconstruct and validate its upstream proof or is
  omitted/rejected.
- Gateway tool discovery never advertises or forwards an unadmitted
  upstream schema or a partially filtered page.
- One legacy upstream does not force unrelated modern upstreams into
  legacy mode.
- A weak upstream does not erase a capability supplied by a different
  eligible upstream.
- Disabled upstream extensions stay hidden.
- Auth identities remain separated.
- Ambiguous collisions fail catalog construction or are omitted with a
  hard diagnostic; they are never silently resolved by arrival order.
- Cross-server disambiguation remains stable when two peers report the
  same `serverInfo.name`, when one changes it, or when a peer spoofs
  another's value.
- Same-origin HTTP endpoints at different paths and separately
  configured identical stdio commands remain different upstream
  instances and cannot alias a route, cache, era decision, cursor, or
  opaque handle.
- Reordering upstream configuration or health changes cannot retarget
  an already selected opaque handle.
- Codec reuse cannot reverse proxy leg direction or turn malformed
  upstream output into a gateway-originated error response.

Tests:

- Modern-modern.
- Multiple modern upstreams.
- Per-route extension intersection and union-catalog behavior.
- Stateless extension-notification proof termination and independent
  upstream reconstruction for both self-contained and negotiated-owner
  descriptors; include wrong endpoint/security/settings/owner/
  generation, stale mapped owner, non-lossless representation,
  downstream-receipt reuse, prior-request reuse, and no-upstream-send
  rejection cases.
- Packaged out-of-tree extension proxy test using only EXT-DEV-01's
  public facade types on both legs, plus malformed output, one-sided
  registration, settings/version mismatch, capability-negative,
  authorization, cancellation, and no-unchecked-passthrough cases.
- OPS-01 fixed-cardinality proxy contributor tests for route outage,
  saturation, recovery, failover, and floods of unique endpoints,
  names, extensions, principals, and handles.
- Upstream tool-page default/explicit/unsupported dialect, invalid
  schema/reference, page-atomic failure, no partial union/cursor/cache/
  forwarding, and sibling-upstream isolation tests.
- Tool/prompt/resource/template/completion collision matrix.
- Equivalent-descriptor explicit grouping and different-schema
  rejection.
- Configured alias grammar/round-trip and deterministic-priority
  tests.
- Duplicate/mutable/spoofed `serverInfo.name` tests proving only the
  trusted `UpstreamInstanceId` affects disambiguation.
- Same scheme/host/port with `/mcp-a` versus `/mcp-b`; default-port and
  canonical-host equivalents; path/query/config-generation changes;
  two duplicate-command stdio entries; argv/cwd/environment-profile
  changes; custom transport missing/duplicate identity; and
  instance-ID substitution tests. Prove the origin remains a separate
  credential/security comparison and can never win a route collision.
- Health change, reorder, and forbidden side-effect fan-out tests.
- Upstream outage.
- Identical malformed-byte/downstream-server-role versus upstream-
  client-role tests with one/multiple in-flight calls, no response-
  back upstream, downstream error-shape correctness, sibling-route
  isolation, and no cross-leg envelope/error forwarding.
- Array-of-one-valid-request and mixed-array negatives on each downstream
  server and upstream client leg, proving their distinct role dispositions,
  zero partial route/catalog/dispatch/correlation/authorization/cache/
  task/session/subscription/proxy/response effects, and sibling isolation.
- Identity separation.

Dependencies:

- SRV-02.
- CLT-02.
- EXT-01.
- FND-04.
- TOOL-01.
- OPS-01.
- EXT-DEV-01.
