ITEM 1 DISCHARGED FROM THE CARD, NOT FROM TMS-033942 — AND THE BEAD'S PREMISE DISSOLVES.
SilentSquirrel, 2026-09-21. With a correction to my own citation first.

*** MY CORRECTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ***
I told WildMountain (msg 25578) that the core-only profile is recorded in "ahet.85.1 comment 24".
IT IS COMMENT 25. I cited a neighbour. The feature set I quoted was right; the pointer was wrong,
and a wrong pointer is how a reader concludes the record does not exist. Verbatim, comment 25:

    "Runtime profile with e2e-fixture,native-tls-roots and no CLI defaults discovered 52 e2e_cli
     IDs; frozen 7 bearer-file IDs all passed (45 other IDs filtered), and the exact feature-off
     diagnostic ID passed (51 other IDs filtered)."

*** ITEM 1 IS DISCHARGED, AND IT NEVER NEEDED A RUN ***
The criterion's own text: "...DETERMINED AND RECORDED, feature set verbatim, FROM A RUN RECEIPT OR
THE DISPATCHED CARD -- not inferred from the scope prose." The disjunction is in the criterion.
Comment 25 is the card, it states the feature set verbatim, and it is not scope prose.

    PROFILE: e2e-fixture, native-tls-roots, and NO CLI defaults.
             (i.e. --no-default-features --features e2e-fixture,native-tls-roots)

The internal arithmetic closes on itself, which is what makes it a record and not an assertion:
    7 bearer-file IDs  + 45 filtered  = 52
    1 feature-off ID   + 51 filtered  = 52
Two independent partitions of the same discovery, agreeing. All EIGHT declared IDs were discovered
AND PASSED.

*** THEREFORE ITEM 2'S ANTECEDENT IS FALSE, AND THE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD DISSOLVES ***
Item 2 reads "IF TASKS IS ENABLED IN THAT RUN: state whether ... appeared in THAT RUN's --list
output." "That run" is item 1's referent: ahet.85.1's core-only E2E scope run. tasks is NOT in that
feature set and CLI defaults are off. The antecedent is false, so item 2 imposes no obligation.

And the worry behind it is answered directly rather than vacuously: the card says the feature-off
diagnostic ID PASSED in that run. A test gated cfg(not(feature = "tasks")) cannot pass in a run
with tasks enabled, so its passing IS the proof that tasks was off.

SO THERE IS NO CONTRADICTION IN THE SCOPE. All eight named IDs exist and passed under one coherent
profile. The scope sentence is not WRONG, it is UNDER-SPECIFIED: it names the IDs without naming
the feature set that makes them exist. That is exactly and only item 3.

*** TMS-033942 CROSS-CHECKS THE CARD EXACTLY: 48 + 4 = 52 ***
This is the strongest thing in the receipt and it was not the thing it was dispatched to show.
Both of WildMountain's arms listed 48 under profiles lacking e2e-fixture and native-tls-roots.
mod authenticated_http (e2e_cli.rs:1983) is gated all(unix, e2e-fixture, native-tls-roots) and holds
exactly four of the seven bearer-file IDs. The card's profile supplies both features:

    48  (WildMountain, fresh, no e2e-fixture/native-tls-roots, HEAD ef9e3fcd)
   + 4  (mod authenticated_http, lit by the card's profile)
   = 52 (MistyForest, historical, e2e-fixture+native-tls-roots, overlay 1591db3d)

A fresh receipt and a historical card, taken on different revisions by different agents through
different routes, agreeing to the unit. Neither was derived from the other.

*** THE SWAP IS REAL, BUT THE INFERENCE FROM "48 = 48" IS PROFILE-CONDITIONAL ***
Verified verbatim, and WildMountain is right about the pair:
    :1933  #[cfg(not(feature = "tasks"))]  cli_02_feature_off_is_actionable_and_absent_from_help
    :1945  #[cfg(feature = "tasks")]       cli_02_a_planted_negative

the third one matters:
    :1814  #[cfg(feature = "tasks")]  -- an inner BLOCK inside a test body, not a test. No effect.
    :2367  #[cfg(all(unix, feature = "tasks", feature = "e2e-fixture"))]  mod task_commands

the feature. The conclusion about what tasks does was drawn from a run under a profile that hides
most of what tasks does -- which is this bead's own defect, reproduced inside the run dispatched to

One field, and it is the only thing standing between this bead and items 1/2/5 all being settled.

title: fastmcp-server --all-features --lib: 806 never-executed rows, and 10 fail on two independent hosts at one revision (9 of them proxy)
description:

executed by anything. Running it lights 806 additional rows, and ten of them
fail on TWO INDEPENDENT HOSTS at the same revision. Nine of those ten are
proxy. This is zero-prior-coverage territory, not a regression.

WHY THIS SURFACE WAS DARK. `-p fastmcp-server --lib` at default features
discovers 2365 rows. Under `--all-features` it discovers 3171: +806 rows, a
34% larger surface. Nothing in the tracker or in any receipt I can find had
ever run them. The gated regions live in four features, by cfg-region count in
crates/fastmcp-server/src:

      proxy                    110
      apps                      50
      oauth-client-credentials  34
      websocket-experimental     0
      enterprise-auth            0
      jwt-resource-auth          0
      native-tls-roots           0
The last four have no gated regions in this crate at all; they are forwarding
names, which an independent inert-feature sweep the same day confirmed.

THE TWO RUNS, identical in everything but host.

  features   in scope: --all-features
  threads    1
  revision   8a3234c5ca83 on BOTH
  counts     3171 discovered / 3171 executed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered on both,
             6342 json events for 3171 rows on both, so both parses are
             complete and the denominators are identical.

  worker vmi1152480 (root@109.205.181.92)   3160 passed / 11 FAILED
  worker hz3        (ubuntu@194.140.197.98)  3152 passed / 19 FAILED

TEN NAMES FAIL ON BOTH HOSTS. These are the host-independent core and the
substance of this bead:

    public_proxy_completion_forwards_exact_legacy_and_final_results

  proxy::tests::
    proxy_resource_prompt_caller_runtime_positive
    proxy_resource_prompt_caller_runtime_planted_negative
    proxy_resource_prompt_mcp_deadline_positive
    proxy_resource_prompt_mcp_deadline_planted_negative
  lib_unit_tests::
    live_websocket_auto_accepts_fresh_eras_and_fences_cross_era_traffic

Nine of the ten are proxy. The tenth is WebSocket era fencing.

THE HOST-SPECIFIC REMAINDER, recorded so nobody mistakes it for part of the
core. Set difference at the same revision:

  only vmi1152480 (1)
    providers::filesystem::tests::test_handler_read_listing_and_read_with_uri
  only hz3 (9)
    async_stdio::tests::async_stdio_server_refuses_raw_parameters_beyond_the_document_bound
    async_stdio::tests::async_stdio_server_retains_exact_parameter_bytes_within_shared_admission_bound
    async_stdio::tests::hosted_tasks::async_stdio_tasks_without_supervisor_refuse_creation_without_store_mutation
    lib_unit_tests::forced_subscription_ack_order_under_recv_lock_is_written_when_recv_returns
    lib_unit_tests::legacy_application_content_roundtrips_and_strict_mode_rejects_extensions
    lib_unit_tests::public_stdio_cancellation_fence_drops_interleaved_progress_before_commit
    proxy::tests::proxy_resource_hooks_caller_runtime_positive
    proxy::tests::proxy_resource_hooks_caller_runtime_planted_negative

Note the third proxy cluster, proxy_resource_hooks_caller_runtime_*, appears
ONLY on hz3. It is the same shape as the prompt cluster that fails on both, so
it may belong to the core and simply have not fired on vmi; that is a
hypothesis, not a finding, and it needs repeats on both hosts.

A STRUCTURAL READING THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE FIRST HOUR OF WORK. Two of the core
failures are complete RH-5 PAIRS failing in BOTH halves:
    proxy_resource_prompt_caller_runtime_positive AND _planted_negative
    proxy_resource_prompt_mcp_deadline_positive   AND _planted_negative
A positive and its near-identical planted negative differ in exactly one
dimension by construction, so a change in the behaviour under test flips one
and holds the other. When BOTH fail, the usual cause is something they SHARE: a
fixture, a feature-gated import, a setup path. On that reading those four rows
are probably TWO causes, not four, and the same may be true of the five builder
rows, which all live in one `proxy_registration_tests` module. Read the shared
setup before reading the assertions. I have not read any of them.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY, and these matter.
  - I have NOT read any failing test or captured any failure message. This bead
    reports names, counts, hosts and a denominator. Whoever takes it should
    start by capturing the actual diagnostics, which no receipt of mine has.
  - NOT a regression claim. There is no earlier green for this surface to
    regress from, because nothing had ever run it. Calling it a regression
    would require a prior reading that does not exist.
  - NOT claiming the ten are ten distinct defects. See the pair reading above.
  - NOT claiming the nine hz3-only rows are sound. On the same day I measured

    fails on one host is unproven either way until it is repeated on both.
  - One run per host, no repeats. The ten-name intersection is the strongest
    thing here precisely because it survived a host change; it has NOT survived
    a repeat on either host.

FIRST STEPS I WOULD TAKE, for whoever claims this: re-run the same scope twice
more per host to see whether the ten-name core is stable (it should be, if it
is real), capture the failure messages for the five builder rows and the two
prompt pairs, and read the shared setup of proxy_registration_tests before any
assertion. Do not widen a bound anywhere in here on the strength of a
single-host reading.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
COMPLETE CAUSAL CHAIN FOR THE FOUR-ROW CLUSTER, and the precise reason a naive
fixture fix would be a vacuous pass. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14.

I previously recorded this cluster as "the fixture serves none of the three
yielding paths" and left it to the owner citing a vacuous-pass risk I did not
spell out. I traced it end to end today. The diagnosis holds, and the risk now
has a specific mechanism rather than a feeling.

ALL FOUR ROWS CARRY THE IDENTICAL ERROR, confirmed from the full-target run at
HEAD 5a634642 (3175 executed, 9 failed; these four among them):

  -32600 "Proxy backend has no asynchronous request implementation; implement
          ProxyBackend::prepare_async_request or use an explicitly synchronous
          API"

  builder_proxy_dual_era_preserves_final_catalog_and_routes_bound_calls   :6560
  public_builder_proxy_relays_modern_tasks_input_required_and_listener    :6422
  public_proxy_completion_forwards_exact_legacy_and_final_results         :6741
  public_proxy_completion_replace_installs_upstream_mapping_for_replaced_target :7084

THE CHAIN, with line numbers in crates/fastmcp-server/src/proxy.rs.

  1. The server routes completion through complete_typed_async (:10042). That
     function serializes the CompletionParams, then tries exactly two things:
     try_final_mrtr_request (the async pair) and
     request_legacy_yielding_with_context (legacy yielding). If neither
     yields it returns proxy_async_backend_unavailable() (:8211). IT NEVER
     CALLS complete_result, complete_result_with_context, OR
     complete_result_with_context_and_final_progress.

  2. That is deliberate and documented. The ProxyBackend trait doc on
     prepare_async_request (:1214) states: "The explicitly synchronous methods
     remain usable independently; async client entry points never invoke them
     as a fallback."

  3. CompletionProxyBackend (builder.rs:5431) implements supports_completion
     and complete_result -- the SYNCHRONOUS surface -- and overrides neither
     async_protocol_era nor prepare_async_request. The sync/async delegation
     chain is intact in the other direction (complete_result_with_context at
     :1361 does delegate down to complete_result), so the fixture's override is
     reachable from the sync surface; the async surface simply never reaches it.

  So the fixture is wired to the wrong surface. This is a FIXTURE defect, not a
  product hole, and that is consistent with the earlier retraction confirming
  the production side complete.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THE OBVIOUS FIX WRONG. try_custom_async_request
(:11342) refuses a mismatched era outright:

    if bound_era.is_some_and(|bound| bound != era) {
        return Err(.. "Proxy async backend era contradicts the selected route")
    }

so async_protocol_era() must equal the era the route binds -- which is why I
originally wrote "one path MATCHING THE ERA bound_proxy_client binds". The
template to copy is TypedToolBackend/OwnedTypedResult (proxy.rs:19194-19240),
which returns Some(self.result.era()) and boxes an owned request.

AND HERE IS THE VACUOUS-PASS MECHANISM, which is the part I could not previously
name. These tests do not merely assert that a completion succeeds. They assert
rich properties OF THE PARAMS THE PRODUCT BUILT, from the call log:

    legacy_calls[0].reference matches CompletionReference::Prompt{name:"legacy-deploy"}
    legacy_calls[0].context.is_none()
    final_calls[0].reference matches CompletionReference::PromptWithTitle{name,title}
    final_calls[0].context.arguments["region"] == "us-east-1"

The sync hook receives a ready-made fastmcp_client::CompletionParams, so
logging it is faithful by construction. The async hook does NOT. Its execute
receives a fastmcp_protocol::CoreRequest, built at :11406 by
CoreRequest::decode(era, method, Some(&parameters)) -- a DIFFERENT type, across
the client/protocol boundary, and for the modern era the parameters have had a
_meta object inserted (:11395) that was never part of the caller's
CompletionParams.

So a fixture implementing prepare_async_request must reconstruct
CompletionParams from a typed CoreRequest. Any such reconstruction is fixture
code deciding what the reference variant, the title and the context are -- and
those are precisely the four things the assertions check. The test would then
be asserting against values the FIXTURE computed rather than values the PRODUCT
forwarded, which is the exact inversion that makes a green meaningless. Getting
it subtly wrong turns four honest reds into four dishonest greens, and nothing
in the suite would catch it.

WHAT A CORRECT REMEDY HAS TO ESTABLISH, as acceptance for whoever takes it:
  - the logged params must demonstrably originate from the product's own
    serialization, not from fixture-side reconstruction. The cleanest form is
    for the product to hand the async completion path the same
    CompletionParams the sync hook receives -- i.e. an async completion hook
    analogous to complete_result_with_context -- rather than for every test
    backend to re-derive them from a CoreRequest;
  - a planted negative differing only in the forwarded field: change the
    upstream's reference title or context argument and the test must fail. If
    it still passes, the assertions are reading fixture state (RH-5);
  - era agreement with the bound route, since a mismatch is refused before any
    user code runs.

WHY I AM STOPPING HERE RATHER THAN IMPLEMENTING. The first bullet is a design
question about the async proxy surface, not a test edit: the async path
currently has no completion hook carrying CompletionParams, and adding one is
a product decision with an owner who is not me. Implementing the fixture-side
reconstruction instead is the cheap path, it would turn all four rows green
today, and it is the move most likely to be wrong in a way that looks right --
which is the specific failure this repository's rules exist to prevent. I have
already retracted one p1 this session for reasoning past evidence I had not
read; I am not going to manufacture four greens on the same day.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE MY EARLIER NOTE: nothing about the disposition, everything
about its justification. "Left to the owner because of vacuous-pass risk" is now
a named chain with line numbers, a named constraint (era agreement), a named
mechanism (cross-type param reconstruction across a _meta-mutated payload), and
a named acceptance test (the planted negative on a forwarded field).

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
REFINEMENT TO MY OWN REMEDY SPEC, same day. The first acceptance bullet above implies a PRODUCT change, and on reflection that framing is wrong and a safer remedy exists.

Why the product is probably right as it stands: the async path exists for backends that talk to a real upstream over a wire. For those, serializing CompletionParams to JSON and sending it is exactly correct -- there is no use for a typed in-process hook, because the params leave the process. Adding an async completion hook carrying a typed fastmcp_client::CompletionParams would be adding product surface whose only consumer is test fixtures, which is the shape the creation gate exists to refuse.

So this is a TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE gap, not a product gap: there is no shared helper that gives an in-process async test backend the typed params the product built.

BETTER REMEDY, and it inverts the risk rather than accepting it. Write ONE shared test-side adapter that implements ProxyAsyncRequest, decodes CompletionParams from the CoreRequest exactly once, and logs it. Every fixture that needs an async completion path uses that adapter instead of hand-rolling its own reconstruction.

That changes the safety argument completely:
  - N fixture-side reconstructions means N chances to silently assert against fixture-computed values. One shared decode means ONE place to get right and one place to review.
  - The shared decode can carry its OWN planted negative, validated once: feed it a CoreRequest whose reference title or context argument differs and assert the decoded params differ accordingly. That proves the adapter reads the product's payload rather than inventing one, and every fixture then inherits that proof instead of needing its own.
  - The _meta the modern path inserts at proxy.rs:11395 is handled once, in the open, with a comment saying why it is dropped or retained -- rather than being silently ignored in four places.

This is still not a change I am making. It is still a decision for this bead's owner, and it still requires the era-agreement constraint (async_protocol_era must equal the bound era or try_custom_async_request refuses before any user code runs). But it is a materially better starting point than what I wrote above, and it needs no product surface at all.

Recording the correction rather than editing the earlier comment, because the earlier framing -- 'the product should grow a hook' -- is the kind of suggestion that gets acted on, and I no longer think it is right.

comments.text:
## THE ANSWER IS ALREADY IN THE TYPE: ResultMeta::empty(). TAKE (b). DO NOT DERIVE Default.

MagentaSummit. **I claimed this bead and then found ProudValley holds an exclusive
reservation on the file — they are on it and I am not editing.** Analysis posted so
they do not re-derive it, and so the one-line option is not taken by default.

### ResultMeta already has a public, const, documented constructor for exactly this

    crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/result.rs

        /// Creates empty metadata for a locally authored result.
        ///
        /// This preserves the absence of the optional `_meta` member on the wire.
        #[must_use]
        pub const fn empty() -> Self {
            Self { server_info: None, meta: None, exact_meta: None }
        }

The failing call site wants exactly "empty metadata" and spells it
`Default::default()`. **`ResultMeta::empty()` is that value, with the wire
semantics documented at the definition.**

### AND IT IS THE HOUSE PATTERN — the broken site is the only outlier

    ResultMeta call sites using Default::default()  : 1   <- the failure
    call sites using ::empty() or ::server_generated : 8+  measured across the workspace
        trybuild_tests.rs:1959, :1989, :2008, :2225
        trybuild/prompt_typed_return.rs:13
        e2e_workflow.rs:2105, :2213
        macro_expansion.rs:2208

**Every other construction in the tree names what it means.** The fix is one token:
`Default::default()` -> `ResultMeta::empty()`.

### WHY (a) IS WRONG, not merely heavier

The orchestrator's framing is right — "a Default on a result-metadata type asserts
that an empty ResultMeta is meaningful, and that is a semantic claim". Three
reasons it should be refused:

1. **The claim is already made, better, by a NAMED constructor.** `empty()` carries
   a doc comment stating the wire consequence. `Default` carries none, so a reader
   at the call site learns nothing.
2. **It creates a second spelling of one value** on a public protocol type, and the
   two cannot be told apart at the call site. Eight existing sites use the named
   form; a ninth using `Default` would be the only one whose intent is invisible.
3. **It silently overrules a design decision that is documented in place.** The
   authors wrote `empty()` rather than deriving `Default`; adding the derive now
   reverses that without argument, and widens a PUBLIC PROTOCOL SURFACE to do it.

**The one-line fix is the one that changes the protocol. The correct fix is also
one token and changes nothing public.**

### Same shape as two other findings today

`Sleep::with_timer_driver` — 26 sites used `Sleep::new` + ambient, 3 outliers
reached for a `pub(crate)` item. `ordinary_b_r3_live_matrix` — the correct
structure was in its sibling 200 lines away. **When a fix appears to need a new
capability, check whether the neighbours already have the idiom.** Third instance
in one day.

### Claim

I hold this bead only because I claimed it before discovering the reservation.
**ProudValley should keep it** — they reserved the file first and the refusal is the
coordination working. Reassign to them; I will not touch the file.

description:

        |                                                                --------------- mutable borrow
    284 | assert!(credential.has_refresh_token());          <- immutable borrow
    285 | assert!(!credential.bearer_credential().is_revoked());
    286 | }   <- mutable borrow might be used here, when `pinned` is dropped and runs the destructor

stays live until end of block at :286. The assertions at :284-285 then cannot take an immutable

title: SRV-MW-01 implementation A: middleware traits/context propagation
description:
Section 36.4.1 A leaf: disjoint real-production middleware traits and context propagation with same-Bead positive and planted-negative tests.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:SRV-MW-01:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for SRV-MW-01.

Owned capability slice: middleware traits/context propagation.
Named shipped consumer: public middleware API.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### SRV-MW-01 — Rebuild middleware around modern packages

Outcome:

Make middleware composition preserve modern envelopes, security
partitions, notification streams, cache hints, and extension results.

Reason:

The current request/response middleware abstraction predates required
result discriminators, per-request metadata, MRTR, and request-owned
streams.

Implementation:

- Define a typed `RequestPackage` containing validated method,
  parameters, sanitized context, frozen extension registry, limit
  snapshot, and authorized catalog view.
- Define a typed `ResponsePackage` containing a complete,
  input-required, or negotiated extension result plus its
  request-owned notification channel.
- Make middleware incapable of reading raw transport credentials.
- Preserve result discriminators and any present result metadata
  through every layer, and preserve metadata required by the selected
  result type.
- Preserve PRT-04 `UnknownResultMembers` and exact nested numeric
  representations through every no-op, cache, short-circuit,
  validation, and serialization layer. Middleware may observe them as
  inert bounded peer/custom data but cannot reinterpret them as
  routing, authorization, cache/pagination, MRTR, Task, or extension
  authority; a declared response transform that replaces one must use
  the explicit bounded custom-result API and pass phase-8 collision
  and result validation.
- Require a middleware to declare whether it can observe, transform,
  cache, retry, or short-circuit each method class.
- Forbid generic retries of handler-reaching requests.
- Keep transport admission, raw-header validation, authentication,
  operation authorization, authorized catalog resolution, recognized
  parameter-header validation, and capability/extension validation
  outside application middleware and ahead of middleware entry.
- Give post-validation authorization policy, rate limit, cache,
  transform, observability, and handler layers one explicit order.
- If a deployment needs a pre-auth connection limiter, expose it as a
  transport admission control with no access to parsed private
  catalogs, not as ordinary request middleware.
- Publish this fixed phase table in server crate documentation and
  encode the phase in sealed internal types:

| Order | Phase | User-extensible | May short-circuit |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | transport admission, era parse, auth, authz, routing/header/capability/schema guards | no; configured providers only | typed transport/auth/protocol error |
| 2 | authenticated tenant rate/admission policy | policy implementation | rate-limit result only |
| 3 | typed request policy/observation | yes, `Cx`-aware | declared uncacheable typed result/error |
| 4 | safe canonical-result cache lookup | cache provider | canonical complete cache hit only |
| 5 | handler | registered handler | typed outcome/error |
| 6 | canonical result/schema/extension validation and generation-checked cache commit | no plus cache provider | validation error; no replacement result |
| 7 | exactly-once typed response transforms | yes, `Cx`-aware | no retry or second dispatch |
| 8 | final result/metadata/schema/extension revalidation and observation | no plus observers | validation error |
| 9 | transport serialization and stream ownership | no | transport outcome only |

- Make request middleware read-only with respect to the validated
  method, parameters, auth decision, routing fields, and capability
  set.
  A component that needs different parameters must construct a new
  explicit client request, not mutate the authenticated inbound
  package.
- Permit response transforms to change only declared typed payload
  fields and require phase-8 revalidation afterward.
- Define the cache value as the canonical, validated phase-6 result
  before any response transform. A hit resumes at phase 7, so every
  response transform runs exactly once on both hit and miss and
  per-request transform behavior is never frozen into a shared value.
- Require any request-side policy/provider configuration that can
  change cache eligibility or the canonical handler result to declare
  its complete result-affecting key projection plus revision before
  lookup, or mark that request uncacheable. A typed short circuit from
  phases 2 or 3 is uncacheable unless a separately sealed canonical
  cache contract proves its complete key and generation.
- Require every asynchronous middleware/provider hook to accept
  `&Cx` or `&McpContext`, honor cancellation, and own no detached work.

title: SUB-01 implementation A: subscription protocol/handle model
description:
Section 36.4.1 SUB-01 A slice. Implement the subscription protocol/handle model with same-Bead positive and one-variable planted-negative tests. Retains the parent external prerequisites; emits the public subscription-API contribution.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:SUB-01:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for SUB-01.

Owned capability slice: subscription protocol/handle model.
Named shipped consumer: public subscription API.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### SUB-01 — Implement subscription protocol and registry

Outcome:

Provide filtered, correlated, multi-subscription event delivery.

Reason:

`subscriptions/listen` replaces both the HTTP GET stream and resource
subscribe/unsubscribe.

Implementation:

- Add final listen request, filters, acknowledgement, and result types.
- Support exact filter members `toolsListChanged`,
  `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged`, and
  `resourceSubscriptions`, mapped respectively to
  `notifications/tools/list_changed`,
  `notifications/prompts/list_changed`,
  `notifications/resources/list_changed`, and
  `notifications/resources/updated`.
- Preserve the final all-optional filter semantics: an absent member,
  explicit `false`, and an empty resource array all mean “not
  subscribed” for that member, and an entirely empty `notifications`
  object is a valid idle subscription. A safe implementation may
  advise against it, but must acknowledge an empty supported subset
  and keep/cancel the bounded stream normally rather than inventing an
  Invalid Params error or silently broadening the filter.
- Decode every `resourceSubscriptions` entry through PRT-02's
  byte-preserving `AbsoluteUri`, despite the generated filter schema's
  missing `format` annotation, and jointly enforce per-URI, identifier-
  count, aggregate URI/encoded-byte, and enclosing message bounds
  before registry insertion.
- Resolve each accepted resource URI at registration time to one
  provider-owned, revisioned `ResourceSubscriptionMatcher` under the
  caller's authorization. The matcher defines exact identity plus any
  explicit provider-semantic sub-resource relation allowed by the
  final notification note. It is not raw-string prefixing, generic URI
  resolution/normalization, RFC 6570 template guessing, path
  containment inference, or cross-provider equivalence.
- Require the first event to be acknowledgement.
- Use the listen request ID as subscription ID.
- Define ack-first ordering per subscription ID, not globally on the
  shared stdio channel.
- In `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`, return only the
  supported subset of the requested notification filters.
- On the client, compare the acknowledgement semantically with the
  exact requested filter before admitting the subscription. Missing
  requested categories or resource URIs are a valid partial
  acknowledgement: expose the accepted subset and the unsupported
  remainder to the caller, and deliver only the accepted subset. An
  acknowledgement that widens a boolean category, adds an unrequested
  resource URI, or otherwise is not a semantic subset is a peer
  protocol violation; terminate/cancel that one listen operation
  without admitting any event under the widened filter. An explicit
  `false` acknowledgement member is semantically the same as omission,
  while its wire presence remains available to lossless diagnostics.
- Tag every subscription event with exactly one accepted
  subscription ID.
- Tag every server-sent notification belonging to a subscription—
  acknowledgement, accepted data event, and server-initiated
  `notifications/cancelled` control—with
  `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"]` exactly equal to
  the originating listen request ID. Client-initiated cancellation is
  an ordinary request-ID cancellation signal and does not acquire
  subscription metadata merely because the target is a listen.
- Bind each registry entry and ID to `SubscriptionPartitionKey`,
  accepted filter, AUTH-00's purpose-typed
  `SubscriptionAuthorizationGuard`, and its owning connection/request
  lifetime. Use `Authenticated(AuthorizationLease)` whenever any
  accepted category, resource matcher, or resulting event visibility
  depends on principal/grant/tenant; refuse that authenticated
  subscription when the auth mode cannot issue a lease with the
  promised revocation semantics. Use
  `PublicUnauthenticated(PublicAuthorizationProof)` only after atomic
  registration proves the entire accepted subset and its possible
  event surfaces public and auth-invariant for the captured provider/
  catalog/visibility/policy generations.
- Recheck event visibility and revalidate the applicable guard before
  delivery. For the authenticated branch, enforce lease maximum
  staleness and terminate on token expiry, revocation, lost scope,
  provider outage beyond the bound, or policy revision. For the public
  branch, reprove public/auth-invariant visibility and terminate on
  provider/catalog/matcher/public-policy/configuration generation
  drift, private/auth-varying reclassification, or an indeterminate
  result. Never upgrade an existing public subscription in place or
  use its anonymous quota bucket as event authority.
- For `notifications/resources/updated`, accept the emitted URI only
  from the same registered provider/matcher revision and require either
  exact subscribed identity or the matcher's explicit sub-resource
  relation. Reauthorize both the subscribed parent and emitted child
  immediately before enqueue/delivery; visibility loss for either
  suppresses the event and follows the configured revoke/terminate
  policy. Never let possession of a parent URI disclose an otherwise
  hidden child.
- Allow multiple concurrent subscriptions.
- Deliver only requested event categories.
- Add bounded per-subscription queues.
- Define slow-consumer overflow behavior.
- Implement Section 5.2's pinned teardown decision. A FastMCP server
  emits cancellation-only for its own teardown. A FastMCP client
  tolerates cancellation-only, empty-complete-only, and
  cancellation-then-complete peers with one atomic first-terminal
  winner; if a peer complete result is accepted, its result metadata
  must carry the same subscription ID as the stream it completes.
- Define reconnect behavior.
- Apply CLT-01's bounded subscription idle and absolute lifetimes.
  Only the valid acknowledgement or a valid delivered event in the
  accepted filter resets idle time; on HTTP, HTTP-03's syntactically
  valid bounded SSE comment may also reset idle as a transport
  keepalive but never becomes a subscription event. Rejected
  categories, unrelated request notifications, and arbitrary raw
  traffic do not reset it. Expiry cancels through the active transport
  and an optional reconnect is a fresh listen request/ID under
  explicit backoff, original policy, and cumulative reconnect bounds;
  it never resets an absolute lifetime silently.
- Exclude progress and request-scoped logs.
- Let extensions register subscription event variants.
- Contribute bounded active/capacity, enqueue/delivery/drop, slow-
  consumer, reconnect, expiry, authorization-loss, and cancellation
  observations to OPS-01 without subscription IDs, filters, resource
  URIs, principals, or extension identifiers as dimensions.

Acceptance:

- No event precedes acknowledgement.
- Every event carries the correct ID.
- Every server-sent acknowledgement/event/cancellation notification
  carries the exact listen ID in subscription metadata; the
  client-sent cancellation shape remains distinct.
- Filters are enforced.
- Resource updates are delivered only for an authorized exact match or
  provider-declared sub-resource relation; lexical similarity grants
  nothing.
- One slow subscription does not block unrelated requests.
- Closing one subscription does not close another.
- Task notifications require negotiated Tasks support.
- An unacknowledged subscription ID receives no event, and an
  unaccepted filter category receives no event on that subscription.
- A client exposes a valid partial acknowledgement instead of silently
  assuming the requested filter, and a widened acknowledgement cannot
  create delivery authority.
- Exactly one terminal outcome is observable. A peer's accepted empty
  complete result is last and correlated to exactly one subscription
  ID; a cancellation-first path ignores any later result.
- Idle or absolute expiry terminates one subscription without keeping
  it alive through unrelated traffic or affecting another handle.
- Auth-disabled HTTP and stdio can sustain proven-public
  subscriptions, while anonymous private/auth-varying subscriptions
  cannot be registered or delivered.

Tests:

- Ack-first property.
- Filter matrix.
- Empty-filter, all-false, empty-resource-array, and omitted-member
  acceptance with an empty acknowledgment and zero delivered
  categories.
- Resource-subscription URI syntax, unknown-scheme preservation,
  per-URI/count/aggregate/enclosing-body N-1/N/N+1, and no-partial-
  registry-insert tests.
- Resource matcher tests for exact identity, legitimate provider-
  declared child, sibling, deceptive lexical prefix, dot-segment/
  percent-encoded/case/default-port aliases, template-looking URI,
  cross-provider/cross-server relation, matcher-revision drift,
  parent/child authorization loss, hidden-child non-disclosure, and
  child visibility changing between enqueue and delivery.
- Virtual-time idle/absolute acknowledgement/event-reset matrix,
  bounded HTTP-comment reset versus malformed/comment-flood
  non-extension, unrelated/rejected/request-notification non-reset,
  explicit fresh-ID reconnect, cumulative reconnect bound, and two-
  handle isolation.
- Multiple concurrent listeners.
- Auth-disabled HTTP and stdio public-listen/event positives;
  authenticated lease positives; anonymous private/mixed/auth-varying
  filter negatives; public-policy/catalog/provider/matcher revision
  teardown; and no public-to-authenticated in-place upgrade.
- Overflow policy.
- Local cancellation-only teardown plus peer cancellation-only,
  empty-complete-only, and cancellation-then-complete interop.
- Extension event registration.
- Cross-subscription isolation.
- Partial filter acknowledgement, unsupported-remainder reporting,
  explicit-false/omission equivalence, widened-boolean, unrequested-
  resource, and no-event-before-client-admission tests.
- Peer final-result discriminator/subscription-ID metadata and
  first-terminal-winner/late-second-signal tests.
- Exact client-cancel versus server-cancel wire goldens, proving only
  the server-sent subscription control carries subscription metadata
  and that its metadata value equals `params.requestId`.
- Numeric listen-ID alias (`1`/`1.0`/`1e0`, signed zero, beyond
  `2^53`) acknowledgement/event/final/cancellation correlation and
  duplicate-active rejection through PRT-01's canonical key.
- Cross-tenant key swap, token expiry/revocation, and policy-revision
  teardown tests.
- Opaque-token introspection, JWT expiry, provider outage on both sides
  of the staleness boundary, cancellation, and lease-drop cleanup.
- OPS-01 capacity/readiness, slow-consumer/drop/reconnect/expiry/recovery,
  and unique-ID/filter/URI/principal/extension cardinality tests.

Dependencies:

- PRT-04.
- SRV-01.
- CLT-01.
- AUTH-00.
- EXT-01.
- LIMIT-01.
- OPS-01.

description:
Section 36.4.1 SUB-01 integration slice. Wire only the named shipped public subscription API from its A and B slices. It has no external prerequisites beyond A and B.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:SUB-01:I:BEGIN -->
Canonical I role for SUB-01.

Owned capability slice: public subscription API.
Named shipped consumer: public subscription API.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### SUB-01 — Implement subscription protocol and registry

Outcome:

Provide filtered, correlated, multi-subscription event delivery.

Reason:

`subscriptions/listen` replaces both the HTTP GET stream and resource
subscribe/unsubscribe.

Implementation:

- Add final listen request, filters, acknowledgement, and result types.
- Support exact filter members `toolsListChanged`,
  `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged`, and
  `resourceSubscriptions`, mapped respectively to
  `notifications/tools/list_changed`,
  `notifications/prompts/list_changed`,
  `notifications/resources/list_changed`, and
  `notifications/resources/updated`.
- Preserve the final all-optional filter semantics: an absent member,
  explicit `false`, and an empty resource array all mean “not
  subscribed” for that member, and an entirely empty `notifications`
  object is a valid idle subscription. A safe implementation may
  advise against it, but must acknowledge an empty supported subset
  and keep/cancel the bounded stream normally rather than inventing an
  Invalid Params error or silently broadening the filter.
- Decode every `resourceSubscriptions` entry through PRT-02's
  byte-preserving `AbsoluteUri`, despite the generated filter schema's
  missing `format` annotation, and jointly enforce per-URI, identifier-
  count, aggregate URI/encoded-byte, and enclosing message bounds
  before registry insertion.
- Resolve each accepted resource URI at registration time to one
  provider-owned, revisioned `ResourceSubscriptionMatcher` under the
  caller's authorization. The matcher defines exact identity plus any
  explicit provider-semantic sub-resource relation allowed by the
  final notification note. It is not raw-string prefixing, generic URI
  resolution/normalization, RFC 6570 template guessing, path
  containment inference, or cross-provider equivalence.
- Require the first event to be acknowledgement.
- Use the listen request ID as subscription ID.
- Define ack-first ordering per subscription ID, not globally on the
  shared stdio channel.
- In `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`, return only the
  supported subset of the requested notification filters.
- On the client, compare the acknowledgement semantically with the
  exact requested filter before admitting the subscription. Missing
  requested categories or resource URIs are a valid partial
  acknowledgement: expose the accepted subset and the unsupported
  remainder to the caller, and deliver only the accepted subset. An
  acknowledgement that widens a boolean category, adds an unrequested
  resource URI, or otherwise is not a semantic subset is a peer
  protocol violation; terminate/cancel that one listen operation
  without admitting any event under the widened filter. An explicit
  `false` acknowledgement member is semantically the same as omission,
  while its wire presence remains available to lossless diagnostics.
- Tag every subscription event with exactly one accepted
  subscription ID.
- Tag every server-sent notification belonging to a subscription—
  acknowledgement, accepted data event, and server-initiated
  `notifications/cancelled` control—with
  `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"]` exactly equal to
  the originating listen request ID. Client-initiated cancellation is
  an ordinary request-ID cancellation signal and does not acquire
  subscription metadata merely because the target is a listen.
- Bind each registry entry and ID to `SubscriptionPartitionKey`,
  accepted filter, AUTH-00's purpose-typed
  `SubscriptionAuthorizationGuard`, and its owning connection/request
  lifetime. Use `Authenticated(AuthorizationLease)` whenever any
  accepted category, resource matcher, or resulting event visibility
  depends on principal/grant/tenant; refuse that authenticated
  subscription when the auth mode cannot issue a lease with the
  promised revocation semantics. Use
  `PublicUnauthenticated(PublicAuthorizationProof)` only after atomic
  registration proves the entire accepted subset and its possible
  event surfaces public and auth-invariant for the captured provider/
  catalog/visibility/policy generations.
- Recheck event visibility and revalidate the applicable guard before
  delivery. For the authenticated branch, enforce lease maximum
  staleness and terminate on token expiry, revocation, lost scope,
  provider outage beyond the bound, or policy revision. For the public
  branch, reprove public/auth-invariant visibility and terminate on
  provider/catalog/matcher/public-policy/configuration generation
  drift, private/auth-varying reclassification, or an indeterminate
  result. Never upgrade an existing public subscription in place or
  use its anonymous quota bucket as event authority.
- For `notifications/resources/updated`, accept the emitted URI only
  from the same registered provider/matcher revision and require either
  exact subscribed identity or the matcher's explicit sub-resource
  relation. Reauthorize both the subscribed parent and emitted child
  immediately before enqueue/delivery; visibility loss for either
  suppresses the event and follows the configured revoke/terminate
  policy. Never let possession of a parent URI disclose an otherwise
  hidden child.
- Allow multiple concurrent subscriptions.
- Deliver only requested event categories.
- Add bounded per-subscription queues.
- Define slow-consumer overflow behavior.
- Implement Section 5.2's pinned teardown decision. A FastMCP server
  emits cancellation-only for its own teardown. A FastMCP client
  tolerates cancellation-only, empty-complete-only, and
  cancellation-then-complete peers with one atomic first-terminal
  winner; if a peer complete result is accepted, its result metadata
  must carry the same subscription ID as the stream it completes.
- Define reconnect behavior.
- Apply CLT-01's bounded subscription idle and absolute lifetimes.
  Only the valid acknowledgement or a valid delivered event in the
  accepted filter resets idle time; on HTTP, HTTP-03's syntactically
  valid bounded SSE comment may also reset idle as a transport
  keepalive but never becomes a subscription event. Rejected
  categories, unrelated request notifications, and arbitrary raw
  traffic do not reset it. Expiry cancels through the active transport
  and an optional reconnect is a fresh listen request/ID under
  explicit backoff, original policy, and cumulative reconnect bounds;
  it never resets an absolute lifetime silently.
- Exclude progress and request-scoped logs.
- Let extensions register subscription event variants.
- Contribute bounded active/capacity, enqueue/delivery/drop, slow-
  consumer, reconnect, expiry, authorization-loss, and cancellation
  observations to OPS-01 without subscription IDs, filters, resource
  URIs, principals, or extension identifiers as dimensions.

Acceptance:

- No event precedes acknowledgement.
- Every event carries the correct ID.
- Every server-sent acknowledgement/event/cancellation notification
  carries the exact listen ID in subscription metadata; the
  client-sent cancellation shape remains distinct.
- Filters are enforced.
- Resource updates are delivered only for an authorized exact match or
  provider-declared sub-resource relation; lexical similarity grants
  nothing.
- One slow subscription does not block unrelated requests.
- Closing one subscription does not close another.
- Task notifications require negotiated Tasks support.
- An unacknowledged subscription ID receives no event, and an
  unaccepted filter category receives no event on that subscription.
- A client exposes a valid partial acknowledgement instead of silently
  assuming the requested filter, and a widened acknowledgement cannot
  create delivery authority.
- Exactly one terminal outcome is observable. A peer's accepted empty
  complete result is last and correlated to exactly one subscription
  ID; a cancellation-first path ignores any later result.
- Idle or absolute expiry terminates one subscription without keeping
  it alive through unrelated traffic or affecting another handle.
- Auth-disabled HTTP and stdio can sustain proven-public
  subscriptions, while anonymous private/auth-varying subscriptions
  cannot be registered or delivered.

Tests:

- Ack-first property.
- Filter matrix.
- Empty-filter, all-false, empty-resource-array, and omitted-member
  acceptance with an empty acknowledgment and zero delivered
  categories.
- Resource-subscription URI syntax, unknown-scheme preservation,
  per-URI/count/aggregate/enclosing-body N-1/N/N+1, and no-partial-
  registry-insert tests.
- Resource matcher tests for exact identity, legitimate provider-
  declared child, sibling, deceptive lexical prefix, dot-segment/
  percent-encoded/case/default-port aliases, template-looking URI,
  cross-provider/cross-server relation, matcher-revision drift,
  parent/child authorization loss, hidden-child non-disclosure, and
  child visibility changing between enqueue and delivery.
- Virtual-time idle/absolute acknowledgement/event-reset matrix,
  bounded HTTP-comment reset versus malformed/comment-flood
  non-extension, unrelated/rejected/request-notification non-reset,
  explicit fresh-ID reconnect, cumulative reconnect bound, and two-
  handle isolation.
- Multiple concurrent listeners.
- Auth-disabled HTTP and stdio public-listen/event positives;
  authenticated lease positives; anonymous private/mixed/auth-varying
  filter negatives; public-policy/catalog/provider/matcher revision
  teardown; and no public-to-authenticated in-place upgrade.
- Overflow policy.
- Local cancellation-only teardown plus peer cancellation-only,
  empty-complete-only, and cancellation-then-complete interop.
- Extension event registration.
- Cross-subscription isolation.
- Partial filter acknowledgement, unsupported-remainder reporting,
  explicit-false/omission equivalence, widened-boolean, unrequested-
  resource, and no-event-before-client-admission tests.
- Peer final-result discriminator/subscription-ID metadata and
  first-terminal-winner/late-second-signal tests.
- Exact client-cancel versus server-cancel wire goldens, proving only
  the server-sent subscription control carries subscription metadata
  and that its metadata value equals `params.requestId`.
- Numeric listen-ID alias (`1`/`1.0`/`1e0`, signed zero, beyond
  `2^53`) acknowledgement/event/final/cancellation correlation and
  duplicate-active rejection through PRT-01's canonical key.
- Cross-tenant key swap, token expiry/revocation, and policy-revision
  teardown tests.
- Opaque-token introspection, JWT expiry, provider outage on both sides
  of the staleness boundary, cancellation, and lease-drop cleanup.
- OPS-01 capacity/readiness, slow-consumer/drop/reconnect/expiry/recovery,
  and unique-ID/filter/URI/principal/extension cardinality tests.

Dependencies:

- PRT-04.
- SRV-01.
- CLT-01.
- AUTH-00.
- EXT-01.
- LIMIT-01.
- OPS-01.

Modern HTTP has no standalone GET event channel.

- Return an SSE response for listen.

- Do not attach event IDs.
- Do not resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

title: fastmcp-server --lib has a rotating ~2-per-run bounded-test failure population: 13 distinct names across 3 full runs with zero repeats, while count and 440-450s runtime hold steady
description:
Two tests fail in the full serialized fastmcp-server --lib target and PASS when
run alone. Neither was tracked anywhere: a tracker search for both names
returned zero matches, so this is the first record of either.

MEASURED 2026-10-14, both arms at the same revision.

  FULL TARGET, the configuration that matters
    command   cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --lib -- --test-threads 1
    host      hz3, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
    subject   HEAD 5a6346425bf99e4ceafb0bb1fcc626d690f35833, manifest agrees
    counts    2369 discovered / 2369 EXECUTED / 2367 passed / 2 FAILED
              0 ignored / 0 filtered, exec_time 449.86 s
    verdict   INVALID (2 failures)

  SAME TWO IN ISOLATION
    same command plus two --filter arguments, same host, same revision
    counts    2369 discovered / 2 executed / 2 PASSED / 0 failed / 2367 filtered
    verdict   GREEN

So the discriminator is the full-target context, not the tests themselves.

THE TWO ROWS, and both are HARNESS BOUNDS rather than product assertions.

1. async_stdio::tests::native_memory_tests::
   memory_server_routes_cancellation_while_a_handler_is_pending
     panics at crates/fastmcp-server/src/async_stdio.rs:3513
     "native memory serving must make bounded runtime progress:
      Elapsed { deadline: Time(71511548787ns) }"
   The site is a test helper wrapping the body in
   asupersync::time::timeout(cx.now(), Duration::from_secs(8), ..). So an
   8-SECOND bound elapsed. The helper also builds
   RuntimeBuilder::current_thread().blocking_threads(0, 0), a single-threaded
   runtime with NO blocking pool, which makes the row sensitive to any
   scheduling stall rather than only to its own work.

2. lib_unit_tests::live_http_post_admission_canonical_error_is_one_terminal_sse_response
     panics at crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:24423, which is the live-HTTP
     whole-test-bound harness doing result.unwrap(), with
     "post-admission capability acknowledgement read failed:
      Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)"

   THE MESSAGE IS MISLEADING AND I NEARLY MISDIAGNOSED IT. os error 11 is
   EAGAIN, so the string reads as a non-blocking-read bug leaking EWOULDBLOCK
   into an error path -- which in an async runtime would be a real correctness
   defect. It is not that. The read is test-side blocking std::net::TcpStream
   with set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2))), and on Linux an expired
   SO_RCVTIMEO on a blocking socket returns EAGAIN. So this is a 2-SECOND READ
   BOUND ELAPSING, wearing an OS-error costume.

   I have fixed the message only, no bound change: the WouldBlock/TimedOut
   kinds now report the named bound, the byte count received so far and those
   bytes as text, and say explicitly that this is the bound elapsing rather
   than a transport fault; other error kinds keep a plain message plus the byte
   count. The bound value is now bound to a single local so the message cannot
   drift from the value installed on the socket. That separates three states
   the bare string collapsed into one: peer sent nothing, peer sent a partial
   response, genuine transport error.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT.
  - NOT a deterministic product defect. Two for two green in isolation.
  - NOT cleared by that isolation green either. A row that passes alone and
    fails in the full target is a real failure of the full target, which is the
    configuration every batch verification and every AC that says "full --lib
    green" actually runs. Isolation tells you where the cause is NOT.
  - The common shape is two short harness bounds, 8 s and 2 s, evaluated 450
    seconds into a 2369-test serialized run on a shared worker that reported
    95 percent disk use. That is the profile of a bound calibrated on a quiet
    host rather than of a hang.

WHY NOT JUST WIDEN THE BOUNDS. That is the obvious remedy and it is RH-1:
relaxing a bound on a failing assertion makes the row green without
establishing anything about why it was missed. Someone has to decide whether
these bounds are wrong or whether the suite has acquired a real slowdown, and
that decision needs a cause, not a greener number. Specifically unresolved:
whether the 450-second serialized runtime is itself a regression. Nobody has a
baseline for that figure, which is part of why this bead exists.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP, cheapest first: repeat the FULL target two or three more
times on a quiet host and record whether the same two names fail, different
names fail, or none do. If the names rotate, the finding is suite runtime and
bound calibration. If these same two recur, they earn individual investigation.
I ran the full target once; one observation cannot distinguish those.

CONSEQUENCE FOR bd-x3273. Its AC3 requires a full fastmcp-server --lib green in
two profiles, and it has been in_progress since 2026-09-26 waiting for that.
These two rows block the default-profile arm at a current revision, and they are
NOT the bd-m037p rows that blocked it historically, nor the
live_http_legacy_reverse_response_* quiescence family that WildMountain
observed. So AC3 is blocked on a third, previously unrecorded cause. Reported
there.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY.
  - ONE full-target observation and ONE isolation observation. Not a
    determinism claim in either direction.
  - ONE host. Host-sensitivity is untested; in this repository nine of ten
    timeout families I examined earlier turned out to be host-sensitive and one
    was not, so the prior is genuinely uncertain.
  - The --all-features arm is a separate run and is not covered here.
  - I did not change either bound, either test body, or any assertion. The only
    code change is the diagnostic message on row 2.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
THE --all-features ARM: 9 failures of 3175, and its failure set is DISJOINT
from the default arm's. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14. This bead now carries the full
failure inventory for the fastmcp-server --lib target at one revision in both
profiles.

  command   cargo test --locked -p fastmcp-server --all-features --lib
            -- --test-threads 1
  host      hz4, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  subject   HEAD 5a634642, manifest agrees True
  counts    3175 discovered / 3175 EXECUTED / 3166 passed / 9 FAILED
            0 ignored / 0 filtered
  verdict   INVALID

THE TWO ARMS DO NOT OVERLAP AT ALL. Default: 2369 rows, 2 failures. All-features:
3175 rows, 9 failures. Neither of the default arm's two names appears among the
nine, and none of the nine appears among the default arm's two. Eleven distinct
failing names across two profiles of the same crate at the same revision.

That disjointness is itself the finding. If these were deterministic product
defects in shared code, the default arm's rows would mostly recur in the
superset profile, because --all-features is a strict superset of default
(it adds apps, enterprise-auth, oauth-client-credentials, builtin-auth-server,
proxy, proxy-legacy, proxy-tasks, native-tls-roots, websocket,
websocket-experimental, jwt-resource-auth). They do not recur. Combined with
both default failures passing 2-for-2 in isolation, the shape is a POPULATION of
context-sensitive bounded rows of which a handful fire on any given run, not a
fixed set of broken tests.

and three were not.

In the all-features inventory above I called returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_modern_child_before_cleanup 'the most regression-shaped row in the nine', on the grounds that it fails on a concrete boolean rather than a deadline. I traced the boolean and the trace refutes that.

A guard that was already present when the row passed twice cannot be the new cause. So the boolean is downstream of whether quiescence was established, which is timing-dependent in a test that deliberately pits a non-quiescent tool against bounded drain windows.

It keeps one distinguishing feature worth noting -- it reports through a boolean rather than a deadline, so its failure mode is legible where the bounded rows' are not -- but that is a diagnostic convenience, not evidence of a different cause.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
THE FAILURE IDENTITIES ROTATE COMPLETELY WHILE THE COUNT AND THE RUNTIME HOLD
STEADY. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14. This is the decisive measurement on this bead
and it changes what is worth chasing.

THE REPEAT, same command, same host, same scope, same profile:

  run 1   2369 discovered / 2369 executed / 2367 passed / 2 FAILED
          exec_time 449.86 s, subject 5a634642
            memory_server_routes_cancellation_while_a_handler_is_pending
            live_http_post_admission_canonical_error_is_one_terminal_sse_response

  run 2   2369 discovered / 2369 executed / 2367 passed / 2 FAILED
          exec_time 440.53 s, subject 0ef7bf17
            public_stdio_final_progress_cancellation_suppresses_post_cancellation_frames
            returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_legacy_handler_before_owned_cleanup

FOUR DISTINCT NAMES, ZERO OVERLAP. The count is identical (2 of 2369 both
times) and the two name pairs share nothing. The only source difference between
the subjects is 0ef7bf17, which changed a diagnostic MESSAGE inside one of run
1's failing tests and nothing else; it cannot have caused run 2's two.

THE RUNTIME IS STABLE TO WITHIN 2 PERCENT, 449.86 s versus 440.53 s, AND THAT
IS THE SHARP PART. If the cause were gross host load, the suite's own wall time
would be the first thing to move, and the explanation would be "a slow run
missed some bounds". The wall time barely moved and a completely different pair
of rows failed. So the cause is finer-grained than host load: per-row
scheduling jitter against bounds that sit close to their actual requirement,
not a suite-wide slowdown.

ACROSS ALL THREE FULL RUNS SO FAR, THIRTEEN DISTINCT FAILING NAMES WITH ZERO
REPEATS among the bounded rows:
  default run 1   2 names
  default run 2   2 names, disjoint from run 1
  all-features    9 names, disjoint from both
Only one name recurs anywhere and it is the deterministic websocket row
(bd-jlu7o, 6 observations across 4 hosts), which exists only in profiles
carrying the websocket feature.

A FAMILY SIGNAL worth noting: run 2's
returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_LEGACY_handler_before_owned_cleanup and
the all-features arm's
returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_MODERN_child_before_cleanup are siblings
in one family, and only one fired in each run. The same is true of the
live_http_* rows, four of which reported through the single harness unwrap at
lib.rs:24423 in the all-features arm. So the at-risk population clusters by
test FAMILY -- live-HTTP harness rows, returning_split rows, stdio
cancellation rows -- rather than being spread uniformly.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR WHAT TO DO, which is the point of the bead.

  CHASING INDIVIDUAL NAMES IS LARGELY WASTED EFFORT. The two names in this
  bead's title are two draws from a pool, not two defects. Any bead filed
  against one of them would be chasing a row that may not fail again, and
  three runs have produced thirteen such names. I am retitling this bead
  accordingly: it is about the rotation, not about its first two samples.

  TWO ITEMS REMAIN GENUINELY ACTIONABLE AND BOTH ARE ALREADY TRACKED:
    - the four proxy assertion rows, one named cause, bd-sdf4b. They fail on
      value comparisons, not bounds, and they are the only rows here that do.
    - the websocket cross-era row, bd-jlu7o, deterministic and blocked on a
      ruling. Its two instrumented captures establish that no close arrives at
      any headroom, so it is not part of this rotation.

  THE SYSTEMIC ITEM IS A BOUND-CALIBRATION QUESTION, not a set of bugs. The
  honest framing: this crate's --lib target has a population of rows whose
  bounds are close enough to their real requirement that ordinary scheduling
  jitter flips roughly two of them per serialized run. Nobody can currently say
  whether those bounds were always marginal or whether something made them so,
  because there is NO RECORDED BASELINE for serialized suite runtime anywhere I
  could find. 440 to 450 seconds is now recorded twice; that is the first
  datum.

WHY I AM NOT PROPOSING TO WIDEN THEM. Thirteen rotating names means a blanket
bound increase would turn an unknown number of marginal rows green without
establishing anything about any of them, which is RH-1 at scale rather than in
one row. The decision needs the baseline first, and then an owner for the
question "are these bounds right", which is not a question any single failing
row can answer.

NO-CLAIM.
  - Three runs. Two in default, one in all-features, two hosts total. Thirteen
    names is a lower bound on the at-risk population, not a measurement of it.
  - I have NOT repeated the all-features arm at all, so its nine are one draw.
  - exec_time is recorded for the two default runs only. The all-features arm's
    wall time was not captured in a form I can quote.
  - The rotation claim covers the BOUNDED rows. The four proxy assertion rows

  - Nothing here identifies a root cause for any individual row.

comments.author: claude-opus-5-session
comments.text:
THE ROTATING POPULATION IS THE BOUNDED-HARNESS POPULATION, AND EVERY BOUND IN
THIS CRATE IS AN ABSOLUTE WALL-CLOCK LITERAL. That is a mechanism which
predicts all three of the signatures measured here -- stable count, rotating
identity, stable runtime -- and it reframes the fix from per-test debugging to
bound calibration. Static measurement at HEAD 5748fea8; I ran no tests.

===========================================================================
1. EVERY ROTATING NAME SITS UNDER A BOUNDED HARNESS
===========================================================================

I extracted the test names from this bead's text and located each one in the
source. All 13 resolve, and they fall into exactly four families, each with its
own wall-clock harness:

  LIVE SOCKET          lib.rs, set_read_timeout harness
    live_http_post_admission_canonical_error_is_one_terminal_sse_response :44563
    live_http_sse_write_half_close_before_election_preserves_response     :44877
    live_http_non_sse_shutdown_suppresses_the_pending_response            :47150
    live_websocket_auto_accepts_fresh_eras_and_fences_cross_era_traffic   :23220
  NATIVE MEMORY        async_stdio.rs, asupersync::time::timeout 8 s
    memory_server_routes_cancellation_while_a_handler_is_pending          :3567
  PROXY SOCKET         builder.rs, proxy.rs set_read/write_timeout harness
    public_builder_proxy_relays_modern_tasks_input_required_and_listener  :6234
    builder_proxy_dual_era_preserves_final_catalog_and_routes_bound_calls :6496
    public_proxy_completion_forwards_exact_legacy_and_final_results       :6678
    public_proxy_completion_replace_installs_upstream_mapping_...         :7014
  STDIO / RETURNING    lib.rs, explicit from_secs bounds in the body
    returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_legacy_handler_...     :32482  (2 s)
    returning_split_waits_for_non_quiescent_modern_child_...       :32530  (START_BOUND 5 s)
    public_stdio_final_progress_cancellation_suppresses_...        :50211  (2 s)
    returning_subscription_background_response_write_succeeds      :51137

No row in the rotating set is a plain assertion test. Every one waits on a
clock.

===========================================================================
2. THE BOUNDS ARE ABSOLUTE, NOT BUDGET-DERIVED. 48 SITES, 11 AT OR UNDER 2 s.
===========================================================================

Every wall-clock bound in `crates/fastmcp-server/src` is a literal
`Duration::from_secs` / `from_millis`. None is derived from the caller budget,
from a measured host baseline, or from any calibration:

      50 ms  x1      3000 ms  x5
     100 ms  x1      5000 ms  x4
    1000 ms  x2      8000 ms  x5
    2000 ms  x7     10000 ms  x19
                    30000 ms  x1
                    60000 ms  x3
    48 sites in total, of which 11 are at or under 2 seconds.

The two tightest are the ones to look at first:
    lib.rs:22299       asupersync::time::timeout(..., from_millis(50), ..)
    lib.rs:44949       set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(100)))
A 100-millisecond absolute read bound on a shared build worker is one scheduler
preemption away from elapsing, and it sits in the same live-HTTP harness as
four of the thirteen.

===========================================================================
3. WHY THIS MECHANISM PREDICTS ALL THREE SIGNATURES
===========================================================================

Under `--test-threads 1` exactly one test is in flight at any moment. If the
host stalls for longer than the bound of whatever is running:

  STABLE COUNT. The failure count tracks the number of stalls per run, not a
  per-test probability. That is why 2-of-2369 recurs instead of varying the way
  independent per-test flakiness would -- under independent trials a count of
  exactly 2 three times running would be a coincidence worth noticing, and this
  bead noticed it.

  ROTATING IDENTITY WITH ZERO OVERLAP. Which test is in flight during a stall
  is uncorrelated between runs, so the names should rotate freely across the
  bounded population and essentially never repeat. Thirteen distinct names and
  zero repeats is what that looks like.

  RUNTIME STABLE TO 2 PERCENT. A few seconds of stall against a 450 s serialized
  run is under 2 percent, so the suite's own wall time barely moves. This bead
  already identified that as the sharp observation and concluded the cause is
  finer-grained than gross host load. It is: it is BRIEF load, clipping tight
  absolute bounds, rather than sustained load stretching the whole run.

===========================================================================
4. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT, cheaply, on the next run anyone does
===========================================================================

  - A failure in a test with NO wall-clock bound would falsify it outright.
    Every one of the thirteen has one; a fourteenth that does not would mean
    something else is going on.
  - The failures should cluster in the TIGHT families rather than spread evenly
    across all 48 bound sites. Four of thirteen are in the live-HTTP harness
    that also owns the 100 ms bound, which is consistent but is not yet a
    measured distribution.
  - Running the same target on an idle host should reduce or eliminate the
    count without any source change. That is the decisive experiment and it
    needs no code edit -- just a quiet worker.

===========================================================================
5. WHAT THE FIX SHAPE LOOKS LIKE, offered as input rather than a plan
===========================================================================

If this holds, chasing the individual rows is wasted effort: the next run
invalidates the list. The durable repairs are to the bounds, in rough order of
return -- raise or remove the two sub-second bounds, make the live-socket read
bounds proportional to a measured baseline rather than a literal, and leave the
10 s and 60 s bounds alone since they are not the ones clipping.

I am not making those edits. Bound values are assertions about the product's
timing contract in some cases and pure harness patience in others, and telling
those apart needs the author of each harness. Widening a bound that is actually
asserting a product deadline would silently delete a real check, which is the
RH-1 shape pointed at a test.

===========================================================================
NO-CLAIM
===========================================================================
  - STATIC ONLY. I ran no tests, reproduced no failure, and measured no stall.
    This is a mechanism consistent with three measured signatures, not a
    demonstrated cause. A mechanism that explains the data is not the same as
    the data showing the mechanism.
  - The 13 names come from extracting long identifiers out of this bead's text,
    so the set may include a name mentioned for another reason or miss one
    written differently. Every name I extracted did resolve to a bounded
    family, which is the claim; the exact membership is this bead's to state.
  - The 48 bound sites are lines matching `set_read_timeout`,
    `set_write_timeout`, `time::timeout` or a `*BOUND*: Duration` const with a
    literal argument. A bound expressed any other way is not counted, so 48 is
    a floor.
  - Nothing here addresses the `os error 11` diagnostic already repaired on
    this bead, which was a message fix and is unaffected.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
A THIRD DATA POINT, WITH A CONFOUND THAT MATTERS. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14.

The first complete workspace lib run put fastmcp-server at 2727 passed / 0 FAILED (HEAD 59788afa, 0 dirty, manifest ddccadf74f6119b0, --no-fail-fast, --test-threads 1). Full receipt on bd-e3en4.

Zero server failures reads like a refutation of the rotating population this bead records. IT IS NOT, and the reason is the test count. This run discovered 2727 server tests; a dedicated -p fastmcp-server --lib run discovers 2369. The difference is Cargo FEATURE UNIFICATION: a workspace build activates the features other members request from fastmcp-server, so this run compiled a larger cfg surface than the per-crate form does.

So this is a third observation of a DIFFERENT configuration, not a third observation of the same one. A test count is meaningless without its feature set, and 2727 != 2369 is exactly that warning firing.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT ADD:
  - It does NOT contradict the two dedicated runs (2 failures each, rotating identities, 440-450 s).
  - It DOES show that under feature unification, with the suite run as part of a 7,560-test workspace pass, no server row failed. If the marginal-bound hypothesis is right, that is unsurprising: a different schedule and a different cfg surface draw a different sample, and sometimes the sample is empty.
  - It adds a THIRD distinct configuration to the inventory, which strengthens the general point that this crate's bounded rows are configuration- and schedule-sensitive rather than individually broken.

The practical consequence for this bead is unchanged: chasing individual names remains near-wasted effort, and the open item is still a bound-calibration owner plus the runtime baseline. The two baseline figures recorded here (449.86 s and 440.53 s for the 2369-test per-crate form) do NOT transfer to the 2727-test unified form, so that configuration has no baseline at all.

title: FND-01 pinned tool-version os: line is forgeable by removing one binary (os_info bitness comes from getconf)
description:
The FND-01 bootstrap's terminal gate pins cargo -Vv line by line
(fnd_01_dependency_evidence.rs:17591). Line 9 is

  os: Ubuntu 25.10.0 (questing) [unknown bitness]

MEASURED 2026-10-05, docker ubuntu:25.10 on hz3 with nightly-2026-07-11:

  getconf present   os: Ubuntu 25.10.0 (questing) [64-bit]
  getconf masked    os: Ubuntu 25.10.0 (questing) [unknown bitness]   byte-identical to the pin

os_info derives bitness by executing getconf; absent getconf it returns Bitness::Unknown,
which renders "[unknown bitness]". `chmod 000 /usr/bin/getconf` is therefore sufficient to
satisfy the strongest-looking component of this pin.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The os: line exists so retained FND-01 evidence
binds the environment that produced it, and everything downstream treats FND-01 as the frozen
root. But:

  * the release and codename are reproduced by any ubuntu:25.10 container, so they bind
    nothing about the host;
  * "[unknown bitness]" looks like a strong machine fingerprint and is in fact the EASIEST
    field to forge, because it is produced by ABSENCE rather than presence -- a lane satisfies
    it by subtracting a file rather than by possessing anything;
  * lines 1-8 are satisfied by an ordinary rustup install (verified on hz4 and in the
    container), so they bind the toolchain, which is already pinned elsewhere.

So a lane under pressure to produce FND-01 evidence can pass this gate on a host of its
choosing. I declined to (RH-12: environment-sniffed success paths, demo-path hardcoding), and
recorded the refusal on bd-o590u, but the gate should not depend on a lane's restraint.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION, not a prescription: bind an observable a lane cannot subtract -- an
attested container image digest, a kernel/boot identity, or a signed host statement -- rather
than a tool's self-report of its environment. The same shape protects every other pinned tool
line in the same table (rustdoc-pinned-1.99, rustfmt-pinned-nightly, clippy-pinned-nightly,
lld-gnu-version), so the question is general.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this bead reports a gate-strength defect. It does not assert that any
existing FND-01 evidence was forged, and I have no reason to think it was.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus5-20261011
comments.text:
RealityCheck-Opus5-20261011, 2026-10-11. Read-only. Not claiming this bead, not
authoring acceptance, nothing ticked. I assessed it as a candidate for code work
during a ready-pool sweep and concluded it is NOT code-actionable by a coding
lane. Recording why, plus one wrong fix to rule out, so the next lane does not
spend the sweep I just spent.

THE OBVIOUS NARROW FIX IS WRONG AND WOULD BREAK FND-01.

The tempting reading is "make the verifier fail closed on `[unknown bitness]`
instead of accepting it". That inverts the situation. Line 9 of the pin IS

    os: Ubuntu 25.10.0 (questing) [unknown bitness]

so the legitimate authoring host is itself a host without `getconf`; the string
is the recorded truth about it, not a sentinel for a missing measurement.
Refusing that value would make the frozen pin unsatisfiable by the very
environment it was frozen against, i.e. it would weaken/alter a frozen
requirement to chase a forgeability property (RH-10), and it would break the
FND-01 root rather than harden it. Any lane that reaches for that edit should
stop.

WHY NO NARROWER CODE FIX EXISTS EITHER. This bead's own analysis is already the
complete one: the weakness is structural, not a missing check. Lines 1-8 are
reproduced by an ordinary rustup install, release and codename by any
`ubuntu:25.10` container, and line 9 by *subtracting* a file. There is no
additional predicate over `cargo -Vv` output that fixes this, because the defect
is that the whole subject is a tool's self-report of its own environment. The
remedy the description names -- bind an observable a lane cannot subtract (image
digest, kernel/boot identity, signed host statement) -- changes WHAT FND-01
binds. That is an evidence-model decision owned by the structure owner, and
implementing it re-freezes the same FND-01 inputs that bd-o590u and bd-rb77i are
already stopped on pending an operator ruling. So it is not merely "needs a
decision"; it is downstream of a decision already queued elsewhere.

SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE. Fixing this bead before that ruling would author a
second, competing freeze of the same inputs. It should be sequenced WITH the
FND-01 re-freeze, not ahead of it, and whoever takes that re-freeze should pick
up this bead's generalisation at the same time -- the description is right that
the same shape protects rustdoc-pinned-1.99, rustfmt-pinned-nightly,
clippy-pinned-nightly and lld-gnu-version, so doing it once per line later is
strictly worse than doing it once now.

I am leaving it unassigned, P2, with its no-claim boundary intact: this remains
a gate-strength report and asserts nothing about existing evidence having been
forged.
