comments.text:
MEASUREMENT REFUTES THE active() BOXING HYPOTHESIS. Nothing pushed for the overflow; my boxing branch stays unpushed and unmerged.

I had a structural case that active() (client_credentials.rs:770, defined ONCE and awaited at ~38 sites, several nested three deep) was the multiplier: it takes `future` by value into its generator prefix, re-pins it inside unless_revoked, and hands a block to within() which pin!s by value again. That is the bd-n5dvm mechanism, so it looked like the same class.

size_of says no. Diag run on hz3, base 89d43bdc (diag probes only, never landed), cargo test -p fastmcp-client --lib --all-features -j 4 -- diag_ --nocapture --test-threads=1, 2 passed:
  DIAGSZ leaf=1 active1=968 active2=1056 active3=1056
  DIAGSZ submission_next_event=3760 submission_resume=11000
active() nesting does NOT multiply: layer 2 costs +88 bytes over layer 1, and layer 3 costs the SAME as layer 2. rustc is overlapping the moved-from parameter slot with the pinned local, so the doubling I reasoned about does not exist here. Boxing active() would have moved ~1 KB to the heap and fixed nothing, and I would have burned your verify lane proving a no-op.

The real submission chain futures are also far too small to overflow anything: next_event 3.7 KB, resume 11 KB.

CONCLUSION: the 40 child stack overflows are NOT this layer. Either a much larger future lives elsewhere on the live drive path (creation / drive / recovery / resume / journal, which I have not yet sized), or it is genuine recursion, in which case no boxing helps at all. Those two are distinguishable only by the stack bisection, which is what I am doing next, per your instruction.

Method for the bisection, and it does not touch the isolation harness in any landed code: first a plain run of the live subtree at origin/main 3fdfcdcc to capture WHICH children print "stack overflow" (your log had 40 but did not name them, and comment 5912's 6 residue items are assertion failures, so I must not assume the overflow set). Then a ladder on one confirmed overflower. If every stack size fails it is recursion and the whole approach changes; if a threshold exists it names the layer and the headroom.

RH-2 note: the active1/active2/active3 numbers are a static layout measurement, not a runtime proof of the overflow cause. I am not claiming a root cause for the 40 until the bisection and the per-layer sizes on the actual failing path are in.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text:
DIAGNOSTIC HANDOFF for the 40 child stack overflows (WildMountain). I did NOT box anything, because boxing without a size measurement is guessing, and the wrong layer costs a full RCH cycle to disprove.

WHAT I ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE (no run needed)
The 46 failures all die at the parent assertion live.rs:60:61 'assertion failed: status.success()', which is isolated_run asserting its re-exec'd child exited 0; the log carries 40 'stack overflow' lines, so the children abort. The child is spawned as Command::new(current_exe) with --exact <name> --nocapture --test-threads=1, and libtest still names the spawned thread after the test, so the child runs on an ordinary 2 MiB spawned test stack, NOT the larger main-thread stack.

THE SPECIFIC SUSPECT
crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/discovery/client_credentials/tasks/subscriptions/watch/drive/tests/live.rs:99

    async fn pair<L: Future, R: Future>(left: L, right: R) -> (L::Output, R::Output) {
        let mut left = std::pin::pin!(left);
        let mut right = std::pin::pin!(right);
        ...

It takes both futures BY VALUE and then pin!s them, so each argument occupies the enclosing async fn's state slot AND the pin! slot - two copies of a large product future per pair() call. There are 28 pair() call sites in the live tree and ZERO nesting, so the effect is 2x per layer rather than compounding. Whether 2x is enough to cross 2 MiB depends entirely on how big the arguments already are, and the arguments are real product futures (discover(...), tasks.subscribe(...)).

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES IT, AND WHY IT MATTERS WHO OWNS THE FIX
Add a temporary diagnostic #[test] that prints std::mem::size_of_val on the concrete futures at one failing call site - the bare argument future, and the pair(...) future that wraps it. Then:
- if the ARGUMENT future is already close to or over 2 MiB, this is a PRODUCT defect: the shipped machine watch/drive future is oversized and a real caller on an ordinary thread can overflow too. Fix it in product code by boxing the offending inner step, exactly as b0bf22bb did for logout/renewal.
- if the argument is modest and only the doubled pair(...) future crosses the line, this is a TEST-HARNESS defect confined to live.rs: fix pair() to accept already-pinned futures (or Box::pin at the call sites) and claim NOTHING about product stack behaviour.
Those two outcomes have different owners and different no-claim boundaries, so do not merge them. Also bisect the child thread stack (RUST_MIN_STACK on the child only, as a MEASUREMENT not a fix) to learn the actual requirement; my n5dvm ruling still forbids shipping RUST_MIN_STACK, a big-stack test thread, cfg(test) boxing, or #[ignore] as the remedy.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus5-20261005
comments.text:
EVIDENCE-LOSS CONTROL APPLIED. 42 commits cited as evidence by review-status
beads were DANGLING -- resolvable only because gc had not run -- and several of
them are the RH-5 planted negatives themselves. They are now pinned and pushed.
Measured and executed 2026-10-05 at a156246c.

THE MEASUREMENT, over all 49 review-status beads:

    distinct 8-hex commit ids cited and resolvable     315
      ancestors of HEAD (receipt still bound)          263
      ORPHANED (resolve, not in HEAD history)           52
        held by some ref (survive gc)                   10
        DANGLING (destroyed by the next gc)             42

14 of the 49 review beads cite at least one orphaned commit, including two P0s
(bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-a-kkj8 and bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-b-y6od, four each). This is
AGENTS.md PL-6 exactly: a rebased commit sha still resolves under git show while
no longer being in HEAD history. The reflog carries 557 rebase/reset entries,
consistent with the shared-worktree rebase damage already recorded here.

WHY THIS WAS URGENT RATHER THAN UNTIDY. Many of the 42 are not superseded
intermediates. Their own subjects say what they are, and several say
"never pushed":

    a41165b9  PLANT2: 900ms stall after TCP accept, before TLS accept
    be9e7def  PLANT new: 21s slow storage with the fixed deadline
    2718a3ee  PLANT old: 21s slow storage before the pre-computed deadline
    152520ab  PLANT builder on fix: slow child start
    03da2186  PLANT builder: slow child start, 5s cap
    6380dd15  PLANT: 900ms host stall per peer rpc
    3ea6f43f  PLANT: service ping before era selection
    3d93dcfc  snapshot: delete post_jsonrpc_response
    1c4884d6  snapshot: facade dead_code
    cabfd12d  snapshot: live initializer property tests
    adf63b86  snapshot: bd-tls7a T3 + builder probe fixes on origin/main
    657f572a  test(fnd-01): RH-5 planted negative for the secure_file sealed API
    878d235b  test(fnd-01): plant both baseline directions, two-way closure
    5353df78  test(fnd-01): arm C, planted negative fails when evidence moves
    15976ed8  test(transport): RH-5 pair for the stdio close budget checkpoint

A planted negative is the artefact that proves a gate FIRES. Losing it does not
weaken a claim slightly; it makes the claim unfalsifiable after the fact, and
re-deriving it means re-running the experiment. bd-tls7a and bd-xstbj were the
most exposed: their planted-negative and snapshot evidence existed ONLY as
unpushed dangling objects on one workstation.

WHAT I DID, deliberately the minimal control. For each of the 42, a new ref:

    git update-ref refs/evidence/review-cited/<short> <full>

then pushed that namespace to origin. 42 pinned, 0 failed, 42 verified present
on origin. This creates refs ONLY: no commit, no branch, no tag, no history
edit, nothing deleted or overwritten, and git status unchanged. The
refs/evidence/ namespace cannot collide with branches or tags. The objects are
now gc-safe and available to every lane rather than to whichever machine
happened to hold them.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It does not make any receipt valid. An orphaned commit is
still outside HEAD history, so a receipt bound to one remains unbound under
Code-First 4 (relevant source movement invalidates it). The control buys exactly
one thing: the evidence can still be READ and re-derived when the orchestrator
reaches these beads, instead of being gone. Re-binding is the orchestrator job
and the right form is PL-6 -- bind to BLOB hashes, which survive both rebases
and unrelated tree edits.

RETIREMENT CONDITION for the refs: remove them once the 14 affected beads are
closed or their receipts re-bound to ancestors of HEAD. They are a recovery
control, not a permanent fixture, and I deleted nothing.

THE 14 AFFECTED BEADS: bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-a-kkj8, bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-b-y6od,
bd-bi6mo, bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.3.1, bd-mcp-2026-07-28-support-ahet.3.3,
bd-mcp-auth-00-a-ry15, bd-mcp-auth-00-b-ykgm, bd-mcp-fnd-04-a-jmi7,
bd-mcp-http-03-integration-vx7y, bd-pgnvs, bd-tls7a, bd-k1yii, bd-to4cj,
bd-xstbj.

NO-CLAIM. Citing an orphan does not by itself invalidate a bead: the orphan may
be a superseded step whose conclusion a later ancestor also carries. I measured
"cites at least one orphan", not "receipt is wrong". Per-bead adjudication is
the orchestrator decision.

title: fastmcp-client: automatic_catalog_lists_expire_while_waiting_for_the_second_page is wall-clock flaky under the parallel suite
description:
tests::automatic_catalog_lists_expire_while_waiting_for_the_second_page (crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs, from outside commit f2fd5cea) fails intermittently under the parallel full client --lib suite. It passes serially and in the other parallel run.

Observed at 56ad2552 on vmi1152480, a non-hz worker, no disk-pressure signature (17.89s suite, 0 "running for over 60 seconds"):
  panicked at crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:36373:27:
  late tombstoned output cannot poison the next request; the peer sees exactly one matching cancellation only after timeout:
  McpError { code: InternalError, message: "Request timed out at the absolute deadline", data: Some({"timeoutSource":"absolute"}) }
Same revision, same worker: the next parallel run was 1321/0, and the serial run was 1321/0.

Mechanism, read from source: the peer is a shell script that paces its replies with wall-clock `sleep 0.35` and `sleep {delay}` against a Duration::from_millis(550) request budget, and the test then pings through the same client. Under a loaded parallel suite the follow-up ping itself can hit the absolute deadline. That makes the outcome depend on the host's scheduling, not on the client's deadline logic.
Related pattern: bd-tls7a (913a174a) removed the same class of wall-clock sensitivity from two other client tests.

Fix direction: make the ordering observable instead of timed. Gate the peer's late reply on an event the test controls, or on virtual time where the harness allows it, so the ping and the absolute-deadline assertion do not race host scheduling. Do not lengthen budgets or sleeps.
acceptance_criteria: The test's pass or fail no longer depends on host scheduling: its late-reply and ping ordering is gated by an event or virtual time, not by wall-clock shell sleeps against a 550 ms budget. It keeps its positive and negative arms, with no budget or sleep lengthened. Three consecutive parallel full cargo test -p fastmcp-client --lib runs on RCH, at least one on a non-hz worker, report it ok.

comments.author: SilentSquirrel
comments.text:
SUBMISSION for batch verification (SilentSquirrel).

Fix f7b59165 "test(client): event-gate the automatic catalog deadline pair and pin the traversal cap directly". It is on main+master as plain merge baa58485 (parent f769cceb; the merge diff is exactly crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs). Test code only; no product change.

WHAT CHANGED:
- assert_automatic_catalog_deadline, both arms: the wall-clock `sleep 0.35` / `sleep {delay}` pacing is gone.
  - The timely peer answers each page as soon as it reads the request.
  - The late peer withholds page 2 until it reads the client's own notifications/cancelled for request 3, then writes that page as late output and answers the ping at once.
  - The 550 ms budget and every assert are unchanged. That covers both automatic_catalog_lists_expire_while_waiting_for_the_second_page and its sibling automatic_catalog_lists_accept_the_same_second_page_before_the_deadline, which is the one WildMountain saw fail at ac863b2e all-features.

The old timed arm was the only guard that a later page's wait is capped by the traversal deadline, not a fresh request budget: expired_at breaks idle/absolute ties toward Absolute, so both label "absolute". An event-gated stall cannot see that, so it is pinned by ratio instead.
  - Setup: request policy 20 s, traversal deadline 200 ms.
  - Required: the stalled page 2 errors "absolute" in under 10 s; next_id == 4; 0 pending; clean ping; close.

title: TOOL-01 implementation A: tool schema/catalog and registration
description:
Section 36.4.1 A leaf: disjoint real-production tool schema/catalog and registration with same-Bead positive and planted-negative tests.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:TOOL-01:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for TOOL-01.

Owned capability slice: tool schema/catalog and registration.
Named shipped consumer: public tool API.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### TOOL-01 — Implement final tool metadata and listing

Outcome:

Make tool discovery exact, deterministic, cacheable, and safe for HTTP
header projection.

Reason:

Tool listings feed both model context and client transport behavior.

Implementation:

- Implement final Tool metadata fields.
- Make safe constructors and local registration enforce the dated
  interoperability name profile: 1 through 128 ASCII characters,
  exactly `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, case-sensitive, and unique by exact name
  within one server. `foo` and `Foo` are distinct; an exact duplicate
  is rejected.

- Implement final Tool metadata fields.
- Make safe constructors and local registration enforce the dated
  interoperability name profile: 1 through 128 ASCII characters,
  exactly `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, case-sensitive, and unique by exact name
  within one server. `foo` and `Foo` are distinct; an exact duplicate
  is rejected.

  during tolerant decoding with a diagnostic rather than inventing a
  schema rejection. Preserve duplicate peer entries in the raw ordered
  catalog, but make name-based convenience lookup report exact
  ambiguity instead of silently choosing one.
- Support title.
- Support icon arrays.
- Support annotations.
- Apply display-title precedence exactly as `Tool.title`, then
  `Tool.annotations.title`, then `Tool.name`.
- Treat every `ToolAnnotations` member as an untrusted hint. Model the
  exact absent defaults: `readOnlyHint=false`,
  `destructiveHint=true`, `idempotentHint=false`, and
  `openWorldHint=true`, without synthesizing absent fields back onto
  the wire.
- Support open `_meta`.
- Retain local version/tags only as internal catalog data or a
  documented FastMCP extension.
- Require object-rooted input schemas.
- Require the `outputSchema` wire field itself to be a JSON object, as
  required by the final MCP schema.
- Permit that object schema to describe any JSON instance type; do not
  impose an object instance root.
- Route both fields through SCH-01's shared admission service. For
  local construction/registration, admit both schemas before one
  atomic catalog commit; a failure leaves registration order, catalog
  revision, list-change state, and caches unchanged. A server stores
  and emits only `AdmittedTool` entries and cannot serialize a raw or
  partly admitted schema into `tools/list`.
- At client and gateway ingestion, admit every Tool on each bounded
  `tools/list` page after wire/message limits but before catalog/cache
  mutation, name lookup, header projection, UI/model exposure, cursor
  successor commit, collision/union routing, or downstream forwarding.
  Admission is page-atomic: one unsupported dialect, invalid schema, or
  unresolved/over-limit reference rejects the entire page as a typed
  peer catalog error identifying only the bounded page index, safe
  tool name when available, schema role, and stable SCH-01 code. It
  never filters a bad Tool into a shorter page, exposes a partial
  catalog, advances local pagination state, or retries under a
  different dialect/reference policy. The deterministic admission
  failure terminates that logical listing attempt rather than causing
  an automatic same-cursor retry loop.

  metadata. Run `x-mcp-header` analysis only on an admitted input
  schema; admission itself never grants header-exposure approval.
- Return tools in deterministic registration order.
- Return required TTL and cache scope.
- Add catalog revision invalidation.
- Parse `x-mcp-header` annotations from statically reachable
  properties.

  registration-time `NonSensitiveHeaderExposure` review bound to the
  exact tool/schema revision and property path. Default registration

  framework knows is a secret wrapper or marks `writeOnly`/password-

  conditionals.

  list and emit a warning.

- Cache-hint tests.
- Header-name token matrix.
- Case-insensitive duplicate test.
- Safe-integer boundary test.

title: TOOL-02 implementation A: tool handler/builder integration
description:
Section 36.4.1 A leaf: disjoint real-production tool handler/builder integration with same-Bead positive and planted-negative tests.

<!-- MCP-2026-07-28-BRIDGE-V1:DESCRIPTION:TOOL-02:A:BEGIN -->
Canonical A role for TOOL-02.

Owned capability slice: tool handler/builder integration.
Named shipped consumer: public tool registration path.
Rationale: none.

This role is self-contained against the following frozen package contract. The embedded package body is context, not separate capability credit:

### TOOL-02 — Implement final tool call semantics

Outcome:

Support complete, input-required, and task-capable tool calls with
full validation.

Reason:

Tool calls are the richest result surface in the final protocol.

Implementation:

- Implement final call parameters.
- Include MRTR input responses and request state.
- Validate inputs against the full input schema.
- Apply the final tools error taxonomy exactly. A malformed
  `CallToolRequest`—including a structurally invalid/missing method
  parameter shape—or an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC protocol error
  (`-32602` under the dated tools specification). Once the request is
  structurally schema-valid and resolves one tool, an `arguments`
  object that fails that tool's registered `inputSchema` is instead a
  tool execution error: do not invoke the handler, and return one
  schema-valid `resultType: "complete"` result with `isError: true`.
  Never remap this second class to a JSON-RPC error.
- Make validation feedback bounded and model-actionable while
  disclosure-safe. Include only approved public field locations,
  constraint classes, and corrective summaries; do not echo secret
  values, the complete argument object, private schema annotations,
  regex internals, filesystem/application paths, or validator stack
  details. TOOL-02 owns a closed public-validation-feedback
  classifier and passes the synthesized result through ordinary
  result/content limits. It does not depend on OBS-02's later MCP-log
  or terminal-rendering policy; any later human-facing consumer still
  applies that policy independently.
- Preserve absent versus empty arguments correctly.
- Return complete content.
- Return arbitrary structured content using a presence-aware
  representation: absent and explicitly present JSON null remain
  distinct because `structuredContent?: unknown` permits the latter.
- Model tool-level `isError` as presence-aware with an effective
  default of false. Preserve absent, explicit false, and true
  distinctly on round trip; explicit null and wrong types are
  structural errors, and no semantic path treats absence as a third
  state.
- For every locally emitted complete result whose tool declares
  `outputSchema`, regardless of effective `isError`, require
  `structuredContent` to be present and validate its exact JSON value
  against that schema before server emission. Explicit null, false,
  zero, an empty string, array, or object all count as present and are
  accepted only if the schema admits them. Register the bounded
  schema-valid tool-error mapper required by Section 5.18 before
  accepting such a tool.
- At client ingestion, require and validate declared structured output
  for non-error results. Apply Section 5.18's client-only pinned-peer
  tolerance to an effective `isError: true`: missing or nonconforming
  structured content is diagnosed, bounded, and treated only as
  untyped error payload, never as typed successful data. A proxy cannot
  propagate that deviation onto a modern downstream leg. Do not apply
  a tool's complete-result `outputSchema` to input-required or
  task-result branches.
- When `structuredContent` is present, mirror its serialized JSON in a
  `TextContent` fallback by default as the final interoperability
  SHOULD recommends. Permit an explicit advanced opt-out only with a
  documented SHOULD-deviation diagnostic.
- Treat locally produced `EmbeddedResource` tool-result content as a
  declaration that the server uses embedded resources. Safe server
  construction therefore requires the effective `resources`
  capability and its dispatchable APIs before such a result can be
  emitted. An advanced deployment that intentionally returns an
  embedded snapshot without implementing resources must opt into a
  reviewed, documented SHOULD-deviation; the content remains fully
  validated and the framework must not synthesize a false capability.
- Route every locally produced `ResourceLink` and `EmbeddedResource`
  in an ordinary, input-required continuation, or eventual Task
  terminal tool result through PRT-02's current
  `ResourceUriUsePolicy` at the exact attachment/emission site. A
  registration-time resource check, resources capability, or prior
  admission at another content site cannot substitute.
- Carry result metadata.
- Allow input-required through MRTR.
- Allow task result only through the negotiated Tasks extension.
  Negotiation adds the server-directed task branch to the eligible
  `tools/call` result union; it does not remove the ordinary complete
  or capability-permitted input-required branches and does not expose
  any client task-preference flag.
- Enforce required capabilities before handler execution.
- Produce request-associated progress and log events through the
  transport policy: token-correlated progress, per-response HTTP logs,
  and Section 5.21's conservative stdio log
  emission/attribution rule.
- Require an injected client `ToolInvocationPolicy` for model/user-
  initiated calls. It identifies the verified server and exact tool,
  lets a human deny, shows the complete validated inputs before send,
  and requires explicit confirmation for policy-classified sensitive
  or destructive calls. Tool annotations are untrusted hints and never
  decide sensitivity alone. A headless client records an explicit
  reviewed SHOULD-deviation and equivalent allow/deny policy.
- Bound execution with a caller-visible timeout/budget and record a
  redacted audit outcome. Validate the complete wire/result
  discriminator, content limits, and declared output schema before
  exposing a result to the model.
- Deliver a schema-valid complete tool result with `isError: true` to
  the model as tool execution output for possible self-correction,
  rather than converting it into a transport/protocol exception.
  Invalid output, protocol failure, timeout, and denied invocation stay
  distinct typed outcomes.
- Classify disconnect retry safety using annotations plus execution
  state, never annotations alone.

Acceptance:

- Structurally valid calls whose arguments violate `inputSchema` fail
  before handler invocation as `complete`/`isError: true` tool
  execution results; malformed calls and unknown tools remain
  JSON-RPC protocol errors.
- Invalid declared outputs fail at the server boundary with a clear
  internal/configuration error.
- Tool-level error remains a complete result.
- For every locally emitted complete result, declaring `outputSchema`
  makes structured-content presence and conformance mandatory,
  including `isError: true`; explicit null and other falsy JSON values
  remain valid only when that schema admits them.
- Tool-level absent `isError` has effective false without changing its
  wire representation. Error results remain complete. A nonconforming
  peer error result is accepted only through the diagnosed client
  compatibility path and never becomes valid server/proxy output.
- Explicit-null structured content round-trips while absent structured
  content remains absent for tools without `outputSchema`; a tolerated
  peer error deviation preserves its actual field presence.
- Default structured output includes a semantically equal text
  fallback and the opt-out remains explicit and visible.
- Local embedded-resource results either have a truthful,
  dispatchable `resources` capability or an explicit reviewed
  deviation; they can never cause capability over-advertisement.
- An unnegotiated task discriminator is rejected.
- Negotiating Tasks never forces task creation; the same client API
  accepts the applicable ordinary result branches or a task result as
  the server decides per eligible call.
- MRTR continuation verifies request state.
- A client cannot silently invoke a sensitive tool, pass unvalidated
  output to a model, or confuse tool-level failure with protocol
  failure.

Tests:

- Input validation positive/negative corpus.
- Golden error-taxonomy matrix: malformed envelope/params, non-object
  `arguments`, and unknown tool produce the required JSON-RPC error;
  missing required argument, wrong format/type/range, failed
  composition, and additional-property violations on a structurally
  valid call produce `resultType: "complete"` plus `isError: true`.
  Assert zero handler calls, schema-valid bounded public feedback, and
  no raw argument/schema/regex/path/stack disclosure for every
  execution-error case.
- Arbitrary structured JSON values.
- Cross `outputSchema` absent/present with effective `isError`
  absent/false/true and `structuredContent`
  absent/null/false/zero/empty-string/empty-array/empty-object/
  conforming/nonconforming values at both server-emission and
  client-ingestion boundaries. Prove absent `isError` means false
  without being synthesized, explicit null/wrong type fails,
  every schema-declared local complete-result omission/mismatch fails,
  present falsy values are validated rather than mistaken for
  omission, and only client ingestion of the effective peer-error
  branch has the bounded diagnosed compatibility path.
- Tool registration/error-mapper tests proving a declared output
  schema can represent framework input-validation and handler errors
  truthfully; absent, invalid, or misleading dummy error mappings fail
  before server emission.
- Proxy tests prove a tolerated upstream error deviation is never
  forwarded as a nonconforming modern downstream result.
- Input-required and task-result branches are not checked against the
  declared complete-success `outputSchema`.
- Absent-versus-explicit-null structured-content schema parity for
  tools without `outputSchema` and tolerated peer error deviations.
- Structured-content text-fallback equality and explicit opt-out
  diagnostics.
- Embedded-resource result with enabled resources, missing resources,
  explicit deviation, and no-false-capability tests.
- Dynamic tool-result `ResourceLink`/`EmbeddedResource` policy tests
  over ordinary, MRTR-resumed, and Task-terminal emission; client-
  direct HTTPS, accidental server-mediated HTTPS, custom scheme,
  stale/wrong-use admission token, and post-registration construction.
- Output mismatch tests.
- Tool-level error tests.
- MRTR integration.
- Task negotiation/result-union matrix, including no-preference
  request construction, declared-plus-ordinary, declared-plus-task,
  undeclared-plus-ordinary, undeclared-plus-task rejection, and task
  result on an ineligible method.
- Cancellation before and after handler commit.
- Tool policy deny, server/tool disclosure, full-input review,
  sensitive confirmation, misleading-annotation non-authority,
  headless explicit-deviation, timeout, and redacted audit tests.
- Invalid wire/output-before-model denial and `isError` result-to-model
  self-correction fixtures distinct from protocol/transport errors.

Dependencies:

- TOOL-01.
- SRV-04.
- MRTR-01.
- HTTP-04.
- SCH-01.

title: RESOLVED pending verification: fastmcp-client now compiles with --features tasks and both previously-never-run Tasks targets execute and pass (2 + 24 tests, 0 filtered) - repair unattributed
description:
`fastmcp-client` does not compile with `--features tasks`. Both of the crate's
Tasks test targets declare `required-features = ["tasks"]`, so without the flag
cargo silently skips them and with the flag the library does not build. Those
two targets have never run and currently cannot.

MEASURED 2026-10-12. This is a COMPILE failure, not a test failure, which is
why one observation is enough: same source plus the same pinned toolchain gives
the same result. I have been careful all session to repeat test failures before
reading anything into them; that discipline does not apply to a build error and
I am not pretending it does.

  scope     -p fastmcp-client --features tasks --test task_01_b
            --test task_resume_store
  worker    hz3 (ubuntu@194.140.197.98), 70391480 KiB free, 93% used
            -- NOT a disk failure; the verifier checks for that explicitly and
            did not flag it
  toolchain nightly-2026-08-25, rustc 1.100.0-nightly e7769602,
            x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  manifest  6ff29d2d77f07ed4f2e51533ffdc8edabc046e235d9447263acbfc9265e68245
  result    RECEIPT_BUILD_RC=101, RECEIPT_VERDICT=BUILD_FAILED, 0 tests
            discovered, 0 executed

      error[E0277]: the trait bound
        `CompleteResult<FinalSubscriptionsListenResult>: serde::Serialize`
        is not satisfied
      error: could not compile `fastmcp-client` (lib) due to 1 previous error

Note "(lib)": this is the library target, not a test target.

THE BOUND CANNOT BE SATISFIED AS THINGS STAND, and that part is checkable
without building anything:

  crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/result.rs:698
      #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
      pub struct CompleteResult<T> { payload: T, meta: ResultMeta,
                                     extras: UnknownResultMembers }

  `CompleteResult` derives only Debug and Clone. A search for a manual
  `impl ... Serialize for CompleteResult` across fastmcp-protocol/src returns
  nothing. So `CompleteResult<T>: Serialize` holds for NO T, and the payload
  type is not the problem: FinalSubscriptionsListenResult does derive Serialize
  (messages.rs:3419).

  Whatever requires that bound has therefore never compiled, at any feature
  set, since `CompleteResult` acquired its current derive list.

CANDIDATE SITES, offered as candidates only. These are the four places that
name the exact generic instantiation; I did NOT get the compiler's file:line
(see below) and have not read any of them:
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:857            field `terminal` of
                                                      SubscriptionListenCollector
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/lib.rs:11795
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_executor.rs:1248
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_executor.rs:3257 field `terminal`
A `cargo check -p fastmcp-client --features tasks` names it in one line for
whoever picks this up.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT. crates/fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml:

      [[test]] name = "task_01_b"           required-features = ["tasks"]
      [[test]] name = "task_resume_store"   required-features = ["tasks"]

with a manifest comment stating the flag is "mandatory, not optional" per
AGENTS.md. So the gate swallows its own surface from both directions: WITHOUT
`tasks`, cargo skips both targets silently and reports nothing; WITH `tasks`,
the library does not build. Either way those two targets contribute zero
executed rows, and no receipt I can find in this repository has ever executed
them.

For scale on what else is unaffected: `-p fastmcp-client --lib` at DEFAULT
features reads 1523/1523 GREEN (measured today, complete parse, nothing ignored
or filtered). So the crate is healthy at its default feature set and the break
is specific to `tasks`.

RELATED BUT NOT A DUPLICATE. Two beads already track client compile breaks, and
both differ from this in error, target and configuration:
    bd-client-libtest-e0308-capset-4pamt [review]  E0308 CapSet mismatch at
        validity.rs:363, the LIB-TEST target, default features
    bd-bb11e [review]                              E0282 at lib.rs:13037, the
        lib test target, default features
Both are in review, and today's 1523/1523 green at default features suggests
both may already be resolved. Mine is E0277, on the LIB target, only with
`tasks`. Searched the tracker before filing: the exact bound
`CompleteResult<FinalSubscriptionsListenResult>` appears 0 times, and none of
the 19 beads mentioning task_01_b concerns a compile failure.

WHAT I COULD NOT GET, and why it is not a project problem. I tried to capture
the compiler's file:line through `rch exec -- cargo check`. RCH refused on both
workers it tried with "source-authority lock ... exited before acquisition;
unfinished overlapping source owner" and then "refusing local fallback",
exiting 103. That is another lane holding the source-authority lock and it is
retryable; it says nothing about this crate. Worth noting separately that the
rch wrapper's exit code does not reflect the remote result -- a first attempt
of mine exited 0 having run nothing.

NO-CLAIM.
  - I have not identified WHICH of the four sites fails, and have read none of
    them.
  - I have not dated the break. It could be longstanding or recent; the
    `CompleteResult` derive list and whichever site needs Serialize would both
    need `git log -L` to place.
  - I am NOT proposing that `CompleteResult` derive Serialize. It holds an
    `UnknownResultMembers` and a `ResultMeta`, and whether a complete result
    should be serializable as a unit looks like a protocol-shape decision
    rather than a missing derive. The alternative -- that the client site
    should serialize the payload rather than the wrapper -- is equally
    plausible and I have no basis to choose.
  - Not claiming the two test targets would pass if the crate built. They have
    never run, so nothing is known about them beyond that.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
CrimsonFjord, 2026-10-12. ADDENDUM: I tried to pin the failing site by reading and could NOT. Recording the dead ends so nobody repeats them, and stopping rather than inferring further.

WHAT I CHECKED. All four sites that name
`CompleteResult<FinalSubscriptionsListenResult>`, and the enclosing item for
each, with its attributes:

  lib.rs:857            pub struct SubscriptionListenCollector
                        #[derive(Debug, Clone)]                     no Serialize
  lib.rs:11795          pub enum FinalTaskWatchEvent (decl :11782)
                        #[derive(Debug, Clone)] #[cfg(feature = "tasks")]
                                                                    no Serialize
  http_executor.rs:1248 pub enum ModernHttpSubscriptionListenEvent
                        #[derive(Debug, Clone)]                     no Serialize
  http_executor.rs:3257 pub struct ModernHttpSubscriptionListenCollector
                        #[derive(Debug, Clone)]                     no Serialize

So NONE of the four is under a `#[derive(Serialize)]`, which was my first
hypothesis: a derive on a struct holding that field would generate the bound
definitively and would have ended this in one step. It does not.

My second hypothesis was FinalTaskWatchEvent, because it is the ONLY one of the
four that is `#[cfg(feature = "tasks")]`-gated and the break appears only with
`tasks`. That looked strong. But a search for any serde usage of
FinalTaskWatchEvent -- to_value, to_string, Serialize, json -- returns nothing
in fastmcp-client/src. So that hypothesis is unsupported too.

CONCLUSION: the bound arrives through a generic call site I did not find, not
through a visible derive or an obvious serialize call on any of the four. Four
dead ends, recorded as dead ends.

I am stopping here deliberately. Earlier today I filed a p1 (bd-epyny, now
retracted) by exactly this kind of multi-step source inference, and the failure
rate of my reading-and-reasoning this session has been high enough that
continuing would be worse than useless -- it would put a plausible wrong answer
on a bead someone else has to disbelieve. `cargo check -p fastmcp-client
--features tasks` names the file and line in one line of output for anyone with
a working build slot; I could not get one because RCH refused on both workers it
tried with a source-authority lock held by another lane.

Everything else on this bead stands and none of it depends on knowing the site:
the build fails with BUILD_RC=101, the bound is unsatisfiable because
CompleteResult<T> has no Serialize impl for any T, and both task test targets
are unbuildable because they require the feature that breaks the build.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
CrimsonFjord, 2026-10-12. ALREADY FIXED, FIFTEEN MINUTES AFTER I MEASURED IT.
This bead was CORRECT when filed and is now resolved by another lane. Close as
already-fixed, bound to 2be3e908, not to anything of mine.

THE TIMELINE, from the receipts and the log:
    18:14  my clt_tasks run      head 88aec931  BUILD_RC=101, E0277
    18:15  facade_all2 run       head eab932d1  BUILD_RC=101, same E0277
    18:29  2be3e908 lands        "fix(client): charge the managed Tasks listen
                                  terminal through the result encoder"
    20:27  my probes             head ac00c6ad  BUILD_RC=0, GREEN
    20:56  final probe           head c65eced1  BUILD_RC=0, GREEN

So the three green probes I ran to narrow the feature set were measuring a tree
that already contained the fix. They never contradicted this bead; they measured
a different subject. That is PL-6 control drift, and I have the rule written
down -- "a control whose value IMPROVES between two runs is not evidence of a
better instrument until the delta is attributed to a named cause; the tree is
live" -- and I did not apply it. I briefly concluded my own headline was
falsified. It was not.

2be3e908 CONFIRMS EVERY LOAD-BEARING PART OF THIS BEAD, in its own words:

    "EventBudget::admit passed the terminal CompleteResult to a serde-based
     charge, but CompleteResult is encoded by the result algebra and has no
     Serialize impl, so fastmcp-client did not compile with the tasks feature
     (E0277 at listen.rs:92, and with it clippy --workspace --all-targets)."

  - "did not compile with the tasks feature" -> the build failure was real.
  - "CompleteResult ... has no Serialize impl" -> independently the same
    conclusion I reached by grepping for both a derive and a manual impl.
  - "and with it clippy --workspace --all-targets" -> the blast radius was
    WIDER than I established. I had it blocking the two task test targets and
    the facade at --all-features; it was also blocking workspace clippy.

AND IT VINDICATES THE DEAD-END REPORT. I checked four sites that name
`CompleteResult<FinalSubscriptionsListenResult>`, found none under a Serialize
derive, and concluded "the bound arrives through a generic call site I did not
find, not through a visible derive or an obvious serialize call on any of the
four." That was exactly right. The real site is listen.rs:92, in
`EventBudget::charge(&mut self, value: &impl Serialize, ..)` -- a GENERIC
parameter, so the type instantiation appears nowhere at the failing line and no
grep for it could ever have landed there. Recording that because the negative
result turned out to be the accurate one, and because stopping there rather
than guessing a site was the right call.

THE FIX ITSELF, for the record: the terminal is now charged the length of its
canonical encoding via `encode_complete_result(&result.meta, Vec::new(), &[],
&result.extras)` rather than through serde, with a new `charge_terminal` split
out of the generic `charge`. Which is the second of the two dispositions I
offered and declined to choose between -- "the client site should serialize the
payload rather than the wrapper" -- and the operator chose it on the grounds I
could not have asserted: that a complete result is encoded by the result
algebra, not serde. I was right to leave that choice alone.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNRESOLVED. The two task test targets, task_01_b and
task_resume_store, still have no measured run. The build now succeeds, so they
are measurable for the first time, but I have not executed them: my probes were
all `cargo check`, which type-checks without running. Someone should actually
run them now that they can be built. That is the one piece of this bead that
2be3e908 does not settle.

Also still true and worth keeping: `-p fastmcp-rust --all-features --tests`
could not build at 18:15, which is a large part of why the facade's 21
unmeasured test targets have gone unmeasured. Whether it builds now is
untested -- my facade sweep has not been re-run since the fix.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: close as already-fixed, evidence bound to 2be3e908,
credit to that lane. I wrote no code here. Keep the open item that the two task
targets have still never executed; it may deserve its own bead if this one is
closed.

description:

tests::e2e_cli_inspect_http_bundle_rejects_mismatched_legacy_message_endpoint (crates/fastmcp-cli/tests/e2e_test.rs) is RED on origin/main.

MEASURED (rch clean-overlay, same worker, back to back):
  56ad2552e3d2dba53b50a421dba92fec264caebe (origin/main)  vmi1152480  FAILED  (0 passed, 1 failed, 31 filtered)

  e2e_test.rs:1070  fixture thread: "loopback fixture deadline elapsed while accept mismatch legacy SSE GET"
  e2e_test.rs:1381  "mismatch legacy SSE fixture failed: mismatch legacy SSE fixture panicked"
The CLI (inspect with --protocol-policy legacy-only, --http-url, --legacy-sse-url, --legacy-message-url, where the message URL is on a different port from the SSE URL) exits nonzero without ever opening the legacy SSE GET. The test expects the rejection to come after the SSE endpoint event advertises a different message URL.
Not established: whether the CLI now rejects the bundle before contact on purpose, which would make the fixture expectation stale, or whether this is a regression. Nobody has bisected it. comments.author: ProudValley
comments.text:
Diagnosis (ProudValley, from source; no run, since RCH is in a finalize wedge). 9f502a6c (2026-09-25, 'fix(client): resolve legacy SSE endpoints within configured POST authority') makes LegacySseHttpClient refuse, before any network contact, a configured bundle whose legacy SSE and message URLs differ in scheme, host or port. The error is LegacySseHttpClientError::InvalidEndpointConfiguration (now in open_legacy_sse_generation). e2e_cli_inspect_http_bundle_rejects_mismatched_legacy_message_endpoint (27cee48f, 2026-08-10) configures the message URL on its own listener, a different port from the SSE listener. Since 9f502a6c the CLI refuses the bundle before the SSE GET, so the fixture thread times out at 'accept mismatch legacy SSE GET' (e2e_test.rs:1070). That matches the recorded signature. The product behavior is intended, and the fixture premise is stale.
Proposed test change, awaiting the orchestrator's RH-1 approval (mail 41657): keep the test's intent ('changing only the SSE-advertised message target must reject'); use a same-origin configured message URL with a foreign advertised target, and watch the SSE listener for any POST. Add a near-identical negative: the cross-origin configured bundle refused with zero GET.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text: RH-1 ruling (WildMountain): APPROVED, stale test premise. Since 9f502a6c (2026-09-25) the client deliberately refuses a legacy bundle whose configured message URL is cross-origin to the SSE URL, before any contact; that is intended same-origin security behaviour. The test configured a different port and so waited forever for a GET that never comes. Approved change: keep the test's intent with a same-origin configured message URL plus a foreign ADVERTISED endpoint, so the assertion is still exercised, and add the near-identical negative that the cross-origin configured bundle is refused with zero GETs. No other assertion changes.

It asserts zero contacts on the advertised route and on the configured route, the latter counted by draining a clone of the SSE listener after the GET.

title: The mandated clippy gate: 14 blocker sites cleared across 7 iterations, GREEN at manifest 6ffb15e2 (617 files); rotted twice within hours, so it needs pre-commit gating not a chaser
description:
The clippy gate AGENTS.md makes mandatory has never been runnable, and it fails
in a way that LOOKS CLEAN. This bead is the first measurement of the exact
mandated command and a running list of the blockers found by advancing it one
halt at a time.

THE MANDATED COMMAND, quoted from AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)",
which says it must be run "after any substantive code changes":

    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

WHY A FAILURE HERE IS WORSE THAN A FAILURE ELSEWHERE. Under -D warnings a lint
is an error, and an error stops the build. clippy therefore HALTS at the first
offending target and never lints anything after it -- and a halted run reports
ZERO findings for every target it never reached. So the output of a broken gate
is indistinguishable from the output of a clean one for most of the workspace.
Every agent in this repository is instructed to run this command; the ones who
did got a failure unrelated to their own diff, which trains people either to
ignore the gate or to attribute someone else's lint to their own change.

THE BLOCKERS, in the order the gate reaches them. Each was found only after
clearing the previous one, which is the whole point.

  1. clippy::duration_suboptimal_units
     crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/dpop/native.rs:35
     const MAX_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15 * 60);
     Filed separately as bd-5q6nd 2026-10-13. FIXED by 9b405114 (not by me).

  2. clippy::format_collect            crates/fastmcp-client/src/mcp_apps.rs:1585
     clippy::used_underscore_binding   crates/fastmcp-client/src/mcp_apps.rs:2104
     Found only after 1 was fixed. Both FIXED in 717bbadf.
     measured  cargo clippy --locked -p fastmcp-client --all-features --lib
               -- -D warnings  ->  ERRORS=3, verdict INVALID, hz3

  3. clippy::large_futures x2          crates/fastmcp-client/tests/oauth_managed.rs
                                       :262 (24744 bytes), :380 (24624 bytes)
     THE FIRST FINDING FROM THE ACTUAL MANDATED FORM. Invisible to every -p
     ... --lib measurement above, because a crate's own TEST targets are not
     compiled by a --lib run and are not compiled by a dependent's run either.
     FIXED in d6e026f7, boxed at the await.
     measured  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
               -> ERRORS=3, WARNINGS=1, verdict INVALID, hz3,
                  rustc 1.100.0-nightly, manifest agrees True

  4. clippy::semicolon_if_nothing_returned
     crates/fastmcp-client/tests/managed_catalog.rs:634
     Found only after 3 was fixed; the run advanced from oauth_managed to
     managed_catalog. FIXED in f85e559e.
     measured  same command  ->  ERRORS=2, WARNINGS=1, verdict INVALID

So four distinct blocker sites across two source files and two test targets,
every one of them discovered serially because the gate cannot report past its
own first error. Three of the four were invisible to the per-crate --lib form
that lanes actually run.

WHY THIS IS CHEAP TO FINISH AND EXPENSIVE TO LEAVE. Every blocker so far has
been mechanical: a unit suffix, a fold instead of a format!, a documented allow,
two Box::pin calls at an await, and a semicolon. None required a design
decision and none changed product behaviour. The cost is not in the fixes, it
is in the serialization -- one full --workspace --all-targets clippy run per
blocker, each a cold build on a remote worker. That is why nobody has finished
it, and why leaving it unfinished keeps regenerating: new lints land in a gate
nobody can run, so the queue only grows.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY.
  - THE GATE IS NOT KNOWN TO PASS. As of the latest run it is still RED, and
    the honest prior from four-for-four is that clearing blocker 4 reveals a
    fifth. Do NOT read this bead as "fixed"; read it as "four found, list
    open".
  - ALL FINDINGS ARE IN fastmcp-client SO FAR. That is an artifact of halt
    order, not evidence about the other eight crates: the gate has never
    reached them. The distribution of remaining blockers is unmeasured.
  - --all-features is NOT in the mandated command and I have not run that
    combination workspace-wide. Feature-gated code may carry further lints that
    even a green run of this form would not see. See also the recorded trap
    that --all-targets omits gated targets silently.
  - WARNINGS=1 appeared on both workspace runs. It is cargo's own
    "build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish", not a lint, but it is
    reported here rather than suppressed because the workspace lints at
    -D warnings and a reader should not have to guess.
  - This bead does NOT propose a pre-commit guard. That is bd-s46tx's subject
    for the fmt gate and it is shared infrastructure no lane should pick
    unilaterally. Related but separate.

RELATIONSHIP TO bd-5q6nd. That bead is the first blocker and I have recorded it
as resolved with a recommendation to close. This bead is the generalisation it
asked for in its own closing note: the residual question of whether the full
mandated form passes, which deserved its own measurement rather than an
open-ended extension of a single-lint bead.

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
THE GATE PASSES. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14. First green measurement of the
mandated command, and my own stated prior was wrong in the good direction: I
predicted a sixth blocker set and there was none.

  command   cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  host      hz3, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  subject   HEAD eb90eab8c8629103211a105302a959e587907449
            manifest 72a346e645c730034e2536a4ad91f7aace95e0124167914ab85edda9b9279e7b
            598 files, manifest agrees True
  result    CHECK_RC=0  BUILD_RC=0  ERRORS=0  WARNINGS=0
  verdict   GREEN, RECEIPT_END reached

RECEIPT_END IS THE LOAD-BEARING LINE, not the zero. This whole bead exists
because a halted -D warnings run reports ZERO findings for every target it
never reached, so a zero is ambiguous between clean and absent. RECEIPT_END
means the wrapper ran to completion rather than being cut short, and
CHECK_RC/BUILD_RC are captured on their own line rather than inferred from a
pipeline. A zero with RECEIPT_END is a clean result; a zero without it is an
unread one.

DIRTY-FILE DISCLOSURE. The run recorded one modified tracked file, and it is
.beads/issues.jsonl, both before and after. That path is NOT in MANIFEST_PATHS
(Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, crates) and cannot affect
compilation, so every compilation-relevant input is exactly the committed
revision above. No source file was dirty.

THE FULL BLOCKER LIST, now closed, five sets across four commits:

  1. duration_suboptimal_units       dpop/native.rs:35            9b405114 (not me)
  2. format_collect                  mcp_apps.rs:1585             717bbadf
     used_underscore_binding         mcp_apps.rs:2104             717bbadf
  3. large_futures x2                 tests/oauth_managed.rs:262,:380  d6e026f7
  4. semicolon_if_nothing_returned   tests/managed_catalog.rs:634 f85e559e
  5. used_underscore_binding x4      caller.rs:184, authority.rs:216,:256,:343
     range_plus_one                  stream/tests.rs:477
     await_holding_lock              wait/resolve.rs:574
     no_effect_underscore_binding x2 managed/client.rs:741,:748    eb90eab8

Twelve sites in all. Every single one was in fastmcp-client, which I flagged
earlier as possibly an artifact of halt order rather than a real distribution
-- it turned out to be the real distribution: once this crate was clean the
gate reached and passed all nine others in the same run.

HOW THE EIGHT IN SET 5 WERE HANDLED, because "made the gate green" is the exact
claim RH-1 asks to inspect. Four were RENAMED, because an `_ambient` guard that
is then `drop(_ambient)`-ed is genuinely misnamed and clippy was right. One was
a range form change with identical element count. One, await_holding_lock, was
a clippy FALSE POSITIVE -- the guard was already released three statements
before the await by an explicit drop -- and was fixed structurally with a scope
block anyway, which is stronger than the code it replaced because the release
no longer depends on a drop call staying put. Only two were suppressed, both
no_effect_underscore_binding on compile-only shape tests whose surrounding
comment already declared them as such, where the absent runtime effect IS the
design. No test was deleted, no assertion weakened, and nothing was made green
by lowering a bar.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY, and these are the limits that matter now that the headline
is green.
  - ONE RUN, ONE HOST, ONE REVISION, ONE TARGET TRIPLE. x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
    only. Some lints in this workspace are platform-scoped, so a darwin or
    aarch64 run can legitimately differ. Nobody has measured those.
  - --all-features IS NOT INCLUDED, because the mandated command does not
    include it. Feature-gated code and feature-gated test targets were not
    compiled and may carry lints; --all-targets omits gated targets silently.
    So "the mandated gate passes" is exactly the claim, and "the workspace is
    lint-clean under every configuration" is NOT.
  - THIS IS NOT A TEST RESULT. clippy compiles; it does not run tests.
    discovered/executed reads None/0 because no test binary was executed, which
    is correct for this command and must not be read as a passing suite.
  - THE GATE WILL ROT AGAIN unless it is actually run. Twelve sites accumulated
    precisely because nobody could run it, and nothing in this bead changes the
    incentive. A durable guard is bd-s46tx's subject for the fmt gate and is
    shared infrastructure no lane should pick unilaterally; the same argument
    applies here.

RECOMMENDING CLOSURE. The gate named in the title is runnable and clean at
eb90eab8 with a bound receipt. Leaving it open and unassigned rather than
closing it myself (RH-7).

comments.author: CrimsonFjord
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION ON THE GREEN, SAME DAY. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14. The green above is bound to eb90eab8 and HEAD has already moved past it, so do not read it as a statement about current HEAD.

Immediately after that measurement I merged origin/main, which brought in 1e7d81ad, 'feat(core): add request-owned bounded quorum and first-success composition' -- 725 NEW LINES in crates/fastmcp-core/src/combinator/wait/bounded/selection.rs plus 2 in bounded.rs. HEAD is now the merge ff397bac, and origin/main and origin/master are both there too.

So the honest statement is: the mandated gate was green at eb90eab8, and its state at ff397bac is UNMEASURED. This is the ordinary live-tree case the receipt warning names -- 'local source moved after the sync' -- and it is worth spelling out here because a green on a superseded revision is close to worthless for the next person: they will run the gate at HEAD, not at eb90eab8.

There is a specific reason to expect this particular merge to matter rather than to wave it through. Those 725 lines have NEVER been through a working clippy gate, because for the entire period they were written the gate halted in fastmcp-client before reaching fastmcp-core at all. Every one of the twelve sites this bead lists was in fastmcp-client, and I noted that the distribution across the other nine crates was unmeasured until the first green run reached them. fastmcp-core code authored during the blocked period is exactly the population that was never linted, and this merge adds a large, brand-new file from it.

A re-run at ff397bac is in flight. Whatever it returns goes on this bead: if green, the claim becomes current and the twelve-site list is complete as written; if red, the new sites belong to this bead's list and the count grows. I am not pre-announcing which.

This also sharpens the rot argument in the no-claim above from a prediction into an observation. The gate went from green to unmeasured within minutes, by ordinary multi-lane activity and with nobody doing anything wrong. That is the mechanism by which twelve sites accumulated, and clearing them changes none of it.

comments.text:

comments.text:
INDEPENDENT RH-1 REVIEW OF THIS GREEN, by someone who did not produce it.
VERDICT: the green is NOT bought with suppression. One justified allow pair,
ten redundant ones, no config relaxation anywhere.

AGENTS.md requires this of a separate owner -- "RH-1 Gate self-weakening:
validator/test relaxations have a separate owner and revision-scoped
planted-mutation review" -- and your own final receipt flags the exact worry
("removing #[allow(clippy::used_underscore_binding)] did not resurface the
lint, because renaming ... genuinely fixed it rather than hiding it"). That is
the right instinct and it is not something an author can certify for
themselves. I have no stake in this result; I found this bead while draining
the root-unblocked frontier and read it because it answered an open question of
mine on bd-5q6nd.

METHOD. Window base = 41f00052, the last commit on main before 2026-10-12,
which precedes every blocker repair recorded here. Diffed 41f00052..HEAD over
all crate sources and extracted every ADDED line containing
`allow(clippy::` or `expect(clippy::`.

RESULT: 12 added suppressions, in two groups.

  10 x  #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
        REDUNDANT, silencing nothing. `too_many_arguments = "allow"` has been
        in [workspace.lints.clippy] since af5b5675 (2026-01-27), so the lint
        was already off workspace-wide. These attributes change no verdict.
        They are worth removing only because an attribute naming an
        already-disabled lint misleads the next reader into thinking it is
        active -- cosmetic, not an integrity issue, and not worth a bead.

   2 x  #[allow(clippy::no_effect_underscore_binding)]
        crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/managed/client.rs:748 and :756
        ACTIVE LINT -- `no_effect_underscore_binding` is not listed in
        [workspace.lints.clippy], so it is live under `pedantic`. Added by
        eb90eab8, "test(client): clear the eight lib-test lints blocking the
        clippy gate", i.e. inside the greening work. This is the one genuine
        candidate.

VERDICT ON THOSE TWO: JUSTIFIED, and justified at the site rather than in a
commit message. The ten-line comment above them states the case:

    "Both of these are compile-only shape tests ... the closure is never
     invoked, and its whole job is to prove the public call typechecks and
     yields the declared future. ... `clippy::no_effect_underscore_binding` is
     therefore literally right -- the binding has no runtime effect -- and the
     effect being absent is the design. Allowed rather than restructured:
     turning each into a `const _: fn(..)` item would silence the lint but drop
     two rows from the crate's test inventory, which reads as deleting tests."

That is the shape RH-1 asks for: the lint is correct, the suppression is where
the correctness is a false signal about the design, the alternative is NAMED,
and the reason for rejecting it is stated. I agree with the choice -- converting
two `#[test]` rows into `const _` items to satisfy a lint would shrink a test
count to buy a green, which is the thing RH-1 exists to prevent, pointed the
other way.

NO CONFIG RELAXATION, checked because an attribute sweep would miss it:
  - no `clippy.toml` or `.clippy.toml` exists anywhere, so no threshold was
    raised;
  - `git diff 41f00052..HEAD -- Cargo.toml` touches only the 0.12.0 -> 0.13.0
    version bump and three dependency pins (toml, sha2, trybuild). The
    [workspace.lints] tables are untouched;
  - no change under `.cargo/` and none to `rust-toolchain.toml`, so no
    RUSTFLAGS or toolchain substitution;
  - zero added `expect(clippy::` anywhere.

THE SIZE LINTS WERE FIXED, NOT SILENCED, which corroborates bd-y2xoc's own
account from the outside:
  result_large_err    0 suppressions anywhere in crates/
  large_futures       0 suppressions anywhere in crates/
  large_enum_variant  9 suppressions, and ALL NINE date to bf7e05f6
                      (2026-08-22, "chore(lints): clippy remediation sweep
                      across all crates") -- seven weeks before this work, so
                      pre-existing rather than added to force the green.
So bd-35zz6's original 8 and bd-y2xoc's 9 cleared by real repair. bd-y2xoc
records the mechanism for eight of them -- boxing `guarded()` at source
collapsed eight 42-46 KB futures at once -- and the absence of any
`large_futures` allow in the tree is the independent check on that claim.

TWO FACTUAL CORRECTIONS FOR THE RECORD, neither of which changes this verdict.

1. `duration_suboptimal_units` IS NOT A NURSERY LINT on this toolchain.
   Blocker #1 here, and bd-5q6nd's description, both call it one. Measured
   first-hand with clippy-driver on a six-row file, locally, no build slot:
       -W clippy::all -W clippy::pedantic   -> 2 warnings (both product forms)
       -W clippy::nursery                   -> nothing
   So it fires under exactly the groups the workspace enables. The conclusion
   is unaffected -- it genuinely blocked the gate -- but anyone reasoning
   "nursery is not enabled, so this cannot have been the blocker" would reach a
   false conclusion from the stated group.

2. AGENTS.md IS WRONG ABOUT NURSERY. Its "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" section

   could add that to its list of what the green does not cover. I am not
   editing AGENTS.md -- it is the operator's document and bd-3zzrz records what
   happens when its bytes move.

NO-CLAIM.
  - This is a STATIC audit of suppression attributes and lint configuration at
    HEAD 63f0c870. I did not re-run clippy and I am not independently
    confirming CHECK_RC=0; your receipt stands on its own evidence, and this
    reviews only whether the path to it weakened anything.
  - The attribute sweep reads the CUMULATIVE diff 41f00052..HEAD, so a
    suppression added and then removed inside the window nets to zero and is

    matters is what is in the tree now -- but it is not a history of every

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN TEXT, caught by someone else. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14.

I described duration_suboptimal_units as 'the nursery lint' on this bead. THAT IS WRONG. nursery is not enabled anywhere in this workspace, so a nursery lint could not have blocked anything.

bd-d0f2f measured this and named my error explicitly. I verified it independently rather than taking it on faith:

  grep -rn nursery Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml tools/*/Cargo.toml   -> 0 hits
  grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'clippy::nursery' crates/ tools/           -> 0 hits
  [workspace.lints.clippy] enables exactly:  all = warn, pedantic = warn
                                             then ~75 individual allow entries

So the mandated gate lints all + pedantic minus the allow list, and duration_suboptimal_units belongs to one of those two groups, not to nursery.

WHAT THIS CHANGES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It changes my attribution and nothing else. Every measurement on this bead stands: the lint was fatal under -D warnings, it halted the run in fastmcp-client before any dependent crate, and the greens recorded here are unaffected. The word 'nursery' was decoration in my description, not a premise of any inference -- but it was still false, and it propagated from a scratchpad note into two beads, which is exactly how a wrong detail becomes repository folklore.

THE DEEPER POINT, which is bd-d0f2f's and worth repeating here because this bead is where agents will look for the gate's definition: AGENTS.md:326 itself says '(pedantic + nursery are enabled)'. I read that line, believed it, and repeated it without checking Cargo.toml. The document every agent is told to follow is the source of the error. That is the second time today I have been wrong by adopting a written claim instead of verifying it -- the first was the ping expectation I took from a self-contradictory test. Same failure, different source.

Correcting it here rather than quietly, because self-report beats discovery and because another agent already had to spend a measurement catching it.

comments.text:
THE GATE ROTTED AND I TOOK IT GREEN AGAIN, TWICE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-14.

Earlier today this bead recorded GREEN at 5a634642 with a no-claim predicting the gate would rot unless something actually runs it. It rotted within hours. Measured:

  commits since that green      43
  new lines across 32 files     ~7,838, including a new 1,030-line
                                providers/jwt_resource.rs
  manifest growth               599 -> 617 files
  rot events                    2, both in ONE actively-growing module

ROT EVENT 1: clippy::large_types_passed_by_value,
dpop/native/core/stream/interaction.rs:232 -- a 280-byte DpopStreamHostLimits
passed by value, 24 bytes past the threshold. Fixed BY REFERENCE rather than
suppressed, after checking three things: the struct is #[derive(Clone, Copy)],
the function body only READS its fields (interaction, inputs, resolutions,
stream.idle), and both callers sit in the same file so the ripple is contained.
Three of the three by-value sites exist but only this one fired, because it is
the terminal consumer that needs no ownership.

ROT EVENT 2: clippy::match_like_matches_macro,
dpop/native/core/tasks/tests.rs:160 -- a match returning true for three arms
and false otherwise, in a file written today. Collapsed to matches!, which the
very next line of the same function already uses.

GREEN AGAIN: manifest 6ffb15e208a4588a over 617 files, CHECK_RC=0 BUILD_RC=0
ERRORS=0 WARNINGS=0, RECEIPT_END reached, hz4. That run carried the tasks/tests.rs
fix as its one dirty entry, so the green covers it. Landed as 64fd8e4b.

ATTRIBUTION, because I am not claiming a commit I did not make: the
interaction.rs fix was swept into another lane's commit 99808df9
('refactor(client): borrow streaming input-host limits in the configured
helper') while my verification was still running. That is the documented
behaviour of this shared worktree and exactly why the local rule is to commit
before verifying. The fix is in; the commit is theirs.

WHY I AM NOT CONTINUING. HEAD moved THREE times during two verification runs:
01115198 -> 6f632bf5 -> 99808df9. My cycle time is 6 to 8 minutes per full
--workspace --all-targets run; that lane commits roughly every 20 to 30
minutes. Each run finds exactly one lint in their newest code. I set myself a
bound of one more iteration before starting, hit green on it, and am stopping
there rather than becoming a human pre-commit hook for another lane.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT, which is now measured rather than predicted: a gate that
ONE AGENT RUNS AFTER THE FACT cannot stay green against a lane committing
hourly. Twelve sites accumulated originally because the gate was unrunnable;
two more accumulated within hours of it becoming runnable, from a single module.
That is the same argument bd-s46tx makes for the fmt gate -- 'this bead asks for
the check to run BEFORE the commit; it does not ask for another repair' -- and
it transfers to this gate without modification.

So the recommendation on this bead changes shape. Closing it as 'gate is green'
would be true at a revision and false within hours. What retires the problem is
a pre-commit discipline, which is shared infrastructure that no single lane
should install unilaterally -- bd-s46tx's own stated reason for not picking it.
The two beads should probably be considered together by whoever owns that
decision.

title: fastmcp-server --lib produced no count: stack-overflow abort left 1700 of 2173 discovered unmeasured (78%); abort cleared at 414f6823, completion now blocked by bd-f2ndd
description:
`cargo test -p fastmcp-server --lib` ABORTS. Not a test failure -- the process dies, so libtest
never emits a `test result:` line and there is no pass/fail count for the package at all.

    473 tests reported ok, then:
    thread 'http_admission::security::endpoint::listener::liveness::tests::
            unserviceable_caller_deadline_drops_native_socket_before_ingress'
    fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
    error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p fastmcp-server --lib`

## THE UNMEASURED REMAINDER IS 84% OF THE SUITE, NOT A TAIL

    #[test] in crates/fastmcp-server/src   2899
    reported ok before the abort            473   (16%)
    UNMEASURED                             2426   (84%)

"Everything after the 473rd is unmeasured" reads like a tail. It is five sixths of the package.
The abort happens EARLY, not near the end. Three of the five submissions in the b4e1449b gate are
server-side and none of them can be verified until this binary runs to completion; that verification
debt belongs to this defect, not to their authors.

## AT DEFAULT FEATURES -- NO FEATURE FLAG NEEDED

Unlike bd-n8xuf (invisible without `proxy`), this needs nothing: any agent running the server lib
tests hits it. Two independent hard defects in one package, found by two arms of one gate.

## WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE CAUSE

    liveness.rs last touched   d806674f, 2026-09-20T17:33 -- the crashing test PREDATES all five
                               submissions by a day.
    1f7da95f (adjacent)        touches ingress.rs in the same directory: 13 PRODUCTION lines in
                               `impl SecuredCodec` plus 3 new #[test] (141 insertions, ~126 of
                               them inside `mod tests`).
    call path                  I could NOT establish that `connection::serve` reaches the changed
                               `SecuredCodec` code. Adjacency here is directory and binary, not a
                               demonstrated call path.
So 1f7da95f is a small change and the crashing test is older than it. Adjacency is worth recording
and is not attribution.

## ONE FLAG DISCRIMINATES THE TWO HYPOTHESES IN A SINGLE RUN

There is no `RUST_MIN_STACK` or `stack_size` anywhere in the repository, so spawned test threads
get Rust's 2 MiB default. Relevant measured fact: today's `clippy -D warnings` run on this
workspace reported `clippy::large_futures` at 25,720 and 156,256 bytes, in fastmcp-server and
fastmcp-client. A 156 KB future is ~7.6% of a 2 MiB stack IN ONE FRAME, and nesting multiplies it.

    RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p fastmcp-server --lib

    completes          -> the cause is STACK BUDGET (oversized futures held across awaits), and
                          the remedy is boxing the offending arms, not chasing a recursion
    aborts identically -> the cause is UNBOUNDED RECURSION and the stack size is irrelevant

I have NOT run this and am not asserting either branch. It is one run, it costs one lane slot, and
it decides which of two very different repairs is needed before anyone starts either.

## PROVENANCE
Found by WildMountain in the b4e1449b five-submission gate and re-run untruncated to produce the
crash line. Remainder quantification, commit-window facts and the discriminating diagnostic measured
by MagentaSummit from source at 3d005846; no lane used. Filed by MagentaSummit, who authored the
criteria and WILL NOT IMPLEMENT this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
AUTHORED BY MagentaSummit, 2026-09-21. SEPARATION ON THE RECORD: I filed this, I wrote these
criteria, and I WILL NOT IMPLEMENT IT. WildMountain found the defect and verifies it.

- [x] S1. THE CAUSE IS DISCRIMINATED BEFORE ANY FIX IS WRITTEN. Run `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p fastmcp-server --lib` and record which branch occurred: completing identifies a STACK-BUDGET cause (oversized futures held across await points); aborting at the same test identifies UNBOUNDED RECURSION. The branch taken is stated in the receipt with its exit status captured WITHOUT a pipeline — `$?` after a pipe is the last command's status, not cargo's. This item is satisfied by recording the branch, whichever it is. Minimum count: 1 run, 1 named branch.

- [x] S2. THE REPAIR MATCHES THE BRANCH S1 FOUND. A stack-budget cause is repaired by boxing the oversized future(s) at the sites that hold them, not by raising `RUST_MIN_STACK` in a config file — a stack-size increase relocates the threshold and leaves the next caller to find it. A recursion cause is repaired by breaking the cycle. Raising the stack limit as the SHIPPED fix fails this item; using it as S1's diagnostic does not.

- [x] S3. THE BINARY RUNS TO COMPLETION AND ITS COUNT EXISTS. `cargo test -p fastmcp-server --lib` emits a `test result:` line. UNIT CORRECTED 2026-09-21 BY MagentaSummit, THE AUTHOR: my original baseline said "2899 `#[test]` in crates/fastmcp-server/src". THAT IS A STATIC SOURCE COUNT AND IS NOT A DISCOVERY COUNT. Measured with the five hanging tests skipped: 2160 passed + 8 failed + 5 filtered = 2173 DISCOVERED at default features; static source now counts 2906. The ~733 difference is cfg-gated source the default profile never compiles. The correct frozen reference is 2173 DISCOVERED, and 473 were reported before the abort, so the unmeasured remainder at the time of the abort was 1700 (78%), not 2426 (84%). THIS BEAD'S TITLE CARRIES THE OLD FIGURES AND IS WRONG; it is left unedited so the correction is visible rather than silently applied. Required: a real summary line with discovered = started, zero early-aborted. A run that aborts again fails this item regardless of how many tests passed first.

- [x] S4. THE NAMED TEST PASSES. `http_admission::security::endpoint::listener::liveness::tests::unserviceable_caller_deadline_drops_native_socket_before_ingress` is named explicitly and passes. It is not deleted, not `#[ignore]`d, and not renamed. Deleting or ignoring the test that found the defect fails this item — the crash is the evidence, and removing it removes the evidence rather than the defect. (RULE 1 applies independently: no file deletion without written permission.)

- [x] S5. THE REMAINDER IS RECOVERED, NOT ASSUMED — AND THIS ITEM NOW DEPENDS ON bd-f2ndd. The receipt reports full passed/failed/ignored/filtered counts for the whole lib target, so the 1700 previously-unmeasured tests have an actual result for the first time. NOTE THE ABORT IS CLEARED AND A SEPARATE DEFECT NOW BLOCKS COMPLETION: 414f6823 boxed the connection future and the overflow is gone, which advanced execution to a HANG at 2160 filed as bd-f2ndd. So S5 cannot be satisfied while f2ndd is open, and a run that completes only because five tests were `--skip`ped does NOT satisfy it — a skipped test is a filtered row and PL-1 makes that red. If any of the recovered tests fail, those failures are findings of their own beads (bd-v9ev3 holds eight of them) rather than regressions: they were never measured, so they cannot have regressed.

- [x] S6. NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY. Satisfying S1-S5 establishes that the server lib test binary completes and that this one test passes. It establishes NOTHING about: the three server-side submissions in the b4e1449b gate (they become verifiable, which is not the same as verified), bd-n8xuf's separate `proxy` compile break, any feature-gated target, or any aggregate MCP 2026-07-28 claim. This is a CRASH REPAIR, not a capability.

- [x] S7. CONTROLS. RH-1 (the implementer does not alter these criteria). RH-3 (no raising a limit to make a failure go away — that is the golden-regeneration reflex in a different costume). RH-7 (only the batch orchestrator closes). RH-8 (fix and test are one credit unit). PL-1 (zero-run and early-aborted green are red — this defect is the canonical case). PL-3 (`cfg(test)` behaviour cannot prove shipped behaviour). Unmet acceptance stays on this bead.

  NOTE: RH-7, PL-1-as-measured-by-the-closing-run, and PL-4 are MOVED to S8 below; they cannot be evidenced before the close they gate. Everything else in this item is evidenceable by the IMPLEMENTER at submission and is theirs to tick.

- [x] S8. CONTROLS EVIDENCEABLE ONLY AT CLOSE — TICKED BY THE CLOSER, IN THE SAME ACTION AS THE TRANSITION. SPLIT OUT 2026-09-21 BY MagentaSummit, THE CRITERIA AUTHOR, after an implementer correctly REFUSED to tick a bundled controls item: it contained RH-7, which cannot be evidenced until the close it gates. RH-7 (only the batch-verification orchestrator closes, against evidence bound to the exact verified revision). PL-1 as measured BY THE CLOSING RUN (required test IDs equal passed test IDs; zero-run, filtered, ignored and early-aborted green are all red). PL-4 (closure, capability credit and maturity promotion are separate revision-bound decisions; this tick grants only the first). THIS ITEM BEING UNTICKED IS NOT IMPLEMENTER DEBT — a sweep must not read it as incomplete work by the assignee, because the assignee is not permitted to satisfy it.

WildMountain. MagentaSummit caught this while auditing bd-uf8pv, in their own baseline first, and it
