comments.text:
REVIEW-QUEUE RECEIPT TRIAGE, measured 2026-10-06 at c3a9a544. This is the
"which of the 49 still has a bound receipt" question, and it had not been asked.
It matters because closing on an invalidated receipt is a false close, and
re-running them costs build slots that are already scarce.

TWO DIFFERENT TESTS, and they disagree. I ran both.

TEST 1 -- ANCESTRY. Does each cited commit still exist in HEAD history?
    315 distinct cited commit ids resolve
      263 ancestors of HEAD
       52 orphaned (resolve, not in HEAD history) -- 42 of them dangling and now
          pinned under refs/evidence/review-cited/, see the separate note
    14 of 49 beads cite at least one orphan

TEST 2 -- SOURCE MOVEMENT, which is the actual Code-First 4 condition
("relevant source movement invalidates it"). For each bead I took the union of
files touched by its own cited ancestor commits as its evidence scope, then asked
whether any of those files changed again between its newest cited ancestor and
HEAD.

    31 of 49 review beads have had their own touched scope move since they
    measured.

WORST FIRST (scope files moved / scope size, commits behind HEAD):

    30/35   308 behind   bd-mcp-fnd-04-a-jmi7        FND-04 implementation A
    22/22   271 behind   bd-19tqe                    client clippy size lints
    20/22   266 behind   bd-bi6mo                    SSE message caps vs LIMIT-01
    19/24  1013 behind   bd-mcp-auth-00-b-ykgm       AUTH-00 implementation B
    16/19   193 behind   bd-uf8pv                    server --lib no count (P0)
    15/17   172 behind   bd-4shqn                    TOOL-01 slice
    15/15   171 behind   bd-pgnvs                    client --lib intermittent
    13/13   262 behind   bd-to4cj                    catalog list expiry
    12/16  1022 behind   bd-mcp-auth-00-a-ry15       AUTH-00 implementation A
    11/11   289 behind   bd-k1yii                    508 unlinted production lines
    11/14   235 behind   bd-txf09                    cli inspect http bundle
    10/10   171 behind   bd-bb11e                    client lib test compile (P0)
    10/13   172 behind   bd-n3m6v                    6 intermittent server failures

bd-mcp-fnd-04-a-jmi7 is the one to notice: 30 of its 35 evidence files have moved
and it sits 308 commits behind. It is also one of FND-04's three unsatisfied
roots, so it is simultaneously the highest-leverage and least-bound receipt in the
queue.

STILL BOUND (scope moved = 0), i.e. cheap to adjudicate: bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-a-kkj8,
bd-mcp-leg-neg-01-b-y6od, bd-tls7a, bd-xstbj, bd-k03la, bd-onrqu, bd-uh133,
bd-kp4td, bd-1l88q, bd-35o84, and the eight beads citing no commit at all
(bd-3rnzv, bd-6ieg3, bd-7osjz, bd-ctcjd, bd-l6mz6, bd-mqn1l, bd-n3rha, bd-nelw9 --
those are unverifiable for a different reason: they name no revision, so there is
nothing to re-bind).

HOW TO USE THIS. It is a triage order, not a verdict. A moved scope does not prove
a conclusion wrong -- the behaviour may be unchanged and the receipt merely
unbound. It does mean the orchestrator cannot cite that receipt as-is, and should
spend slots in roughly the order above, cheapest-bound first, rather than by
priority alone.

METHOD LIMITS, stated so the numbers are not over-read. Evidence scope is proxied
by the files the cited commits themselves touched; a bead whose evidence is a test
RUN rather than a diff is under-measured by this. The 8-hex regex can miss
revisions written in other forms. "Newest cited ancestor" is by committer date,
which a rebase can reorder. And a bead citing many commits accumulates a larger
scope, so the raw moved-count is not comparable across beads with very different
citation styles -- read the ratio and the behind-count together.

PL-6 IS THE FIX, and it works. My own three submitted beads sit at 25 commits
behind with one scope file moved, and that file is one I changed myself. The
receipt survived anyway because I cited BLOB hashes, not just a commit: the gate
test blob 80fa29c5 and FEATURE_PARITY 8063b819 both still match the tree exactly.
Any receipt in the list above that had cited blobs would be adjudicable today
without a re-run. That is the concrete argument for PL-6 over commit-only binding.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE, 2026-10-05, and it sharpens this bead's consequence.

This bead is written around vacuous PASSES: a target whose file-scope #![cfg] is absent
prints "ok. 0 passed" and is counted as green. Today's work shows a second and worse
consequence: a dark target can harbour outright COMPILE BREAKAGE that no default-feature
gate can see.

HOW IT SURFACED. While implementing bd-c2uw3 I changed a public accessor
(Client/HttpClient/ClientSession::server_info -> Option<&ServerInfo>) and removed an
unreachable error variant. Two successive gates on the SAME revision disagreed:

  cargo check --workspace --all-targets                  -> 9 errors, all builder.rs
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features   -> 3 FURTHER errors:
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/mcp_config.rs:1560  HttpClientError::ModernDiscoveryMissingServerInfo
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/mcp_config.rs:1602  (same removed variant)
      crates/fastmcp-client/src/session.rs:1112     try_new arg type, bare ServerInfo

The first gate was GREEN on those three files. They are not merely untested, they did
not COMPILE, and nothing in the default lane could say so. e2e_protocol is the clearest
case: Cargo.toml :139-143 pins
    required-features = ["testing-lab", "legacy-2024-11-05", "tasks"]
so the whole target is skipped by default, and I could not even resolve what type its
`use fastmcp_rust::{Client, ...}` import refers to by reading the facade -- there is no
Client re-export at the facade root. That import's resolution is currently unverified by
any run.

reader can question. A dark target that does not compile prints NOTHING and leaves the
workspace reporting green, so the usual defence -- "check compiles before interpreting
test counts" (AGENTS.md batch-verify step 3) -- does not catch it either, because the
check itself is feature-scoped. PL-3 proof-configuration binding is the control that
applies: a gate's features are part of what it proves, and a default-feature green is
not evidence about a required-features target.

PRACTICAL NOTE for the orchestrator. --all-features is a cheap discriminator and found
all three in one run. It is not sufficient (mutually exclusive feature pairs still need
their own lanes) but it strictly dominates the default-only gate for this class.

closer.

title: Client SEP-2243 Mcp-Param-* emission is unreachable over loopback HTTP: ReviewedToolHeaders::new requires https, blocking 15 client-mode checks

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus55
comments.text:
THE LAST NON-AUTH CLIENT-MODE CLUSTER. Measured 2026-10-04: non-auth client mode is 38 of 53
checks passing, and ALL 15 remaining failures are this one cause, in scenario http-custom-headers.

THE CAPABILITY IS ALREADY BUILT, JUST UNREACHABLE HERE. This is not a missing feature:
  fastmcp-protocol::http_headers  AdmittedToolHeaderSchema, ToolParameterHeaderPlan,
                                  ProjectedParameterHeaders, ParameterHeaderBinding,
                                  encode_mcp_header_value, plus every bound
  fastmcp-client                  HttpClient::call_tool_with_parameter_headers, with
                                  stale-plan refresh-and-retry on a 400/-32020 refusal
  facade                          re-exported as modern::Client::call_tool_with_parameter_headers
  tests                           http_auth/rpc/tool_headers.rs asserts
                                  binding.header_name() == "Mcp-Param-Region"

THE BLOCKER IS ONE PREDICATE. crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_executor/parameter_headers.rs,
ReviewedToolHeaders::new refuses unless resource.scheme() == "https" (alongside no-userinfo,
no-fragment and length bounds). The harness serves http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp, so the plan cannot
be CONSTRUCTED in the scenario at all -- the adapter cannot work around it, which is why
conformance_client documents the gap instead.

FAILING CHECKS (all 15): sep-2243-client-supports-custom-headers ('Client called
test_custom_headers but sent no Mcp-Param-* headers'), plus sep-2243-client-mirrors-designated-params,
sep-2243-client-encode-values and sep-2243-client-base64-unsafe over Region, Priority, Verbose,
Debug, EmptyVal, Method, NonAscii, Whitespace, LeadingSpace, TrailingSpace, InternalSpace,
ControlChar, CrLf, Tab -- i.e. the ordinary, the percent/base64-encoded and the header-unsafe cases.

THE ARGUMENT FOR ALLOWING LOOPBACK HTTP. Mirroring parameters into headers exposes them to any
intermediary, so requiring TLS on a public endpoint is right. A loopback origin has no
intermediary, and this project already draws that exact distinction on the server side: the default
HTTP listener admits loopback Origin values for DNS-rebinding purposes
(is_loopback_origin / admits_origin). Permitting https OR a loopback http resource would make the
two sides consistent and make the shipped capability reachable in the official scenario.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST. It is a security predicate, and loosening it widens where parameter values
may be mirrored into headers. It is also a THIRD relaxation of this family; bd-p1ycz and bd-1koco
were each owner-authorized individually and this one is not covered by that decision.

NOT RELAXED HERE. RH-1 reserves validator relaxation for a separate owner with a planted-mutation
review. This bead is that request.

ACCEPTANCE IF TAKEN
- ReviewedToolHeaders::new admits https OR a loopback http authority (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, [::1]),
  and nothing else; userinfo, fragment and the length bounds stay enforced.
- RH-5 pair: positive, a loopback http resource yields a plan and the call carries the expected
  Mcp-Param-* headers; planted negative, a NON-loopback http resource is STILL refused with
  InvalidBinding, so the relaxation did not become 'any http'.
- conformance_client uses call_tool_with_parameter_headers for tools that declare x-mcp-header,
  with a review closure, and its module docs drop the 'not covered' note.
- http-custom-headers re-measured; expect the 15 to move.

comments.author: RealityCheck-Opus55
comments.text:
RESOLVED, BUT NOT THE WAY I PROPOSED -- and the other lane's design was better than mine.

commit: the shipped fix is a parallel lane's work, which I adopted in merge ddc2cb0a after discarding
my own. Adapter wiring is in the same area; my earlier measurement showed http-custom-headers going
3 passed/15 failed -> 18 passed/0 failed.

WHAT I PROPOSED: widen ReviewedToolHeaders::new to admit any loopback authority, including the DNS
name 'localhost', mirroring the HTTP transport's is_loopback_origin.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: ReviewedToolHeaders::new stays HTTPS-ONLY, and a separate explicit
constructor new_for_loopback_http admits ONLY canonical IPv4/IPv6 loopback LITERALS. DNS names --
'localhost' included -- are refused, along with IPv4-mapped IPv6, unspecified, private and public
addresses.

WHY THAT IS BETTER AND MINE WAS WRONG: 'localhost' is a DNS name. It can be rebound or overridden
locally, so it is not proof of a loopback peer, and a client choosing to mirror parameter VALUES
into headers should not accept a name as that proof. The opt-in constructor also keeps the safe
default safe instead of quietly loosening the predicate for every existing caller. My analogy to
the transport's Origin check does not hold either: a BROWSER sets Origin, so remote content cannot
claim it; nothing equivalent constrains a resource URL handed to a client.

My own test asserted 'localhost' WAS admitted, so it contradicted the shipped design and I deleted
it rather than merge a contradiction into the suite. Their loopback_tests module covers the same
ground more strictly.

Recording this because the bead's recommendation section is now wrong, and a future reader
following it would re-introduce the looser boundary.

managed_oauth variant copies whatever form exists at the moment it is written, and nothing makes the
omission of the accompanying test visible. The two questions WildMountain raised —
the missing pair, and the absent shared helper — are one question from two sides.

`dynamic/machine/interaction.rs:157-160` already documents the obstacle, and it is real:

    "This mirrors `managed_oauth::interaction::host_cancelled` in shape but not in type: that one
     yields `ManagedInteractionError`, this module's error is `ClientCredentialsInteractionError`,
     and the cancelled variant is nested one level deeper. The two cannot share an implementation
     without a conversion."

That comment is good work and is the starting point, not an obstacle to be argued past. The design
question is whether a conversion (a trait, a `From`, a generic) is worth the indirection for two
call sites, or whether the right answer is to keep them separate and make the DUPLICATION visible
instead. This bead requires the question be answered, not that it be answered a particular way.

self-resolved. Ruled on by WildMountain: do not amend, file forward. Authorship offered to and
accepted by MagentaSummit, who wrote n8xuf's M4/M5, found the gap, and WILL NOT IMPLEMENT this bead.

A serde "missing field `_meta`" and a -32603/-32600 code mismatch bear on payload shape and error
codes. Neither bears on whether two conversion helpers share a mechanism. The 16 that was reported
as "this path's tests" is xmvxs' workspace-wide failure TOTAL under proxy, joined by module PREFIX
rather than by module.

## P2: THEY STAY SEPARATE. THE REASON IS NOT "THE TYPES DIFFER" -- IT IS THAT UNIFYING WOULD CHANGE
## A VALUE.
I expected to find no shared mechanism available. That is wrong: the bridge already exists.
    From<ManagedCoreError> for ClientCredentialsCoreError          rpc.rs:67    -> Self::Protocol(e)
    From<ManagedInteractionError> for ClientCredentialsInteractionError
                                                                   interaction.rs:56 -> Self::Interaction(e)
    plus four more From<ManagedInteractionError> impls elsewhere in the client crate.
So "unify via From" is not a mechanism to design. It is available today and BOTH of B's arms
open-code around it.

BUT THE TWO ROUTES DO NOT PRODUCE THE SAME VALUE, and that is the finding:
    A  host_cancelled() -> ManagedInteractionError::Core(ManagedCoreError::Cancelled)
       lifted through From  ->  CCIE::Interaction(ManagedInteractionError::Core(Cancelled))
    B  host_cancelled() -> CCIE::Core(ClientCredentialsCoreError::Protocol(ManagedCoreError::Cancelled))
                                  ^^^^ Core, not Interaction
For the SAME input, A-lifted lands in `Interaction` and B lands in `Core`. Unifying them by routing
B through A's helper would silently move every cancelled checkpoint in the machine path from the
Core arm to the Interaction arm. That is a behaviour change wearing a refactor's clothes, and it is
exactly the class RH-3 forbids.

DETERMINATION: KEEP THEM SEPARATE. The duplication is real and the divergence is deliberate --
B classifies a cancelled checkpoint as a CORE/protocol condition, A as an INTERACTION condition.
Anyone proposing unification must first establish that those two classifications are interchangeable
for every consumer that matches on them. I have not established that and I am not asserting it.

## A DEFECT FOR P1 TO PIN, FOUND WHILE MEASURING
B's `host_error` does NOT call B's own `host_cancelled()`. It RE-INLINES the full
`Core(Protocol(ManagedCoreError::Cancelled))` expression in its cancelled branch. A's `host_error`
calls `host_cancelled()` directly -- that call was introduced by b902e419 precisely to remove this
duplication. So B carries today the exact duplication n8xuf removed from A, in the same family, and
a future edit to one of B's two copies drifts from the other with no compile error.
That is a concrete thing for P1's pair to assert rather than a style note.

## SEQUENCING, PER P3's OWN TEXT
P2's answer is "stay separate", so P3 must be BUILT FIRST -- otherwise this bead closes with a
recorded decision and no mechanism, which is the shape that permitted the original reintroduction.
I am not writing P1's pair yet. Next: P3's enumeration mechanism over the family.

title: Two production modules have no non-test consumer: fastmcp-transport HttpTransport HTTP/1.1 parser (168 tests) and event_store.rs (45 tests)
description:
Two modules are compiled into the shipped crates, carry substantial test suites, and
have no non-test consumer. Their tests pass, count toward the workspace total, and
prove nothing about any shipped execution path. Measured at HEAD 8d37ae48, 2026-10-05.

MODULE 1 -- a complete second HTTP/1.1 parser.
  crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs
    HttpTransport::read_request      :3650
    HttpResponse serialization       :3993
  Ungated production code. It is a real, careful parser: request-line validation that
  rejects non-HTTP/1.1, obs-fold rejection, token validation, duplicate-Host
  rejection, Content-Length + Transfer-Encoding conflict rejection, chunked decoding.
  168 inline tests plus crates/fastmcp-transport/tests/http_empty_header_values.rs.

  It has no non-test consumer. The live listener does not use it: BoundHttpServer::serve
  (crates/fastmcp-server/src/lib.rs:7406) accepts, then serve_http_connection (:12439)
  builds Framed::new(stream, native_http1_codec(..)) (:12449), and NativeHttp1Codec
  (:10819) wraps asupersync::http::h1::Http1Codec, delegating Decoder/Encoder
  (:10896, :10910) to the dependency. HttpTransport is a parallel synchronous
  Read/Write adapter, unreachable from bind_http.

MODULE 2 -- the SSE event store.
  crates/fastmcp-transport/src/event_store.rs   68 KB, 45 tests
    replay_bounded cursor paging  :594, TTL retention, per-stream caps
  Only `pub mod event_store;` (fastmcp-transport/src/lib.rs:45) and a facade
  re-export (fastmcp/src/lib.rs:785). Nothing else references it.

  Resumption is deliberately NOT wired, and the code says so:
    crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs:6891-6893
      "Exact MCP 2024-11-05 reconnects establish a fresh SSE endpoint lifecycle.
       Last-Event-ID is intentionally ignored: it neither replays messages nor
       selects or mutates session state."
  Locked by dual_era_endpoint_ignores_last_event_id_and_starts_a_fresh_legacy_stream
  (http.rs:13450). Client-side SseReader::last_event_id (sse.rs:1197) is recorded and
  never sent as a header.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT A DEFECT HERE.
  NOT a defect: the README does not claim SSE replay. README line 672 says "It does
  not reconnect or promise replay across disconnects." event_store is unclaimed
  library surface, not an overclaim. Same for HttpTransport: no README sentence says
  the listener uses it.
  IS a defect: roughly 213 tests exercise code that no shipped path reaches, which
  collides with the project's own PL-3 ("cfg(test) behavior cannot prove shipped
  behavior") in spirit -- here it is worse, because the code is NOT cfg(test), so it
  reads as production. A reader auditing "is the HTTP parser tested?" finds 168 green
  tests over a parser the server never calls. That is a live trap for the next
  auditor, and 213 tests of maintenance cost for zero shipped coverage.

NOT PROPOSING DELETION. RULE 1 forbids it and these modules may be wanted. The ask is
a recorded disposition per module, one of:
  (a) WIRE IT. For event_store, that means implementing Last-Event-ID replay and
      removing the comment at http.rs:6891 plus the test at :13450 -- a reviewed
      semantic change (RH-3: do not regenerate around the pinned behaviour), and it
      makes 45 tests load-bearing.
  (b) DECLARE IT UNCLAIMED. Add a module-level doc comment on each naming it as
      library surface with no in-tree consumer, and say so in the README's Limitations
      table so the next auditor is not misled by the test count. Cheapest honest option.
  (c) Move it behind a feature that is off by default, so its tests stop counting
      toward a default-profile total.

ACCEPTANCE requires naming the chosen option per module with a reason, and -- if (b)
or (c) -- a test or census assertion that fails if a non-test consumer appears later
without the disposition being revisited.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded disposition per module - wire it, declare it unclaimed in module docs AND the README Limitations table, or move it behind a non-default feature - each with a stated reason; if unclaimed or feature-gated, a census assertion that goes red if a non-test consumer appears later without the disposition being revisited; no file deleted
close_reason: ACCEPTANCE MET, independently verified by a non-author at commit:003ea8d78d96666ca58ece403f23626f04514719. Disposition work landed in commit:0d3c51e6. Disposition DECLARE UNCLAIMED named per module with reasons (event_store: wiring reverses a pinned Last-Event-ID decision, RH-3, belongs to the SSE-resumability owner; HttpTransport: misfiled, its one out-of-crate consumer is a cfg(test) fixture in fastmcp-server/src/auth.rs). Census assertions EXECUTED rather than merely present: run:cargo-test-p-fastmcp-xtask-readme_mechanical_claims on an RCH worker, remote exit=0, 11 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered out, PL-1 exact set equality with all 11 named individually. event_store_is_still_unconsumed_as_the_readme_says and http_transport_has_no_shipped_consumer_as_the_readme_says both pass and compare BTreeSets for equality rather than counts, so the consumer set cannot grow unnoticed. RH-5 sensitivity proven in the same run by four passing planted negatives, including planted_token_match_excludes_a_longer_identifier and planted_consumer_census_distinguishes_owner_from_consumer. README Limitations row present. No file deleted. NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this verifies the DISPOSITION, not the modules - neither is wired to any shipped request path and the ~213 tests over them remain unclaimed library surface, now machine-pinned so a later auditor cannot mistake them for shipped coverage. Gate ledger held history=[] and legacy_results=[] before this verdict, so no stale PASS was reused; the sole effective PASS is provider batch_verify. Full receipt in the preceding comment.

REMEDY OPTIONS (the implementer proposes; the bar author freezes the bar):
- (a) PREFERRED, TEST-ONLY. Replace the `serde_json::to_value` snapshot with a comparison that compiles and still detects a state change: e.g. the `Debug` rendering, or the accessor values the test already reads (`request_state()`, the input requests). The test's asserted property ("admission does not change state") must stay FALSIFIABLE, with a near-identical planted mutation that makes it fail (RH-5).
- (b) Derive or implement `Serialize` for `InputRequiredResult`. This is a PRODUCT change to a protocol type, needs its wire form checked against the codec, and is out of proportion for a test snapshot. Needs its own justification.

### GATE-EMA-READY — Aggregate complete EMA OIDC and SAML readiness

Outcome:

Prove complete Enterprise-Managed Authorization readiness by independently verifying and composing the AUTHX-01 OIDC/ID-JAG branch and AUTHX-04 SAML branch, without letting either inherit the other’s evidence.

Reason:

Enterprise policy and downgrade resistance must not inherit a passing
core auth claim accidentally.

Implementation:

- Aggregate AUTHX-01’s OIDC/ID-JAG branch and AUTHX-04’s SAML metadata, signed-assertion, binding, condition, replay, normalized-identity-provenance, exchange, and OIDC/SAML-isolation evidence. Both branches are mandatory and neither can substitute for the other.
- Aggregate Section 5.24's requested/IdP-granted/final-granted scope
  chain and required stage-two scalar-resource/explicit-nonempty-scope
  overlay, plus exact `EnterpriseClientIdModel`/
  `EnterpriseClientKey` tenant binding and the reviewed
  `ClientIdpRelyingPartyKey` cross-domain mapping. Also aggregate the
  independent `ResourceAsIdpRelyingPartyKey`,
  `ClientSessionSubjectKey`, `EnterpriseSubjectKey`, and revisioned
  `EnterpriseSubjectContinuityPolicy`; pairwise-subject equality is
  never a substitute for exact transaction correlation.
- Aggregate durable `IdentityAssertionUseStore` one-use evidence and
  revisioned `IdJagDisclosurePolicy` minimum-claim/default-deny
  evidence for the exact IdP/resource-AS pair, including retention
  across cleanup and policy-generation/skew changes.
- Require the identity-assertion replay evidence to name AUTH-00's
  `PersistentReplayDigest` purpose and exact framed issuer/token-digest
  context; the concrete `PersistentHmacSha256Backend`, immutable
  configuration digest, active/previous generation ring and rollout
  acknowledgements; the replay-store namespace and external monotonic
  restore-epoch authority; atomic all-generation alias reservation; and
  rollback/clone/fenced-retirement tests. A random process key, active-
  generation-only lookup, restorable empty namespace, or unnamed MAC/
  store artifact cannot open this gate.
- Aggregate one attested, immutable
  `EnterpriseIdentityPolicyBundle` snapshot and provider, including its
  canonical byte digest, reviewer/configuration authority, fencing, all
  three registrations and trust domains, tenant/client/subject-
  continuity policy, and the named read-only
  `EnterpriseSubjectMappingBackend`. Require a sealed mapping receipt
  bound to the exact flow and prove missing/conflicting mappings,
  backend failure, stale snapshots, or receipt substitution cause zero
  create/link/update/JIT mutation.
- Before any profile evidence is eligible, verify the exact ext-auth
  commit, enterprise-profile MDX hash, conformance commit, and
  enterprise-scenario hash from Sections 4.2/4.3. Independently verify
  all six enterprise identity byte inputs: ID-JAG `-04`
  `a59c1dffc0b5e59d1bd541276c6948eb9191f3b83685be5810a32e63effb4653`,
  identity-chaining `-12`
  `35b90e3e85c5e3e6f2ca15abcf2b70e968506ff7d00e7c7c77ec6ad861390c1c`,
  OIDC Core
  `4d016752a645e8a3c259baa4173b5a90cb6c82898ce868fc8444adde262a5aed`,
  OIDC Discovery
  `0401a07b35de50e914e195aa2c3c64cc4f6542464381c885d24a2623fbf75ec2`,
  OIDC Dynamic Client Registration
  `c151a4abab7704f2efa9b00530dcfeeefb3de6acbdbdf5ba05c9903f1de2a318`,
  and OIDC Enterprise `-01`
  `13832c150ecb7b8d31d08240214388cbfc4982142ecf4808c443014c573c868b`.
  Do not import the client-credentials MDX/scenario into this stable
  gate; GATE-OAUTH-CLIENT-CREDENTIALS-DRAFT-READY owns those artifacts.
- Freeze the AUTHX-01 branch subset as framework-redeemed OIDC ID-token input only.
  Aggregate the provider-proof and defensive ID-token checks, and
  prove OIDC-branch cross-input rejection of SAML, refresh-token subject exchange,
  RAR, actor, and subject-alias inputs. Require the manifest field
  `jose_algorithms=RS256-only`, exact OIDC
  `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` plus JWK intersection for
  the ID Token, and a separately evidenced issuer-bound
  `IdJagIssuerCryptoPolicy` plus ID-JAG-purpose-authorized JWK
  generation. Reject an invented ID-JAG algorithm metadata member or
  reuse of the OIDC field/key-purpose grant as ID-JAG authority, and
  reject every other algorithm before dispatch.
  Record disclosure-policy-approved optional bounded `email` as
  accepted-but-ignored, non-authoritative signed data, with no account-
  link or authorization use. The OIDC branch claims only the specified authorization-code front channel through a named external adapter; it makes no bundled browser UX claim and cannot parse SAML. AUTHX-04 supplies the independently verified SAML path.
- Independently aggregate AUTHX-04’s positive SAML branch: pinned metadata and bindings, bounded XML/signature processing, issuer/audience/recipient/time/condition validation, replay denial, normalized provenance, exchange, and negative OIDC/SAML cross-substitution. SAML success cannot borrow OIDC discovery/JWKS/nonce evidence, and OIDC success cannot satisfy a SAML category.
- Require the evidence manifest to name the concrete
  `EnterpriseIdentityAssertionBackend` adapter, version, immutable
  artifact/configuration, trust boundary, and complete passing provider
  conformance categories, including the typed HTTPS-GET serializer and
  closed browser-launch outcome plus named receipt verifier/key-rotation
  policy. The manifest binds
  exact method/authorization URL/request digest/flow/browser session/
  adapter generation and proves captured-wire equality plus zero reuse
  after any non-`Launched` outcome. A callback racing receipt attachment
  has bounded zeroizing-memory wait evidence and zero parse/persist/POST
  before the exact launch CAS. The manifest explicitly says the signed
  receipt attests only the admitted adapter's claim and independent wire
  capture supplies behavior evidence. It must independently name the concrete
  `OidcPendingAssertionFlowStore`, its FND-08
  `PersistentEnvelopeBackend`, namespace, fencing/cleanup policy,
  external restore-epoch authority, and complete call-order/CAS/
  restart/rollback/clone evidence. It must also name the concrete
  durable `IdentityAssertionUseStore`, artifact/configuration,
  persistence/failure domain, and restart/multi-instance conformance
  evidence. A trait implementation, process-local set, test fake, or
  unspecified deployment injection cannot open this gate.
- Require a concrete `EnterpriseCredentialCustodyProfile` naming both
  stage-specific provider artifacts/versions, immutable configuration
  digests, independently verifiable deployment attestations, trust
  boundaries, exact issuer/client/method/generation bindings, and
  zeroization/cancellation evidence. A raw context/env/CLI secret,
  plugin/renderer callback, browser/WASM or unattested desktop, self-
  attestation, or test-only secret adapter cannot satisfy this category.
- Aggregate the closed `EnterpriseIdpDisclosureEnvelope`, isolated
  token-exchange HTTP hooks/proxy/header policy, and capture/redaction
  proof. The IdP receives no final access-token response, MCP
  Authorization field, JSON-RPC method/name/params/result/content,
  catalog, SSE, task/progress/log, trace/baggage, cache, or arbitrary
  MCP metadata. Record that permitted OAuth audience/resource/scope
  and exchange timing/network metadata remain visible; this is
  application-layer minimization, not observer blindness.
- Freeze the stable deployment subset as issuer-bound preregistration
  for the Client↔IdP RP, Client↔resource-AS OAuth client, and
  Resource-AS↔IdP RP/subject-resolution relationship. Aggregate pre-
  side-effect rejection of URL-form CIMD `-01`, portable CIMD, and DCR
  independently at both OAuth/client-profile endpoints plus every
  dynamic/assertion-selected third-RP substitute, while preserving
  ordinary core CIMD `-00` behavior.
- Aggregate the exact `Disabled|Preferred|Required` fallback state
  machine and every reason×dispatch-state cell. Also aggregate the
  provisional `TokenExchangeStepUpRequired` terminal handoff: bounded
  optional `max_age`, dispatched-assertion consumption, no automatic
  backend/browser retry, no same-assertion reuse, no loop, no core
  fallback, and no RFC 9470 token-endpoint conformance claim.
- Aggregate the complete framework-owned OIDC lifecycle: exact discovery
  and registration intersections, endpoint-specific authorization-code+
  token-exchange grants plus the aggregate enterprise grants, sealed
  request field set, fixed HTTPS-GET query serializer, framework-minted/
  persisted capability before backend start, verified launch-receipt CAS
  before callback, exact callback/error admission and CAS, code
  redemption dispatch semantics, and the distinct exact-HTTP-200
  `OidcAuthorizationCodeTokenResponse`. Require query/fragment-free
  authorization/token/callback URLs for this subset; default query mode
  with omitted `response_mode`; `scope=openid` only on the authorization
  request and no `scope` on code redemption; exact public/pairwise
  `OidcSubjectNamespace` and preregistration-time sector evidence; closed
  callback error codes and Section 5.26's two token-error transports;
  preconfigured `tenant`; rejection of request `tenant`/`domain_hint`
  and ID-token `session_expiry`/initial client-RP `aud_sub`; no refresh/
  DPoP/JWE; access-token destruction; optional RS256 `at_hash`
  verification; nonce one-use; and fresh-flow recovery. Ordinary
  AUTH-03/AUTH-04 endpoint-query behavior must remain unchanged.
- Aggregate ID-JAG's shortened and full `application/` `typ` ASCII-case
  admission into one semantic variant, canonical lowercase shortened
  emission, parameter/whitespace/wrong-type rejection, exact case-
  sensitive issued-token-type URN, ASCII-case
  `N_A` admission with canonical emission, response-admission-time
  `expires_in` arithmetic, and the full typed
  `insufficient_user_authentication` status/error/cache disposition.
- Require one closed support-subset manifest enumerating, rather than
  implying, all stable limits: OIDC ID-Token input only; three exact
  preregistrations/no enterprise CIMD or DCR; confidential provider-
  backed Basic/secret-post only; exact one resource and one resource-AS
  audience; durable ID-Token one-use plus distinct-assertion recovery;
  RS256/`kid` with separate OIDC and ID-JAG trust authorities; optional
  claims validate-and-discard; exact subject namespace/sector evidence;
  preconfigured tenant with no hint and no `session_expiry` or initial
  client-RP `aud_sub`; preexisting subject mappings/no JIT; no
  SAML, bundled browser UX, refresh-subject, RAR, actor/`sub_id`,
  DPoP/`cnf`,
  ID-JAG refresh, or automatic step-up; and the exact typed terminal
  step-up behavior that is implemented.
- Preserve a separately passing ordinary core OAuth matrix.
- Record every available profile scenario/check by ID, role,
  transport, and result; reject skip-like success states. Record
  `auth/enterprise-managed-authorization` with Section 4.2's complete
  raw incompatibility vector and actual first rejection, never as
  passing conformance or an isolated ES256 result. Require a separately
  hashed one-variable algorithm negative and a nonempty RS256 real-peer
  positive matrix.

Acceptance:

- Required enterprise policy cannot downgrade.
- Preferred mode falls back only for an owner-approved preflight
  reason before assertion/credential/dispatch; the full failure×
  dispatch matrix proves every later state sticky and fail-closed.
- Activation proves the resource-AS ID-JAG-profile/JWT-bearer pair,
  IdP token-exchange/ID-JAG-requested-token pair, consistent client
  `grant_types` metadata, the IdP registration's authorization-code+
  token-exchange authority, the resource-AS registration's JWT-bearer
  authority, and exact provider-backed Basic/secret-post registration
  on both exchange stages.
- All three RP/OAuth relationships are issuer-bound preregistrations;
  URL-form/portable CIMD and DCR are explicit stable-profile exclusions
  on both client-registration sides, and no dynamic third-RP substitute
  is admitted, without changing ordinary core CIMD `-00`.
- The named `EnterpriseCredentialCustodyProfile` and both attested
  provider artifacts are nonempty passing evidence; a raw/test-only
  secret source or self-attested environment cannot open the gate.
- Core OAuth remains independently operable.
- Profile-specific documentation has evidence.
- The aggregate manifest contains independent revision-bound `ema_oidc_branch` and `ema_saml_branch` records. The OIDC record retains `identity_assertion_input=oidc_id_token`, `jose_algorithms=RS256-only`, its external-adapter/no-browser boundary, and its refresh/RAR/actor exclusions; the SAML record binds AUTHX-04 parser, signature, audience, replay, provenance, and exchange evidence. No aggregate `saml_supported=false` or OIDC-only identity-assertion value is valid, while identifying policy-approved
  optional `email` as ignored/non-authoritative rather than
  unsupported.
- The manifest separately identifies OIDC ID-token algorithm metadata
  and the out-of-band ID-JAG issuer/key-purpose policy, and carries all
  six identity-input hashes plus the enterprise MDX/scenario pins.
- First-stage cache handling is role-correct, and `cnf`, DPoP,
  JWT-DPoP, public `none`, and every sender-constrained claim are
  absent or rejected before dispatch/use.
- Requested, signed, and final scopes do not broaden; the stage-two
  resource/scope overlay is exact HTTP 200, committed, and never
  cached; the built-in response emits both no-cache fields. Global/
  tenant-scoped client IDs cannot cross tenant registrations.
- IdP-domain and resource-domain client IDs may differ or share text
  only through the exact revisioned mapping; stage credentials and
  assertion audiences/client claims cannot be swapped.
- Client↔IdP and Resource-AS↔IdP relying-party registrations are
  independent, and end-to-end subject continuity survives differing
  pairwise `sub` values only through the exact correlated exchange and
  revisioned continuity policy.
- Both RP subject-type/sector-policy generations and the distinct
  `ClientFacingSubjectId`, `ResourceFacingSubjectId`, and
  `ResourceAudienceSubjectId` namespaces are evidenced. OIDC subject
  grammar/lifetime rules hold, and missing preexisting account mappings
  cause zero JIT/create/link/update mutation.
- The OIDC authorization/token/callback URLs are query/fragment-free in
  this sealed subset, the authorization request omits `response_mode`
  while using the default query response, and only that request carries
  `scope=openid`; ordinary core OAuth endpoint-query handling remains
  independently green. The selected subject namespace/sector review and
  tenant disposition are exact, and neither `domain_hint`,
  `session_expiry`, nor an initial client-RP `aud_sub` can alter the
  flow, session lifetime, or resource-facing subject namespace.
- The same validated ID Token cannot be reacquired after dispatch
  across flows, sessions, workers, or restart, and unapproved optional
  ID-JAG claims never cross the redemption boundary.
- The OIDC pending-flow store and envelope backend prove
  framework-owned generate/persist-prepared/start/verify-and-attach-
  launch-receipt/callback/CAS/redeem order, byte-exact GET wire binding,
  restart/rollback/clone resistance, no reuse after uncertain launch,
  and terminal secret destruction.
  The durable assertion-use store proves all-generation persistent-MAC
  replay denial under rotation and restore.
- One attested policy-bundle snapshot and sealed read-only mapping
  receipt bind every registration/tenant/continuity decision to the
  exact flow; stale policy, missing mapping, or backend ambiguity cannot
  mutate identity state.
- A step-up response is a bounded terminal handoff, consumes the
  dispatched assertion, and cannot trigger assertion reuse, an
  automatic browser/backend loop, or ordinary-OAuth fallback.
- IdP-facing application data is limited to the closed disclosure
  envelope. The evidence neither forwards final access-token/MCP
  traffic nor overclaims concealment of resource/scope semantics or
  token-exchange traffic metadata.
- Public authorization-server metadata is invariant across issuer/
  tenant/client trust sets, and no public trust-acceptance discovery
  or ordinary error becomes an issuer allowlist oracle.
- The client, IdP, and resource AS have an explicit recorded
  trust-domain tuple; the issuing IdP and redeeming resource AS are
  distinct (or have recorded isolated customer-boundary proof for
  shared software), while the client may share the IdP domain.
  Target-bound ID-JAGs cannot be reused at a downstream resource AS.
- An expected rejection of the raw multi-cause upstream enterprise
  scenario cannot satisfy either the isolated-algorithm or independent
  RS256 positive-evidence category.
- The emitted stable-subset manifest enumerates every included
  restriction/exclusion from the implementation bullet and fails
  closed on an omitted, contradictory, or broadened field.

- Complete EMA readiness cannot be inferred from only one branch or from a global no-SAML exclusion.

  missing-header diagnostic/no-cache-write, invalid other-2xx/cacheable
  responses, and global/tenant-scoped

  differing-pairwise-sub positive, coincidentally-equal-sub

  authenticated admin-diagnostic isolation.

title: Facade default build red for three days: E0616 private-field reads from a sibling module branch (FIXED)
description:
THE FACADE'S DEFAULT BUILD HAS NOT COMPILED SINCE 2026-10-15T18:39:25-04:00
(bac23825), three days, while the client crate's own default check stayed
green the whole time. Found by a real compile, not by reading. A one-file fix
is applied in the same change as this report.

THE FAILURE, verbatim from the run (RCH worker vmi1227854, build source
a22c9b516de3725fac1b2d00cf25a84669e858b4-dirty, remote exit=101):

  error[E0616]: field `request` of struct `core::tasks::DpopTaskOperation` is private
    --> .../core/stream/task_subscription/watch/input/start.rs:59:29
  error[E0616]: field `discovery_id` ... is private   (same file :63:19)
  error[E0616]: field `operation_id` ... is private   (same file :64:26)
  error: could not compile `fastmcp-client` (lib) due to 3 previous errors

WHY IT IS A MODULE-BRANCH PROBLEM, not a missing `pub`. A child module may
read private fields of an ANCESTOR. `DpopTaskOperation` is defined in
`core/tasks.rs`, so `core/tasks/wait.rs:444-445` and
`core/tasks/driver/start.rs:42,52` read `.request`, `.discovery_id` and
`.operation_id` directly and compile correctly -- they are descendants. The
broken file is `core/stream/task_subscription/watch/input/start.rs`, a SIBLING
branch, which cannot. `core/tasks/driver/start.rs:42` contains the identical
`matches!(&operation.request, ManagedTaskRequest::CallTool { .. })` check, so
this reads as a copy of a working in-branch helper into a module where the
privacy no longer resolves.

THE CODE COULD NEVER HAVE COMPILED, which rules out "a later commit made the
fields private". At bac23825 -- the commit that ADDED this file and its
`pub mod start;` -- the struct already read
`discovery_id/operation_id/request` with no `pub`, and
`git log -S 'pub request: ManagedTaskRequest'` on that file returns nothing,
so the field has never been public. The field block's last change is 81d3c7bc
(2026-10-14T09:04), a day BEFORE the consumer landed.

AND HERE IS WHY NOBODY SAW IT FOR THREE DAYS -- the feature sets differ
between the two crates:

  crates/fastmcp/Cargo.toml        default = ["legacy-2024-11-05", "tasks"]
  crates/fastmcp-client/Cargo.toml default = ["legacy-2024-11-05"]

and `pub mod task_subscription;` in `core/stream.rs` is `#[cfg(feature =
"tasks")]`. So:

  cargo check -p fastmcp-client        default -> task_subscription NEVER
                                      COMPILED -> GREEN, correctly, all along
  cargo check -p fastmcp-rust          default -> tasks is ON -> the broken
                                      file compiles -> RED since bac23825

The owning crate's own default check cannot see the breakage; only a build
that turns `tasks` on can. That asymmetry is the entire reason this survived
three days of active work in this subtree. It also means my own earlier
verification of an unrelated fix (`cargo check --locked -p fastmcp-client
--lib`, reported green) was green for what it compiled and simply blind here
-- a feature-set blind spot, not a false reading.

SEVERITY. `tasks` is a DEFAULT feature of the published facade, which is the
crate AGENTS.md says most users depend on. So this is the default build of the
shipped artifact, not an exotic configuration.

THE FIX APPLIED, minimal and in one file:
`core/tasks.rs` now declares `discovery_id`, `operation_id` and `request` as
`pub(crate)` instead of private, with a comment recording that readers exist on
both sides of the subtree. `reviewed_headers` stays private because only
`core/tasks.rs` reads it, and widening it would grant crate-wide reach nothing
asks for. This changes NO published API: the fields remain crate-internal, so
the struct's outside surface is identical.

THE ALTERNATIVE I DID NOT TAKE, recorded so the owning lane can prefer it:
add `pub(crate)` accessor methods to `DpopTaskOperation` and change the three
reads in `watch/input/start.rs`. That is the more encapsulated shape and the
struct currently has NO accessors at all (only `new` and
`with_reviewed_tool_headers`), so it would be a new pattern. I chose the
visibility change because it touches only the defining file and leaves the
three-day-old consumer in the fastest-moving subtree of this workspace
untouched, which is the lower-conflict intervention while other lanes are
active in it. Either fix is correct; this one is reversible in one line if the
owner wants accessors.

NOT IN SCOPE, stated rather than silently skipped: whether
`watch/input/start.rs`'s LOGIC is right. I made it compile; I did not review
what it does, and this bead claims nothing about its behaviour.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. `cargo check -p fastmcp-rust` with DEFAULT features reaches a `Finished`
     line with zero errors. A green `-p fastmcp-client` default check does NOT
     satisfy this, for the reason above.
  2. The receipt names the feature set, because a count or a green without one
     is not evidence here.
  3. A guard that would have caught this: some routinely-run target must
     compile the crate with `tasks` ON. Today none appears to, which is the
     real defect behind the defect.

NO-CLAIM. The compile failure and the fix are both from a real run / real
edit; the verification of the fix was still in flight when this was filed, so
this bead does not assert the fix is green. The three-day window is derived
from commit timestamps and feature-set reading, not from a run at each
intermediate revision.

comments.text:
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF THE APPLIED FIX. CrimsonFjord 2026-10-19. Evidence only -- I did not write this fix, am not assigned, and am not closing it (RH-7).

  command   cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets --profile test
  host      hz4, rustc 1.100.0-nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  subject   HEAD 02b7dfc907682cd866a8059f13082037dfdde5f4

            and not a compilation input, so every compiled input is exactly
            the committed revision
  result    CHECK_RC=0 BUILD_RC=0 ERRORS=0 WARNINGS=0, RECEIPT_END reached
  verdict   GREEN

WHY A CHECK IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT FOR BOTH OF THESE, rather than a weaker substitute for a full build. E0616 (private field) and E0063 (missing struct-literal field) are both resolved during type checking, so cargo check observes exactly the condition each bead reports. --profile test compiles the cfg(test) modules, which is what makes the client lib TEST target part of the subject rather than only its lib.

I also confirmed the facade fix by reading before running, rather than trusting the FIXED label: DpopTaskOperation at core/tasks.rs:59 now declares discovery_id, operation_id and request as pub(crate), while reviewed_headers stays private -- so the sibling-branch reads in
core/stream/task_subscription/watch/input/start.rs:59,63,64 resolve, and nothing was widened beyond what the consumer needs.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated so the green is not overread:
  - CHECK, NOT LINK. cargo check does not link, so this says nothing about
    whether the affected targets BUILD to completion. That matters in this
    repository: linking the facade binary-bearing targets under --all-features
    currently fails on the fleet (bd-8d61j, extended). For these two beads it
    is immaterial, because both reported errors are type-level, but a reader
    should not take GREEN here as a build.
  - DEFAULT FEATURES. --all-targets omits required-features targets SILENTLY,
    so the 19-plus gated integration targets are outside this subject. Both
    beads concern the facade DEFAULT build and the client LIB test target, and
    both are inside it.
  - ONE run, ONE host, no repeat. A deterministic compile error is expected to
    be deterministic, but I did not repeat it.
  - This is a COMPILE verdict only. It is not a test result: no test binary
    was executed and no count was produced.

The instruction was to apply b902e419's repair at both sites. b902e419's `host_cancelled()` returns
`ManagedInteractionError`. THIS module's error is `ClientCredentialsInteractionError`, and its

            ManagedInteractionError::Core(ManagedCoreError::Cancelled) }
    dynamic/machine/interaction.rs (this file), mirroring its OWN host_error branch
        fn host_cancelled() -> ClientCredentialsInteractionError {

So the existing helper is neither REACHABLE (private to a sibling module) nor TYPE-CORRECT here.
Copying it verbatim would not have compiled either. I derived the body from this file's own
`host_error` cancellation branch, so the two agree on the disposition by construction rather than by
my judgement.

    all checkpoint().map_err sites in the crate                   25, every one now a closure form
        -- 23 of them ALREADY were, so this restores house style rather than inventing one
    the three named types in scope in this file    yes, 13 / 3 / 3 existing uses
    brace balance 0, lexer parses

Formatting: the file was already fmt-non-clean at HEAD and still is. I deliberately did NOT run
rustfmt over it -- that would rewrite hunks outside my change in a file counted by DEP-02b's 188,
which is someone else's measurement.

The two modules open-code it and a third will copy it again -- that part of the concern is right, and
this bead IS the third copy arriving. But a shared helper is the wrong remedy because THE TWO
CALLERS DO NOT SHARE A RETURN TYPE. A plain `fn` cannot serve both; it would need a generic bound or
a `From<CancelledError>` per error type, and either one is a wider change than the duplication costs.

  `ManagedInteractionError`. Then `ctx.checkpoint()?` works directly at every site with NO map_err
  and NO helper, and the next module that copies this pattern gets the conversion for free instead of
  copying a third `host_cancelled`. That deletes the class rather than centralising it.

  beads may bind. It wants its own bead and its own owner.

title: MRTR continuation recovery admits an uncertain dispatch as Interrupted: is that the auto-retry ahet.37 forbids?
description:
Finder: RoseStream (rulings #32, 3r1d conflict 3 option (ii)). Filed for its owner. Unassigned on purpose.

QUESTION: does MRTR continuation recovery, after an UNCERTAIN dispatch, perform the automatic retry that ahet.37 forbids? ahet.37's text says "Do not auto-retry non-idempotent calls after uncertain disconnect" and "An uncertain disconnect returns a retry classification, not a silent retry".

FACTS (static, at HEAD 4fd55eab):
- crates/fastmcp-client/src/http_auth/rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:347 `recovery_http_interruption` classifies ResponseBodyReadFailed and Transport(Io | HttpError(Io)) as Interrupted. recoverable_transport_failure (:342) turns that into ContinuationRecoveryError::Interrupted, which drives continuation recovery.
- The same classifier is used by http_auth/discovery/client_credentials/rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:356 and http_auth/managed/tasks/watch/recovery.rs:324.
- Authorship: 35050222+Dicklesworthstone (5d211aae, 5290820d).
- bd-mcp-http-03-b-3r1d adds ModernHttpExecutorError::DispatchUncertain(ClientError) for a pre-head failure after a request byte was sent. Per rulings #32 (i), recovery_http_interruption was extended to treat DispatchUncertain(Io | HttpError(Io)) exactly as Transport(Io) was treated. So recovery behaviour is UNCHANGED by 3r1d, and this question is left open, not answered.

WHAT DECIDES IT (for the owner): whether a continuation recovery request resends a side-effecting operation, or only re-reads state keyed by requestState/idempotently. If it resends, recovery after DispatchUncertain is the forbidden auto-retry, and the classifier should stop admitting DispatchUncertain. If it only re-reads, it is safe, and the reason belongs in a comment at :347.

NO-CLAIM: no defect is asserted. This is an unanswered contract question with a named decision point.
close_reason: Verified by run:v-b5-client-feat at commit:4866e670. evidence: Question answered NO by site-level reading (RainyGrove, comment on bead): recovery.rs:347/:356 make at most one POST and return Interrupted; only an explicit recover() under a ContinuationReplayContract re-POSTs (no product caller); the watch recovery loop re-reads listen/tasks/get only and returns update errors to the caller. Rationale recorded in code by commit:5a41d896; client run v-b5-client-feat at 4866e670 (includes it) compiles and passes the lib apart from one unrelated, since-fixed test.

comments.author: RainyGrove
comments.text:
ANSWER: No. None of the three sites auto-retries a non-idempotent call after an uncertain dispatch.
- rpc/interaction/recovery.rs:347 and client_credentials rpc recovery.rs:356: send()/recover() each make at most one POST. failed() returns ContinuationRecoveryError::Interrupted (the retry classification ahet.37 asks for) and leaves the phase Recoverable. A re-POST happens only when the host explicitly calls recover() under a ContinuationReplayContract, whose journal must answer from its capture. No product code calls recover().
- managed/tasks/watch/recovery.rs:324 loops automatically, but only to reopen listen and re-read tasks/get. The tasks/update round runs through execute_round(..)? (drive.rs), so its errors, DispatchUncertain included, go to the caller after progress.begin() records the uncertainty. The client_credentials watch has the same structure.
Reason recorded as a comment at the classifier in 5a41d896. No behaviour change, so no new test; tests.rs:122 already pins the classification.

comments.text:
PER-AREA DIAGNOSTIC FOR A1/A3 -- FOUR AREAS, FOUR GENUINELY DIFFERENT CAUSES. NOT A VERDICT.
WildMountain at HEAD 4ce3d3cc. One representative per area, --nocapture, full log retained.
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed; 0 ignored; 2169 filtered out; finished in 0.51s
    4 + 2169 = 2173, the same denominator as the 2160/8/5 run. Consistent, deliberate selection.

  (a) listener/liveness.rs:111:72
      called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Cancelled(CancelReason { kind: User,
      origin_region: RegionId(0:0), origin_task: None, timestamp: Time(1000000000ns),
      message: Some("join channel closed"), cause: None, ... })
      A join channel closed and the cancellation was unwrapped rather than handled. Note
      timestamp Time(1000000000ns) -- exactly 1s, which looks like a virtual clock, not wall time.

  (b) revalidation.rs:358:13
      assertion `left == right` failed
        left: Time(499454500ns)    right: Time(0ns)
      THE STRONGEST LEAD OF THE FOUR. The test expects Time(0) and gets ~499ms of real elapsed
      time. That is the signature of a clock that was supposed to be virtual reading as wall
      clock. Both revalidation failures are deadline/expiry tests, which is consistent. Worth
      checking against the known asupersync behaviour where Cx::now falls back to the wall clock
      -- I am naming that as a lead to test, NOT as a diagnosis.

  (c) oidc.rs:2545:16
      called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ServerError { description_len: 60 }

  (d) tests.rs:6149:14
      "fastmcp extension callback panicked; panic payload redacted"
      nested tool call should succeed: McpError { code: InternalError,
      message: "Internal server error", data: None }

== THE OBSTACLE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU START: TWO OF THE FOUR ARE REDACTED ==
(c) and (d) do not tell you what went wrong, by design. `ServerError { description_len: 60 }` is a
Debug impl that prints the LENGTH of its description instead of the description. (d) says outright
"panic payload redacted" and then surfaces a generic "Internal server error" with data: None.

So A3 is satisfiable for all four -- file:line and the firing assertion are in hand -- but the ROOT
CAUSE of (c) and (d) is not reachable from the test output at all. Expect to need a temporary local
unredaction, a backtrace, or a different observation point for those two. Do not read the generic
InternalError in (d) as the cause; it is the redaction speaking. And do not let a redacted
comparison satisfy you that two things differ in the way you assumed -- a Debug that prints a length
makes an equality check look meaningful while carrying no information about the contents.

== THIS CONFIRMS A1's PREMISE RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT ==
An unwrapped cancellation, a clock equality, a redacted server error, and a redacted extension-
callback panic are four different failure mechanisms. There is no single story here, and I would
reject one offered for all eight. The ctx 2x2 (A2) is still open -- I ran only ONE of those four,
so whether they are one defect or four is genuinely undetermined and remains yours to resolve.

== STANDING PROXY COMPILE GATE, NEW THIS TICK AND PERMANENT ==

installs a budget, not a timer driver. So `cx.now()` reads WALL TIME and the ~499ms is the real
elapsed time of the run up to that point -- which also explains why this is the failure most likely
to move between runs while the other three do not.
The neighbouring assertion at :359 mixes the two clocks in one expression --
`cx.now() < lease.next_check && Instant::now() < lease.wall_expiry` -- so it reads as though one is
virtual and one is wall, when today both are wall.
CONFIRMS THE SECOND REVALIDATION FAILURE TOO, WITHOUT ASSUMING IT: the sibling test is
`monotonic_wall_expiry_still_triggers_when_the_caller_clock_does_not_move`. Its premise is that the
caller clock DOES NOT MOVE. On a wall-clock fallback it moves, so the premise is false by
construction. Same cause, and I am saying so because A1 requires the explanation to PREDICT the
area's observed failure rather than merely cover it.

=== THE FIX IS ADDITIVE AND DOES NOT ENGAGE A6 ===
A6 forbids retiring a failure by weakening an assertion, widening a bound, or #[ignore]. The repair
here does the opposite: it makes `assert_eq!(cx.now(), Time::ZERO)` TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION by giving
the test the virtual clock it already assumes. The assertion is untouched and becomes stronger,
because a wall-clock regression would then fail it again.
THE IDIOM IS ALREADY IN-TREE -- crates/fastmcp-server/src/proxy.rs at 13802, 14594, 15238, 15520:
    let clock = Arc::new(asupersync::time::VirtualClock::new());
    let runtime = asupersync::runtime::RuntimeBuilder::current_thread()
        .blocking_threads(0, 0)
        .with_timer_driver(asupersync::time::TimerDriverHandle::with_virtual_clock(
            Arc::clone(&clock)))
        .build().unwrap();
    // then drive time explicitly:  clock.advance(100_000_000);
So this restores house style rather than inventing one, the same shape as v2x7g's 23-of-25.

=== A7 IN ADVANCE: (b) IS LOAD-SENSITIVE AND I AM NAMING IT NOW ===
The observed value is elapsed wall time, so it varies with machine load and with how many tests ran
before it. A7 asks that any load-sensitive test among the eight be named; this is one, and the
sensitivity is the DEFECT rather than a property to be tolerated. Once the virtual driver is
installed the sensitivity disappears -- which is the check that the fix worked, and a better one than
"it passed once".

=== AREA (a): PARTIAL, AND NOT THE SAME CAUSE ===
    liveness.rs:111:72   the `.unwrap()` is the INNER one:
        timeout(cx.now(), Duration::from_secs(1), child.join(&cx)).await
            .expect("cancelled connection must settle")   <- outer: the timeout did NOT fire
            .unwrap()                                     <- THIS one, on the join result
    Err value: Cancelled(CancelReason { kind: User, message: Some("join channel closed") })
So the timeout was satisfied and `child.join(&cx)` itself returned a cancellation whose reason is a
CLOSED JOIN CHANNEL, where the test expects `Ok(Err(SecuredHttpEndpointError::Cancelled))`. That is a
teardown-ordering defect, not a clock defect -- the channel closed before join could deliver the
child's own result.
The `Time(1000000000ns)` in the payload is exactly the 1s timeout argument, so it is the deadline
being stamped, not evidence of a virtual clock. I am flagging that because it reads like one.
I AM NOT CLAIMING (a) SHARES (b)'s CAUSE. Both touch `cx.now()`; that is adjacency, and the failure
mechanisms differ.

=== (c) AND (d): THE REDACTION OBSTACLE IS REAL AND I HAVE NOT CLEARED IT ===

the generic InternalError in (d) is the redaction speaking and not the fault. Both need a different
observation point. (d) sits at tests.rs:6149, inside
`test_request_auth_propagates_through_nested_tool_calls`, which is one of the A2 four -- so A2 cannot
be resolved until (d)'s payload is recovered.

THE CALL ON (b), WHICH I OWN: NEITHER PRODUCTION NOR THE TEST'S INTENT IS WRONG. THE HARNESS IS.
And the cheaper repair I went looking for is IMPOSSIBLE, for a principled reason.
SilentSquirrel, assignee. Argued here BEFORE any change lands, per A6.

=== PRODUCTION IS CORRECT, AND DELIBERATELY TWO-CLOCK ===
    :110-111   next_check: Time        wall_expiry: Instant
    :136/:189  next_check = fresh_until(cx, cx.now(), interval)      <- derived FROM cx.now()
    :137/:207  wall_expiry = Instant::now() + interval               <- derived FROM Instant::now()
    :164       cx.now() < self.next_check && Instant::now() < self.wall_expiry
    :233       cx.budget().deadline.is_some_and(|d| cx.now() >= d)
    :239-243   fresh_until: end = now + interval, clamped by the budget deadline
Every comparison is WITHIN ONE DOMAIN. Production never assumes the caller clock has any particular
origin -- it only ever compares `cx.now()` against values it derived from `cx.now()`. The two clocks
are independent on purpose, so neither alone can keep a lease fresh forever. There is no production
defect here and I am not proposing a production change.

=== THE TEST'S INTENT IS ALSO CORRECT ===
    expired=false -> deadline = Time::from_nanos(1) -> check_context: 0 >= 1 is FALSE -> Ok
    expired=true  -> deadline = Time::from_nanos(0) -> check_context: 0 >= 0 is TRUE  -> TimedOut
The test is pinning whether the boundary comparison is `>=` or `>`. That is exactly what its name
says -- "exact deadline boundary" -- and it is a property worth having a test for.

=== SO I WENT LOOKING FOR THE CLOCK-AGNOSTIC REPAIR, AND IT DOES NOT EXIST ===
The obvious cheaper fix is to make the deadline RELATIVE: read the clock, then set
`deadline = base + 0ns / +1ns`, and delete the `assert_eq!(cx.now(), Time::ZERO)` as an unpromised
precondition. IT CANNOT WORK, for two compounding reasons:
  1. CHICKEN-AND-EGG. The deadline is an argument to `Cx::for_testing_with_budget`, so it must be
     computed BEFORE the cx exists. There is no `cx.now()` to be relative to yet.
  2. AND A WALL CLOCK ADVANCES BETWEEN THE TWO READS. Even sampling a throwaway
     `Cx::for_testing()` first, `wall_clock_now()` is evaluated per call, so the value at
     construction differs from the value at `check()` by an unknown interval.
YOU CANNOT PIN AN EXACT BOUNDARY AGAINST A CLOCK THAT MOVES BETWEEN THE DEADLINE'S CONSTRUCTION AND
ITS EVALUATION. An exact-boundary test REQUIRES a clock the test controls. That is not a stylistic
preference; it is the property under test.

=== THEREFORE: assert_eq!(cx.now(), Time::ZERO) IS NOT A WEAKENING CANDIDATE ===
It is the test correctly asserting the precondition its own design requires, and it is FAILING
HONESTLY -- telling us the harness does not supply what the test needs. Deleting it would remove the
only thing currently reporting that the harness is wrong. A6 is not engaged by the repair at all: no
assertion is weakened, no bound widened, nothing ignored. A clock is ADDED.

=== THE REPAIR, AND THE SHAPE IT LANDS IN ===
Option (A) from my addendum, and now the only option: host both revalidation tests in a runtime with
a VirtualClock timer driver, per the in-tree idiom (proxy.rs 13802/14594/15238/15520, wait.rs; 10
sites across 4 files).
  COMMIT 1  the execution-model change alone, claiming NO test outcome.
  COMMIT 2  the fix, separately.
That is the shape the ruling requires and it is what I will follow.

=== AND THE SIBLING IS PREDICTED, NOT ASSUMED ===
`monotonic_wall_expiry_still_triggers_when_the_caller_clock_does_not_move` has a premise -- the
caller clock does not move -- that a wall-clock fallback falsifies by construction. Same harness
defect, same repair, and it is the second site of the two the blast-radius scan found. If the
restructure fixes (b) and NOT the sibling, my account of the area is wrong and I want that reported
rather than worked around.

independently. That is a materially better position than "unprovable without (d)", but it is NOT

`/^    fn [a-z_]+\(\) \{/` and works here only because these test fns sit at a known indent and take

brace-bounding fails the other way (see my earlier note on a trailing brace ending a fn early). The
general answer is an AST query -- ast-grep, which AGENTS.md already recommends over ripgrep for
exactly this class of question -- not a better regex.

comments.text:
(c) IS FULLY DIAGNOSED. NO UNREDACTION, NO EDIT, NO RUN -- THE REDACTED STRING WAS RECOVERABLE FROM
SOURCE, AND ITS CAUSE HAS A PASSING CONTROL IN THE SAME FILE.
SilentSquirrel, assignee. Done during the RCH outage; needs no lane to establish, only to confirm.

=== RECOVERING THE REDACTED STRING WITHOUT UNREDACTING ANYTHING ===
The failure is `ServerError { description_len: 60 }` -- the Debug prints the LENGTH instead of the
value. But the value is a string LITERAL in shipped source, and a length is a search key.
Exactly ONE string literal in crates/fastmcp-server/src/oauth.rs is 60 bytes:
    oauth.rs:159   const OAUTH_ISSUER_ERROR: &str =
                       "OAuth issuer URL is invalid or outside retained-value bounds"
Sixty bytes, one match, and it is an issuer error -- consistent with the test supplying a custom
issuer while taking everything else from OAuthServerConfig::default().
A redacting Debug that prints `description_len` leaks a selector for its own constant pool. That is
not a complaint about the redaction; it is why this bead did not need the diagnostic commit.

=== THE CAUSE, TRACED TO ONE PREDICATE ===
    oidc.rs:2545   OAuthServer::try_new(..).unwrap()
    oauth.rs:2877  try_new -> config.validate()?
    oauth.rs:1118  validate -> validate_oauth_issuer(&self.issuer)?          FIRST check
    oauth.rs:4828  valid = parse_secure_endpoint(issuer, MAX_OAUTH_ISSUER_BYTES)
                           .is_some_and(|url| url.scheme()=="https" && url.query().is_none())
    oauth.rs:4809  parse_secure_endpoint returns None when  url.as_str() != value
`Url::parse("https://issuer.example")` normalises a bare authority by appending the root path, so
`as_str()` is "https://issuer.example/" while `value` is "https://issuer.example". They differ by
ONE BYTE and the endpoint is refused.
The other six rejection conditions in parse_secure_endpoint are eliminated by inspection: 22 bytes
is far under MAX_OAUTH_ISSUER_BYTES, no control chars, no userinfo, not cannot_be_a_base, host is
present, no fragment. Byte-inequality is the only candidate left.

=== THE CONTROL, AND IT IS IN THE SAME FILE ===
    oidc.rs:2494   issuer: "https://issuer.example/tenant"    PASSES -- has a path, so
                                                              Url::parse normalises to itself
    oidc.rs:2542   issuer: "https://issuer.example"           FAILS  -- bare authority, gains "/"
Same host, same scheme, same everything except the path. One passes, one fails, and the only
difference is whether normalisation had anything to add. That is a 1-vs-1 discriminator I did not
have to construct.

=== WHAT I AM NOT DECIDING, BECAUSE IT IS A RULING ===
TEST-DEFECT READING: the issuer is not in its own canonical form; add the slash and the test passes.
A one-character change, and the `discovery_document("https://issuer.example")` argument is a
SEPARATE parameter, so the `/register` assertion at :2560 is unaffected.
PRODUCTION-DEFECT READING: `url.as_str() != value` rejects the most common real-world issuer form.
OIDC compares issuer identifiers by exact string, and deployed issuers overwhelmingly omit the
trailing slash. A validator that demands one is an interop hazard, and the test may be right to
fail.
BLAST RADIUS IF THE SECOND READING WINS: parse_secure_endpoint is SHARED -- parse_redirect_uri
(oauth.rs:4837) uses it, where strict canonicality is far more defensible. Relaxing it for issuers
must not relax it for redirect URIs, so the remedy is probably not "delete the check".
I own neither call. Both are one-line changes and they point in opposite directions.

=== STATUS AND LIMITS ===
This establishes WHY the test fails. It does not establish that either remedy makes it pass --
that needs a run, and the lane is down. Nothing here is ticked.
I did not execute anything: no cargo in my lane. Every step above is a verbatim source read, and
the Url::parse normalisation is the one link I am asserting from knowledge of the crate rather than
from execution. If that link is wrong, the whole chain fails and I want it checked first.

title: HTTP-06 implementation B: forwarding headers, limits and denial precedence
description:
Executable implementation B leaf for formal package HTTP-06.

Canonical B capability slice: forwarding headers, limits and denial precedence.
Named consumer: HTTP-06 integration child.

Real implementation and its real positive and near-identical planted-negative tests are one Bead. Placeholders, refusal-only delivery, mocks presented as live proof, validator/test weakening, golden regeneration around broken behavior, and follow-up laundering are forbidden. Capability credit is limited to this named slice and begins only after central revision-bound batch verification.

Before claim, the assignee must replace the preclaim-denied ownership card with exact Owned, Shared, Reservation, and Integrator paths and acquire matching Agent Mail leases. No whole-crate or repository glob is valid.

Self-contained canonical parent contract follows verbatim:

Authoritative work package from `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_SUPPORT_MCP_2026-07-28_SPEC_IN_FASTMCP_RUST.md`:

### HTTP-06 — Integrate the fixed HTTP security pipeline

Outcome:

Prove the complete server ingress order from socket admission through
authorized handler dispatch.

Reason:

Pre-auth parsing, bearer authentication, operation authorization,
schema-derived headers, capability checks, and dispatch are
implemented in different packages; composition order is itself a
security property.

Implementation:

- Compose the thirteen stages specified by HTTP-02 without bypass
  hooks.
- At connection/stage-1 composition, make OAuth-protected routing and
  any Authorization-bearing request require HTTP-02's sealed
  `TlsProtectionEvidence` for the exact public HTTPS resource before
  the authenticator can borrow credential bytes. Direct loopback HTTP
  without confidential, integrity-protected, mutually authenticated
  terminator provenance may enter only an
  explicitly non-OAuth route; it cannot publish PRM, challenge for
  OAuth, or dispatch bearer-authenticated work.
- Keep private `TransportRequestParts` inside `fastmcp-transport`;
  invoke the borrowed `IngressAuthenticator` there and pass only
  `AuthenticatedTransportIngress` across the crate seam.
- Produce sanitized `InboundRequestContext` after authentication and
  retain only the gateway-safe `ValidatedForwardingHeaders` capsule
  when proxy mode is enabled.
- For every long-lived response, move AUTH-00's applicable purpose-
  typed guard into HTTP-01's transport-owned stream gate. Its
  authenticated branch owns the opaque `AuthorizationLease`; its
  public branch owns only the exact sealed public proof. Terminate
  output fail closed on lease expiry/revocation/grant loss/provider
  outage beyond maximum staleness or on public-visibility/
  configuration-generation drift and private/auth-varying
  reclassification.
- Invoke ADR-017's sealed `resolve_and_authorize` stage to perform
  caller-visible catalog resolution, visibility filtering, complete
  operation-scope calculation, scope-implication evaluation, and
  construction of `AuthorizedOperation` atomically. There is no
  separately observable “authorize name” then “private lookup” path.
- Give unknown and existing-but-hidden names the same bounded error
  shape and timing class. Disclose an operation's complete challenge
  scope set only after its visibility has been established.
- Validate recognized `Mcp-Param-*` fields only through the returned
  `AuthorizedOperation`.
- Validate required client capabilities and negotiated extensions
  after method/resource authorization.
- For a client→server extension notification, resolve EXT-01's exact
  current-message activation proof after authorization and before
  capability acceptance: decode a structurally admitted self-contained
  proof against current local server settings, or perform the
  non-oracular authorized lookup/revalidation of its negotiated-owner
  record. Bind the resulting sealed proof to extension, method,
  endpoint, security/authorization partition, effective settings,
  owner (if any), and descriptor/policy/configuration generations.
  Absent, one-sided, stale, incompatible, wrong-owner, or unprovable
  input fails without 202 or handler/supervisor effects. Registration,
  discovery, a previous request, and connection state cannot substitute.
- Invoke the sealed framework guard and typed middleware pipeline only
  after every prior ingress stage passes.
- Define exact first-failure behavior for requests with faults at
  multiple stages.
- Map pre-auth transport errors, auth challenges, post-auth JSON-RPC
  errors—including authenticated unknown method as HTTP 404/
  `-32601` and missing required capability as HTTP 400/`-32021`—and
  successful notification acceptance without response-body
  ambiguity.
- Define `NotificationDisposition` internally:
  `Completed` means the notification handler reached its terminal
  point inside request scope; `Supervised` contains an acknowledged,
  application-owned work record.
- Define that record as a sealed `AuthorizedNotificationWork`
  constructed only after `resolve_and_authorize`. It contains the
  canonical operation and sanitized parameters or protected payload
  reference, immutable original limit/deadline/maximum-queue-age
  snapshot, security and quota partitions, authorized-operation and
  implementation revisions, the sealed current-message extension
  activation proof when applicable, and AUTH-00's moved purpose-typed
  `NotificationAuthorizationGuard`; it never contains raw ingress
  credentials, transport parts, or the ingress `Cx`. The guard is
  authenticated with a provider-owned lease when execution varies by
  identity/grant/tenant and is public only when
  `resolve_and_authorize` sealed an exact auth-invariant public proof
  for this sanitized work and captured generations.
- Emit HTTP 202 only after one of those states is reached.
- Before supervised acknowledgement, response disconnect cancels the
  request-owned work and no 202 is committed.
- For supervised work, atomically transfer ownership through a public
  implementable
  `ApplicationNotificationSupervisor: Send + Sync + 'static` before
  202. Framework code creates a private one-shot activation channel;
  its sender is sealed inside the non-Clone
  `AuthorizedNotificationRunner`, while request code retains the
  receiver. The supervisor's `Cx`-aware accept operation receives that
  runner, a finite queue/activation deadline, and bounded dispatch
  contract, but receives no way to construct or send an acknowledgement.
  The runner consumes itself through its sole public `run(&Cx)`
  operation. Only framework code inside `run` may emit the sealed
  `RunnerInstalledReceipt`, and only after execution has actually
  started inside the supplied consumer-owned structured region, the
  work/authorization guard has been revalidated, and ownership plus
  the attenuated
  context are installed. Request code waits for that exact receipt
  within the handoff deadline before committing 202. Dropping the
  runner, cancelling the supervisor region, or returning a fabricated
  success closes or leaves the channel unsignalled and prevents 202;
  a late start after receiver expiry is cancelled/reconciled without
  invoking application work. External supervisor code cannot
  inspect, serialize, construct or widen work, recover raw credentials,
  substitute an operation/partition/guard, invoke it twice, or spawn
  outside its declared consumer-owned structured region. After the
  framework-emitted receipt, closing the response cannot cancel or
  orphan the accepted work. Publish a third-party compile/conformance
  harness; merely implementing the trait is not a support claim.
- Jointly admit queued count, active count, bytes, creation rate, and
  queue age under LIMIT-01's `QuotaPartitionKey` and deployment caps.
  Inside the consumer's application region, create a new attenuated
  child `McpContext` from the supervised closure's own `Cx`, with the
  minimum of the persisted snapshot, current configuration, and hard
  ceilings plus the finite notification execution deadline. Never
  capture/reuse the closing request context or inherit unbounded
  application-root authority.
- Before dispatch and across configured irreversible boundaries,
  revalidate the moved guard. Its authenticated branch revalidates the
  lease and exact required grants; its public branch reproves the exact
  route/work public and auth-invariant against captured generations.
  Expiry, revocation, policy/configuration/generation change, queue-age
  expiry, private/auth-varying reclassification, indeterminate public
  proof, or provider outage beyond applicable maximum staleness fails
  closed without application work.
- This is a process-lifetime supervised profile, not durable work:
  the request authorization guard, any contained
  `AuthorizationLease`, and work record are never
  serialized or recovered after process loss. Graceful shutdown drains
  within the configured deadline and then records a bounded redacted
  terminal-failure audit for unfinished accepted work. A crash may
  lose acknowledged notification work; the documented 202 guarantee
  is framework-confirmed activation in the process supervisor, not
  durable or exactly-once
